134. So it is also to be understood concerning **God** and the **Devil**: he is in God, but **shut up** in the Divine **Night** in the Center of Nature, with darkness in the essence of his life. And he has a magic fire-light from the **Ens** <note>original: "Ens"; a philosophical term for "being" or "essence"</note> of cold and heat; that is, a horrible light to our **eyes**, but to **him it is good**.

<margin>* Luke 19:18.</margin>
135. The Scripture says, *the great Prince Michael strove with the Dragon*, but the Dragon did not prevail. And in another place, *I saw Satan fall from heaven like lightning*, says Christ.

136. This Prince Michael is a throne-angel, and in the power of Christ—that is, in the **Word** of the Holy Power—he strove with him. It was in this **Word** that **Adam** was created. That Word of power is understood to be in all the three principles <note>In Boehme's theology, the three principles are the dark world (fire/wrath), the light world (love/majesty), and the outer world (nature/matter).</note>.

137. For when Lucifer fell and gave himself up into the Kingdom of the Fantasy <note>original: "Phantafy"; here referring to the realm of self-will and delusion</note>, he lost the Kingdom in the **Holy Power** and was thrust out. This was done by the enterprise and administration of the angels, who thrust him out as an apostate by Divine Power.

<insert>Handwritten blue bracket in left margin</insert>
138. And in the same power, in the **Word**, out of all the three principles, was **Man** created.

<margin>* Anointed.</margin>
139. But when the Kingdom of Wrath overcame Man and thrust him out from the Temperature <note>original: "Temperature"; refers to the perfect, harmonious balance of all spiritual qualities</note>, then the Highest Name of the Deity manifested itself in him (that is, in Man). This was that most sweet power, JESUS, which overthrew the Kingdom of the Fantasy and of the Wrath, and **tinctured** <note>original: "tinctured"; spiritually infused or transformed</note> Man with the highest Love.

<margin>* The Anointed.</margin>
140. And there also was the Devil’s kingdom, dominion, and authority destroyed in the power of Man. From this springs the name **CHRISTUS**, or **CHRIST**.

# The Fifth Chapter.
## Of the Origin of Man.

<margin>¶ Genesis 2:7.</margin>
<margin>* Extract.</margin>
<image-desc>Ornate woodcut initial letter M featuring floral and vine motifs.</image-desc>
1. **M**oses says, God created Man out of the dust or clay, or a lump or clod of earth. Understand this to be the body, which is a **limus** <note>original: "Limus"; Latin for mud, slime, or clay</note> of the Earth.

<margin>f Expressed, or out-spoken.</margin>
<insert>Handwritten blue asterisk in right margin</insert>
2. And the Earth is an **Ens** <note>being or essence</note> out of the three principles—an exhaled, contracted, and coagulated **power** out of the Word of all the three principles, **from the Great Mystery** <note>original: "ex Mysterio magno"</note>; that is, out of the first three and out of the seven forms or properties of nature.

3. They have imprinted themselves in the kindled desire—that is, in the **Fiat** <note>original: "Fiat"; Latin for "let it be," the creative command of God</note>—and brought themselves into substance, each property in itself becoming a solid compaction.

<margin>g Or Mass.</margin>
4. Which God, in the **Fiat** (that is, in the substantial science <note>In this context, "science" refers to active knowledge or creative power</note>), has contracted into a lump or clod. In this clod, all powers of the spiritual world—according to God's love and anger, and also according to the Fantasy—lie fixed. They are not there in the manner of a mind, but in the manner of an **Ens**.

<insert>Handwritten "Man" in blue ink with a line pointing to paragraph 5</insert>
5. In the Mind, first, is understood the living substantiality which is spiritual—a totally spiritual substance, a spiritual **Ens** of the **Tincture**, wherein the highest power of the fire and light is introduced into a being.

6. And second, in the **Ens**, the life of the seven properties of nature is understood—the sensible vegetative life—which is the expressed, outspoken Word that, in its growth, expresses, forms, and coagulates itself again.

<insert>Handwritten asterisk in left margin</insert>
7. But the **Mind** <note>original: "Mens"; Latin for mind</note> lies in the **Ens**, or Being, just as the soul lies in the body; the mental Word speaks forth the "ental" <note>the word belonging to the essence or being</note>.

<margin>
A useful "genealogy"
</margin>

8. The Heaven includes the *Mens* <note>Latin: "Mind"</note> or Mind, and the Phantasy includes the *Ens* <note>Latin: "Being" or essence</note> or *Being*; understand it this way:
9. Within the *Mens* or Mind, we understand the divine, holy power in the comprehension or framing of the Word. Here, the Word of Power compresses or compacts itself into a spiritual substance, through which the Word of Power becomes *substantial*.
10. Thus, the *Mens* or Mind is the spiritual water, and the power within it—which forms itself into a "Spirit-Water"—is now the highest *Tincture* <note>original: "Tincture," a term in alchemy and mysticism for the essential spiritual quality or life-force</note>, which exists in the "Temperature" <note>original: "Temperature," meaning a state of perfect balance or harmony</note>.
11. And the ground <note>original: "Ground," meaning the underlying foundation or source</note> of that very *Tincture* is the *spiritual Wisdom*.
12. And the ground of that *Wisdom* is the *Trinity* of the *Abyssal Deity* <note>original: "Abyssal Deity," referring to God as the "Unground" or the bottomless source of all being</note>.
13. And the ground of the *Trinity* is the *one and only unsearchable Will*.
14. And the ground of the *Will* is the *Nothing* <note>Referring to the mystical "No-thingness" before creation</note>.
15. Therefore, the mind should first learn what is understood to be in the Earth before it says, "*Man is Earth*." It should not look upon the Earth as a cow does, which assumes the Earth is merely the *mother* of grass and requires nothing more than grass and herbs.
16. But man desires to eat the best of what proceeds out of the Earth; therefore, he should also learn to recognize that he is also the *best thing* that proceeds from the Earth.
17. For every *Ens* <note>being or essence</note> desires to feed upon its mother, from which it proceeded.
18. Accordingly, we see very well that man does not desire to feed upon the grossest or coarsest of the earthly *Ens*, but upon the purest and most subtle—that is, he desires the *Quintessence* <note>the "fifth essence," the purest part of a substance</note> for his life's power, which he had for his food even in Paradise.
19. But when he went out of the "Temperature" <note>balance</note> and into the "Science" <note>original: "Science," meaning the knowledge or root experience</note> of divisibility or distinction, God set the *Curse* between the element of the Temperature and the four elements. Man had entered, with his desire, into the disagreement of properties, which had condensed within him into a beast-like, hard, graspable, palpable, and physical substance of enmity in the Phantasy—namely, into the four elementary, gross drossiness of heat and cold, and the venomous quality of the dark world—which is *mortality*. Consequently, he must now eat of those properties within himself.
20. For inequality or discord does not belong to the balance of the one holy element, but to the four elements <note>earth, air, fire, and water</note>.
21. Therefore, the Curse is the mark or *limit* of separation, ensuring that the unclean does not enter the clean.
22. For the Curse is nothing else but a retreating of that which is good—which the one holy element had contained within itself—and *hiding* it from the substance of evil and wickedness.
<margin>Genesis 3:6</margin>
23. For in *Adam’s* innocence, the holy element in its balanced state sprang up through the four elements and bore heavenly fruit. As *Moses* says, this fruit was *lovely to behold and good for food*. It is in that "springing forth" that Paradise is understood to exist.
24. For that fruit existed in the quality of balance, and *Adam* also stood in that balance; thus, he could and should have eaten paradisical fruit.
25. But when he introduced himself—through longing or lust—into the multitude of properties (that is, into the *Phantasy* of inequality or difference in the center) and wanted to know all things and be wise, trying how heat and cold and all other properties tasted in their wrestling strife, then those *properties* in conflict took hold of him and awakened within him. With that desire, they compacted themselves into the substance of the Phantasy.
<margin>* in inverse relation to the last passage</margin>
26. Thus, the Image of God (consisting of that balanced state) was destroyed, and the light in the substance of the holy element was extinguished in him, through which he once knew God. Thus, he <gloss>circled</gloss> died to the balance and <gloss>circled</gloss> awakened to the four elements and the unequal or discordant "science" or root, which now cause him sickness and death; and that is the true ground of his condition.

27. But so that we may satisfy the enquiring mind, who asks after its Father’s or native country and is on the journey of its pilgrimage, we will set before that person the following:

->I. What he properly is.<-
->II. Of what he is created.<-
->III. And what his soul and body are.<-
->IV. Also his Fall and Restoration.<-

By this, we shall be able very fundamentally to show him the basis of the *Divine Will* toward him.

28. And after that, we will prove it by the *Holy Scriptures* and demonstrate it by their *supposed* contradiction, so that thereby, if possible, the eyes of *some* might be opened. We shall do this faithfully, according to our gift.

<margin>! Genesis 1:27.</margin>
29. *Moses* says very rightly, *God created man according to his image*; yes, to the *image of God created he him*. Also, God made man out of the <term>limus</term> <note>original: "limus," referring to the slime, mud, or clay-like dust of the earth</note>, or of the *dust of the earth*.

30. In saying that God created man in *his image*, *Moses* does not mean: 1. that God is a physical image, or 2. that God has created man according to *his own* physical model.

31. Rather, he understands the "science" <note>In this context, "science" refers to the divine knowledge or the cognitive root of being</note> or root in the **power**, in which all things have modeled themselves from eternity within that knowledge, in the <term>temperature</term> <note>original: "temperature," meaning the perfect balance or harmonious mixture of all qualities</note> within the powers in the Spirit of *Wisdom*.

32. These were not yet creatures, but a shadow, idea, *representation*, *reflection*, or pre-modeling in a mirror, where God has from eternity seen in his *Wisdom* what could be.

<margin>
* Platform, or design.
</margin>
33. By this *resemblance*, the Spirit of God has acted out a scene in the *Wisdom*, in the contained *model. In this model, the spirit of the knowledge or root in the *Wisdom* has from eternity—within the nature of the powers—modeled itself into a *scene*. (This model was not a creature, but like the shadow of a creature.) By this resemblance, God has created the creaturely man—specifically into man’s own image.

34. Which was not yet a man, but was God’s *image*. In this image, the Spirit of God modeled itself out of all principles into a shadow of equality, harmony, uniformity, and conformity to the *Substance* of all substances.

<margin>
* Note.
</margin>
35. * Just as a man standing before a looking glass sees himself—his image being in the glass, but having no *life*—so we are to conceive of man as the image of God from eternity. This applies also to the whole creation: how God has seen or foreseen all things from eternity in the *scene* of his *Wisdom*.

<margin>
<note>Blue ink mark, possibly "INT" or a monogram next to a bracket</note>
</margin>
36. And when God had gathered all the powers of all the three principles in the divine knowledge into a *substance*, and contracted them into a lump—which is called Earth, acting as a solidification of the generating spiritual power—he then divided the elements of the <term>temperature</term> of the one primordial element into four physical elements to create a *moving* life.

37. And further, he gathered the spiritual power of nature—out of which the *material* solidification found in the Earth and other materials comes—into the stars.

38. For from the same substance that the Earth is physical, the stars are spiritual. Yet they are not living spirits; rather they are a spiritual <term>ens</term> <note>original: "ens," a philosophical term for an essence or "beingness"</note>, specifically powers, a <term>quintessence</term> <note>original: "quintessence," the "fifth essence" or the pure, subtle power from which the four elements arise</note>. This is the subtle power from which the Earth—the density or grossness—has separated itself, and which God, in the knowledge of his speaking, formed into a variety of powers.

39. And they are called *stars* because they are a moving, hard, greedy <note>In Boehme’s vocabulary, "greedy" implies an attractive, pulling, or contracting force</note>, contracting <term>ens</term>, in which the properties of nature are understood.

40. All that nature is in itself spiritually, in its perfect balance, is what the stars are in their difference and *variety*, as I present it here for your *understanding*.

41. If the stars were all extinguished or passed away and returned again into that from which they proceeded, then *nature* would be as it has been from eternity: for it would stand again in its perfect balance.

42. And so shall it be again in the *end*; yet in such a way that all substances or things shall be <insert><note>Circled in blue ink</note>tried by the fire</insert> and separated into *their own principle*.

# Chapter 5.
## Of the Origin of Man.

43. Through this division, understanding, and framing of the power of the stars and the four elements, we understand *Time* and the beginning of the world's creatures.

44. Now, when God had created the Earth and the firmament of the stars, and had placed the *planetary* orb of the seven properties of nature (with the Sun as their ruler) in the middle, the Spirit of the World revealed itself from all the properties of these powers—from the stars and the elements.

45. For every power has an *emanation* <term>original: "Emanation"; a flowing out or manifestation of a divine or natural source</term>, according to the law of nature, within the "speaking Word" <note>Boehme refers to the "Word of God" as an active, creative force that speaks through reality</note>.

46. This eternal Word has enclosed and contained itself within the *Mysterium Magnum* <note>Latin: "Great Mystery"; in Boehme's theology, the source or "chaos" from which all things are manifested</note> for a period of time, as a representation of the spiritual *Mysterium Magnum*. It is like a great clockwork, in which a person understands the spiritual Word through its physical manifestation or form.

47. The entire work of creation is the formed *Word of God*. Understand this as the *natural* Word, within which the *living* Word of God—who is God himself—is understood in its deepest inwardness. This Word speaks through nature, manifesting as the Spirit of the World (*Spiritum Mundi* <note>Latin: "Spirit of the World"</note>), serving as the soul of creation.

48. Within this "speaking forth" or expression, there is again a distinction or separation into the fiery astral science <note>original: "Science"; here meaning a fundamental principle, root, or structured form of natural knowledge</note> within the *Spiritum Mundi*. In this state, the fiery science manifests as a spiritual distribution.

49. This distribution includes the spirits within the elements. These are categorized according to the distinction of the *four* elements <note>Earth, Air, Fire, and Water</note>, with each spirit belonging to an element based on its specific property.

<margin>Or "in."</margin>
50. For every element has its own resident spirits, according to the quality of that element. These are a *shadow*, *image*, and resemblance of the Eternal, yet they possess a true and perfect life derived from the *science of nature*. This life comes from the spoken or expressed Word *ex Mysterio Magno* <note>Latin: "From the Great Mystery"</note>.

<margin>Fiery spirits, airy spirits, watery spirits, earthly spirits.</margin>
51. This life does not come from the true divine life, but from the natural life. These spirits hold dominion over fire, air, water, and earth, following patterns, orders, and systems just as the stars follow their constant inherent *paths*. This is to be understood as applying to both of the poles.

52. The Spirit of the World is now the *life of the external world*. The stars and constellations exist in a circumference or sphere surrounding everything; they contain the "three first" <note>likely referring to Boehme's three primary qualities: Sulfur, Mercury, and Salt</note> within them in a sharp, fiery science or root. Indeed, they are that very substance itself, though with great difference, distinction, and variety.

53. Those various powers proceed from the Spirit of the World and act as a "hunger" <note>Boehme uses "hunger" to describe an inherent desire or attraction toward a specific substance</note> based on their inherent nature—specifically toward the Earth and its physical materials.

54. Similarly, the Earth "hungers" for the Spirit of the World, because it originated from it and was divided from it. <gloss>divided?</gloss>

55. Thus, the superior desires the inferior, and the inferior desires the superior. The higher hunger is directed strongly toward the Earth, and the hunger of the Earth is directed toward the higher powers.

56. Therefore, whatever is material falls toward the Earth, just as water is also attracted to the Earth.

57. On the other hand, the fiery spirit in the higher realms draws the water up into itself for its own refreshment.

58. This process generates water, releases it, and then—after it has been tempered with the Earth—attracts it back into itself. They are to each other like body and soul, or like a husband and wife who conceive children together.

<margin>Womb.</margin> <margin>Genesis 1:20, 22, 23.</margin>
59. From this birth, as if from the *Matrix* <note>original: "Matrix"; the womb or source of origin</note> of nature, God—through the Word *Fiat* <note>Latin: "Let it be done"</note> (that is, the substantial desire of the powers)—commanded all creatures on the fifth day to emerge from every science or root, according to *their property or kind*; namely, the body...

### Of the Origin of Man. Chapter 5.

...from the firmness of the earth, and the spirit from the *Spirit of the World* <note>original: Spiritu Mundi</note>; and this is done in the conjunction of the superior and inferior; that is:

60. The inward Divine Word spoke or breathed itself out, through the outward spoken Word, into *every differentiation <note>original: "Science"; here meaning a distinct branch or specific quality of the divine power</note> in the fiery property of the powers* into a creaturely life.

61. These are now the creatures upon earth, and in the water, and in the air—the birds and every creature—from its own essential nature <note>original: "Science"</note> or *root* of good and evil, according to the properties of all the three principles. Each of them is an image of the similarity of the *inward ground*, originating from the kingdom of imagination <note>original: "Phantasy"; in this context, the realm of forms and appearances within nature</note> as well as from the original good life.

62. Thus it is apparent to the sight that there are good and also evil creatures: namely, venomous beasts and worms, according to the *center* of the nature of darkness, from the force of the wrathful property. These desire only to dwell in the dark, such as those that live in holes and hide themselves from the sun.

63. On the other hand, humans also find many creatures in which the *Spirit of the World* from the kingdom of imagination has modeled itself, such as apes and similar beasts and birds, which play tricks, worry, hunt, vex, and disquiet other creatures.

64. So it is that one is an enemy to the other continually, and they all strive against one another after their kind, just as the Three Principles <note>The Three Principles are a core concept in the author's cosmology: the dark fire-world (wrath), the light-world (love), and the outward world (nature)</note> play out or act a scene with one another in their powers. Thus, God has introduced that play or scene before him, by the *Spirit of the World* in its essential nature or root, into a living, creaturely substance. <insert>Hand-drawn blue bracket marks the end of this paragraph in the right margin.</insert>

65. We also find there are good, quiet, friendly creatures, according to the resemblance and model of the angelic world, wherein the *Spirit of the World* has modeled itself in the good, spoken powers; these are the tame beasts and birds.

66. And yet there are also many evil beasts—that is, evil properties—among the tame ones, which are also formed and captured in the mixture of properties.

67. In the food and habitation of every beast, humans see from where they have sprung; for every creature desires to dwell in its *mother* <note>The "mother" refers to the source or element from which the creature originated</note>, and longs after her, as is clearly seen.

68. The *Spirit of the World*, from which all outward creatures proceeded as to their spirit, is included within a time, limit, and measure of how long it shall endure.

69. It is like a clockwork mechanism made of the stars and elements, wherein the Most High God dwells and uses this clockwork as his instrument. He has included his making and work within it, which proceeds freely and generates according to its *minutes* <note>The specific intervals or programmed movements of nature</note>, as a person might compare it to a machine.

70. All things lie within it—whatever is done in the world, and whatever shall be done.

71. It is God's predestined purpose toward and in the creature, wherein he manages all things by this *government of nature*.

72. For in God himself, so far as he is called "God," there is *no* predestined purpose to evil or to anything else, for he is the one and only Good, and has nothing else perceivable in him except *only himself*.

73. And in his Word which he has spoken forth from himself—that is, *in the Spirit of the World out of the Great Mystery* <note>original: in Spiritu Mundi ex Mysterio Magno</note> of the Eternal Nature—he has comprised his predestined purpose, and included it in the free clockwork of the *Spirit of the World*. That mechanism generates and corrupts everything according to its natural course, and produces both fruitfulness and barrenness.

<margin>*</margin> 74. But God in his essence or substance pours forth his love-power into it; that is, he sheds *himself* abroad within it, just as the sun does in the essential nature or root of the elements and fruits. That is, the holy Divine nature gives *power and virtue* to the natural root.

<margin>1 John 4:16.</margin> 75. God loves all his creatures, and can do nothing else but love; for *he is the only love itself*.

It emphasizes that while nature contains conflict and wrath, God himself is pure love and pours his virtue into the world like sunlight.</summary>

76. But his *Wrath* is understood to be in both Eternal and Temporal Nature: in the Eternal, it is in the Center of Darkness—namely, in the cold and hot source of fire; and similarly, in the Spirit of the World, it is understood to be in the fiery "science" <note>original: *science*. In this context, "science" refers to an essential root, a disposition, or the active knowledge-principle of a thing’s properties.</note> or root, or the division and distinction of all properties.

<margin>A fullness or ripeness of sin.</margin>
77. And so now, if a city, country, or creature awakens or stirs up that wrath in the fiery root within the Spirit of the World <note>original: *Spiritu Mundi*</note> in itself—that is, if it introduces an abomination into that wrath—then it is like wood in a fire. The wrath becomes active and cooperative, devouring everything around it and putting the life within the creature's root into the highest torment.

78. And then, the angry, fiery Word speaks in the awakened *Turba* <note>original: *Turba*, a term used by Jacob Boehme to describe a state of "disturbance" or "turmoil" that leads to destruction or divine judgment.</note> through the prophetic spirit in the *Turba Magna* (the Great Turmoil): 
> I will call for misery, mischief, and desolation upon a city and country, and will see my desire executed in vengeance and indignation upon it; so that the wrath may devour their abominations, until it has quite consumed this wicked people.

<margin>Wrath?</margin>
79. For that is the very joy, recreation, and mighty force of the *Wrath* in nature: when men introduce such fuel—namely, impious blasphemy and other sins and filthiness—into it, the wrath devours them; they are its food.

80. Especially in such a case where the human "science" or root breaks itself off from the love of God and commits adultery with the wrath of nature, it fattens itself to the full, until the universal fabric, or "clockwork" <note>original: *Clock-work*. The author views the physical universe as a complex, mechanical system governed by natural laws.</note>, moves into a fiery root. There all things stand in the *Proba* <note>original: *Proba*, meaning a trial or test.</note> or trial; then the wrath kindles itself within, and as the *Turba* is kindled in the wheel or orb of the cosmic machine, one specific property is manifested, and then comes the *Plague*.

81. And thus it is spread abroad upon that country, city, and creature; often in venom and poison through the pestilence, often by drought and infertility, and often by embittering the minds of superiors and the "Great Ones," from which *wars* arise. Now it follows:

### Concerning Man.

82. Man is created in the image of God from this great machine or clockwork—from that which is superior and inferior—in which all things lie together, one within the other.

<margin>JEHOVAH, Gen. i. 26.</margin>
83. For *Moses* says: *The LORD said, "Let us make man, an image of us, or according to our image; so that he may rule over, or within, all the creatures upon the earth: the beasts, birds, fish, and all the earth, and every creeping thing that moves upon the earth."*

84. Now, if he is to rule in all of them, he must also consist of the substance <note>original: *Ground*</note> of them all; and moreover, he must come out of the best power and virtue of them.

85. For nothing rules any deeper than its "mother" <note>The source or material from which a thing originates.</note> from which it has proceeded—unless it is transformed or metamorphosed into something better; and even then, it rules in that better thing, yet no further than the fundamental ground of that thing.

<margin>Gen. ii. 7.</margin>
86. And then *Moses* says further: *God made man of the dust of the earth (or a clod of earth) and breathed into him the living breath, and then man became a living soul.*

87. But we are to understand here that God did not stand by in a personal and physical manner like a man, take a lump or clod of earth, and make a body out of it. No, it was not so.

88. Instead, the Word of God—namely, the *Speaking Word*—was present in all properties within the Spirit of the World <note>original: *Spiritu Mundi*</note> and in the *Ens* <note>original: *Ens*, referring to the essential being or substance of a thing.</note> or being of the earth. It stirred from the Spirit of the World and spoke or breathed forth a life into every essence.

89. This was the *Fiat* <note>The Latin command "Let it be done," used here as the creative power of God's desire.</note>, or creating power, which is the desire of the Word in the "science" or root that was in the model or *Idea* of man, which was eternally seen, which...

# Of the Origin of Man. Chapter 15.

...which stood in the Wisdom, and attracted the *Ens* <term>Latin: essence or being</term> of all properties of the earth, and whatever could possibly be within it, into a mass or physical form.

90. This was the quintessence <term>the purest, most concentrated essence of a substance</term> of the four elements, which contained the *tincture* <note>In alchemy, a spiritualized essence or "soul" of a substance</note> of all powers from all the three principles. Furthermore, it contained the *property* of the entire creation of all creatures—that is, the substance of all substances from which all creatures originated.

91. For you must understand it correctly: the earthly creatures of time have bodies made from the four elements. But the body of man is made from the *Temperature* <note>original: "Temperature"; here meaning a state of perfect balance or harmony where no single element dominates</note>, in which all four elements exist together in *one substance*. This is the same source from which the earth, stones, metals, and all earthly creatures have their origin.

92. Indeed, it was made from the *Limus* <term>Latin: slime or clay, referencing the dust of the ground in Genesis 2:7</term> of the earth, but not from the coarseness of the compacted substance that resulted from the division into different properties—where each property hardened itself into a *distinct substance* like soil, stones, or metals.

93. Instead, it was formed from the quintessence, where the four elements exist in a state of balance. In this state, neither heat nor cold was dominant; they were all in equal *weight or balance*.

94. For if man is to rule over all creatures, he must possess the supreme power within him—namely, the highest *Ens* or being of the creatures. The creature itself is a degree further outward, lower, or inferior—or as one might say, a degree "less"—so that the stronger may rule over the weaker, just as God rules over nature, which is indeed *less than He*.

95. But this should not be understood as if animal-like properties were then active or visible in man; rather, the *Ens* or being of all creatures existed within the human essence in a state of perfect balance.

96. Man is an image of the entire creation and of all the three principles. This is true not only in the *Ens* or being of the outward nature—the stars and the four elements of the created world—but also in the essence of the inward spiritual world, the Divine Substantiality.

97. For the holy Word, in its own *Ens* or being, gathered itself *together* into the spoken or expressed Word. That is, Heaven gathered itself into the substance of the outward world, just as the power of growth <note>original: "Vegetation"</note> gathered in the inward world’s substance—namely, *Paradise*. The holy element was present in its active, life-giving power <note>original: "boiling springing Dominion"</note>.

98. In brief, the human body is a *Limus* <term>essence or clay</term> drawn from the "substance of all substances"; otherwise, it could not be called a likeness or an image of God.

99. The invisible God—who from eternity has expressed himself in *substance*, and also through this world into *time*—has modeled himself through man’s image into a creaturely form: a visible figure of the invisible substance.

100. Moreover, He did not give man a mere animal life drawn from the root of other creatures (for that life should have remained undivided, remaining in a state of balance). Instead, <insert>he breathed</insert> into him the *living breath*—the true, original, understanding life found in the *Word* of divine power.

101. That is, He breathed into him the true *soul* of all the three principles in their balanced state.

102. From within, He breathed the "Magic Fire-World"—the center of nature mentioned previously. This is the true creaturely fire-soul, which is why God calls himself a "strong, zealous, or jealous God" and a "consuming fire"—referring to Eternal Nature.

103. And together with this, He also breathed in the Light-World—the kingdom of the power of God. Just as fire and light exist within one another without being separated, so it is to be understood here.

104. And from the outside, He also breathed into him the spirit of the world: the *air-soul.*

# Chap. 5. Of the Origin of Man.

105. Thus the entire speaking Word breathed itself into all of Nature, according to both time and eternity.

106. For Man was an image of God, in whom the invisible God was manifested; that is, a true temple of the Spirit of God.

<margin>John 1:4.</margin>
107. As it is written in the first chapter of *John*: *the life of man was in the Word*; and it was breathed into the created image.

108. That is, the Spirit of God breathed into him the life of nature in the <term>Temperature</term> <note>original: "Temperature"; a state of perfect balance or harmony between the various qualities of nature, before they became conflicted.</note>—specifically, the spirit of the **Divine Revelation** or **Manifestation**, where the **Divine Science** <note>original: "Divine Science"; referring here to the divine knowledge or the fundamental "root" of God's wisdom.</note> or root introduces itself into a natural life.

<margin>Matthew 22:30.</margin>
109. In that divine natural life, Man is like the angels of God regarding the soul—that is, the spiritual world—as it is written: *In the resurrection they are as the angels of God.*

110. And thus we enter again into the first created divine image, and *not* into another creature.

111. Therefore, we are to understand Man rightly in this way:

->**I. What he *was* in innocence.**<-
->**II. What he *became* afterwards.**<-

<margin>Genesis 3:6.</margin>
112. Man was in Paradise, which is the Temperature: he was placed in one certain location where the *holy world* sprouted forth through the earth and bore paradisiacal fruit. This fruit also existed in its essence within the Temperature; *that fruit was good and pleasant to behold, and also good for food, to be eaten in a heavenly manner.*

113. It was not to be swallowed down into a carcass for the worms, as it is now in our awakened animal-like property, but was consumed in a magical manner.

114. It was indeed to be eaten in the mouth, but the *centers* of distinction and separation were in the mouth; they divided each principle into its own, in the same way that it may be done in eternity.

115. Just as the spirit of the world generates water from the three primary elements—namely, from the fiery **Sulphur**, **Mercury**, and **Sal** <note>Sulphur, Mercury, and Salt: In alchemical philosophy, these represent the three fundamental principles of all matter: the combustible (Sulphur), the volatile (Mercury), and the solid/stable (Salt).</note>—and gives it forth from itself (specifically in the <term>Sal Nitrum</term> <note>original: "Sal Nitrum"; saltpeter, representing here a transformative or creative spiritual force</note> of the separation) and also draws it up again from the earth into itself without being satisfied; so it is also to be understood in Man.

116. *Adam* was naked, yet clothed with the greatest glory—namely, with Paradise. He was a totally fair, beautiful, bright, clear, crystalline *image*, neither man nor woman but both; that is, a masculine virgin, with both <term>Tinctures</term> <note>original: "Tinctures"; the spiritual qualities or "colors" of the soul, representing the active/masculine and passive/feminine principles.</note> in a state of balance.

117. That is, there was the heavenly <term>Matrix</term> <note>original: "Matrix"; a womb or creative source.</note> or womb in the generating fire of love, and also the <term>Limbus</term> <note>original: "Limbus"; the essential "extract" or substance of the earth's nature.</note> from the nature of the essential fire; in both of these, the first and second principles of the holy **Divine Nature** are understood.

118. Within this, the <term>Tincture of Venus</term> <note>original: "Tincture of Venus"; the spiritual quality associated with love and the feminine aspect of creation.</note>—which is the generating and giving forth out of the Son’s property—is understood to be the Woman, or the Mother; that is, the <term>Genetrix</term> <note>original: "Genetrix"; Latin for "one who gives birth" or "mother."</note> or bringer forth.

119. And the fiery property is understood to be from the Father’s property—namely, the "science" or root is understood to be the Man. These two properties afterwards divided and distinguished themselves into man and woman, or husband and wife.

<margin>Or, as a candle set between two large looking-glasses produces an infinite, wonderful reproduction.</margin>
120. For if *Adam* had remained in his original state, then the birth and reproduction of Man would have been magical—one coming out of the other: *Just as the sun penetrates through glass without breaking it.*

121. But seeing that God knew very well that *Adam* would not remain in that state, he ordained for him the Savior and Regenerator before the foundation of the world.

122. And yet, at the beginning, he created him in a right, true image and put him into Paradise, where he was intended to be eternally.

## Of Man's Fall, and of his Wife.

2. This is so they might not dwell on the idea <note>original: "Conceit" here means a notion or misconception</note> that God had a predestined purpose to *damn* one group of people and, by grace, to *save* the other according to his predestined purpose. He cannot exist in eternity in a twofold life—namely, in a masculine and feminine form—according to the property of the Father and the Son, who together are only one God, undivided. So, he also created his image and likeness as one single image.

7. For perfect love does not consist of one tincture alone, but it consists in *both*, with one entering into the other. From that union arises the great, fiery desire of love.

This is also how we are to understand the nature of *Adam*.

## Chapter 6. Concerning Man's Fall, and his Wife.

11. But when the spiritual essence <note>original: "Tincture"; refers to the vital, transformative quality or soul-spirit</note> of Light and Water was *divided* and *separated* from him into a Woman, or Wife, he could no longer remain eternally in that image which he afterwards became. For his inner Rose-Garden of Paradise, in which he had loved himself, was taken away from him.

### Question.

12. Then *Reason* says: Why did God do so? Why did he divide him and bring him into *two images*? Surely it must have been his predetermined purpose, or else he would not have done it. Moreover, he foresaw before the foundation of the world that he would will and do it.

### Answer.

13. And here *Reason* reaches a dead end and can go no further without the knowledge of God in the Holy Spirit; this is the source of all dispute and conflict.
14. God’s predetermined purpose and pre-ordination are *not the same thing* as his foresight and foreknowledge.
15. *All things* have been foreseen in the spoken Word <note>original: "out-speaking or expressing Spirit"</note> from the knowledge of the Fire and Light within the Wisdom of God from eternity. He saw whatever might or could be, if God’s being or substance *once stirred* itself according to the *Genitrix* <note>original: "Genitrix of Nature"; the generating source or "mother" of nature</note> of Nature.
16. That is, in the property of the fiery knowledge regarding the Darkness, he saw what would be a *Devil*; likewise, in the knowledge of the Light-Fire, he saw what would be an *Angel*, should the fiery knowledge ever separate itself from the Light.
<margin>But by predestination.</margin>
17. But God created no Devil. Now, if there had been any divine predetermined purpose, then *there would have been* a Devil created by that very purpose.
18. The one and only Will of God gave and yielded itself *solely* in an angelic form. However, the fiery knowledge—according to the property of the dark-world—pushed forward and conceived itself into a predetermined purpose, insisting on becoming a creaturely being as well.
19. And so, when the Light and shining Fire became creaturely, the dark, cold, painful fire also pushed forward with the forming of *Fantasy* <note>original: "Phantasy"; here meaning the power of false imagination or illusion</note>. It united itself with the fiery knowledge, which it clung to like a *playful ape* <note>original: "jocund Ape"</note>, and pushed out of the Temperature <note>original: "Temperature"; the state of perfect balance and harmony between opposing qualities</note>. Thus, the new will generated itself contrary to that harmony and was *cast out* from God.
<margin>Margin: predestination.</margin>
20. One must understand that the beginning of *division* and separation did not arise in God, as if God conceived a will in himself to *have* a Devil. Rather, it happened in the knowledge within Eternal Nature, in the speaking of the Word according to Fire and Light. It was brought to pass in the "first three" <note>likely referring to the first three properties of eternal nature in Boehme's cosmology</note>, so that one princely throne in the fiery knowledge divided itself into its own kingdom—namely, into the *Archia* <note>original: "Archia"; the ruling principle or dominion</note> or dominion of *Fantasy*.
21. But the kingdom of *Fantasy* according to the Darkness has existed from eternity, and this was also a *cause* of the Devil’s fall. However, the fiery knowledge of *Lucifer* stood in his own will and surrendered to it *without any pressure or compulsion*.
22. But Man was betrayed by the Devil and fell. Because Prince *Lucifer* fell before the foundation of the world during the *first movement* or impression of nature, and was cast out from his *royal* place, *Adam* was therefore created in his stead and place.
23. And seeing that *Lucifer* did *not* remain standing, God created *Adam*—out of Love—in a *material substance* (namely, in a "fountain of water") so that God might help or save him.
24. And then, instantly, the holy name JESUS incorporated itself into Man to be a Regenerator.

27. The human soul, the Devil, and the holy angels all come from one and the same source and foundation. The only difference is that humanity also has the external world within it *in part*. The Devil also possesses the external world, but in a different principle: namely, in *fantasy* <term>the realm of illusion or false imagination</term> and in false or wicked *magic* <note>original: "Magia"; the creative or formative power of the soul</note>.

He recommended the inequality of properties to him and introduced his own wicked desire into Adam. As a result, Adam’s free will in that fiery root was infected, like a poison or venom that enters the body and begins to work.

29. From this arose a beginning will toward self-lust, and the "temperature" <term>the state of perfect balance and harmony</term> was at an end. The properties of the creation, which all lay balanced within Adam, awoke and rose up individually. Each property drew the free will into itself, demanding to be expressed.

30. Also, the *Spirit of the World* <term>original: "Spiritus Mundi"</term> in the external world drew the balance out of Adam—specifically that part of the external world within Adam—into itself, and began to rule and sway over him.

<margin><unclear>lawless spirit</unclear></margin>

32. And there he stood in the *trial* <term>original: "Proba"; a test or proof</term>, to see whether he would stand or not. His "science" or root originated from:
> I. The division or distribution of the magic fire in the world of power.
> II. The Father’s property.
> III. The will of the *Abyss* <term>the "Unground" or bottomless source of all being</term>. 
The root that grew out of these was free.

It stood in three principles in a state of balance; it could turn itself into any one of them, whichever way it willed.

33. This does *not* mean it was meant to be "free" just for the sake of the creature itself; for the commandment was given *not* to turn away from God into the longing or lust for both evil and good.

34. But the foundation of the creature—the fiery root of the soul—stood in the bottomless, abyssal will that preceded all beings or substances. It was a particular branch or portion of the Eternal Will.

<margin>Just as the Earth divides itself into various roots for many fruits, yet remains the same Earth.</margin>
35. This Eternal Will, in the "fiery word of separation" toward nature, had divided itself into several roots or dispositions. Thus, the soul was a part of this divisibility.

36. This divisibility—within the "Word of power" in nature (specifically in the first three and the seven forms of nature and their propagation)—was shaped into creatures such as angels and high eternal spirits. Within this, we must also understand the fiery soul that was breathed into man.

38. *That is*, the fiery soul will lose its light. Consequently, the divine power in the holy *essence* <term>original: "Ens"; the spiritual being or substance</term>—which comes from the "second principle" through the working of the Holy Spirit—will go out or be extinguished.

39. For the Spirit of God does *not* manifest itself in any animal-like property, much *less* in the kingdom of <term>Phantasy</term> <note>original: "Phantasy"; here meaning the world of mental illusions or the realm of fragmented imagination separated from God's light</note>.

40. And *therefore* God said to him that he should not leave the <term>Temperature</term> <note>original: "Temperature"; a state where all properties of nature exist in perfect, harmonious balance</note> and enter into the *lust* <note>original: "lust"; used here to mean a strong, misdirected desire or craving</note> or longing for the specific properties of nature. He was not to try and taste them in their fragmented desires; otherwise *mortality* would spring forth and show itself in him—namely, the dark world from the center of the <term>three first</term> <note>the first three "properties of nature" in Boehme's system: harshness, bitterness, and anguish</note>—and would devour the Kingdom of God within him.

## Question.

41. Then *Reason* asks: Why does God not *prevent* this with his holy power? Is he not *all-powerful*, and able to break the fiery <term>Science</term> <note>original: "Science"; from the Latin *scientia*, meaning innate knowledge, consciousness, or the "spark" of self-awareness</note> from which the will to longing or *lust* arose?

## Answer.

<margin>a That is, a Father of the Being of all Beings; and <term>Magia</term> <note>creative, magical power</note> is the Mother of the Being of all Beings: See the book "Of the Small Six Points," verse 65.</margin>

42. Listen, *Reason*. The fiery <term>Science</term> comes from the *Will of the Abyss* <note>the "Ungrund" or the bottomless, primordial void</note>. This Will is called the "Father of all things," in which God is generated; specifically, the Father generates the Son. This Will introduces itself into power through the Word—that is, through the *Expression* or "speaking forth" of creation.

43. Now know that a specific portion of the highest omnipotence of the "Substance of all substances" is understood to be in the *soul*; namely, in the <term>Science</term> or Root which has existed from eternity. This <term>Science</term>, through the moving of the all-powerful Word, compressed or compacted itself into an image within the first three properties of nature.

44. And so, that <term>Science</term>—arising out of the Will of the <term>Abyss</term>—is *its own property*; for nothing existed before it that could destroy or shatter it.

45. Indeed, the created being came after it; but the *Science* within the creature is from eternity. That consciousness, along with the creature (specifically in the first three properties), has introduced itself into a longing *lust* that is *against* or contrary to the <term>Temperature</term> in nature.

<margin>n By these words, "Being of all Beings," the one and only God is not the only thing understood or meant.</margin>

46. To that <term>Science</term>, or Root, the command was given to hold and keep the creature in the <term>Temperature</term>; that is, it was meant to keep the properties of nature in equal agreement and harmony. For the consciousness itself was the might and strength intended to do that, being a *spark* proceeding from the Omnipotence; and *besides* this, it possessed the kingdom of holy power in the light of God.

47. What more should God give to it—meaning the <term>Science</term> or Root of the soul—to prevail over it or compel it? He had given it *himself*; just as he had also done for King *Lucifer*.

48. This <term>Science</term> or Root broke itself off from God's power and light and desired to *be its own master*; it wanted to be its own self-working god according to the properties of *nature*, working in both evil and good, and manifesting this work within the *Kingdom* of the *Holy Power*.

<margin><insert>3 Kingdoms</insert></margin>

49. This was a will that stood in opposition to the divine power and property. For that *reason*, King *Lucifer*, and also *Adam*, were thrust out of the Kingdom of the Holy Power.

50. That is: *Lucifer* was cast into the kingdom of <term>Phantasy</term> and darkness, and *Adam* was cast into the inequality and discord of the creation—into the *animal-like* property in the <term>Spiritu Mundi</term> <note>original: "Spiritu Mundi"; the Spirit of the World or the astral/physical realm</note>. Consequently, all the creature's properties, both evil and good, instantly awakened in man.

51. For this reason, God has appointed the *Final Judgment* in the <term>Spiritu Mundi</term> <note>Spirit of the World</note> to separate evil from good, and to reap and carry all things home, each into its own principle.

52. # Of Man’s Fall, and of his Wife. Chap. 6.

Fire: that is, it shall be tested by the Fire of the Eternal Nature, according to which God calls himself a *consuming fire*.

53. For how else would God judge the creature if it only does that which it must *inevitably do*, as if it had no **Free Will**?
54. The last judgment is nothing else but a reaping and gathering in of the *harvest* by the Father of all beings—even of all that which he has generated through his Word.
55. Into whatever any thing has distributed and divided itself through Free Will, into that it will go; and in that eternal reservoir <note>original: "reservatory"</note>, according to the character of that same principle, it is *good*.
56. For God has generated nothing opposite or contrary to himself; in him *all is good*. However, this is true so long as everything remains within its own source <note>original: "Mother," a term the author uses to describe the origin or essential environment of a natural property</note>; so long as it runs on in a *foreign* <note>original: "strange"</note> source, it is an opposite or contrary will. We will offer you an analogy <note>original: "similitude"</note> of this.
57. Consider heat and cold, or fire and water: these come from *one* origin and divide and separate themselves from one another. Each of them goes on in its own will, according to its own source or *quality*.
58. Now, if they should enter into one another again, there is enmity, and one *kills* the other; and this creates its own self-will within that property.
59. While they lie together in a balanced state <note>original: "the temperature," meaning a state of tempered balance</note> they have great peace, but as soon as they go forth from one another, *each* of them wants to be its own self, to rule, and to be predominant over the other.
60. This is also where strife comes from in the *Spiritu Mundi* <note>original: "Spirit of the World"</note>, between the four elements, and between heat and cold. *Each* wants to rule: suddenly one prevails, and then the other; suddenly it rains, then it is suddenly cold, then suddenly hot; suddenly the air and wind go this way, and then another way. All this happens according to the power and *strength* of the seven properties of nature and the emergence of the first three of them, from which everything that *moves* or *stirs* was produced and created.

### Question.

61. **Then *Reason* <note>The author often personifies "Reason" as the limited, earthly logic of humans</note> says: *God rules and orders it so that strife occurs*.**

### Answer.

62. That is true, but Reason is blind and does not see by what means, with what, or *how* it happens. It does not understand the Word as it is divided into properties, which is what this rule, government, and *effect* consists of.
<margin>Nigel</margin>
63. For in the *Spiritu Mundi* <note>original: "Spirit of the World"</note>, many evil workings spring forth which appear contrary to God—such as when one creature hurts, worries, and skins <note>original: "flays"</note> another. Also, that wars, pestilence, thunder, and hail happen: all this lies in the *Spiritu Mundi* and arises from the "three first" <note>Referring to the first three properties of nature—often identified by the author as contraction, expansion, and rotation—which form the basis of material reality</note>, where the properties break or form themselves in their *opposite will*.
64. For God can give or provide *nothing* but that which is good, for he alone is the only Good and *never* changes into any evil at all; nor can he, for then he would *cease* to be a God.
65. But in the Word of his revelation or manifestation—where the forms, qualities, or dispositions arise (that is, where nature and creatures arise)—there exists the working or framing into *evil and good*.
66. That Word has compacted itself into a clockwork or machine included in time, and therein now stands the *making* or producing of evil and good, according to the divisibility or distribution of the power in the Word; just as the powers of Divine Manifestation divided themselves at the beginning into several *distinct* principles.

73. Some part of the soul's science gazed upon the creation of the formed Word in its distinction and variety, and knew that *within itself also* existed that same power for divisibility and distinction, and *so it lifted itself up into a longing after that divisibility and distinction*.

80. God introduces His sole and only Will into the forming and compaction of His Word for the purpose of variety—namely, for the manifestation or revelation of God—and *within that variety, the will remains free*.

81. For variety is Nature, and also the Creation, and within variety God wills both good and evil.

### Question.

83. Now Reason says: If God, in his poured-forth formed Word itself, is *All*—namely, evil and good, life and death—where then does the human strife stand? Why do people struggle about God’s will, seeing that God in his formed Word is all things and wills all things, whether it be evil or good, and every thing according to its own nature <note>original: "Property"</note> from which it originally proceeded?

### Answer.

84. Behold, in *this* lies the strife: that Reason, in its dimness of opinion and without the Divine Light, is *folly* in the sight of God. It does not know what God is. It always imagines and frames some strange thing, far away, when it speaks of God; it makes the one and only unchangeable God, in his Eternal Trinity, <margin>Or beginning.</margin> have starting wills and predestined purposes that have a beginning in time.

85. And it does not understand:
I. How all beginnings, decrees, and pre-determined purposes arise in the formed Word through Nature, where the Word solidifies <note>original: "compacts"</note> and forms itself into *Nature*.
II. That these beginnings all lie in the *formation* of the Word—that is, in the Creation and in the creature—namely in the "great mystery" of divisibility or distinction, in which the creatures have their origin.
III. That all evil proceeds from and out of Nature and the creature.
IV. And that the hardening in Nature and the creature exists in the <term>science</term> <note>original: "Science"; in Boehme's writing, this refers to a root-knowledge or the concentrated power of the will within a being.</note> or root of the creaturely *self*.
<margin>The science or root of the creature.</margin>
V. So that if it *turns itself* into the wrath of Nature, then it is seized and hardened within it.
VI. That it contains within itself the "speaking into wrath" and retains it.
VII. And all of that which is written—*He hardens their hearts so that they do not believe, and so are not saved*—is performed and effected in the formed Word of the eternal and temporary Nature.

<gloss><unclear>Wherein it is received</unclear></gloss>
<margin>Psalm 58:10.</margin>
86. For from that formed Word God speaks in the Psalms of David, saying, *You shall see and have great pleasure in it, when the wicked shall be repaid*; also, *you will rejoice when the wicked shall be overthrown and destroyed*. That is, when the wicked shall be swallowed up into the wrath—those who have been an adversary and a contradiction, and a continual infection and poisoning to the holy. When that venom is taken away from the holy soul, then it rejoices that it is delivered from necessity <note>original: "Necessity"; often referring to the compulsory or mechanical forces of nature and wrath that bind the soul.</note>.

87. And *therefore* the Word also exists in pain within Nature, so that joy may be manifested.

88. But the divisibility or distinction from the Word goes into the free will without *compulsion*, every property into its own.

89. For in the Holy Word all is good, but in the introduction of one's own self-will, it is evil.

90. But this is now done in Nature and the creature, and *not at all* in God. Otherwise, the Devil’s will would have to be in God’s Word, if God in his Word inevitably drove all things forward.

91. But the Devil’s will, as also Adam’s sinful will, existed in its own <term>science</term> or root within the creature, and not in God. Rather, in the center of Nature, its *own* science or root solidified <note>original: "compacted"</note> itself into a will of pride, wanting to be like—and even more than—the speaking Word of the Trinity of the Deity.

# Chap. 6. *Of Man's Fall, and of his Wife.*

92. *Humility* was despised and abandoned, and instead, the *Might* of the *Fire* <note>The "Might of the Fire" refers to a state of harsh, self-centered power or wrath, as opposed to divine love.</note> was taken up or seized.

93. Then the *Holy Spirit* departed from its nature, and it is now a *spirit* in its own self-will, trapped in *Fantasy*, as we see in *Adam*.

94. Now, when the *Science* or *Root* of the *soul* elevated itself—through the Devil's infusion, inspiration, or infection—the *Holy Spirit* departed into its own *Principle*. Thus, *Adam* became weak and feeble in the *Image* of *God*, specifically in the *Temperature* <note>original: "Temperature" refers to the perfect, harmonious balance of the soul’s internal properties.</note>; he could no longer magically bring forth his *likeness* out of himself in that same state.

95. His *Omnipotence*, which he possessed while in that *Temperature*, was *broken* within him, for the animal-like *property* of the *Creation* was stirring inside him.

<margin>Genesis 2:21</margin>
96. And now, says *Moses*, *God caused him to fall into a deep sleep, and he fell asleep*: *Here, he slept in and toward the Temperature of the Divine World.*

97. *Christ* must awaken him from *this sleep*, or else, as a creature, he can never see *God* again. For this *sleep* was nothing other than the *loss* of God's light in *Love*—specifically the *Love-Fire* that was extinguished in the *Ens* <note>original: "Ens" refers to the essential substance or "being" of a thing.</note>, or *essence*, of the heavenly world’s substance. He was *half dead*.

98. The *length of time* that *Adam* stood in the right, true *Image* of *God* is presented to you in the *figures* of *Moses* and *Christ*, as is the *duration* of the *sleep*. If you have insight, then view *Moses* through *Christ’s figure*, and *Christ* through *Adam’s figure* when *Adam* was in his *innocence*.

99. *Moses was on the mountain for forty days when Israel was tested and proven; Israel was in the wilderness for forty years; and Christ stood for forty days in Adam’s trial during the temptation in the wilderness. He also spent forty days after his resurrection in the right, true, and perfect trial in which Adam should have lived in his innocence to establish himself in the Magic Birth <note>original: "Magic Birth" refers to a spiritual, supernatural way of generating life.</note>.*

100. But since that could not be—which was indeed well known to *God*—*Adam* fell into a *sleep*. Therefore, *Christ* had to rest in *Adam’s sleep for forty hours* and awaken *Adam* within himself back into the Kingdom of *God*. Consider this, and you will learn to understand the whole foundation of the *process* of *Christ*.

101. Now, put *Christ* in *Adam’s place*, and you shall find the *entire foundation* of the *Old* and *New Testament*. See *Adam* in the formed *Word* of the *Creation*, as the *image* of the outward and inward *Eternal Nature* of all three *principles*.

102. And see *Christ* in the *Eternal Speaking Word*, according to the true divine *nature* in which no *evil* can exist; he is solely and purely the *Love-Birth* of the divine manifestation, according to the *Kingdom of Glory*.

103. Bring *Christ* into *Adam*, so that *Christ* may regenerate *Adam* within himself and tincture <note>original: "tincture" means to spiritually infuse or transform the quality of something.</note> him with *love*, so that he may awake from that *deep sleep*. Then you have the whole *process* or *scene* of *Adam* and *Christ*.

104. For *Adam* is the spoken, formed, creaturely *word*, and *Christ* is the *Holy, Eternal, Speaking Word*. In this way, you will bring *time* into *eternity* and see more than you can learn from all the *books* of *men*.

105. For when *Eve* was made out of *Adam* during *Adam’s sleep*, that was done by the *Fiat* <note>Latin: "let it be done," referring to God's creative command.</note> in the *Spiritu Mundi* <note>Latin: "Spirit of the World."</note>—the *creative word* acting in the *spirit* of the *world*. And then they became *creatures* of the outward *world*, living in the outward *natural life* and in *mortality*—that is, in an *animal-like life*, shaped with an *animal-like form*. They also became a *carcass* or *sack of worms*, to be filled with earthly *food*.

106. For after the *woman* came out of *Adam*, the *Image* of *God* in the *Temperature* was immediately broken and *ruined*, and then the *Paradise* within them could not remain.

<margin>Romans 14:17</margin>
107. For *the Kingdom of God does not consist of eating and drinking*, say the *Scriptures*, *but of peace and joy in the Holy Spirit.*

111. But then **Reason** asks: Why did God let that **tree** grow?

### Answer.

112. Listen, **Reason**: This world’s *proba* <note>original: "Proba"; a test or trial</note> or trial is *better* than a trial in the center of the fire after the manner of eternity—which is how *Lucifer* was proved and tested.

114. For the science or root of the soul possesses a **divine property**, relative to God's omnipotence. Herein lies the foundation of all hidden secrets; the Fall remains, now and always, the result of the *self-will* of man and the **deceit** and **treachery** of the Devil.

# The Seventh Chapter.

## Of the Bestial Manifestation in Man.

### How *Adam* and *Eve*’s Eyes were opened; and how that is fundamentally to be understood, in its foundation.

1. <image-desc>Illuminated capital W inside a square decorative border of repeating floral and star motifs.</image-desc> When we correctly consider the very distinct <note>original: "express"</note> Image in its true magical foundation <term>Ground: A common term in mystical writing referring to the underlying reality or essence of a thing.</term>, we see how it forms a reflected image in the Spirit of the World <note>original: *Spiritu Mundi*</note>, according to all things. Just as we see a reflection in a looking-glass or a shadow in water, we shall quickly approach the reason and cause why every being arises out of only one thing. We see how all creatures lie within the Spirit of the World—that is, in the spoken or expressed Word of God.
2. Therefore, we can say with good reason that all creatures existed even within *Adam*. This does not mean they physically came out of *Adam* to be created, but they existed in the eternal knowledge <note>original: "Science"</note> of the soul. In this knowledge, the Word of God forms and images itself into a natural and creaturely foundation, in which all properties are understood to exist.
<margin>Genesis 1:28.</margin>
3. As *Moses* testifies, *man was meant to rule over all creatures*; but now, since the Fall, they all rule over him.
4. For when the soul remained in a state of balance <term>Temperature: A state of perfect balance or harmony among the various qualities of the soul.</term>, then the will-spirit of the soul pressed through all creatures and met no resistance. No creature could lay hold of or grasp it, just as no creature can grasp the power and beams of the sun by its own will but must allow them to pass through; so it was also with the spirit of man’s will.
5. But once he was captured by the poison or venom of the serpent, within the Devil’s will or desire, he became an enemy to all creatures and lost this power and might.
6. Thus the creatures also triumphed and gained <insert>power</insert> over him, elevating themselves within him. This is now plain to see: many people possess the nature <note>original: "Property"</note> of a subtle serpent—full of wicked, sly, and cunning schemes, and venomous malice. Others have the nature of a toad, a dog, a cat, a basilisk <note>A mythical reptile, often called a king of serpents, said to kill with a glance.</note> or cockatrice, a lion, bear, wolf, and so on, through all the characteristics of beasts, worms, and crawling things.
7. Such people still bear the outward shape of the *first* created image, but an *evil beast occupies their inner nature*.
8. The same applies to tame, good animals; many people possess the nature of a kind or good beast.

### Chapter 7: Of the Bestial Manifestation in Man

9. Hardly any human born from the seed of Adam lacks a *bestial property* in their earthly body; many have evil traits, and many have good.

10. This is understood as a consequence of the *Fall*: all the properties in the *Spirit of the World* <note>original: "Spiritu Mundi"</note> have manifested themselves in humanity. Every fiery principle <note>original: "Science," here meaning an active force or essential knowledge</note> regarding heat and cold, as well as all other specific qualities and the property of *nature as a whole*, was revealed in him, according to both Evil and Good.

11. For as soon as they ate the earthly fruit into the body, their inner balance <note>original: "Temperature," meaning the perfect harmony of elements</note> broke apart and drifted away from the harmony of its properties. The *body* then manifested according to all the properties found in the *Spirit of the World*.

12. Then heat and cold seized them and pressed into them. *All* the properties of nature, which form the foundation of nature itself, forced a contrary and opposing will into them. From this came *sickness* and the *death* caused by human frailty and decay.

<margin>*</margin> 13. And because of this bite <note>referring to the eating of the forbidden fruit</note>, *he died to the Kingdom of God* and woke up to the Kingdom of Nature. He was taken from a state of being *incapable of suffering* <note>original: "Impassibility"</note> and placed into a state of *vulnerability* <note>original: "Passibility"</note>. Regarding his outward body, he became a beast among all beasts—the bestial or *animal image* of God, in which the Word of God had revealed itself in a bestial form.

14. Thus, in his outward body, man became a master, lord, and prince over all beasts, and yet he himself was *but* a beast—though of a more noble essence than other animals—and he still possessed a bestial property and *condition*.

15. At that very hour, a gate to the dark world in God's anger was *opened in man—namely, Hell*, or the jaws and throat of the Devil. The Kingdom of *Fantasy* <note>original: "Phantasy," referring to the realm of illusion or distorted imagination</note> was also revealed in him. The "angry God" (so-called because of the Kingdom of Darkness) was revealed in him and took hold of him, affecting the soul's essence *within the created being*.

16. The foundation of the soul's essence <note>original: "Science"</note> cannot be destroyed. Only the *created being*—formed from the "three firsts" (the eternal nature) and the temporal nature in the *Spirit of the World*—is what can be broken.

17. The temporal nature was placed in the earthly property, and the eternal nature was placed in the wrath of the dark world, becoming a *neighbor* to the Devil.

<margin>Matthew 27:45, 51, etc.</margin> 18. When these *shackles* were broken for both natures through the death of Christ, *the earth trembled* and the *sun lost its shining light*. This signified that when the eternal light was to be generated again, the temporal light had to cease once more.

19. But to rightly consider and understand *what part of man* died in the Fall, we must not only look at temporal death (where man dies, rots, and decays). That is only the *bestial* death, not the eternal death.

20. *Neither* must we be so blind as to say that the soul is dead within its created form; no, that could not be.

21. That which is eternal is incapable of death. However, the express image of God that had formed and modeled itself in the soul—the Divine *Substance* <note>original: "Ens"</note>—disappeared, vanished, or was *extinguished* when the wrath of fire was awakened.

22. In God, there is no dying, only a *separation* of principles. This should be understood in the same way we see the night swallow the day, and the day swallow the night; one is as it *were* dead within the other because it cannot show itself.

23. Furthermore, you may understand this through a comparison: if the *sun* were extinguished, then the *Spirit of the World* <note>original: "Spiritus Mundi"</note> would be an empty, crude enmity, and there would be *perpetual night*. Then the four elements could not express themselves or operate in their current qualities and properties; no fruit would grow, and no creature living within the four elements would survive.

He clarifies that while the body and temporal nature suffer decay, the soul remains eternal, though its divine essence was obscured by the awakening of "wrath."</summary>

24. In this very manner also Adam and Eve died to the Kingdom of the Power and Virtue of the *Divine Sun*—namely, of the *Divine Will* and *Essence* or *Substance*. The fierce, wrathful nature awakened from within in the soul, and also from without, externally, in the bestial property.

<margin>f One copy has it: in a *Free Will*.</margin>
25. The knowledge <note>original: "Science"; here referring to the essential consciousness or capacity for knowing</note> of the soul from the abyssal <note>bottomless or originating from the "Abyss," a term Boehme uses for the groundless source of all being</note> Will, wherein God begets, generates, or works, is not dead; nothing can break or destroy that, and it remains eternally a *free will*.

26. But its form as a creature—namely, the soul, which was formed into an *Image* by the Spirit of God—that same *Image* lost the *Holy Essence* <note>original: "Ens"</note> from the *Eternal Nature* wherein *God's Light and Love-Fire* burned.

<margin>g Or hidden.</margin>
27. It is not that the same *Essence* <note>original: "Ens"</note> or *Being* has become nothing; indeed, it became nothing to the creaturely soul (meaning it became *imperceptible*), but the holy power—namely, the *Spirit of God*, which was the working life within it—hid itself.

28. This did not happen by God's own determined, predestinated purpose; rather, the *Eternal Knowledge* <note>original: "Science"</note>—the abyssal will of the foolish creature—departed from the *Love-Will* and went out into its own stinging, prickly property and the disposition of foolish nature.

29. God did not withdraw himself from the soul, but the *knowledge of the Free Will* withdrew itself from God.

30. Just as the Sun does not withdraw itself from the *Thistle*, but the *Thistle* withdraws its prickly nature <note>original: "Science"</note> from the Sun and introduces itself into a prickly substance; and the more the Sun shines upon it, the more prickly and stronger is its *consciousness of opposition and contrary will*. So also it is to be understood concerning the soul.

<margin>h *John 1:5.*</margin>
31. God dwells through and through all things, also thoroughly in the Darkness, and through and through in the Devil; but the *Darkness* does not comprehend him, and so also the Devil and the wicked soul do not comprehend God.

## Question.

->32. If you ask, "Why is that?"<-

## Answer.

I answer: Because the creaturely will toward true resigned humility, lowliness, and submission under obedience to God is *dead*, and there is only a mere thistly and thorny will in the life of the creature.

33. Thus, the thorny will holds the noble knowledge <note>original: "Science"</note> of the abyssal Eternal Will captive, or covered within itself. They are within one another like day and night; the creaturely soul had become *Night*.

34. In the beginning, the Spirit of the World <note>original: *Spiritus Mundi*</note> stood in a state of balance <note>original: "Temperature"</note> within the body, and yet it existed in both Evil and Good, as all temporary things do.

35. But the Devil’s *Thistle-Seed* had entered into it, in which temporal death lay. At that point, it was understood that man was nothing else but a *beast* above all *beasts*.

36. The equilibrium, balance, or harmony of the formed, expressed Word <note>original: "out-spoken Word"</note> stood in *enmity* and *opposite will*. The angelic *Image* was quite destroyed, both in the mind and in the thoughts or senses.

<margin>i *John 3:3, 5.*</margin>
37. We see plainly at this day that the senses or thoughts continually shape themselves into a bestial will and a desire for *self-love*. They very scarcely and hardly ever reach the point of loving God and equality or equity; instead, they always lift themselves up on high and want to have everything in their sole possession. They would gladly be the fairest and most beautiful child in the house or family. From this, pride, covetousness, envy, and malice exist. All of this is from the *Essence* <note>original: "Ens"</note> or *Being* of the *Serpent* and of the property or disposition introduced by the Devil, *which cannot inherit the Kingdom of God*.

It describes how the human soul lost its divine "Essence" and became dominated by the "Spirit of the World" and the "Thistle-Seed" of the Devil.</summary>
