# Chap. 7. Of the Bestial Manifestation in Man.

38. Now to remedy this, the living Eternal Word of the most high Love Property <term>Property: a specific quality, nature, or disposition</term> came by mere Grace and spoke itself again into the faded *Ens* <term>Ens: a Latin term for "being" or "essence"; here referring to the spiritual substance of the soul</term> of the heavenly world's substance, to create an active, working, and effective life.

39. And just as the Devil's word had spoken itself into the soul, so the Word of God's love came and spoke itself again into the faded *Ens*.

40. This signifies that there is a target, mark, or boundary of an eternal gracious covenant, wherein God's love, in the name JESUS, would destroy the works of the devil. It would reintroduce a living, holy *Ens* in the name JESUS into this speaking-in, or spoken-in Word again; this was accomplished in Christ's Incarnation <term>Incarnation: the embodiment of God in human flesh</term>.

<margin>* 1 Peter 1:20.</margin>
41. Here we must understand the foresight, provision, or inspection by which the Spirit of God—*k before the foundation of the world*—saw this Fall in the property and disposition of the fire and the wrath of nature. He foresaw or provided the holy name JESUS, with the highest essence of love within it, to be a new *Regenerator* <gloss>Redeemer</gloss>.

<margin>l express Hebrews 1:3.</margin>
42. For the one and only root of the Divine *Ens* from Divine Love—namely, the heavenly world's substance—faded, vanished, or disappeared in *Adam*. This was the true *l express* <note>original: "express," meaning a direct and exact representation</note> reflected image of God, according to His divine, holy property.

43. And in that one image, which disappeared in *Adam* regarding its connection to God, God pre-inspected or foresaw the scope, time, mark, or limit of His *eternal holy Will* in *Christ*.

<margin>m Genesis 3:15.</margin>
44. God's holy Word spoke into that very place when the poor creaturely soul became blind to God, saying: *m The seed of the woman shall tread upon, crush, or break the serpent's head.*

45. And in that spoken-in or inspired voice, the poor soul obtained breath and life again.

46. That same spoken-in voice was in human life as a figure of the true *express* reflected *image*. In this limit or time of God's covenant (which He had foreseen in the Divine *Ens* before the foundation of the world), it was implanted from then on, from person to person, as a covenant of grace.

47. For the "inspaking" <note>original: "inspaking" or "infection"; a literal translation of the German *Einsprache*, referring to an internal speaking or influence</note> or infection of the devil, from which an evil or malignant will arose, was finally completed in *Adam*. This happened when he was both man and woman and yet *neither* of them separately, but one entire image of God; it then pressed on from *Adam* into *Eve*, who began the sin.

48. Therefore, the "inspaking" or inspiration of God also came and pressed into *Eve*, as the mother of all humanity. It set itself against the source of sin that had begun through *Eve* and moved into *Adam*.

49. For in *Eve* lay the *tincture* <term>Tincture: in Boehme's thought, a spiritual essence or life-force that colors and vitalizes substance</term> of the *light* and of the spiritual water. In that same place, the holy tincture incorporated itself into the Word in the name JESUS, as a pledge that it would break the bestial *matrix* <term>Matrix: a womb or generative environment</term> and change it into a holy matrix.

50. This was not to be done through *Adam's* fiery tincture, but through that part of the Adamical light's tincture where *love* burned. This was divided into the woman—that is, into the *genetrix* <term>Genetrix: a female parent or mother</term> of all people.

51. Into this, God's voice promised to introduce again a *living holy Ens* from heaven, and to generate anew in divine power the faded, disappeared image of God that stood within it.

<margin>n John 3:13.</margin>
52. For Christ said, *John 3:13, n He was come from heaven*, by which one should understand His substance. The Word does not need to "come" in a physical sense, for it is already there; it only needs to move and stir itself.

53. Now, regarding our perished, foolish property, all people lay in the seed of *Adam*. On the other hand, all people lay in the *Matrice Veneris* <note>original: "Matrix of Venus," referring to the generative feminine principle</note>, in the matrix of Venus—that is, in the feminine or woman’s property in *Eve*.

It emphasizes that this redemption was prepared before the foundation of the world and specifically targeted the feminine "tincture" in Eve to reverse the Fall.</summary>

54. Into *Eve*—that is, into the *Matrix* <term>womb or creative source</term> of Love—God placed his Covenant. He did this within the substance of the heavenly world that had faded or disappeared in both *Eve* and *Adam*. God brought *his Word* into that part which belongs to the Kingdom of God, so that the "Seed of the Woman" (meaning the heavenly seed which the Word would introduce again) would tread upon and crush the head of the serpent’s power and the Devil's will. In this way, God and Man would again be one person, destroying the Devil's work and deception that he had attempted to carry out in both soul and body.

55. *Understand* it correctly in this way: This work was to be done by the first created human in *Adam*—specifically that part from the heavenly world's substance—and by the part that was to be introduced through God’s Word. These would become one and the same substance with human nature. *That is what* should do this; namely, the God-Man and the Man-God *should* perform it.

56. This was not a totally foreign or strange Christ, but that very same *Word* which had originally made Man out of itself as an image of God. Therefore, this work *should* be done by: 1. The Word that makes, 2. The Word that is made in power, and 3. The Holy Spirit.

57. The heavenly *Ens* <term>essence or being</term> within the Word—which is the temple of the Holy Spirit—was meant to take on two things within the "Woman’s Seed": 1. a foolish seed <note>Boehme often uses "foolish" to describe the fallen, earthly nature of man that lacks divine wisdom</note>, and 2. a physical seed from *Adam's* substance, derived from the *Limus* <note>original: "Limus"; Latin for mud or slime, referring to the "dust of the ground" from which Adam was created</note> of the earth.

58. In the same way that God has taken on the world yet still dwells in Heaven in his holy *Ens*, the Word also took the faded or vanished holy *Ens* and placed it upon his living *Ens*. He made that faded essence living again through his power, while the foolish and physical nature from both the inner and outer world remained attached to that same essence.

59. Just as nature is attached to God, and he manifests himself through it, the holy Word (together with the holy *Ens*) chose to manifest itself through our foolish and physical nature. It would tincture <term>transform or spiritually "color"</term> the soul again with the highest *Tincture*, and destroy the Devil’s fortress of prey that had been built within the "Wrath of eternal nature." All of this was fulfilled in the *Process* <note>original: "Process"; the entire sequence of Christ’s life, suffering, death, and resurrection</note> of Christ.

### Question.

60. Now tell me, *Reason*, where in this does God's predestined purpose and will to "harden" humanity exist? Where is the predestined purpose by which he supposedly ordained one part of humanity to damnation and the other to eternal life?

<margin>INTERNAL</margin>
61. For *Sin* began in *Eve*, and *Grace* also began in *Eve*. Before she ever conceived a child, all of humanity lay in *Eve* equally in death, and also equally within the one Covenant of Grace in life.

<margin>Romans 5:17, 18.</margin>
62. As the Apostle says: *As sin came from one and spread to all, so also grace came from one and spread or entered into all.*

63. For the Covenant did not apply only to a specific part—as if it were only for one piece of *Eve*—but it applied to the whole of *Eve*, except for the Devil’s work which he had thrust into her. Christ was meant to break all of that work.

64. No soul should or *could* be produced out of the essence introduced by the Devil, because the Word of God stood *interposed* in the way with the Covenant.

65. And so the Covenant pressed through *Eve’s* soul into *Adam*—that is, from the *Tincture* of Light into *Adam’s* fiery *Tincture*.

66. For in the Word, *Adam* and *Eve* were one entire human being; therefore, Grace also pressed upon that one entire human being, *Adam* and *Eve*.

<summary>Boehme argues that God's Covenant of Grace was given to all of humanity through Adam and Eve, rejecting the idea of double predestination. He explains how the "God-Man" (Christ) restores the faded heavenly essence in humans by manifesting through their fallen nature.</summary>

### Question.

67. Where is the divine, eternal, predestined purpose now? Human "Reason" claims she will demonstrate this purpose using the Scripture, yet she does not actually understand it.
68. For the words of the Scripture are true, but discernment <note>original: "Understanding"</note> is required to distinguish them. It is not reached by outward assumptions or personal fantasies, through which men chatter about a foreign, strange God who lives somewhere above, in a heaven far away.
69. But we will show "Reason" in a brotherly spirit how the Scripture is to be understood where it speaks of the predestined purpose and God's choice <note>original: "Election"</note>. We will give her the true understanding and meaning of what "election" is, and what the predestined purpose entails.
70. In doing so, we do not intend to look down on <note>original: "contemn"</note> anyone for their current understanding. Rather, for the sake of better information and the uniting of Christian understanding, we will explain and clear up the Holy Scripture—which is the very reason why *this book is written*.
71. To understand this, we will compare the first and second "Principles." First, the *Kingdom of Nature*—where God’s anger and the hardening of hearts are understood—which we will compare with the *Divine Manifestation*. Second, we will look at the *Kingdom of Grace*—the true divine essence <note>original: "Substance"</note>—setting them against one another to see how the foundation of spiritual hardening exists.
72. By doing this, we will test, prove, and examine the sayings and texts of Scripture that seem to contradict one another. This is so everyone may see the foundation of their own opinions and meanings. We will not bind or tie ourselves to any single opinion just to please men, but will lay down the groundwork in *love*, for the brotherly uniting and reconciling of the opinions of *all parties*.

### Answer.

<margin>Psalm 14:1, 3.</margin>
73. When Adam and Eve fell, they became blind to the Kingdom of God and were *as if they were dead*. <gloss>p</gloss> *There was no ability or possibility in them to do anything that was good*; understand this as referring to the foolish and physical creature.

<margin>See the *Clavis* <note>Latin: "Key"</note>, Verse 210, the word "Science," or "Root."</margin>
74. But there is a <gloss>q</gloss> "science" <note>In this context, "science" (from the Latin *scientia*) refers to a root of knowledge, a creative power, or a fundamental spiritual dynamic.</note> or root of the Abyss <note>The "Abyss" refers to the bottomless, unmanifested source of all existence.</note> from the Father’s property, in which a soul was formed in the fiery Word. Because that soul was unbound and unlimited, it was neither evil nor good; it is the *one only Will*.
75. In this "one only Will," God the *Father* generates his Son. Yet, beyond or outside of this process of generation <note>original: "Geniture"</note>—that is, the Divine Power—He is not called Father, nor is He called God. Instead, He is called the eternal, unfathomable, abyssal *Will* toward "something." In this Will, we understand the birth of the Holy Trinity, as well as the origin of Nature and the *beginning* of all things or essences.
76. That very Will is the *eternal beginning* of Divine Wisdom—the visionary power that sees into the Abyss—and is also the beginning of the "Word," which is the outward expression of the Fire and the Light.
77. However, this "speaking" is not performed within the Will of the Abyss itself, but in the "compaction" or framing of the "science" or root. This is where that Will compresses or frames itself into the "City of God"—the Trinity of the generation—and there the Word of Power (the Son) speaks itself into a diversity of "sciences" or roots.
78. And in that diversity of the expressed roots and eternal workings, the Image of God—which is Man—was seen or foreseen from eternity within the Divine Power and Wisdom. This existed in a "magical" <note>The author uses "magical" to describe a spiritual, non-material, or supernatural state of being.</note> form or manner, without being a physical creature.

<summary>This page argues that human reason cannot understand God's "election" or predestined purpose without comparing the "Kingdom of Nature" and the "Kingdom of Grace." Boehme describes the soul's origin in an eternal, "abyssal" Will that precedes the manifestation of the Trinity and the creation of Man's spiritual image.</summary>

-># Of the Bestial Manifestation in Man. Chapter 7.<-

79. And in this seen or foreseen *image*, the Spirit of God in the highest love—which is the name JESUS—has loved himself; for it was a *figure* of his likeness in terms of power and birth.

80. But since God's love would not have been manifested without the eternal nature—that is, the love-fire would not have been manifested without the anger-fire—the root of the <term>science</term><note>original: "science"; from the Latin *scientia*, here meaning the active principle of will, consciousness, or the "knowing" power of the soul.</note> in its natural ground was the anger-fire. The anger-fire was the manifestation of the love-fire, in the same way that light comes from fire. Here we understand the foundation and basis in this way:

81. When the light in the creaturely, eternal, natural soul vanished or went out, then the creaturely soul was only a source or fountain of God's anger—namely, a fiery nature.

<margin>Ephesians 1:4</margin>
82. But now God's love—namely, the name JESUS, which is the ONE or the Unity, as a person may conceive it—had incorporated itself into the eternal seen or foreseen image in the "science" of the outspeaking (or expression). Understand this as the *human eternal image* in which the creaturely soul was created; and in this incorporation or grafting, *man was foreseen in Christ before the foundation of the world.*

83. *But* when the creaturely natural soul fell and lost the light, then the Word of Power, which had formed the soul in the fiery "science," spoke itself into the will of the abyss toward the creature.

<margin>John 1:1, 9</margin>
84. *From eternity*, the name JESUS stood in an immovable love within man—namely, in the likeness of God. For if it had been movable, then the image would have had a life of its own. But now, *the true life was only in the Word of Power* (John 1).

85. *But* when the soul lost the light, then the Word spoke the name JESUS, in its active movement, into the faded, disappeared <term>Ens</term><note>Ens: An ontological term meaning "being" or "essence"; the spiritual substance of a thing.</note> of the heavenly world's substance.

86. Before his fall, *Adam* had the divine light from JEHOVAH—that is, from the one and only God in whom the high name JESUS stood *hidden*.

87. It was not hidden within God, but within the creature; understand that it stood hidden in the "science" (the consciousness) of the creature.

88. But in this state of necessity, when the soul fell, *God manifested the riches of his glory* and holiness in the abyssal will of the soul—that is, in the eternal seen or foreseen image. He incorporated himself through the living voice of the Word out of the love-fire into the eternal image, as a *pledge* to the soul, which the soul should then strive to enter and penetrate.

<margin>Note.</margin>
89. And although the soul could not force its way in (for it was as if dead toward God), yet the divine breath pressed into the soul and *warned it to stand still* and refrain from acting or working evil, so that its voice might begin to work in the soul again. This is what God’s voice "inspoke" <note>original: "inspake"; the internal speaking of God's Word into the human heart.</note> to *Eve* regarding the *seed* of the woman.

90. For the true woman from the heavenly world's substance, when she was still within *Adam* (understood according to the light's <term>tincture</term><note>Tincture: In this context, a spiritual essence or quality that permeates and transforms nature.</note>), was the Virgin *Sophia*—namely, the eternal virginity or love of the man (or husband), which was manifested in JEHOVAH within *Adam*.

<margin>Galatians 4:4</margin>
91. She was now manifested in the voice of the "inspeaking" in the name JESUS, which had revealed itself out of JEHOVAH by *this covenant*: that the name JESUS would, *in the fullness of time*, introduce the holy substance of *Sophia* (namely, the heavenly holy substance of love, which surrounds and encompasses the love—or as one might say, the substance in which the fiery love exists) and bring it into the faded, disappeared substance from JEHOVAH.

<margin>Genesis 7:17 and 3:3</margin>
92. And when I say the substance from JEHOVAH faded and vanished in the Fall, it is true; it is even *the death in which Adam and Eve died*. For they lost the right fire, and the hot and cold fire of enmity or hostility awakened within them. *Sophia* is not manifested in that fire, for that is not the divine fire-life, but the natural one.

<header>Chap. 7. Of the Bestial Manifestation in Man.</header>

# Of the Bestial Manifestation in Man.

93. And in this natural fire-life of the soul, there is now the distinction, or *diversity*, between God's love and anger: the natural fire-life, without the Light, is God's anger, which only desires its own kind. This *hardens* the soul and brings it into a foreign or strange will of its own, which is opposite to the quality of the love-fire.

94. And yet, it is not any foreign or strange will from an "anger-fire" that flies into the natural soul from the outside; rather, it is the soul's own proper *fire*, the very substance of which the soul is made.

95. The wrath of self-nature hardens itself by embracing the abomination that has arisen in the first three forms of nature—namely, in the quality of the *dark world*—which is manifested in evil, false, or wicked desire. This also arises from outward occurrences or occasions, which draw into themselves the outward lust or longing from the fiery desire.

96. Just as *Adam* and *Eve* hardened and poisoned themselves with the serpent's longing (or lust) that was introduced to them, that same introduced poison then also began to *hunger* after qualities like itself. Thus, one abomination generated another.

<margin>Romans 7:17, 18.</margin>
97. As the Apostle Paul says concerning it: it was not he in the Spirit of Christ who willed and committed sin, *but it was sin in the flesh that did it.* That is, sin which is in nature—namely, the manifested wrath of the eternal and temporal nature. Whatever the bestial lust introduces into the flesh, *this is what does it.*

98. But now understand me correctly: the most inward ground in man is <term>Christ</term> <note>original: *CHRISTUS*</note>. This is not according to the human nature of man, but according to the *divine quality* in the heavenly substance, which he has born or generated anew.

99. And the other, or second ground of nature, is the *soul*. Understand this as the eternal nature in which Christ manifested himself and which he assumed.

100. And the third ground is the *created man made from the <term>limus</term> of the earth* <note>original: *limus*; Latin for slime or mud, referring to the "dust of the ground" in Genesis 2:7</note>, along with the stars and elements.

101. 1. In the first ground, which is Christ, is the working, active life in *divine love*. 2. In the second ground is the natural fire-life of the creaturely soul, in which God calls himself a zealous or jealous God. 3. In the third ground lies the creation of all properties, which in *Adam* existed in <term>temperature</term> <note>original: "temperature"; here meaning a state of perfect balance or harmony between opposing qualities</note>, but in the Fall, these properties separated *from one another*.

<margin>John 17:6.</margin>
102. In the first ground is God, <term>Jehovah</term> <note>original: *JEHOVA*</note>, who has given the people (who were his in the beginning) to the name and manifested power of Jesus. As Christ says: *Father, the men were yours and you have given them to me, and I give them eternal life.*

103. First, they stood in Jehovah's quality—in the Father's property—and *now* they stand in the Son's quality, according to the inward ground of the kingdom of heaven.

<margin>Deuteronomy 5:12; Hebrews 4:10; Isaiah 58:13.</margin>
104. For the inward ground is the inward heaven; it is the *Sabbath*—namely, *Christ*—whom we should *sanctify*. That is, we should *rest from our own willing and working* so that the Sabbath, *Christ in us*, may work.

<margin>Matthew 28:18.</margin>
105. The second ground now is the kingdom of eternal nature, according to the Father's quality, in which *God's anger* and the dark world are understood. God has appointed his Son to be a *judge* over this. For Christ said: *All power in heaven and earth is given to me by my Father.* These words also include the judgment over all things.

<margin>Matthew 11:28.</margin>
106. This Jesus Christ now says: *Come to me, all you who are weary and heavy laden, and I will refresh you.*

### Question.

107. Now the question is: why are not *all* people weary <note>That is, weary of their worldly, "beastly" nature.</note> and why do they not come to the refreshment, namely, to the *New Birth*?

### Answer.

<margin>John 6:44</margin>
Christ says: *No one comes to me, except my heavenly Father draws him.*

### Question.

108. *Whom* then does he draw to Christ?

### Answer.

<margin>John 1:13</margin>
The Scripture answers: even *those who are born, not of flesh and blood, nor of the will of man, but of God.*

### Question.

109. Then, who are *these*?

### Answer.

These are *they* who are born of grace; these he chooses or elects to himself.

### Question.

110. And what is grace?

### Answer.

It is the inward ground <term>ground: the deepest essence or foundation of the human soul</term>, namely, Christ <note>original: "CHRISTUS"</note>, who in grace gave himself again into the *faded, vanished, inward ground.*

<margin>Ephesians 5:30</margin>
<margin>2 Corinthians 6:16</margin>
<margin>Romans 11:17</margin>
111. Now those who are newborn out of that inward ground, out of *Wisdom* <note>original: "SOPHIA". In this mystical context, Sophia represents Divine Wisdom or the "heavenly virginity"—the pure, spiritual image of humanity that was lost in the Fall of Adam and is restored through Christ.</note>, namely, out of the heavenly virginity—those are members of the *body of Christ*, and the *temple of God*. *These are elected as children; the rest, or the others, are hardened*, as the Scripture says throughout.

### Question.

112. But how does it happen that they are hardened?

### Answer.

<margin>2 Corinthians 5:14</margin>
They are *all dead in Adam*, and cannot, without the grace in Christ, have or attain the divine life.

### Question.

113. But can the creaturely <note>That is, the human soul in its created, natural state, separate from the divine.</note> soul, by its *own* ability and will within itself, receive nothing of this grace?

### Answer.

<margin>Romans 9:16</margin>
No, it cannot: for *it lies not in any man's own willing, working, or running*, but in God's mercy or compassion, which is only in Christ—in grace.

### Question.

114. Now to ask further: *how* then does mercy and compassion come *into* the soul, so that it comes under election?

## *Question.*

118. Now it may be asked: *How then does this innate birth as a child of God happen, since all are dead in Adam?* Surely, therefore, some must be born as children to God out of a predestined purpose and be elected, while others remain hardened in God's predestined purpose. How can the child help it if God does not want them? Here now lies the "nut that is so hard to crack," which causes so much conflict and debate.

## *Answer.*

<margin>
o Matthew 7:18.
p Genesis 2:9. Revelation 2:7.
</margin>
119. Christ said, <margin>o</margin> *A corrupt tree cannot bear good fruit, and a good tree cannot bear bad fruit.* Now, if we wish to search and understand this foundation <note>original: "Ground"</note>, then we must search into <margin>p</margin> the *Tree of Life*, which contains both *Evil* and *Good*. We must see: 1. What fruit it bears; and 2. From what essence <note>original: "Essence"</note> *every* fruit grows. In this way, we reach the true goal, aim, and meaning, as we see how every power draws or attracts into an *Ens* <note>Ens: a Latin term for "being" or "essence," used here to describe a spiritual substance</note> and a will.

120. The Scripture says that God has *included all things in time, limit, measure, and weight*, according to how they should happen. But we cannot say that man was included in *Time* at the beginning, for in *Paradise* he was included in *Eternity*.

121. God had created him in His image; but when he fell, that inclusion in *Time* captured him, where all things are governed by limit, measure, and weight. And that clockwork, or machine, is the "outspoken" <note>Boehme uses "outspoken" to mean the expressed or manifested Word of God in the physical world</note> or expressed, formed Word of God, according to both Love and Anger, in which the whole creation exists—including man, according to nature and creaturely existence.

<margin>q Matthew 28:18.</margin>
122. Now the name JESUS has manifested itself in this outspoken Word, in the Father's property, in that <margin>q</margin> *all power in heaven and earth is given to him.* Therefore all is His, both the evil and the good.

123. Not as something possessed or inherent to its own self-centered nature, but to the good as a *Savior*, and to the evil as a *Judge*.

<margin>r Matthew 25:32, etc.</margin>
124. And therefore all things are set against one another: love against anger, and anger against love, so that the one may be revealed in the other on <margin>r</margin> *the Day of the Judge's decision or separation, when He shall sever all things.*

125. For if He were not Lord over evil, He could not be a judge of the devil and the wicked.

126. This Tree of Life now stands in the greatest labor <note>original: "Anguish in the Birth"</note>; on one side it is *Christ*, and on the other it is the kingdom of *Nature*, in the wrath of God the Father, according to the properties of the dark and fiery world.

148. Now when the seed is sown, the main point <note>original: "Matter"</note> lies in this: specifically <note>original: "viz." (videlicet)</note>, in the quality of the ground into which the seed falls.

149. If it should fall into a stony, hard path—namely, into a bestial property <note>In this context, "property" refers to a core characteristic or inherent nature.</note> where a gross, filthy beast sits within the flesh—then it is trodden underfoot by the coarseness and lack of respect for it.

150. But if a covetous, greedy beast—such as a dog, wolf, or the like—sits within that nature, then cares and greed lie in the way and choke the seed.

151. But if it should fall into a prideful mind, which dwells in the power, honor, and pomp of the world, then pride and greatness have blocked the way. This seed has fallen upon a rock and brings forth no fruit.

<margin>* The good ground.</margin>
152. But if it falls into a good *reason* <note>original: "Reason"</note>, which possesses the property of a true human—namely, true lowliness and humility—there it is caught and received. This is the good ground; for God's very substance is humility. Therefore, this quality is an image <note>original: "Similitude"</note> of Him, and it springs up and bears *much fruit*.

153. Therefore, people should rightly consider the Scripture when it says, *“Many are called, but few are chosen.”* The Scripture understands it this way: many—indeed, the *majority*—are reached by the *divine call* and could achieve sonship <note>original: "Filiation"</note>, but their wicked lives, their business, their wealth, or the actions to which they devote themselves *harden* them.

<margin>* Mark 10:14.</margin>
154. Therefore, many times a child is *more* blessed than an old person. As Christ also says, *“Suffer little children to come unto me, for of such is the kingdom of God.”* Christ has received them into His calling or covenant.

155. But when a person grows older and turns away from the divine calling, yielding themselves up to the devil's will, they comfort themselves with an outwardly received sonship <note>original: "Filiation"</note> and adoption of grace, just as *Babel* <note>Babel here refers to the "confused" or corrupt institutional religious systems.</note> does. Such a person says, “Oh! It is Christ who has done it; He has satisfied and paid for everything. I only need to comfort myself with that and receive it. His grace will be credited <note>original: "imputed"</note> to me as a gift. I am saved and blessed in God's predestined purpose, regardless of the works of my own will. Indeed, I am dead in sins and can do no good thing without Him, unless He should draw me into it. But He will make His predestined purpose known in me, making me a child of grace through His external reception, and pardon my sins. Though I live wickedly, I am still a child of grace in His predestined purpose.”

<margin>Psalm 69:22, 23. Romans 11:9, 10.</margin>
156. Concerning these, Christ says, *“Make their way a snare and a stumbling-block, that they may fall; and let their light go out in the midst of the darkness, and harden them in their own devices,”* for their ways are abominable. Predestination applies to these people, for they were called at first, and were called continuously throughout, but they would not come.

<margin>Matthew 11:17.</margin>
157. And so Christ says, *“We have played the flute <note>original: "piped"</note> for you, and you have not danced. O Jerusalem! How often would I have gathered your children together, as a mother hen <note>original: "Clockhen"</note> gathers her chickens under her wings, and you yourself would not.”* You were reached by the call of God, but you turned away from it into your own will.

### Objection.

158. But then human reason objects: “They could not.” Why could they not, since they were called? Only those who are outside the call cannot come; but who can say who those people are?

### Answer.

<margin>Luke 8:12.</margin>
159. The *devil* within them will not. *“He tears the word from their hearts, so that they do not believe, nor are they saved,”* as Christ says. Therefore, they are rejected in the process of election and predestination. For the election passes over them until the *time of the harvest*—when the corn is ripe and iniquity has filled the cup to the brim. Then, when the floor is winnowed <note>original: "fanned"</note>, the chaff remains behind, being too light in weight.

160. It is as *Christ* says: <margin>Luke 8:5.</margin> *“The Kingdom of Heaven is like a sower who sows good wheat, and then the enemy comes and sows tares and weeds within it; and when the tares and weeds grow up, they choke the wheat so that it cannot grow and bear fruit.”* Thus also it is with man: many a soul is good grain, but the Devil's tares <note>original: "Tares"; weeds that resemble wheat, often used in the Bible to represent the seeds of evil</note> and weeds destroy it.

### Objection.

161. You will say, "That cannot be, because *Christ* says, <margin>John 10:28.</margin> *‘My sheep are in my hands, and no one can pluck them away from me.’*”

### Answer.

And all this is true; so long as the will or *desire* remains in God, the Devil cannot pluck them from there.

162. But when the soul breaks itself off from God's will, then the *science* <note>original: "Science"; here meaning the root of consciousness or inner knowledge</note> or root of the *abyssal* <note>original: "Abyssal Will"; referring to the 'Ungrund' or the bottomless, foundational will that exists before all nature and light</note> will, where *Christ* dwells, is obscured, dimmed, or darkened. *Christ* is then crucified and slain within his members <note>meaning individual believers who are spiritually part of the "Body of Christ"</note>, and the temple of the Holy Spirit is made into a prostitute's temple—understand this in terms of the *soul*. It is not that *Christ* himself is slain, but his temple—that is, a *member* of him—is slain.

163. For here is the separation in the election <note>original: "Election"; the theological concept of being chosen by God for salvation</note>: the election is the *Spirit of Christ*, which then passes away from this soul; for his voice is no longer in the soul, and it no longer has divine hearing, for it is outside, having gone away from God.

<margin>John 8:47.</margin>
<margin>* That is, the great turmoil and disturbance by which the Spirit of God in the temple of Christ is destroyed by sin.</margin>
164. For *Christ* says, *“He who is of God hears God's word; therefore you do not hear it, because you are not of God.”* They have lost the *divine* voice within them and have received and taken in the *Devil's* voice in the *Turba Magna* <note>Latin: "Great Turmoil"; in Boehme’s philosophy, this is the wrathful or chaotic principle in nature that breaks things apart</note>.

# The Eighth Chapter.

## Concerning the sayings or texts of Scripture and how they appear to contradict one another; how a man should understand them. Also concerning the Tree of Life and the Knowledge of Good and Evil.

1. <image-desc>Decorative drop cap 'W' containing a capital 'W' inside a square frame filled with intricate floral and vine patterns.</image-desc> WE will represent this high mystery in an *image* or *similitude* <note>original: "Similitude"; a comparison or allegory used to explain a complex idea</note> for the weak to consider, and show how the children of God and the children of perdition <note>original: "Perdition"; a state of eternal punishment or spiritual ruin</note> are: 1. generated from their origin; and 2. how they live their whole lives on earth.

2. Consider a tree, which springs and grows from its *ens* <note>Latin: "Ens"; the essential being or internal "seed-essence" of a thing</note> and seed. In that seed lies the tincture <note>original: "Tincture"; a spiritual quality or vitalizing energy that gives a thing its properties</note> of growth, together with the substance of the body—that is, the wood. Within it lie all four elements, together with the stars, or *astrum* <note>Latin: "Astrum"; the celestial or "starry" influence that shapes the character of a living thing</note>, of the constellations, as well as the power and virtue of the sun.

3. The *seed* falls into the earth, which receives it; for the earth is also a substance of the constellations and elements.

4. And the stars and elements are a substance of the *spiritus mundi* <note>Latin: "Spiritus Mundi"; the "spirit of the world," an animating force that connects the celestial and terrestrial realms</note>.

12. But if this a threefold life is equally manifested in relation to one another in a thing, so that one sees and understands the other, then that thing is *divine*. 17. The third Principle comes from the *power* of the substance. It begins from the power of Fire and Light, arising from the fiery exhalation breathed forth or expressed from the Fire and Light into a form. This is the Great Mystery (*Mysterium Magnum*), in which everything lies.

### Chapter 8. *How to understand some opposite Texts.*

...other, wherein we understand the great Mystery of God; how it has gone with the whole Creation.

22. Consider a grain or seed of a tree, as is mentioned above; for therein the Great Mystery <note>original: "Great Mystery" (Mysterium Magnum), a term used by Jacob Boehme to describe the chaotic source of all potentiality from which God created the universe</note> lies, according to the property of the seed. For the whole tree, with its root and fruit, lies within it, and yet is *not manifested* while it is still a seed. But as soon as it is sown into its mother, the Earth, then these things are manifested, and the tree begins to put forth in the fiery science <note>original: "fiery science," referring to the energetic or spiritual impulse that drives life and growth</note>.

23. Now the Earth cannot excite or kindle the <term>Ens</term> <note>Ens: The internal essence or spiritual substance of a thing</note> in the seed, where the "three first" <note>original: "three first," referring to the three primary spiritual properties—often identified as sulfur, mercury, and salt—that Boehme believed made up all matter</note> manifest themselves, if the Sun—that is, the Light—*did not first kindle it*. For the "three first" lie in the Earth shut up in the cold fire.

24. But when the Sun kindles the Earth, then the hot fire unfolds itself and creeps forth, out of which the light of nature arises; that is, it unfolds itself outward, and in that unfolding, the seed is now *received*.

25. That is, the power of the Earth then receives its dear son in the seed which is born of her, and receives him with joy; for the seed is more noble than its mother *in its substance*.

26. But now we are to consider the fundamental ground of the Earth: whether the "three first" (regarding the place where the seed is sown) are similar in quality to the seed in its operative, manifested <term>Ens</term> or not. If they are, then the Earth receives the seed as a dear son or child, with joy.

27. Likewise, on the other side, the <term>Ens</term> of the seed yields itself into its mother, the Earth, with great longing and desire; for it finds its true mother, out of whose property it is born or generated. Thus also the <term>Ens</term> of the Earth finds a very truly dear son in the <term>Ens</term> of the seed, and the one rejoices in the other, and so the *growth* <note>original: "Vegetation"</note> springs forth.

28. But if the <term>Ens</term> of the Earth in that place be *unlike* in quality to the <term>Ens</term> of the seed, the Earth receives it indeed, but only as a stepson. It does not bring its joy and desire into it, but lets the *stepson stand*. The seed may pull to itself an <term>Ens</term> out of its own true mother, which is hidden very deeply in that place; because it is so deeply hidden, *many* a seed perishes before it can reach the true mother of its own property.

29. And though the seed receives an <term>Ens</term> from this mismatched quality, it still stands in great danger before it can transform <note>original: "metamorphose"</note> its own essence into a foreign <term>Ens</term>. It never becomes as good and healthy <note>original: "lusty"</note> a tree as when the seed is sown into its right and true mother.

30. For that *opposite <term>Ens</term>* is always against the seed, and their essences stand in conflict. This is why the tree is so knotty, gnarled <note>original: "knurling"</note>, and crooked, as well as so small and slender; and many times, if an evil constellation, alignment <note>original: "configuration"</note>, influence, or *astrological aspect* affects it from the outside, it bears bad fruit, or else quite withers and dies.

31. For if the <term>Ens</term> of the Earth mingles with the opposite constellation, alignment, or *aspect*, and receives it, then the Earth rejoices in the property of that constellation or influence (since they share a will of the same or *similar property*, and will generate a new son in their union or mixture). In that case, the tree is forsaken by the <term>Ens</term> of the Earth; it withers and brings forth bad, little, or no fruit.

32. Now if we consider the growth and development of that tree, we then find the hidden ground of all secret mysteries. For then it first receives the <term>Ens</term> of the stepmother to itself, and gives its own <term>Ens</term> to the stepmother.

33. She also receives the <term>Ens</term> of the seed, but *not with such joy* as if it were a similar <term>Ens</term>. She attracts the <term>Ens</term> of the seed to herself, which is where the root exists, but there is soon an *opposing will* in the "three first" of the mother, which is why the root is knotty and lumpy <note>original: "burry"</note>.

# How to understand some opposite Texts.
## Chap. 8.

**34.** Now, in this conflict <note>original: "Strife"</note>, the fire ignites within the essence <note>original: "Ens"</note> of the seed through the power of the sun. In this ignition, the Great Mystery in the Spirit of the World <note>original: "Mysterium Magnum in Spiritu Mundi"</note> is revealed.

**35.** For it takes hold of the essence of the sun and rejoices in it, because the sun’s power becomes substantial within it. It draws the essence of the seed from the root up into itself so that it might produce fruit.

**36.** The sun gives its power to every seed without making any distinction; it loves every fruit, sprout, and plant, and withdraws from nothing. It desires nothing else but to nurture good fruit in every herb or whatever else it may be.

**37.** It receives them all, whether they are evil or good, and grants them their desired will or longing. It cannot do otherwise, for in its own essence, it is nothing other than the fulfillment of every desire.

**38.** But we must carefully consider how the sun is also a poison to what is evil and a blessing to what is good. For within its power, the vegetative soul exists, and within its power, that soul also dies. You must understand it in this way:

**39.** If the forms or qualities of nature within the "three first principles" <note>the alchemical principles of Sulphur, Mercury, and Salt</note> in the root of the tree are in harmony with the "Mother of the Earth," then the earth gives its power, virtue, and sap to the root with great longing. Then the sun’s power rejoices in it and speeds the growth <note>original: "Vegetation"</note>.

<margin>☛ Or, wonders in the tree.</margin>
**40.** However, if the earth and the root are in opposition, then the earth’s power and virtue are withheld from the root. If the sun then ignites the <gloss>root and the tree</gloss> with its beams of light, the three first principles—namely <term>Sulphur</term> <note>the combustible or oily principle</note>, <term>Mercurius</term> <note>Mercury; the fluid or volatile principle</note>, and <term>Sal</term> <note>Salt; the solid or stabilizing principle</note>—ignite within themselves in their harshness <note>original: "Malignity"</note>. They burn and scorch the essence of the sun and dry up the water, causing the trunk or the branches to wither.

**41.** But when these three principles can obtain the sap of the earth, they remain in a state of harmony and do not provoke conflict within themselves. In that case, they agree with the beams of the sun's light.

**42.** We see this also in the Mystery in the Spirit of the World: when the fiery quality rises up and the sun ignites it, a parching heat follows, preventing herbs and grass from growing.

**43.** Furthermore, we see in this image how a branch grows. When the stalk or stem sprouts, the conflict in nature rises with it. For when nature is ignited in its balanced state <note>original: "Temperature"</note>, it remains constantly in a state of separation and distinction.

**44.** The power and virtue of the sun would always try to cast off the harshness of the three first principles. These principles also move quickly according to their own will. From this separation and pulling away from one another, twigs push forth and spring from the main stock.

**45.** For in the winter, the cold locks them in with their internal conflict. When springtime arrives and they can finally reach the heat, they enter into conflict again. This conflict pushes out into the branches and twigs, as one can see in a "year’s shoot" or the annual growth of every tree.

**46.** Now we must consider the inner foundation, as well as the driving force that puts forth branches. We see that one branch grows large and bears fruit, while another withers. We understand this to be caused by the capacity for separation in the Spirit of the World <note>original: "Spiritu Mundi"</note>, where every quality tries to solidify itself within the essence of the tree, abandoning harmony and equality.

**47.** These qualities then push out from that harmony, rising in pride above one another through the power of fire. They refuse to remain within the will of the sun in the balanced state...

nature, we see how they are stunted or stifled in their emergence, even when they are forced out or sprouted from the stock.

48. For that <term>consciousness</term> <note>original: "Science," from the German *Wissenschaft*, meaning the active power or innate knowledge within a thing</note> in that specific <term>quality</term> <note>original: "Property"</note> has brought itself into its own self-will. In its pride, it wants to push forward sooner or *earlier* than the other qualities that exist in the <term>harmony</term> <note>the balanced state of nature</note>, but it does not have enough power or virtue to *sustain* itself.

49. And so, when a strong influence from the stars, or an *influence* of an astrological aspect from the outside, penetrates into this proud branch and searches, sifts, and tests it—to see whether it originates from the equal *harmony* or not—it becomes tainted, infected, or poisoned, and it *withers*. It is a rebellious, separated branch, and thus the heat of the sun (within the spirit of this world) dries all such branches.

50. But the other branches come from a state of balance and from the power and virtue drawn out by the sun. In these branches, the sun rejoices in their qualities; it tempers them and expresses itself through them. The sun draws those branches out in their power or virtue strongly, for their qualities exist in harmony with the sun's will or desire.

51. We see further how the qualities of nature in the branches, as they grow, are destroyed by outward accidents and occasions—specifically from the patterns and aspects of the stars. They are also harmed by impure air, which prevents the sun from helping them with his beams, so that they become knotty, crooked, and gnarled. In this way, many a branch is blasted, withered, and falls off.

52. Just as it happens with the original springing and growth of a *tree*, it also happens with the original springing, growing, and development of a human being. Although humans—in the qualities of nature within the Light—are higher than the plants growing from the earth, everything follows one and the same order and course. Everything emerges from one and the same fundamental *source* <note>original: "Ground," referring to the *Ungrund* or the underlying divine reality</note>, namely through the outspoken or expressed Word of God, in which the Divine Speaking works within the <term>Great Mystery</term> <note>original: "Mysterio Magno"</note>.

53. The only difference is that a human, in the <term>essence</term> <note>original: "Ens"</note> of his body, holds a higher degree of pre-eminence than the earth and its fruit. As for the soul, it is even higher than the spirit of this world. Yet all things proceed in their origin from the same fundamental source, even as they separate themselves and organize into different beginnings within the creation.

### Of God's predestinate Purpose.

54. God's only preordained purpose is his Eternal *Speaking Word*. He speaks or expresses this Word through his wisdom, out of his power and into <term>innate knowledge</term> <note>original: "Science"</note>, creating separation and distinction to manifest or *reveal* himself.

55. He has no other preordained purpose within him, nor is it possible for him to have any other. If there were another, then something would have to exist before him that caused him to have that purpose.

56. Therefore, the speaking of his power—for the sake of self-manifestation—is *not* a purpose that has a beginning or a starting point, but rather a *generating* or ongoing purpose.

57. And the preordained purpose of the Word is the <term>innate knowledge</term> <note>original: "Science"</note> of the "separability," or the distinction and formation of the one and only Divine Power.

58. This "separability" and formation of the only God into his *Trinity* has, from eternity, spoken itself forth into a beginning through the Word. This happened in an <term>essence</term> <note>original: "Ens"</note> of all the qualities of distinction, so that all these distinct qualities lie within one another.

### Of God’s Predestinate Purpose. Chapter 8.

59. And that which is spoken out or expressed is the *Mysterium Magnum*, the Great Mystery, and the true, only predestinate <note>The "predestinate purpose" refers to God's pre-ordained plan for creation.</note> purpose of the Word.

60. The Word desires nothing more than to manifest its own holy power through "separability" (distinction); and in the Word, the *Deity* becomes manifest in this distinction through the fire and the light.

61. Thus these two—namely the Word and the *Mysterium Magnum*, the Great Mystery—are in one another like soul and body. For the *Mysterium Magnum* is the "substantiality" <note>original: "Substantiality"; the spiritual or essential substance that gives form to the Word.</note> of the Word, in which and through which the invisible God in His Trinity is manifested, and becomes manifest from eternity to eternity. For whatever the Word is in its power and sound, the *Mysterium Magnum* is its *substance*; it is the eternal, substantial Word of God.

62. But now understand us correctly: The spiritual, sounding Word is the *Divine Understanding*. Through the *Mysterium Magnum*—that is, through the eternal substance of the Word—it has expressed or spoken itself forth, forming a beginning and entering into time.

63. And the "separabilities" or distinctions which lie in the *Mysterium Magnum* as a working *Ens* <note>original: *Ens*; a philosophical term for a fundamental "being" or "essence."</note>, the Eternal Speaking Spirit has made manifest, so that it is a *moving*, compacting, and generating *life*; and that is the Spirit of the outward world.

64. Its motion is the life of creatures; the four elements are its substance. The "science" <note>In this context, "science" refers to the organized knowledge or inherent logic of the stars' influence.</note> of distinction in the Spirit of the world is the *Astrum* or the stars, in which the "vegetable" <note>meaning plant-like or growth-oriented</note> life exists.

65. In the beginning of its distinction, this Eternal *Mysterium Magnum* (Great Mystery) divided and separated itself by the speaking out of the Word of the Deity. That is, it has separated the subtle *Ens* from the coarse, thickened, and congealed *Ens*.

<margin>Extrusion or Excrement.</margin>

66. The subtle *Ens* is the *Astrum* or stars—namely, a "quintessence"—and the coarse, thickened, concrete *Ens* is a <gloss>rejection</gloss> <note>original: "Rejection"; here meaning the solid matter cast off or precipitated during the creation process, like dross from metal.</note>, which is the earth, stones, and metals.

67. This rejection was made so that there might be a clarity in the Spirit of the world—namely, a shining, sensible life.

68. This "rejection" also has a twofold property: 1. A subtle property, from the power of the light in the Word; and 2. A coarse property, according to the thickening of darkness at the origin of fire.

69. By the *coarse* property, we understand the earth; and by the *subtle*, we understand the power within the essence of the earth. From this power, through separation or distinction, herbs, trees, and metals grow. Also, all flesh <note>meaning the physical bodies of living creatures</note> comes out of the subtle essence of the earth. Everything that exists only in time and whose life depends on the Spirit of the world has its body from the essence of this subtle earth.

70. This Spirit of the world—together with the configurations or stars of its "science," the subtle bodies of fire, water, and air, and the solidity of the earth—is now the spoken or expressed *life and substance* from the inward Eternal Mystery (the inward substantial Word of God).

71. This Eternal Word of God dwells and works in the "inward ground" <note>The spiritual foundation or core of reality.</note> in holy power and virtue. At the beginning of this world, through the inward mystery, it expressed itself into an outward mystery.

72. And from that outward mystery, the entire creation of the outward world proceeds and is included within it, as if in its *mother’s body* or *womb*. There, the Eternal Word, using the "science of distinction" from its powers, has introduced itself into a *figured* (shaped) *life*.

73. This outward *Mysterium* of the formed Word is now in a wheel or orb—like a moving sphere or clockwork—enclosed with its generating life, wherein the

### Chapter 8: Of God's Predestined Purpose.

74. Properties are wrestling for the primacy; suddenly one is on top, then quickly another, then the third, fourth, fifth, sixth, and seventh. This is also how we should understand the emergence of the *seven properties*.

75. Suddenly the Spirit in the fire overcomes, from which *heat* arises; just as suddenly the Spirit in the water overcomes, from which it rains; then in the air or wind, by which it lifts or raises itself; and then in the earthliness, from which *cold* arises.

<margin>Melting or softening.</margin>
76. What one property builds up, another pulls down and destroys; what one property yields or gives, the other hardens, stops, or hinders <margin>Melting or softening.</margin> the giving, so that it perishes. One gives a good *essence* <term>Ens</term> <note>original: Ens; in Boehme’s thought, this refers to the inner "being" or essential substance of a thing.</note> and will, while the other gives or puts an evil essence into a thing and hinders the good, so that the one may be manifested through the other.

77. God has now spoken or inspired the light of nature into this outward mystery of the properties—in which we understand the separability or distinction of the spoken word—out of the Great Mystery <note>original: *ex Mysterio Magno*</note>, through and from the power of the eternal light. Thus, in every evil essence there lies a good fundamental ground, namely a good power or virtue from the holy Word; no evil exists alone without the good.

78. Moreover, God has placed the *sun* within the properties of the outward world to be a beneficial, active life, so that all things may harmonize within it and reach a balance in their struggle, and thus be able to grow and bear fruit.

79. And yet, even though the light of *nature* from the divine power works within everything, and the sun from the outside gives itself to and enters *every* living and growing thing, the fiery property in the "wrath" <note>In this context, "wrath" refers to the harsh, contractive, and "dark" quality of nature before it is enlightened by divine love.</note> is so strong that the properties compress themselves so hard and close—due to the power of the darkness—that many living creatures and plants must exist in malignancy. The hunger in that dark compression is so strong that it holds all creatures in its power.

<margin>The first predestined purpose of God.</margin>
80. Now this working substance within the properties, along with light and darkness (in which the whole creation is contained), is the *only* predestined purpose of God's Word: namely, that it may generate life—such as animals and other creatures—and manifest the spoken word in physical forms <note>original: "Images or Representations"</note>. This ensures that every power in the knowledge of distinction exists as a living form, according to both the property of the light's power from the holy Word and the fire's power.

81. However, the light is given to all things for a balance <term>Temperature</term>. This light does not only shine on the outside of a thing or substance; it works cooperatively within every essence in all that live and grow. *Therefore*, no creature has cause to complain to its Creator that he has created it to be evil.

82. Only two things cause this: first, the *wrath* of nature makes a thing hardened and blocks the power of the light.

<margin>Note.</margin>
83. And second, the *curse* hinders it so that the holy "tincture" <term>Tincture</term> <note>In theosophy, a tincture is a spiritualizing or life-giving principle that transforms base matter.</note>—the holy foundation of the Speaking Word in the eternal light—has withdrawn into itself because of the vanity of the devil, humanity, and other creatures. Now, it only gives itself to that which brings itself into a resemblance of the light’s power, and it will not cooperate with that knowledge which surrenders itself to the wrath of the darkness.

<margin>Psalm 18:25–26.</margin>
84. The reason is this: otherwise the darkness would seize the holy power and pull it into its own malignancy. Then it is as the Scripture says: <margin>Psalm 18:25–26.</margin> "*With the perverse, you are perverse, and with the holy you are holy.*"

<margin>Against its will.</margin>
85. Just as the sun must <margin>Against its will.</margin> suffer the thistle to consume its good essence into its own prickly nature and use it for its thorns; therefore the highest tincture will... <note>The sentence in the original text appears to break off or continue onto the next page.</note>

...will not give itself into the *falsehood* or *malignity* of that science <note>original: "science" here refers to a branch of knowledge or the active root of a being's nature</note> or root, in which the eternal, abyssal <note>original: "abyssal" refers to the *Ungrund*, the bottomless void or nothingness before creation</note>, unfathomable will is turned into an image or *resemblance* of the dark world’s property.

<margin>The second predestinate purpose of God.</margin>
85. Now the other, or second predestinate purpose of God through the speaking Word of God, by which God would manifest himself through the *Mysterium Magnum* <note>Latin for "Great Mystery"—the source of all potentiality and creation</note>, the Great Mystery, is the most dear holy name JESUS.

86. When man had turned himself away from God and toward the creature <note>referring to created things rather than the Creator</note>, he then lost the voice of God. Therefore, God spoke it in, or inspired it again in grace, into the "seed of the woman" with the imprinted or modeled name JESUS—namely, with the second predestinate purpose out of the divine ground.

87. The *first* predestinate purpose, concerning nature and the creature, is from the Father’s property. The *second* predestinate purpose—to relieve, redeem, and deliver nature from the curse and torment—is the name JESUS, namely, the highest tincture <note>original: "tincture" refers to a spiritual essence or transforming power</note> of the divine power to manifest the same through the outspoken or expressed Word in the property of the good that lies captive in the evil.

88. This name JESUS—namely, the predestinate purpose of his *love*—God has spoken into or inspired into the mother of *all* men; and as a living power, he incorporated it into an eternal covenant.

89. And he fulfills that covenant with the introduction of the divine *ens* <note>original: "ens" is Latin for "being" or "essence"</note> into the human property. So now, just as all bring with them into the world the curse and perdition, in which all <margin>Eph. 2:3</margin> are *children of the wrath of God* and are shut up under that wrath, so also all bring with them into the world the covenant of grace in the incorporated name JESUS.

90. Which covenant God has confirmed and established in Christ, with the seal of *infant baptism* <note>original: "pædobaptism"</note>, and for those of old, by the *circumcision* of the foreskin.

91. Therefore, know now that God has manifested no other predestinate purpose through his Word than the fundamental ground of the creation—namely, the nature of separability or *distinction*, in which the predestinate purpose toward evil or malignity takes its origin.

92. In this, the science <note>active knowledge/manifestation</note> of the abyssal will introduces itself into the fiery separation or distinction: as to one part, into the power of *light*; to the other, into the fiery property of painfulness; and a third, into the *fantasy* <note>the realm of self-delusion or false imagination</note>, according to fire, light, and darkness—namely, into self-pride, as *Lucifer* and *Adam* did.

93. But yet, whatever is separated or distinguished into the power of the light is good; and whatever remains standing in the temperature <note>original: "temperature" refers to a state of balance or harmony between opposing qualities</note> at the fiery separation or distinction, the highest tincture of power unites itself to that. But to the other in the separation, the tincture of the sun and of the spirit of the world unites itself.

What the predestinate purpose of God is, as well as the *drawing* of the Father in both the good and the evil; and 2. How the predestination or *election* concerns man; and after that, compare it with and examine it by the texts of *Scripture*.

...or where the *Distinction* itself lies; for <margin>i The Word of Separability <note>Boehme uses "Separability" to describe the process by which the unified divine power divides into distinct qualities or individuals.</note>.</margin> **i** as to the outward body, it is an *Ens* <note>original: "Ens"; a philosophical term meaning "being" or "essence."</note> of the four elements; as to the outward life, it is an *Ens* of the Spirit of the World; and as to the inward body, it is an *Ens* of the Eternal Word of God—namely, *the holy Mystery of the substantiality of God's power*.

96. Yet as to the inward Spirit, it exists in two properties: first, the *creaturely soul* comes out of the Father’s nature—that is, out of the Eternal Separation or Distinction of the Word of God into Light and Darkness.

97. This property is the *Self-hood* of the creaturely soul, springing out of the ground of the Eternal Will.

98. The other property is the true *Divine Property* in the power of the Light, which is *Christus* <note>original: "CHRISTUS"; Christ</note>, in whom the name JESUS is manifested. That is the true Eternal *predestinate purpose* of God from before the *foundation of the world*, when the soul was not yet a creature but only an *Ens in Mysterio Magno* <note>original: "Ens in Mysterio Magno"; a being within the Great Mystery or the divine potentiality before creation.</note>—that is, a being in the Great Mystery.

99. This second property was in man in the beginning, *before sin was manifested* in Jehovah; but when the soul broke itself off from that state and turned itself toward the creation, the creaturely soul became *speechless* toward God. Therefore, the predestinate purpose in the holy name JESUS put itself forward as a dowry or *free gift of grace* and entered into the light of life.

100. This *free gift of grace* is *not* now the creaturely soul’s *own self*; the soul does not possess it by *natural right*. Instead, it stands within the soul in a center of its own, calling to the soul and presenting itself as a *pledge* to manifest itself within it.

101. The soul should remain still and turn away from all imaginations of earthly creatures, refusing to bring any earthly *Ens* into its *fire-life* <note>Boehme describes the soul's fundamental energy as a "fire-life" that must be fueled either by earthly desires or divine light.</note>, from which a false or evil light arises. Then this *Divine predestinate purpose* in the highest *tincture* <note>original: "Tincture"; a spiritual essence or transformative power that can "dye" or change the quality of a being.</note>, coming out of the holy *love-fire*, will manifest itself with the *holy light*.

102. Just as fire thoroughly enlightens red-hot iron so that the iron seems to be *mere fire*, so also this love-fire—this predestinate purpose of the *free gift of grace*—changes the soul into its own property. Yet the soul retains its nature, just as the iron in the fire retains its own nature.

<margin>k John 1:4, 9.</margin>
103. *First*, every child born of man and woman has this free gift of grace presented to it in its inward ground, **k** *in the light of life*.

<margin>l Matthew 11:28.</margin>
104. It presents itself as a pledge to every soul and reaches out its desire toward the soul throughout a person's entire life, calling and saying, **l** "*Come here to me*, and depart from all earthly imaginations and desires in the *Wrath*, out from the *phantasy* <note>original: "Phantasy"; the realm of illusion or the distorted images produced by the fallen mind.</note>."

105. *Secondly*, on the other side, as soon as its life begins, the fierce, wrathful, awakened *anger* of God stands in every soul within the essence of the "Separability," wherein also lies the introduced *poison of the serpent*, along with the *devil’s desire*.

106. And *thirdly*, every "seed" of the body, according to the outward world, stands under the power and authority of the spirit of the world, in the "constellation" or *configuration* of the stars. For just as the great clockwork or *machine* <note>A common 17th-century metaphor for the mechanical, predictable movements of the cosmos.</note> of the universe stands in a certain figure at that time, the *Spiritus Mundi* <note>original: "Spiritus Mundi"; the Spirit of the World or the cosmic soul that influences physical life.</note> gives the soul that same figure in the property and condition of its outward life. It models, fashions, or frames it as a *beast* in the property of the outward life; for the spirit of the outward world, made of the four elements, can produce nothing but a *beast*.

107. And such a *beast* exists because the entire creation lies within *man*. Because he fell away from the "Temperature" <note>original: "Temperature"; a state of perfect balance and harmony between opposing qualities.</note> and entered into earthly *desire* and "imagibility" <note>The capacity to form images or be shaped by mental focus.</note>, the spirit of the world has become manifest in him with all its divisions and distinctions.

111. Whereupon many a man, *if he does not continually slay and mortify the earthly, implanted, innate, engrafted beast, and break the malignant or evil will with the divine free gift of grace, falls into the hands of the executioner.*

112. <margin>The drawing of the Father, according to Love and Anger.</margin>
113. And herein now lies the drawing out of the Father's property toward evil and toward good; into whatever <term>Ens</term> <note>original: "Ens" (essence or being)</note> the life has configured or constituted itself, just so that very constellation draws it into its likeness or resemblance: like will always dwell with like.

114. As an honest, virtuous man chooses to dwell with the honest and virtuous, and a scorner with a scorner, a thief with a thief, a greedy glutton, drunkard, gambler, womanizer, and such like, with companions *like themselves*, their nature—out of the property of God's anger—draws them to it.

115. Thus also the *actual* sins of the parents come together in the property, for every child is generated out of the seed of the parents; as the parents are, such is also the child. Yet oftentimes the constellation or configuration of the stars alters it powerfully with authority, and constrains it in its power and might, if it be strong.

119. For out of the *total Divine nature* <note>original: "Property"</note> no creature can come; for that has no ground nor beginning.

Separation or Distinction of the Speaking, wherein the Speaking must introduce itself into Nature, otherwise the *Word* would not be manifested.

The inward property or disposition of the soul now lies in the first created configuration of the stars—the eternal beginning ground—which is not formed or framed together within the outward, bestial <note>original: "beastial"; referring to the animalistic or earthly nature</note> constellation of the stars.

122. For the soul's essence <term>original: "soulish Science"; referring to the innate knowledge or root-power of the soul</term> has its own unique form, like a magical source of fire; it separates or distinguishes itself within life itself, in the shape of the body.

123. Within this lies the foundation of eternal nature, which is capable of both good and evil; for it is the cause of both the fire and the light, yet it lies fast and firmly bound in sin.

<margin>Exodus 20:5</margin>
124. For within this lies the *inherited*, original, or *innate* sin at the center of nature, where the devil has made his home. Here also lie the inherited sins passed down from parents and grandparents, like an evil poison, concerning which God says: *He will punish the children for the sins of the fathers to the third and fourth generation.* Furthermore, within this also lie the good deeds of the parents and God’s blessing, which descend upon the children.

125. These properties also align themselves into a pattern according to their kind, through which the *soul shapes* itself into the image or *disposition* of either an angel or a devil.

126. And here lies the difficult or hard foundation upon which God’s election or predestination gazes, waiting to see what kind of angel will be formed there; yet no final conclusion has been made yet.

127. For the free gift of grace resides in the inner foundation and unites itself with the essential root <note>original: "Science or Root"</note> of the soul’s depths—that is, with the will of the Eternal Father.

128. Here Christ *prays* for the poor captive soul, as the Scripture says; for the soul lies in the bonds of God’s anger and is hardened in its sins.

129. And here, Life pulls itself through or penetrates *Death* and sifts the soul to see if any small spark of good remains that is capable of receiving divine power; if so, then it is *drawn* toward God.

130. For Christ desires to be revealed, and the wrath of nature also desires to be revealed; thus, these *two* predestined purposes within the formed Word <note>The "formed Word" refers to the "Fiat," the creative power of God manifested in physical and spiritual form.</note> stand in conflict over humanity—that is, over the image of God.

131. The Kingdom of Grace within the Light seeks to *possess* the soul and manifest itself there; likewise, the Kingdom of Nature within the wrath of fire—in the distinctions of nature—seeks to have it and manifest itself there. Both of these exist within the *formed Word*: namely, the Father’s property in *wrath* and the Son’s love-property in the *light*.

132. Now observe this previously mentioned illustration and comparison of a *tree*: the woman is the ground or soil, and the man is the grain or seed of the human tree that is sown.

### Objection.

133. Then Reason says: God brings and joins them together just as he intends them to be.

### Answer.

Yes, that is correct; but it happens through his predestined purpose, which he has organized into a system of governance within the Word, through the great clockwork or machinery of nature.

Therefore, life mostly proceeds according to the alignment of the *soul*, which excels the outward world in power and status. It is just as it lies within the *sower* to sow his seed or grain where he pleases, even if other ground might be more capable and better for it.

<margin>Love or Body.</margin>

It is aligned in the correct divine order: according to the soul in the *Great Mystery* <note>original: "Mysterio Magno"</note>, and according to the body in the *Spirit of the World*. Then, a life is awakened within it according to the property of true similarity or likeness.

138. And then, if a man follows this and *does not care for riches, nobility, beauty, or courtly manners and behavior*, then his own nature—which he has from birth—attains the right and true likeness. It becomes a soil that is acceptable to the grain or seed, and conflict does not so suddenly arise in their offspring; for they stand with one another in equality and likeness, and there the inward and outward sun can better align within the child.

139. But men see plainly how it goes in the world regarding what nature brings and binds together. Oftentimes, two young people align together in the *highest love*, which happens through the great predestined purpose of the true constellation in the Spirit of the World and the formed Word; yet the parents and friends disagree because of the disparity between the parties in poverty, riches, or birth.

<margin>Genesis 6:2, 3.</margin>
140. Just as God says to *Noah*: *“The men will not allow my Spirit to draw them, but they take wives and lie with the daughters of men according to whether they are beautiful, rich, and noble,”* which is entirely a human contrivance.

<margin>The Sin-Flood (Deluge). And he destroys them by bringing destruction upon their heads.</margin>
141. It is from such unions that mighty tyrants, kings, and rulers proceed. Against these, God sets the flood of his anger in their self-framed alignment to confront them, and he hardens their own self-will.

142. Consequently, many people are compelled, out of respect for status and riches, to match and couple together. Afterward, they become enemies to one another, and all their lives they wish in their minds and hearts for the divorce, separation, and death of each other.

143. These couples will then introduce their *spiritual essences* in their seeds in a union with one another to form the human life of a child—the woman being the ground or soil, and the man sowing the grain or seed.

144. And so, when the two essences enter one another to transform into one (namely, into the female and male seed), the *essential being* <note>original: "Ens"; the fundamental substance or inner essence of a thing.</note> should manifest itself in a joyful likeness. Instead, they are mismatched and antagonistic in their wills; the "soil" there receives the seed or grain like an unwanted stepson.

145. The soil must indeed receive the seed, for it presses into it and draws the *essential being* out of the ground into itself; but the soil does not give the seed its goodwill.

148. and it very suddenly brings its hateful, malignant beams *from the Great Turba* <note>original: "ex Turba Magna"; in this context, the "Turba" is a disruptive or destructive force in nature that arises when properties are out of balance</note> into the formation of the creature, causing many a fruit to perish before it attains life.

149. Now, I leave it to Reason to consider what kind of work can take place here in the center of nature to produce life. Also, consider how nature *hardens itself* in its contrariety and opposition. One should carefully consider what kind of "foolish fire" it awakens and generates in itself, about which the Scripture says: *God’s anger hardens them, so that they cannot come to the true holy Light.*

150. For whatever property and condition the foolish fire possesses, the light that arises out of it is exactly the same; and the life consists within this foolish fire.

<margin>* Psalm 18:25, 26</margin>

<margin>* Genesis 3:8</margin>

It should manifest itself through the kindled fire of the soul and enter into and work with the light of the creature.

153. The soul should now stand still before the Spirit of Christ, so that the Spirit may work in it; even though the soul (meaning the foolish property or condition in which the soul’s fire burns and becomes living) exists in the *wrath* of strife.

<margin>* Romans 6:16</margin>
154. And here now is a pulling toward the "wrath," and also a pulling toward Christ through the Light of Nature. It is rightly said here: whatever the "inclination" <note>original: "Science"; here meaning the directed knowledge or root-will</note> or root of the abyssal will—arising from the ground of eternal nature in its foolish property—turns toward and obeys as a servant, it becomes a servant to that thing. It is either a servant to the anger of God in the wrath of eternal nature, or to the life of Christ in grace, as St. Paul says.

<margin>* Sin and wickedness.</margin>

->Answer.<-

156. Indeed, by *itself* it cannot do this. But Christ, who assumed this foolish property, has broken the wrath and the *Turba* of the false will to pieces with his love. He has introduced his love into the creaturely word and has given it to the *essence* <note>original: "Ens"</note> of the soul as a help.

157. And it simply comes down to this: which property prevails over the other—the light-fire or the anger-fire; *God’s love or His anger.*

158. For the *essence* of the soul does not yet have understanding, but the ground of the will has it, arising from the abyssal eternal will toward the generating of the "City of God," wherein the Father’s abyssal will generates the Son—*namely, the power and virtue.*

### Question.

163. But why does the Scripture say, *Many, and not all?*

### Answer.

<margin>c 1 Timothy 2:4.</margin>
Christ stands ready and present to all, and he calls them all; for the Scripture says, $^c$ *God wills that all men should be helped or saved.*

<margin>d John 1:5.</margin>
164. But not everyone is capable of receiving the calling; for the essence <term>original: "Ens"</term> of many people is more **devilish than human**, having been overpowered and hardened by God's **wrath**.
