165. Regarding this foolish essence, the calling passes over it; for the foolish property is seized and held captive in **darkness**.

166. Indeed, the light shines through it clearly, but it finds no essence <term>original: "Ens"</term> of love within it where it can ignite itself. Therefore, the essence of the creaturely soul remains without God dwelling in it, and **Christ** also remains dwelling only in himself.

<margin>e Luke 16:26.</margin>
167. And yet they are near one another, but a principle separates or distinguishes them—namely, the great **cliff** or **gulf** between the rich man and poor Lazarus; for they are to each other as life is to death.

<margin>f Romans 9:22.</margin>
168. Concerning these people, it is understood $^f$ *that God makes his wrath known and hardens them*. This does not happen because of some strange, foreign, or divine will, or a pre-planned purpose <term>original: "predestinate Purpose"</term>, but out of the way God has introduced his Word into nature and into the state of **distinction** <note>original: "Separability or Distinction," referring to the process of creation where things become individual and separate from the source</note>.

169. It is not that the **holy will of God** withdraws itself from them so that they *must* remain hardened (as human reason wrongly suggests). Rather, God's will is **in them** and would gladly have them and manifest itself in them as the Image of God.

170. However, the wrath in the center of nature—where the will of the abyss has separated itself into darkness—has captured them. It has filled the broken gates of Divine Love with the **abominations** of innate, inherited, or original sins.

171. The opposing "constellation" <note>Boehme often uses astrological terms to describe spiritual influences</note> of disagreement and unlikeness also helps this along. In this state, both the man and the woman, as husband and wife, sow only **hatred** and the **curse** into one another through their wills, effectively sowing **death** itself.

172. They shape the vital quality <term>original: "Tincture"</term> of their lives into a **hostile will of enmity**. They come together in the mixture of their seeds in **beastly lust**. Neither of their wills or purposes is faithful to the other; their intentions are only venom, poison, and death. They are always cursing one another and living together like dogs and cats.

And just as their **Life** and constant **Will** are, so also is their foolish *Tincture* <note>original: "Tincture"; in the context of Boehme’s philosophy, this refers to the inner spiritual quality or essence that defines a soul's nature.</note> in the Seed. ->Question.<-

174. But you will say, "How can the child help it?"

->Answer.<-

The child and the parents are one and the same tree; the child is a branch of that tree.

175. Listen, **Reason**: When does the **Sun** ever change a branch on a sour crab-apple tree so that it becomes sweet? And should God then go completely contrary to the predestined purpose of his expressed **Will** and **Word** for the sake of a *thistle*?

<margin><sup>h</sup> 2 Cor. 2:16.</margin>
176. For the Kingdom of Darkness must also have creatures; they are *all* profitable and useful to God. To Him, the wicked is <sup>h</sup> *a fragrance of death leading to death*, and the holy is a *fragrance of life leading to life*, as the Scripture says.

177. But the **will** toward perdition <term>eternal ruin or damnation</term> exists in the *Ens* <term>the fundamental spiritual substance or "being" of a creature</term> of the creature, and the **will** toward the holy **life** exists out of God in *Christ*. These are both within one another as *one thing*, but they are to be understood as existing in *two* distinct principles.

178. As long as both are working in the creature, it is drawn by both of them. But if it happens that *Christ* can find *no place of rest* for himself, then the **Devil** takes possession of the <margin><sup>i</sup> Or City.</margin> <sup>i</sup> place where *Christ* should work.

<margin><sup>k</sup> Mat. 20:16.</margin>
179. And here is what *Christ* means when he says, <sup>k</sup> *Few are chosen, or elected from among them*. And why? Because *many* of them still have a little spark of the good *Ens* in them, in which *Christ* works and *without ceasing* warns and calls to them.

<margin><sup>l</sup> Resemblance or Likeness to God.</margin>
<margin><sup>m</sup> 1 Pet. 1:2.</margin>
180. But the false *Ens* is so abundant and strong that it attracts a heap of evil occasions and accidents from the outside into itself. This obscures and dims the <sup>l</sup> **Image** of God, kills the good *Ens* and **will** or **desire**, and crucifies the **image** of *Christ*. This is the **image** which *Christ*, in his breaking through, has <sup>m</sup> *sprinkled with his blood, and redeemed and delivered with his death*. The false nature crucifies this within them through sins, killing *Christ* in his **member** <note>original: "member"; meaning a part of Christ's spiritual body, the individual believer.</note>.

<margin><sup>n</sup> Matt. 22:11, 12.</margin>
181. And when <sup>n</sup> *the Father of the house comes to see the guests at the wedding* of the Lamb, he finds that this redeemed, delivered **image** of *Christ*, which is invited to the wedding, *has no wedding garment on*.

<margin><sup>o</sup> Matt. 22:13.</margin>
182. <sup>o</sup> *Then he commands the servant of his wrath to take this guest, instead of Christ, to bind him hand and foot in the essence of life, and to cast him out into the darkness, where there is weeping and wailing and gnashing of teeth*, as *Christ* says in the Gospel.

183. This evil wedding guest—though he may perhaps boast of *Christ's* name—is *not* elected to the *eternal supper* of the Lamb. Only those are elected whose soul draws *Christ* to it and who crucify and always kill the **will of sin** in the **flesh**. Thereupon *Christ* <margin><sup>p</sup> Matt. 22:14.</margin> says, <sup>p</sup> *Few are elected or chosen*.

<margin><sup>q</sup> Jer. 33:11. John 3:29.</margin>
184. For only those are elected to be the children of God in *Christ* who *obey* the voice of *Christ* within them, who—within their good spark of grace—<sup>q</sup> listen to the *voice of the bridegroom*. When *Christ* says within them, "Turn and repent; enter into the vineyard of Christ," these are the ones who *hear, receive*, and *do* this.

<margin><sup>r</sup> Note. Against that blockish and stupid Repentance.</margin>
185. <sup>r</sup> They do not just wait and expect God to fall upon the false, malignant **will** and break it with **power** to make them happy and blessed. **Reason** erroneously perverts the sayings or texts of Scripture concerning *predestination* and the *election of grace* in this way, which is contrary to all the parables and metaphors in the words of *Christ*.

It uses the metaphor of a sour tree and the parable of the wedding guest to explain that salvation requires active participation and the "wedding garment" of a transformed life.</summary>

186. <margin>*Matthew 26:26*</margin> For *Christ* says to his disciples when he offered his body for food, *Take, eat; take and drink, this is my flesh and blood.* He commanded the soul to lay hold of it and receive it.

187. <margin>*Matthew 11:28*</margin> It is likewise so in the <term>inward ground</term> <note>original: "inward Ground"; the deepest center of the human soul</note>, when he gives himself to the soul as a pledge in the light of life, he says: "*Come here to me, I will refresh you; receive me, open your desire wide toward me, and then I will enter in and be with you.*"

188. <margin>*Revelation 3:20*</margin> "*He stands before the door of the soul's <term>Ens</term> <note>original: "Ens"; a philosophical term for "being" or "essence"</note> and knocks; and that soul which opens to him, he will enter into that soul, and keep his supper with it.*"

189. His calling and knocking is his *drawing* and *willing*; but the soul also has an eternal will and an <term>abyssal</term> <note>foundational or bottomless</note> will.

190. In short, the soul is the Eternal Father's natural *fire-will*, and *Christ* is the Eternal Light's *love-will*; they stand within one another.

191. *Christ* desires to image, frame, or represent himself in the foolish creature; and so the fire-will in its own selfhood desires to image, frame, or represent itself. Whichever of them prevails is the one in which the image or representation stands.

192. <margin><unclear>...</unclear></margin> This struggle of imaging or representation goes on instantly in the "seed" <note>the initial spiritual spark of a person</note>, along with the framing of the creature. Because of the inequality of the seed and the ground in quality and disposition, many a twig or branch instantly becomes a *wild thistle* due to the conflict and enmity of the <term>tinctures</term> <note>original: "Tinctures"; the spiritual energies or qualities that define a being's nature</note>.

193. Yet from this "thistle-child," the light of nature—in which Christ dwells in the inward ground—does not withdraw itself until the will of the soul itself, in its natural light, darkens and obscures itself with the venom and poison of anger.

194. <margin><unclear>...</unclear></margin> Just as a struggle in the root of a tree ignites itself in a hostile ground or soil, causing the twig from that root to perish before it grows up;

195. <margin>*John 1:9*</margin> and then just as the *sun* comes to help the twig of the tree with its light and power or virtue <note>original: "Virtue" in the sense of inherent efficacy or strength</note> as soon as it sprouts out of the root; so also *Christ* comes to help the soul as soon as it comes out of the body or womb of the mother. He helps from the outside because of evil accidents, casualties, and circumstances.

196. <margin>*Galatians 3:27*</margin> And he has instituted a bath or *washing* <note>original: "Laver"</note> of regeneration in his *covenant* through *baptism*. In this, he shines into *infants* and little children with his *eternal sun* and works in them. He pours himself into them in his covenant to see whether their foolish essence is capable of receiving the bestowed grace.

197. <margin><unclear>...</unclear></margin> Afterward, when the soul comes to have the *use of reason*, he then draws and calls it through his revealed word *taught* from the *mouths of the children of God*. He gives himself as a pledge to the soul for the whole time of its outward life and sounds like a trumpet every day and hour, with his word and power within it. He does this to see whether the soul will stand still for him and turn away from beastly imaginations and thoughts so that he may generate it anew.

198. Just as the power and virtue of the sun in the *essence* <note>original: "Ens"</note> of wood draws itself up together in the tree and balances the property of the struggling nature, so likewise *Christ* winds himself with his power out of the inward ground without ceasing in the soul. He balances the *habits*, *dispositions*, or conditions of life so that they may not divide or tear themselves into a contrary will and enmity, and thus turn toward a false or wicked lust; it is through these false lusts that the properties of the soul introduce a poisonous fountain or source into themselves.

199. And just as the body or trunk of a tree with its branches becomes knotty and crooked because of the inward struggle of nature and the outward influence from the stars <note>original: "Constellations"; referring to the belief that celestial bodies influenced human temperament</note>, so the soul—through the opposition and disagreement of the natures of the father and the mother, and through the outward temptations or injections of the world's wickedness—brings itself into a deformed shape or figure in the presence of God.

## Chap. 8. Of God's predestinate Purpose.

200. Consequently, the *Wedding Garment* of *Baptism* is turned into a bestial mask <note>original: "vizard"</note>, within which *Election* or *Predestination* passes over it, so long as the soul wears this knotty, shrivelled, mask-like image.

201. This mask hinders the *Essence* <note>original: "Ens"</note> of Christ, so that it cannot work toward bringing forth fruit to the praise of God. For the Devil continually sows his desire into this mask, so that false, evil, young twigs grow from it—with evil, false, divisive, apostate wills. These wills bring themselves into the Devil’s will through pride and break away from *humility*, just as young twigs sprouting from the root of a tree break away from the balance <note>original: "Temperature," referring to the harmonious state of elements</note> and want to be trees themselves.

202. And once they have broken away, they exist within the constellation of the world, just like sprouts growing out of a tree. Then the configuration of the stars sifts through them by way of busy, critical, annoying, rigid, interfering, and scheming people, leading them from one design, care, and project into another.

203. Then pride, covetousness, envy, anger, lying, treachery, deceit, and everything else that rules in the world suddenly falls upon them. The young, proud twig climbs up through arts and consumes itself in all *such things*.

204. Now, if the Divine Sun shines within it and tries to help that divided twig, but finds the "fiery life" <note>the soul's own selfish intensity</note>, then that twig lifts itself up high like *Lucifer*. It claims wisdom, cleverness, and understanding for itself, and despises <note>original: "contems"</note> the simple.

205. From this come the people who are "wise" in their own *intellect* <note>original: "Reason," often used by Boehme to mean worldly logic separate from divine spirit</note>, who are full of pride and lust after their own honor. They consume themselves through the light of grace that shines in them, using it for the desires of the flesh; in this way, Christ is made to be a cover and a cloak for their knavery and wickedness.

206. All of these are false, evil twigs, upon whom predestination passes *as the harvest time approaches*.

207. For they are called in Christ’s *Spirit*; it has offered itself to them and worked with them; it has enlightened their *intellect*, but they are not born out of Christ’s Spirit, but rather out of the pleasure and luxury of the world.

208. They have only trodden Christ underfoot and *not served him at all*.

209. His name has indeed moved in their mouths, but their soul has continually turned itself toward the self-lust of the world and of the Devil. They have let Christ stand there merely to *hold the light for their wickedness* <note>original: "hold the Light or Candle to their Wickedness," an idiom meaning to assist or facilitate evil</note>.

210. These have turned themselves out of the body or trunk of the balance <note>original: "Temperature"</note> and have *not* grown up in the true sun, Christ. Thus, they are not born of God, but in the self-will of their own nature, where their fruit consists only of human fictions, inventions, and ideas.

211. And though perhaps they are high-ranking people in the world and learn many arts and languages, yet *it is all born from the vanity of nature*. All their works are, in the sight of God, like *filthy dirty rags, dung, and mire*.

212. But that soul which has its origin in good soil—whose parents have placed their will and desires in God and stand in the bonds of true *love* (that is, in the true constellation) and put their hope in God, in whom Christ is *within them*, lives, and works—from these spring and flow *streams of living waters*, as Christ says.

213. And though the corruption or ruin inherited from Adam <note>original: "Adamical Corruption"</note> is indeed in their flesh, and though an evil "constellation" <note>astrological or spiritual influence</note> often falls into the flesh as a source or fountain of *sin*, yet *Christ* remains in the inward ground of the soul within them.

214. And so, the soul is generated or *propagated* from the soul, and the body from the seed of the body.

215. And though the outward seed may be earthly, evil, and corrupt, and infected or poisoned by such a constellation, yet Christ possesses the *most corrupted* ground in the inward center. The *Essence* <note>original: "Ens"</note> of Christ is and remains in the essence of the soul regardless; the soul is conceived, generated, and born within the *Essence* of Christ.

# Of God's Predestinate Purpose. Chapter 8.

216. <margin>* John 8:47</margin> And here is what Christ says: *He who is born of God hears God's Word.* But to the proud Pharisees he says, *Therefore you do not hear, because you are not born of God;* that is, although they indeed carried his Word and Law in their mouths, yet their souls were not born or generated in the Divine <term>Ens</term> <note>original: "Ens"; a philosophical term meaning "being" or "essential substance"</note>.

217. And although they had the Light of Nature, yet it shone out of a strange, foreign fire, in which Christ did indeed shine and reflect; but they were not capable of receiving him, because their foundation was false and evil.

218. Thus a good seed is sown, and sometimes into an evil soil or field; yet the underlying ground or foundation of the seed remains good.

219. But where a false, evil grain or seed is sown into an evil soil or ground, there something similar to its own substance grows out of it.

220. And as good grain or seed must often stand in an evil ground or soil, and yet bears fruit if outward accidents do not destroy it; so likewise the seed of faith is often sown from one of the <term>Tinctures</term> <note>original: "Tinctures"; in this context, spiritual qualities or life-forces</note> in either the man or woman, while the other sows its poison into it. By this, the outward man is wild and inclined to baseness and wickedness.

221. But the inward ground is good; and even if the person does something that is evil, they quickly bewail it and are sorry for it, and enter into repentance.

222. Also, many are like this: in one part, they are poisoned and infected with the source and fountain of sin, so that they have an evil inclination and propensity in them—perhaps toward thieving, robbing, murdering, or toward unchastity, backbiting, bearing false witness, and perjury; but the other part, in Christ’s <term>Ens</term>, always draws them away from it.

223. And although one may transgress in weakness and infirmity through the snares of the devil, yet the Divine <term>Ens</term> comes to help them, if they *do not lie dead in sin*; as was the case with the thief upon the cross, Mary Magdalene, and other great sinners besides.

224. For there is indeed no man who does not have a source or fountain of sin in his flesh, proceeding from his beast-like desires.

225. Consider how a tree must grow up in strife and against an opposing will or opposition, where it meets with "dislike" on all sides: suddenly heat, suddenly cold, suddenly the wind bows it down so that it is ready to break; suddenly a malignant influence or poison falls upon it from the <term>Astrum</term> <note>original: "Astrum"; the constellations or the configuration of the stars believed to influence earthly life</note>; yet it grows up in the power and virtue of the Sun, in its inward Light-<term>Ens</term> of nature, and bears good fruit. This fruit does not have the taste and relish of the earth, but the noble Tincture has introduced itself into a good, well-tasting <term>Corpus</term> <note>original: "Corpus"; body</note>. This is how we should understand the nature of man.

226. The Divine <term>Ens</term>, which is spiritual, cannot be manifested except through the <term>Strife of Nature</term> <note>original: "Strife of Nature"; the inner tension or conflict between opposing forces through which life and consciousness emerge</note>. It sows itself together into the soulful <term>Ens</term> of the Eternal Nature and gives itself into the strife of the "separation" or "distinction" of the fire. There, it receives its light and brings itself forth out of the fire, into the power and properties of the Love-Desire.

227. In the fire of the soul, the Divine <term>Ens</term> receives properties and a will. For in God it is one, and only one entire will, which is the only Good.

228. But it is not manifested to itself in that way. Rather, it is in the fiery separation or distinction of the soul that it becomes manifested to itself, so that the power or virtue goes forth in many working virtues into a form, image, or representation. Just as a tree is made manifest in the strife with its branches and fruit, so that it is seen what lay hidden in the mystery of the tree's grain or seed.

229. Therefore, the divine power or virtue united itself to the soul of man so that they might grow up together within it, and so that it might manifest its virtue in the fiery separation, where evil and good work among one another. Thus the Spirit of God in Christ presses into the Good and works toward the producing of fruit—namely, toward the divine formation and representation.

It argues that spiritual life is realized through the inner tension between divine light and the "fire" of natural desires.</summary>

231. The fire of the soul must have the right fuel or wood if it is to give a *clear*, bright, and powerful light. For from the soul's fire, God's Spirit becomes separable, distinct, and manifest in its power within the soul's nature: just as light is *manifested* from fire, as air is manifested from fire and light, and as a subtle dew or vapor goes forth from the air. This vapor becomes substantial after it goes forth, and from it, the light draws power and virtue back into itself as its food.

<margin>x John 6:53.</margin>
232. Thereupon Christ says, *x He that eats not the flesh of the Son of Man, and drinks not his blood, has no life in him.*

233. Just as a tree cannot grow or bear fruit without the light of nature—which the sun, pressing into it, makes *living*—and just as the light of nature and the power of the sun could not be manifested and become active in the tree without the fiery "science" <note>original: "Science"; here used in the sense of an innate operating principle or knowledge.</note> from the fiery ground of nature (which is the *soul* of the tree).

234. In the same way, *Christ* cannot be manifested in *man*—even though he is indeed in man, drawing and calling him, and pressing himself into the soul—unless the soul eats the fiery *Ens* into its own nature.

<margin>* △ ♁<br>† ☿<br>+ +</margin>
235. This [divine essence] hardly enters into the proud fire [of the self], which ought to eat of the water-source or fountain of the love-life and meekness. The proud fire would rather eat of * Sulphur and † Mercury <note>In Boehme’s system, Sulphur (△ ♁) and Mercury (☿) represent the turbulent, conflicting qualities of nature before they are harmonized by divine light.</note>—that is, it prefers its own disharmony or lack of balance.

236. But if it eats of the water-source, as mentioned above, then the spirit of love and meekness—the Divine *Ens*—becomes fiery. It lays hold of the fiery root from the "three first" <note>The "three first" refers to the first three properties of eternal nature: the harsh/desire, the bitter/motion, and the anguish/fire.</note> and *transmutes* them into itself.

237. As a "tincture" <term>Tincture: In alchemy, a substance that can transform and perfect base matter; here, it refers to the transforming power of Christ's love.</term> falls upon a glowing, burning iron and turns the iron into gold, so also the soul's center (from the Father's nature) is *changed* into a love-fire. In this love-fire, Christ becomes manifested and generated, or *born*, in the soul.

238. And then out of the soul-fire, the true *Divine* air-spirit goes forth out of the fire and light, and brings forth its spiritual water out of itself and out of the light.

239. This becomes *substantial*; the power of the light eats of it, and through the desire for love, introduces itself into a holy substance—namely, into a *spiritual corporeity* <note>original: "spiritual Cor-poreity," referring to the formation of a spiritual body or "heavenly flesh" within the believer.</note>.

240. Within this substance the Holy Trinity dwells; this *substance* is the true temple of the Holy Spirit—indeed, even God in the manifestation or revelation of himself.

<margin>y John 11:38.</margin>
241. And this is what Christ meant when he said, *y That he would give us the water of eternal life, which would flow in us as a fountain of eternal life.* <note>The marginal citation John 11:38 refers to the raising of Lazarus; the quote itself is from John 4:14.</note>

242. This is done when the soul receives his Word, which is himself. Then he pours his *substantial* power (which he made manifest in our humanity) into it. That is his tincture, which changes the soul's *enmity*—born of its fiery nature—into a love-fire.

243. For there Christ stands up in the dead soul-nature and arises from the dead. The soul becomes a member of Christ's body and draws Christ to itself; indeed, it becomes wholly planted into Christ according to the nature of love.

<margin>z John 6:56.</margin>
244. Therefore Christ says, *z He that eats my flesh and drinks my blood continues in me, and I in him*; which happens in the way described above.

<margin>a John 14:27.</margin>
245. Also, *a We will come to you, and make our habitation or abode in you*; that is, the whole or universal God is manifested in this New Birth in Christ within the soul, and works or produces good divine fruit.

246. Just as the power of the sun is manifested in a tree and kindles the light in the *Ens* of the sulfur-spirit in the mercury—that is, in the *harsh*, hard property—wherein the tree grows and bears fruit.

### Of God’s Predestined Purpose. Chapter 8.

247. 250. Just as the one and only God speaks or expresses and always generates his word from and out of himself—yet the *speaking* continues within him, and he is himself the *speaking* and the spoken word.

251. And although the fallen, corrupt nature and disposition in the flesh of our earthly property *clings* to a person and assaults them, fighting against the soul, yet that *does not hurt the soul*.

252. For the soul has now overcome the wrathful, fallen, and corrupt fiery property through Christ. Christ in the soul *crushes* and treads upon the head of the serpent's poison in the flesh, and raises *himself* up within the flesh into a *new body*.

253. In the same way that precious pure gold lies and grows within a coarse, dross-filled, dirty stone—where the impurities *help the process*, even though they are nothing like the gold—so the earthly body must also help to generate Christ within itself.

254. Even though the body is *not Christ*, nor *can it be* for all eternity—and it is not useful for the Kingdom of God—it *must help* by being an instrument.

256. That is, our earthly body—which he helps to carry within us—is *his yoke* in us. The holy soul must take this upon itself with patience and suffer all *adversity* from the outside, along with the assaults and buffeting of the flesh that come from the devil and the malice and wickedness of the world.

Thus, in the midst of trouble, it grows up with Christ’s noble *Tree of Pearl* <note>a metaphor for the precious, growing spiritual life within the believer</note> despite all evil deeds. Like a true sprout or branch, it works, generates, and produces pure, good, *holy*, and heavenly fruits.

<margin>Philippians 3:20</margin>

### Chap. 8. Of God’s predestined Purpose.

263. My beloved reader, this is the true ground of the new regeneration, and not at all in the way that reason supposes: 1. That we are *outwardly* adopted and received as children of grace.

264. And 2. That we are, through a divine predestined purpose, spoken or pronounced free from sin. No! A man must be *born again* out of this previously mentioned *water and Holy Spirit*.

<margin>f Or, the soul's will.</margin>
265. The soul must turn away from its own will into the drawing of Christ, and bring its desiring will toward Christ's desire, which mightily presses toward <sup>f</sup> it and in <sup>f</sup> it. With the desire, it must enter into <sup>f</sup> it and open wide the fiery jaws—namely, the *spiritual brimstone worm* <note>original: "spiritual Brimstone Worm"; a reference to the soul's inherent, restless, and consuming hunger or drive</note> in the mercury <note>In this context, "mercury" refers to the active, moving principle of life and spirit</note> of the spirit-life. Then the Spirit of Christ presses into the essence of the soul, and that is called *faith* or <insert>{ Glauben / Believing }</insert> and receiving, or partaking.

266. Knowing, comforting, tickling, and wrapping Christ's mantle about themselves, while always speaking of grace, *free grace*, and earnestly wishing to be a child of grace while *continuing in the evil malignancy and malice of the devil—this is not to believe.*

267. Instead, one must be in spirit like a child hanging on its mother's breasts, desiring nothing else but to suck the breasts of the mother; for it is only the true "New Man" who grows in Christ's <term>Ens</term> <note>Ens: a philosophical and alchemical term for the "essence" or "spiritual substance" of a thing</note>.

268. But when reason says we are first to be born again in the resurrection, and then put on Christ in the flesh, that is *Babel* <note>Babel: a common term in this period for spiritual confusion or false, hypocritical religious systems</note>; and it is not agreeable to the words of Christ.

269. *Indeed, the body from the earth shall then, at the resurrection, first put on Christ essentially.*

270. But the soul must, in *this lifetime*, put on Christ in his heavenly flesh, and the new body must be given to it in Christ.

271. *Not from the blood of man, or from flesh, but from and out of the Word and the divine essence;* in that which was faded or extinguished regarding the divine <term>Ens</term>—which faded in *Adam* and was dull and senseless to the operation of God. In this, Christ must be born anew and become a God-man, and man must become a man-God.

272. Thus, beloved brethren, understand that, on one hand, Christ is the *divine predestined purpose* and will of grace. Whoever is born of him, and attracts and puts him on, is seen, foreseen, and elected in Christ, and is a <sup>g</sup> child of grace.

<margin>g Or, grace-child, or true gracious child of God.</margin>
273. And on the other hand, the *predestined purpose* of God is the fiery will of the soul, coming out of the center of *eternal nature*, where light and darkness separate from each other. There, one part goes into the center of darkness—namely, the coarse, illusory sulfur <note>original: "phantastical Sulphur"; likely referring to the "burning" or "combustible" nature of the lower self</note>—and the subtle, pure part goes into the light.

274. Now, into whichever "science" <note>original: "Science"; here meaning a branch of knowledge, a state of being, or a specific root of the will</note> or root of the bottomless will the nature separates itself, in *that* it is a creature, whether in the light or in the darkness.

275. The predestined purpose of God goes throughout from the *natural ground* <note>original: "foolish Ground"; here likely meaning the "simple" or "undifferentiated" foundational state of the soul</note>; for the inward ground of the soul is the divine nature to the eternally speaking Word, and is neither evil nor good.

276. But in the divisibility of the fire—that is, in the kindled fire of the soul—there that will separates or distinguishes itself either into God's anger or into God's love-fire.

277. And that happens in no other way than by the property or *disposition* that the natural essence has in itself.

278. It is itself its own ground for evil or good; for it is the center of God, where God's love and anger lie in one entire ground, unrevealed and undiscovered.

The author emphasizes that true faith requires a total turning of the soul's will toward God, distinguishing this from superficial claims of "free grace."</summary>

**279.** Therefore, this is the predestined purpose of God: that he will manifest himself through the spoken-out, formed Word. Of this Word, the soul is a **substance** <note>original: "Substance"; here meaning the essential spiritual reality</note> in the expression of its own distinctiveness. In that state, the density or impurity <note>original: "Grossness or Drossiness"</note> hardens itself in original sin—both the sin we are born with and the actual, committed, **active** abominations that leave their mark.

**280.** For there is no other "will of God" in the substance of this world except that which is manifested out of the eternal ground—appearing as fire and light, as well as darkness.

**281.** The soul is, in itself, elected to be a child of grace when it is born out of Christ from the *Divine Ens* <note>original: *Divine Ens*; a Latin term meaning "Divine Being" or "essence"</note>, which is the only predestined purpose of divine grace. It is through this essence that God's grace is manifested in the soul.

**282.** Conversely, the soul is, in itself, elected, chosen, or predestined to damnation out of the ground of its own substance, if that substance is a false or evil *Ens* <note>essence</note> in which no light can be born or generated.

**283.** God's predestined purpose regarding "hardening" <note>referring to the hardening of hearts, as in the story of Pharaoh</note> is found in its own substance—namely, the *abyssal will* <term>abyssal will</term> <note>the "Ungrund" or bottomless, unconditioned will that precedes all nature</note> directed toward nature. This manifests in every substance according to that substance's own property or condition.

**284.** That is, we may well conclude that by taking in the coarse impurities, the soul has enclosed and separated itself into the dark world or **Hell**.

**285.** For the will which is in Hell and the will which is manifested in Heaven are both one thing in the inward ground—beyond and before they are manifested. The separation or **distinction only begins** in the speaking forth or expression of the Word.

**286.** Heaven and Hell are truly within one another, like day and night; and Hell is a "ground" <note>a foundation or starting point</note> for Heaven. For God's **wrathful fire** <note>original: "Anger-Fire"</note> is a ground for the **love-fire**, namely, the light.

**287.** Therefore, dear brothers, please see: never dispute about the will of God.

**288.** **We** ourselves are God's will toward evil or good. Whichever of these is manifested in us, that is what we are—whether it be Hell or Heaven.

**289.** Our own internal Hell hardens us—that is, that specific property or quality within us. And our own internal Heaven also makes us happy and blessed, if only it can be manifested.

**290.** All the things men have disputed about for so long are merely fictions.

<margin>Matthew 28:18</margin>
**291.** **Christ** has been found: let eternal praise and thanks be given to him, as well as might, honor, and dominion, together with <gloss>b</gloss> all authority and power in Heaven and Earth.

<summary>Jacob Boehme argues that predestination is not a divine decree made from afar, but a manifestation of whether a soul's internal essence aligns with God's light or darkness. He concludes that Heaven and Hell coexist within the human will, and that human disputes over God's "will" are largely based on misunderstandings of this internal reality.</summary>

# Chapter 9

## Concerning Objections from Texts of Scripture, namely, the proper understanding of Scripture.

### *Objection*

<margin>Romans 9:21</margin>
1. <image-desc>Ornamental woodcut initial letter H decorated with floral and foliate scrollwork.</image-desc> **H**as a potter not the power to make out of one lump of clay one *vessel* for *honor* and another for *dishonor*?

### *Answer*

2. The *lump of clay* signifies and denotes the Great Mystery, *Mysterium Magnum* <note>original: *Mysterium Magnum*; a term used by the author to describe the primary source or "chaos" out of which all things were created</note>, in which the eternal God has expressed or spoken himself out through the Word.

3. Out of this single substance, two substances emerge: one into the fiery separation or distinction into *darkness* (according to the coarse dross of the impression or compaction), and the other into the *light* (according to the substance of the divine property, condition, or quality). They both come from *one source* <note>original: "one Ground"</note>.

4. Similarly, the false or wicked soul and the holy soul both come from *Adam's* soul, as if from *one lump* or clod of earth.

5. This must be understood spiritually within the *Mysterio Magno*, the Great Mystery; however, one part separates or *distinguishes* itself into light, and the other into darkness.

6. This Potter makes a *vessel* out of every separation or distinction, suited to whatever the separated or distinguished matter is useful and fit for.

7. He himself does not take a holy <term>Ens</term> <note>original: *Ens*; a philosophical term meaning a thing's being or essence</note> and then make a devil out of it.

8. As the *essence* <term>Ens</term> of the soul is, so also is the will that forms it.

9. God does not sit over the will and shape it as a potter shapes a pot; rather, he *generates* it out of its own nature or constitution.

### *Question*

<margin>Romans 9:20</margin>
10. Why then will the ungodly and wicked say, *Why have you made me this way, so that I am evil?*

### *Answer*

<margin>Psalm 18:25, 26</margin>
11. God works to *produce* a life out of everything: an evil life out of an evil *essence* <term>Ens</term>, and a good life out of a good *essence*: As it is written, *With the holy you are holy, and with the perverse you are perverse.*

12. Therefore, no one can blame God for having produced an evil life within them.

<margin>Romans 9:21</margin>
13. Had the clay been better, he would have made a *vessel of honor* out of it.

14. But if it serves for *dishonor*, then he makes a *vessel of his anger* out of it.

15. For *God's Word* is the life, substance, and beginning of everything.

<margin>Or, which will give it substance.</margin>
16. But since zealous or jealous anger is also present within it, that anger also introduces itself into a life; *who shall prevent it?*

<meta>catchword: Substance</meta>

<summary>This page addresses the theological problem of predestination and the nature of evil using the metaphor of the potter and the clay. It argues that while all souls come from one source, their eventual nature (holy or wicked) depends on their internal essence and the way they distinguish themselves into light or darkness.</summary>

17. But Christ has come forth from the Eternal Word to help and save Man, and he says: *As I live, I do not desire the death of a sinner, but that he convert and live.*

18. However, if the soul's <term>Ens</term> <note>original: "Ens"—the inner essence or spiritual substance of a thing.</note> is so evil, stubborn, and incapable of receiving the Divine essence, what *can* Christ do? Is Christ at fault?

<margin>Matthew 28:18.</margin>

<margin>Romans 9:21.</margin>
24. Therefore Paul says: *Does not the potter have power and might to make what he will?* This "Potter" is God in the speaking of his <term>Separability</term> <note>Separability: The process by which the unified God differentiates Himself into various distinct qualities or "distinctions."</note>, through which he manifests his glory, as has been sufficiently confirmed before.

25. Since Christ alone has all power, *therefore* there can be no other will involved in creation outside or beyond him.

26. Therefore, the wicked *should not dare to say*, "God makes me evil." Rather, the "God in him"—the <term>Ground</term> <note>Ground: The foundational source or underlying reality of the soul's being.</note> on which he stands—makes him into whatever he is capable of serving as, according to the greatest possibility.

27. The <term>Ground</term> of the wicked soul’s own substance, from which it originates, is the beginning. As soon as life is generated out of it, the "Maker" is suddenly present in that life—specifically, the angry side of God manifested within him, who makes and frames that life.

28. Just as Christ works in his children, introducing *his* willing into those who are born *in him*, so does God's Anger work within itself with its own children, who are *born or generated out of it*.

29. For in the soul, God is manifested either in Love or in Anger.

30. Nature is the soul, and the working or acting life is God himself—understood according to the "Word of Separability."

31. For the mere pure God, outside and beyond the creature, is *not* a maker of individual wills, for he is only ONE.

32. But in his Word, where he introduces himself into <term>Separability</term>, the will toward both evil and good arises. From every distinction of that which is separated, a will arises according to its own property and condition. Into whatever quality, condition, or source the <term>abyssal will</term> <note>Abyssal Will: The primal, bottomless will of God that precedes all created things.</note> has introduced itself in that separation, such a will exists.

33. But because *Adam* brought himself out of the <term>Temperature</term> <note>Temperature: A state of perfect balance or harmony between opposing spiritual forces.</note> and into <term>Separability</term>, his descendants exist in that same condition.

34. And from that comes a *new* making will; every <term>Ens</term> gets a will according to its substance.

35. But yet the <term>predestinate purpose</term> <note>Predestinate Purpose: The eternal plan or design of God.</note> manages the government—namely, the "Fiery-Word" of Nature and the "Love-Word" of Grace. Both of these are the makers of "vessels" to honor and to dishonor, and *both* of these are within Man.

# The Highest Gate.

## Of Cain and Abel: Also of Ishmael and Isaac, and of Esau and Jacob.

36. The Kingdom of Nature is the foundation of the speaking Word; for if a creature is to exist, then nature must exist beforehand. Therefore, the Word of God is now the foundation of all substances and the beginning of all properties, qualities, or conditions.

37. The Word is God's speaking and remains in *God*; but the expression—that is, the *exit* <note>original: "exit" (the departure or going forth)</note> from the Word, wherein the abyssal <note>original: "abyssal" (referring to the *Ungrund*, the infinite or bottomless source of being in the author's theology)</note> Will introduces itself into separability <note>the state of being distinct or individual</note> through the expression—that is Nature and property, as well as its own self-will.

37. For the abyssal Will separates itself by the speaking, and forms or compacts <note>solidifies into a tangible form</note> itself into its own self-speaking within separability or distinction—namely, into a beginning or commencing will derived from the only eternal, total, *universal* Will. From this, the properties came into existence, and out of those properties, the creation—namely, all creatures—*exists*.

39. This is now the *first* predetermined purpose of God, in which the Word of Power has projected from itself for its own sake; that is, it has placed the abyssal, incomprehensible Word of Life into a *comprehensibility* <note>a state that can be grasped, perceived, or contained</note> in which it lives.

40. This *comprehensibility* is Nature; and the *incomprehensible Life* within Nature is God's Eternal speaking Word, which remains in God and is God himself.

41. The *second* predetermined purpose of the Word is this: that the comprehensibility or compaction—namely, the self-contained or solidified will—shall allow the incomprehensible, one only Will of God to *dwell* within it.

42. And therefore, the one only Life has put itself into comprehensibility or compaction and will be manifested within that comprehensibility.

43. The comprehensibility should contain and compact the incomprehensible Life within itself and make it tangible; a person has an example of this in fire and light.

44. The fire is Nature—namely, the tangible or compacted life—and it contains within itself the life that is *beyond nature*—namely, the Light.

45. For in the light, the powers of the beyond-natural life are manifested through the fire; then the light dwells in the fire, and the beyond-natural life in the light is introduced into *power*—namely, into the tincture <note>original: "tincture" (an alchemical and mystical term for the spiritual essence or inner life-force that infuses matter)</note>, air, and water.

46. You must also understand that God's *holy* life would not be manifested without Nature, but would remain only in an eternal stillness where nothing can exist without the expression or <margin>* Generating out of itself.</margin> out-speaking; and then the <margin>** Formation.</margin> comprehensibility or compaction—God's holiness and love—would *not* be manifested.

47. Now, if it is to be manifested or exist, then there must be something that has need of the love and grace—something that is *not like* the love and grace.

48. And that is the will of Nature, which in its own life stands in opposition and contrariety or *adversity*; it has need of the love and grace so that its pain may be changed into joy.

49. And in that *change* or *transmutation*, the holy, incomprehensible Life is *manifested* in the Word as a co-working Life within Nature.

50. For the painfulness of Nature causes the *Will* of the *Abyss* <note>The "Abyss" here refers to the infinite, bottomless void or the pre-manifest state of God.</note>—which in the "outspeaking" <note>The manifestation or expression of the Divine Word.</note> has separated itself into a *self-centered singularity*—to unite itself again to the holy, abyssal Life, so that it may be softened, calmed, and mitigated.

51. And in this calming or mitigating, it is manifested in the *Life of God*; for Nature takes that Life into its own desire, and so the holy Life of the Abyss is revealed within it.

52. In this manifestation of the holy Life within Nature, the holy Life is called *Power* or *Virtue*.

53. And the "comprehensibility" <note>The state of being graspable or material.</note> of Nature, which takes hold of this Life, is called *Tincture* <note>original: "Tincture," a spiritual essence or quality that transforms and illuminates whatever it touches.</note>; for it is the power of the flash of the fire and light.

54. If this were not so, then no fire could shine.

55. For this comprehensibility or denseness is a shutting-in and is the foundation of *Darkness*. Thus, we <sup>x</sup> introduce our deep foundation regarding *Adam*, and further <sup>y</sup> regarding *Cain* and *Abel*.

## Of Cain and Abel.

56. In *Adam* stood the Kingdom of *Grace*—that is, the revealed Divine Life; for he existed in the "temperature" <note>original: "Temperature," meaning a state of perfect balance or harmony where no single quality dominates others.</note> of all properties.

57. But he did not *know* that God was manifested in him, for he had known no evil. Therefore, his own self-will did not know what "good" was.

58. For *how* could there be joy when there was no knowledge of pain or sorrow?

59. For this is what joy is: when Nature (the self-will) is delivered and released from pain, it then rejoices at the good that happens to it.

60. But if that good were within its *own* power and might to achieve, then there would be no *joy*; for the self-will would live however it pleased. It would have *no hope* toward anything if it were able to get everything for itself by its own might and strength.

61. But if it cannot do it itself, *then* it rejoices at what happens to it out of Grace, or at what it *hopes* will happen to it.

62. All joy exists in the *hope of Grace*, which always happens without the strength of one's own *ability* to obtain it.

63. And *therefore* Nature exists in pain and struggle so that the Kingdom of Grace and Love might be manifested in it, and so that it might become a Kingdom of Joy based on what continually *happens* to it.

64. In this, God's Life is manifested in Nature, and Nature thereby obtains a holy Tincture, which transforms the pain and changes it into joy—that is, into an image or resemblance of the holy Life.

65. When *Adam* stood in that equal harmony or likeness, he *did not know* it; he did not know what the evil in Nature was, and so he also knew nothing of the Kingdom of Grace, for both of these were held in *balance*.

<margin>* That is, in the mentioned Will.</margin>
66. But when the free will introduced itself into the "separability" or *distinction* of the Word of Power, then the painfulness of the Kingdom of Nature was manifested <sup>*</sup> within it.

67. Therefore, it was now necessary that the power of Grace should also move within it. The Kingdom of Nature could *not* do this on its own, for there is no such possibility within its own will.

68. For Nature itself is "comprehensible" <note>graspable or physical</note>, but the Kingdom of Grace is "incomprehensible" <note>beyond physical grasp; spiritual</note>; and therefore the soul—that is, the graspable will—can receive *nothing* from the incomprehensible Life on its own.

73. And nature, currently hungering for grace, allowed itself to be comprehended—or bound together—into an image of the natural soul and the body.

74. And that image was *Abel*, a figure in the image and likeness of *Christ*.

75. <margin>Galatians 4:4</margin> This continued until *the fullness of time*, until that incomprehensibility of love moved itself and compressed itself into an *ens* <term>Ens: A philosophical term for "being" or "essence."</term> of a substance in human property, so that the deity itself was a substance within the human substance.

76. This *substance* indeed lay within *Adam* before, but he did not know it.

77. And when he led himself—by the self-will of nature—*out* from this *substance*, the soul became blind to God and lived only in itself.

78. Now, if we choose to see and not make ourselves blind, we may distinguish between *Cain* and *Abel*.

79. *Cain* must be the first, for he is *Adam's* image after the Fall; for *Adam* was created in the kingdom of God.

80. *Cain* represents the kingdom of nature—that is <note>original: "viz." (videlicet) means "namely" or "that is to say."</note>, a true image of what *Adam* was in himself without grace.

81. And *Abel* is the image of what *Adam* was in the newly-spoken grace; this represents *Christ*, who would give himself into human nature and speak or inspire grace into the perished, corrupted nature in *Cain's* image.

82. <margin>Matthew 28:18</margin> Therefore *Christ* said, > "*All power was given to him by his Father*"; so that he had the power to speak grace into the will of nature.

83. Therefore, God now presents the figure in *Cain* and *Abel*, as well as in *Ishmael* and *Isaac*, and in *Jacob* and *Esau*, signifying that God would send *Christ* into the flesh. God had already spoken him into *Adam* and *Eve* through the power of his Word, as a fountain of life.

84. He would fulfill this power with human substance, which was accomplished in *Christ*. To this *Man-Christ*, in that power and voice, might and power were given to overthrow sin through his own voice and to make nature within it live again a divine life.

85. Yet for this to be done, grace—in the power of love—had to give itself into the opposition and contrariety of painful nature and into its own will, so that it might bind nature together.

86. And through this impression into high love, nature was transmuted into the divine love-will and died to its own established <note>original: "impressed" here refers to a state that has been fixed or solidified</note> will.

87. This was not a death in the sense of dying, but a *losing* of one’s own self-will, which was accomplished in *Christ* in our humanity.

88. Now, when the self-will loses its perceived right, then the spoken Word becomes substantial. 93. But how did it happen that *Cain* did *not* rule over it? Could he not?

### Answer.

No: He could not.

### Question.

94. Why could he not? *Had God hardened him so that he could not?*

### Answer.

95. God *had not hardened him*. 96. For the predestined purpose of God, according to His wrathful nature, had compressed itself within *Cain* and made him *deaf* or *dead*, so that he could not hear the voice of the incorporated grace.

97. For though he heard it externally, from the outside, he did not hear it in the essence <note>original: Ens</note> of the soul; otherwise, Grace would have moved itself so that the soul would have ruled over the serpent's poison.

98. He (*Cain*) supposed he should and would *externally* rule over *sin*, and therefore he rose up against *Abel*.

100. *This* will be as effective as it was for *Cain*, unless the inward ground is awakened or stirred so that Grace becomes active in the soul—namely, the incorporated voice of God in the "seed of the woman," which is *Christ in us*; so that the soul hears the voice of God stirring in its essence.

# Chapter 9: On the Right Understanding of Scripture.

...have authority to prevail over you: For if he had moved the inward ground of the soul in the voice of the incorporated grace, then he would have heard it inwardly in the soul, which is lord of the body, and then the outward ground could not have raised itself up.

->Answer.<-

102. This voice which was effectively spoken to Cain, saying, *Rule over sin, and let it not have dominion or authority over you*, was God’s *righteousness* in his predestined purpose—namely, in the speaking Word. In this Word, the Divine voice wills that the personal will of the insight <note>original: "Science," meaning the soul's creative or cognitive power</note>, or root of the abyssal eternal will, should introduce itself into a divine generating of what is good.

103. This Word requires God’s righteousness to be performed, so that the will should not incline toward evil; this is the true ground of the *Law* in the Old Testament.

104. But it does *not* attain grace, for it requires one's own personal ability.

105. Neither does it give itself up into grace, for *God needs no grace*.

106. Grace must give itself up into him—namely, into God’s righteousness.

107. As indeed, grace, which was manifested in Christ—namely, in the incorporated voice of grace—must give itself up into God’s righteousness, namely, into the eternal, single, predestined purpose. This is for the manifestation of the *glory* of God in his speaking Word—that is, in the distinctness <note>The author refers to the way the Father's will is distinguished or expressed</note> of the Father.

108. And it must bring the *will of man* (which had departed from the predestined purpose of righteousness) into the *fire of God's anger*, in itself and with itself. It must bring it to the Father—that is, to the predestined purpose of God in his righteousness, namely, in the origin of the soul.

109. And it must drown the soul’s will (which had departed from righteousness) in his blood, out of the divine, holy essence <note>original: "Ens"</note> of love, so that the soul might be manifested in grace, in that love-blood, in the predestined purpose of righteousness.

110. And *therefore* Christ had to *suffer and die* in us, in the righteousness of God in our humanity, so that grace might be manifested in righteousness.

111. For in *Cain*, grace was not manifested in the righteousness of God, for it had not yet taken any soul into itself, until the grace in Christ took the soul to itself.

112. Therefore, righteousness now lay in the soul, for it was God’s image.

113. Therefore God requires *righteousness* from the soul, so that it should rule over sin.

114. <margin>f Or rejected.</margin> Just as God ruled over the apostate <note>rebellious</note> will of the devils and <margin>g Reject.</margin> cast it out from the good order or decree of righteousness when they became apostate, so must Cain here also cast away from him the source or fountain of *sin*.

115. But it was *not possible* for him to do it, for sin had taken hold of him—namely, the free will. Human ability was lost.

116. <margin>h Note: The will of the soul must stand still and hear what the Lord says.</margin> And it rested now in the second predestined purpose of the righteousness spoken within the *grace*, that the soul gives its will up into it and *stands still* to hear what is spoken within.

117. For in the speaking of the righteousness of God, there was now in the soul nothing but necessity and *adversity*, or an opposing will.

118. For righteousness requires harmony <note>original: "Temperature," referring to the perfect balance of qualities</note>, namely, to stand still before God as his instrument, through which God would manifest his voice.

119. But now the instrument was broken and had departed from the divine harmony. Therefore, it now depended no longer on Cain’s *willing, going, or running*, but on grace—namely, on mercy and compassion.

# Of the right understanding of the Scripture. Chapter 9.

<margin>Romans 9:18.</margin>
120. According to this, St. *Paul* says, *He has mercy or compassion on whom he will, and he hardens whom he will.*

121. In this lies the whole ground of error in human reason; it does not understand how the "Will of Grace" is produced.

122. For that which wills the Grace is also one and the same Will as the Grace itself; for Grace has no will in the Devil, nor in Hell, but only in that which is born of God.

123. The willing of Grace is not found in the desires of flesh and blood, nor in the will of man’s own self-centered seed, but in the Divine *Ens* <note>original: "Ens"; referring to the essential being or spiritual substance of a thing</note>.

124. Grace will not speak into <note>original: "inspeak"; to manifest or breathe life into</note> the "serpent’s seed" introduced into *Cain*, but will tread upon and crush its head.

125. It would not crush or tread upon the head of the poor captive soul in *Cain*, for that soul also sprang from *Adam’s* soul; rather, it would tread upon the serpent’s seed within *Cain’s* soul.

126. But the serpent’s poison had so taken hold of the soul and hardened it that the soul surrendered itself to the *Anger* of Divine Righteousness. That Anger then took the soul and used it as an instrument, which Righteousness—acting within Grace—used to kill the Man *Christ*, namely in his *Type* <note>original: "Type"; a figure or person who foreshadows a later reality, such as Abel prefiguring Christ</note> in *Abel*.

127. For just as sin entered the soul through human works, so must it be slain by human works within the Grace of God's Righteousness—namely, in the humanity of *Christ* through manslaughter, as was done by the *Pharisees*, who held and managed the Law of God's Righteousness.

128. Therefore, *Abel* (the type of *Christ*) and also *Christ* himself had to die to their own Adam-like will within God’s Righteousness through human actions.

129. And those whom God’s Righteousness, in the wrath of his eternal plan <note>original: "predestinate purpose"</note>, had captured, had to be instruments to do it. This was so that the Grace of God—within the Righteousness of the eternal plan in the Anger—might be revealed.

<margin>Matthew 18:7.</margin>
130. For it is written, *Woe to that man by whom offenses come; yet there must be offenses, so that Righteousness and Truth might be made manifest together in the midst of untruth.*

131. For otherwise, Grace would not be revealed if falsehood and evil were not there in opposition to the Truth.

132. Just as Free Will could not have been revealed in Grace if Righteousness had not slain it, so Grace made it living in itself after it lost its self-chosen will. Thus, it no longer willed or lived for itself, but Grace lived and willed within it—which was revealed in *Christ*.

133. Therefore, we are all but one in *Christ* in the life of Grace; for we have lost the natural life of God’s Righteousness in his eternal plan and have obtained sonship <note>original: "filiation"; the state of being a child of God</note> in Grace.

<margin>1 Timothy 2:4.</margin>
134. Therefore the Scripture says, *God wills that all men should be helped or saved*; that is, Grace wills this. It can will nothing else but mercy and compassion, for it is nothing else in its own substance.

135. But natural Righteousness, in the eternal plan of God, requires the soul to remain in obedience to the Divine Ordinance *without* the Grace; for the soul was not created in Grace, but in the Ordinance—the first institution or constitution of things.

136. And if Righteousness does not find the soul in that obedience, then it takes the soul into its own property of separation or distinction of the Word, from which the soul's substance is made.

137. That is, if the soul is an evil *Ens* <note>essential being</note>, then it attracts what is like itself. This is how we should understand *Cain*: that the fallen, apostate Adam-like will has turned itself into a self-centered creaturely existence.

# Chapter 9. Of the right understanding of the Scripture.

138. And that introduction of the soul’s *essence* <note>original: *Ens*</note> into the serpent’s poison is a *thistle*, which is not capable of receiving grace.

<margin>Hebrews 6:6</margin>
139. For although the spoken voice of grace lies within the inner foundation, that essence grows into a thistle; it crucifies Christ within itself and is guilty of his death.

140. Just as the *essence* <note>original: *Ens*</note> of the sun must allow itself to be present in the thistle, yet the sun withdraws its *goodwill* or influence from it—namely, the holy life, which it manifests in a good plant—and lets the thistle make of its essence what it will.

<margin>Job 18:6</margin>
141. Thus it also goes with the wicked thistle-essence of man, as the Scripture says: *He lets their light go out in the midst of darkness*; that is, the holy life within the voice of the implanted grace.

->Question.<-

142. You will say: "Why is it so? If he would manifest the holy life in them, then the soul would be holy."

->Answer.<-

143. No. We have an example of that in the devil, in whom the holy life was manifested, but the essence of his will was a *thistle*. Likewise, a child of the thistle uses *grace* only for pride, just as Lucifer did.

144. For God knows the internal nature <note>original: science</note> or root of the abyss—how it has formed or manifested itself in its own foundation <note>original: ground</note>. He knows whether it is a root out of the darkness (namely, out of the dark fire-life) or a root out of the bright, shining fire-life.

->Question.<-

145. But you will say: "Is Cain a root out of the dark fire, and therefore cannot attain grace?"

->Answer.<-

146. No; for he came from Adam’s soul. However, the dark fire from anger—the property of the dark world—had forced or crowded itself into the true soul.

147. This did not happen from the outside, but rose up from the center; it came from the *Fall* of Adam, and Cain proceeded from that root.

148. Therefore, he had to be a servant of God’s righteousness, with which that righteousness *slew* the free will in Abel through grace.

149. In Adam’s soul, the properties divided or distinguished themselves. By these properties, understand the soulful *will* which was manifested in the *one and only* soul at the beginning of God’s image, according to God’s predetermined purpose.

150. This was a free will, but it was *poisoned* so that it was blind to God; this same will now separates itself in the death of its self-centeredness.

<margin>Genesis 2:17</margin>
151. For God said: *You must surely die if you eat of evil and good.*

152. And that soul entered into death, and God spoke his voice into that death, so that the original will might live again in *grace*; and from this came Abel.

153. The other will, reborn in *sin*—which did not exist in the beginning but arose during the Fall—separates itself into the natural life; and that was Cain.

154. Therefore, this will was a thistle-child, which God had not created; rather, it emerged from the center of the soul.

155. After the one and only soul left its state of balance <note>original: temperature</note>, so that the dark foundation was revealed within it, darkness entered a will in the soul that *was not there in the beginning*.

156. Regarding the substance of the soul, they both (Abel and Cain) came from one essence; but regarding their *will*, they separated from each other.

<summary>This page explores the spiritual origins of Cain and Abel, explaining that while both came from Adam's soul, they represent two different "wills" or essences—one aligned with grace and the other with the dark "thistle" of the Fall.</summary>

# Of the right understanding of the Scripture. Chapter 9.

157. It is not that **Abel** was born pure and without sin; for sin clung to him within the "will of death."

158. This was not a final death; rather, the Voice of Grace *killed* his sinful nature so that it might make him alive within *Grace*.

<margin>Romans 7:25</margin>
159. But in the flesh, the will toward sin was revealed. Therefore, the righteousness of God killed him through **Cain**; for Abel also <gloss>according to the flesh, was subject to the law of sin</gloss>.

160. However, the Voice of Grace had killed the selfish will of the soul and made that soul alive within *itself*. Therefore, Abel was a "type" of Christ <note>original: "Christ’s Type" — a person or event in the Old Testament seen as a symbolic precursor to Christ</note> and stood in the image of Christ.

161. This, therefore, is the true reason for **Cain's** hardening: It was not because God hardened him by His own will—for that is impossible, as God is *only good*. Instead, the newly arisen will, coming from the center of the soul, *hardened itself* through its own desire.

<margin>The desire of the new, false will that had arisen.</margin>
162. That is, the <gloss>desire</gloss> within the wrath of nature entered into its own likeness. Thus, it was found within the predetermined purpose of nature—namely, in the separation or distinction between darkness and light. It found, I say, its own *likeness*, which consumed and possessed it. Understand this as the newly arisen false will, which was a *murderer* and a servant of divine wrath.

163. But the true soul—originally created and formed out of **Adam's** essence, where the imprinted and modeled Voice of God lay—was *not yet* judged or predestined to damnation. Human reason errs in its assumptions on this matter; such judgment belongs to the righteousness of God, not to man.

164. Nor is it at all as some suppose—as if **Cain** were born or generated from the Devil's will and the "seed of the serpent." He was born from **Adam's** soul and body, yet the fallen natural will that **Adam** had received *ruled* him.

165. He was an image of the fallen, unregenerated <note>original: "unregenerated" — not yet spiritually reborn or renewed by grace</note> **Adam**, in whom the *Promise* and the "spoken-in" Divine Voice remained. However, it was without an active or working life; it was merely a true *possibility* for the New Birth.

166. But that *possibility* did *not* reside in **Cain's power**, as far as his false will was concerned. Instead, it lay deep in the foundation of the soul and waited for the Voice of Christ.

<margin>Luke 23:43</margin>
167. That Voice awakened itself within that possibility through the highly precious and dear name **JESUS**, receiving poor sinners into Grace. With its voice, it called out to those trapped in sin and awakened the dormant foundation of God's first "speaking-in" to humanity—just as was done <gloss>to the thief or criminal upon the Cross</gloss> and many others.

168. For *if it were true* that God, in His predetermined and purposeful will, had hardened **Cain**, then no *judgment* from the righteousness of God could have passed upon **Cain**, nor could any *curse* have entered him.

169. For whatever God's predetermined purpose creates, the righteousness of God does *not* curse—yet Cain was cursed.

170. For righteousness is the governing law <note>original: "Ordinance"</note> of the Word spoken at the beginning. All things remain within that law or order as the "speaking" brought them into life. Whatever continues to stand in the order in which it was created does not face judgment.

171. So now, if any will arising from God's predetermined purpose—understand, from the *Divine* predetermined purpose—had hardened **Adam** and **Cain**, then Righteousness would have had no cause to speak against or contradict them. This is because the will that caused the hardening would have been part of the Divine law or order.

172. Therefore, it must be that the will toward hardening in **Adam** and **Cain** arose from the disharmony <note>original: "unlike Discord"</note> of the various conflicting properties <note>original: "Properties" — Böhme's term for the fundamental spiritual forces or attributes of being</note> within them. This occurred when each property solidified itself into substance and obscured, dimmed, and *killed* the Image of God within the Light.

<summary>This page argues that Cain's "hardening" was a result of his own soul's false will and the disharmony of nature's properties, rather than a direct act of predestination by a purely good God. It emphasizes that every fallen human, including Cain, retains a dormant "possibility" for spiritual rebirth through the Voice of Christ.</summary>

### Chapter 9: On the right understanding of the Scripture.

173. God's predestined purpose is the center of the human ground or foundation, which is the **Word of God**; and that same compacted human will rightly becomes **hardened** in that predestined purpose of God, just as the Scripture says.

->**The Word of God**<-

| **Jesus** | **Nature** |
| :--- | :--- |

174. But no one wants to understand the foundation <note>original: "Ground"</note>. People only say that God's predestined purpose does it, and no one will search for the *foundation* of that purpose; for it lies within man himself, *and not in God*.

175. If God had intended to have a devil, that very predestined purpose would have been the *will* of the devil.

176. But in the separability or distinction of the Speaking, the predestined purpose toward evil or malice entered into a principle; it manifested itself in the compacted separability or distinction *out of the Great Mystery* <note>original: ex Mysterio magno</note>, according to which God calls himself an angry God.

177. And yet it is not God, but the *center of nature*—namely, *the cause of the divine manifestation to the Kingdom of Joy*; for in God no anger is *manifested*, but only a burning love.

<margin>Psalm 5</margin>
178. For if there were in God a will to harden hearts, then those sayings would not be true which say, *You are not a God who is pleased with wicked deeds*. Also, *As surely as I live, I do not desire the death of a sinner*; nor would the *Ten Commandments*, which forbid evil, be true.

<margin>* Otherwise the sixth commandment.</margin>
179. If God had willed it so that *Cain* should slay *Abel*, then the *fifth commandment* <note>Boehme likely refers to "Thou shalt not kill," which is the sixth commandment in most modern Protestant traditions but the fifth in the Lutheran tradition he followed.</note> would not have been right.

180. And then God would have placed a heavy reproach upon *Cain*, saying, *Whoever sheds human blood, by humans shall his blood be shed in return*.

181. If he willed it to be so, then no one ought to keep his commandments; and then where would his righteousness be, and the judgment in and according to the *truth*?

<margin>* Hosea 13:4</margin>
182. The Scripture says, *O Israel! Your destruction is from yourself*.

183. Now, therefore, we should condemn nothing but the abominations and sins which appear manifest in the wicked; and those proceed from the Cain-like and Adam-like <note>original: Adamical</note> *self-will*, out of the center of the dark world.

184. This will was not something God manifested or generated in humanity in the beginning; rather, the devil is *guilty* of that.

185. It is this false or evil will—in its substance, matters, and actions—that we must condemn, and not the poor soul which lies hidden in this hard prison, within the voice of the spoken-in *grace*.

186. This voice of grace, which was first instilled <note>original: incorporating</note> in Paradise after the Fall, may well be awakened by Christ's voice through, or in, his children in whom the Spirit dwells.

<margin>* 1 Timothy 1:15 & 4:9, 10</margin>
187. This was done for the poor tax collector <note>original: Publican</note>; also for the criminal <note>original: Malefactor</note> on the cross; also for *Mary Magdalene*, and many hundreds of thousands of poor captive souls. For the Scripture says, *It is a most highly precious and worthy word, that Jesus Christ has come into the world to save all poor sinners*.

<margin>* Revelation 3:20</margin>
<margin>* Matthew 11:28</margin>
188. And in Revelation it says: *He stands before the door and knocks*, namely, before the door of the poor captive soul; and he says, *Come to me all you who are weary and heavily burdened with sin, and I will refresh you or give you life* <note>original: quicken you</note>.

189. He stands in the inward foundation of grace spoken into *Adam* in the center of the soul, and calls to it as long as the soul *remains* in the body upon the earth, to see whether the poor soul will turn toward him.

<margin>* Matthew 7:7</margin>
190. And then, when it happens that they turn to him, he says, *Knock and it shall be opened to you*: Knock at the instilled first voice of grace, and then it will move...

Understand this as the divided properties of nature.

204. "I have heard your affliction, you poor captive soul, in this wilderness. Turn back. You are indeed pregnant with a scorner born of the kingdom of nature and the influence of the stars, and you will bring him forth."

214. Therefore, Nature shall *not vanish and pass away*; rather, only the *false will*—which has arisen from itself out of disharmony or discord—shall be cast out and die. We see a representation of this here.

<margin>Gen. xvi. 13, 14.</margin>

217. This means the poor soul said: "I had run away from the Free-Woman—the harmony of God’s Kingdom—and was blind toward God. But now I have seen Him who has looked upon me in my suffering with His gaze <note>original: "Inspection or Aspect"</note> of grace."

218. That is, He looked back into me, whereas I was blind to the sight of God. This is called "looking back after me" because the Kingdom of Nature—possessing a new, selfish will—had already become a Scorner.

<margin>Gen. xvi. 14.</margin>

221. This is the Fountain of Him who lives, who looked upon the poor soul after the Fall, and who looked upon *Hagar* and *Ishmael* while he was still in his mother’s womb.

222. For it was shown to the "Scorner"—the divided or distinct properties of nature—namely, to that same scornful will, that it would arise out of the Kingdom of Nature, which the poor soul must endure in its prison and blindness.

224. But God would bring forth from it—that is, from the inward essence where grace had established itself—twelve princes whose descendants would be beyond counting.

225. Yet outwardly, Nature was to be governed by twelve princes of the fallen, corrupted natural realm, as indeed twelve princes were born from him. Therefore, the Spirit of God through *Moses* hints at this inward essence, as is clearly evident to us.

226. For when *Ishmael* was born, his outward nature—belonging to the fallen and corrupted Kingdom of Nature—was a Scorner, whom God commanded to be cast out.

244. Indeed, it is very right that the *outward* Ishmael—representing the scornful will—should be condemned. 248. Now, *Ishmael* originated from the image of God’s righteousness which he created in *Adam*.

## Of Jacob and Esau.

251. The figure of *Jacob* and *Esau* serves as a representation showing how *Christ* would be cast out from the kingdom of nature by its own innate, false, and evil will.

<margin>John 18:36</margin>
252. For when he had taken our sins upon himself in the nature of Adam—meaning the fountain or source from which sin flows, the divided qualities of life in human nature—he nevertheless said, * "My kingdom is not of this world." That is, his kingdom is not within the divided four elements, but in the "temperature" <note>original: "Temperature"; a state of perfect balance and harmony, as opposed to the conflict of the four elements</note>.

253. But because Christ had assumed humanity in its divided properties, the righteousness of the *outward world's order* would not tolerate him. He had grown from a different kind of righteousness—a heavenly one—and entered our poor humanity in this world’s state to save us.

<margin>Matthew 8:20; Luke 9:58. * Matthew 28:18.</margin>
254. Therefore he says, "The Son of Man has nowhere to lay his head"; and yet he also says, "All power in heaven and on earth has been given to me by my Father."

255. By this, he means the inward foundation of all things—eternity—which lies hidden within this world and is revealed in Christ.

256. That same revelation was *not* "at home" in this world and possessed nothing of this world as its own property.

257. The figure illustrating how Christ would be forced out of this world was *Jacob*. His brother *Esau*—representing the kingdom of the outward world's righteousness—always wanted to kill him. Just as *Jacob* had to flee from *Esau*, so did Christ flee from the righteousness of the Pharisees in the kingdom of nature, until *Jacob* returned from *Laban* with his gifts and surrendered himself to *Esau*, leaving it to him whether to kill him or let him live.

<margin>Ishmael and Esau.</margin>

**294.** For Christ should be manifested in the righteousness of God's anger, so that it might be *known* what *Grace* was.

**295.** *Adam* stood *both* in God's grace and in His anger in the <term>Temperature</term> <note>original: "Temperature"; refers to a state of perfect harmony or balance between opposing forces</note>, and neither of them was manifested in his life, for they stood in *equal* or like weight.

**298.** For a thing that stands in equal balance or like weight has no movement or desire toward anything; it is one, and is of itself.
