### Question.

352. *You will say, "Why does God follow such a course, way, or process? Might God not have left the Jewel to Adam, who held it by the right of nature—that is, the right of the firstborn—in the Word of the predestined purpose of God within the divine image or representation?"*

### Answer.

353. No.

### Question.

354. Why?

### Answer.

355. Because then the Jewel, being in the highest love of God in man (namely, in the image of God), would have remained *hidden*.

356. Therefore, it had to be manifested through such a course, way, or process in the regeneration <note>rebirth or spiritual renewal</note>.

I. So that the love and grace of God might be *known* and manifested or revealed in man.

II. So that man might have a *reason* to love God and to exalt His praise through grace.

357. This exaltation is a purely divine forming and begetting within the wisdom of God, where the *Word* of God is also born in man. In this way, man also "generates" God, so that he becomes a substantial God—namely, a harmony of the divine kingdom of joy.

358. For when Christ surrendered the Jewel of God's righteousness into the hatred, then the anger transformed itself into a highly *triumphing* kingdom of joy, and the praise of God was revealed.

359. This could not happen in *Adam* when he stood in the "temperature" <note>original: "Temperature"; a state of perfect balance between the divine properties before the Fall</note>. For the wrath now rejoices that it has been turned from enmity into a fire of love.

360. And this is now the *resurrection* of Christ and of his children, whom he turns into a love-fire through this process. So, when the soul allows itself to be *drawn* when Christ calls from within, it must then give itself up to him.

361. Then Christ rises up within the anger-fire and changes it into the divine kingdom of joy in the praise of God.

362. Therefore, dear brother, please understand *how God has hated Esau*. Although, indeed, it is not God Himself, but God's predestined purpose—namely, the *righteousness* in the separable "science" <note>original: "Science"; the divine knowledge or root from which all things differentiate and are known</note> or root—that hated this image, because it was not the original, right image that was first created.

# Of the Right Understanding of the Scripture. Chapter 9.

362. ...created in righteousness; for the jewel—that is, the *essence* <note>original: *Ens*</note> of divine love—was extinguished or lost within it, and Jacob possessed that.

363. Therefore, God’s predestined purpose "hated" this image of Esau because it was not the first image born of love, but rather of anger. Esau himself was the image of that hatred.

364. For it is not God—in His essence as Love—who can hate; rather, it is the predestined purpose found in the fiery nature of His "speaking" <note>The author refers to the "Speaking Word" or *Logos* through which all things were created</note>. This is where the fire kindles and concentrates itself into a principle for the manifestation of God, and it is within this that creaturely life exists.

365. Therefore, understand that creaturely life, without the manifestation of light, is nothing but fire, hatred, anger, and envy.

366. Such was Adam after the Fall without the gracious "re-speaking" <note>The author uses "re-inpeaking" to describe the promise of the Gospel or the "crushing of the serpent's head" spoken back into the soul</note>. The same was true for Cain, Ishmael, Esau, and all people who lack the "grace-essence" <note>original: *Grace-Ens*</note> of love from which the light originates.

### Question.

367. But now the question is: Has God’s righteousness, through His predestined purpose, hated Esau unto eternal damnation?

### Answer.

368. Indeed, by his own power and ability, it could no longer be any other way.

### Question.

369. Furthermore, it may be asked: Was it the simple, true, and pure *will* of God that Esau, Cain, and many thousands of others should perish eternally?

### Answer.

370. No. Christ was God’s predestined purpose, insofar as God is called "God" <note>In the author's theology, God is only called "God" in His light and love; His fiery aspect is called "Wrath."</note>.

<margin>1 Timothy 2:4</margin>
371. In Christ, **God wills that all people should be helped or saved**; but His anger wills to devour everyone in whom *it* is manifested.

<margin>John 3:17</margin>
372. But the Scripture says, **God sent His Son into the world**—that is, into humanity—**not so that He should judge, harden, and destroy it, but so that He should save it.**

### Objection.

373. You will say, "Yes, but He saves whomever He wills."

### Answer.

374. Indeed, He calls everyone to Him; they all should come.

### Question.

375. Why, then, do they not all come? You might say it is because He does not draw them to Himself from within.

### Answer.

376. That is not true. He draws them all; He teaches everyone from within. For they know what is right through the "light of nature," in which He meets the wicked in their...

<header>Chapter 9. Of the right understanding of the Scripture.</header>
<sig>L l 2</sig>

[He enlightens their] understandings and shows them what is right; they themselves also acknowledge and teach it, but do not practice it.

->Question.<-

377. But why is that?

->Answer.<-

<margin>y John 17:24. z John 6:44.</margin>
378 Christ says, <sup>y</sup> *Father, I desire that those whom you have given me be where I am;* also, <sup>z</sup> *No one comes to me unless my Father draws him to me.*

->Question.<-

379. Why is it that he does not draw everyone?

->Answer.<-

380. There lies the reason: Dear defiled piece of wood <note>original: "Piece of Wood"; a metaphor for the soul in its natural, corrupt, or "stiff" state</note>, smell your own heart <note>original: "smell in thy Bosom"; an exhortation to self-examination of one's internal spiritual state</note>.

->Question.<-

381. What do you smell there?

->Answer.<-

382. If you are grasped only by the predestined purpose of God's fierce wrath within its configuration <note>original: "Constellation"; referring here to the spiritual alignment or the specific makeup of an individual's soul</note>, as were *Esau*, *Ishmael*, and others like them, there is still remedy enough.

<margin>a Exod. 20:5.</margin>
383. But if you are a *thistle*—born from innate, inherited, and active sins in which God’s predestined purpose in his anger has shaped or formed itself into a representation of life—then it is dangerous. This is what God meant regarding the predestined purpose of his righteousness when he said, <sup>a</sup> *He would visit or punish the sins of the parents upon the children unto the third or fourth generation;*

384. For this living, predestined purpose in the *anger* of God already has a clear form in the "science of the speaking Word" <note>original: "Science of the speaking Word"; likely referring to the divine logic or the creative power of God's Word</note>; it is once again severed and divided from the foundational ground of grace.

385. This happens not because of God's original predestined purpose, but because of the source or *fountain* of sin. This fountain has completely united itself with the anger in that predestined state and introduced it into a *life of darkness*.

386. In that state, the inherent grace lies far away. Christ remains dead and rests in the grave there; and *before* he can rise, this evil spirit must be cast into the abyss.

387. God’s predestined purpose now holds these people back and does *not* give them to the *grace* of Christ, for they are "thistle-children." Their will is a *living devil* appearing in the form or likeness of an angel among other men.

388. God’s predestined purpose knows every *ens* <term>original: "Ens"; the essential being, spiritual essence, or "seed" of a person's character</term> while it is still a seed within a man and a woman; he knows what this "sprig of wood" will be useful for when it eventually grows into a tree.

389. And the thistle does not come *only* from the mother's body or womb (the primary ground); it also comes through external influences, accidents, and the circumstances of the times, which cause most people to perish. Christ calls out to all of these.

390. Many of them still have a small spark of the "divine drawing" <note>the internal pull or attraction toward God's grace</note> within them. This gives them over to the predestined purpose of Christ—that is, his voice—so that they sometimes hear Christ teaching within them; these people are invited and called to loudly.

391. But external influences, accidents, and circumstances destroy that spark again. they crucify Christ's voice and inward calling before he is made flesh or born within them, and they introduce the "serpent’s essence" <note>original: "Serpent's Ens"; the sinful or diabolical nature</note> in Christ's place.

It emphasizes that while Christ calls to all, some are so hardened in a 'life of darkness' that they reject the divine drawing.</summary>

<header>Of the right understanding of the Scripture. Chap. 9.</header>

392. And then, when it comes to the election or predestination <note>the theological concept of God choosing who will be saved</note> at the time of harvest—when people thresh, winnow, and toss the grain—these people are but the chaff of the grain and do not have the divine weight and firmness in them.

<margin>Matthew 20:16</margin>
393. Then they remain behind in the center of darkness, within God’s righteousness in His anger; and then it is rightly said, *“Few are chosen out of them.”*

394. For the master of the house chooses only the good fruit for his own food, and the rest he gives to the animals. So it is here: *“Whatever has not grown up in the divine* ens <note>original: "Ens"; a Latin term meaning "being" or "essence"</note> *and is not born of God cannot see God.”*

### Question.

395. And now you will say: In the end, did *Esau* escape the hatred of God, become born again, and achieve salvation or blessedness?

### Answer.

<margin>Romans 12:19</margin>
396. We must not judge that; for God says, *“Vengeance is mine, and I will repay it in my righteousness.”*

397. We say with good reason that *Esau* was born in *Adam's* sin—namely, a true image of *Adam* after the Fall—and according to the predestined purpose of God's anger, he was seized within his mother's womb, just as all poor sinners are.

398. But *Jacob* was born in the image of Christ in newborn love, acting as a *type* or *prefiguration* <note>a person or event in the Old Testament that foreshadows someone or something in the New Testament</note> of Christ.

399. This Christ came to call poor sinners and to save them, so far as God's *righteousness* in His anger allows them to follow Him—considering the innate, inherited abominations or wickedness rooted in their eternal being <note>original: "Eternal Science"; referring to the soul's essential nature or internal disposition</note>, as well as the actual wickedness or abominations which act as *obstacles*.

400. But *Esau*, though proceeding from and born of holy parents, was presented there only in the separation as an image of perished, corrupt nature.

401. And God also separated the image of Christ out of the *same* seed of those parents—namely, his brother *Jacob*—and set him before Himself.

402. This same *Jacob* eventually brought *Esau* to a state of great compassion through his gifts and *humility*. This signifies the "present" or free gift of Christ within *Esau*, which would thus convert him and draw him out from the angry, captivating, predestined purpose of the righteousness of God, so that he should be sorry for his evil will and should bewail and repent of it.

403. He did exactly this when he embraced *Jacob*, wept on his neck, and let go of his murderous spirit toward him; therefore, we must not condemn him.

404. We condemn him only according to the Scripture, which condemns him in *Adam's wickedness* when he was not yet born again.

405. In that state of sin, God’s righteousness is satisfied; but grace is revealed through repentance.

406. We do not know for certain, but it is possible God converted him, as the symbol of *Jacob* returning to him from *Laban* suggests.

407. For though he was dead in *Adam*, he might be alive in Christ. The gates of grace stood as *open* for him as for his parents, who were themselves in the lineage of Christ.

408. Yet the fact that they also possessed *Adam’s* poison and death in their flesh—the source or fountain of sin from *Adam*—is shown in *Esau*, *Ishmael*, and *Cain*.

409. But we must not listen to human reason here, which claims that God hardened *Esau* and ordained him to eternal damnation.

The author emphasizes that the gates of mercy are open to all, despite the inherited sin of Adam seen in figures like Esau, Ishmael, and Cain.</summary>

# Chap. 10. How to understand the Objections of Scripture.

410. It cannot be shown in the Holy Scripture that God has hardened him, or that it is the Divine Will; rather, the predestined purpose within God’s righteousness has done it.
411. This occurs not through an outward entering in and taking hold by a Divine Will, but from the perished or corrupt nature out of *Adam’s* property or quality in *Esau’s* own substance itself; it is not a strange accident or influence entering into him, as Reason or [the human] grasp <note>original: "gripe"; refers to the conceptual 'grip' or limited understanding of human logic.</note> judges.
412. This Reason knows nothing of God, or what He is; it always represents Man to be *far away* from God, whereas God is manifested or revealed in all men—in every man according to the *property* of his life.
413. We have explained this foundation thus largely for the reader, so that he may understand our meaning in the following short conclusions.

# The Tenth Chapter.

### *A brief collection and examination of objections from Scripture; which objections hold Reason captive: how they are to be understood.*

<margin>1 Pet. 2:8.</margin>
1. In the Epistle to the Romans, the ninth and eleventh chapters, Reason goes astray; and they are "a stone of stumbling, and a rock of offense" to the wicked; but to the holy, they are a light of life.

# Objection 1. Rom. 9:6, 7, 8, 9.

<margin>
Rom. 9:6.
7.
8.
9.
</margin>
2. For it is there mentioned: *They are not all Israelites who are of Israel:* Also, *All who are of the seed of Abraham are not therefore the children of Abraham; but in Isaac shall your seed be called.*
3. *For they are not children who are children according to the flesh, but the children of the promise are accounted as the seed: For this is the word of promise, where he says, "About this time will I come, and Sarah shall have a son."*

# Answer.

4. Reason understands this as if the promise began in this seed of *Abraham*: But we see that the promise began in *Paradise*; and through this, *Abraham* was formed into a figure or representation of the Kingdom of Nature in *Ishmael*, and of the Kingdom of Grace in *Isaac*—namely, into an image of that which was to come, as it was also in *Cain* and *Abel*.
5. The Kingdom of Nature was in man in the original predestined purpose to the human image, comprised in the <term>Anger</term>; and that can no more generate God’s children and the true seed of God, but only children of <term>Wrath</term> <note>In the author's theology, the 'Anger' or 'Wrath' refers to the first principle of nature, the fiery foundation of existence that remains dark without the light of God's love.</note>, and of the corrupt flesh.
6. Therefore St. *Paul* says that all the children and seed of God were not from *Abraham* [by biology alone], but those who were newborn of the promise—namely, out of the incorporated Word in Paradise; which God *renewed* with *Abraham*, when He would represent and produce His image out of the promise.
7. For every person who shall be saved, in them must the word of promise from Grace be an <term>Ens</term> and substance; <note>original: "Ens"; a Latin term for 'being' or 'essential substance.' Here it refers to the spiritual seed taking actual form in the soul.</note> this is not done for everyone in the mother’s womb, like *Isaac*, but in repentance and conversion.

# How to understand the Objections of Scripture. Chapter 10.

8. **As God says in** *Isaiah*, <margin>* Isaiah 1:18.</margin> *If your sins were as red as blood, if you turn and convert, they shall be as wool, white as snow;* and this is done when the **Kingdom of Grace** is manifested in the Kingdom of Nature.

9. **Here it is rightly said, as it was said to** *Abraham*; *this is the Covenant; about this time I will come, and then Sarah shall have a son.*

10. **That is, when the poor sinner repents, then God comes in Christ’s Spirit and generates a new son out of Christ’s flesh and blood in him. That is, the soul lays hold on Christ in itself, in faith and hope, and imprints or compacts that hope into an** *Ens*, <term>Ens: A philosophical and alchemical term referring to "essence" or "actual being."</term> **wherein lies the living promised Word within.**

11. **And then the conception of the new humanity proceeds forth out of Christ; and that is then the** *right* **seed of faith, out of which God’s children are generated or born, as the dew of the morning redness.** <note>original: "morning redness"; likely a reference to Boehme's first work, *Aurora*, symbolizing the dawning of spiritual truth.</note>

12. **And then the old** *Adam* **only clings to them, as with** *Abraham, Isaac*, **and** *Jacob*, **who, as to the outward man, were also mortal and sinful; but the Temple of God, the inward man in them, was holy. So it is also in us.**

### Objections further in the Text, Romans 9:10, 11, 12, 13.

<margin>Romans 9:10-13. ^h Or, the elder shall serve the younger. ^i 13.</margin>
13. *And not only thus: But when Rebecca also conceived from one, even our father Isaac: Before the children were born, and had done neither good nor evil, so that the purpose of God according to election might stand: It was said to her—not because of the merit of works, but because of the grace of him who calls—thus: The ^h greater shall serve the less.*
14. *^i As it is written; Jacob have I loved, but Esau have I hated.*

### Answer.

15. **Now here reason lies blind, and it is as was declared before at large; for this was the predestined purpose of God, which he bestowed on** *Adam* **after the Fall.**
16. **The** *first* **predestined purpose is the natural first** *Adam*, **which was the greater or elder, and the first image of God, in the predestined purpose of the Divine Science** <term>Divine Science: The inherent wisdom or systematic knowledge of God.</term> **or Root, out of the speaking Word of the separability or distinction of powers.**
17. **But the grace was not manifested in him, much less the great love and humility in JESUS.**
18. **And therefore God came with the** *second* **predestined purpose which lay hidden in the grace, and gave it into the first image, and manifested the grace through the first image, and killed the first life in the grace. He** *lifted up* **the life of grace in the first predestined purpose, above the predestined purpose of the greater or elder image—namely, of the first natural image.**
19. *Therefore* **the text in** *Moses* **says to** *Rebecca*, **the greater shall serve the less, so that the predestined purpose in the manifestation of grace may stand.**
20. **For** *Esau*, **in the greater first image of** *Adam*, **I have hated; when he would be his own lord, and live in evil and good, and not know, acknowledge, or regard grace.**
21. **But** *Jacob*, **in my right Divine predestined purpose, which I have generated out of my Divine will of grace from eternity; him have I loved, and set him to be lord over nature.**
22. **Therefore Christ said,** *All power was given to him*. **For he was the less or younger—namely, out of God’s humility and love—which God set above the kingdom of his anger, so that the lesser (in God’s grace) might serve and manifest God.**
23. **And therefore outwardly the inheritance was withheld or withdrawn from** *Ishmael*, **to signify that God had given the inheritance to the man who was born of grace.**

# Chapter 10. How to Understand the Objections in Scripture.

24. Regarding this hatred, reason errs and does not understand the basis of it, as was mentioned above.

## Further Objections in the Text: Romans 9:14–18.

<margin>Romans 9:14.</margin>
25. *What shall we say then? Is God unrighteous?*

<margin>15.</margin>
26. *Far be it from us! For he says to Moses, "I will be gracious to whom I am gracious; and I will have compassion on whom I have compassion."*

<margin>16, 17.</margin>
27. *Therefore, it does not depend on any man’s will or effort, but on God’s mercy and compassion. For the Scripture says to Pharaoh, "For this very purpose I have raised you up, that I might show my power in you, and that my name might be proclaimed in all nations."*

<margin>18.</margin>
28. *Therefore, he has compassion on whom he wills, and he hardens whom he wills.*

### Answer.

<margin>1 Corinthians 2:14.</margin>
29. In this matter, reason lies completely dead without the divine light, as it is written: *The natural man does not receive or understand the mysteries of God; they are foolishness to him.*

30. Here St. Paul justifies God and says that God judges correctly by having compassion on whom he wills; and this is the fundamental basis of the matter.

<margin>Note: On whom God will have mercy.</margin>
31. For he will have no one in his mercy or compassion except those who are born of his predestined purpose of grace through *Christ*. He has compassion on these poor, captive souls.

<margin>Romans 4:3. Galatians 3:6.</margin>
32. That is, when the soul takes hold of the word of promise and receives it as *Abraham* did, then that receiving of the new *essence* <note>original: "Ens"</note> of grace is credited as righteousness, just as it was to *Abraham*, according to what is written: *Abraham believed God, and it was credited to him as righteousness.*

33. For believing is called receiving, taking in, or "impressing"—that is, taking hold of the word of promise within oneself so that it becomes substantial. Then, mercy and compassion arise within it.

34. For the "lesser" or "younger" <note>The author likely refers to the spiritual birth or the second principle overcoming the first.</note>, which in the beginning is only a word of power, becomes so very great that it overcomes the greatest thing—namely, the fiery soul of the eternal nature in God’s first eternal predestined purpose.

35. But where it is written that he has mercy or compassion on whom he wills and hardens whom he wills, one must understand this in the context of *two* predestined purposes.

36. That is, the divine predestined purpose is in *Christ*, through whom he has mercy. For *Christ* is his will toward mercy and compassion; there is no other will in God toward mercy or compassion but that single will which he has *manifested* in *Christ*.

37. For the *first* divine will in *Adam’s* original image, when he was in a state of innocence, has faded or been extinguished in man, just as the light of a candle goes out. That same goodwill is lost—not in God, but in humanity.

38. And out of that goodwill—which is the name JEHOVAH—the will of love and grace has revealed itself in the name JESUS in *Adam* after the Fall, through the "in-speaking" <note>A term for internal divine revelation or the Word entering the soul.</note> of the "Treader upon the Serpent" <note>A reference to the "seed of the woman" from Genesis 3:15 who would crush the head of the serpent.</note>.

39. For through this *new* goodwill in the name JESUS, God gave the goodwill in man to his son JESUS. As *Christ* says: "Father"—that is, you *great God*, or JEHOVAH in the fire and light—"these men are yours, and you have given them to me, and I give them eternal life."

40. The other, or *second will*, is the predestined purpose of the first foundation of God as JEHOVAH. When the light-part in *Adam* faded or disappeared, the fiery property or quality—namely, the *angry God manifested* in this will—was revealed. This will, according to its nature, now intends to consume all things and cast them into darkness.

<summary>The author explains Romans 9 by distinguishing between God's will of mercy manifested in Christ (the name Jesus) and God's "fiery" will of justice and wrath (the name Jehovah) which hardens those outside of grace.</summary>

# How to understand the Objections of Scripture. Chapter 10.

**41.** Therefore, here the Spirit of Moses speaks of the Will of God in both Love and Anger, stemming from both preordained purposes: 1. from the *original righteousness in which God created Adam.*

**42.** And then 2. from the preordained purpose of Christ stemming from Grace: namely, **those I have mercy and compassion on in Love, whom I apprehend and *feel* within it; those I have mercy and compassion on.**

**43.** And those whom I *find* in my Anger, defiled with the sin that leads to death and in the sinful fountain of a wicked or evil life like a thistle—meaning, a *devil's will*—those I harden in my preordained purpose of zeal or jealousy. <note>original: "of Zeal or Jealousy"; in this context, it refers to God's intense, consuming fire that reacts against sin.</note> *God knows well what purpose everyone serves.*

**44.** Therefore, people should not suppose here that in God’s preordained purpose—so far as he is called *God*—any will to harden a person enters into them from the outside. Rather, it happens within a person’s own internal foundation. The fountain and origin of that hardening is found in the preordained purpose of God's righteousness <note>Böhme argues that "hardening" is not an arbitrary act by God, but a natural result of God's perfect righteousness reacting to a person's chosen wickedness.</note>.

**45.** For it is the Will of Anger in which he hardens whom he will; for the entire creaturely nature of a person in God’s Anger is *that will to hardening*, because it desires only vanity <note>original: "Vanity"; here meaning futility, selfishness, or the temporary things of the world.</note>, and that vanity also hardens it.

<margin>Note.</margin>
**46.** Therefore, *it does not lie in the "willing"—meaning that the wicked person simply "wills" to be saved or happy—nor does it lie in the work* of his hands, but in God’s mercy and compassion. It requires that he *converts*, becomes like a child with a false or wicked will, and is born anew from the mercy and compassion of Grace.

**47.** For if it depended on the willing of nature's *own self*, then the lost, corrupt nature of Adam could achieve sonship <note>original: "Filiation"; the state of being a child of God.</note>.

**48.** But no: it must *die* to self-will and be born out of the Will of Grace, so that the Grace of Christ may be *manifested* in God’s willing, in which alone there is mercy, compassion, and good-will.

<margin>Note.</margin>
**49.** This is what is *meant* by "whom he wills in Love and Anger": he wills the *wicked* in the Anger, and the *holy* in the Grace; each one from and within its own internal foundation.

**50.** Understand it correctly: it was said to Pharaoh, *"I have therefore hardened you and stirred you up, so that I might make my Name known among all nations."*

**51.** Pharaoh was not generated or born out of Grace—that is, out of the *Grace-willing*—but out of the *Anger-willing*.

**52.** And when God wanted to make his Name known—that he is Lord, and how his Grace *rules* over Anger—he stirred up the Anger in the hardened Pharaoh. He took hold of him in the preordained purpose of the Anger within him and held him so that he might not see the works of God. For he was blind to God until God let him see the form, manner, or way of his wrath in the *great upheaval* <note>original: "Turba magna"; Böhme's term for a state of extreme spiritual chaos, disruption, or divine wrath.</note>.

<margin>Genesis 15:13.</margin>
**53.** Scripture indicates that at this time the wickedness of the Egyptians was full and ready for punishment. It says *that the Israelites must serve the Egyptians for four hundred years, and then God would judge that people*; for their wicked deeds, leading to their hardening, *were not yet full.*

**54.** But by Pharaoh's time they were full, and the hardening in them was at hand; *therefore*, the preordained purpose of God in his Anger used him as an instrument.

<margin>Wisdom of Solomon 11:20.</margin>
**55.** For the Egyptians had stirred up the plagues; therefore, they had to serve the glorious manifestation of divine Grace upon God's children. In this way, God could cause his Anger to be seen in the wicked and his Grace to be seen in his children; for the time of Pharaoh was a time of a limit, in which all things lie in *time, measure, and weight.*

**56.** The *supposed preordained purpose from the outside* is strongly thrown to the ground in this one text by St. Paul. In that false view, human reason supposes that God elects some special, peculiar people based on a *distinct, singular name*; just as the religious sects rage in their strife...

# Chapter 10. How to understand the Objections raised in Scripture.

### *For example, where Paul says in Romans 9:24, 25, 26:*

<margin>Romans 9:24, 25.</margin>
57. *Whom he has called—that is, us—not only from among the Jews, but also from the Gentiles. He confirms this through the prophet Hosea, saying:*

<margin>26.</margin>
58. *“I will call those my people who were not my people, and her my beloved who was not beloved. And it shall come to pass in the place where it was said to them, ‘You are not my people,’ there they shall be called children of the living God.”*

### Answer.

59. Here we clearly see the *first* calling in Paradise, through the *inspoken* Word <term>inspoken Word: the Divine Word or "Verbum Fiat" that God breathed into humanity at creation and again as a promise after the Fall</term> of Grace, which extends from the one [Adam] to everyone.

60. For the Gentiles were not of Abraham's seed, the people with whom God made a specific Covenant; yet the Covenant of the *inspoken* Word of Grace remained within them as a foundational basis.

61. Therefore, St. Paul says that God has called and chosen not only the Jews through their Covenant, but also the Gentiles through the Covenant of Christ. He has called those people his "beloved" who did not previously know him and who, outwardly in their ignorance, were not considered his people.

62. However, the predestined purpose of Grace—which had established itself in Paradise after the Fall through the *inspoken* Word—remained within them. Because of this, God calls them his beloved.

63. He stirred up this established Word within them through the Spirit of Christ, once that Voice of Grace had taken on a soul <note>This refers to the Incarnation of Christ</note>. Thus:
1. Their soul, which had been trapped in darkness, heard the established Voice of Grace through the voice of Christ. It was like the awakening of a new "in-speaking," and so love was kindled within the soul.

64. And 2. God does not see according to human knowledge. He chooses a people for filiation <term>filiation: the process of becoming children and heirs of God</term> based on his predestined purpose, rather than choosing those who simply know how to speak of his name better than all other people. 
3. God looks toward his predestined purpose, which was raised up and established in Paradise—the purpose he had from eternity regarding the faded, extinguished, and disappeared figure or idea of man. That is, he looks upon the *first* foundational ground of humanity.

65. In this purpose, humanity was seen or foreseen in the name of Jesus <note>original: JESU</note> within Divine Wisdom, as a "magical" <note>original: "magical" here refers to the spiritual power of God's will and imagination forming a spiritual reality, not sorcery</note> impression, idea, form, or representation.

66. This impression or image was also present in the inner foundation of the Gentiles or heathens, passing from the one image [of Adam] to everyone—excepting only the "children of anger" or "children of perdition," in whom that image manifested itself through God's wrath.

67. This imprinting of anger does *not* affect entire generations or nations, but only those caught in the predestined purpose of wrath due to inherited, innate, and actual sins; these are the "thistle-children" <term>thistle-children: a metaphor for people who produce the "weeds" of sin and anger rather than the fruit of the Spirit</term>.

68. As it was said to Elijah, when he told God, *"Israel has completely departed from you, and I am the only one left, and they hunt for my life"*: He was answered by God, who said, *"I have kept for myself seven thousand who have not bowed the knee to Baal."*

69. Such are those who, although they outwardly lived alongside the Gentiles or heathens and dwelt among the wicked Jews, nevertheless had hearts inclined toward the true God, and were...

It distinguishes between those chosen by God's eternal purpose and the "thistle-children" who are consumed by spiritual wrath and sin.</summary>

# How to understand the Objections of Scripture. Chapter 10.

<margin>* Afterwards Paul.</margin>
He was zealous in blindness and ignorance as Saul, * until the grace within him awakened so that he gained sight.

70. For Saul believed he was serving the true God when he overthrew and suppressed those who sought to walk in God’s Law in another form or appearance—a way he knew nothing about.

71. He was zealous for the *Law of God* from the bottom of his heart, intending to please God through his actions.

72. He did *not* do this because of a predestined purpose of God’s anger, as if wrath had seized him and placed him in a *life of darkness*, or as if God looked upon him as completely hardened in death due to a specific, *distinct* election or predestination.

73. No: he was actually *one* among the "Seven Thousand" <note>original: "Seven Thousand"; a reference to 1 Kings 19:18, referring to the faithful remnant known to God but hidden from the world.</note> in whom lay the Covenant of Grace from the *true seed of Abraham* and the *Promise in Paradise*.

74. But the *way* of that grace was *not yet* revealed to him; he was zealous for the Law of Righteousness and demanded exactly what he *himself* could not achieve or perform.

75. However, the *hidden grace within him* could achieve it; this grace revealed itself through his zeal and used that passion as an instrument to *witness* to grace.

76. Therefore, it is blindness and ignorance for one group of people to say, "We have Christ’s doctrine; God causes Christ to be preached among *us* and not among others; and *therefore* God has elected or chosen us according to his predestined purpose to be children of his grace."

77. And even though we are *not at all* better in our conduct than others, they say, "He has elected us in his predestined purpose, and in Christ he has borne the *penalty* or punishment for our actual and original inherited sins, so we *only need* to comfort ourselves with that and receive it as a gift and free gift of grace."

78. For they claim our works *count for nothing* in the presence of God, but only the *election* of his predestined purpose counts; by this, they say, he justifies the wicked in his predestined purpose, and by the predestined purpose of his will, he pulls the wicked out of hell and saves them.

79. Listen, you *blind Babylon* <note>original: "blind Babylon"; Boehme uses this to refer to the confused and corrupt state of institutional churches that rely on external rituals or theories rather than internal spiritual transformation.</note>, covered under Christ’s purple cloak like a prostitute under a garland—one who is full of the *lust of whoredom* and yet calls herself a virgin: What is this election or predestination and grace that you comfort yourself with? Why do you cover yourself with that mantle of *grace* while continuing in your "prostitutions" and the abominations of malice and wickedness?

80. Where is it suggested in the Scripture that a prostitute becomes a virgin simply through the *order*, warrant, or commission of a lord or prince, or by his free gift or *generosity*? What emperor can make a deflowered woman a virgin again by his favor and goodwill? Can such a thing be?

81. Where, then, is the *virginity of the heart and of purity*?

<margin>* Matthew 5:18. Luke 16:17.</margin>
82. God requires the *depths of the heart* and says that *“not one jot or tittle of his Law of Righteousness shall pass away until it is all fulfilled.”*

83. How will you fulfill that righteousness if you do not have the divine substance within you?

84. You will say, "Christ has already fulfilled it for me and satisfied the Law."

85. That is true, but what is that *to you*, who are and remain outside of Christ?

<margin>* Matthew 12:30.</margin>
86. If you are not in Christ through *actual*, active *grace*, then you have no part in him; for he says, *“Whoever is not with me is against me; and whoever does not gather with me scatters.”*

87. No outwardly credited <note>original: "imputed"</note> grace is effective, but only an inward, child-like *grace* born from Christ’s flesh and blood; it is that internal reality which draws the merits of Christ to itself.

# Chapter 10. How to understand the Objections of Scripture.

88. It is not the person who is born of man and woman from our fallen, corrupt nature that attains the grace of <term>filiation</term> <note>original: "Filiation"; the status of being a child of God through spiritual adoption</note>, so that he can comfort himself and say, "Christ has done it; he now pronounces me free from sin; I only need to believe that it is finished."

89. No; the Devil knows this, and so do the damned, who comfort themselves with this "imputed grace"; but what does it benefit them when they are damned regardless?

<margin>Matthew 7:21.</margin>
90. For Christ says, *“Not everyone who says to me, ‘Lord, Lord,’ shall enter into the Kingdom of Heaven, but those who do the will of my Father in Heaven.”*

91. But what is *that will* which they must do so that they may attain filiation?

92. Christ says that those who *convert* and become as children, and are born of God *out of water and the Spirit*—these are the ones.

93. For *Christ* is the will of God; and those who wish to do that will must be *born of Christ*, out of his flesh and blood, out of the Word that became man, which overthrew death and sin in <term>humanity</term> <note>original: "the Humanity"; referring to human nature in general</note> and turned it into love. They must *put on* the merit of Christ in the soul, and according to the internal, incorporated ground, become the living Christ, like a true *branch* on his vine.

94. This is not achieved by comforting oneself with a strange, assumed appearance or *show*, but by becoming essentially existing, substantial children of Christ, in whom the <term>inspoken</term> <note>original: "inspoken"; referring to the divine Word spoken into the human soul at creation or after the Fall</note> covenant of grace is fulfilled with *substance*—in whom the *soul eats and lives of Christ’s flesh and blood*, and that not outwardly, but *within itself*.

<margin>John 6.</margin>
95. In such a person, Christ *continually* says to the fiery soul in God’s righteousness: *“Take, eat my flesh and drink my blood; so shall you remain in me, and I in you.”*

<margin>See the word "Science" in the *Clavis* <note>original: "Clavis"; Latin for "Key," referring to Boehme's explanatory work, *The Clavis*</note>, verses 210 to 219.</margin>
96. The fiery <term>Science</term> <note>original: "Science"; from the Latin *scientia*, meaning a dynamic, creative knowledge or the innate "will-activity" of the soul</note> or root of the soul, according to the inward eternal ground of the true righteousness of God in his predestined purpose for the creature of the soul, must introduce itself into Christ’s flesh and blood in *substance*.

97. And this is not through a strange show or appearance, but through that which God manifested in *Adam* after the Fall and *fulfilled* in Christ with his humanity; wherein God became man, and man became God.

98. So it is also in his members <note>the individual believers</note>, who spring and sprout out of the *same root*, in which Christ became living in the incorporated covenant of grace and assumed the soul and humanity to himself.

99. Therefore, the matter here does *not* lie in outward knowledge alone—in the fact that I know I have a gracious God in Christ who has overthrown sin in humanity—but it lies in the fact that this same work is also done in me.

100. It requires that Christ, who is risen from the dead, also arises in me and rules over sin in me. He must also kill sin—that is, the evil will of nature—*within me*, so that this nature is crucified and slain in me through Christ. Then a new will out of nature, in Christ’s spirit, life, and will, may arise *in me*; a will which lives and is obedient to God’s will and fulfills the Law.

101. That is, a will which gives itself up in *obedience* to the Law and fulfills it with the divine <term>Love-Will</term>; so that the Law in its righteousness is subject to the <term>Love-Desire</term> and also rejoices in that love.

102. And then the anger of God sinks down from the soul; and *so* the soul is released or delivered in the Spirit of Love from pain, and *lives in God*.

<margin>Matthew 7:7.</margin>
103. To this process belongs earnest *repentance*, in which the poor soul opens its jaws—namely, the fiery mouth in God’s predestined purpose of anger—and encompasses itself in the incorporated grace of the promise of Christ, who said *he will give the Holy Spirit to those who ask him for it*.

104. This freely presented, bestowed grace must be impressed or apprehended by the soul as a living, speaking Word in the inward ground of the first inspoken voice of grace in *Adam*. This happens through the center of nature, by the divine "Science" or root of the <term>Abyss</term> <note>original: "Abyss"; the "Unground" or the bottomless depth of God's being</note>.

The author emphasizes that Christ must be "born" and "arise" within the individual to overcome the soul's fallen nature and fulfill God's Law through love.</summary>

## How to understand the Objections of Scripture. Chap. 10.

...that it be a predestined purpose <note>original: "predeſtinate Purpoſe"</note> toward repentance and conversion from a will inclined toward abominations.

105. In this predestined purpose, the Spirit of Christ—within the primary foundation of incorporated grace, where it spreads from one person to all according to the Scriptures—gives birth to a new life.

106. In this new life, the *will* to sin is suppressed and dies, and a true branch grows out of Christ’s tree; afterward, sin *only* rules in the mortal flesh.

<margin>

</margin>
107. This new branch, within Christ, is then pressed through the anger of God in the predestined purpose of that anger, moving entirely through *eternal death* into the *life of grace*. As Christ says, "He who believes in me shall never die again," but has pressed—or passed—entirely from death to life.

108. Therefore, faith is not an outward matter, so that anyone should say, "The election of grace is with us, for Christ is *taught* and acknowledged among us; he has chosen us above other people so that we hear his voice."

109. Even though we are *evil*, he has forgiven our sins in his predestined purpose and destroyed them through the merit of Christ. We need *only to receive* it and comfort ourselves with it; it will be outwardly credited <note>original: "imputed"</note> to us as a free gift and present of grace.

110. No, no, that is not enough; *Christ himself* is the credited grace and the free gift or dowry, as well as the *merit*.

111. Whoever has that within them and is fundamentally the same in their own inner being <note>original: "inward Ground"</note> is a *Christian*. Such a person is crucified and dead with Christ and lives in his resurrection. To those people, the grace in Christ's spirit and life is *credited* <note>original: "imputed"</note>, reckoned, or accounted.

112. For he *does not need* to let himself be hung on a cross; rather, he *draws in* <note>original: "attracts"</note> Christ in all his merit. He draws the crucified and risen Christ into himself and simply *takes* his yoke upon him.

113. But this is not merely a matter of *knowing* and *comforting*; for Christ does *not* dwell in a body characterized by malice, evil intent, and wickedness.

114. If Christ is to rise within you, then the *will* toward death and the devil must die in you.

115. For *Christ* has broken death to pieces and destroyed hell, and has become Lord over death and hell.

116. Wherever he draws near within a person, death and hell must be broken to pieces and vanish in the inner being <note>original: "inward Ground"</note>—that is, in the *soul*.

117. He destroys the devil’s kingdom in the soul and gives birth to it as God’s child and his temple. He gives the soul *his will* and kills the will of lost or corrupt nature.

<margin>
* 1 Cor. 1:30.
* Rom. 5:9.
</margin>
118. That is, he transforms <note>original: "tranſmutes"</note> or changes it into the true image of God; for it is written, *Christ is made our righteousness* through his blood.

119. Now, if a person wants this righteousness, they must drink his blood so that it may justify them. For justification is accomplished through the blood of Christ *within a person*—in the soul itself—not through an outward, credited, and external appearance <note>original: "imputed, accounted ſtrange Shew"</note>.

120. This is the *true* credited external gift <note>original: "right imputed ſtrange Shew"</note> given to us through the blood of Christ by grace when we are dead in sin; therefore, God gives us this free gift of grace *within us* for a new life.

121. This new life kills sin and death and presents us before God as children of grace.

122. For Christ, with his love-bought blood <note>original: "Love-Blood"</note> within us, fulfills God's righteousness amidst his anger and turns it into divine joy.

123. And now, if a person does not find themselves in the divine will—or even possessing a *hearty desire* to wish they could repent, be obedient to God, and put on Christ—let them *not* say they are a true Christian.

# Chap. 10. **How to understand the Objections in Scripture.**

124. The babbling mouth—when people acknowledge Christ as the Son of God with their tongues and comfort themselves with his grace, but keep the "Serpent" (with its poisonous will toward pride, greed, envy, and malice) in their hearts, desiring only to do evil—is of no help at all.

125. Such a person only *crucifies* Christ and mocks his merit; for while he acknowledges him with his tongue, he throws stones and dirt at him with the serpent's poison in his heart.

126. He does no more than the devils do, who *acknowledged* Christ to be the power of God when he drove them out of the *possessed*.

127. For those who acknowledge Christ only with their mouths are not therefore his children; rather, those who do the will of his Father in heaven—*namely, in Christ himself*—are his children.

128. For Christ is the good will of the Father, which no one can do unless he is in Christ and does it in Christ’s Spirit and life.

129. For not all those who are descended from *Abraham* are God’s children; rather, the children of the promised Seed—those newborn from that Seed—are the children. These are reborn out of the blood of Christ and die away from their original nature <note>original: "first Ground"</note> in the blood of Christ, in the *grace* and love of God. They arise as a new person who lives before God in *righteousness and purity*, to whom sin clings only through the desires <note>original: "Lust"</note> of the animal-like <note>original: "beastial"</note> *mortal flesh*.

130. The new man in Christ rules over this sin, taming and *subduing* it, and rejecting the will of the flesh.

131. But he who lives and acts according to the will of the flesh is *dead while he lives*; his confession and acknowledgment with the mouth do not help him.

<margin>Note the Antichrist.</margin>
132. For acknowledging with the mouth without the inward, *essential* foundation <note>original: "substantial Ground"</note> of Christ is *the very Antichrist*. He indeed acknowledges Christ but denies him in power and virtue <note>original: "virtue" here refers to efficacy or inner strength</note>, and has set himself in *Christ's place*; he says one thing and wills and does another.

133. Therefore, the prophet *Hosea* says that *the Lord calls those his beloved who were not his beloved*. That is, those who did not know Christ by name or essence, and knew nothing of his manifestation or revelation in humanity, yet who go with their souls into the inward foundation <note>original: "Ground"</note> where grace was *infused* <note>original: "incorporated"</note> in *Paradise* through the divine "inspeaking" <note>The "inspeaking" or *Einsprechen* is a key term in Boehme's theology, referring to God's Word being spoken into the human soul since the Fall</note>. Thus, they lay hold of grace through God’s mercy and compassion.

134. These are the people who neither hear nor enjoy the *Gospel*, yet *believe* in the one and only God. They surrender all their powers and faculties to him and would gladly acknowledge and love God if they only knew how; they are also zealous with their whole hearts in *righteousness* and *truth*.

135. As long as these people neither hear nor know Christ in his manifested voice, they are outwardly not God’s beloved; but according to the *inward* foundation <note>original: "Ground"</note>, they are implanted and rooted in the love of grace—namely, in the Paradisiacal Covenant in the embodied Word.

<margin>* Rom. 2:1</margin>
136. These, God said, he would have compelled and brought into his supper; for they were his beloved. Therefore, they testify in power and efficacy that the works of *the law* and the love of God's grace are *written in their hearts, and so they are a law unto themselves*.

137. Christ, in his grace, has fulfilled this law through his blood, which reached and passed from one man to all people. All these are born of that infused <note>original: "incorporated"</note> grace in *will* and spirit.

138. For although the text in *John* 3 says, "*He that believes not in the name of the only begotten Son of God is already judged*," one cannot say that these people do not believe in him.

## How to understand the Objections of Scripture. Chap. 10.

139. Indeed, their outward self <note>original: "outward Man"</note> does not believe in or acknowledge him, for they do not know that he became a human being.

140. But that same inward, established foundation <note>original: "Ground"</note> of the spoken Word of Grace—into which they have grafted, bound, and incorporated themselves along with their souls—believes in them, *against the Day of the Manifestation or Revelation of Jesus Christ*, when he will reveal his Kingdom.

141. For even the ancestors of the *Jews* did not know him in the flesh, but only as a type or symbol <note>original: "Prefiguration"</note>—namely, in the established grace that revealed itself through *the figure* in the Covenant of their Law. But when Christ had fulfilled that Covenant through his humanity, and had satisfied the law of [divine] anger against sin with his blood, and had killed *sin in them* (which had held back and disfigured humanity), then all those who *believed in him through his Covenant* put on Christ in the flesh.

143. That is, those who had put on the Covenant in its power and virtue—namely, in the *Spirit*—were filled with heavenly substance. This also applies to those whose physical bodies had long since passed away and decayed in the grave, but whose souls lived in the Covenant of *Power*.

All of these took Christ into themselves during his Resurrection; and *many of them rose with him in his body after his resurrection from death, appearing in Jerusalem* as a testimony that they had risen in Christ and had put on Christ in the flesh, for he had fulfilled their faith through his humanity.

145. Therefore, it is said to you, blind Christendom, with your talkative mouth: you are *without* Christ in the flesh. You are as far—and *much farther*—from Christ than the honest and virtuous *Heathens, Turks* <note>In this period, "Turks" was a common term for Muslims.</note>, and other nations who do not know Christ but still stand upon the *inward* foundational ground.

147. Now, if a stranger or foreigner draws near to God the Father and surrenders himself to him, God the Father gives that person to Christ.

148. For Christ also said, *Father* (meaning JEHOVAH), *I have lost none of those whom you have given me.* This means that God is revealed in the soul of a converted sinner; this revelation surrenders itself to the *established* Covenant of Grace as its own.

149. This Covenant of Grace, along with the receiving of the soul, shall be revealed *when God reveals the hidden secrets of humanity on the day of his return in the flesh and the resurrection of the dead.*

150. Therefore, it is said to you—you who are Christians in name only <note>original: "titulary and verbal Christendom"</note>—in the zeal of God: because you have a talkative mouth but lack Christ’s Spirit, flesh, and blood within you, you are just as much a heathen, a Turk, or a foreigner in the presence of God as *they* are.

Arrogant <note>original: "stately"</note> in the mind of the Devil, they desire might, honor, authority, and power to suppress the miserable and those in distress, necessity, and want.

153. Outwardly they glitter, dissembling with flattery and hypocrisy, and cover over this wicked knavery with the grace of Christ. 156. O God! The time of your visitation is near; but who knows your arm, because of the gross vanity of the Antichrist in his established kingdom?

157. Destroy him, O LORD! And tear away his might and power, *so that your child JESUS may be manifested to all languages and nations, that we may be delivered from the might, pomp, pride, and greed <note>original: "covetousness"</note> of Antichrist. Hallelujah.*

158. From the East and North, from the sunrise and the midnight, the Lord kisses with his power and might; who will hinder it? *Hallelujah.*

159. In all lands and countries his eye of love beholds and sees; and his truth remains eternally. *Hallelujah.*

160. We are delivered from the yoke of the oppressor <note>original: "driver"</note>, *none shall build it up anymore*; for the Lord has enclosed it in his wonders.

### Clearing the Texts concerning Election. Chap. 11.

5. How will the wicked be converted through a foreign or strange display of received sonship <note>original: "Filiation"</note>, unless he receives the Word into his heart—the same Word he carries in his mouth to acknowledge Christ—so that the soul grasps it in its deepest foundation?

6. Where is this received sonship found, except where the Word takes root and dwells in the heart of the soul?

7. Where did God ever take a person dead in sin, in whom only His wrath lives, and force them through a special election into the predestined purpose of His grace?

8. He allows His Word to move in the mouths and ears of the wicked; but if the heart does not grasp it within the soul, then He lets the light within the Word in the wicked person’s ears and heart fade out and be extinguished.

9. This happens because the wicked person is caught in the predestined purpose of God's anger. The soul has awakened and ignited a life of darkness through its inherited, innate, and self-inflicted vanity, becoming like the life of a serpent or a thistle—something to which the Word of God’s love does not unite itself.

10. Now, if the Word moving in our mouths and hearts makes us children of faith, then no foreign or strange "reception" through a special, outward, elected show or appearance can help. Instead, it is the innate and reborn Word—spoken from that same inward birth where Christ speaks from His own foundation with and through the soul—that constitutes the sonship of reception.

<margin>Rom. x. 9.</margin>
11. <gloss>b</gloss> *For if you confess with your mouth that JESUS is Lord, and believe in your heart that God has raised him from the dead, then you shall be saved.*

12. But this does not happen through a specific personal concept or opinion. Instead, the Spirit of Christ must confess and acknowledge within you that JESUS CHRIST has risen from the dead within you.

<margin>John xv. 5.</margin>
13. Confession and acknowledgment with the mouth, without the resurrection of Christ within you, is worthless to you. For Christ says, <gloss>c</gloss> *Without me you can do nothing.* No one can truly call God "Lord" without Christ being within him.

<margin>Rom. x. 12.</margin>
14. For without Christ, a person does not grasp the word "Lord" in its power; therefore, his saying the word "Lord" is without life. For <gloss>d</gloss> *there is no difference between the Jew and the Greek; there is but one only Lord over all, who is rich toward all who call upon him.*

<margin>13.</margin>
15. *For whoever calls upon the name of the Lord shall be saved.* Here St. Paul makes no distinction between people; rather, to all who desire God in their hearts, He gives the salvation which He offers and bestows in Christ.

16. Where is the "elect people" now in this context—those who boast that God has elected and chosen them above others simply because they can speak about the humanity of Christ?

17. If He has His kingdom among both Jews and Greeks, and only those are truly Jews or Christians who are so in the hearts of their souls, then what is the value of an outward, "imputed" grace <note>imputed grace: the theological concept that Christ's righteousness is credited to a believer externally</note> without the sonship of the soul?

18. When did God ever choose or elect a devil and make him a child of God? *Never.*

19. Therefore, observe this: grace does not come from the merit of our works, but from Christ alone, the fountain of life.

20. However, works testify that the grace of Christ is living within the soul.

21. For if the work does not follow, *then Christ has not yet risen from the dead within you*, or out of your spiritual death.

22. He who belongs to God performs divine works; but he who belongs to sin serves sin with his works.

23. No one should boast that he is a Christian unless he desires to *work* and perform divine works in the love of Christ. Otherwise, it is merely a strange outward show without the life of Christ.

24. The "election of sonship" <note>original: "Election of Filiation"</note> applies only to those who are living in grace and who perform good works through that grace.

<summary>The author argues that spiritual sonship (filiation) is an internal reality where Christ is resurrected within the soul, rather than an external label or an arbitrary choice by God. He emphasizes that true faith must be evidenced by "divine works" and an inward transformation of the heart.</summary>

25. But the others who comfort themselves with their status as children of God <note>original: Filiation; the state of being a son or child</note> by a receiving of Grace, and yet work only abominations in their *hearts*; these are hardened by the predestined purpose of God’s anger.

<margin>Romans 11:7, 8.</margin>

<margin>Isaiah 29:10. Isaiah 6:9.</margin>

<margin>Psalm 69:22. Psalm 69:23.</margin>
29. And *David* says, *Let their table be a snare, so that they may fall backward; and an offense, that they may stumble as a recompense to them: blind their eyes so that they may not see, and bow down their backs always.*

30. Which people of *Israel* does the Spirit mean here in *Isaiah* chapter 6 and in *St. Paul*—those who are not under the Election, whom God in his anger will thus harden?

31. He means *those* who, when they hear the Word, receive it into their ears and understand it as a doctrine or intellectual learning, but do not understand it within the soul so that it may take root in the *Abyss* <note>original: Abyss; the deepest, fundamental core of the human spirit</note>; it reaches the first incorporated grace, but pride, pomp, and self-seeking lie before it, as well as worries about the belly <note>meaning: physical or worldly appetites</note>.

32. Covetousness is a grate or a bolt before it; and the pride of the "self," arising from their own love of the flesh, has set itself in God’s place.

33. These people outwardly perform a show-like pageantry with Grace and take it into their hands, and insist on meriting Grace through their works, just as the wicked, false *Jews* did, who clung only to the outward work and did not have *Faith* in the ground of the soul.

34. Of these *St. Paul* says, "That which *Israel* seeks in the work he attains not; but the Election attains it."

35. For the Election applied only to those *Jews* who were *Jews* in the Abyss of the soul, and were born or generated out of the Seed of Faith; who were born out of the promised Seed—that is, out of the inspoken Word <note>original: inspoken Word; a Böhmean term for the divine breath or creative word placed within humanity</note> in the Covenant of *Abraham* and *Adam*—who were circumcised by the Word in their hearts.

36. For it was not the circumcision of the foreskin in the flesh that mattered before God, but the circumcision in the *heart*.

37. The circumcision in the flesh was a seal and sign of the inward ground, showing how Grace cut off sin from the soul.

38. But with those who were concerned only with the outward work, it was not so; for they were among *Israel* like weeds among wheat, which grow up above the wheat and flourish greatly in size, wanting to be seen as great plants.

39. But they bear no good fruit, and are good for nothing but to be burned at the time of harvest; for they only sting and prick, and take up space.

40. Likewise, the wicked man sets himself in the *Temple of God* and calls himself a Christian, performing many seemingly holy works by which he seeks respect and wants to appear as if he were the best Christian; he learns arts and sciences; he studies hard and knows how to speak much of God; he teaches others, but he does it for the sake of profit and honor.

<margin>Matthew 23:5.</margin>
41. Just as the *Pharisees* did, who made a show of great holiness, *who had great phylacteries <note>original: Philacteries; small leather boxes containing scripture, worn by Jews during prayer</note> upon their priestly garments, and made long prayers for a show of outward piety, virtue, and honesty.*

<margin>Matthew 23:14, 15.</margin>
42. But Christ said, *They devour widows' houses, and travel over sea and land to make one Jewish proselyte <note>original: proselyte; a convert</note>; and when they have made him so, they make him a child of hell twofold more than themselves.*

**50.** They do whatever they want and claim it is right; their office holds the authority, so people must call everything *right* that they do.

**51.** And yet they do not seek *within that office* the righteousness of God in his predestined purpose for the order and course of nature, much less the righteousness of love which he has revealed through the *grace of Christ*.

60. Human **Reason** assumes that God takes a "seed" that is completely false or evil and turns it into a child of God just to demonstrate the riches of His grace through a **special** predestined purpose. No! That is not how it happens.

61. A wicked person—someone who comes from a good lineage <note>original: "Seed"</note> but has allowed sins and evil <note>original: "Abominations"</note> to take root within themselves because of their natural, inherited inclinations—must repent. They must go deep into their inner foundation and be born of grace; only then can their wickedness be transformed.

<margin>Exodus 20:6.</margin>
62. For God says through **Moses**, "I will show mercy to all those who love me and keep my commandments, even unto a thousand generations."

63. This "well-doing" or bounty from God is nothing other than the planting or propagating of the Covenant of Grace within their descendants. Just as **Abraham**, **Isaac**, **Jacob**, and **David** were promised that God would so greatly bless and multiply their seed—because of the grace woven into them—that they could not be numbered.

64. However, the "Kingdom of Nature" also existed within this seed according to God’s plan for righteousness and the properties of the soul; these forces were meant to work together.

65. But in many people, the soul’s will turns away from the Kingdom of God’s plan of grace. Such a soul is seized by the Kingdom of Nature in a state of anger, and it grows into a "thistle" <note>a metaphor for a person who rejects God and produces only "prickly" or evil fruits</note>.

66. This was not God’s fault, but the fault of the "science" <note>original: "Science"; here meaning the active, knowing power or root of the will</note> or root of the soul’s foundation. It stems from the eternal foundation of nature—specifically, the fault of the **free will** emerging from the **Abyss** <term>Abyss: the formless, bottomless void out of which the soul's will arises</term> into the foundation of the soul's nature.

67. This is the **primary origin** of the "thistle-children," who trample upon the grace woven into them by the spoken Word with the feet of their false and wicked lusts, refusing to be children of grace.

<margin>Micah 7:1.</margin>
<margin>Matthew 23:37.</margin>
68. Regarding them, Christ—the gateway of grace itself—said that he was like a grape-picker gathering leftovers. He said, "He would often have gathered Israel’s children together, as a hen <note>original: "Clock-Hen"; a mother hen that clucks to her chicks</note> gathers her chickens under her wings, but they would not."

69. Then Reason says, "They could not!"
70. It is true indeed: They could not!
71. But why?
72. They were "thistle-children."
73. But why? Was it caused by God’s predestined purpose?
74. **Yes**; it stems from the plan of Divine Righteousness, following the order or course of the creation of nature. It comes from the way the spoken Word is divided, where the "science"—the selfhood of the **Abyss**—concentrates itself into its own foundation.

75. For in that state, God’s wrath concentrates within the center of nature in the human **seed**, arising from inherited sins as well as the person's own future evil acts.

76. In this way, God’s anger often takes root through the sins of the **parents** and concentrates into a "science" of the Abyss. From this, a "thistle-root" later grows in the seed. In this way, God punishes the sins of the parents in their descendants unto the third and fourth generation, according to the meaning of the Scripture.

77. Thus, these "thistle-children" also come from **Israel**, but not from its grace. The grace that was woven into them in **Paradise** grows within them only to their **judgment**.

78. Just as the hot essence <note>original: "Ens"; the essential being or substance of a thing</note> of the sun shines upon a thistle, it does not provide the "tincture" of love <term>Tincture: a spiritual quality or essence that transforms or colors a substance</term>, but rather fuels the thistle's own harsh nature.

79. For the thistle can only receive the sun's energy according to its own **likeness**; it is like a toad, which sucks only **poison** out of a good essence <note>original: "Ens"</note>.

It explains how inherited sin and the "Kingdom of Nature" can lead descendants away from the Covenant of Grace despite God's desire to gather them.</summary>

# Clearing the Texts concerning Election.

## Chap. II.

95. That is, let them repay one another in their *Blindness*, in that they—while holding Christ’s Office—hunt only after power, pleasure, and luxury, so that they may persecute, disdain, despise, and scorn one another, and attribute the Name of Christ within them to the Devil.

96. And they plot in their beds how they may get even with one another and outwit them with subtlety, covering their wickedness with the Scripture as if they did it out of Divine Zeal for the *Truth*, to please God, and to serve their brothers by doing so.

97. These run like raging wolves and evil, ravening, furious beasts in the burning anger of God. They snatch and tear the Name of Christ out of the ordinary people's mouths and stuff their hearts and mouths full of the blasphemies of the deceitful schemes of their own hearts, which they pour out and spread abroad. Consequently, one man despises, slanders, and blasphemes another, labeling them as heretics and considering them shameful and unfit for society because of the Name of Christ, all according to their own invented opinions.

98. And thus they also torment and devour themselves, so that one party destroys the other, repaying the malice, falsehood, and wickedness of one another, as *David* says here.

<margin>Luke 11:43</margin>
99. These are the ones of whom Christ says: *They sit in the most important seats of the schools, synagogues, or churches, and enjoy being greeted in the markets; they make a show of wisdom, judgment, and reason, but their hearts are full of bitter gall, and their ways are dangerous. The poison of asps is under their lips, and they serve me superficially and insincerely*, says the Prophet.

<margin>John 13:35</margin>
100. None of these are at all among the <term>Election</term> <note>original: "Election"; refers to the theological concept of being chosen by God for salvation</note> of God’s children. Only those of whom Christ speaks are chosen, where he says: *Love one another, for by this men will know that you are my disciples.* Also: *If you continue in my teachings, you are happy if you do them.*

101. Also: *He who does not leave house, money, goods, wife, and children, and denies himself and follows me, is not my servant or minister.*

102. The heart must give up everything and hold nothing as its own, but think that in his status and work he is only a servant of God and of his brothers; he must handle all that he has and act as God requires and wishes him to do.

103. And he must not cover himself with the cloak of Christ and his merits, remaining greedy, proud, envious, and wrathful underneath it.

<margin>Learn from me, for I am meek and lowly, and you shall find rest for your souls.</margin>
104. All these—however many there are—so long as they remain this way, are those of whom *Paul* and *David* speak here. They are indeed "called," but they are not among the chosen of grace unless they repent during this time of grace, forsake everything in their hearts, and imitate and follow Christ.

105. They receive no outwardly <term>imputed grace</term> <note>original: "imputed Grace"; the theological idea that Christ's righteousness is credited to the believer's account rather than earned by the person</note> unless they are children of grace; then the imputed grace, which is Christ, receives them into itself.

106. Without Christ, they are nothing but Pharisees and flattering hypocrites; though they glisten with "imputed grace" as much as they like, they are still wolves, whom Christ tells us to avoid.

107. Even if they say, "Here is the church of Christ," it means nothing. By their works, says Christ, *you shall know them.* They do not follow Christ; therefore, *they are thieves and murderers*, says Christ.

<margin>Hebrews 7:28</margin>
108. And though they argue that the position and duty make men into high priests who have failings and weaknesses, and though they cover themselves neatly with that excuse, it still amounts to nothing; the heart must be in Christ, and live in him.

109. And although, as St. *Paul* says, lust clings to the flesh and *sin dwells in the outward flesh*, people can see very well who truly desires to kill that lust and follow Christ.

The author argues that true "election" or being chosen by God is shown through a humble heart and following Christ's teachings, not through outward titles or "imputed grace" used as a cover for sin.</summary>

### Clearing the Texts concerning Election. Chapter 11.

110. Where *Greed* and *Pride* reside within, there a *Pharisee* <note>The author uses "Pharisee" to represent a hypocrite who is obsessed with outward religious rules but lacks inner transformation.</note> dwells; no matter how you excuse yourself, you still carry him around your neck.

<margin>g Romans 11:15</margin>
111. St. *Paul* says, <sup>g</sup> "For if their rejection <note>original: "Loss"</note> means the reconciliation of the world, what will their acceptance be but life from the dead?"

112. "If the first-fruit is holy, then the whole batch is holy; and if the root is holy, then the branches are also holy."

113. This one text overthrows all opinions concerning God attributing grace to the ungodly; I say, it overthrows them all completely and places them upon the true foundation of the "Root."

114. And it shows that God does not harden some people out of his own will and purpose just so he can *show* what his grace is.

115. For St. *Paul* says, "What should that be but receiving life from the dead?" He places the *hardening* upon the "Root"—meaning that an evil tree bears evil fruit, and a holy tree bears holy twigs or branches. The anger of God produces "children of anger" <note>original: "Children of the Anger," referring to those born into spiritual darkness</note> out of the *sins* and *vanity* of humanity.

<margin>h Romans 8:28</margin>
116. Yet this must serve as a light to the *heathens* or *Gentiles*; as he says to all who love God, all things must work together for the best for those who are <sup>h</sup> *called and born according to his predestined purpose of grace*.

117. The forgiveness of sins—where the Scripture says he forgives their sins and attributes grace to them for justification—applies only to those in whose inner being <note>original: "inward Ground," a mystical term for the center of the soul</note> *Christ* lives, even if sin still clings to their flesh (as it did with *David* and others who often fell). In these people, the grace within helps them up again and overthrows and destroys sin and its sudden attacks.

118. And this does not happen to the hardened without repentance and conversion. They should not dare to sin based on the assumption that God would use their damnation (while they lie dead in sin by their own will) as an opportunity to display his grace and convert them through a special calling or *compulsion*—as if he would, by a special purpose, make an angel out of a devil.

119. For if that were true, then *Lucifer* and his followers would have *some hope as well*.

120. Instead, he lets his sun shine into their mouths and ears throughout their whole life; he calls them and says, "*Do not harden your hearts with actual sins, so that the Word may resonate in your hearts and take root.*"

121. For it is possible for a poor sinner, dead in sin, to be converted if he will stop focusing on his own mental images, fantasies, or selfish *desires* and—even for just the blink of an eye—*listen to what the Lord is speaking within him*.

122. But the hardened, bitter, and perverse spirit will not listen to the Lord’s voice speaking within himself. Instead, he insists, "The letter! The letter! The written Word *alone* is the thing!" He twists the scripture this way and that and boasts about it, but he will neither tolerate nor listen to the living Word—which has spoken or *expressed* the written word—within himself.

123. But if he wants to gain knowledge through experience, he must first allow himself *to die to the letter* <note>To "die to the letter" means to let go of a purely intellectual or legalistic understanding of scripture in favor of a spiritual experience.</note>; only then does the Spirit make itself truly *living* within the written word.

124. That is, he must die to the literal word and consider himself so unworthy that he does not even deserve the written Word—just like the poor *tax collector* <note>original: "Publican," referencing the parable in Luke 18:9–14.</note> in the Temple. He must realize he has no righteousness regarding the literal word, as one who has lost everything and is *not worthy to lift up his eyes to God*, or for the earth to support him, or to be counted among the number of the children of God.

<margin>i 2 Corinthians 3:6</margin>
125. Then he has lost everything, and <sup>i</sup> *the letter has killed him*, for he has surrendered himself to God's justice and judgment.

<summary>This page argues that divine election and grace are rooted in a person's inner spiritual state rather than an arbitrary choice by God to harden some and save others. It emphasizes that true conversion requires "dying to the letter" of scripture to hear the living Word of God within the soul.</summary>

## Chap. 11. Clarifying the Texts concerning Election.

126. Along with this, he must hope in the pure mercy of God alone, without any worthiness of his own, and plunge himself into it as one who is dead, who has no life in him, letting *anyone* do whatever they will with him. He must despair of all his *own* works and sink <note>original: "demerse"</note> himself solely with hope into the most inward, purest, and most absolute grace of God.

127. This the soul must do; and if it does so, even if it only stays so for the twinkling of an eye, then the first incorporated covenant—namely, the *freely* given, presented, and bestowed grace—takes hold of it and gives itself into the soul.

<margin>k Romans 8:26</margin>

<margin>l Matthew 9:13</margin>

137. But to these others, the foundation in God’s anger is revealed; and here God shows them how life has sprung up out of death, and how Christ destroys the Devil’s kingdom and breaks hell to pieces.

<margin>n Certain Conclusion</margin>
138. Therefore, this is our certain conclusion: <margin>n</margin> no predestined purpose or decree of damnation is made for any man such that it is impossible for him to be converted.

139. Though indeed he *cannot* convert himself, yet his soul has might and power from its very *origin*—out of the eternal knowledge <note>original: "Science"</note> of the abyss—to throw itself into the abyss, into the ground where God generates and *speaks his Word*.

140. In this abyss of the creature, the *free* gift of bestowed grace lies in *all people*; and it inclines itself toward the soul even sooner than the soul turns toward this deep grace.

141. And then the soul may indeed be taken hold of by God’s grace when it falls into Christ’s arms, for he is much readier to give it the possibility and ability than the soul is to desire it.

### The Twelfth Chapter.

->*A brief clarification of some questions that cause reason to stumble, by which it assumes that God hardens humanity through a specific, predestined plan; and how these questions should be understood.*<-

<margin>Acts 13:48.</margin>
