1. **I**t is mentioned in the Acts of the Apostles: *And they believed, as many of them as were destined <note>original: "foreseen, or ordained"</note> for eternal life.* This is the stumbling block of human reason, and reason does not understand it.

2. When did this foreseeing or ordaining begin?

3. You might say: from *eternity*, BEFORE the creature existed.

4. Yes, I say *so too*. But it was IN the creature, not from eternity; for the creature did not exist then.

5. God saw from eternity, in both love and anger, what *would be* if He condensed or compacted <note>original: "compressed, comprised, comprehended, or compacted"</note> the Eternal Nature into a creaturely form.

### Chapter 12.
## A brief clarification of some questions.

6. For he <note>Referring to God</note> saw clearly within himself that if the perfect harmony <note>original: "Temperature"; referring to the balanced state of divine forces</note> were to be divided, separated, or distinguished, and if that separability should form itself into a creature's individual will, there would be conflict <note>original: "Contrariety"</note>; and yet this very separation is the ground of the divine manifestation or revelation.

7. But the Scripture does *not* say that God has ordained the will into separation from eternity to an eternal *evil willing* and an eternal *good willing*, so that every person must will exactly as they are inevitably ordained to do. For the change in the wills of *Adam* and *Lucifer* demonstrates that they were *free* in their wills; however, in the Fall, *Adam* lost his *good-will* <note>original: "Well-willing"</note>.

8. Now, concerning the time after the Fall, it is said: those who were previously foreseen in the eternal will at this time; for the text sounds clearly, saying, *And the Lord added as many of them as were foreseen, or seen in the light of grace.*

<margin>Acts 2:47.</margin>
9. Those to whom the divine eye was open were seen and foreseen at this time out of and within the eternal ground; as it is very clear in the second chapter of *Acts*: *The Lord added daily those who should be saved.*

10. Not those who *were* saved from eternity, but those who *should be*, says the text; those who were then saved out of the eternal election in Jesus Christ, those he daily added to the *Church* or congregation.

11. Why *not all at once?*

12. Answer: They had not yet become saved. They were indeed within the foreseeing or "seeing" of God—that they should be saved—but the ordaining only took place when they were added to the Church upon being saved.

<margin>Acts 2:41.</margin>
13. Why did only *three thousand* souls convert on the Day of Pentecost, and some continually afterwards?

14. They were not yet "foreseen" *within* themselves: that is the meaning of the word { *Versehung* / foreseeing } in this context.

15. When grace begins to stir and breaks through the *VER-*—namely, through the anger—then the creaturely { *VER-SEHEN* / fore-seeing } or { *EIN-SEHEN* / insight } or internal seeing out of the eternal grace begins. <note>The author is playing on the German prefix "ver-", which can imply "covering up" or "blocking," suggesting that grace must break through a blockage for the "seeing" to happen.</note>

16. For how can a thing be ordained from eternity that has *not existed* from eternity?

<margin>Or, to be damned.</margin>
17. How can the soul, when it was an essence <note>original: "Ens"; a Latin term for "being" or "existence"</note> and a scene within the *divine wisdom*, be ordained from eternity to be a *devil*? This would be an abominable thing to say; and yet no other understanding or meaning is currently permitted or admitted by some.

18. If people should build their faith upon such an "ordination from eternity," then all *teaching* would be in vain.

19. Why would grace *need* to be preached to those who cannot fall—those who stand in an irresistible, uncontrollable predestination?

20. This "foreseeing from eternity" is understood to be in *Christ*: those who believe were foreseen from eternity within the Divine Wisdom.

21. This means that when God chose to move himself and introduce nature into "separability" (to reveal himself through creatures), the name JESUS—which is the *highest love of God*—would give itself into the active power <note>original: "Science"; here meaning the dynamic urge or internal principle</note> of the fiery will within that separation. It would introduce itself through that fiery power into the Kingdom of Joy and would change the wrath into a love-fire within the soul of man, which must arise out of that fiery power or root.

<margin>Banner, Ensign, or Mark, or Aim.</margin>
22. Then the grace in the name of Jesus would *wed* itself as a *pledge* or a channel into the "foolish ground" <note>The corrupted state of humanity</note>, just as it was done in Paradise after the Fall.

23. That same pledge or earnest was marked, fixed, or imprinted in the "one only woman’s seed" <note>A reference to the promise in Genesis 3:15</note>, in which the "foreseeing" lay, and from which all humanity proceeded.

<summary>This page argues against the doctrine of absolute double predestination, asserting that God did not ordain souls to evil from eternity but rather provided a "pledge" of grace through Christ to transform the human soul's "fiery" nature into a "love-fire." The author emphasizes that while God foresees salvation, the actual ordaining occurs when an individual responds to grace and is added to the Church.</summary>

<header>Of the <term>Supersensual: That which exists beyond the reach of the physical senses; spiritual or divine.</term> Life.</header>

### Disciple.

**O my loving Master,** please teach me how I may achieve such a constant course of holy penitence <note>original: "penitence"; an act of repentance or sorrow for sins</note>, and such a daily dying from all creaturely objects; for how can I remain continually in repentance?

### Master.

When you leave that which loves you, and love that which hates you; then you may remain continually in repentance.

### Disciple.

What is it that I must leave in this way?

### Master.

**All things** that love and entertain you, because your will loves and entertains them: all things that please and feed you, because your will feeds and cherishes them: all creatures in flesh and blood; in a word, all visible and sensible things, by which either the imagination or the sensory appetite in men are delighted and refreshed. The will of your mind, or your supreme part, must leave and forsake these; and must even consider them all its enemies. This is the leaving of what loves you. 

And the loving of what hates you is the embracing of the reproach <note>original: "reproach"; shame, disapproval, or social disgrace</note> of the world. You must learn then to love the cross of the Lord Jesus Christ, and for his sake to be pleased with the reproach of the world which hates you and derides you. Let this be your daily exercise of penitence: to be crucified to the world, and the world to you. In this way, you shall have continual cause to hate yourself *in the creature* <note>original: "in the creature"; meaning the lower, worldly, or carnal self as opposed to the spirit</note>, and to seek the eternal rest which is *in Christ*. Having attained this rest, your will may safely rest and repose itself there, according to what your Lord Christ has said: "In me you may have rest, but in the world you shall have anxiety: in me you may have peace, but in the world you shall have tribulation."

### Disciple.

How shall I be able to survive in this anxiety and tribulation arising from the world, so as not to lose the eternal peace, or fail to enter into this rest? And how may I recover myself in a temptation such as this, by not sinking under the world, but rising above it through a life that is truly heavenly and supersensual?

### Master.

If once every hour you throw yourself by faith beyond all creatures, beyond and above all sensory perception and understanding—yes, even above discourse and reasoning—into the abyssal <note>original: "abyſſal"; bottomless or unfathomable</note> mercy of God, into the sufferings of our Lord, and into the fellowship of his intercession, and yield yourself fully and absolutely to it; then you shall receive power from above to rule over death and the Devil, and to subdue hell and the world under you. Then you may survive all temptations and be the brighter for them.

### Disciple.

**Blessed** is the man who arrives at such a state as this. But alas! Poor man that I am, how is this possible for me? And what, O my Master, would become of me if I should ever reach that place with my mind where no creature exists? Must I not cry out, "*I am undone!*"

### Master.

**Son,** why are you so discouraged? Keep your heart strong; for you may certainly still attain it. Only believe, and all things are made possible for you. If it were—

<summary>The Master explains that spiritual peace is found by detaching the will from worldly pleasures ("what loves you") and embracing the world's rejection ("what hates you"). He advises the Disciple to hourly cast his mind into God's mercy to rise above the anxieties of the material world.</summary>

# Of the Supersensual Life.
<note>This text is a dialogue from Jakob Böhme's *The Way to Christ* (1622), specifically the section on "The Supersensual Life," which describes a state of being above the reach of the five senses.</note>

If only your **Will**, O you of little courage, could break away from all creatures for one hour, or even for just half an hour, and plunge itself into that place where no creature is or can be; it would immediately be penetrated and clothed with the supreme splendor of the Divine Glory. It would taste the most sweet love of **Jesus** within itself—a sweetness which no tongue can express—and would find within itself the unspeakable words of our Lord concerning his great **mercy**. Your **spirit** would then feel the cross of our Lord **Jesus Christ** to be very pleasing; and would thereafter love the cross more than the honors and goods of the world.

->Disciple.<-

This would indeed be exceedingly well for the **soul**. But what would then become of the **body**, seeing that it must of necessity live in the **created world**? <note>original: "creature" — here meaning the realm of created things or physical nature.</note>

->Master.<-

By this means, the body would be brought into the imitation of our Lord **Christ** and his body. It would stand in the communion of that most blessed body, which was the true temple of the Deity, and participate in all its gracious effects, virtues, and influences. It would live in the **created world** not by **choice**, but only as it is made **subject** to **vanity** <note>In this context, "vanity" refers to the temporary, fleeting, and fragile nature of the physical world (cf. Romans 8:20).</note>, and in the world as it is placed there by the ordination of the Creator for its cultivation and higher advancement. It would groan to be delivered out of it in God’s time and manner, for its perfection and resurrection in eternal liberty and glory, like the glorified body of our Lord and his risen saints.

->Disciple.<-

But since the body, in its present constitution, is made **subject** to **vanity** and lives in a vain image and creaturely shadow—like the life of the lower <note>original: "undergraduated"</note> creatures or brutes, whose breath goes downward to the earth—I am still very afraid that it would continue to depress the mind which is lifted up to God by hanging onto it like a dead weight. I fear it will continue to distract <note>original: "amuse"</note> and perplex the mind, as before, with dreams and trifles, by letting in objects from the outside to draw me down into the world and its hurry, while I would gladly maintain my conversation in heaven even while I am living in the world. What, therefore, must I do with this body so that I may be able to keep up such a desirable conversation and no longer be in subjection to it?

->Master.<-

There is no other way for you that I know of but to **present** the body you complain of (which is the **beast** to be sacrificed) as a **living sacrifice, holy and acceptable to God**. This shall be your rational **service**, by which your body will be put, as you desire, into the imitation of **Jesus Christ**, who said his kingdom was not of this world. Do not be conformed to the world, but be **transformed** by the renewing of your **mind**. This renewed mind is to have dominion over the body, so that you may prove, in both body and mind, what the perfect will of God is, and perform it by his grace operating in you. Consequently, the body—or the **animal life**—being thus offered up, would begin to die, both from **without** and from **within**. From **without** means from the vanity and evil customs and fashions of the world; it would be an utter enemy to all the world's pomp, and to all the gaudiness <note>original: "gaudery"</note>, pageantry, pride, ambition, and haughtiness within it. From **within**, it would die to all the lusts and appetites of the flesh, and would receive a mind and will wholly new for its government and management, being now made subject to the spirit, which would continually be directed toward God—and consequently, that which is subject to the spirit would be directed there as well.

<summary>A Master instructs a Disciple on how the human will can experience divine glory by detaching from the physical world and offering the body as a "living sacrifice" to God.</summary>
<keywords>Jakob Böhme, Supersensual Life, asceticism, Imitation of Christ, transformation of the mind, animal life, spiritual discipline</keywords>

<meta>This page continues the dialogue between the Master and the Disciple regarding the transformation of the physical body into a spiritual temple and the challenges of living a "supersensual" life—one that exists above the level of the five senses—in a world that is often hostile to such a path.</meta>

<page-num>80</page-num>
<header>Of the Supersensual Life.</header>
<sig>2</sig>

And thus your very body has become the Temple of God and of His Spirit, in imitation of your Lord’s body.

->Disciple.<-

But the world would hate it and despise it for doing so, seeing that it must therefore contradict the world, and must live and act quite differently than the world does. This is most certain. And how then can this be endured?

->Master.<-

The soul would not take that as any harm done to it, but would rather rejoice that it has become worthy to be like the image of our Lord Jesus Christ, being transformed from the image of the world. And it would be most willing to bear that cross after our Lord, simply so that our Lord might bestow upon it the influence of His sweet and precious love.

->Disciple.<-

I do not doubt that in some people it may be exactly so. Nevertheless, for my own part, I am in a strait <note>original: "Straight"; here meaning a difficult position or dilemma</note> between two, not yet feeling enough of that blessed influence upon me. Oh, how willingly my body would bear *that*, if I could safely depend upon it according to what is urged! Therefore pardon me, dear sir, in this one thing, if my impatience still further demands: "What would become of the body if the anger of God <note>In Jacob Boehme's theology, the "Anger of God" refers to the harsh, fire-like principle of nature that exists without the tempering light of Divine Love.</note> from within, and the wicked world also from without, should assault it at once, just as "the same really happened to our Lord Christ?"

->Master.<-

Let it be to the body even as it was to our Lord Christ when He was reproached, reviled, and crucified by the world, and when the anger of God so fiercely assaulted Him for our sake. Now, what did He do under this most terrible assault both from without and from within? He commended His soul into the hands of His Father, and so departed from the anguish of this world into eternal joy. Do the same; and His death shall be your life.

->Disciple.<-

Let it be to me as it was to the Lord Christ, and to my body as it was to His; which I have commended into His hands, and for the sake of His name I offer up according to His revealed will. Nevertheless, I am desirous to know what would become of my body as it presses forth from the anguish of this miserable world into the power of the Heavenly Kingdom.

->Master.<-

It would escape from the reproach and contradiction of the world by conforming to the passion of Jesus Christ. The spirit would penetrate into itself; it would sink into the *great love of God*; it would be sustained and refreshed by the most sweet name JESUS; and it would see and find within itself a *new world* springing forth, as if through the anger of God, into *love and eternal joy*. And then a man should wrap his soul in this—in the *great love of God*—and clothe himself with it as with a garment. He should then consider all things equal; because in any creature <note>original: "Creature"; meaning any created thing or being other than God</note> he finds nothing that can give him the least satisfaction *without God*. Because of this, nothing harmful can touch him any longer while he remains in this love, which is indeed stronger than all things. It makes a man invulnerable both from *within* and *without* by removing the sting and poison of created things and destroying the power of death. And whether the body—

These are friends worth having; and though they may be unknown to him here, they will remain his friends beyond death, for all eternity. 

Nor can he lack even outward, natural friends, just as our Lord Christ did not lack them while on earth. For although the high priests and the powerful rulers <note>original: "potentates"</note> of the world could not love him—because they did not belong to him, nor did they have any relationship to him, since he was not of this world—those who were capable of his love and receptive to his words did love him. In the same way, those who love truth and righteousness will love that man and will join themselves to him. Even if they are perhaps outwardly distant or seem to be in disagreement due to their worldly affairs or out of certain social considerations, in their hearts they cannot help but be drawn to him. ...confinements, and everything that springs from a contracted spirit or this evil *selfhood*, because it is a hateful and deadly thing. For *Love possesses* Heaven and dwells within itself—which is to dwell in Heaven. But that which is called "I"—this vile selfhood—possesses the world and worldly things. It also dwells within itself—which is to dwell in Hell—because this self-centeredness is the very root of Hell itself. Therefore, just as Heaven rules the world and as eternity rules time, so also should Love rule the natural, temporal life. There is no other way, nor can there be, to attain that life which is supernatural and eternal, and which you so greatly desire to be led into.

->*Disciple.*<-

Loving Master, I am quite content for this Love to rule in me over the natural life, so that I may attain what is supernatural and supersensual <note>original: "supersensual," meaning that which exists beyond the reach of the five senses</note>. But please tell me now: why must love and hatred, friend and foe, exist together? Would not love alone be better? Why, I ask, are love and trouble joined in this way?

->*Master.*<-

If Love did not dwell in trouble, it would have nothing to love. But because its *substance* <note>original: "substance," referring here to the essential object of Love’s focus</note>—which is the poor soul—is in trouble and pain, Love has a reason to love its *own substance* and to deliver it from pain, so that Love itself may be loved in return by the soul. No one could know what Love is if there were no hatred, or what friendship is if there were no foe to contend with. In short, Love must have something to love so that it can manifest its virtue and power by working to deliver the beloved from all pain and trouble.

->*Disciple.*<-

Please, what is the virtue, the power, the height, and the greatness of Love?

The virtue of Love is *Nothing* and *All*, or that *invisible Nothing* <note>original: "Nothing visible," likely meaning the "No-thing" or the unmanifest source of all existence</note> from which *all things* proceed. Its *power* moves through *all things*; its *height* is as high as God; its *greatness* is as great as God. Its virtue is the principle of all principles; its power supports the heavens and upholds the earth. Its height is higher than the highest heavens, and its greatness is even greater than the manifestation of the Godhead <term>the essential nature or "beingness" of God</term> in the glorious light of the Divine Essence, as it is infinitely capable of greater and greater manifestations throughout all eternity. 

What more can I say? Love is higher than the highest. Love is greater than the greatest. Indeed, in a certain sense, it is greater than God—even while, in the *highest sense of all*, God is Love and Love is God. Since Love is the highest principle, it is the virtue from which all other virtues flow. Since Love is the greatest majesty, it is the power from which all other powers operate. It is the holy magical root, or spiritual <note>original: "ghostly," used here in the archaic sense of "spiritual" (from the German *geistlich*)</note> power, through which all the wonders of God have been performed by the hands of His chosen servants throughout every generation. Whoever finds it, finds *Nothing* and *All Things*.

# Of the Supersensual Life. <note>original: "Superfensual" meaning a life that exists beyond the reach of the physical senses; a spiritual or mystical existence.</note>

When you have turned away from the creature <note>original: "the Creature," referring to any created being or the state of being a created thing rather than the Creator.</note> and from that which is visible, and have become nothing to all that is nature and creature, then you are in that *Eternal One*, which is God himself. Then you shall perceive and feel in your interior the highest virtue of Love. When I said, *its power is through all things*, I meant that which you perceive and find in your own soul and body through experience whenever this great Love is kindled within you. It will burn more than any physical fire can do, just as it did in the ancient prophets, and later in the Apostles, when God conversed with them bodily and when His Spirit descended upon them in the Oratory of Zion <note>The "Oratory of Zion" likely refers to the "upper room" in Jerusalem where the Apostles received the Holy Spirit at Pentecost.</note>. You shall then also see in all the works of God how Love has poured itself forth into all things and penetrates all things. It is the most inward and most outward ground in all things: inwardly in the virtue <term>the inherent power or essence</term> and power of every thing, and outwardly in its figure and form.

And when I said, *its height is as high as God*, you may understand this within yourself; for it brings you to be as high as God himself is by being united to God. This may be seen in our beloved Lord Christ in our humanity. Love has brought that humanity up to the highest throne, above all angelic principalities and powers, and into the very power of the Deity itself.

But when I also said, *its greatness is as great as God*, you are to understand that there is a certain greatness and breadth of heart in Love which is inexpressible. It expands the soul as wide as the whole creation of God. This shall be truly experienced by you, beyond all words, when the throne of Love is set up in your heart.

Moreover, when I said, *its virtue is the principle of all principles*, it is intended for you to understand that Love is the originating cause of all created beings, both spiritual and physical. By virtue of Love, secondary causes <note>Secondary causes are the natural laws and mechanisms through which God (the Primary Cause) operates in the world.</note> move and act as needed, according to certain eternal laws implanted from the beginning in the very constitution of things. This virtue which is in Love is the very life and energy of all the principles of nature, both superior and inferior. It reaches to all worlds and to all types of beings contained within them, as they are the workmanship of Divine Love. It is the *First Mover* and the *First Moved* both in heaven above and on the earth beneath, and in the water under the earth. Because of this, it is given the name of the *Lucid Aleph*, or *Alpha* <note>Aleph is the first letter of the Hebrew alphabet, and Alpha the first of the Greek; both symbolize the divine beginning or the "A" in the alphabet of existence.</note>. By this is expressed the beginning of the *Alphabet of Nature* and of the *Book of Creation and Providence*—or the *Divine Archetypal <term>the original model or pattern</term> Book*—in which is the light of wisdom and the source of all lights and forms.

And when I said, *its power supports the heavens*, you will come to understand that just as the heavens, both visible and invisible, originated from this great principle, so are they necessarily sustained by it. Therefore, if this Love were to be withdrawn even the slightest bit, all the lights, glories, beauties, and forms of the heavenly worlds would immediately sink into darkness and chaos.

And whereas I further said *that it upholds the earth*, this will appear no less evident to you than the former point. You shall perceive it in yourself by daily and hourly experience; for without Love, the earth—even your *own earth* (that is, your body)—would certainly be formless and empty. By the power of Love, the earth has been upheld for this long, despite a foreign, usurped power introduced by the folly of sin. Should Love once fail or recede, there could no longer be any growth or life upon it. Indeed, its very pillars would be completely overthrown. The bond of union—which is that of attraction or magnetism, called the *centripetal power*—being broken and dissolved, everything would run into the utmost disorder. Falling away into fragments, the world would be dispersed like loose dust before the wind.

But when I said, *its height is higher than the highest heavens*, you may also understand this within yourself. For should you ascend in spirit through all the orders of angels and heavenly powers, the power of Love is still undeniably superior to them.

### Of the Supersensual Life.

...all. And just as the Throne of God, who sits upon the Heaven of Heavens, is higher than the highest of them, even so must Love also be—which fills them all and encompasses them all.

And when I spoke of the *Greatness of Love*, saying that it is *greater than the very manifestation of the Godhead in the light of the Divine Essence*, that is also true. For Love enters even into those places where the Godhead is not manifested in this glorious Light, and where God may be said not to dwell. By entering there, Love begins to manifest the Light of the Godhead to the soul; thus the darkness is broken through, and the wonders of the new creation are revealed one after another.

In this way, you shall come to understand truly and fundamentally what the virtue and power of Love is, and how great its height is. It is indeed the *virtue of all virtues*, though it is invisible and appears to be *Nothing*. This is because it is the worker of all things and a powerful *vital energy* passing through all virtues and powers, both natural and supernatural. It is the *power of all powers*; nothing can hinder or obstruct the omnipotence of Love, nor resist its invincible, penetrating might, which passes through the whole of God’s creation, inspecting and governing all things.

Because of this, you may perceive a glimpse of the supreme height and greatness of Omnipotent Love, which infinitely transcends everything human sense and reason can reach. The highest archangels and the greatest powers of Heaven are like dwarfs in comparison to it. Nothing higher or greater can be conceived in God himself, even by the highest and greatest of his creatures. There is such an infinity in it that it encompasses and surpasses all the Divine attributes.

But regarding the statement that *its greatness is greater than God*, that is also very true in the sense it was spoken. For Love, as I observed before, can enter where God does not dwell, since the most high God does not dwell in darkness, but in the light—the darkness of hell being put under his feet. For example, when our beloved Lord Christ was in hell, hell was not the mansion of God or of Christ; hell was not God, nor was it with God, nor could it be with him at all. Hell existed in the darkness and anxiety of nature, and no light of the Divine Majesty entered there. God was not there, for he is not in the darkness or the anguish; but Love was there, and Love destroyed death and conquered hell.

Similarly, when you are in anguish or trouble—which is a *hell within*—God is not the anguish or trouble, nor is he in the anguish or trouble. But his Love is there, and it brings you out of the anguish and trouble into God, leading you into the light and joy of his presence. Even when God hides himself from you, Love is still there and makes him manifest in you. Such is the inconceivable greatness and vastness of *Love*, which will appear to you as *great as God above nature, and greater than God within nature, or as considered in his revealed glory*.

Lastly, when I said, *Whoever finds it, finds Nothing and All Things*, that is also certain and true. But how does one find *Nothing*? I will tell you. He who finds it finds a supernatural, *supersensual abyss* <note>supersensual: beyond the reach of the physical senses</note> which has no ground or *Byss* <term>Byss: a foundation or base (from the Greek 'abyssos', meaning bottomless)</term> to stand on, and where there is no place to dwell. He finds that *Nothing* is like it, and therefore it may appropriately be compared to *Nothing*. It is deeper than anything else and is like *Nothing in relation to All Things*, because it cannot be grasped by any of them. And because it is *Nothing* in this sense, it is therefore free from *all things*. It is that "only Good" which a person cannot express or describe, because there is *nothing to which it can be compared to express it*.

But regarding my final point, that *whoever finds it, finds All Things*, nothing could be truer. It has been the beginning of all things, and it rules...

## DIALOGUE II.

### ARGUMENT.

In this section is described the way to cross the gulf that divides the two principles or states of heaven and hell. It specifically shows how this transition takes place within the soul and what the "partition wall" is that separates us from God.

It explains the breaking down of this partition wall and how it is achieved; what the "center of light" is and how one enters it; and what the light of God and the light of nature are. It describes how they operate in their separate spheres and how to keep them from interfering with each other. It also provides an account of the two wills and their opposition in our fallen state; the "magical wheel of the will" and how its motion may be controlled; the eye in the middle of it; what the "right eye" and the "left eye" represent for the soul, and especially what the *single eye* is and how it is obtained. It covers purification from the contamination of matter; the destruction and total removal of evil as the will moves from being its own "something" into "nothing"; and "naked" <note>Meaning pure, simple, or unadorned</note> and magical faith, which attracts a certain divine substance and garment. Finally, it explains how everything depends on the *will* and proceeds from *one point*; where that point is located and how it may be found; and what is the safest and nearest way to reach the high supersensual state and the internal kingdom of Christ, according to true heavenly *magia* <note>original: "Magia," referring here to divine wisdom or the spiritual power of God's creativity</note> or wisdom.

<summary>The first dialogue concludes with the Master promising to show the Disciple how to find the "pearl" of divine wisdom within himself. The second dialogue begins with an "Argument" outlining the mystical process of soul purification and the transition from the state of nature to the state of God.</summary>

## Of the Supersensual Life.

->Disciple. Master.<-

The Disciple, being very earnest to be more fully instructed on how he might arrive at the supersensual <note>original: "supersensual" — meaning beyond the reach of the physical senses; spiritual or divine</note> life, and how, having found all things, he might become a king over all of God’s works, came again to his Master the next morning. He had spent the night watching in prayer so that he might be prepared to receive and understand the instructions that would be given to him by a divine irradiation <note>original: "irradiation" — a spiritual enlightenment or an inward shining of divine light</note> upon his mind. And the Disciple, after a brief period of silence, bowed himself and spoke out:

->Disciple.<-

O my Master! My Master! I have now endeavored to focus <note>original: "recollect" — to gather one's wandering thoughts or soul into a state of meditative stillness</note> my soul in the presence of God, and to cast myself into that deep where no creature does or can dwell, so that I might hear the voice of my Lord speaking within me and be initiated into that high life of which I heard such great and amazing things yesterday. But, alas! I neither hear nor see as I should. There is still such a partition wall within me which beats back the heavenly sounds as they pass and obstructs the entrance of that light by which alone divine objects are discoverable. Until this wall is broken down, I can have only small hopes—indeed, none at all—of arriving at those glorious attainments which you urged me toward, or of entering into *that place where no creature dwells*, and which you call *Nothing and All Things*. Therefore, please be so kind as to inform me what is required on my part so that this partition which hinders me may be broken or removed.

->Master.<-

This partition is the "creaturely will" <note>original: "creaturely will" — the individual, selfish will of a created being, which acts independently of God</note> in you. This can be broken by nothing except the grace of self-denial, which is the entrance into the true following of Christ; and it can be totally removed by nothing but a perfect conformity with the divine will.

->Disciple.<-

But how shall I be able to *break* this creaturely will that is in me and is at enmity with the divine will? Or, what shall I do to follow Christ in such a difficult path and not faint in a continual course of self-denial and resignation <note>original: "resignation" — the act of surrendering one's own desires and will to God</note> to the will of God?

->Master.<-

This is not to be done by yourself, but by the light and grace of God received into your soul. This grace will, if you do not resist <note>original: "gainsay" — to deny or fight against</note> it, break the darkness that is in you and melt down your own will (which works in the darkness and corruption of nature) and bring it into the obedience of Christ. By this, the partition of the "creaturely self" is removed from between God and you.

->Disciple.<-

I know that I cannot do it by myself. But I would gladly <note>original: "fain" — happily or willingly</note> learn how I must receive this divine light and grace into me, which is to do it for me, if I do not hinder it myself. What, then, is required of me in order to admit this "breaker of the partition" and to promote the achievement of the goals of such admission?

->Master.<-

There is nothing more required of you at first than not to resist this grace which is manifested in you. In the whole process of your work, nothing is required but to be obedient and passive to the *light of God* shining through the darkness of your creaturely being—which does not understand <note>original: "comprehendeth" — used here in the biblical sense of John 1:5, where darkness cannot grasp or overcome the light</note> it, as your natural self reaches no higher than the *light of nature* <note>original: "light of nature" — human reason and natural instinct, as opposed to supernatural revelation</note>.

### *Disciple.*

But is it not possible for me to attain both the Light of God and the Light of outward Nature, and to use them both for ordering my life wisely and prudently?

### *Master.*

I confess that it is right to do so. It is indeed a treasure above all earthly treasures to possess the Light of God and the Light of Nature, each operating in its own sphere; and to have both the Eye of Time and the Eye of Eternity open together at once, and yet not have them interfere with each other.

### *Disciple.*

It is a great satisfaction to me to hear this, as I have been very uneasy about it for some time. But the difficulty lies in how this can be done without them interfering with each other. Therefore, I would dearly like to know—if it were lawful—the boundaries of the one and the other. How may both the Divine and the Natural Light act and operate in their several spheres respectively, to manifest the mysteries of God and Nature and to conduct my outward and inward life?

### *Master.*

So that each of these may be preserved distinct in their several spheres—without confounding heavenly and earthly things or breaking the golden chain of wisdom—it will be necessary, my child, first to wait for and attend to the Supernatural and Divine Light. This is the superior light appointed to govern the "day" <note>referring to a state of spiritual enlightenment</note>, rising in the true East, which is the center of Paradise. It breaks forth in great power from the darkness within you, as if through a pillar of fire and thunderclouds. By doing so, it also reflects a sort of image of itself upon the inferior Light of Nature, which is the only way nature can be kept in its due subordination. Thus, that which is *below* is made subservient to that which is *above*, and that which is *without* to that which is *within*. In this way, there will be no danger of interference; all will go right, and everything will remain in its proper sphere.

### *Disciple.*

Therefore, unless my reason and the Light of Nature are sanctified <note>original: "sanctifyed"; meaning purified or made holy</note> in my soul and illuminated by this superior light—as if from the central East of the holy Light-World, by the Eternal and Intellectual Sun—I perceive there will always be some confusion. I shall never be able to rightly manage what concerns either time or eternity; I must always be at a loss, or break the links of wisdom’s chain.

### *Master.*

It is exactly as you have said. All is confusion if you have nothing more than the dim Light of Nature, or unsanctified and unregenerated <note>meaning the natural mind that has not undergone a spiritual rebirth</note> reason to guide you, and if only the "Eye of Time" is opened in you, which cannot pierce beyond its own limits. Therefore, seek the fountain of light, waiting in the deep ground of your soul for the rising of the "Sun of Righteousness." Through this, the Light of Nature within you, along with all its properties, will be made to shine seven times brighter than usual. For it shall receive the stamp, image, and impression of the <term>Supersensual</term> <note>original: "Superſenſual"; that which exists above or beyond the reach of the physical senses</note> and Supernatural; so that the sensual and rational life will, from then on, be brought into the most perfect order and harmony.

<summary>The Master explains how a seeker can balance divine revelation with natural reason by ensuring that the internal "Divine Light" governs and illuminates the "Light of Nature."</summary>

->*Disciple.*<-

But how am I to wait for the rising of this glorious Sun, and how am I to seek in the Center this Fountain of Light, which may enlighten me throughout and bring all my properties into perfect harmony? I am in Nature <note>original: "Nature" — Here, Böhme refers to the physical world and the inherent biological/psychological makeup of a person.</note>, as I said before; and which way shall I pass through Nature and its light, so that I may come into that supernatural and <term>supersensual ground</term> <note>The realm of spiritual reality that exists beyond the perception of the physical senses.</note> from which this true light—the light of minds—arises? And how can I do this without the destruction of my nature, or quenching its light, which is my reason?

->*Master.*<-

Only cease from your own activity, steadfastly fixing your eye upon *one point*, and with a strong purpose relying upon the promised grace of God in Christ to bring you out of your darkness into his marvelous light. For this end, gather in all your thoughts, and by faith press into the center, laying hold upon the Word of God, which is infallible and which has called you. Be obedient to this call; and be silent before the Lord, sitting alone with him in your inmost and most hidden cell, your mind being centrally united in itself and attending to his will in the patience of hope. So shall your light break forth as the morning; and after its redness has passed, the Sun himself, whom you wait for, shall arise for you, and under his most healing wings you shall greatly rejoice, ascending and descending in his bright and health-giving <note>original: "salutiferous"</note> beams. Behold, this is the true supersensual ground of life.

->*Disciple.*<-

I believe it indeed to be even so. But will not this destroy nature? Will not the light of nature in me be extinguished by this greater light? Or must the outward life then perish, along with the earthly body which I carry?

->*Master.*<-

By no means at all. It is true, the evil nature will be destroyed by it; but by its destruction you can be no loser, but very much a gainer. The *eternal band* <note>original: "Eternal Band" — Böhme's term for the fundamental forces that bind the soul and nature together.</note> of nature is the same afterward as before, and the properties are the same. Thus, nature is only advanced and improved <note>original: "meliorated"</note> by this; and its light, or human reason, is only made useful by being kept within its due bounds and regulated by a superior light.

->*Disciple.*<-

Please, therefore, let me know how this inferior light ought to be used by me; how it is to be kept within its due bounds; and in what manner the superior light regulates and ennobles it.

->*Master.*<-

Know then, my beloved son, that if you will keep the light of nature within its own proper bounds and make use of it in just subordination to the light of God, you must consider that there are in your soul *two wills*: an *inferior will*, which drives you toward things outside and below; and a *superior will*, which draws you to things within and above. These two wills are now set together, as it were back-to-back, and in direct opposition to each other; but in the beginning it was not so. For this opposition of the soul in these two is nothing more than the *effect of the fallen state*; since before that, they were placed one under the other—that is, the superior will...

# Of the Supersensual Life

The superior should be *above*, as the Lord, and the inferior *below*, as the subject. And this is how it ought to have continued. You must also further consider that, answering to these two Wills, there are likewise two *Eyes* in the soul, by which they are separately directed; because these *Eyes* are not united in one single view, but look in quite contrary directions at once. They are set against each other in a similar way, without a common medium to join them. And therefore, so long as this double-sightedness remains, it is impossible for there to be any agreement in the determination of this or that Will. This is very plain: and it shows the necessity that this malady, arising from the disunion of the rays of vision, be somehow remedied and redressed, in order to have true discernment in the mind. Both these eyes, therefore, must be made to unite by a concentration of rays; there being nothing more dangerous than for the mind to remain in this duplicity, and not to seek to arrive at unity. You perceive, I know, that you have two wills in you, one set against the other—the superior and the inferior—and that you also have two eyes within, one against another; of which one *Eye* may be called the *Right Eye*, and the other the *Left Eye*. You doubtless perceive too, that it is according to the *Right Eye* that the wheel <note>original: "Wheel"; in Boehme’s philosophy, this refers to the "wheels" or "properties" of nature and the soul’s internal movements</note> of the superior will is moved; and that it is according to the motion of the *Left Eye* that the contrary wheel in the lower will is turned about.

->*Disciple.*<-

I perceive this, Sir, to be very true; and this is what causes a continual combat in me, and creates greater anxiety for me than I am able to express. Nor am I unacquainted with the disease of my own soul, which you have so clearly declared. Alas! I perceive and lament this malady, which so miserably disturbs my sight; from which I feel such irregular and convulsive motions drawing me this way and that way. The Spirit does not see as the flesh sees; neither does, or can, the flesh see as the Spirit sees. <note>A reference to Galatians 5:17: "For the flesh lusteth against the Spirit, and the Spirit against the flesh."</note> Hence the Spirit wills against the flesh, and the flesh wills against the Spirit in me. This has been my difficult case. And how shall it be remedied? O, how may I arrive at the unity of will, and how come into the unity of vision!

->*Master.*<-

Mark now what I say: The *Right Eye* looks forward in you into *Eternity*. The *Left Eye* looks backward in you into *Time*. If you now allow yourself to be always looking into nature and the things of *Time*, and to be leading the will and seeking something for itself in its desire, it will be impossible for you ever to arrive at the unity which you wish for. Remember this, and be on your watch. Do not give your mind leave to enter into, nor to fill itself with, that which is outside of you; neither look backward upon yourself, but quit yourself and look forward upon *Christ*. Do not let your *Left Eye* deceive you by continually making one representation after another, and thereby stirring up an earnest longing in the self-propriety <note>original: "Self-Propriety"; refers to the ego, self-centeredness, or the sense of "owning" one's own will</note>; but let your *Right Eye* command this *Left* back, and attract it to you, so that it may not gad abroad <note>original: "gad abroad"; to wander restlessly or aimlessly in search of pleasure</note> into the wonders and delights of nature. Indeed, it is better to pluck it quite out and cast it from you than to suffer it to proceed forth without restraint into nature and to follow its own lusts <note>A reference to Matthew 5:29 regarding plucking out an eye that causes one to sin.</note>. However, there is no necessity for this, since both eyes may become very useful if ordered rightly; and both the Divine and natural light may subsist together in the soul and be of mutual service to each other. But you shall never arrive at the unity of vision or uniformity of will except by entering fully into the will of our Savior Christ, and therein bringing the eye of *Time* into the eye of *Eternity*; and then descending, by means of this united vision, through the light of God into the light of nature.

# Of the Supersensual Life.

## Disciple.

So then, if I can only enter into the will of my Lord and remain there, I am safe. I may both attain the light of God in the spirit of my soul and see with the eye of God—that is, the eye of eternity in the eternal ground of my will. I may also, at the same time, enjoy the light of this world nonetheless, not degrading but rather adorning the light of nature. By beholding eternal things with the eye of eternity and natural things with the eye of nature, I can contemplate the wonders of God in both, while also sustaining the life of my outward <term>vehicle</term><note>original: "vehicle"; here meaning the physical body as a vessel for the soul</note> or body.

## Master.

That is exactly right. You have understood well. You desire now to enter into the will of God and to remain there as in the <term>supersensual</term><note>original: "supersensual"; meaning that which is beyond the reach of the five senses; the spiritual realm</note> ground of light and life. In that state, you may behold both time and eternity in His light, and bring all the <term>wonders</term><note>original: "wonders"; the various manifestations of God's power and creativity in the physical world</note> created by God for the outer life into the inner life. Thus, you may eternally rejoice in them to the glory of Christ, once the barrier of your self-centered will is broken down and the eye of your spirit is made simple in and through the eye of God manifesting itself in the center of your life. Let it be so now, for it is God's will.

## Disciple.

But it is very hard to be always looking forward into eternity, and consequently to attain to this *single eye* and *simplicity of divine vision*. The entrance of a naked soul into the will of God—shutting out all imaginations and desires, and breaking down the strong barrier which you mention—is indeed quite frightening and shocking to human nature in its present state. Oh, what shall I do so that I may reach this which I so much long for?

## Master.

My son, do not let the eye of nature, which seeks after worldly wonders, turn away from that eye which is turned inward toward divine freedom and into the eternal light of the holy majesty. Instead, let the eye of nature draw those wonders to you by uniting with that heavenly internal eye—wonders which are externally worked out and manifested in visible nature. For while you are in the world and have an honest employment, you are certainly obliged by the order of providence to labor in it and to finish the work given to you according to your best ability, without complaining in the least. You should seek out and manifest the wonders of nature and <term>art</term><note>original: "art"; in this context, human skill, craft, and technology as opposed to natural growth</note> for God's glory.

Since whatever nature is, it is all the work and art of God; and whatever art is, it is still God's work and His art, rather than any skill or cleverness of man. All things in both art and nature serve abundantly to manifest the wonderful works of God, so that He may be glorified for all and in all. Indeed, if you know rightly how to use them, all things serve only to gather you more inward and to draw your spirit into that majestic light where the original patterns and forms of visible things are to be seen. Keep, therefore, in the center, and do not move away from the presence of God revealed within your soul. No matter how much noise and bustle the world and the Devil make to draw you out, pay them no mind; they cannot hurt you. Your "eye of reason" is permitted to seek food, and your hands are permitted to labor to get food for the earthly body. But then, this eye must not enter into the food prepared with greed—which would be covetousness—but must, in a state of surrender, simply bring it before the eye of God in your spirit. Then you must seek to place it close to this very eye, without letting it go. Mark this lesson well.

# Of the Supersensual Life

Though your hands or your head may be at work, your heart should nevertheless rest in God. God is a Spirit; dwell in the Spirit, work in the Spirit, pray in the Spirit, and do everything in the Spirit. For remember that you also are a spirit, and were created in the image of God. Therefore, ensure you do not attract **matter** <note>In this context, "matter" refers to worldly attachments, physical desires, and the heavy, spiritual "density" that pulls the soul away from God.</note> into yourself through your desire. Instead, abstract yourself as much as possible from all matter whatsoever. Standing thus in the center, present yourself as a naked spirit before God in simplicity and purity; and be sure your spirit draws in nothing but Spirit.

You will still be greatly enticed to draw in matter and to gather what the world calls **substance**, so that you might have something visible to rely on. But by no means consent to the Tempter, nor yield to the lusts of your flesh against the spirit. For by doing so, you will inevitably darken the Divine Light within you. Your spirit will become stuck in the dark, greedy root, and from the fiery source of your soul, it will blaze out in pride and anger. Your will shall be chained to earthliness and shall sink through anguish into darkness and materiality; you will never be able to reach that quiet liberty or stand before the majesty of God. Since this would open a door for the one who reigns in the **corruption of matter** <note>referring to the Devil or the fallen state of the physical world</note>, the Devil may perhaps roar at you for this refusal. Nothing can vex him more than such a silent withdrawal of the soul and the turning of it toward the point of rest, away from everything worldly and external. But ignore him; do not admit even the slightest dust of that matter to which he may claim any right. To you, any **matter** drawn in by the desire of your will will be total darkness. It will obscure God's majesty from you and close your spiritual eye by hiding the light of His beloved countenance. This is what the Serpent longs to do, but he longs in vain unless you permit your imagination—following his suggestion—to receive the alluring matter. Otherwise, he can never get in. 

Behold then: if you desire to see God’s light in your soul and be divinely illuminated and guided, this is the direct path you must take. Do not let the eye of your spirit enter into matter or fill itself with anything at all, whether in heaven or earth. Instead, let it enter through a naked **faith** into the light of God's majesty. Thus, receive the light of God through pure love and attract the Divine power into yourself, putting on the Divine body and growing in it to the full maturity of the humanity of Christ.

->*Disciple*<-

As I said before, I say again: this is very difficult. I understand well enough that my spirit ought to be free from the contagion of matter and be wholly empty so that it may admit the Spirit of God. I also understand that this Spirit will not enter except where the will enters into **nothingness** <note>original: "Nothing." A mystical term for a state of total detachment from self-will and worldly desire.</note> and resigns itself in the **nakedness of faith** and the **purity of love** to God's guidance—feeding spiritually <note>original: "magically." In Boehmian theology, "magical" refers to the creative power of the will or the soul's ability to "draw in" spiritual realities.</note> upon the **Word of God** and clothing itself thereby with a **Divine substance**. But alas, how hard it is for the will to **sink into nothing**, to **attract nothing**, and to **imagine nothing**!

->*Master*<-

Granted that it is so. Is it not surely worth your while, and worth everything you could ever do?

->*Disciple*<-

It is so; I must confess it.

->*Master*<-

But perhaps it may not be as hard as it first appears. Only make the trial and be in earnest. What is required of you but to stand still and see the salvation of your God? <note>A reference to Exodus 14:13.</note> Could you desire anything less? Where is the hardship in this? You have nothing to care for, nothing to desire in this life, and nothing to imagine—

By this means you shall come to hear and see God; and after this earthly life is ended, to see with the eye of eternity all the wonders of God and of nature. Here the virtue and power of the love of God is displayed. Here the height and depth, the breadth and length of it are revealed, as much as the capacity of your soul can contain. By this you shall come into that Ground out of which all things originate, and in which they exist; and in it you shall reign over all God’s works, as a prince of God.

Pray tell me, dear Master, where does it dwell in man?

->Master<-

->*Disciple.*<-

Where is that place in a person where they do not live within themselves?

It is the resigned <term>original: "resigned ground"; the mystical state of *Gelassenheit*, or yielding one's will entirely to God</term> ground of a soul, to which nothing clings.

Where is this "ground" in any soul where nothing will stick? Or where is that which remains and does not dwell within something else?

It is the center of rest and motion in the resigned will of a truly contrite spirit, which is crucified to the world. Consequently, this center of the will is impenetrable to the world, the devil, and hell. Nothing in all the world can enter into it or cling to it, no matter how many devils might join in a conspiracy against it. This is because the will is dead to the world with Christ, but is brought to life <note>original: "quickened"</note> with him in its very center, according to his blessed image. This is the place where the human "self" does not live, and where no *Self* remains or can remain.

->*Disciple.*<-

Oh, where is this naked ground of the soul, free of all "self"? And how shall I reach the hidden center where God dwells, and not man? Tell me plainly, dear sir, where it is, and how I may find and enter into it?

->*Master.*<-

This shall appear wherever the soul has slain its own will and no longer wills anything from itself, but only as God wills and as his Spirit moves upon the soul. Where the love of self is banished, there the love of God dwells. For every bit of the soul's own will that is dead to itself, the will of God—which is his love—takes up an equal amount of room in that soul. The reason for this is as follows: where the soul's own will previously sat, there is now nothing; and where nothing else exists, that is the place where the love of God works alone.

->*Disciple.*<-

But how shall I understand <note>original: "comprehend"</note> it?

->*Master.*<-

If you try to grasp <note>original: "comprehend"</note> it, then it will fly away from you; but if you surrender yourself wholly up to it, then it will stay with you, become the life of your life, and become natural to you.

->*Disciple.*<-

And how can this happen without me dying, or the complete destruction of my will?

->*Master.*<-

Upon this entire surrender and yielding up of your will, the love of God within you becomes the life of your nature. It does not kill you, but brings you to life <note>original: "quickeneth"</note>. You, who are now dead to yourself in your own will, are made alive according to its true life, even the life of God. And then you live, yet not for your own will, but you live for God's will; because your will has from that point forward become his will. So then it is no longer your will, but the will of God—no longer the love of yourself, but the love of God—which moves and works within you. Then, being thus embraced <note>original: "comprehended"</note> by it, you are dead indeed as to

->Master.<-

They all seek it in *something* <note>original: "somewhat"; here referring to a specific object, attachment, or self-centered desire</note>, and so they do not find it. For where there is something for the soul to cling to, there the soul finds only *that specific thing*, and takes its rest there, until she sees that it is to be found in nothing, and goes out of the "something" into "nothing"—even into that nothing out of which all things may be made. The soul here says:

“*I have nothing*, for I am utterly naked and stripped of everything.
“*I can do nothing*; for I have no kind of power, but am like water poured out.
“*I am nothing*; for all that I am is no more than an image of being, and only God is to me ‘I AM’; and so, sitting down in my own nothingness, I give glory to the Eternal Being, and *will nothing* of myself, so that God may *will everything* in me, being my God and all things to me.”

This is why so very few find this most precious treasure in the soul, though everyone would so gladly have it; and they might also have it, were it not for this *something* in everyone which hinders <note>original: "letteth"</note> them.

->Disciple.<-

But if Love should offer itself to a soul, could not that soul find it, or lay hold of it, without going into "nothing" for it?

->Master.<-

Truly, no. Men seek and do not find because they do not seek it in the naked *foundation* <note>original: "Ground"; the fundamental essence or depth of the soul</note> where it lies, but in something or other where it never will be, nor can be. They seek it in *their own will*, and they do not find it. They seek it in their *self-desire*, and they do not meet with it. They look for it in an *image*, or in an *opinion*, or in *affection*, or a natural *devotion* and *fervor*, and they lose the substance by thus hunting after a shadow. They search for it in something sensible <note>perceptible by the senses</note> or imaginary—in something for which they may have a more peculiar natural inclination or attachment—and so they miss what they seek for want of diving into the supersensual and supernatural foundation where the treasure is hidden. Now, should Love graciously condescend to offer itself to such as these, and even to present itself evidently before the eye of their spirit, it would still find no place in them at all; neither could it be held by them or remain with them.

->Disciple.<-

Why not, if Love should be willing and ready to offer itself and to stay with them?

->Master.<-

Because the *imaginary concepts* <note>original: "imaginariness"; the tendency of the mind to create its own mental images or "idols" of truth rather than receiving the reality of God</note> which are in their own will have set themselves up in its place. And so this state of imagination would try to have Love within itself; but Love flees away, for that state is its prison. Love may offer itself, but it cannot remain where *self-desire* attracts or creates images. Only that will which attracts nothing, and to which nothing clings, is capable of receiving it; for Love dwells only in "nothing," as I said, and therefore they do not find it.

<summary>The Master explains that the "Treasure" of divine Love is missed by most because they seek it through their own will and specific attachments rather than in the "nothingness" of self-surrender. Love cannot be imprisoned by human desire or mental images; it only dwells in a soul that has been stripped of selfhood.</summary>
<keywords>Jacob Böhme, mysticism, self-denial, Nothingness, divine love, self-will, the Ground of the soul, spiritual seeker</keywords>

<page-num>96</page-num>
# Of the Supersensual Life

->Disciple.<-

**If it dwells only in nothing, what is its function <note>original: "Office"</note> in nothing?**

->Master.<-

The function of Love here is to penetrate incessantly into "something"; and if it penetrates into and finds a place in something that is standing still and at rest, then its business is to take possession of it. And once it has taken possession there, it rejoices in it with its flaming Love-fire, just as the sun does in the visible world. Then its function is to continually ignite a fire in this "something" which may burn it up; and then, with those flames, to exceedingly inflame itself and raise the heat of the Love-fire by it, even seven degrees <note>In Böhme’s mystical philosophy, the "seven degrees" or "seven properties" represent the process of spiritual and natural manifestation.</note> higher.

->Disciple.<-

**O loving Master, how am I to understand this?**

->Master.<-

If it once ignites a fire within you, my son, you shall then certainly feel how it consumes everything it touches. You shall feel it burning up your selfhood and swiftly devouring all *egoity* <note>original: "Egoity"; the self-centered state of the "I" or "me" when separated from God</note>—or that which you call *I* and *me*—as it exists in a separate root, divided from the Deity, the fountain of your being. And when this ignition takes place in you, then Love rejoices so greatly in your fire that you would not want to be out of it for all the world; indeed, you would rather suffer yourself to be killed than to enter into *your "something"* <note>the state of being a separate, self-willed individual</note> again. This fire must now grow hotter and hotter until it has perfected its function within you; therefore, it will not give up until it reaches the seventh degree. Its flame will then be so great that it will never leave you, even if it should cost you your temporal life; it would go with you in its sweet, loving fire into death. And even if you went into hell, it would break hell into pieces for your sake. Nothing is more certain than this, for it is stronger than death and hell.

->Disciple.<-

Enough, my dearest Master; I can no longer endure anything diverting me from it. But how shall I find the shortest way to it?

->Master.<-

Where the way is hardest, go there; and what the world throws away, take that up. What the world does, do not do; but in all things walk contrary to the world. In this way, you take the shortest path to what you are seeking.

->Disciple.<-

**If I should walk contrary to other people in all things, I would surely be in a very restless and sad state; and the world would not fail to consider me a madman.**

->Master.<-

I am not telling you, child, to do harm to anyone, or thereby to create misery or restlessness for yourself. This is not what I mean by walking contrary to the world in everything. But because the world, as the world, loves only deceit and vanity and walks in false and treacherous ways, if you intend to act in a completely contrary...

<summary>The Master explains that divine Love acts as a fire that consumes the "egoity" or self-centered nature of the seeker, eventually leading them to a state of unity with the Deity. He advises the Disciple to find the path to this state by walking contrary to the vain and deceitful ways of the world.</summary>
<keywords>Love-fire, Egoity, selfhood, spiritual purification, seven degrees, the World, mystical path, Jakob Böhme</keywords>

# Of the Supersensual Life.

[...] part to the ways of it, without any exception or reserve whatsoever, walk only in the right way, which is called the *Way of Light*, just as the way of the world is properly the *Way of Darkness*. For the right way—even the Path of Light—is contrary to all the ways of the world.

But while you are afraid of creating trouble and unrest <note>original: "inquietude"</note> for yourself by doing this, that will indeed be the case according to the flesh. In the world you must have trouble, and your flesh will not fail to be restless <note>original: "unquiet"</note> and give you cause for continual repentance. Nevertheless, in *this very anxiety* of soul—arising either from the world or the flesh—divine love most willingly ignites <note>original: "enkindle"</note> itself. Its cheering and conquering fire is made to blaze forth with even greater strength to destroy that evil. 

And since you also say that the world will consider you mad for this, it is true that the world will be likely enough to judge you as a madman for walking contrary to it. You should not be surprised if the children of this world laugh at you, calling you a silly fool. For the way to the love of God is folly to the world, but it is wisdom to the children of God. Therefore, whenever the world perceives this holy fire of love in God’s children, it immediately concludes that they have become fools and are *beside themselves*. 

But to the children of God, what is despised by the world is the greatest treasure. Indeed, it is such a great treasure that no life can express it, nor any tongue even name what this inflammatory, all-conquering love of God is. It is brighter than the sun; it is sweeter than anything called sweet; it is stronger than all strength; it is more nourishing <note>original: "nutrimental"</note> than food; more cheering to the heart than wine, and more pleasant than all the joy and pleasantness of this world. Whoever obtains it is richer than any monarch on Earth; and he who gains it is nobler than any emperor can be, and more powerful <note>original: "potent"</note> and absolute than all power and authority.

### OF
# HEAVEN AND HELL.
### A
# DIALOGUE
### BETWEEN
## JUNIUS A SCHOLAR, AND THEOPHORUS HIS MASTER.

<margin>Decorative woodcut initial T</margin>
**T**HE Scholar asked his Master, saying: Where does the soul go when the body dies?

His Master answered him: There is no necessity for it to go anywhere.

"What! No?" said the inquisitive Junius. "Must the soul not leave the body at death, and go either to heaven or hell?"

"It does not need to go out," replied the venerable Theophorus. "Only the outward mortal life and the body shall separate themselves from the soul. The soul already has heaven and hell within itself, just as it is written: *The Kingdom of God comes not with observation; neither shall they say, 'Look here!' or 'Look there!' For behold, the Kingdom of God is within you.* <note>Luke 17:20-21</note> And whichever of the two—that is, either heaven or hell—is revealed in it, in that state the soul remains."

Here Junius said to his Master: "This is hard to understand. Does it not enter into heaven or hell, as a man enters into a house; or as one goes through a hole or window into an unknown place? Does it not go into another world?"

The Master spoke and said: "No. There is truly no such kind of entering in; because heaven and hell are everywhere, being universally co-extended <term>co-extended: existing together in the same space or time</term>."

"How is that possible?" said the scholar. "What, can heaven and hell both be present here, where we are now sitting? And if one of them might be, can you make me believe that both could ever be here together?"

Then spoke the Master in this manner: "I have said that heaven is present everywhere; and it is true. For God is in heaven; and God is everywhere. I have also said that hell must likewise be everywhere; and that is also true. For the *wicked one*, who is the devil, is in hell; and the whole world, as the Apostle has taught us, lies in the *wicked one*, or the *evil one*; <note>1 John 5:19</note> which is as much as to say, not only that the devil is in the world, but also that the world is in the devil. And if it is in the devil, then it is in hell too, because he is there. So hell, therefore, is everywhere, as well as heaven; which is the thing that was to be proved."

The scholar, startled by this, said: "Please, help me to understand this."

To whom the Master replied: "Understand then what heaven is: It is but the turning of the will into the *love of God*. Wherever you find God manifesting himself in—"

<summary>A philosophical dialogue between a student and a teacher exploring the nature of the afterlife, arguing that heaven and hell are internal spiritual states rather than physical locations. The teacher explains that because God and the devil are both present in the world, their respective realms exist everywhere simultaneously.</summary>
<keywords>Junius, Theophorus, Jakob Böhme, mysticism, heaven, hell, internal kingdom, spiritual state, soul, omnipresence of God</keywords>

Love—there you find Heaven, without traveling even one foot for it. And by this, understand also what Hell is, and *where* it is. I say to you, it is nothing but the *turning of the will into the wrath of God*. Wherever the anger of God manifests itself more or less, there certainly is more or less of Hell, in whatever place it may be. So it is only the turning of your will either into His love or into His anger; and you are accordingly either in Heaven or in Hell. Mark this well. And this happens even in this present life, of which St. Paul spoke when he said, *Our conversation <note>original: "Conversation"; in the 17th century, this meant one's citizenship, social conduct, or way of life (Philippians 3:20).</note> is in Heaven*. And the Lord Christ also says: *My sheep hear my voice, and I know them, and they follow me, and I give them eternal life; and none shall pluck them out of my hand*. Observe, he does not say, "*I will give*" them life after this life is ended; but "*I give*" them—that is, now, during the time of this life. And what else is this gift of Christ to his followers but an eternity of life, which certainly can be nowhere but in Heaven? Also, if Christ is certainly in Heaven, and those who follow him in the regeneration <note>original: "Regeneration"; the spiritual rebirth or process of being made new in Christ.</note> are in his hand, then they are where he is, and so cannot be outside of Heaven. Yea, moreover, no one shall be able to pluck them out of Heaven, because it is he who holds them there, and they are in his hand, which nothing can resist. All, therefore, consists in the turning in, or entering of the will into Heaven, by hearing the voice of Christ, and both knowing him and following him. And so it is also on the contrary. Do you understand this?

His Scholar said to him: I think, in part, I do. But how does this entering of the will into Heaven come to pass?

The Master answered him: I will endeavor to satisfy you in this; but you must be very attentive to what I shall say to you. Know then, my son, that when the ground <term>original: "Ground" (German: *Ungrund* or *Grund*); the fundamental essence or deepest foundation of the soul where it meets God.</term> of the will yields itself up to God, then it sinks out of its own self, and out of and beyond all ground and place that is or can be imagined, into a certain unknown deep where God alone is manifest, and where He alone works and wills. And then it becomes nothing to itself, as to its own working and willing; and so God works and wills in it. And God dwells in this resigned will, by which the soul is sanctified and so fitted to come into divine rest. Now, in this case, when the body breaks <note>i.e., when the person dies.</note>, the soul is so thoroughly penetrated all over with the divine love, and so thoroughly illuminated with the divine light—just as a glowing hot iron is by the fire—that by being penetrated throughout, it loses its darkness and becomes bright and shining. Now this is the *hand of Christ*, where God’s love thoroughly inhabits the soul and is in it a shining light and a new, glorious life. And then the soul is in Heaven and is a temple of the Holy Ghost; it is itself the very Heaven of God, wherein He dwells. Look, this is the entering of the will into Heaven; and this is how it comes to pass.

Please, sir, proceed, said the Scholar, and let me know how it fares on the other side.

The Master said: The godly soul, you see, is in the *hand of Christ*—that is, in Heaven, as he himself has told us—and you have heard in what manner this comes to be so. But the ungodly soul is not willing in this lifetime to come into the divine resignation <term>original: "Resignation" (German: *Gelassenheit*); the act of yielding one's self-will and ego to God's will.</term> of its will, or to enter into the will of God. Instead, it goes on still in its own lust and desire, in vanity and falsehood, and so enters into the will of the Devil. It receives into itself nothing but wickedness—nothing but lying, pride, covetousness, envy, and wrath—and it gives up its will and whole desire to those things. This is the vanity of the will; and this same vanity, or vain shadow, must also in like manner be manifested in the soul which has yielded itself up to be its servant. It must work therein, just as the love of God works in the regenerated will, and penetrate it all over, as fire does iron.

<summary>The Master explains that Heaven and Hell are internal states of the will rather than geographical locations, where a soul "resigned" to God's love experiences Heaven even in this life. Conversely, a soul that follows its own selfish desires and "vanity" enters into the wrathful state of Hell.</summary>
