And it is not possible for this soul to come into the *Rest of God*, because God’s anger is manifested within it and works within it. Now, when the *body* is separated from this soul, then the eternal melancholy and despair begin; for the soul now finds that it has become nothing but vanity <note>original: "Vanity" — here meaning worthlessness, futility, or a lack of true substance</note>, even a vanity most distressing to itself, a distracting fury, and a self-tormenting abomination. Now it perceives itself disappointed by everything it had previously imagined; it finds itself blind, naked, wounded, hungry, and thirsty, without the slightest prospect of ever being relieved or obtaining even one drop of the water of eternal life. It feels itself to be a mere devil to itself, and its own vile executioner and tormentor. It is frightened by its own ugly, dark form, appearing as a most hideous and monstrous worm; it would gladly flee from itself if it could, but it cannot, being fast bound with the chains of the dark nature into which it had sunk itself while in the flesh. And so, having neither learned nor accustomed itself to sink down into the divine grace, and being also strongly possessed by the idea of God as an angry and jealous God, the poor soul is both afraid and ashamed to bring its will into God—the only act by which deliverance might possibly come to it. The soul is afraid to do so, fearing it will be consumed in the process, as it perceives the Deity as nothing but a *devouring fire* <note>original: "meer devouring Fire" — a reference to Hebrews 12:29</note>. The soul is also ashamed to do it, being confounded by its own nakedness and monstrosity. Therefore, it would—if possible—hide itself from the majesty of God and cover its abominable form from His most holy eye, even by casting itself still deeper into the darkness. Therefore, it *will not* enter into God; indeed, it *cannot* enter with its false will. Even if it should strive to enter, it cannot enter into the Love because of the will that has reigned within it. For such a soul is held captive in wrath; indeed, it is itself nothing but *wrath*, having—by the false desire it awakened within itself—captured and shut itself up within that wrath, transforming itself into its very nature and property.

And since the light of God does not shine in it, nor does the love of God incline toward it, the soul is, moreover, a *great darkness*. It is also an anxious <term>fire-source</term> <note>original: "Fire-Source" — in Böhme’s philosophy, this represents the agonizing, burning hunger of the soul's own raw desires when separated from the cooling light of God</note>, carrying a hell within itself and being unable to discern the slightest glimpse of the light of God or feel the smallest spark of His love. Thus, it dwells within itself as in hell and does not need to enter a physical hell or be carried there; for in whatever place it may be, as long as it is within itself, it is in hell. And though it should travel far and cast itself many hundreds of thousands of miles from its present place to escape hell, it would still remain in that hellish source and darkness.

"If this is so," said the Scholar to *Theophorus*, "then how does it happen that a heavenly soul does not perfectly perceive the heavenly light and joy during this life? And why does the soul that is 'without God in the world' not feel hell here as much as hereafter? Why should they not both be perceived and felt as well in this life as in the next, seeing that both of them are within man, and one of them (as you have shown) works in every man?"

To whom *Theophorus* immediately returned this answer: "The Kingdom of Heaven is active in the saints and reveals itself through *faith*. Those who carry God within them and live by His Spirit find the *Kingdom of God in their faith*; and they feel the love of God in their *faith*, by which the will has surrendered itself to God and is made God-like. In short, everything is experienced within them by *faith*, which is to them the evidence of eternal invisible things and a great manifestation in their spirit of this divine kingdom that is within them. But their natural life is nevertheless surrounded by flesh and blood. Because the flesh stands in opposition to the spirit, and—due to the <term>Fall</term> <note>The biblical Fall of Man, which Böhme interprets as a descent into the "anger" of the material world</note>—is placed within the principle of God’s anger and surrounded by the world (which can by no means be reconciled to faith), these faithful souls cannot help but be very much exposed to attacks from this world in which they are sojourners; neither can..."

<summary>Theophorus explains that hell is an internal state of wrath and darkness created by the soul's own will, while the Kingdom of Heaven is experienced through faith despite the limitations of the physical body.</summary>

<meta>The previous page concludes with a discussion on how the soul is surrounded by the "kingdom of this world" while yet living in the body.</meta>

# *Of the Supersensual Life* <note>original: "Supersensual Life"; refers to a life that exists above or beyond the reach of the five physical senses.</note>

They are unaware of being thus surrounded by flesh and blood and by this world's vain desires <note>original: "Lust"</note>, which do not cease to continually penetrate the outward mortal life and to tempt them in many ways, just as happened to Christ. From this, the world on one side and the Devil on the other—not without the curse of God’s anger within flesh and blood—thoroughly penetrate and sift through one's life. 

It so happens that the soul is often in anxiety when these three <note>The world, the Devil, and the "curse" or corruption of the physical body.</note> all set upon it together, and when Hell thus assaults the life and seeks to manifest itself in the soul. But the soul, upon this, sinks down into the hope of the grace of God and stands like a beautiful rose in the midst of thorns, until the kingdom of this world shall fall away from it at the death of the body. Then the soul first becomes truly manifest in the love of God and in His kingdom, which is the kingdom of love, having from then on nothing more to hinder it. But during this life, she <note>Boehme traditionally refers to the Soul using feminine pronouns.</note> must walk with Christ in this world; and then Christ delivers her out of her own Hell by penetrating her throughout with His love, standing by her in Hell, and even changing her Hell into Heaven.

But regarding what you asked further—why do the souls who are separated from God not feel Hell in this world? I answer: They carry it about with them in their wicked consciences, but they do not know it because the world has put out their eyes, and its deadly cup has cast them into a sleep—a most fatal sleep. Nevertheless, it must be admitted that the wicked do frequently feel Hell within them during this mortal life, though they may not recognize that it is Hell because of the earthly vanity <note>original: "Vanity"; meaning emptiness, worthlessness, or futile worldly pursuits.</note> which clings to them from the outside, and the physical pleasures and amusements with which they are intoxicated. 

Furthermore, it should be noted that the outward life in every such person still possesses the light of outward nature, which rules in that life; so the pain of Hell cannot be revealed as long as that light is in control. But when the body dies or breaks away, so that the soul can no longer enjoy such temporary pleasure and delight, nor the light of this outward world (which is then entirely extinguished for it), then the soul stands in an eternal hunger and thirst after the same vanities it loved here. Yet it can reach nothing but that false will <note>The "false will" is the self-centered desire that turns away from God.</note> which it had impressed upon itself while in the body, and in which it had lived to its great loss. 

Now, whereas it had too much of its own will in this life and yet was not satisfied with it, after this separation by death, it has as little of it. This creates an everlasting thirst for that which it can never obtain again and causes it to be in a perpetual, anxious craving <note>original: "Lust"</note> for vanity, according to its former impressions. It exists in a continual rage of hunger for those sorts of wickedness and lewdness in which it was immersed while in the flesh. It would gladly do more evil still, but it has neither the place nor the means left to do so; therefore, it performs this only within *itself*. All is now experienced internally as if it were outward. Thus, the ungodly person is tormented by those furies which are in his own mind, born of himself, by himself. For he has truly become his own devil and tormentor. That by which he sinned here, once the shadow of this world has passed away, remains with him as an internal impression and is made his prison and his Hell. But this hellish hunger and thirst cannot be fully manifested in the soul until the body—which provided the soul what it craved, and with which the soul was so bewitched that it obsessed over it and pursued all its cravings—is stripped away.

"I perceive then," said *Junius* to his Master, "that the soul, having behaved self-indulgently <note>original: "played the Wanton"</note> with the body in all sorts of pleasure-seeking <note>original: "Voluptuousness"</note> and having served its desires during this life, still retains the very same inclinations and affections <note>original: "Affections"; meaning deep-seated emotional states or desires.</note> it had before, even when it no longer has the opportunity or capacity to satisfy them. And when this satisfaction is impossible, Hell is then opened in that soul, having been shut up within it before by—"

<summary>The Master explains that Hell is an internal state of unsatisfied, selfish desire that becomes fully apparent only after the distractions of the physical body and the "light of nature" are removed at death. The soul's own "false will" and earthly cravings become its eternal prison and tormentor.</summary>

<meta>This page continues the dialogue between Theophorus (the Master) and his disciple (the Scholar) concerning the "Supersensual Life," specifically focusing on the nature of Heaven, Hell, and the spiritual "place" of the soul after death.</meta>

## Of the Supersensual Life.

[You mean] the means of the outward life in the body, and of the light of this world. Do I understand you correctly?

*Theophorus* said: You have understood it very well. Continue.

"On the other hand," said he, "I clearly see from what I have heard that Heaven must exist within a loving soul that is possessed by God and has thereby brought the body into the obedience of the spirit in all things, perfectly immersing itself in the will and love of God. And when the body dies and this soul is redeemed from the earth, it is now clear to me that the life of God which was hidden in it will reveal itself gloriously, and Heaven will consequently be made manifest. However, if there is not also a physical <note>original: "local"</note> Heaven and a physical Hell, I am still at a loss as to where to place a large part of the creation—if not the greatest part. For where must all its intellectual inhabitants reside?"

"In their own principle," answered the Master, "whether it be of Light or of Darkness. For every created intellectual being remains within its own deeds and essences, its wonders and properties, its life and image. In that state, it beholds and feels God, who is everywhere—whether in love or in wrath."

"If it exists in the love of God, then it beholds God accordingly and feels Him as He is: Love. But if it has imprisoned itself in the wrath of God, then it cannot behold God as anything other than a wrathful nature, nor perceive Him as anything but an incensed and vengeful spirit. All places are the same to it if it is in God's love; and if it is not there, every place is equally Hell. What place can confine a thought? Or why would any understanding spirit need to be kept in one place or another for its happiness or misery? Truly, wherever it is, it is in the *bottomless world* <note>original: "abyssal world"</note>, where there is neither end nor limit. And where, I ask you, should it go? For even if it should travel a thousand miles away, or ten thousand times ten thousand miles, and do this ten thousand times over—beyond the boundaries of the universe and into the imaginary spaces above the stars—it would still be in the exact same point from which it started."

"For God is the *place of spirit* (if it is lawful to give Him such a name, to which the body has a relationship). In God there is no limit; both near and far are the same here. Whether it be in His love or in His anger, the *bottomless will* <note>original: "abyssal will"</note> of the spirit is entirely unconfined. It is as swift as thought, passing through all things; it is magical, and nothing physical or external can hinder <note>original: "let"</note> it. It dwells within its wonders, and they are its house."

"This is how it is for every intellectual being, whether of the order of angels or of human souls. You need not fear that there will not be enough room for them all, no matter how many there are. They will find the place that best suits them, according to their own *choice and determination* <note>original: "election and determination"</note>; which may then very well be called their *own place*."

At which the Scholar said: "I remember, indeed, that it is written concerning the great traitor <note>Refers to Judas Iscariot; see Acts 1:25.</note> that after death he went *to his own place*."

The Master then said: "The same is true of every soul when it departs from this mortal life. And it is true in the same way for every angel or spirit; they are necessarily defined by their own choice. Just as God is everywhere, so the angels are everywhere—but each one exists within its own principle and its own property, or (if you prefer) in its *own place*. The same essence of God, which serves as a place for spirits, is acknowledged to be everywhere. However, the sharing or participation in it is different for everyone, according to what each has magically attracted through the earnestness of their will. The same divine essence that is with the angels of God above is also with us below. And the same divine nature that is with us is likewise with them, but it is communicated and shared in different ways and degrees."

"And what I have said here regarding the *Divine* should be considered by you also regarding the participation in the diabolical essence and nature, which is the *power of darkness*..."

# Of the Supersensual Life.

...the many modes, degrees, and attachments <note>original: "appropriations"</note> of it within the false will. In this world, there is strife between them. But when this world has reached its limit for anyone, then each principle claims what is its own; and so the soul receives companions accordingly—that is, either angels or devils.

To whom the **Scholar** again: If Heaven and Hell are at war within us during this life, and God himself is also so near to us, where can angels and devils live?

And the **Master** answered him thus: Where you do not live according to your *self-hood* <term>Self-hood refers to the ego or the state of being focused on one's own desires apart from God.</term> and your *own will*, there the holy angels live with you, and everywhere all around you. Remember this well. On the other hand, where you live for yourself, in self-seeking and self-will, there the devils will surely be with you; they will take up their residence and live all over and around you everywhere. May God in His mercy prevent this.

I do not understand this as perfectly well as I could wish, said the **Scholar**. Please make it a little clearer to me.

The **Master** then spoke: Pay close attention to what I am going to say. Where the will of God wills something, God is revealed; and in this very revelation <note>original: "manifestation"</note> of God, the angels live. But where God does not will within a creature's own will, God is not revealed to it, nor can He be. Instead, He remains within Himself, without the creature's cooperation or its humble subjection to Him. There, God is an unrevealed God to that creature. Therefore, the angels do not live with such a person; for wherever they live, there is the glory of God, and they create His glory. What then lives in such a creature as this? God does not live there; the angels do not live there; God does not exercise His will there, and neither do the angels. The situation is clearly this: in that soul or creature, its own will exists apart from God's will, and there the devil lives; and with him everything that is outside of God and outside of Christ. This is the truth; take it to heart.

*The Scholar.* It is possible I may ask several irrelevant questions; but I beg you, good sir, to have patience with me and to pity my ignorance if I ask what may appear to you perhaps ridiculous, or may not be at all fit for me to expect an answer to. For I have several questions still to propose to you, but I am ashamed of my own thoughts in this matter.

*The Master.* Be plain with me and propose whatever is on your mind; yes, do not be ashamed even to appear ridiculous, so long as by asking questions you may become wiser.

The **Scholar** thanked his **Master** for this liberty and said: How far then are Heaven and Hell apart?

To whom he answered thus: As far as day and night; or as far as "something" and "nothing." They are within one another, and yet they are at the greatest distance from each other. In fact, one of them is as nothing to the other; and yet, they nevertheless cause joy and grief to one another. Heaven is throughout the whole world, and it is also outside the world over everything—even everywhere that is, or that can even be imagined. It fills all, it is within all, it is outside all, and it encompasses all; without division and without a physical place. It works through a divine revelation <note>original: "manifestation"</note> and flows out universally, but without ever leaving itself. For it works and is revealed only within itself, being one and undivided in all. It appears only through the revelation of God, and never except within itself. And in whatever being enters into it, or in whatever it is revealed, there also God is revealed. Because Heaven is nothing other than a manifestation or revelation of the Eternal One, in whom all working and willing exists in peaceful love.

In the same way, Hell is also throughout the whole world, and it lives and works only within itself and within that where the foundation of Hell is revealed—namely, in self-

...hood, and in the False Will. The visible world has both within it; and there is no place where Heaven and Hell may not be found or revealed. Now man, in regards to his temporal life, belongs only to the visible world; therefore, during the time of this life, he does not see the spiritual world. For the outward world and its substance act as a cover to the spiritual world, just as the body is a cover to the soul. But when the outward man dies, then the spiritual world is manifested to the soul, which has now had its covering taken away. It is revealed either in the Eternal Light with the holy angels, or in the Eternal Darkness with the devils.

The Scholar further questioned: What is an angel, or a human soul, that they can be manifested in either God’s Love or Anger, either in Light or Darkness?

To whom *Theophorus* <note>original: Theophorus; Greek for "God-bearer"</note> answered: They come from one and the same original source. They are little branches of the Divine Wisdom and the Divine Will, sprung from the Divine Word <note>The "Word" or Logos refers to the creative power of God</note>, and made objects of Divine Love. They emerge from the ground of eternity, from which both Light and Darkness spring: Darkness, which consists of receiving "Self-Desire"; and Light, which consists of willing the same thing that God wills. For Heaven exists in the conformity of the human will with God’s Will; and wherever this "willing with God" exists, the Love of God is undoubtedly at work, and His Light will not fail to manifest itself. 

But in the "Self-Attraction" of the soul’s desire—or when any spirit, whether angelic or human, receives "Self" into its willing—the Will of God works with difficulty. To that soul or spirit, God’s Will is nothing but Darkness; though even out of this, the Light may eventually be manifested. This Darkness is the "Hell" of the spirit in which it dwells. For *Heaven and Hell are nothing else but a manifestation of the Divine Will in either Light or Darkness, according to the properties of the spiritual world.*

## What the Body of Man is; and why the Soul is capable of receiving Good and Evil.

->*Scholar.*<-
**WHAT** then is the Body of Man?

->*Master.*<-
It is the visible world; an image and quintessence <term>the purest, most concentrated essence or compound</term> of all that the world is. The visible world is a manifestation of the inward spiritual world, which came out of the eternal Light and the eternal Darkness, out of the spiritual connection of the two. It is also an image or figure of Eternity, through which Eternity has made itself visible, and where "Self-Will" and "Resigned Will" (namely, Evil and Good) work with one another.

The outward man is made of such a substance. For God created man out of the outward world and breathed into him the inward spiritual world to serve as a soul and an intelligent life. Therefore, in the things of the outward world, man can receive and perform both Evil and Good.

# Of the Destruction of the World; of Man's Body, in and after the Resurrection; where Heaven and Hell shall be; of the Last Judgment; and why there must be Strife in the Created Being <note>original: "Creature"</note>.

->Scholar.<-

"What shall happen after this world, when all things perish and come to an end?"

->Master.<-

Only the material substance ceases—namely <note>original: "viz."</note>, the four elements, the sun, moon, and stars. Then the inward world will be wholly visible and manifest. But whatever has been worked by the will or spirit of man during the time of this world, whether evil or good—I say, every such work shall separate itself there in a spiritual manner, into either the Eternal Light or the Eternal Darkness. For that which is born from each will penetrates and passes again into that which is like itself. There, the darkness is called Hell, and is an *eternal* forgetting of all good; and the light is called the Kingdom of God, and is an *eternal joy* in and to the saints, who continually glorify and praise God for having delivered them from the torment of evil.

The Last Judgment is a kindling of the fire of both God's love and anger, in which the matter of every substance perishes, and each fire shall attract into itself its own—that is, the substance that is like itself. Thus, God's fire of love will draw into it whatever is born in the love of God, or the <term>Love-Principle</term> <note>The "Love-Principle" refers to the divine energy of light and grace, contrasted here with the fire of "Anger."</note>, in which it shall also burn in the manner of *love*, and surrender itself into that substance. But the torment will draw into itself what is worked in the anger of God in darkness, and consume the false substance; then there will remain only the painful, aching will in its own proper nature, image, and form <note>original: "Figure"</note>.

->Scholar.<-

With what matter and form shall the human body rise?

->Master.<-

It is sown a natural, heavy <note>original: "gross"</note> and elementary body, which in this lifetime is like the outward elements; yet in this heavy body, there is a subtle power and <term>virtue</term> <note>In this context, "virtue" means an inherent spiritual power or essential quality.</note>. Just as in the earth there is also a subtle, good virtue which is like the sun, and is one and the same with the sun—which also, in the beginning of time, sprang and proceeded out of the Divine power and virtue, from which all the good virtue of the body is likewise derived. This good virtue of the mortal body shall come again and live forever in a kind of transparent, crystalline material property, in spiritual flesh and blood; the good virtue of the earth shall also return, for the earth likewise shall become crystalline, and the Divine Light shall shine in everything that has a being, essence, or substance. And as the heavy earth shall perish and never return, so also the heavy flesh of man shall perish and not live forever. 

But all things must appear before the Judgment, and in the Judgment be separated by the fire; yes, both the earth and also the ashes of the human body. For when God shall once move the spiritual world, every spirit shall attract its spiritual substance to itself. A good spirit and soul shall draw to itself its good substance, and an evil one its evil substance. But we must understand "substance" here as such a material power and virtue, the essence of which is mere virtue, like a material <term>tincture</term> <note>A "tincture" is a spiritual or alchemical essence that gives a substance its specific qualities or "colors."</note>—something that has all forms, colors, and vir-

->*Scholar.*<-

Shall we not rise again with our visible bodies, and live in them forever? *See the Forty Questions of the Soul, Question 21, Verse 12.*

->*Master.*<-

When the visible world perishes, then all that has come out of it and has been external shall perish with it. Only the heavenly crystalline nature and form of the world shall remain; and of man, only the spiritual earth. For man shall then be completely like the spiritual world, which is hidden for now.

->*Scholar.*<-

Will there be husband and wife, or children or relatives, in the heavenly life? Or will people associate with one another as they do in this life?

->*Master.*<-

Why are you so focused on the flesh? There will be neither husband nor wife, but all will be like the angels of God—namely, <term>masculine virgins</term> <note>In Boehme’s mysticism, this term describes a state of spiritual perfection that transcends biological sex, representing a return to a unified, angelic state.</note>. There will be neither son nor daughter, brother nor sister, but all will be of one stock and family. For all are one in Christ, just as a tree and its branches are one, though distinct as individual creatures; but God is all in all. Indeed, there will be spiritual knowledge of what everyone has been and done, but there will no longer be any possessing or enjoying—or even the desire for possessing—earthly things or enjoying fleshly relationships.

->*Scholar.*<-

Will they all have the same eternal joy and glory?

->*Master.*<-

The Scripture says, *As the people are, so is their God.* And in another place, *With the holy you are holy, and with the perverse you are perverse.* And St. Paul says, *In the resurrection, one person shall differ from another in glory, just as the sun, moon, and stars differ.* 

Therefore, know that the blessed shall indeed all enjoy the divine working within and upon them; but their virtue and illumination (or glory) shall be very different. This depends on how they were endowed in this life with different measures and degrees of power and virtue through their <term>painful working</term> <note>original: "painful Working"; this refers to the spiritual struggle and internal labor the soul undergoes to overcome its lower nature and align with the divine.</note>. For the "painful working" of the creature in this lifetime is the opening and bringing forth of divine power, through which that power is made active and operative. 

Now, those who have worked with Christ during this life, and not in the lust of the flesh, shall have great power and transcendent glory within and upon them. But others have only expected and relied upon an <term>imputed satisfaction</term> <note>The theological concept that Christ's righteousness is legally credited to a believer, which Boehme warns should not be a substitute for actual inner transformation.</note>, and in the meantime served their <term>belly-god</term> <note>original: "Belly-God"; a person who prioritizes physical appetites and worldly pleasures over spiritual growth.</note>, yet eventually turned and obtained grace; I say that these people shall not attain such a high degree of power and illumination. There will be as great a difference in degrees between them as there is between the sun, the moon, and the stars—or between the flowers of the field in their various beauties, powers, and virtues.

->*Scholar.*<-

How shall the world be judged, and by whom?

## Master.

Jesus Christ, that Word of God who became Man, shall by the power of his divine stirring or motion separate from himself all that does not belong to him; he shall fully manifest his Kingdom in the place or space where this world now is, for the separating motion works all over the universe, through everything at once.

## Scholar.

Where shall the devils and all the damned be thrown when the place of this world becomes the Kingdom of Christ and of those who are glorified? Shall they be cast out of the place of this world? Or shall Christ have and manifest his dominion outside the sphere or place of this world?

## Master.

Hell shall remain everywhere in the place or sphere of this world, but hidden from the Kingdom of Heaven, just as the night is hidden in and from the day. *The light shall shine forever in the darkness, but the darkness can never comprehend or reach it.* <note>original: John 1:5. Böhme uses this to explain that Heaven and Hell occupy the same space but exist in different dimensions or states of being.</note> And the light is the Kingdom of Christ; but the darkness is Hell, where the devils and the wicked dwell. Thus they shall be suppressed by the Kingdom of Christ and made his footstool—namely, a state of reproach <note>original: "viz. a Reproach"; meaning a state of shame or disgrace</note>.

## Scholar.

How shall all people and nations be brought to judgment?

## Master.

The Eternal Word of God, from which every spiritual creaturely life has proceeded, will move itself at that hour—according to both love and anger—in every life which has come out of eternity. It will draw every creature before the judgment of Christ to be sentenced by this motion of the Word. Life will then be manifested in all its works, and every soul shall see and feel its judgment and sentence within itself. 

For the judgment is, indeed, manifested in and to every soul immediately upon the departure of the body. The Last Judgment is simply a return of the spiritual body and a separation of the world, when the evil shall be separated from the good in the substance of the world and of the human body, and everything enters into its eternal receptacle. And thus, it is a manifestation of the mystery of God in every substance and life.

## Scholar.

How will the sentence be pronounced?

## Master.

Consider here the words of Christ. He will say to those on his right hand: *“Come, you blessed of my Father, inherit the kingdom prepared for you from the foundation of the world. For I was hungry and you gave me meat; I was thirsty and you gave me drink; I was a stranger and you took me in; naked, and you clothed me. I was sick and you visited me; in prison, and you came to me.”*

Then they shall answer him, saying: *“Lord, when did we see you hungry, thirsty, a stranger, naked, sick, or in prison, and ministered to you in this way?”*

Then shall the King answer and say to them: *“Inasmuch as you have done it to one of the least of these my brothers, you have done it to me.”*

->Scholar.<-

Dear Master, please tell me why Christ says, *“What you have done to the least of these, you have done to me; and what you have not done to them, you have not done to me.”* How does a man do this in such a way that he does it to Christ *himself*?

->Master.<-

Christ dwells truly and essentially in the faith of those who wholly yield themselves up to him. He gives them his flesh for food and his blood for drink, and thus possesses the very ground of their faith according to the interior or inward man <note>original: "interior or inward Man" refers to the spiritual soul as opposed to the physical body.</note>. A Christian is called a "branch of the vine, Christ" and a "Christian" because Christ dwells spiritually in him. Therefore, whatever good anyone does for such a Christian in his bodily needs, it is done to Christ himself who dwells in him. For such a Christian is not his own, but is wholly resigned to Christ and has become his peculiar <note>original: "peculiar" here means "exclusive" or "private property," rather than "strange."</note> possession; consequently, the good deed is done to Christ himself. 

Therefore, also, whoever withholds their help from such a needy Christian, and fails to serve him in his necessity, they thrust Christ away from themselves and despise him in his members <note>original: "members" refers to the parts of the "Body of Christ," or the community of believers.</note>. When a poor person who belongs to Christ in this way asks anything of you, and you deny him in his need, you deny it to Christ himself. And whatever harm anyone does to such a Christian, they do it to Christ himself. When any mock, scorn, revile, reject, or thrust such a person away, they do all that to Christ. But he who receives him—giving him food, drink, or clothing, and assisting him in his needs—does it likewise to Christ, and to a fellow member of his own body. Indeed, he does it to himself if he is a Christian; for we are all one in Christ, just as a tree and its branches are one.

->Scholar.<-

How then will those survive on the day of that fierce judgment, who afflict and vex the poor and distressed, depriving them of the very fruit of their sweat <note>original: "deprive them of their very Sweat" refers to exploiting the labor of the poor.</note>? These people force and constrain the poor to submit to their wills, trampling upon them like footstools only so that they themselves may live in pomp and power, spending the fruits of these poor people's labor on luxury, pride, and vanity.

->Master.<-

Christ suffers in the persecution of his members. Therefore, all the wrong that such harsh oppressors do to the poor wretches under their control is done to Christ himself; it falls under his severe sentence and judgment. Besides that, they help the Devil to grow his kingdom; for by such oppression of the poor, they drive them away from Christ and make them seek unlawful ways to fill their bellies. In fact, they work for and with the Devil himself, doing the very same thing he does—he who, without ceasing, opposes the kingdom of Christ, which consists only in love. All these oppressors, if they do not turn with their whole hearts to Christ and serve...

->*Scholar.*<-

But how will it fare with those, and how will they be able to stand that severe trial, who in this time so fiercely argue about the kingdom of Christ, and slander, insult, and persecute one another for their religion, as they do?

->*Master.*<-

All such people have not yet known Christ; they are only like a <term>Type or Figure</term> <note>original: "Type or Figure"; a symbolic representation or shadow of a deeper reality</note> of heaven and hell, fighting with each other for victory.

All rising, swelling pride which argues about opinions is an image of "Self." And whoever has no faith or humility, and does not live in the spirit of Christ—which is love—is only armed with the anger of God. They help advance the victory of the imaginary "Self," which is the kingdom of darkness and the anger of God. For at the Day of Judgment, all "Self" shall be given to the darkness, as will all the useless arguments of men. In these arguments, they do not seek love, but merely their own imaginary "Self," so that they may exalt themselves by promoting and establishing their own opinions. They even stir up princes to war for the sake of these opinions, causing the destruction of entire countries and peoples. All such things belong to the Judgment, which will separate the false from the true. Then all images and opinions shall cease, and all the children of God shall live forever in the love of Christ, and Christ in them.

Everyone in this time of conflict—namely, from the Fall to the Resurrection—who is not eager in the spirit of Christ to promote peace and love, but instead seeks and strives for themselves alone, belongs to the devil and the pit of darkness. Consequently, they must be separated from Christ. For in heaven, all serve God their Creator in humble love.

->*Scholar.*<-

Why, then, does God allow such conflict and contention to exist in this time?

->*Master.*<-

Life itself exists in conflict so that it may be made manifest, felt, and tangible, and so that wisdom may be made distinguishable and known.

This conflict also creates the eternal joy of victory. For great praise and thanksgiving will arise in the saints from the personal experience and knowledge that Christ in them has overcome darkness and all the "Self" of <term>Nature</term> <note>original: "Nature"; refers to the fallen, material, or driven state of existence</note>, and that they are at length totally delivered from the conflict. They shall rejoice eternally when they see how the wicked are repaid. And therefore God allows all souls to exist in a state of free will, so that the eternal dominion of both love and anger, of light and darkness, may be made manifest and known; and so that every life might determine and find its own sentence within itself. For that which is now a conflict and pain to the saints in their difficult struggle here shall in the end be turned into great joy for them; and that which has been a joy and pleasure to ungodly people in this world shall afterwards be turned into eternal torment and shame for them. Therefore, the joy of the saints must arise for them out of death—just as light arises from a candle by the destruction and consumption of the candle in its own fire. In this way, life may be freed from the pain of nature and possess another world.

And just as light has a completely different property than fire—for light gives and yields itself outward, whereas fire draws inward and consumes itself—so the holy life...

### *Hebrews 12:22, 23, 24.*

> *Give thanks to the Lord, for you have now come to Mount Zion, to the city of the living God, to the heavenly Jerusalem, to the innumerable company of angels, and to the general assembly and church of the firstborn, whose names are written in heaven.*
> *And to God the Judge of all; and to the spirits of just men made perfect; and to Jesus the Mediator of the New Covenant.*
> *And to the blood of sprinkling, which speaks of better things than that of Abel <note>In Genesis, Abel's blood cried out from the ground for vengeance; in Christian theology, Jesus's blood "speaks" of forgiveness and reconciliation</note>. Amen.*
> *Praise, glory, and thanksgiving, honor, wisdom, and power, be unto him who sits on the throne, to our God, and the Lamb forever and ever. Amen.*

### THE
# WAY FROM DARKNESS
### TO
## TRUE ILLUMINATION.

There was a poor soul that had wandered out of Paradise and come into the kingdom of this world; there, the Devil met it and said, "Where are you going, you soul who are half-blind?"

->*The Soul said,*<-

I want to see and look deeply into the creatures of the world which the Creator has made.

->*The Devil said,*<-

How will you see and look deeply into them when you cannot know their essence <note>original: "Essence and Property"; refers to the inner spiritual nature and specific characteristics of a thing</note> and property? You will look only upon their outside, as if looking at a carved image, and cannot know them thoroughly.

->*The Soul said,*<-

How can I come to know their essence and property?

->*The Devil said,*<-

Your eyes would be opened to see them thoroughly if you only ate of *that* from which the creatures themselves have come to be *good* and *evil*. You would then be as God himself is and know what the creature truly is.

->*The Soul said,*<-

I am now a noble and holy creature; but if I should do so, the Creator has said that I would die.

->*The Devil said,*<-

No, you would not die at all; rather, your eyes would be opened, and you would be like God himself and be master of good and evil. Also, you would be mighty, powerful, and very great, as I am; all the subtlety <note>original: "Subtilty"; here meaning the hidden complexity or craftiness</note> that is in the creatures would be made known to you.

->*The Soul said,*<-

If I had the knowledge of nature and of the creatures, I would then rule the whole world as I pleased <note>original: "listed"; an archaic term meaning to desire or choose</note>.

<summary>This page presents an allegorical dialogue in which the Devil tempts a soul to seek forbidden knowledge of the inner essence of the world, echoing the biblical story of the Fall. The Devil promises that by understanding "good and evil," the soul will gain god-like power and mastery over nature.</summary>

# The Way from Darkness to True Illumination.

->*The Devil said,*<-

The entire foundation <note>original: "Ground"</note> of that knowledge lies within you. Simply turn your will and desire away from God or goodness and toward nature and created things, and then a craving to taste will arise in you; and so you may eat of the *Tree of Knowledge of Good and Evil*, and by that means come to know all things.

->*The Soul said,*<-

Well then, I will eat of the *Tree of Knowledge of Good and Evil*, so that I may rule all things by my own power; and be a lord on Earth by myself, and do what I want, just as God himself does.

->*The Devil said,*<-

I am the prince of this world; and if you would rule on Earth, you must turn your desire <note>original: "Lust"</note> toward my image, or desire to be like me, so that you may gain the cunning, wit, reason, and subtlety that my image possesses.

In this way, the Devil presented to the soul the *Vulcan* <note>In alchemy and Boehme's philosophy, Vulcan represents the transformative power of fire or the internal "artificer" who shapes nature.</note> in the *Mercury* <note>Mercury here refers to the vital, moving spirit or the "quicksilver" of the soul's inner nature and desire.</note> (the power that is in the fiery root of the creature)—that is, the fiery wheel of essence or substance, in the form of a serpent. Upon which,

->*The Soul said,*<-

Behold, this is the power which can do all things. What must I do to get it?

->*The Devil said,*<-

You yourself are also such a fiery *Mercury*. If you break your will away from God and bring it into this power and skill, then your hidden foundation will be revealed within you, and you may work in the same manner. But you must eat of that fruit in which each of the four elements <note>The traditional elements: Earth, Air, Fire, and Water.</note> in itself rules over the others and is in conflict; the heat striving against the cold, and the cold against the heat; and so all the properties of nature work through direct feeling. And then you will instantly be as the fiery wheel is, and so bring all things into your own power and possess them as your own.

->*The soul did so, and what happened next.*<-

Now when the soul broke its will away from God in this manner and brought it into the *Mercury*, or the fiery will (which is the root of life and power), there presently arose in it a desire <note>original: "Lust"</note> to eat of the *Tree of Knowledge of Good and Evil*; and the soul ate of it. As soon as it had done this, *Vulcan* (or the craftsman in the fire) instantly ignited the fiery wheel of its substance, and thereupon all the properties of nature awoke in the soul and exercised each its own craving and desire.

First arose the desire <note>original: "Lust"</note> of pride; a desire to be great, mighty, and powerful; to bring all things under subjection to it, and so to be lord itself without control; despising all humility and equality, as considering itself the only prudent, witty, and cunning one, and accounting everything folly that is not according to its own mood <note>original: "Humour"</note> and liking.

Secondly arose the desire of greed <note>original: "Covetousness"</note>; a desire for getting, which would draw all things to itself, into its own possession. For when the desire of pride had turned the will away from God, then the life of the soul would not trust God any further, but would take care of itself; and therefore brought its desire into the creatures—namely <note>original: "viz."</note>, into the earth, metals, trees, and other creatures. Thus the ignited fiery life became hungry and greedy, when it had broken itself off from the unity, love, and meek—

# ->The Way from Darkness to True Illumination.<-

...likeness <note>The text begins mid-sentence; the full word is likely "likeness."</note> of God, and attracted the four elements and their essence to itself. It brought itself into the condition of animals; thus, its life became dark, empty, and wrathful. The heavenly virtues and colors faded away, like an extinguished candle.

Thirdly, within this fiery life, the painful, stinging desire of envy awoke. This is a hellish poison and a trait shared by all devils; it is a torment that makes life a pure enemy to God and all creatures. This envy raged furiously within the desire of greed <note>original: "covetousness"</note>, just as a poisonous sting does in the body. Envy cannot endure—but rather hates and seeks to hurt or destroy—whatever greed cannot seize for itself. Through this hellish passion, the soul’s noble love is smothered.

Fourthly, a fire-like torment—namely, anger—awoke in this fiery life. This anger sought to murder and remove anyone who would not submit to pride. Thus, the foundation of Hell (which is called the "Anger of God") was fully revealed in this soul. Because of this, the soul lost the beautiful Paradise of God and the Kingdom of Heaven. It became a worm like the fiery serpent which the Devil presented to it as his own image and likeness. So the soul began to rule on Earth in an animal-like <note>original: "bestial"</note> manner, doing everything according to the Devil's will. It lived in pure pride, greed, envy, and anger, no longer possessing any true love for God. In its place arose a wicked, animalistic love of filthy lust <note>original: "lechery"</note>, arrogance, and vanity. No purity remained in the heart, for the soul had abandoned Paradise and taken possession of the Earth. Its mind was entirely focused on deceptive knowledge, cunning, and gathering a multitude of earthly things. No righteousness or virtue remained in it at all. Instead, whatever evil or wrong it committed, it cleverly and subtly covered up using the cloak of its own power and legal authority, calling it "right" and "justice" and considering it good.

### ->The Devil came to the Soul.<-

At this point, the Devil approached the soul and led it from one vice to another, for he had captured it within his own nature <note>original: "essence"</note>. He placed joy and pleasure before it, saying: "Behold, you are now powerful, mighty, and noble. Strive to be even greater, richer, and more powerful. Display your knowledge, wit, and cunning, so that everyone may fear you and stand in awe of you—that you may be respected and gain a great name in the world."

### ->The Soul did so.<-

The soul did as the Devil advised, yet it did not know its counselor was the Devil. Instead, it thought it was guided by its own knowledge, wit, and understanding, and believed it was doing quite well and rightly the entire time.

### ->Jesus Christ met with the Soul.<-

While the soul continued in this way of life, our dear and loving Lord Jesus Christ—who had come into this world with both the love and the anger of God to destroy the Devil’s works and to judge all ungodly deeds—met with it. He spoke into the soul with a powerful force—namely, through his suffering <note>original: "passion"</note> and death. He destroyed the Devil’s work within it, revealed the way to his grace, and shone upon it with his mercy. He called for the soul to return and repent, promising that he would then deliver it from that monstrous, deformed shape or image it had acquired and bring it back into Paradise.

### *How Christ Worked in the Soul.*

Now, when the spark of the love of God, or the Divine Light, was revealed within the soul, the soul immediately saw that its own will and its works were in a state of hell and subject to the wrath of God. It found that it was a misshapen, ugly monster in the Divine Presence and the Kingdom of Heaven. At this sight, it was so terrified that it fell into the greatest possible anguish, for the judgment of God was made manifest within it.

### *What Christ Said.*

Upon this, the Lord Christ spoke to it with the voice of his grace, and said: "Repent and forsake vanity, and you shall attain my grace."

### *What the Soul Said.*

Then the soul, in its ugly and misshapen image and wearing the defiled coat of vanity, went before God and begged for grace and the pardon of its sins. It became strongly persuaded within itself that the satisfaction and atonement of our Lord Jesus Christ belonged to it. 

But the evil properties of the Serpent <note>In the mystical tradition of Jacob Boehme, "the Serpent" represents the fallen, selfish nature of humanity</note>, which were formed in the astral spirit <term>the "astral spirit" refers to the rational mind or the outward personality influenced by the physical stars and the material world</term>—the reason of the outward man—would not allow the will of the soul to come before God. Instead, these properties brought their own lusts and inclinations into the soul. For those evil properties would not die to their own lusts nor leave the world, because they had come out of the world; therefore, they feared the world's reproach if they should forsake their worldly honor and glory.

But the poor soul turned its countenance toward God and desired grace from him, asking that he would bestow his love upon it.

### *The Devil Came to it Again.*

When the Devil saw that the soul prayed to God and intended to enter into repentance, he drew near to it. He thrust the inclinations of earthly properties into its prayers and disturbed its good thoughts and desires, which were pressing forward toward God. He drew them back again to earthly things so that they might have no access to him.

### *The Soul Sighed.*

The central will of the soul indeed sighed after God, but the thoughts arising in the mind—which should have penetrated into him—were distracted, scattered, and destroyed, so that they could not reach the power of God. At this, the poor soul was even more terrified and began to pray more earnestly. 

But the Devil, with his own desire, took hold of the "Mercurial kindled fiery wheel of life" <term>A term used by Jacob Boehme to describe the restless, turbulent, and rotating forces of nature and human passion</term> and awakened the evil properties. This caused evil or false inclinations to arise in the soul, which focused on the very things in which the soul had previously taken the most pleasure and delight.

The poor soul very much wanted to go forward to God with its will and therefore used all its efforts. However, its thoughts continually fled away from God into earthly things and would not go to him.

Because of this, the soul sighed and lamented to God, feeling as if it were completely forsaken by him and cast out from his presence. It could not receive even a single look of grace, but was in mere anguish, fear, and terror. It dreaded every moment that the wrath and severe judgment of God would be revealed within it, and that the Devil would seize it. Thereupon, it fell into such great heaviness and sorrow that it became weary of all the temporal things which, before, had been its chief joy and happiness.

<summary>This page describes the soul's initial terror upon recognizing its sinful state and its subsequent struggle to pray as the Devil and worldly inclinations distract its thoughts from God.</summary>

The earthly, natural will indeed desired those things still, but the soul wanted to leave them entirely. It desired to die to all worldly lust and joy whatsoever and longed only for its original homeland, from which it first came. Yet it found itself far from there, in great distress and need, and did not know what to do; nevertheless, it resolved to look inward and try to pray more earnestly.

### The Devil’s Opposition.

But the Devil opposed it and held it back, so that it could not reach a greater intensity of repentance.

He awakened earthly lusts in its heart, so that they might maintain their evil nature and false claims there, setting them at odds with the soul's new-born will and desire. For these lusts would not die to their own will and light but wanted to keep their worldly pleasures. Thus, they kept the poor soul captive in their evil desires, so that it could not move, even though it sighed and longed deeply for the grace of God. Whenever it prayed or tried to press forward toward God, the lusts of the flesh swallowed up the rays and <term>ejaculations</term> <note>original: "Ejaculations"; here meaning sudden, short, and passionate prayers or spiritual outbursts</note> that came from it. These lusts pulled the soul away from God and into earthly thoughts, so that it could not share in divine strength. 

This caused the poor soul to think it was forsaken by God, not knowing that he was actually so near, drawing the soul toward him. The Devil also gained access to the soul and entered into the <term>fiery Mercury</term> <note>A term from alchemy used by Jacob Boehme to describe the restless, driving energy or "wheel" of a person's life force</note>, or the fiery wheel of its life. He mingled his desires with the earthly lusts of the flesh and tempted the poor soul, speaking to it through its earthly thoughts: 

"*Why do you pray? Do you think that God knows you or cares about you? Just consider what thoughts you have in his presence; are they not entirely evil? You have no faith or belief in God at all; how then should he hear you? He does not hear you—stop! Why will you needlessly torment and vex yourself? You have enough time to repent at your leisure. Are you going mad? I beg you, look at the world for a moment; does it not live in jollity and mirth? Yet it will be saved well enough despite all that. Has Christ not paid the ransom and satisfied the debt for all people? You only need to persuade and comfort yourself that it is done for you, and then you shall be saved. You cannot possibly reach any feeling of God in this world; therefore, stop and take care of your body, and seek worldly glory. What do you suppose will become of you if you become so dull and melancholy? You will be the scorn of everyone, and they will laugh at your folly. You will spend your days in mere sorrow and gloom, which pleases neither God nor nature. I beg you, look upon the beauty of the world; for God has created you and placed you in it to be a lord over all creatures and to rule them. Gather a store of worldly goods beforehand, so that you may not be indebted to the world or stand in need later. And when old age comes, or when you grow near your end, then prepare yourself for repentance. God will save you and receive you into the heavenly mansions then. There is no need for such a fuss in vexing, bewailing, and agitating yourself as you are doing.*"

### The Condition of the Soul.

Ensnared by these and similar thoughts, the soul was led into the lusts of the flesh and earthly desires. It was bound as if with fetters and strong chains, so that it did not know what to do. It looked back a little toward the world and its pleasures, but still felt within itself a hunger for divine grace. It would always prefer to enter into repentance and find favor with God. For the hand of God had touched and bruised it, and therefore it could find no rest anywhere. Instead, it always sighed within itself, longing for true sorrow for the sins it had committed, and it would gladly be rid of them. Yet it could not achieve true repentance or even a full knowledge of sin, though it had a powerful hunger and longing desire for such penitential sorrow.

The Devil argues that the soul should focus on worldly pleasure and wealth, claiming that God is distant and that repentance can wait until old age.</summary>

### The Way from Darkness to True Illumination.

The Soul, being so heavy and sorrowful and finding no remedy or rest, began to consider where it might find a suitable place to perform true repentance—a place where it might be free from business, cares, and the distractions of the world. It also considered by what means it might win the favor of God. At length, it decided to withdraw to some private, solitary place and give up all worldly employment and temporal concerns. It hoped that by being generous and compassionate <note>original: "pitiful"</note> toward the poor, it would obtain God’s mercy. 

Thus, the Soul devised all kinds of ways to find rest and regain the love, favor, and grace of God. But nothing worked; its worldly business still followed it through the desires <note>original: "lusts"</note> of the flesh, and it was ensnared in the devil's net now just as much as before, unable to attain rest. Although for a short time it was somewhat cheered by earthly things, it presently became as sad and heavy again as it was before. 

The truth was, it felt the awakened wrath of God within itself but did not know how that had happened or what was wrong. Often, great trouble and terror fell upon it, making it comfortless, sick, and faint with sheer fear—so powerfully did the first "bruising" <note>This refers to the painful but necessary spiritual awakening caused by God's light.</note> by the influence of the stirring of grace work upon it. Yet the Soul did not know that Christ was present within that wrath and severe justice of God, fighting against Satan—that spirit of error which was incorporated into the soul and body. Nor did it understand that the hunger and desire to turn and repent came from Christ himself, by whom it was being drawn in this manner. It did not know what hindered it from reaching a divine state of feeling. It did not know that it was a monster and bore the "image of the serpent," through which the devil had power and access to it. The devil had confounded all its good desires, thoughts, and motions, leading them away from God and goodness. Concerning this, Christ himself said: *The devil snatches the word out of their hearts, lest they should believe and be saved.*

---

->*An enlightened and regenerate soul met the distressed soul.*<-

By the providence of God, an enlightened and reborn <note>original: "regenerate"</note> soul met this poor, afflicted, and distressed soul and said: 
"What is wrong with you, distressed soul, that you are so restless and troubled?"

->*The distressed soul answered:*<-

"The Creator has hidden his face <note>original: "countenance"</note> from me, so that I cannot enter into his rest. Therefore I am troubled, and I do not know what to do to regain his loving-kindness. Great cliffs and rocks lie in my way to his grace, so that I cannot reach him. Though I sigh and long for him ever so much, I am kept back and cannot partake of his power, virtue <note>original: "virtue" here means spiritual efficacy or strength</note>, and strength."

->*The enlightened soul said:*<-

"You carry the monstrous shape of the devil and are clothed in it. Because this shape is the devil's own property <term>In this context, "property" refers to an essential quality or characteristic nature.</term> or principle, he has access and the power to enter you. By this, he keeps your will from penetrating into God. If your will could penetrate into God, it would be anointed with the highest power and strength of God through the resurrection of our Lord Jesus Christ. That unction <term>The act of spiritual anointing; the influence of the Holy Spirit.</term> would break into pieces the monster you carry about you, and your original image of Paradise would revive in your center. This would destroy the devil’s power within you, and you would become an angel again. Because the devil envies you this happiness, he holds you captive to his desire in the lusts of the flesh. If you are not delivered from this, you will be separated from God and can never enter into our society."

### *The distressed Soul terrified.*

At these words, the poor distressed soul was so terrified and amazed that it could not speak another word. It realized that it stood in the state and condition of the Serpent <note>The "Serpent" represents the fallen, self-centered nature of humanity, characterized by pride and separation from God.</note>, which separated it from God. It saw that the Devil was very near in that condition, injecting evil thoughts into the soul’s will and holding so much power over it that the soul was near damnation, stuck fast in the abyss <term>abyss: an immeasurably deep chasm; here, the "bottomless pit" of spiritual separation</term> of hell within the anger of God. 

The soul would have even despaired of divine mercy, but the power, virtue, and strength of the first stirring of God's grace—which had previously "bruised" the soul <note>original: "bruised the Soul" - an allusion to Genesis 3:15, referring to the painful process of conviction and the breaking of the ego</note>—upheld it and preserved it from total despair. Yet, it still struggled within itself between hope and doubt; whatever hope built up, doubt threw down again. It was agitated by such continual unrest that, at last, the world and all its glory became loathsome. The soul no longer wished to enjoy worldly pleasures; and yet, for all this, it could not find rest.

### *The enlightened Soul came again, and spoke to the troubled Soul*

In time, the enlightened soul came again to this soul. Finding it still in such great trouble, anguish, and grief of mind, it said:

"What are you doing? Will you destroy yourself in your anguish and sorrow? Why do you torment yourself by your own power and will? You are but a worm <note>In 17th-century spiritual writing, the "worm" was a common metaphor for the humble, fragile state of human existence</note>, and your torment only increases by your own effort. Indeed, even if you could sink yourself to the bottom of the sea, fly to the farthest reaches of the dawn, or raise yourself above the stars, you would still not be released. For the more you grieve, torment, and trouble yourself, the more painful your nature will become, and yet you will not be able to find rest. Your own power is completely lost. Just as a dry stick burnt to a coal cannot grow green and sprout again by its own power, nor regain the sap to flourish alongside other trees and plants, you cannot reach the place of God by your own power and strength, nor transform yourself back into that angelic image which you had at first. Regarding God, you are withered and dry, like a dead plant that has lost its sap and strength; you have become a dry, tormenting hunger. Your internal qualities <note>original: "Properties" - refers to the fundamental forces or spiritual "elements" that make up a being's nature</note> are like heat and cold, which continually struggle against each other and can never unite."

### *The distressed Soul said,*

"What then shall I do to sprout forth again and recover the original life I had, where I was at rest before I became an 'image'?" <note>In this context, becoming an "image" refers to the soul taking on a self-defined, worldly identity separate from God.</note>

### *The enlightened Soul said,*

"You shall do nothing at all but forsake your own will—that is, the thing you call *'I'* or *'yourself.'* By doing this, all your evil qualities will grow weak, faint, and ready to die; then you will sink down again into that **One Thing** from which you originally began. At present, you lie captive in 'the creatures' <note>original: "the Creatures" - refers to created things, i.e., worldly objects and desires, as opposed to the Creator</note>. But if your will forsakes them, those creatures and their evil inclinations will die within you—those are the things that currently block and hinder you from coming to God. If you take this course, your God will meet you with His infinite love, which He has manifested in Jesus Christ’s human nature. That love will impart sap, life, and vigor to you. By this, you may bud, spring, flourish again, and rejoice in the living God, like a branch growing on His **True Vine**. In this way, you will at length recover the image of God and be delivered from the condition of the Serpent. Then you shall become my brother and have fellowship with the angels."

### *The poor Soul said,*

**How** can I forsake my own Will, so that the <term>Creatures</term> <note>original: "Creatures"; here referring to worldly attachments, selfish desires, or created things that distract from the Creator</note> which lodge within it may die, seeing as I must live in the World and have need of it as long as I live?

### *The enlightened Soul said,*

**Now** you have worldly power and riches, which you possess as your own to do with as you please. You do not care how you get or use them, employing them only in the service and indulgence of your worldly and empty <note>original: "carnal and vain"</note> desires. Indeed, even though you see the poor and needy wretch—who is your brother and lacks your help—you do not help him. Instead, you lay heavy burdens upon him by demanding more than his abilities can bear or his necessities can afford. You oppress him by forcing him to spend his labor and sweat for your sake and for the gratification of your own pleasure-seeking <note>original: "voluptuous"</note> will. Furthermore, you are proud and insult him; you behave roughly and sternly toward him, exalting yourself above him and thinking little of him compared to yourself. 

Then that poor, oppressed brother of yours comes and complains with sighs toward God that he cannot reap the benefit of his own labor and pain, but is forced by you to live in misery. By these sighs and groans of his, he raises up the wrath of God within you, which makes your inner fire and restlessness even greater. These are the "Creatures" you are in love with. You have broken yourself off from God for their sake and have brought your love into them—or brought them into your love—so that they live within you. You nourish and keep them by continually receiving them into your desire; they live in and through your mind because you bring the lust of your life into them. They are nothing but unclean, filthy, and evil offspring of your <term>Bestial Nature</term> <note>the lower, animalistic part of human nature that seeks only self-gratification</note> which, by your receiving them into your lust or desire, have taken on a shape and formed themselves within you. 

That image is a **Beast with four Heads**: First, **Pride**. Second, **Covetousness** <note>Greed or the craving for more wealth</note>. Third, **Envy**. Fourth, **Anger**. In these four properties, the foundation of Hell consists, which you carry within and around you. It is imprinted and engraved in you, and you are held completely captive by it. For these properties live in your natural life, and by them you are severed from God; you can never come to him unless you forsake these evil "Creatures" so that they may die within you.

**But** since you ask me to tell you how to forsake your own perverse, creaturely will so that these "Creatures" might die while you still live with them in the world, I must assure you that there is only one way to do it. It is a **narrow** and **straight** <note>original: "strait"; meaning narrow or difficult</note> way. It will be very hard and tiresome to you at the beginning, but afterward, you will walk in it cheerfully.

**You** must seriously consider that in the course of this worldly life, you walk in the anger of God and in the foundation of Hell. This is not your true native country. A Christian should and must live in Christ and truly follow him in his conduct. One cannot be a Christian unless the spirit and power of Christ lives in them so fully that they become completely subject to it. Now, since the Kingdom of Christ is not of this world but in Heaven, you must always be in a state of constant <term>Ascension</term> <note>a spiritual rising or moving toward the divine</note> toward Heaven if you wish to follow Christ, even though your body must dwell among created things and use them.

**The** narrow way of this constant ascension into Heaven and the imitation of Christ is this: You must despair of all your own power and strength, for by your own power you cannot reach the gates of God. You must firmly purpose and resolve to give yourself up entirely to the mercy of God and to sink down with your whole mind and reason into the suffering <note>original: "Passion"</note> and death of our Lord **Jesus Christ**, always desiring to persevere in the...

This ensures that no creature, person, or thing remains able to take hold of your will and captivate it; instead, your will should be sincere and purged of all created things. 

Furthermore, if it should be required, you must be willing and ready to forsake all your worldly honor and profit for Christ’s sake. You should regard nothing on earth so highly as to set your heart and affections upon it. Instead, whatever your state, degree, or condition—regarding worldly rank or riches—you must consider yourself to be only a servant of God and of your fellow Christians, or a steward in the office where your Lord has placed you. All arrogance and self-exaltation must be humbled, brought low, and so completely destroyed <note>original: "annihilated"</note> that nothing of your own, or of any other created thing, may stay in your will to fix your thoughts or imagination upon it.

This love is indeed already within you. It will deliver you from your attachments to created things, enlighten your will, and kindle it with the flame of love, through which you shall have victory over the devil. 

This does not mean you can will or do anything in your own strength. Rather, you must enter into the suffering and resurrection of Jesus Christ and take them for yourself. With them, you must assault and break the kingdom of the devil within you and put to death <note>original: "mortify"</note> your worldly attachments. You must resolve to enter into this way this very hour and never depart from it, but willingly submit yourself to God in all your endeavors and actions, so that he may do with you as he pleases.

When your will is thus prepared and resolved, it has then broken through its own attachments to created things. It is sincere in the presence of God and clothed with the merits of Jesus Christ. It may then freely go to the Father like the Prodigal Son, fall down in his presence, and pour out its prayers. Putting forth all its strength in this divine work, the soul must confess its sins and disobedience and how far it has departed from God. This must be done not with empty words, but with all its strength—which really amounts only to a strong purpose and resolution, for the soul has no strength or power of its own to effect any good work.

Now, when you are ready, and your heavenly Father sees your coming and returning to him in such repentance and humility, he will speak to you inwardly and say within you:

> *Behold, this is my son whom I had lost; he was dead and is alive again.* 

And he will come to meet you in your mind with the grace and love of Jesus Christ. He will embrace you with the beams of his love and kiss you with his Spirit and strength. Then you shall receive grace to pour out your confession before him and to pray powerfully. This is truly the right place where you must wrestle in the light of his presence <note>original: "countenance"</note>. 

If you stand resolutely here and do not shrink back, you will see or feel great wonders. For you will find Christ within you assaulting hell and crushing your "beasts" <note>original: "beasts"; refers to animalistic passions or the lower, fallen nature of man</note> to pieces. ## *The Poor Soul’s Practice*

Then the poor soul began to practice this course with such earnestness that it believed it would win the victory immediately. However, it found that the gates of Heaven were shut against it when it relied on its own strength and power. It was, as it were, rejected and forsaken by God, and did not receive even one look or glimpse of grace from Him. At this, the soul said to itself, *“Surely you have not sincerely submitted yourself to God. Desire nothing at all from Him, but only submit yourself to His judgment and condemnation, so that He may kill your evil inclinations. Sink down into Him beyond the limits of nature and created things, and submit yourself to Him, so that He may do with you what He will; for you are not worthy even to speak to Him.”* 

Accordingly, the soul resolved to sink down and to forsake its own will. When it had done so, it was immediately struck by the greatest possible repentance for the sins it had committed. It wailed bitterly over its ugly shape and was truly and deeply sorry that those evil creatures dwelt within it. Because of its sorrow, it could not speak another word in the presence of God. In its repentance, it considered the bitter passion <note>original: "Passion," referring to the suffering of Jesus Christ leading up to and during his crucifixion.</note> and death of Jesus Christ—namely, what great anguish and torment He had suffered for its sake in order to deliver the soul from its own anguish and change it back into the image of God. 

In this consideration, the soul completely sank down. It did nothing but complain of its own ignorance and negligence, and that it had not been thankful to its Redeemer, nor once considered the great love He had shown to it. Instead, it had spent its time idly and not at all considered how it might come to share in His purchased and offered grace; rather, it had formed within itself the images and figures of earthly things, along with the vain lusts and pleasures of the world. Because of this, it had acquired such animal-like inclinations that it now had to lie captive in great misery. Out of pure shame, it did not dare lift up its eyes to God, who hid the light of His countenance from it and would not even look upon it. 

As it was thus sighing and crying, it was drawn into the abyss <note>original: "Abyss," referring here to a bottomless pit of spiritual void or the "dark world."</note> or pit of horror, and was laid, as it were, at the gates of Hell to perish. At this, the poor troubled soul was essentially stripped of its senses and wholly forsaken, so that it nearly forgot all its own actions. It was willing to yield itself to death and cease to be a creature. Accordingly, it did yield itself to death and desired nothing else but to die and perish in the death of its Redeemer Jesus Christ, who had suffered such torments and death for its sake. And in this state of perishing, it began to sigh and pray very inwardly to the Divine Goodness, sinking down into the mere mercy of God.

Upon this, the lovable face of God's love suddenly appeared to it, penetrating through the soul like a great light and making it exceedingly joyful. It then began to pray properly and to thank the Most High for such grace, rejoicing abundantly that it was delivered from the death and anguish of Hell. Now it tasted the sweetness of God and of His promised truth. All the evil spirits that had harassed it before—and kept it back from the grace, love, and inward presence of God—were forced to leave. The Wedding of the Lamb <note>A biblical reference to the union of Christ and the Church; here, it signifies the mystical union between the soul and the Divine.</note> was now celebrated; that is, the noble <term>Sophia</term> <note>Sophia is the Greek word for Wisdom; in Boehme's theology, she represents the "Divine Wisdom" or the "Eternal Bride" of the soul.</note> espoused or betrothed herself to the soul.
