# The Fifth Chapter.

## Containing Advice and Directions for a Soul Surrounded by the Melancholy Complexion.

133. A soul enclosed and locked up in the *melancholy chamber* should not by any means <term>speculate</term> <note>original: "speculate"; here meaning to engage in deep, obsessive, or abstract philosophical contemplation.</note> into or meditate much upon God’s anger, nor should it give itself up to solitude. Instead, it should converse with people who are of an easy and sweet temper and a pious disposition. For then the soul impresses the subject of such conversations and meetings onto the imagination and memory. Being occupied in this more pleasing way, the soul is distracted from those deeper and sadder thoughts. No deep speculation is good or fit for a soul in the state described here, as the soul cannot turn such thoughts to its health and benefit; therefore, it is better to avoid them.

# A Treatise of the Four Complexions. Chap. 5.

**134.** A person of this temperament should also avoid reading books that teach the doctrine of a partial and personal election <note>original: "Election"; here referring to the theological debate over predestination, specifically the idea that God chooses only certain individuals for salvation.</note>. Such books treat that subject without true understanding; they do not explain it according to the meaning and expression of the mystical language of the Holy Spirit, as has been proven and made clear in our other writings.

**135.** Furthermore, he should not confuse or distract his mind by reading a great variety of books. Instead, he should stick solely and closely to the Holy Scriptures, where he may find steady and lasting comfort.

**136.** However, if God has naturally endowed him with a mind and thoughts that are deep, inquisitive, and penetrating—so that his soul cannot stop searching for answers—then let him seek for the opening of the <term>Centre of Nature</term> <note>original: "Centre of Nature"; a term used by Jakob Böhme to describe the fundamental inner source or "ground" of both the physical and spiritual worlds within a person.</note> within himself, doing so in the fear of God and with constant prayer. For in finding that, the soul will find rest. It will see its own ground or foundation, and then all fear, sorrow, and sadness will quickly vanish.

**137.** I speak of this with certainty from my own experience. Therefore, I say that whoever has found the <term>Centre of Nature</term> requires no other knowledge to confirm and establish his comfort. However, a person’s own human reason, through its sharpest speculations or highest natural powers of understanding, cannot attain it. God indeed bars it from no one, but it must be sought in the fear of God and through incessant striving, watching, prayer, and perseverance; only in this way can it be found. It is the greatest treasure in this world; whoever finds it has an easy and immediate deliverance from <term>Babel</term> <note>original: "Babel"; symbolically referring to the "city of confusion," representing the corrupted religious and intellectual systems of the world.</note>.

**138.** A <term>melancholy mind</term> should take great care to avoid drunkenness, so that the soul is not overloaded and oppressed by "earthly power." For when the body burdens itself with liquor, the earthly power takes instant possession of the <term>Complexion-Chamber</term> <note>The "Complexion-Chamber" refers to the inner mental or spiritual state dominated by one's physical temperament.</note>. The soul then enters that state with its imagination, feeds on that earthly source, kindles its inner fire with it, and rejoices or refreshes itself in it for a while.

**139.** But when the earthly strength or power of the drink has worn off and the person becomes sober again, the poor soul feels as if it were rejected or cursed. In that period where the earthly quality predominated, it lost its "Divine Imagination" or its desire for God.

**140.** God’s Spirit will not dwell in an imagination focused on earthly things. Therefore, fresh sorrow and lamentation arise in the soul from the realization that God has departed from it. It feels to itself as if it were reprobated or condemned. God’s anger sets itself against the soul as if it would cast it into the root or centre of darkness. This throws the soul into a horrible depth of anguish. To fly from this feeling, the poor, blind sinner often returns to his drinking companions again, hoping that their noisy mirth and the power of liquor will drown out the power of God’s anger within him. Thus it happens that these infatuated drunkards, in their habit of merriment and jollity, add one day of sin to another. They blindly throw their souls into earthly and hellish darkness—even into the anger of God. I say this in all faithfulness as a most certain truth, of which I have a well-grounded knowledge through the <term>Centre of Nature</term> and the deepest principle of life.

**141.** The <term>melancholy soul</term> should also beware of anger. Anger is its greatest poison and drives it into madness, as can be clearly perceived and known in the "Centre." For the melancholy complexion is like the "wild earth" whose nature or property it shares; it is waste, hungry, empty, and barren, and it has only a very weak hold on the great <term>Wheel of Nature</term> <note>The "Wheel of Nature" represents the driving, cyclical forces of desire and existence that govern the natural world.</note>.

**142.** Now, if it happens that the fierce fire of anger is stirred up too violently, then the <term>Wheel of Nature</term> spins with such an impetuous whirl that the body is seen to tremble. And then, because the <term>Complexion-Chamber</term> is so waste—

And since it is void of substance, the wheel <note>original: "the Wheel," likely referring to the "Wheel of Nature," a concept in Boehmean philosophy representing the driving, cyclical forces of life and the mind</note> cannot easily stop itself again. Nor can the thoughts be brought back to due order and consistency; instead, they all run together in a wild confusion and fierce tumult. During this rapid motion of the wheel, the mind cannot lay hold on or fix the thoughts, nor know what it says or does, as is continually seen in mad people. The Devil is also at hand here, and readily brings his own imagination into this distracted state of the human faculties, thereby often causing much mischief to be done.

143. This wheel indeed belongs to, and stands in, the outward spirit; but the poor soul can, and often does, lay hold of it, and is thereby brought into most dreadful distress. Yet no man should condemn any soul during this lifetime; for the Sign of the Cross remains imprinted in it, and the Door of Grace stands open.

144. The third snare or temptation which the *melancholy soul* must beware of—or, if it is already entangled, must escape from with all possible haste and earnestness—is greed <note>original: "Covetousness"</note>. This corrupt passion or evil property is just as hurtful to the soul as anger is.

145. For greed is an earthly desire, and this temperament <note>original: "Complexion"</note> is also earthly. Since its "chamber" is, as was said, very empty and waste, its desire naturally attracts earthly substance into its void mansion. It fills itself with that dark matter, where falsehood, unrighteousness, and all the other evils resulting from the earthly nature find a place and lie enclosed, together with the fierce, wrathful principle and the anger of God. This causes the temperament (which is itself an earthly desire) to be eventually thoroughly penetrated by and totally swallowed up in earthly properties. When the poor soul "eats" of this earthliness with its imagination, it later feels the severe judgment of God within its fire-essence <note>original: "Fire-Essence," the vital, energetic core of the soul</note>, or constituent principle of life. The fierce and tormenting flame of that fire is ignited and maintained by the falsehood and unrighteousness which greed had introduced as fuel.

146. Now, when the poor soul finds itself burning in God’s anger and surrounded by nothing but that heap of earthly evil—the matter of falsehood and unrighteousness which fuels God’s anger—it begins to doubt and despair of its salvation.

147. Since the poor soul involved in the melancholy temperament stands in the midst of so many dangers, there can be nothing better for it than to lead as simple, plain, and temperate a life as possible, in a moderate condition where there is no temptation to pride. I say, a sober, temperate, retired life, free, if possible, from a multitude of worldly cares. But if that burden cannot be avoided, then the fear of God and prayer should begin and end everything. With that security, all conditions are right and safe.

148. Indeed, the *Melancholy Chamber*, when furnished this way, is an excellent house of counsel. It has a door open toward Heaven. While it maintains sobriety, moderation, and watchfulness as its guards, it reaches or pierces as deep as the *Sanguine Chamber* <note>original: "Sanguine Chamber," the temperament associated with air, warmth, and a naturally cheerful or spiritual disposition</note> does. But without the indwelling fear of God, or the Divine Light constantly governing and directing its search, it attains nothing beyond the sphere of outward or natural reason. In fact, if this chamber stands open in a man who was born under a sign of which *Saturn* <note>Saturn was traditionally associated with the melancholy temperament, representing coldness, restriction, and weight</note> is lord, he is capable of doing the greatest mischief in the world. He builds *Babel* <note>original: "Babel," referring to the Tower of Babel; here meaning spiritual confusion or the construction of prideful, false intellectual systems</note>, and thereby deceives both himself and others, acquiring great power and reverence for himself through his native sternness and severity.

149. Therefore, if any man knows himself to be under this temperament, let him begin nothing without prayer. Before he undertakes any business of importance, let him commit and commend his heart, thoughts, and mind, his willing and doing, to God.

## The Sixth Chapter.

->*Containing brief advice to souls under the other three temperaments <note>The four "complexions" or temperaments (Melancholy, Choleric, Sanguine, and Phlegmatic) were an early modern system of psychology based on bodily fluids.</note>, namely the Choleric, the Sanguine, and the Phlegmatic; making, with what went before, a universal mirror or looking-glass wherein everyone may see himself. It is written just as it was represented or set forth, out of the light of God’s grace, to the eyes of the author’s understanding in the Spirit.*<-

### I. Advice to the CHOLERIC.

<margin>150.</margin> The man who has his best treasure, the noble and precious soul, dwelling in a Choleric house, should above all things practice <note>original: "exercise himself in"</note> humility; otherwise he stands in very great danger. He must pour the water of humility into the fire of his temperament, so that his noble image is not inflamed by it. For the soul in this temperament is naturally subject to the risings and attacks of pride, arrogance, stern severity, and sudden anger, and is therefore prone to exalt itself; this causes it to be feared rather than loved, unless the divine water of God—noble humility—descends and enters into its fire. Then indeed the fire of the soul breaks forth into its original love-flame, which gives a bright and lovely light and attracts the affections of all people.

<margin>151.</margin> For this chamber or temperament of the soul has a shining luster of its own in its outward nature. Yet it is rarely accompanied by a mild and soft temper, unless it has Jupiter or Venus in the Sign of Life <note>The "Sign of Life" refers to the Zodiac sign rising on the eastern horizon at birth, known as the Ascendant.</note>, or the Lord of the Ascendant in its birth chart <note>original: "Nativity"</note>. However, under Venus it has its own particular devil, which plagues it day and night with temptations to unchastity.

<margin>152.</margin> And I must give warning that there is great danger in this temperament; yes, much greater than in the Melancholy. For here the Devil comes in the form of an "angel of light." In the natural fire-glance or luster of this temperament, he tickles the poor soul with the flattering and pleasing sense of its own temperamental light, so that the soul comforts and supports itself with it, and thereupon grows bold, high-minded, and presumptuous. Consequently, it pays little regard to any restraint or obligation and swallows down the poisoned baits of sin without much reluctance or remorse.

<margin>153.</margin> Swearing, cursing, and light, insulting <note>original: "scurrilous"</note>, and lustful <note>original: "lascivious"</note> talk—which are all quite contrary to the holy name and pure nature of God, and profane Him in the soul—are not seldom but frequently practiced in this chamber. The wrathful essence of the fire so elevates and carries up the mind that it can very hardly be brought to sink down

down, through repentance and abstinence from sin, into a due measure of divine love and meekness.

154. Its natural will would rather live and remain in the principle of anger, dominating everything through terror and keeping everyone in fear of it. Furthermore, if a person’s astrological birth <note>original: "Nativity"</note> occurs in an earthly sign, then their natural inclination makes them unlikely to do much for the glory of God or the benefit of others.

155. Whoever, therefore, has their greatest treasure locked in this fiery storehouse <note>This "storehouse" refers to the choleric temperament, which Böhme views as a dangerous but potentially powerful spiritual state.</note> must be very careful and cautious regarding both their inner life and outward actions. For the poor, deluded soul directs its imagination into this temperament <term>Complexion: the ancient and early modern theory that a person’s physical and mental character was determined by the balance of four "humors" or fluids.</term> and becomes inflamed by its fire, not realizing that it sits all the while in the anger of God—even in the fires of Hell—until that fire itself awakens, or until the soul is deprived of the external fiery glow or desire within the temperament by the death of the body. Then the soul first discovers it has become a proud, fierce, and wrathful devil, destined to live in eternal darkness.

156. It is advisable, therefore, for a choleric person not to seek or work toward worldly greatness, power, or honor. If these should fall to them through Divine Providence, they should not satisfy their imagination by dwelling on them. A soul with this temperament naturally has an evil, proud "fire-eye" that is easily inflamed. A constant practice of humble and earnest prayer is necessary here as the soul’s best security against the surrounding danger.

157. In the fiery power of this temperament, the soul is also easily lifted into joy, but this is merely a natural joy arising from the temperament's fire, which the soul mistakenly believes is a fruit of the Holy Spirit. It is no such thing. When God’s Holy Spirit reveals itself in the soul, it always comes with great meekness, humility, and calmness, like the "still, small voice" of God to Elijah <note>1 Kings 19:12.</note>.

158. Oh, what a blessed triumph and full satisfaction and joy that Divine Guest <note>The Holy Spirit.</note> brings into the soul's fiery temperament when He appears! But this rarely happens to people now because the temperament has such a general and powerful dominance.

159. Therefore, you who are *choleric*, take advice and warning. Be humble, and diligently seek meekness in your words and works; then your temperament will not ignite your soul with hellish fire. *For God loves a humble heart.*

160. You are not any further from God because of your temperament; just take care that you do not misuse it. Make right use of its good properties and tendencies, and beware of its evil ones. Mortify and subdue your own will. *Let everything be done for the glory of God, and then nothing can hurt you.*

### Advice to the SANGUINE.

161. You may also live a righteous life according to this temperament; just do not let it turn you into a hypocrite. Because of your deep understanding, you are capable of great knowledge; see that you do not bring "straw and stubble" <note>A biblical reference to 1 Corinthians 3:12, signifying worthless or temporary works compared to "gold and silver."</note> into the *sanguine chamber* and mistake it for the Holy Spirit. For in this temperament, you also have a shining light, yet it is only human and natural. Take care that you do not defile this fair temperament of yours by allowing earthliness into it.

162. A sober, temperate life is appropriate for you. Beware of drunkenness, for that will throw you immediately into your enemy's arms. And as you have a loving nature, also be careful not to set your affections on carnal and impure objects, or the pride and vanity of life.

Böhme emphasizes that while temperaments are natural, they must be governed by humility and the Holy Spirit to avoid spiritual ruin.</summary>

163. **F**or although you are naturally of a humble, gentle disposition, you are still very susceptible to pride. This is because you carry within you a harbor or receptacle for the influence of all the stars, just as the air and upper waters do, and you share in their nature and properties.

164. **I**f you will enter into the fear of God and live according to it, you may very well come to the knowledge of the *Great Mystery* <note>original: "Great Mystery" - likely referring to the *Mysterium Magnum*, a concept in Jakob Böhme’s philosophy regarding the origin of the universe and the manifestation of God</note>. This knowledge comes not indeed from yourself or through the searching and operation of your own intellectual faculties, but through the gracious revelation of God in and to you. For you have a brighter chamber and a more open door to it than those of other complexions. 
Therefore, take care with what kind of food you feed your soul. For there is nothing so good that it may not become evil if evil is introduced into it.

165. **I**f people despise you, do not worry about it, but trust in God. Because of the gentle simplicity of your disposition, this will often happen to you in the world. But you must preserve yourself in that simplicity and have nothing to do with artifice and craftiness, lest you bring a strange and harmful spirit into your noble house. 
Remember that good old distich <note>a poem consisting of a rhyming pair of lines</note>:

> "It is better to suffer scorn here,
> Than to be lost after this life."

166. **I**f you give yourself over to drunkenness, then the devil will introduce much evil into that delicate and tender complexion of yours. He naturally hates your temperament because he has no rightful power or authority within it; nor can he have any until he acquires it through the introduction of sin.

167. **A** simple, private, and quiet life is best for you. You have a broad understanding and a light, wandering imagination; you are receptive to many impressions and just as ready to let them all go again, like the air which you resemble. But watch well what you let into and what you release from your soul, so that it is not merely the result of a starry influence <note>referring to astrological or worldly impulses affecting the mind</note>, but a genuine birth or fruit of God's Spirit within you. Otherwise, you will deceive both yourself and others.

### Advice to the PHLEGMATIC.

168. **I**nward truth and righteousness would be a noble and precious medicine for you, who are naturally full of falsehood and care little about what you say or receive into yourself. Poor soul, in this complexion you have a sea of danger and misery to wade through, for you are inclined to defile yourself with much sin, both in words and deeds.

169. **W**ater has a clear luster or transparency in itself and reflects a shadowy image of things from its smooth and shining surface; yet it is but a false mirror. The poor soul has such a false mirror in this complexion. 
Water readily receives all things into itself, whether they are evil or good; it retains them and becomes darkened by them. This complexion does the same. It admits all the poisonous beams or influences of the stars into its imagination and presents them to the soul as if in a mirror. The soul, mistaking the shadow for a substance, bites at this bait and swallows it, and afterwards shapes its inward and outward life according to that image or model which the magic power of the complexion has received and represents to it.

# Chapter 6. A Treatise of the Four Complexions.

...the influence of the stars. There is no kind of deceit as great as that which lies hidden in this complexion <note>original: "Complexion," referring to the physiological and psychological temperament of a person, traditionally linked to the four bodily humors</note>. Falsehood and hypocrisy are its mantle or cloak. With the bright luster or shining of its watery mirror, it makes a fair show of religion and would gladly pass for a good Christian and true servant of God, though it dwells all the while in *Babel* <note>Babel here symbolizes spiritual confusion, pride, or the "false church."</note>.

171. You do not easily discover the iniquity of your own ways by yourself. But if a man comes near you with a spark of the true Light, you may see it clearly enough in your mirror, which can receive it. The best advice that can be given you is to learn to know and acknowledge how continually you sin; the best thing that you can do is to enter into sincere repentance and to pray earnestly to God for the guidance and government of His Holy Spirit. This is so that the evil desire and influences of the constellation <note>original: "Constellation," referring to the astrological forces or celestial destiny believed to shape a person's natural character</note> may be broken and hindered from possessing your soul and driving it into such folly and misery.

172. A sober, temperate course of life would be health and soundness to you, together with perseverance in watching, in prayer, and in the fear of God. By these means you may be preserved from all the evil of both your complexion and the constellation.

He who is motivated only by those natural principles lives only the life of a beast. But when a man impresses the fear of God in his heart and sets it up there as his ruler, then the soul becomes a lord over the outward life and forces it to submit to its dictates. Otherwise, if that is not done, then the complexion is the master and guide of the soul. Though indeed it cannot govern by its own strength or power, it sets its elementary and starry looking-glass before the soul. The soul speculates <term>original: "speculateth," meaning to gaze into, contemplate, or reflect upon</term> into this glass, directs its imagination into it, and allows itself to be captivated by it.

173. The conclusion of the whole matter is this: seeing these things are so, a man should be a man and not a beast. He should govern himself like a man, with his better part—the soul—not with the brutish instinct of the complexion. In this way, he may attain the highest and eternal good, let his natural complexion be what it will. On the other hand, there is no complexion so noble that it is not open to the evil influence of the stars and the wiles of the devil. So, if a man will live only according to the constellation, the devil will certainly take his range and pastime in it.

174. Therefore, that precept of St. *Peter's* is a seasonable and proper piece of advice to all complexions: *Be sober and watchful, for your adversary the devil goes about like a roaring lion, seeking whom he may devour.* Resist him, standing steadfast in the faith, or through the grace of God, and be at no time secure or careless regarding his temptations.

# PREFACE

### TO THE

## READER.

<margin>ª 1 John 4:20, 8.</margin>
<margin>ᵇ 1 John 4:15.</margin>

These two small books of the *Testaments* <note>original: "Testaments"; here referring to the author's treatises or testimonies on the sacraments</note>, one on *Baptism* and the other on the *Supper* <note>original: "the Supper"; referring to the Lord's Supper or Holy Communion</note>, treat these two great mysteries more deeply and plainly than any book published since the time of the Apostles, and clearly resolve any doubts concerning them. This treatise also shows who is a fit *administrator of Baptism*. Furthermore, it reconciles the differences of opinion regarding <term>Transubstantiation</term> <note>The belief that the bread and wine literally become the body and blood of Christ</note>, <term>Consubstantiation</term> <note>The belief that the body and blood of Christ coexist alongside the bread and wine</note>, and the *participation of mere bread and wine*. It shows how to truly understand the *right participation of the true flesh and blood of Christ under the forms of bread and wine*. 

But we must know God before we can know his institutions. If we do not know *who he is*, how can we know that we love him, or that it is not something else we love instead of him? For the Apostle *John* says, ª *He that says he loves God and hates his brother is a liar, and the truth is not in him. For if a man does not love his brother whom he has seen, how can he love God whom he has not seen? And he that does not love does not know God, for God is love.*

Furthermore, the same apostle says that ᵇ *God is love, and he that dwells in love dwells in God, and God in him.* How can anyone know this excellent thing called "Love"—in which whoever dwells has ᶜ *passed from death to life*—if he does not *know* that he has it *within him*? And if so, how can he either know God or love him? This love must be *in us* if we are to be the disciples of Christ. Indeed, there is nothing mentioned in the *whole Bible* concerning heaven and redemption that we must not have *within us* while we are in this life, or else we are not partakers of it. 

Yes, God has poured out his love into our *hearts*, which is that *Word of Truth* and life that is able to save our souls; it *perfectly* saves those who ᵈ *receive* it (that is, those who *believe*). This love is both poured out and received by many souls who know neither what that *Word* is nor how they received it. For example: when any man is *troubled* by his *evil-doing*, is sorry for it, and wishes from his heart he had *not* done it; when he endeavors to keep a better *watch* over himself and resolves never to do the same again, desiring strength to *resist* doing evil any more; and when he is careful lest evil suggestions in his mind should allure or entice him to any evil again, and constantly walks thus circumspectly in his whole *life* to the *end* of his days—this man has the love of God poured out in his heart and has *received* it. Otherwise, it could not bring forth such *fruits of the Spirit*. *And he that is so led by the Spirit is the child of God*, though such a person might not know how to answer if you asked him what God’s love is, even though he dwells in it. The reason why there is so little progress in the *knowledge of Christianity* and the true *institutions of God* is...

...because people think they can learn those things by rote memory, and not by heart. Some are such enemies to themselves—which is deeply to be lamented—that if they read that the Scripture says a thing, they do *not* care what it means or how to understand it correctly. They fail to seek and find the actual thing spoken of, so that they may be certain of the meaning of what they read in that inestimable Book of God.

The Apostle [Paul] has directed us to *test* <note>original: "try"</note> *or examine all things, but hold fast to that which is good.* In *outward* things, we are easily persuaded to test them before we trust in them; but concerning *inward* things, we are for the most part ready to take them on faith <note>original: "upon Trust"</note> and never test or examine whether those *things* are so or not. We should act as the noble *Bereans* <note>A group of biblical Jews in Acts 17:11 praised for studying the scriptures daily to verify Paul's teachings.</note> did, who were commended for *searching* or examining the Scriptures *to see whether those things were so or not*. They did not just look to see if those *words* were written, but whether the *things* mentioned were truly as described, for they already had experience of those things mentioned in Scripture.

However, some fear that if we were to be so inquisitive and pry into *mysteries*, we would run into the extreme of being *too wise*. This is impossible, *except* in our own conceit [pride]; for our Savior says, "*be wise as serpents, but innocent as doves*." Indeed, true wisdom is required to be capable of apprehending the institutions of God. This requires not only reading and conceptualizing, but *living the life of Christ*. By doing so, we shall come to the true knowledge of Christ within us. Although he has been knocking and calling at the *inward* door of our hearts invisibly and without a form since the beginning of our existence—before our knowing and receiving him—yet after we have *opened to him* and heard his call by yielding our hearts in obedience, he will *take form in us* and *be born in us*. We shall be regenerated in him, and so we shall often feel him and see him within.

But after that, we must attain the *stature of a man in Christ* and be his disciples and students <note>original: "Scholars"</note>. We must be *taught* by the Holy Spirit <note>original: "Holy Ghost"</note> proceeding from him within us before we can know and understand such mysteries as his institutions are. If we did seek, we *would* find God and Christ in our hearts; for though they are in us, we find them *not* because we do not examine what and who they are. We are discouraged in our seeking, partly because many have sought in the way we accounted "right" and have not found anything. But the truth is, they have *not* sought in the *right place*. They look to find God anywhere except in their *hearts*, and yet whoever cannot find him there shall *never* be able to find him at all. But *there*, whoever seeks shall find him who is the fountain from which all things flow. The Scriptures flowed from him, and whatever could possibly have been written *is hidden in him*.

The Prophets and Apostles wrote and spoke what they *understood*, but God was in their hearts and minds and filled them with the *understanding* of the Holy Spirit. *Our Savior Jesus Christ* did not have the Spirit in limited measure <note>original: "by Measure"</note>, *for in him dwelt the fullness of the Deity bodily* <note>original: "corporeally"</note>. He grew in understanding until he had the anointing <note>original: "Unction"</note> above his peers. From this understanding within him proceeded those sayings which caused the people to confess that *he taught as one having power, and not as the scribes and Pharisees*. Though those men were learned in the Scriptures, Christ said to them: "*You err, not knowing the Scriptures*"—meaning the significance of the *things* expressed in them—"*nor the power of God*." He who does not understand the *thing* in his mind which he wishes to utter cannot rightly speak or write about it.

The Scriptures are the writings of men full of divine wisdom and understanding. However, few other books are written by people who even consider that the *Apostles* had such a thorough knowledge of the divine mysteries they wrote about. Some seem to think that the writers of the Scriptures received them through a type of revelation where a man or angel dictated *words* to *them*, while they themselves had no more understanding of the message than their human reason could grasp from the bare hearing of the *words*. In this age, some account that to be the only level of skill possible to attain in the mysteries of God. But we are directed by the Apostle—

# The PREFACE

<margin>* Luke 17:21.</margin>
James—who well understood by experience what he said—states that if we lack *understanding, we should ask it of God*. <note>Refers to James 1:5: "If any of you lack wisdom, let him ask of God."</note> And although God is in everyone, and everyone lives, moves, and has their being in him, we do not know him unless the Spirit of God moves and teaches our understanding. Where the fruits of the Spirit are present, the Spirit of God has moved and taught that person's heart and understanding. But with only a small measure of understanding, a person is not able *immediately* <note>original: "presently"</note> to grasp the *mysteries* of that Spirit and those fruits—that is, where they come from, how they are conceived and brought forth, and how they grow. Nor can they be known except by the same Spirit that produced them. Anyone who does not have the fruits of this Spirit—which are *holiness, peace, righteousness, and joy in the Holy Spirit*—does not enjoy the Kingdom of God. We will not see God until we have sought and found peace and holiness. And unless we are born again of water and the Holy Spirit, we cannot enter the Kingdom of Heaven, even though it is *within us*. Now, can anyone teach what it means to be born again, or what this water and Holy Spirit are, except for someone who *possesses them* and has been born again through them? 

21. I wish that people were diligent in desiring such *spiritual things*. Then God, who dwells in their hearts, would feel and hear their desires, breathe forth his Holy Spirit within them, and *satisfy* their desires with his gifts and graces. Then he would also *fill* their minds and understandings with the knowledge of all his mysteries. In this way, they would learn the true institutions <note>original: "institutions"; refers to established religious practices or ordinances.</note> of God in the school of Christ through *divine experience*.

Every art and trade in the world is a *mystery* <term>In this context, a "mystery" refers to the specialized knowledge or hidden skills of a craft or profession.</term> and is not truly known except by those who have *experience* in them. How then can there be a skillful dispenser of the mysteries of God without experience in them? We can learn them through experience, but without it, we know no more of them than animals do. Even demons, who far surpass mortal men in knowledge, *cannot* know the mysteries of God because they cannot experience them. However, they *practice* the mysteries of darkness and therefore know them. We are placed in this world to *do* the works of God so that we may know what his good and acceptable will is. Therefore, we should *work out our salvation with fear and trembling* through obedience and doing good. This will lead us to feel and know the good Spirit of God, which will teach us how to find everything if we search and inquire within that Spirit. Therefore, let us strive for what is holy, and we will feel and experience what the God of holiness is. Then we will clearly understand the Scriptures and the writings of all other men. We will be able to *reveal* what is true and what is false in any person’s words or writings in a clear and logical way, convincing all who hear us, regarding both spiritual and natural things.

It is to be wished that no one would be so arrogant as to claim they are performing the true instructions of God unless they have the same Holy Spirit *filling* their hearts as those did who are recorded in the Holy Scriptures as performing them correctly. When people are hardly even true children of God, they should be careful not to allow others to think more highly of them than they deserve. Instead, they should sincerely inform them that they are not what people assume. They should not take titles upon themselves such as God’s faithful servants, ministers of God, preachers of the Word, elders, teachers, pastors, overseers, messengers, and ambassadors of Christ, or apostles—those sent by God. Nor should anyone cite those scripture passages about Christ’s true officers as if they applied to themselves. By doing so, they push these claims so strongly that listeners who lack the ability to tell the difference are convinced to stubbornly maintain that these titles apply to modern speakers just as much as they did to the apostles, evangelists,

# LETTER

-> TO <-

## * CHARLES VON ENDERN <note>original: "Carol von Endern"</note>.

-> *Our Salvation is in the Life of Jesus Christ in us.* <-

> Noble Sir, beloved in Christ, with a sincere desire for the Divine Light within the active power of the Holy *Ens* <note>original: "Ens"; a philosophical and theological term referring to essential being or spiritual substance</note> in our *Emanuel* <note>original: "Emanuel" (God with us); a title for Jesus Christ</note>, I send you this small book, *Christ’s Testaments*, along with its preface. The first three sheets should have been written only once, as I intended to rewrite the whole thing, beginning with the first chapter. I also intend to publish this small book in a more simple style <note>original: "child-like Manner"</note> so that common people <note>original: "the simple"</note> can better understand it. However, because of its profound meaning <note>original: "high Sense"</note>, I have allowed the two versions to be written side-by-side <note>original: "the one be written against the other," likely referring to a parallel-text format; see note below</note>, seeing that you and other experienced seekers <note>original: "exercised Lovers"</note> understand this meaning well. In this way, those with deep understanding may have what is complex, and the humble may have what is accessible; yet the underlying truth is the same in both, even though the simpler version uses more basic words. And so I entrust you to the constant, saving love of Jesus Christ.

-> Dated at Görlitz <note>original: "Gerlitz"</note>, May 7, 1624. <-

**JACOB BÖHME <note>original: "Jacob Behmen"</note>.**

1. <insert>C</insert>HRISTIAN loving reader, this little book of the Testaments of Christ should be well considered in these present times, when men strive only about opinions. Mankind has wholly and altogether departed from the right understanding, seeing that they try to maintain Christ’s Testaments with disputing and the sword.

However, it is foolishness to the natural man <note>The "natural man" refers to someone relying on human reason without spiritual enlightenment.</note> and cannot be understood (1 Corinthians 2:14).

3. True understanding requires a completely different kind of earnest sincerity, which is not grasped by human reason. It is rightly understood by no one unless the Spirit of Christ opens it to him in his heart.

4. There lies a firm seal before it which no reason or art can break open, but only that slain Lamb of the House of Israel, who has the Key of David (Revelation 3:7 and 5:5 <note>The original text cites "Chap. iii. 5," likely a misprint for Chapter 5, where the Lamb opens the seals.</note>).

<margin>b Or, might.</margin>

Christ’s Testaments are a seal of the firm and eternal covenant of God. By this covenant, God has received man into grace again after the horrible fall <note>original: "Defection"</note> and sealed him with the outpouring of His love through His blood and death. This was done so that we <gloss>b might</gloss> believe His word and promise, which He has revealed to us in the Holy Scripture concerning His Son, the redemption from sin, and what was previously declared by the prophets.

<margin>c *Aufbeute* <note>original: *Aufbeute*; a German term for yield, profit, or booty, used here to mean a spiritual gain or "talent."</note>, talent, earnest money <note>original: "Earnest Penny," a small payment made to confirm a contract.</note>, or pledge <note>original: "Pawn."</note>.</margin>
6. And so now He gives His Testament to His faithful ones as a <gloss>c pledge</gloss>, and so makes them branches on the vine of His flesh and blood. Thus they are embodied into Him and made His true children, in whom He Himself will dwell with His flesh and blood through this testamentary pledge, so that they may pray to the Father—

<page-num>603.</page-num>

# ADVERTISEMENT

**H**ere, the reader who loves God should know: First, that these two small books were copied from the author's original manuscript as he wrote them in 1623. Secondly, that in 1624, at the request of some good friends and lovers of the Truth, he intended (as may be seen in the preceding letter to Carol von Endern) to rewrite both in a simpler, more "child-like" form for the benefit of the uneducated <note>original: "simple"</note>. However, this revision was only completed up to part of the third chapter of the first book, and no further.

But more specifically, let the reader take notice that the book is printed in parallel <note>original: "double"</note> pages up to the 17th verse of the third chapter. If this is observed well, it will *greatly* help in understanding this work and all his other writings. Where the expression is obscure in one version, it is clearer in the other. Furthermore, by varying the phrasing, everyone may discern the *latitude* <term>the range or scope of interpretation</term> that the author's words allow regarding their *meaning in all his books.*

Furthermore, it is certain that we may be led by these various expressions to a true knowledge of part of the Mystery <term>a religious truth known only by divine revelation</term>.

But this knowledge is not to be attained by outward hearing or reading alone, but by experience. Teachers or listeners who lack experience are *ordinary* teachers and listeners, but not true ones; for true ones are considered *extraordinary* <term>rare or exceptional</term> in our times. Such true listeners are all those who understand the Word in a feeling and perceptible manner, who bring forth fruit in their lives and conduct, and who possess the power of godliness. These people can teach truly from what they know, even if only in a small measure. But those called "ordinary" teachers, who only have a form of godliness but deny its power, cannot teach at all, nor do they deserve even the name of an ordinary teacher; such a person is not even a true listener. <margin>John 7:17</margin> Our Savior teaches us *that whoever will do the will of our Father in Heaven shall know whether his words come from God.* If He submits His own doctrine to be examined by everyone according to this rule, why should not the words of all others be examined by the same rule? Let us do this, and we shall commonly <note>original: "ordinarily"</note> attain what is indeed extraordinary: the true knowledge of spiritual things and the things of God, which are impossible for the natural <note>unspiritual or non-regenerate</note> man to perceive. You are asked to judge the author of this book in this manner, and no otherwise.

## The First Chapter.

### Of *Reason's* viewing of itself; how it tends to function in a creaturely form when it considers *Christ* and his *Testaments*.

---

<margin>* Or, senses.</margin>
1. <image-desc>Decorative woodcut initial 'A' featuring foliate scrolls and floral patterns.</image-desc> All strife and *misunderstanding* concerning *Christ's person* and his *testaments*—which he left behind him—arises from defective, creaturely *reason* <note>original: "creaturely," referring to the limited perspective of a created being as opposed to the Creator</note>. Reason wants to be the mistress of all things or beings, yet it looks only into the multiplicity of beings and into the variety and difference of beings. It only loses itself in such viewing and breaks itself off from its center or origin. It disperses its *thoughts* <margin>* Or, senses.</margin> into the multiplicity of beings so that they cannot see the ground from which they have sprung. Thus, in their confusion and outward wandering, they break themselves off from their *chaos* <note>original: "chaos," used here in the classical sense of a vast, primordial void or the underlying source of all things</note>—namely, from the eternal WORD of God and from the eternal divine speaking. In this spoken Word, all beings—along with *understanding, reason,* and *thoughts*—exist and take their ground and beginning from it.

2. For if the abyssal <note>original: "abyssal," referring to God as the *Ungrund* or the bottomless source</note>, non-natural, uncreaturely God—namely, the Eternal ONE—were to speak his WORD no more, and if that *speaking should cease*, there would be no more understanding, reason, or thoughts. There would likewise be no nature nor creature, and all beings would be an eternal nothing. For every life arises from the exhalation of the Eternal ONE—namely, from the *Abyss*—and there could be no formability in the Eternal ONE according to which, or out of which, *something* might be made.

3. For if there is a formability leading to a figure, then there must also have been a cause from which that form arose; otherwise, God would not be the only God who is without ground, time, and place. For everything that has a beginning has a *ground*; but that which has no *beginning* is without ground and form.

<margin>b Or, exhales it.</margin>
4. Every beginning goes out from the Eternal ONE through the exhalation of the Eternal ONE, by which the Eternal ONE brings itself into self-viewing, perceptibility, and self-discovery <note>original: "findingness"</note> for the purpose of moving and forming itself. Every visible and invisible being, spiritual and corporeal, has taken its origin in the exhalation of the Eternal ONE and stands with its ground therein. For the beginning of every being is nothing else but an "imagination" of the *Abyss*, so that the Abyss brings itself by its own longing into an imagination, and it models and images itself, apprehends that image-likeness, and <sup>b</sup> breathes it forth <margin>b Or, exhales it.</margin> from the Eternal ONE to a viewing of itself.

<margin>c Or, breathing out.</margin>
5. This <sup>c</sup> breathing <margin>c Or, breathing out.</margin> is the eternal Word of the abyssal Deity; it is a speaking forth of the Abyss into a ground, of the unsubstantial into the substantial. In this, the whole creation—along with the speaking forth, as in the separability <note>original: "separability," the process by which the unified source divides into distinct things</note> of the speaking—has taken its beginning, and evermore continues to do so. And every life consists in that separability of the speaking, where the modeled imagination in the exhalation parts itself into separability. In this parting, the sensibility of the only life is understood, where the One views itself in multiplicity.

<summary>This chapter argues that human conflict over religious doctrine arises from limited human reason losing sight of its divine origin. It explains that all existence originates from the "exhalation" of the Eternal One (God) into the "Word," moving from a bottomless void into a diverse, perceptible reality.</summary>

<header>Chapter 1. Concerning Christ’s Testaments.</header>

# The First Chapter.

<margin>In an imaginary manner.</margin>
## *How Reason tends to view itself in a creaturely* <note>original: "Creaturely" — referring to the nature of a created being as opposed to the Creator</note> *image-likeness when it considers Christ and his Testaments.*

### *From where the conflict regarding Christ’s Testaments arises, and how this conflict is an empty, unprofitable thing.*

<margin>At present.</margin>
<margin>Inward senses or thoughts.</margin>
All conflict and misunderstanding concerning Christ's person, office, and being or substance—as well as his Testaments <note>original: "Testaments" — here referring to the sacraments of Baptism and the Lord's Supper</note> which he left behind and through which he works at present <margin>at present <note>original: "presently" here means "currently"</note></margin>—arises from flawed creaturely reason. This reason relies only on image-based opinions and does not reach the foundation <note>original: "Ground"</note> of this mystery. Yet, it insists on being the master of all things or beings and judging all things. In doing so, it only loses itself in such mental images, breaks away from its center, and scatters its <margin>inward senses or thoughts</margin> thoughts. It runs off into a multitude of distractions, by which its foundation is confused and the mind disquieted until it no longer knows itself.

No life can remain in a state of certainty unless it stays in the center from which it originated.

Since the soul originated from God's Word and Will, yet has entered into its own lust and desire to have a will of its own, it cannot reach its first foundation while searching through its own self-will. Consequently, it wanders without a foundation in mere uncertainty until it returns to its origin once more.

<margin>Or, a resemblance or antitype.</margin>
Every beginning comes out of the Eternal ONE—that is <note>original: "viz." (videlicet)</note>, out of the Tri-unity of God—through the exhalation <note>original: "Exhalation" — the breathing out or speaking forth of the Divine Word</note> or the speaking of the Unity of God, just as a fountain flows from its source. Through this flowing forth, the Unity brings itself into self-observation, discovery, and perceptibility, in order to form and image itself. Every visible and invisible being, both spiritual and physical, has its origin in the breathing out of the Divine Power. They are a reflection <margin>or, a resemblance or antitype <note>original: "Antitype" — a person or thing represented by an earlier type or symbol</note></margin> of the distinct <note>original: "separable" — capable of being distinguished or divided</note> will of God and have their foundation within it. For the beginning of every being is nothing but an imagination of the outflowing will of God, which has brought itself into distinct forms and image-likeness; within this lies the whole creation. Every life consists in its own breathing back <note>original: "Re-exhalation"</note> and reflection <margin>or, a resemblance or antitype</margin> in the same manner.

Since human life is an outflowing and reflection of the Divine power, understanding, and skill, it ought to remain in its origin. Otherwise, it loses that Divine knowledge, power, and skill. Through its own self-centered speculation, it moves into centers of its own making and into strange mental images, by which its true origin becomes darkened and foreign to it.

<margin>Comprehends.</margin>
<margin>Comprehensibility.</margin>
6. Also, the foundation of the *Properties* <note>The "Properties" refer to the seven qualities or forces of nature in Boehme's mystical philosophy.</note> should be understood here: the division of the singular Longing brings itself into a state of desire, and encloses itself and makes itself essential or substantial. In this state of being enclosed <note>original: Incloſibility; here meaning the capacity to be contained or made into a substance.</note>, the *seven forms* of Nature take their beginning, as is sufficiently explained in our other writings.

<margin>Or, after.</margin>
7. Therefore, I say that the *reason* why people dispute and argue about God—about His Word, *Essence*, *Being*, and Will—is that their *Understanding* has broken away from its *Center* or foundation. This breaking away is nothing else than the Properties (which emerged from the Eternal speaking-forth of the *Word* into a created life) bringing themselves into "self-lust" <note>original: Self-Luſt; meaning self-centered desire or ego.</note> for their own expression. In their own self-conceived desire, they have broken away from the Eternal Longing toward the Word of the Eternal speaking. They have brought themselves into their own natural perception and become confused within the forms of Nature. Here, all thoughts and senses try to exist and wander without the one God, trapped in self-speculation and *Reason*. They can in no way reach their *Center* or foundation unless they sink down into themselves in their contemplation and return to the ground from which they emerged. They must fall back into the Eternal speaking Word and surrender their own wills to it, so that the individual will of the *created life* may be spoken forth with and within the Eternal speaking Word in its distinct parts.

<margin>Measurableness (original: Messlichheit).</margin>
<margin>Measurableness, and natural and creaturely formation:</margin>
8. This speaking-forth again is what is meant by the *New Regeneration* of human life and will. For in the beginning of humanity, human life was within the *Word* of God; it was manifested through the in-breathing of the Word into the *human body*, coming into a state of feeling, perception, and willing. However, the will then broke itself off from the Word in which that life existed (before it was a separate creature) and brought itself into a self-centered separation and the visible perception of the five senses. In this state of sensory perception, it now runs about and seeks the seat of God, but finds only *measurableness* <note>original: Messlichheit; referring to the finite, quantifiable nature of the physical world as opposed to the infinite.</note> and natural, created forms. Here, it struggles within its own center. For the individual will has created its own *center* and broken itself off from the Whole; in relation to the totality, it has become, as it were, *dead*.

9. Therefore Christ says, "*Unless you are converted and become like children, and are born again through water and the Spirit, you cannot see the kingdom of God*" (Matthew 18:3; John 3:5, 7). The individual will should return to its "nothingness" <note>The "nothing" in Boehme's thought is the "Ungrund" or the selfless state of pure potential before individual desire begins.</note>; then it stands again in the first *Birth* and will be spoken forth again by the Eternal Word into a Divine Will. For whatever exists—whose life and willing acts or moves outside of the Eternal speaking Word—exists outside of Eternity and lives merely in *Time*.

10. But since the soul has its origin in the Eternal Word as a power of it, it cannot find rest in the essence of Time. Instead, it seeks its own *Mother* who birthed it and brought it into a created *form*. However, because the soul has wandered away, it cannot find its Mother.

<margin>Distinguishable.</margin>
11. Therefore, all conflict regarding the *Divine Mysteries* is a useless thing; it is done from the outside, without God, in a state of self-perception where *sensibility* views itself in Nature as a created form. There is no comprehension or true *understanding* or knowledge of God unless *image-like reason* <note>Reason that relies on mental images or worldly concepts rather than direct spiritual experience.</note> abandons itself and sinks down with its own will into its Center again—the point from which it came, namely the Eternal speaking Word of God. It must receive that speaking or breathing of God into itself again and, through Divine science or *skill*, speak in a distinct and perceptible *form*. It must become a dwelling and temple of God, where God's will works, governs, and wills. Otherwise, there is no true knowledge or skill concerning God and His *Being* or essence.

12. For no *spirit* knows God or His Word and Will unless God’s Word and Will are manifested and active within it. Natural *reason*, without the *Light* of God, sees only natural resemblances; it continues in its own speculation and constructs a version of the *Divine Being* or essence in its mind as if God were merely a created thing. From whence is come...

<summary>Boehme argues that religious strife arises because human reason has detached itself from the "Eternal Word" to pursue self-centered desire. True divine knowledge can only be recovered by surrendering the individual will and being "born again" into the divine center.</summary>

# Chapter 1.

As is to be known by *erroneous Reason* <note>original: "erroneous Reason"; here referring to human logic or intellectual pride that is disconnected from divine inspiration</note>, which always teaches concerning GOD, and yet has no true *understanding*: Also, it never comes to *rest* as long as it runs on in strange imaginings.

---

Therefore, I say that this is the only *cause* why men dispute and strive about God—His Word, essence, or being and will: that the *understanding* of man has broken itself off from its *Original* <note>original: "Original"; the divine source or point of origin from which human life began</note> and now runs on in mere *self-will*, thoughts, and images in its own *lust* for *selfishness*. It imagines for itself another foundation for the Divine willing, where yet there is no *true knowledge*. Nor can there be, until the *life* returns to its *Original*—namely, into the *Divine outflowing* and *will*.

---

<margin>Or Image.</margin>
And if this is done, then God’s will speaks forth the *Divine power* and *wonders* again through the *human willing*. In this Divine speaking, the life may know and comprehend God’s will and frame itself within it. Then there is true Divine knowledge and understanding in man’s *skill* <note>original: "Skill"; here meaning human capacity, reason, or intellectual ability</note>, when his skill is continually renewed with Divine power, and when Divine skill presses forth through the life in that same way and manner as it flowed forth from the Divine power and skill in the beginning.

---

As Christ has taught us when he said, *Unless you are converted and become as a child, you shall not enter the Kingdom of God.* That is, that the life must turn itself again into God, out of whom it proceeded, and forsake all its own forming of images and lusts; so it comes to the Divine vision again.

---

<margin>Or, Oracle</margin>
All strife about the Divine will and being or essence, by which men despise one another, comes from *self image-likeness* <note>original: "Self Image-likeness"; the act of creating one's own mental idols or subjective concepts of truth rather than receiving divine truth</note>. This occurs when one man tries to grasp the image of another—namely, his thoughts—and yet cannot rightly understand them. One man sets himself in the thought and mind of another and brings what is his own into it; he compels what is another’s into his own meaning and forcibly sets himself above the thoughts and mind of another. He holds them as his very own and wants to make a show with them, thereby domineering in and over the thoughts and minds of others. He insists that men must worship and reverence his thoughts and mind, and hold them to be the *Word of God* or the speaking of God.

Thus man deludes himself and robs God of His honor. He takes *His covenant* in his mouth and yet hates the *discipline* <note>original: "Nurture"; here meaning the corrective guidance or spiritual training</note> of the *Spirit of God*. This Spirit, therefore, reproves him in his conscience, showing him that he is but a rebellious Lucifer <note>original: "apostate Lucifer"; referring to the prideful fall of the devil, used here as a metaphor for intellectual ego</note> who will compel others into his own image so they shall hold it for the Word of God.

<summary>The author argues that religious conflict arises from human reason breaking away from its divine source to pursue selfish "images" and intellectual dominance. True understanding only returns when the human will is surrendered to the "Divine outflowing," as illustrated by Christ's teaching on becoming like a child.</summary>
<keywords>Jacob Boehme, Divine Will, self-will, religious strife, spiritual rebirth, original source, human reason, pride, apostate Lucifer</keywords>

<header>Of the Original of the Strife Chap. 1</header>

...the conflict among scholars in their reason, so that men fight and argue about God, and about His *Being*, or *Essence* and *Will*. Each of them holds his own *Imagination* <note>original: "Imagination"; here, the mental capacity to form internal images or concepts of reality.</note> to be *Divine* and wants his own *Image*, which he has framed in the *Imagination* of his *Reason*, to be honored as God; yet it is only a natural image created by *Reason*. And thus, men struggle all over the world about these *Images* of *Reason*.

13. But a true person, who stands rightly in the *Image of God*, has no *Strife* in *Religion*: For he lives in his first Mother <note>Likely referring to the divine Wisdom or the creative source from which the soul originated.</note>, who has formed him with soul, spirit, and body, and his whole substance, into an image. He wills and acts in harmony with her. He is resigned to her and yields his will to her, and she feeds and nourishes him. Every property of the true, resigned man is nourished by its own kind. First, the body, made from the *Limus* <term>original: "limus"; the slime or dust of the earth from which Adam was created</term> of the earth, is nourished by the earth. <margin>* Thoughts.</margin> Secondly, the body of the *Senses* and *Reason*, which is a spiritual body, is nourished by its *Astrum* <term>original: "astrum"; the celestial influence or constellation of stars</term>, from which it has its origin. Thirdly, the soul is nourished in its principle from the *Word* and *Being* or *Essence* of God; for it was brought out of God’s Word and entered into a body.

14. Now, if the soul does not bring itself into its own capacity to form images and its own willing—into *Self-hood*—but instead brings its will back into the *Divine* speaking, then it receives its nourishment from the essential *Word* of God, namely, from the *essential Wisdom of God*. This is its food, from which it also reaches and attains *Divine Skill*. For no spirit sees any further or deeper than into its own *essential imagibility* <note>The capacity of a spirit to reflect or be shaped by the substance it dwells within.</note>; that is, into that *Essence* in which it works, which has made it image-like through the imagination. With that essence, it forms itself and views itself, and its *Knowledge* is only as high as that essence.

15. Therefore Christ says: *Unless you turn again with your will and your capacity to form images, and become like a child, who has no preconceived images in its imagination, you shall not see God.* Also, you must be born again, or else you shall not inherit the Kingdom of God. That which is born of *Flesh*—that is, of fleshy image-likeness—is *Flesh*, and cannot inherit the Kingdom of God. But that which is formed and generated *spiritually*, and through the spiritual imagination, that is *Spirit*, *John 3:6*. *For to be spiritually minded is Life and Peace, and to be fleshly minded is Death and Enmity toward God, says St. Paul, Romans 8:6, 7.*

16. Whatever the *Spirit* of the *Will* brings itself into through its imagination, so that it impresses and understands it, it also forms itself into that *Being* or *Essence*. For no spirit can bring anything to pass without being or essence. If the *Eternal One* <note>The "Ungrund" or the absolute, groundless Godhead.</note> were not *essential* <note>Substantial or having real existence.</note>, everything would be nothing. And if that ONE had no will, there would be no desire, nor power, nor word, nor essence.

17. Indeed, we acknowledge that the Will of the Abyss <note>original: "Abyss"; the infinite void or groundless source of all things.</note> has brought itself into a longing and imagination of itself, from which *Nature* and *Creature* have their origin. From this, the natural life also has its origin, which now, out of the divisibility of the exhaled Will, has its own *Will* and imagination to form and image itself according to its longing and *Desire*. We see such changing in Nature—how Nature forms itself into so many kinds and properties, and how those *Image Properties* each desire their own kind again.

<margin>* Perceptive, or conceptual.</margin>
18. Seeing then that we understand in man that he, especially above all other creatures, desires and longs after *three properties*: First, he longs, according to his *perceptive Understanding*, for the *hidden God*; and though indeed he does not see Him with bodily eyes, yet he desires Him. Secondly, he longs after his *Astrum* or *Constellation*, from which the mind and rational life proceeded; therefore, the rational life longs for its mother again. Thirdly, he longs after the *Stars* or *Powers* of the earth and the other elements, and desires them for his nourishment. Therefore, we know by this hunger of his that he must have his origin out of these *three*; for there is a threefold spirit from such an origin to be understood in him; and...

But a true man inclines himself toward his Source <note>original: "Original"</note> and abandons all false mental images. He desires no self-created perceptions <term>original: "Self-Imagibility"; the tendency of the ego to create its own subjective reality or idols of the mind</term> of his *understanding*, except for what God chooses to shape and speak with and through him. He despises *no one*, but only distinguishes the true from the false and the good from the evil, teaching the Truth through the power and will of the Divine flowing through him.

All debate <note>original: "Disputation"</note> concerning God’s being, or nature <note>original: "Essence"</note> and will, is carried out through the images of the senses or *thoughts* without God. For if anyone lives in God and wills what God wills, why would he need to argue about who or what God is?

The fact that he argues about it is a sign that he has never truly felt it in his mind or senses, and it has not been granted to him that God is within him and wills what he wills. It is a *certain* sign that he wants to exalt his own ideas and mental images above others, and that he *desires* control <note>original: "Dominion"</note>.

<margin>1 Thessalonians 5:21.</margin>
People should discuss things together in a friendly way, offering one another their gifts and knowledge in *love*. They should *test things* with one another and *hold onto that which is best*. They should *instruct* one another kindly and not be so stubborn in their own opinions as if they could not be wrong. We have a powerful enemy against us who suddenly brings strange images into a person's thoughts and makes them act with pride <note>original: "insult"; here meaning to behave with arrogant or boastful provocation</note>; this is how sects and divisions <note>original: "Schisms"</note> come to exist.

<margin>1 Thessalonians 5:21.</margin>
It does not depend on any one person’s status, nor should people assume that divine understanding must come *only from specific individuals*. For the Scripture says: *Test all things, and hold onto that which is good.*

The test <term>original: "Touchstone"; a stone used to test the purity of gold or silver, here meaning a standard of quality</term> for this knowledge is as follows: First, the cornerstone, Christ—people should see whether a thing begins in love and results in love, or whether the love of God alone is truly sought and desired, and whether it is done out of humility or pride. Second, whether it agrees with the *Holy Scripture* of the Bible. Third, is it in harmony with the human heart and soul, where the *Book of Life* of God is incorporated and may very well be *read* by the children of God? In that case, the true mind has its *test* within itself and can distinguish all things. If the Holy Spirit dwells in the depths <note>original: "Ground"</note> of the mind, that person has sufficient means to test the truth; *that will lead him into all truth*.

# Of the Original of Strife Chapter 17

Then there is also such a threefold *Essence* or *Substance* in which his Spirit works, where every operation longs for its first Mother and receives its nourishment from her.

19. But we see that the *Soul*—namely, the inward *Ground* <note>original: "Ground"; here meaning the fundamental essence or foundation of a person</note> of man—in *Adam*, the first man, has turned its longing and desire away from its first Mother (its first source), which is the *Divine Word* and Will. Instead, it turned toward the operation of the stars <note>original: "Constellation"</note> and the elements. It formed itself in 그at operation and cultivated a strange imagination. By doing so, the *Divine Food*—the *essential Wisdom* of God—is withdrawn from the soul, because the soul has broken itself off from it with its longing desire. Consequently, the soul is entirely blind regarding God, and the first *Divine Essence* (in which God created it) has departed.

<margin>i Fragility.</margin>
20. When the soul brought its imagination away from that *Divine Essence* or *Substance* and into the earthly and astral property, its body—in which the threefold spirit works—also became entirely earthly, gross, and beastly. For whatever the imagination of the spirit enters into, the *body* also becomes that thing through the impression of the spiritual desire. We see this in man: he has acquired a gross, earthly body in which the principles now stand in mere strife, opposition, and *enmity*. From this, i pain, corruptibility, and death exist. God forbade this to him in *Paradise* while he still stood there, warning that he should not eat of the knowledge of *Evil* and *Good* with his imagination; otherwise, he would fall into such necessity, misery, and death, and *die* to the Kingdom of Heaven—which is exactly what happened (*Genesis* 2:17).

21. When the soul entered into the earthly imagination, it entered into the earthly *image* and lost the heavenly *image*. Whereas it should have shaped itself into the essential *Wisdom*—the holy, heavenly, essential *Word*—and taken its nourishment from there, it instead shaped itself in the outward *Astrum* <note>original: "Astrum"; referring to the celestial or astrological influences of the physical universe</note> or constellation, and in the *serpent’s* and *devil’s desire*. Because of this, in its noble *image*, it became a *wizard* <note>original: "Wizard"; in this context, it means a distorted, monstrous, or spectral being rather than a sorcerer</note> and *monster* in the sight of God. It lost its *Angelical Form* as well as *Paradise* and the Kingdom of Heaven. Now, its *foundation* stood in the impression of *darkness* within the *anger* of God. It would have had to remain in such a distorted image forever if the great *Love* of God had not come to help it again, and if the Divine Word—its first Mother and original source—had not again breathed or spoken *Grace* into it. This same Word, with its most inward secrecy and *Love*, would give itself again into the foundation of the soul as a new wellspring and fountain. It would bring the soul *new* nourishment for its life, whereby its natural fiery and painful property becomes changed back into the image of God.

<margin>k Adverse.</margin>
<margin>l In the Midst.</margin>
22. This great Divine Love would be a *death* to the k contrary will, as well as to the *serpent’s* and *devil’s poison*. It would slay the monstrous *image* and false imagination and bring the first *image* back into a new life. This new life, through this introduced Love, should again eat of the essential *Wisdom* of God and shape itself within it through desire. Thus, the true *Divine Science* <note>original: "Science"; here meaning divine knowledge or systematic understanding of God</note> may be manifested in it again and might work in a creaturely life, bringing itself l together into a creaturely *imagibility* <note>original: "Imagibility"; the capacity to take on a form or image</note>.

<margin>m Formings.</margin>
23. For this *end*, God created angels and men: because he wanted to reflect his Eternal Knowledge through his essential Wisdom in m *forms*. In and with these forms, the Eternal Spirit plays, and has thereby established a *harmony* of divine fullness of joy for the endless comfort of such beings—namely, the *angels* and *men*, and those who have their *origin* out of God’s Word and power.

# Chapter 1. About Christ's Testaments.

<margin>h Or pledge.</margin>
Christ's testaments <note>original: "testaments," referring to the sacraments of Baptism and the Lord's Supper</note> are a secret *mystery*, and are offered to the *minds* and *thoughts* that have turned away from the world and returned to God. Where life brings *itself* back to God, the *thoughts* that return to God will first be fed with *divine power* and *understanding*. These thoughts afterwards *kindle* the life, so that it hungers for God; to which is afterwards given Christ's flesh and blood as a ^h *pledge* <note>original: "pawn"</note> and *seal*. The divine ^h *essence* or *substance* will be imprinted within it; by this, life is brought back into its ^h *earnest* <note>original: "earnest," here meaning the fundamental root or down-payment of the original state</note> origin—namely, into God's *power* and *word*.

A person's false thoughts or mind are nourished by what they resemble—namely, by their own *conjecture*, or from *pride* <note>original: "highness of mind"</note>, or from the *subtlety* of the *serpent*. The mind desires to exalt these things and shape them into an *image*; and that *image* is a *branch* on the *tree* of *Satan*.

Now, the person who is fed by the *divine power* and *spirit* in their *mind* and *thoughts* is divinely minded, and brings forth good *things* out of *their good heart*.

But the person who is fed in their *thoughts* by the *power* and *will* of the *flesh* is *fleshly* minded only.

<margin>i Imaginary.</margin>
When *reason* considers Christ's *testaments*, and ponders how Christ can still be *present* in His *testaments*, it then assumes it happens in an ^i image-like <note>original: "imaginary," meaning figurative or based on a mental picture</note> *manner*.

And when reason realizes that it is not done in a literal, image-like manner, it then completely abandons that idea and thinks He is present only in *remembrance*. It thinks that just as when His word is *preached*, He works powerfully only through that preaching; reason thinks the same regarding His *testaments*—that Christ works only spiritually through *faith*, and that the *testaments* are *only* signs or symbols by which we should instruct ourselves in what He has done for us. It thinks we should use them *only* to declare His death and the shedding of His blood, keeping it in vivid remembrance for our comfort.

<margin>k Or senses.</margin>
Thus *reason* understands nothing at all of the Kingdom of Christ, much less of His *person* or of His *office*. In that respect, people dispute and struggle over it, trying to reach understanding through the searchings of *reason*. None of this achieves true *understanding*, for Christ's testaments are heavenly, and *reason* is earthly and worldly. It seeks Christ in time <note>that which is temporary or physical</note>, and if it does not find Him there according to its own power, it assumes He is present only to the ^k *thoughts* <note>original: "senses"</note> which project themselves up toward heaven. But this will *not* renew the life and bring it back to God; it will *not achieve* the new birth.

All conflict comes from this: that people do not understand the *heaven* where Christ sits at the *right hand of God*—that He is in this world, and that the...

(after the Fall) has *become Man*, and has introduced his *essential Love*—namely, the *essential Wisdom* of God—again into our heavenly <term>Ens</term> <note>original: Ens; a philosophical term for the hidden "essence" or "being" of a substance</note> and substance that had faded away from God. He has made our substance, which had withered in relation to God, living in *him* again through the introduction of his living Divine Essence. There, he made it openly appear before all angels and spirits how this great Grace of Love would destroy the Devil's introduced desire, and death as well. Through this newly introduced Love, he would spring forth through death, bring the human life through death, and change the wrath of God’s anger into *Love*. He would make darkness into light and, through this new Love, convert and *transmute* the coarse (earthly) human image back into a heavenly image.
