## **The World stands in Heaven, and Heaven in the *World*, and they are in one another, just as Day and Night.**

The inward foundation <term>original: "Ground"; the underlying spiritual reality or source</term> of the Word, out of which the *four elements* originated, is Heaven—namely, a spiritual world. In that inward power, Christ rules as true God and Man through the outward world. For where Christ says in *Matthew 28:18, 20*: *All power is given to me in heaven and on earth*; and also, *I am with you always, even until the end of the world*; and also, *He shall rule over all his enemies, until all his enemies are laid under him as a footstool* (1 *Corinthians 15:25*; *Psalm 110:1*). This is to be understood as his inward kingdom, where he rules in inward power over the outward earthly world, and also the hellish world.

For the outward world originated from the inward spiritual world—namely, out of Light and Darkness. This fabric <note>original: "Fabrick"; the structure or constitution of the universe</note>, before the Office of Christ stood in the Eternal Creator’s office, was worked [or effected] by him who from eternity has created Light and Darkness—that is, the spiritual world. This fabric has emanated <note>original: "flown forth"</note> and become visible, and was brought by God into a Creation in which Light and Darkness (Good and Evil) rule together. In this, *Hell* and pain are understood as the emanation of the Eternal Darkness, and the *Light of Nature* as the emanation of the Light; and the realm where Evil and Good rule equally is understood as the Kingdom of *Nature*, with heat and cold and all other properties.

God has given this dominion to the *Office of Christ*, so that he, being both true God and Man, should rule over all the properties <term>original: "Propriety"; the specific qualities, nature, or characteristics of something</term> and the self-will of this kingdom where Evil and Good rule within each other. Just as the *Sun* in the visible world rules over both Evil and Good—and with its light and power, and all that it is, is present *everywhere* and penetrates into every being, yet in its distinct form does not take anything away for itself through its outflow, but wholly gives itself into every being while remaining whole, with nothing of its being lost—this is also how we should understand Christ’s Person and Office. He rules visibly in the inward spiritual world and invisibly in the outward world, and thoroughly penetrates into the *faithful person's soul, spirit, and heart*. 

As fire glows through iron, and as the sun works through a plant so that the plant becomes "solar" [or filled with the virtue of the sun, and is as it were so converted by the sun that it becomes entirely of the nature of the sun], so Christ rules in the surrendered will <term>original: "resigned Will"; a soul that has given up its own desires to follow God's will</term>, in soul and body, over all evil inclinations and over the cravings introduced by Satan. He generates the person to be a new heavenly creature and flows entirely into them with both divine and human power, so that the faithful person becomes a true *branch on his vine*, in which God and Man (as to that same inward New Birth) dwell.

### The Second Chapter

#### Of God’s Covenant after the Fall; what the Fall of Man is, and how God has bound and united himself with him again. What the Circumcision in the Old Testament and the Baptism in the New are.

WHEN anyone wants to kindle a fire, they must have a substance that will catch fire; it must be a substance containing oil and sulfur <note>original: "Brimstone"</note>, or it will not burn. For if they cast a stone or something similar into the fire, it will not burn in a way that produces a shining light. The same is to be understood regarding the poor soul when it broke its desire away from God’s essence of love and meekness. In the beginning, this essence was within the soul like a spiritual oil and water, and the soul itself was like a spiritual sulfur in which the light of God burned. But then the soul turned into its own desire, by which it was shut up like a hard stone and lost all its love and meekness. It became like a burning sulfurous spirit which could not be healed unless the oil of divine meekness and love flowed into it again.

<header>Chap. 2. and the Baptism in the New Testament.</header>

<margin>º Resemblance, or a thing of a similar nature.</margin>
For this [divine love] to flow into human nature, there must be a subject—a <term>medium</term> <note>original: medium; an intervening substance or means</note>, means, or º <term>antitype</term> <note>original: antitype; a symbol or pattern that fulfills a spiritual type, such as baptism fulfilling circumcision</note>—through which it may be done. Human *faith* enters into this and receives virtue or power through such a medium or mean.

<margin>p Healing ointment, or anointing. 
Faith <note>original: Glauben</note>. 
See Chap. 1, Verse 28, on the reverse side.</margin>
In the *Old Testament*, this *medium* is *circumcision*, along with the *sacrifices*. In the *New Testament*, it is *Holy Baptism* and the *Supper of Christ* <note>The Eucharist or Holy Communion</note>, together with the *preached Word*. Through these, Divine Love and gentleness—the true p anointing oil of Divine power—flow into *faith* once more. Thus, the closed mouth of the soul is received into and included in the covenant of God; it is opened again by sweet *Grace* so that it can once more eat of the heavenly *Manna*.

->*What does this anointing mean now?*<-

*Answer.* It means that just as a person is <term>tinctured</term> <note>original: tinctured; chemically or spiritually infused with a new quality or essence</note> again in soul and body, and so thoroughly penetrated and healed that they are once more capable of receiving Divine power (namely, the Divine fire of love), so too must the "brimstone spirit" of the angry, fiery soul—which had perished in relation to God—be restored by God’s covenant through such an anointing oil. In baptism, the *water* of eternal life and Divine gentleness is poured into the soul; in the Lord's Supper, the *burning fire of love* from the life of our Lord *Jesus Christ* is poured into it.

*Reason asks: Cannot God forgive human sin without a medium?*

*Answer.* The issue was not simply about *forgiveness*. The soul required *not only* forgiveness but a *new birth*. It had followed its own will and completely broken itself off from God's will, which caused eternal *darkness* to exist within it. The source of its life—its own <term>separator</term> <note>original: separator; in Boehme’s thought, the internal power that distinguishes and organizes the qualities of life</note> (the cause of its movement and life as a creature)—had exalted itself. The properties of life had left their <term>temperature</term> <note>original: temperature; a state of balanced harmony among conflicting elements</note> and entered a strange, burning fire: an agonizing heat and cold, eternal hunger and thirst, horror, and *despair*. In both the life of the body and the soul, all properties were turned against one another, and humanity existed in an eternal *dying state*. The soul became completely blind and dead toward God. The more it tried to reach God through its own strength, the greater its internal agony became. The poor soul had been led by *lust* into worldliness, where Satan and the spirit of error took it captive and made it entirely monstrous. The more it sought rest there, the greater its pain became.

And this is what God meant when He said to *Adam: "On the day you eat from the tree of the knowledge of good and evil, you shall surely die" (Genesis 2:17).*

<margin>q Contraction or inward pressure.</margin>
Thus, the poor soul is poisoned by false imagination. Through the q **compression** of its own desire, it has become a hungry "fire-source." This state is merely a *closing off* of true life, a foundation of darkness, and a source of conflict and opposition. In this state, there is no longer any true <term>Divine Ens</term> <note>original: Ens; the spiritual substance or "being-ness" of a thing</note> through which the life might enter into the light.

Just as a hard stone is sealed tight, the soul was also shut up. Its good life became an evil life, just as *angels* became devils. These devils now exist in their essence as a horrible, poisonous, stinking "fire-source"; they cannot reach the kindling of the light and are enemies of all love and truth.

***

The great love of God came to help this compressed, blind soul-substance (which had perished in relation to God) immediately after the Fall. God spoke His love back into the center of life as a new covenant—entering the source of gentleness that the soul still possessed, even though that source of love within the soul was no longer able to move on its own.

Boehme argues that humanity needed a fundamental "new birth" or restoration of its spiritual substance, rather than just legal forgiveness of sins.</summary>

It showed how the introduced poison of the serpent must separate itself from the soul, just as smoke separates itself from fire and light; so that the fire and light then become a clearer radiance, no longer shut up within the essence, as it lies hidden within *wood*.

11. For without substance, no work can be done. Therefore, they visualized the *regeneration* for themselves through the sacrifices by fire. They formed or imaged the Serpent-Destroyer within the *fire*, envisioning how HE would change God's fire of wrath within the soul's fire into a fire of light and love, how the enmity would *separate* itself from the soul, and how the soul should be changed into an angel through Christ’s death (where the love of God gave itself up into this fire).

12. By means of this modeled image or type, they reached out with their desire and earnest prayer to God; and God’s Word of grace had also modeled and "inspoken" itself into men in this way. ### Chapter 2: Concerning Baptism in the New Testament.
5

And He placed His new covenant of grace—namely, the Serpent-Destroyer—into the perished heavenly <term>Ens</term> <note>original: *Ens*; here meaning the essential spiritual substance or "being" of humanity</note> of man. God promised that in the fullness of time, He would introduce and manifest His living *Ens* into this "in-spoken" Voice of Grace. This was the living Word of His power and wisdom, combined with the highest Love—the name **JESUS**. Through this, He would make the vanished essence or substance living and growing again. From this, the soul would once more eat of the heavenly substance, so that its anxious "fire-source" would be changed back into a "love-fire." A figure of this was Aaron’s dry rod (mentioned by Moses), which grew again and bore almonds.

<margin>* Text, form, image, or type.</margin>
This in-spoken Grace-Word of the Serpent-Destroyer is what the souls of the holy children of God ignited before the incarnation of Christ. They believed in God and His promise of the fulfillment that was to come; and in *this faith*, they performed their sacrifices.

Their sacrifices—especially those of the first fathers after Adam—were intended only to represent an image or figure of how the soul should be sacrificed in the fire of God’s wrath. They showed how the soul, through this in-spoken ground of grace and covenant, would be changed from the fire of God’s wrath into a fire of love. It showed how the soul should enter into death and die to its own self-will and false desires. The false will would be burned away, and through the power of this in-spoken grace of God’s love and meekness, the soul would spring up and go forth through the *fire* into a clear *light*. In this way, it would become a new-born child—no longer dark, but light—living no longer by its own will, but by God’s will. 

These sacrifices also showed how the serpent’s poison, which had been introduced into man, separates itself during this transformation, just as *smoke* separates itself from fire and light. Once the smoke is gone, the fire and light become a clearer radiance and are no longer "shut up," as light is shut up within the essence of *wood*. Similarly, the holy, divine fire of the soul was shut up through sin. No one could unlock and ignite it except the love of God through this incorporated covenant of grace.

The holy people of old set this image, type, or figure before them through sacrifices, looking toward the future fulfillment. They directed their faith toward the in-spoken grace of the *woman's seed* and the Serpent-Destroyer. In doing so, their faith could form or mold itself into the figure of Christ, so that the spirit of their will might stand in the figure and image of Christ, and their faith might work within that incorporated grace.

Since no work can happen without a substance to work upon, they envisioned or typified regeneration for themselves through fire-sacrifices. They formed or imagined the Serpent-Destroyer within the *fire*, symbolizing how he would change God’s "wrath-fire" in the soul into a "light- and love-fire." They visualized how enmity would *separate* itself from the soul, and how the soul would be transformed into an angel through Christ’s death (in which the love of God would give itself up into this wrath-fire).

By using this modeled image or type, they pressed through the sacrifice toward God with their desires and earnest prayers. God’s Word and grace had also modeled itself in men through the covenant. Thus, there was a conjunction between God and man: the human desire went through the sacrifice in the holy fire into God, and God’s love-desire went into this image of the Serpent-Destroyer. For it was God who ignited the sacrifice with holy fire.

The fire they used in their sacrifices was not a common fire, even though they used wood and offerings. Their fire did not come from a stone or steel, but from the highest <term>tincture</term> <note>original: *Tincture*; in Boehmian theology, this refers to the spiritual life-force or medicinal quality that transforms matter</note> of the paradisiacal ground, from which the fire of life originates. If man could understand this and did not wander in blindness, it would be well for him, and he *would be delivered from Babel and fables* <note>original: "Babel"; a common 17th-century term for the confusion of false religious systems or worldly chaos</note>.

*This* holy fire consumed their sacrifices through God’s imagination and ignition. There, the introduced human will, which clings to earthliness, was cleansed. In that holy fire, it was purged and ransomed from sin in anticipation of the future fulfillment. For the—

# Chapter 2. And the Baptism in the New Testament.

The foundation from which this holy fire emerged later manifested itself in human life, in the person of *Christ*.

Thus the symbolic pattern stood in their sacrifices [to show] how the earthly image of man should be preserved in the fire of God, and how the coarseness of the elements should be consumed. Out of that consuming fire would emerge the right, true, created, pure, bright, and spiritual image found in *Adam*. This image, which was in the fire of God's wrath, would be brought into radiance <note>original: "Clarity," meaning spiritual brightness or transfiguration</note> through this holy fire of great love. In this new image, the great fiery love would itself be the fire of life, so that it might no longer imagine or desire falsehood.

With this faith, the first men *before the time of Christ* (before Christ manifested himself in this incarnate Covenant of Grace and became man) were caught up and taken into the living Word of God—namely, into the grace where their souls found divine rest. *Note*: they remained there until Christ fulfilled this symbolic type and rose from death. Then he also arose and was manifested with his life and substance within them—namely, on the inward ground of the heavenly part which had vanished in *Adam*. They "put on Christ" in soul and spirit, and now they wait for their body to be formed out of the <term>Limus</term> <note>Latin: "slime" or "mud"; here referring to the "dust of the ground" from which man was created</note> of the earth. This refers to the "third principle" <note>In the author's mystical philosophy, the "third principle" is the visible, material world</note> of the property of the visible world: the formed, spoken, substantial word of the resurrection at the last day. This is also how we should understand the state of Christians today.

This foundation of the *holy fire* began with *Adam*, *Abel*, and *Cain*. When *Abel* and *Cain* sacrificed, God looked graciously on *Abel’s* sacrifice and kindled it with holy fire, and the *sweet smell went up before the LORD*. Because the image or type of *Christ* was present in Abel's faith, God kindled his sacrifice with holy fire, and it was acceptable before Him; for it was a union with the divine desire. But He did not look graciously on *Cain’s* sacrifice, for he did not have *such* faith. Instead, he remained in the perished Adamic nature of his own lust and desire, and had focused his mind on the kingdom *of this world*. Therefore, the holy fire would *not* kindle in his sacrifice.

*Cain* stood as a figure of the *fallen Adam* after the Fall, and *Abel* stood as a figure of the New Regeneration, symbolizing how Christ would go into death with his sacrifice and die for mankind. And so the image of Cain stood nearby, symbolizing how *Christ* had come to seek poor fallen man and generate him anew through His sacrifice.

But as human vanity gained the *upper hand* and their nature became even more evil and shameful, this *understanding* of the holy fire was quenched among them until the Flood came and destroyed them. This Flood was a type <note>A "type" is a biblical person, event, or thing believed to foreshadow something in the future, especially in the life of Christ</note> of *Baptism*, symbolizing how the water of eternal life—namely, God’s substantial gentleness—would drown and quench the false, fiery life of the soul, and how the soul would grow up out of the holy water in the gentleness of God into a *new life* of light.

<margin>With.</margin>
Now, when the time came that God renewed His covenant with *Abraham* (which He had first established in Paradise), He gave him the figure of Christ again through circumcision and the holy fire. This can be seen in the sacrifices of *Abraham* in Genesis 15: *how the fire came forth between the divided parts of the sacrifice, and how at the same time a vision of terror and great anguish fell upon him*. All of this signifies the death of Christ and the transformation of souls.

<margin>Abomination.</margin>
The circumcision of the reproductive organs was a symbol showing how the fleshly man, born of male and female seed, should be cut off from the image created in *Adam*. This happens through the death of Christ and the anger of God; through the bloodshed of Christ, man is brought back into "eternal virginity" <note>A state of spiritual purity and wholeness before God, untainted by the "beastly" nature of fallen humanity</note>. Therefore, males had to be circumcised on that specific member to signify the "unclean birth" according to a beastly manner, which is a vanity <note>Something worthless or offensive to God's holiness</note> in the presence of God. Therefore, God placed his Covenant of Grace in the figure of *Christ* upon this member, setting Christ before them as a "Throne of Grace," *so that they might walk before Him and that His anger might not consume them* (Genesis 17).

# Chapter 2. And the Baptism in the New Testament.

**Answer.** As mentioned above: The soul had become so inflamed with wrath within its own qualities that it existed in eternal death. Within it, God’s **essence of love** was no longer manifest, and therefore it was unable to kindle the holy fire of God—namely, the holy life. Because of this, God sent holy baptism beforehand and established it within the Covenant. For when the Word—the power of the holy fire—became man and revealed itself in Christ, then Christ, with the holy fire and through the humanity he assumed, **spoke himself into** <note>original: "inspake"—a term used to describe the divine Word breathing or speaking its power into the human soul</note> his fellow human beings, according to their humanity.

<margin>Immersion <note>original German: *Eintauchen*</note></margin>
<margin>Immersion <note>original German: *Eintauchen*</note></margin>
Now, for this "speaking into" to take effect and become substantial, the divine **infusion** <margin>Immersion <note>original: *Eintauchen*</note></margin> had to happen first. As soon as the Word manifested itself in humanity, the gentle love and grace within the Covenant flowed forth. With this flowing forth of divine love, the Covenant was established in water baptism. 

Since man was made of an elementary, earthly nature, there had to be an elementary **medium** or means for that purpose. This medium allowed the flowing divine love in the Covenant to take hold, acting as an intermediary where the divine and human "imagination" <note>In this context, 'imagination' refers to a creative, formative desire or spiritual focus</note> might enter. This allowed the divine to <margin>infuse <note>original: *Eintauchen*</note></margin> itself into humanity as an **ens** <term>a living essence or spiritual seed</term> or "kindler," through which the holy fire could be lit within the dry "fire" of the soul.

This process was mirrored in the Old Testament circumcision and sacrifices. In those rituals, the **fat** of the animals served as a medium. Through this medium, the human desire (kindled by the Covenant) went to meet God, and God’s imagination likewise went to meet the Covenant in man. In this way, the holy fire stood opposite the divine wrath and consumed the impurity in the human **will**, so that the soul might reach God.

We see this same image in **Moses** on Mount Sinai. There, the Father's attribute of fire first revealed itself, requiring man’s full obedience to live in holiness before God and to approach him in purity through sacrifice. If they did not, he would consume them in a curse through this fire. This was a symbol, "type," or shadow <note>A 'type' is an Old Testament event or person that serves as a prophetic symbol of something in the New Testament</note> signifying how human vanity must be purged through the fire of God's wrath. 

However, Israel could not reach salvation or the love of God through that fire alone, nor could they enter the promised land through Moses. They could only enter through **Joshua** <note>Joshua and Jesus share the same name in Hebrew (*Yeshua*), signifying the transition from the Law to Grace</note> and **Christ**.

Therefore, God brought his heavenly substance and his Covenant into water baptism to provide a manageable **medium**. Through this, he could introduce his essence of love into our faded heavenly substance, allowing the holy fire to be kindled within us once again.

### What the Sacrifices and Circumcision in the Old Testament Signified, Chapter 2.

32. Baptism, with the grace that flows out first into the heavenly *essence* <term>original: Ens; the fundamental spiritual substance or being</term> of man—that is, into the vanished substance where the indwelling paradisiacal <note>original: Paradifical; relating to Paradise</note> covenant of the Serpent-Destroyer <note>A reference to Christ, based on the promise in Genesis 3:15 that the offspring of the woman would crush the head of the serpent</note> stood—pierced into that same covenant.

33. Yet, because the human essence had become earthly, it had to enter through a *medium* <note>a physical means or bridge</note> that the human essence could take hold of. For it cannot take hold of God’s holiness directly, because the human will was severed from it; therefore, there must now be a *similitude* <note>a likeness or physical representation</note> which the imagination <term>In this context, "imagination" refers to the creative or forming power of the human will and spirit</term> of human nature can grasp.

34. For Christ also possessed *this similitude*—namely, the elements he received from us humans—so that the Divine imagination might take hold in the *water*. In this way, the Divine and human imaginations together might awaken and kindle the indwelling paradisiacal covenant, in the same way that a glimmering *mother-fire* <note>a source-fire or spark that gives birth to a larger flame</note> or tinder-fire enters wood and begins to glow.

35. In such a manner, a Divine "mother-fire" of holy fire (a holy and Divine glimmering fire) was introduced through Baptism. This fire destroyed and broke *sin and death* to pieces in the *inwardness* of man—that is, in the vanished heavenly essence—from which the dry, withered tree of the inner ground *might* receive life again. This life is a *spiritual oil*; and in this new spiritual oil of the *power* of the Divine light, the love-fire (the *New Life*) should burn.

36. This is now the *water-baptism*, for which the Holy Spirit in the inner ground *is the hand*. As Divine love flows out from Christ’s suffering, death, and resurrection, the Spirit *baptizes* with Christ's victory. That is, he pours Christ’s humanity, suffering, death, and resurrection into the inner ground and *kindles* the indwelling paradisiacal covenant with this fire, so that the dry rod of *Aaron buds forth* <note>A biblical reference to Numbers 17, where a dry wooden staff miraculously sprouted flowers, symbolizing life coming from death and Divine authority</note>.

37. For through this infusion of the Holy Spirit, Christ is bestowed upon man. Through this, man is incorporated into *Christ*. The heavenly essence—which in the Virgin *Mary* assumed our human essence—is put on him along with the whole process of Christ’s life. It is imprinted into his own heavenly, vanished essence, leading to a new life that has overcome death.

38. Just as a *tincture* <term>an alchemical term for a substance that can transform and "color" another substance's nature through penetration</term> completely transforms and thoroughly penetrates a *metal*, or as fire makes iron glow all the way through, so should this be understood regarding those who are capable of receiving such an infusion, as will be further explained.

<header>Chapter 2. and the Baptism in the New Testament.</header>

Therefore, because the human **Essence** <note>original: "Essence" — here referring to the fundamental nature or spiritual substance of a human being.</note> had become **earthly**, a **Medium** <note>original: "Medium" — a middle ground or intermediary bridge.</note> was needed so that humanity might bear or endure it. For within God's holiness, without such a medium, the human essence cannot take hold, as the human will had been torn away from it.

For this reason, God became **man**, so that He might cause His **Deity** to flow into us through His **Humanity**, enabling us to comprehend or take hold of Him. This also allowed the **Divine Imagination** <note>In this context, "Imagination" refers to the formative, creative power of the spirit to shape reality.</note> to introduce and awaken itself within man and work together with the human imagination. He assumed humanity so that He might work within us with His divine nature through His human nature.

Thus, through water baptism, a glimmering, primal holy fire was imprinted in **God's Love** as a subject or object for the Divine Imagination's work. By this, death—in terms of the **inwardness** of man—would be broken to pieces and a new life would spring forth. Just as fire begins to glimmer in wood, so was this **infusion** or baptizing an <gloss>anointing or unction</gloss> of the Holy Spirit, acting as the oil for a new life in which the Divine Light might ignite itself.

This is the basis of **water baptism**, where the Holy Spirit in the inner depths acts as the **hand**. Through the outpouring of divine love from Christ's suffering, death, and resurrection, the Spirit **baptizes** with Christ's victory. That is, He infuses Christ's humanity, suffering, death, and resurrection into man, and ignites the indwelling **Paradifical Covenant** <note>original: "Paradifical Covenant" — the promise of restoration to a state of paradise.</note> with this fire, so that the dry rod of **Aaron** <note>A biblical reference to Numbers 17, where Aaron’s dry wooden staff miraculously sprouted blossoms as a sign of God's favor.</note> comes to **bud forth** again.

Through this **infusion** of the Holy Spirit, Christ is **bestowed** upon man. By this, man is incorporated into **Christ**, and the heavenly **Ens** <term>Ens: a Latin term for "essence" or "being." Here it refers to the spiritual substance of Christ.</term>—which in Mary took on our human essence—is put on and imprinted in him for a new life, along with the entire process of Christ's life and work.

Just as a **tincture** <note>original: "Tincture" — an alchemical term for a substance that can transform or purify base matter; used here to describe the transformative power of Christ's spirit.</note> transforms metal, or as fire glows through iron, so should this be understood regarding those who are **capable** of receiving this infusion, as will be explained further.

How Man is baptized by the Holy Ghost, etc. Chapter 3.

# The Third Chapter.

## *A briefer and more fundamental instruction on how Man is baptized by the Holy Ghost, through Christ’s suffering, death, and resurrection, in body and soul.*

1. When God intended to transition his covenant from circumcision to water baptism, the Word of the **inspoken grace** <term>the divine word or breath of God directed into the soul</term>, which contained the holy fire of God, first became a man. He took on the "seed of the woman" <note>original: "Woman's Seed"; a biblical reference to the offspring of Eve, interpreted as Christ</note>—meaning **our soul and humanity**—so that he might baptize us with the living covenant that had become human.

2. For the body of man, for which baptism was **necessary**, was made of the elements. Therefore, if it was to be baptized, the covenant first had to enter into an elementary **medium** (as it did in the humanity of Christ) and sanctify that **medium**, so that man might be baptized through it.

3. For this was not to be done **only** for the heavenly substance of man—the part that vanished in **Adam** <note>A reference to the loss of a divine or spiritual state following the Fall of Man</note>, in which the covenant in Paradise had established itself—as if that part **alone** should be baptized. No; it was also for the soul and for the body, made from the **limus** <term>Latin for slime or mud, referring to the "dust of the ground" from which man was created</term> of the earth.

4. The **whole** man **needed** baptism. All three principles of all the **three worlds** within man had to be baptized. These are: first, the **first** principle, which is eternal nature—**namely**, the true life of the soul that entered the body from the "Word of the Inspoken"; second, the **second** principle, which is the true eternal spirit—**namely**, the holy power of light and love (which I call in this book the heavenly, vanished **ens** <term>an existing thing or spiritual essence</term> and substance in **Adam**) in which **Adam** vanished when the soul's will departed from it; and third, the **third** principle, which is the astral animal soul, **from the spirit of the world** <note>original: "ex Spiritu Mundi"</note>, along with its body made from the **limus** of the earth—**namely**, the entire outward, visible man.

5. This **threefold** man was completely fallen. When the divine light in the spirit of the second principle went out, man became quite blind to God and dead to Paradise. A divine **love-ens** (essence of love) had to be infused into him again; in this **love-ens**, the divine fire and light could be rekindled to a new life. But for this to happen, the holy fire first had to manifest itself with the covenant within the threefold humanity (as it did in Christ’s humanity), so that God's Spirit might baptize us out of, with, and through this threefold humanity—so that each principle in us might be baptized with its own likeness. *For the Holy Ghost baptizes through Christ for the forgiveness of sins.*

6. The holy fire of the divine **power** in Christ baptizes his temple within **us**, which the holy fire—**namely**, the divine life in **us**—desires to possess. This includes the vanished **ens** of the heavenly world's substance, the spirit of **understanding** or power—**namely**, the second principle, or **angelical body** from the substance of the angelical world. To this substance, Christ later gives his most holy spiritual flesh as food, in which he himself dwells. This divine love in the holy fire baptizes this spirit, for it is an **ens** of the holy fire in which it burns or lives. And the first principle—**namely**, the **fiery soul** originating from the **divine science** <term>divine knowledge or the structure of God's wisdom</term> of the **separable speaking word** <term>the manifestation of God's Word as it divides into various forms or creatures</term>, from the Father’s property—is baptized with the **fiery spirit** of the Father’s property, as if with fire-burning love.

<summary>This chapter explains that for man to be fully redeemed, baptism must affect all three parts of his nature (eternal soul, spiritual essence, and physical body), which was made possible by Christ taking on human form and sanctifying the physical medium.</summary>

<header>Chap. 3. How Man is Baptized by the Holy Ghost, etc.</header>

## The Third Chapter.

### *A briefer and more fundamental instruction on how man is baptized by the Holy Ghost, through Christ’s suffering, death, and resurrection, in both body and soul.*

When God intended to introduce his covenant through *water baptism* into humanity, the spoken Word of Grace from God’s holy fire—that is, his fiery love—first became man. He first took on the "seed of the woman" <note>A reference to the prophecy in Genesis 3:15, traditionally interpreted as the human nature of Christ inherited through Mary</note>: our *soul*, spirit, and whole human nature, so that he *might* baptize us with the living covenant, which was both God and man.

For the body of man, for which baptism was *necessary*, was made of the elements. If it was to be baptized, the covenant first had to give itself into an elementary *medium*, as it did in the humanity of Christ, and sanctify that *medium* so that man could be baptized through it.

This was not done *only* for the heavenly substance that vanished in Paradise—the most inward ground of humanity where the covenant originally joined itself—so that only that ground should be baptized. No; it was also for the soul and for the body made from the *limus* <term>limus: Latin for "mud" or "slime," referring to the dust of the ground from which Adam was created</term> of the earth.

The *whole man needs* baptism: all three "principles"—the *three properties of the world* within man—must be baptized. The *first* principle is the eternal nature, the *Mysterium Magnum* <term>Mysterium Magnum: The "Great Mystery," a term used by Jacob Boehme to describe the chaos or source from which all things are manifested</term> or "Great Mystery," from which the visible world sprang. This is the ground of the true eternal soul, which entered the body through God's breathing. The *second* principle is the true eternal spirit, the power of holy light (which I call in this book the heavenly *ens* <term>ens: a philosophical term for "essence" or "being"</term> or substance that vanished in Adam). This vanished in *Adam* at the Fall when the soul’s will turned toward earthly things and broke away from it. The *third* principle is the man of the outward world's substance: the "astral soul" <note>In 17th-century mysticism, the astral soul refers to the part of the human spirit influenced by the stars and the physical cosmos</note> with its body, made from the *limus* of the earth, *which exists within the four elements.*

This threefold man was completely fallen. As soon as the light in the spirit of the second principle went out, he became quite blind toward God and dead toward Paradise. Into this state, a divine *love-ens* <note>original: "Love-Ens," referring to a divine essence of love</note> had to be infused or imprinted again, where the divine fire and light could rekindle into a new life. Therefore, the holy fire of God's *great love* in the covenant had to manifest itself in the humanity of Christ, so that God’s Spirit might baptize us out of, with, and *through* this threefold humanity. In this way, each principle within us could be baptized with something like itself. *For the Holy Ghost baptizes through Christ for the forgiveness of sins.*

->*How is this baptism of the Holy Ghost achieved?*<-

*Answer.* God's holy fire of divine *love-power* in Christ Jesus baptizes his temple within *us*. This temple is what the holy fire of life—God's Spirit—will inhabit: the vanished *ens* of the heavenly world's substance, the spirit of power and *understanding*, which is the second principle or "angelical ground." To this ground, Christ later gives his holy spiritual flesh as food, which is what the true <sup>b</sup> express image of God consists of: <margin>One's very own reflected image.</margin> The divine love and sweetness in the holy fire baptize this spirit, for it is an *ens* of the holy fire in which it burns or lives. And the first principle—the fiery soul—is baptized with the *fiery spirit* of the Father’s property, like a fire-burning love. This soul comes from the divine knowledge of the "separable eternal-speaking Word" <note>A reference to the Logos or the creative Word of God that differentiates itself into the variety of the natural world</note> and the Father's fiery substance.

## How Man is baptized by the Holy Spirit. Chapter 3.

7. *This is to be understood as follows:* The soul belongs to the Father’s essence <note>original: "Property"</note>. In this baptism, through His infusion into the soul, He gives it to the Son within His *love-fire*. The Father’s essence in the fire takes hold of the soul, first with the *law of nature*, His strict righteousness, and the eternal birth of the "fire-ground" <note>the underlying foundation of divine power or nature</note>. Because of this, the hardened <gloss>☞</gloss> compressed soul becomes movable through that infusion of fire. Its hard <gloss>☞</gloss> compression—caused by false, magnetic desire—is broken apart and opened, in the same way that a person strikes a flint to start a fire.

8. Now, the divine light of great love resides in the revealed name **JESUS**, which comes out of **JEHOVAH**, at the *center* of the Father’s fire. When the Father’s fire unlocks the fiery soul, the light of divine love *can* shine into it and introduce the love-*ens* <term>Ens: the essential substance or "being" of a thing</term> into it. As soon as the "wrath-fire" <note>the aspect of God's nature that reacts against sin</note> unlocks the soul, the soul *instantly* receives the love-fire of the Son and enters into it, just as fire glows through iron or as a *tincture* <note>original: "Tincture"; in alchemy, a substance capable of transforming or infusing other matter</note> penetrates metal.

9. In this way, the soul is *given* from the Father to the *Son*, and the *Son gives* it the love-fire—that is, *eternal life*. If the Father’s essence did not also move within the closed-off soul, the soul would remain trapped in its own hardened state <note>original: "Impression"</note> in eternal death, and the light *could not* be revealed within it.

<margin>¶ Commotion, or Contrition.</margin>
10. The <gloss>¶</gloss> "shrill sounding" <note>a sharp, piercing spiritual awakening or vibration</note> and kindling of the Father’s fire is the source of human repentance, where a person trembles before sin. For in the "fire-glance" <note>the flash or spark of divine judgment</note>, the false, compressed vanity of *sins* in the darkness of the soul is made manifest. Then, the shining love of the Son acts as the gentle "love-oil" that unites and balances <note>original: "tempereth"</note> that *contrition* or "shrill sounding" once more.

11. For *the Son is in the Father, and the Father is in the Son*, and they baptize with fire. The Father baptizes with fire, and the Son with light. It happens just as when a fire is struck: a gentle flash of light is revealed from the fire, and thus the burning fire is completely transformed and grows into a flash of light. The Father’s fire, with its *terror* <note>the overwhelming awe or dread of divine justice</note>, consumes the vanity within the soul, and the Son’s *love* heals it again.

This is how the baptism of the *inward* foundation <note>original: "Ground"</note> of a person's soul and spirit is to be understood.

Understand it *in this way*: The soul belongs to the Father’s property, according to his fiery omnipotence. In this baptism, in which the Father co-baptizes, *he gives the soul to the Son in his love-fire.* Understand that the soul, originating from the Father’s fire, has become a "wrath-fire." Through his infusion, he gives this wrath-fire to his fire-burning love. The Father’s property in the fire takes hold of the soul first through the *law of nature*, as if by his strict righteousness of the eternal birth of the "fire-ground." By this, the <margin>impressed</margin> dead soul becomes movable in that same <margin>immersion</margin> of the fire of divine life. Its hard <margin>compression</margin> of false magnetic desire is broken apart and opened, in the same way that a person strikes a spark to start a fire. Thus, a new fire of God is kindled; this <margin>trembling</margin> or "shrill sounding" <note>Boehme uses "Schall" (sound/resonance) to describe a spiritual vibration or awakening that signals a fundamental change in the soul's state.</note> is also the basis of repentance.

Now, when the Father’s fire is stirred and kindled, then the divine light of great, sweet love shines within the opened name of JESUS. This light comes out of the holy name JEHOVAH, in the center of the Father’s fire, and out of the unity of God, like beams of divine grace into the soul. For the soul is unlocked by this glimpse; then, suddenly, the light of love takes hold of that unlocked ground and fills it with the substance of love.

And so the Son—that is, the love of the Father—receives the soul, sanctifies it, and thoroughly penetrates it, just as fire penetrates iron. This is what Christ means when he says: *“Father, these people were yours, and you have given them to me; and I give them eternal life.”* Also: *“This is eternal life: that they truly know you,* <margin>Note.</margin> *Father, that you are the true God, and Jesus Christ, whom you have sent.”* (John 17:3, 6).

The new birth exists in this indwelling and shining light, and God is understood and known in the spirit. Immediately after this follows true faith, which desires nothing except what God desires. Thus, Christ is *the light of the little world*—meaning *man* <note>original: "microcosm" (the human being as a reflection of the universe)</note>—and gives the eternal light-life of God to the soul.

<margin>Substance or essence.</margin>
And so the soul lives in the Father, yet it is governed and sanctified by the Son’s office; its anxious "fire-life" becomes a pure burning of love. However, the Father’s "concussion" or "shrill sounding" is necessary so that the soul’s fire-source may be touched, allowing the soul to find what it truly is. It is thereby brought into continual repentance and humility when the beam of God’s wrath frequently touches it, so that it might *consider its fall* and *never feel too secure*. (For it has a great enemy nearby in its own flesh and blood—namely, Satan’s poison.) This prevents the soul from following its own will as it did before. In this beam of wrath, the soul trembles before sin, and so sin is exposed in the light; then comes a heap of sorrow and lamentation over sin. This precious pattern exists in the inner ground; for wherever the self-will of sin is *shaken* through repentance, the holy anointing oil of love instantly penetrates and heals those wounds. Thus, the Father baptizes with fire for repentance, and the Son with love for *sanctification*. The Holy Spirit administers this office, baptizing with a new life. The entire Holy *Trinity* baptizes according to the divine manifestation. Beyond this manifestation, there is only one Triune God in a single, good <margin>substance or essence</margin> and will. In that state, one cannot say the Father is "wrath" or anything else; he is simply the Triune Good Being. But according to his manifestation—from which souls, angels, and every heavenly and hellish being originated (that is, in the manner of the *Mysterium Magnum* <note>original: "The Great Mystery," a term in Boehme's theosophy referring to the divine chaos or the "womb" from which all creation is manifested</note>)—from this arises his wrath or fire-source, which exists from eternity to eternity.

Note: Now a person can understand baptism according to the *inner ground*—according to the soul and spirit. That is, the Father baptizes with the "concussion" or "shrill sounding" unto repentance with fire. In this fire, the bitter suffering and death of Jesus Christ is impressed into the poor soul; for the wrath-fire that holds the soul captive is overcome and softened with *love*. ## Chap. 3. *How Man is baptized by the Holy Spirit <note>original: "Holy Ghost"</note>.*

<margin>*Victory:*</margin> And the Son baptizes with the holy anointing oil of God's love, and heals the poor, shaken soul again. And the true Comforter, the Holy Spirit, who proceeds through Christ's death, through Christ's resurrection, and through the Father in the Son, he baptizes with a *new life* and gives true faith and understanding, so that we may receive and know this.

The third property of the third principle <note>In Boehme's cosmology, the "Third Principle" refers to the visible, material world created from the higher spiritual realms.</note>, along with the water-baptism, by which the body of the outward world's substance as well as the outward life is baptized, is considered as follows: namely, by the element of the body of Christ, the true Adam-like man <note>original: "Adamical Man"</note>—made from the elements which were created in Adam, meaning the outward world's substance—is *baptized*. For here the Holy Spirit baptizes; he who proceeds from the Father and the Son. His proceeding is the formation of the world; and the world is the spoken, formed Word, and *it is the Spirit of God that formed that spoken Word*.

*He* is to be understood in all *three* principles or worlds, in each world according to its property. First, in the Father's wrath according to the darkness, He is the flame of painfulness. Secondly, in the eternal light, he is the *love-flame* of God. And thirdly, in this world, in the *Spirit of the World* <note>original: "Spiritu Mundi"</note>, he is the shaper and master-craftsman of everything, in everything according to its property. Just as the separator or *archæus* <term>a vital force or "chief workman" believed by early chemists to direct the functions of life</term> of the thing is, from which it arises, so also is the spirit that flowed out of the spoken Word in everything.

And it is *not* to be understood that the spirit of the outward substance itself is called *God*, but it is the spirit that flowed out in the spoken Word of God, which has its foundation in the Word of God.

The spirit that flowed out of the outward, natural, and creaturely life has flown forth out of God's love and wrath, out of *light* and *darkness*—namely, out of the first and second principles, out of the eternal nature, and out of the speaking of the Word. For the eternal Word has *breathed* itself with that spirit into a creaturely, image-like life.

It is the soul of the *outward* world; a life consisting of the four elements. Its power is like a fiery and luminous *constellation*. Whatever the whole outward constellation is in itself in its power, that spirit is the same everywhere alone in itself; yet it is like a hidden constellation that lies in the *temperament* <term>the balanced state of the elements</term>, and yet it unfolds itself in every life and makes itself distinct, according to the property of every life.

For in the year of our Lord <note>original: "A. † O." (Anno), likely referring to 1624</note> 1624, in his jubilee year (the 50th year of his age), he returned, according to the Mystery, into his grave, or his magical and mental principle.

<margin>* Note.</margin>
17. Understand us now correctly here concerning the baptism of *this outward spirit*: The inward holy Spirit of Divine Love kindles the out-flowing spirit and anoints it with Divine *power*. For the humanity of Christ, according to our outward spirit, was anointed by the Holy Ghost; and that same outward spirit of Christ—which in Christ's person, within the elements of the body, ruled in a *human* manner—anoints the inward foundation of the *water* in the covenant of his testament in water-baptism. The anointed power in the water, through the Word of the covenant, anoints the *true man*, who in *Adam* was created out of the *limus* <term>original: "limus," referring to the slime, dust, or clay of the earth</term> of the earth. So too, it anoints the *spiritus mundi* <term>original: "spiritus mundi," the spirit of the world or the vital breath of the universe</term>, namely the true * *astral soul* <term>the "star-soul" or the part of the soul governed by the celestial influences</term>, which shall return and be tested on the Last Day.

<margin>The outward and inward soul.</margin>
18. Now understand us clearly and well; it is very important to us: This anointing of water-baptism is anointed with Christ's suffering, death, and resurrection. It is anointed with Christ's shedding of his blood, with which heavenly blood he changed God's wrath into love and *sprinkled* death within human nature <note>original: "property"</note>. He anointed the earth with it when he *shed forth this blood upon and into it*. Note also: The earth was anointed when Christ gave his anointed life of the outward humanity (which he received from us) back into this *spiritus mundi* <term>spirit of the world</term> at his death. He also anointed that spirit with his anointing in his death—specifically, when his outward mortal soul received from us (which died on the cross and surrendered itself into the *hand of God*, as into his expressed Word) departed from the body into the elements. Also: It is anointed when this outward soul, along with the eternal soul in which the Holy Ghost resided, penetrated through death and hell. And finally, it is anointed when the Holy Ghost in the Word received this dead astral soul from death and brought it through death, by his resurrection, into eternal life, where God's love anointed it with eternal life.

19. This anointing of Christ is understood in water-baptism as being within the covenant of God; for in the humanity of Christ, God anoints the *elements* of the body, together with the *mortal and immortal* soul. He brings Christ with this anointing into death and into the wrath, and through death into eternal life. God has *ordained* this anointing (by which Christ has overcome God's wrath, sin, death, the devil, and hell) through his covenant of the Old Testament in water-baptism, and he offers it now to every person.

20. And so now, if a person desires it and inclines themselves toward it as a human being and *not as an animal*, then the Holy Ghost *baptizes* the inward foundation—namely, his temple, which the Spirit himself possesses—which is the true eternal spirit together with the eternal soul. And the anointing of Christ, from the humanity he received from us, anoints and baptizes *in us* the true first man created in *Adam* out of the *limus* <term>clay or slime</term> of the earth, along with the *mortal soul*. Yet, so that one may understand the basis of this, it is *that soul* which shall *arise and live eternally*.

<margin>* Or, fight, or combat.</margin>
21. This is done through Christ's suffering, death, and resurrection in his bloody * *struggle* <note>original: "conflict"</note>. The *victory* of his death is the hand that baptizes. Note: The true man is baptized unto *life*, and the serpent-like, gross earthly man is baptized with Christ's death and dying. Thus, he shall die and leave all his evil lusts and desires to the death of Christ, so that it may kill them and bring a new will out of the death of Christ, arising from both soul and body.

22. The evil *man*, namely that serpent-monster <note>the corrupted, fallen nature of humanity</note>, is caught by this baptism (where the hand of God, his speaking Word itself, takes and baptizes him) and is buried with Christ in his death and in that *hell* which Christ entered in his dying. Understand this as entering into the darkness of God's wrath, the *abyss of humanity*. And this anointing in the baptism binds and unites *itself* with the true first human from Adam...

It details how Christ's death and resurrection sanctify the elements and provide a path for the human soul to pass through God's wrath into eternal life.</summary>

23. Thus, then, according to this anointing, the true person stands in the anointing of *Christ*, and the Serpent-Monster stands in God's *wrath*; yet, during this lifetime, both dwell in one body, but each within its own principle—that is, in its own property. Concerning this, St. *Paul* says in *Romans 7:20, 25*: "Now if I sin, it is not I, but sin in the evil flesh that does it." Also: *"So then, I now serve God with the mind of the anointed foundation <note>original: "anointed Ground"; Jacob Boehme uses "ground" (German: Grund) to refer to the deepest essence or foundation of a person's soul.</note>, and with the mind of the false flesh, I serve the law of sin."*

<margin>That is, the shell.</margin>
24. And he says further in *Romans 8:1, 28*: *"Now then, there is no condemnation to those who are in Christ Jesus in his anointing, who, according to this purpose of God, are called in the Word, or are thus included in the calling in the anointing."* By this, he means the truly anointed person, who during this lifetime remains hidden in the <margin>shell</margin> scales of the earthly body, like fine gold in a rough stone; yet, according to the anointing, that person dwells in *Heaven*. As St. *Paul* also says in *Philippians 3:20*: *"Our conversation <note>original: "Conversation"; in this context, it refers to citizenship or way of life.</note> is in Heaven."* Also, in *Romans 6:15* and *Galatians 2:17*: *"Shall we then, who belong to Christ, still be sinners? Far be it from us."* Here he means the anointed foundation, and not the bestial monster of earthliness, full of evil inclinations, which stands in the wrath of God and condemnation. This monster shall not inherit the Kingdom of God, yet in this lifetime, it clings to the truly anointed person.

25. The anointed foundation is the Christian, not the outward, gross beast. It is the anointing which daily breaks the head of the monster—the serpent—namely, the evil earthly will where the struggle in man exists. In this struggle, one property wills evil and the other good; that which overcomes drives the person to act. *Therefore, a person's works shall and must be judged, and every one shall be gathered into its barn <note>A reference to the parable of the wheat and the weeds in Matthew 13:30; here, "barn" signifies the final destination of one's deeds.</note>; that which is done in the power of the anointing enters into the Kingdom of God, and that which is done in the power of the monster—the serpent—enters into damnation, into the darkness of wrath and death.*

# The Fourth Chapter.

### Of the outward *Water-Baptism* by human hands: *Who is worthy to perform such Baptism? And what baptized infant worthily receives this Baptism; how it goes with the unworthy hand, as also with the unworthy baptized infant.*

->*In this time, highly necessary to be considered.*<-

<image-desc>A large decorative drop cap letter 'W' set within an ornate square frame with floral and geometric engravings.</image-desc>
1. WHEN God established the testament of his holy Covenant of Grace in Paradise out of types and sacrifices, and intended to transform circumcision into water baptism, he brought forth a *branch* out of his covenant in a human manifestation. He began water baptism through this; as is clearly seen in *John* the Baptist, who was announced by an angelic message or embassy, and who was, moreover, from the lineage of the high priests.

2. His incarnation, or becoming man, did not come from the will of the flesh; for his father *Zechariah* and mother *Elizabeth* were elderly people, advanced in years, who—

He then begins a discussion on the origins and spiritual significance of water baptism, starting with John the Baptist.</summary>

# Concerning the outward Water-Baptism by Man's Hand. Chapter 4.

...were clearly dead in the fleshly seed <note>original: "Sperm or Seed"</note>; where the ability of man was clearly gone. The seed of <term>Zechariah</term> <note>original: "Zachary"</note> and <term>Elisabeth</term> was raised up through the *moving* of the <term>Holy Spirit</term> <note>original: "Holy Ghost"</note>, out of the Paradisiacal <note>original: "Paradifical"</note> Grace-Covenant, in their biological properties which had by then quite vanished.

<margin>* The Seed.</margin>
3. *Indeed*, he came out of the human ground, but not out of human *ability*; for the anointing in the Covenant awakened it, so that their seed—beyond the course and power of nature's own ability—was unlocked. This <term>Holy Spirit</term> raised up a seed out of the human biological seed, and for 그 purpose chose it ᵃ in its first beginning.

4. But the anointing of *John* occurred during <term>Mary’s greeting</term> <note>original: "Mary's Salute," referring to the Visitation</note>, when she came to visit the elderly *Elisabeth*. The Divine anointing was stirred in Mary through *Christ's Incarnation* (his becoming man). When Mary, full of this anointing, greeted Elisabeth, the *Incarnation* of *Christ* spread through the anointing of Mary's greeting into *John* in the mother's womb. This happened not only in *John*, but also in his mother *Elisabeth*, so that she was full of this anointing; thus, both mothers prophesied in the spirit of this anointing.

5. And this is the <term>Baptism of John</term>: he was anointed with the *Incarnation* of *Christ*, through *Christ* himself, and received the Baptism of the <term>Holy Spirit</term> from the Covenant while in his mother’s womb. This was so that he could be a forerunner and proclaimer, *declaring that the time of the anointing and the fulfilling of God's Covenant was at hand*. It showed that God has introduced his Covenant of the anointing of Grace into humanity, and that the Covenant has become a man. From this point forward, God will pour out his anointing through the humanity of Christ, using a physical medium <note>original: "elementary Medium"</note> that no longer consists of fire—as in the Old Testament—but in the love and gentleness of *water*. Thus, the *Time of Grace is at hand*, in which God has placed his anointing into humanity.

6. We see then that God began no new Covenant there, but only a new practice <note>original: "Ordinance"</note>; for *John* allowed himself to be circumcised, as did *Christ*. *John* took his power and calling from the Covenant of Circumcision and from the sacrifices of fire; then, by the command of God, he brought them into the water-baptism. This was to signify that, from then on, sin should be drowned by the death of *Christ* in his love and gentleness, and *no longer burn in the fire, as was done by Israel in the symbolic types* <note>original: "in the Type"</note>.

<margin>* Namely, John the Baptist.</margin>
7. Moreover, we see from *John* that he did not yet baptize for the forgiveness of sins, but with *repentance*. This means he baptized with the spirit of anointing toward repentance, which echoes through the hearts of men and prepares the way for the Spirit of Christ. Christ's Spirit unlocks the doors of men's hearts and souls so *that after* ᵇ *him, the King of Glory might enter through those opened gates*. Regarding this, *David* says: *Open the gates wide for the King of Glory; that the King of Glory, namely Christ, may enter in (Psalm 24:7, 9).* And as *John* witnesses: *He baptized with water for repentance and forgiveness of sins, yet he is not Christ; but after him comes he who has the fan in his hand, who will baptize with the fire of the Spirit (Luke 3:16, 17).*

8. We also see in *John* that he had to be the son of a priest who was familiar with circumcision and sacrifices. He had to emerge from the Law of the Covenant and be circumcised himself, putting on the Covenant, so that he could—with the spirit of the Covenant and of circumcision—begin the water-baptism, which is the *practice of grace and forgiveness*. For sin was now to be destroyed no longer by fire, but by love, which God manifested in the Covenant through Christ. Sin was to be drowned and transformed by God's gentleness.

<margin>* The Forgiveness <note>original: "Absolution"</note> of Sins.</margin>
9. Therefore, God also ordained this method of water-baptism for the destruction of sins, to signify that sin should be *drowned* in the blood of Christ—in his love and grace. From *now on*, man should have an open gate of grace to God through love and gentleness; so that now, with repentant sorrow for sins and the ᶜ abandoning of sins, he may enter through this gate into grace.

### Chapter 4. Of the Outward Water-Baptism by Man's Hand.

<margin>
d Or, Power.
</margin>

10. And we see here in *John*—the beginner of water-baptism—what kind of man is worthy to baptize with this new covenant of grace: namely, one who has also been baptized with this grace beforehand. This was true of *John*, who was baptized by Christ even in his mother's womb. Flesh and blood *without* this spiritual anointing cannot baptize; for this power does not reside in the ^d authority of man, but in Christ's ^d authority.

<margin>
Note.
</margin>

11. A *Christian*, in whom the anointing of Christ resides, baptizes with that same anointing. For the Holy Trinity baptizes through the grace-covenant of the anointing, which is joined with Christ's incarnation (becoming man), his suffering, death, and victory. Therefore, if anyone wishes to baptize, they must not only baptize with their hand and the water-baptism, but also with the *faith* of that spiritual anointing.

<margin>
e Or, Thing.
</margin>

12. An unfaithful or unbelieving baptizer does no more in this high work of baptism than the baptismal font (the stone ^e basin) does, which merely holds the water. For though he sprinkles or pours water and uses the words of Christ, he achieves nothing through them. He is spiritually silent (or dead) in the process, unless the covenant of Christ itself works and baptizes. He is merely a *medium* or means—like an inanimate ^e substance—that does not itself work within this covenant, but only performs the outward action; and it is in that action that God works, out of respect for his own covenant.

<margin>
f Or, ineffectual.
g Absents or withdraws itself.
• Therefore all baptized infants ought to be communicants. <note>The author suggests that if infants are holy enough for baptism, they are also eligible for Holy Communion.</note>
</margin>

13. This is not to be understood as if the work performed by an unworthy hand were therefore wholly ^f ineffectual. No; the covenant of God does not ^g withdraw itself because the hand performing it is unworthy, as that hand is only a medium or means. For faithful parents, who live in the anointing of this covenant and have "put on" the covenant, possess that anointing in their "seed" (their offspring). They produce children out of the very nature of their own baptized bodies and souls. Now, if the parents are baptized in body and soul and have put on the anointing of Christ, why then would the <term>Ens</term> <note>original: "Ens"; the essential spiritual substance or being</note> of their children's bodies not be holy as well? If the parents are temples of the Holy Ghost (who dwells in them) and eat *Christ's flesh* and drink his blood so that Christ is in them and they are in Christ—as Christ says in *John* 6:56—why then should the fruit of their bodies not also be holy? For Christ says in *Matthew* 7:18, "*A good tree cannot bring forth bad fruit, and a bad tree cannot bring forth good fruit.*" If the eye of the spirit is light, then the whole body is light; if the leaven is holy, then the whole lump of dough is holy (*Matthew* 6; *Romans* 11).

14. *John* was baptized in his mother's womb through the Spirit of Christ when he heard *Mary's* voice, as was his mother *Elizabeth*. We see clearly how it happened: as *Elizabeth* heard the spirit of *Mary*, the Holy Ghost moved in her and in her "fruit" (unborn child) alike. They both received the baptism of Christ from his humanity; the mother and the son together. Why then should this not also happen today among holy parents in whom the anointing dwells? For *as the tree is, so is its fruit*. However, the covenant of baptism exists so that every person, as they develop their own particular life and will—like a specific branch on a tree—should personally "put on" the covenant of Christ through the outward means ordained for that purpose.

<margin>
h Pathen.
i Transfer, or deliver over.
</margin>

15. This does not mean that a child of honest, "anointed" parents who has attained life is excluded from the anointing of Christ if it dies before baptism. It has indeed "put on" the anointing of its parents, for it exists out of their substance—out of the substance of their baptized souls and bodies. If the child lives, it only needs to enter into the image of the *visible* covenant as a life of its own, and with its own will give itself up to that which it has inherited from its parents. But since a child *cannot understand this*, the parents do it through *their* faith. Everyone called to that work—namely the ^h witnesses, or ^h godparents—uses their faithful desire and prayer to ^i recommend the child to the covenant of Christ. They present the child within the covenant of Christ to the Holy Trinity and desire that the covenant be ^i applied to this child.

<summary>This page explores the spiritual mechanics of baptism, arguing that the ritual's power comes from Christ's authority rather than the person performing it. It emphasizes that children of "anointed" or holy parents inherit a measure of grace from birth, though they still require the outward ritual to formally enter the visible covenant of faith.</summary>

# Of Outward Water-Baptism by Human Hands. Chapter 4

16. All these—both the parents and the bystanders, *namely*, the faithful baptizer and witnesses—work with their faith within the nature of the child. They reach out to the child with their faith and the covenant of Christ. For the desire of their faith takes the child’s will (which is currently *without* understanding) into their own faith’s desire. In this way, they carry the child’s will within their own will, through their anointing into the covenant of Christ—that is, before the Holy Trinity.

17. When the baptizer sprinkles or pours the water upon the child, his faith is present within the water and fastens itself to the *words of Christ*, who says in *Matthew* 28:19: *Go hence into all the world, baptizing all nations in the name of the Father, Son, and Holy Ghost*. Upon Christ’s command, they baptize people; the baptizer baptizes with his hand and with faith, and the parents, together with the witnesses, baptize with their faith’s desire and their anointed *will*. They infuse this will into Christ’s covenant, and Christ infuses himself into it with his blood, death, and victory—that is, with the victory of his death. He kindles the faith's <term>Ens</term> <note>original: "Ens"; a philosophical and theological term referring to the fundamental essence, being, or "spiritual seed" of a thing.</note> of the child with his love-fire.

<margin>* Hatcher, breeder, or ember.</margin>
18. Thus, the grain of mustard seed of the love-fire sows itself into the <term>Ens</term> of the child’s soul and body as a glimmering * Mother of Divine Love. This "Mother" <note>Boehme uses "Mother" here to mean a source or nurturing origin.</note> is later more fully kindled through faith, repentance, and prayer once the child gains understanding of its *own*. It then becomes a high, shining light. When the "mouth of faith" later *eats Christ’s flesh and drinks his blood* <note>A reference to the Eucharist or Holy Communion.</note>, then this holy "Mother Love-Fire" receives the holy oil to fuel the burning of its life.

<margin>Note.</margin>
19. Through baptism, the humanity of Christ is implanted according to the holy love-water—that is, the *water of eternal life*—in which the holy fire may burn. Through the Lord's Supper, one participates in the holy <term>tincture</term> <note>original: "tincture"; a spiritual quality or vital force that transforms or "colors" the soul with divine properties.</note> in the blood and flesh of Christ. This is the true, burning love-fire, a spiritual anointing oil coming out of the divine fire and light, which the "water of love" (the baptismal covenant) kindles. Even if a child is born of *holy* parents and is clearly within this covenant while in the mother’s womb, the child must still personally put on this covenant in its own independent person and its own life’s will. This is because sin and uncleanness are propagated and inherited within the flesh; therefore, the child must personally put on this covenant. The child must, by the covenant of grace, personally break the *head of the serpent* <note>A traditional reference to overcoming original sin or the devil, based on Genesis 3:15.</note> in the flesh. Therefore, the child must personally put on Christ and his victory. Since Christ now offers himself to the child, the child must receive him in its own person with its own will, and give its *own* will up to him.

<margin>l Text: *Auf*, "upon."</margin>
20. For baptism is nothing other than a marriage or contract with God in <note>original: "l"; likely a cross-reference marker.</note> Christ’s blood and death. In this contract, Christ binds himself to man with his victory and resurrection, and places man *within* them. In baptism, man gives up his "Adam-like" <note>original: "Adamical"; referring to the fallen nature inherited from Adam.</note> contrary will to the *death of Christ*. He desires to die to his own will in Christ’s death and to rise again through Christ’s resurrection—out of Christ’s death, with and in Christ—to a *new will*, and to live and will with Christ. For through baptism, by Christ’s victory, we are planted anew in the *Word of God*. Man is the "spoken-out" <note>original: "outspoken"; meaning the expressed or manifested image of God's creative Word.</note> imaged Word of God, which in *Adam* brought its will away from God's speaking and into its own private will and speaking, thereby becoming treacherous to the *Word of God*. With baptism, this "imaged word" promises and incorporates itself again into the eternal speaking of God, so that it will speak and will according to God—namely, God’s *righteousness and truth*.

<margin>m In or into.</margin>
21. Baptism is an oath which man swears <note>original: "m"; likely a cross-reference marker.</note> to God, where he renounces the Devil and his kingdom and gives himself up to God as his own property—namely, to be a temple of God. Although a child does not understand this, the baptizer, parents, and witnesses should understand it and introduce their faith into the child’s will. Thus, with their will introduced into the child’s will, they together plunge or sink...

<summary>This page explains that baptism is a spiritual contract and "marriage" with God, where the faith of parents and witnesses acts on behalf of the infant to implant a divine "mustard seed" of grace. It describes baptism as the death of the fallen "Adam-like" will and a rebirth into the "Word of God."</summary>

# Chap. 4. Of the outward Water-Baptism by Man's Hand.

<margin>Lack of understanding, or ignorance.</margin>
<margin>Thus,</margin>
They commit themselves with this oath into God’s covenant through the *Word* of *Christ* upon his command in water baptism. They grasp the command of *Christ* within themselves—that is, in their faith—and so, in their *understanding*, enter into the covenant alongside the child’s lack of understanding. In the place of the child, and with the child’s will held within their own will, they make such a promise to God. For this the *parents* may, and especially ought to do, seeing the child has sprung out of their life and substance like a branch from a tree trunk; thus, they also have the power to include the will of the child within the will of their faith, and with the child's will, to give it up and bind or unite it to God.

22. Moreover, the *baptizer* has this in his power, who by the command of *Christ* stands there in *Christ's* place. He brings the command of *Christ* in his mouth and baptizes with *his hand* upon the command of *Christ*. Such a person should be the *anointed* of *Christ* and enter into that work *through the door of Christ* <note>original: "through the Door of Christ"; a reference to John 10:7–9, implying the baptizer must be a true believer.</note>. Otherwise, he is but as a piece of wood or a clod of earth, standing by as an earthly *medium*; he himself does *not* baptize along with his faith, but is only an outward instrument of the covenant, like the axe with which the carpenter chops. Indeed, he is not *altogether* like the axe that cuts, but like the *hand* that holds the axe. He neither cuts nor works together with the Spirit, but is only the outward instrument and performs only an outward act. He does not reach the covenant, but only the water, and he carries a *dead word* in his life; but the *office* of *Christ* is in the command.

23. The *living Word* in the covenant which baptizes there does not originate from the power of a wicked mouth, but from the *command* in the covenant. The wicked mouth brings the outward *literal word* as a minister of it, but the covenant brings the *living Word* in *power*. If the parents and witnesses are faithful, they offer the child with their faith to the covenant, and the wicked baptizer with his mouth and hand is but an instrument for it, in the same way that a clock strikes and sounds but has no life, yet gives notice and understanding to the *living* of what it means. Or, it is like a wicked man who, in a show of holiness, names and acknowledges the holy name of God before a *holy person*; instantly, the holy name of God is thereby stirred and becomes active in the *heart* of the holy man who hears it, even though the hypocrite in his own mind *neither* understands it *nor* finds it. This stirring of the good *heart* does not proceed from the wicked mouth and enter into the holy heart, but it proceeds from the *name of God*.

<margin>Note.</margin>
24. Thus, the holy name also baptizes through the *wicked* baptizer. It is not the evil mouth that does it, but he must be an instrument that pronounces the holy name, which works not because of his pronouncing it, but from the *Name* and covenant itself, through the faithful parents' and witnesses' introduction of their faith. For the covenant is *itself* a *faith* [or believing]—that is, God's *Word* and *mouth*. The covenant baptizes everyone who gives themselves up into it, whether worthily or unworthily, and whether the faith of the baptizer and of the parents and witnesses is there or not; but with a great difference, as the Scripture says: *With the holy you are holy, and with the perverse you are perverse* (Psalm 18:25–26). Also, *As the people are, so is the God they have.* And as St. *Paul* says of the Lord's Supper: *Therefore they received it to judgment, because they do not discern the Lord's body* (1 Corinthians 11:29).

<margin>Nurture, or chastisement.</margin>
25. For where God's *love* is present, his *wrath* is also present. Where light is, there is also fire. The <term>ens</term> <note>original: "Ens"; a philosophical/theological term referring to the essence or spiritual substance of a thing.</note> of faith presses only through the fire and out into the light. The covenant stands firm; the child is baptized with the covenant, and the covenant receives it, even if there were only a wicked baptizer and witnesses without faith. But as the mouth is, such is also the food in the mouth, as the Lord says through the prophet: *Why does the wicked take my covenant into his mouth and hate to be reformed?* (Psalm 50:16–17). People should not misuse the name of *God*; for the *Lord will* nurture or *chastise*—

<summary>This page explains that the validity of baptism rests on God's covenant and the faith of the parents rather than the moral character of the baptizer. The baptizer is described as a mere instrument, like an axe or a clock, while the "living Word" within the covenant performs the actual spiritual transformation.</summary>
<keywords>Baptism, Covenant, faith of parents, unworthy ministers, Word of God, spiritual instruments, Psalm 18, St. Paul, sacraments, Jacob Boehme</keywords>
