# *Of the outward Water-Baptism by Man's Hand.* Chapter 4.

25. He will not leave him unpunished who misuses it, (Deuteronomy 5:11). He will not cast pearls before swine (Matthew 7:6). To God, the wicked man who draws near to His covenant is like a scent <note>original: "Savour"</note> that leads to the condemnation of death; but to the holy person, He is a scent that leads to life (2 Corinthians 2:15–16).

26. What else can happen if there are evil parents without faith, except that they also beget wicked children? For as the tree <note>original: "Stock"</note> is, so also is the fruit. Now, if they do not convert and, through true, earnest repentance and prayer, *incorporate* their offspring into Christ and send them with faith to this covenant—but instead *invite* such wicked witnesses or <term>godparents</term> <note>original: "Gossips"</note> who lack faith—and if there is also a wicked baptizer, who shall perform the baptism here? Shall the love of God in the Covenant of Grace perform the baptism? Might it not be as Saint Paul says of the Lord's Supper: *that the wicked receive it unto judgment?* If a man makes a mockery of the covenant, how will God’s glory appear among the scoffers? There it is rightly said: *With the holy you are holy, and with the perverse you are perverse.* If the <margin>¶ Or false.</margin> seed is bad, even if a man casts it into good ground, bad fruit still grows from it; for it draws from the good ground an <note>original: "Ens" (a philosophical term for the internal essence or being of a thing)</note> of its own *likeness* to itself.

27. How, then, can things go well when a child springs from parents who are entirely wicked, and when only wicked witnesses are called—people who stand there only for status and pride, or for human favor? They are called for such reasons even though there is no faith or good will, much less an earnest prayer. Instead, an *earthly Lucifer* <note>In this context, a person filled with demonic pride.</note> stands before the covenant of Christ, and the baptizer is also a spiritually dead person. Who then awakens the holy covenant here? As the faith is that moves or stirs the covenant, such is also the *manifestation* of the covenant, and so is the baptism.

28. Christ says, *Suffer little children to come unto me, for of such is the kingdom of God* (Matthew 10:14; 19:14), but he means children, not wolves and beasts. He bids them to come to him, but not to bring them to him in the devil’s pride and status, accompanied by pompous, high-minded, false, and unfaithful people who do nothing but despise the humility of Christ and scorn love. It must be in *earnest* if a man intends to enter through the wrath of God into His *love*.

29. *Reason says this:* What does it matter to the child who is born of *wicked* parents and is brought by evil people to the covenant of Christ? 
*Answer:* Yes, indeed; what does it matter to God, who does not desire the death of a sinner, that wicked parents beget wicked children, and that a man does nothing but scorn His covenant of grace? Shall He therefore cast pearls before swine? The parents indeed know very well that God says *He will punish the sins of the parents on the children unto the third and fourth generation* (Deuteronomy 5:9). Shall He then pour His love into their wicked *wills*, when they do not actually *desire* that love? There is no earnestness there, but merely the performance of a *custom*. They do it only with a hypocritical show without sincerity, and furthermore, they use people for the ceremony who only scorn the *simplicity* of Christ with their pride.

30. To be familiar with the sacraments <note>original: "Testaments"</note> and covenant of Christ, and to make use of them, requires great earnestness—not only in *show* but in *power*. For the covenant of God in Christ is made through His blood and death. It is intended so that whoever wishes to partake of this covenant and these sacraments should *convert with their will*, enter into repentance, and die to their inherited false lusts within the covenant through Christ’s death, being *born again* out of the covenant of these sacraments.

31. For baptism consists not *alone* in water, but in the Word of God and in faith. The water is only a *medium* in which the Word of God and faith take hold and work; without the Word of God and faith, there is *no* baptism. The faith of man must take hold of the promised Word, and in the water these two—namely, <margin>¶ Or Essence.</margin> faith and the Word of God—bring themselves into one *substance*. That spiritual *substance* is the baptism, which is understood to be under the water. Now if there is no faith—

# Chap. 4. Of the outward Water-Baptism by Man’s Hand.

...at this work, then the Word is without *human* substance, existing only in itself according to and within the Covenant. This Word baptizes man according to the man’s nature <note>original: "Property"</note>, but faith in grace takes hold of the grace in the Covenant and Word, and *brings itself* with the Covenant *into* the water; and so then the Word of God, faith, and the water *baptize* together.

<margin>* Text: Entrance <note>original: "Eing." (German "Eingang")</note></margin>
32. For outward, physical <note>original: "elementary"</note> water is *not* the basis of baptism, but rather the *spiritual* water, which is united and tied with the Word in the Covenant and with faith. For the *Word* pours itself forth as a water-source of life in great meekness and love, and *faith* takes hold of this promised Word of grace in the Covenant. This grace in the spiritual water joins itself with the physical water, in the same way that the invisible world made itself visible through the substance of this world—namely, through the elements. And just as the *invisible* Word of God works through the *visible*, and just as the visible substance of the elements shall return to the invisible, so also in the baptismal Covenant, the invisible element—namely, the *heavenly* substance—unites itself with the visible elements of the *human* body. This is the substance of eternity uniting with the substance of time; the eternally speaking Word of Divine Love uniting with the expressed <margin>* Or formed.</margin> * imaged Word of humanity.

33. For the pure element—belonging to the holy spiritual world from which the four physical elements originated—is what baptizes *through* the four elements of the human body. The true man created in *Adam*, who *remains* <note>original: "sticketh"</note> within the coarse husk of the four elements, is baptized for eternal life. For the pure element *soaks* or *infuses* itself again into the lost <note>original: "vanished"</note> image of man. This image was originally made of the pure element but was lost in *Adam*; and to that end, God has <margin>* Or instituted.</margin> * ordained his Covenant in water-baptism. Now, *faith* and *repentance* are necessary for this reception. Repentance is an unlocking or stirring of the hidden, closed-off parts of man, by which the inward spiritual *desire*—namely, the spiritual mouth for such reception—is opened; and faith is the opened mouth that takes in the holy element.

34. And although a child *without* understanding cannot do this, those who baptize should do it through their faith, along with the *others who are present* at the baptism. Their faith must include itself within the child’s will, for the child does *not yet* have a will toward either good or evil. Their faith includes itself in the child’s *life*—namely, in soul and spirit. This is possible because all *souls* originate from One, and so in their *center* they are one single foundation <note>original: "Ground"</note>—namely, the Word of God from which the soul originated and where they *all* stand together in that foundation. This inclusion within [the child] is nothing more than introducing their *will of love* into the child. And although a man cannot do that by his *own power* and might, if the will of man joins itself to God’s Word and promise and takes hold of the *promised grace*—along with the command that we should perform this *act*—then the *possibility* is there. For the promised Word gives and works the ability within the human will and provides the *deed*. God’s will takes the human will that is resigned to him and performs it through his power *along with* the human will.

35. Therefore, I say it is a dangerous thing to baptize children *without* the faith of the parents, of those who baptize, and of the others present for the work. The Scripture says (Hebrews 11:6), "*Without faith it is impossible to please God*." But this faith is not just a history or knowledge where a man merely *assents* to it and believes that it is God’s work. No; it is an earnest, desiring *co-working*, a *pressing into* the promised grace, an earnest consideration of our inherited sin and of the great seriousness of God, and how he—through this *Covenant of Grace*—receives us again as children and pours his grace into us through *this work*.

<margin>* Turning toward God.</margin>
36. Those who are *present* should, with great humility and * conversion to God and with earnest prayer, apply themselves to this Covenant and consider well what they are doing there—

<summary>This page explains that baptism is a spiritual union of the heavenly element with physical water, requiring the active faith of the participants to effectively restore the divine image in the baptized, especially in the case of infants.</summary>

# Of the outward Water-Baptism by Man's Hand. Chap. 4.

36. As they intend to do, for they stand even before the Covenant of the Holy Trinity, before God’s open face, and must deal with God and man. They should deeply impress upon themselves the bitter sufferings and death of Jesus Christ, into which a child is baptized and of which they are co-working witnesses according to the faith. They should not stand before this Covenant like a *prostitute before a mirror*, with proud hearts, as if this were a worldly honor that a man should use for his own vanity.
<margin>r Or, Assistance.</margin>
Such people, who have no understanding and faith toward this act and come to it only with proud hearts, are not ^r beneficial to this Covenant, but a hindrance. They hinder others, who stare at the pride and finery <note>original: "bravery"</note> and, in doing so, forget the *solemnity*.

37. And although baptism may be performed without such persons—through the parents' and the baptizer’s sincerity and prayer—the *Christian Church* has nevertheless ordained that living *witnesses* should be present to support this solemnity with their prayer. This was well ordained, but it has come to such misuse that it would often be better if such children of infidelity <note>meaning: unbelieving people</note> were not present; for the devil has no place in this work. Now, if the devil has the chief dominion in a man, of what use is such a man in this matter? As mentioned before, the baptismal font or basin and the unfaithful onlooker are worth the same—except that the *proud* man is a hindrance to others.

<margin>z Or, Significance.</margin>
38. Baptism is a *substantial* work, not a mere sign or ^z symbol of the Testament of Christ. The *Holy Spirit* baptizes the soul and the spirit with Christ’s blood and death and with his victory; and the holy element of the spiritual water baptizes the *body* of the four elements for the resurrection of the dead. It baptizes the *Serpent’s essence* <term>Serpent’s Ens</term> <note>original: "Serpent's Ens"; refers to the "being" or "essence" of sin and the devil's influence inherited by humanity.</note> and the awakened, introduced poison, so that it may die.

<margin>Note. * Text. Isa. Note.</margin>
39. It is a substantial, working infusion of the Covenant of God; therefore, if the infant being baptized is to worthily receive it, there must be sincerity. A *Christian*—one who is a Christian in Christ, in whom Christ works, lives, and dwells—should be the one to baptize. For he must enter into this *sheepfold* through the *door* of Christ, namely through Christ’s Spirit, and not climb up elsewhere; otherwise, he is a *thief* and a *murderer* <note>a reference to John 10:1</note> and comes only to rob and steal the honor of Christ and deceive people. He should be a true *shepherd* and not a *hireling* <note>someone who works only for pay without caring for the "flock."</note>. Here, babbling and making a show are of no value; there must be sincerity, for it is a serious matter with God. All *bickering* and disputation about this work is a useless and even hurtful thing; people should approach it with sincerity, follow the command of Christ, and believe what Christ has said.

<margin>* Note.</margin>
40. Nothing more belongs to this work but faith and water, and earnest prayer in true repentance, with a will that seeks to *help* release another from death, the devil, and hell, and to help bring them with oneself into the Kingdom of God. That is the whole process that belongs here. Everyone who is a *true Christian in Christ* is worthy to be a witness and present at this work; but he who is not such a person is unworthy, whether he be the *baptizer* or a *witness*—one is as bad as the other. There is no partiality <note>original: "respect of persons"</note> with God. *In Christ we are ONE; he is the trunk <note>original: "stock"</note>, and we are the branches.* He performs his work through his fellow members, just as the trunk of the tree produces its fruit through its twigs and branches. The trunk uses no foreign tree for its twigs; likewise, Christ only uses *his members* for the work of producing his fruit.

->END OF THE FIRST LITTLE BOOK CONCERNING THE HOLY BAPTISM.<-

<header>Chap. I.</header>

# The First Chapter.

## On the Foundation of the Old Testament; How this Testament was Clearly Represented by the Types among the Jews.

1. <margin>a Smothering.</margin><margin>b Passed over.</margin> When God sent *Moses* to *Pharaoh* and commanded him to let the Children of *Israel* go into the wilderness and offer sacrifices to Him, and *Pharaoh* would not do it, then God sent great plagues and punishments upon him. Lastly, he sent the ^a^ destroying angel, who slew all the firstborn in *Egypt*. There, He commanded *Israel* to observe the *Passover*, or to slaughter and eat the *Paschal Lamb*—namely, a *lamb of one year old*—and to sprinkle the *doors and upper posts with its blood, so that the deadly anger should ^b^ pass over and kill no one in that house* (Exodus 12:12).

2. This was a *type* <note>original: "Type" — In theology, a "type" is a person, event, or object in the Old Testament seen as a symbolic precursor to something in the New Testament.</note> of the New Testament, [showing] how the posts and doors of our *life* should be sprinkled with the blood of the Lamb, *Christ*, so that God’s anger in soul and body might not swallow us up into His wrath. And just as they had to eat that lamb *wholly* or *entirely, leaving nothing behind*, so would the Lamb, *Christ*, give himself in his testament *wholly* as food for his Christian followers, undivided. He would sprinkle the posts of our life with his blood of *love*, so that the destroying angel in God’s anger might not take hold of us and slay us.

3. <margin>c Dough.</margin> We also have a symbol or likeness of this in the *unleavened cakes* which they were required to *bake and eat*. This [showed] that through this figure of the Paschal Lamb, which signified *Christ*, they should be a *new and sweet* ^c^ *lump* <note>original: "Lump" — refers to a batch of dough; see 1 Corinthians 5:7.</note> when they ate the true Paschal ^c^ *dough*, the Lamb, *Christ*, in his testament. All of this was a figure of the New Regeneration [signifying] how the same should be born through the *true Paschal Lamb, Christ* (1 Corinthians 5:7), and how the New Birth would eat the sweet food of Divine Grace.

4. <margin>d Marked or anointed.</margin> This is a powerful figure of the terrible Fall in *Adam*, and then of the New Birth or Regeneration in *Christ*. For in *Adam*, the *first birth*—namely, the first angelic life—was slain by God’s anger; but by the Covenant of Grace in *Christ*, that same life was brought back again and spoken [or breathed] into *Adam* and *Eve*. Thus, the Spirit of God signifies by this figure of *Moses* in *Egypt* how that same "inspoken" grace should be fulfilled with heavenly and divine *substance* <note>original: "Ens" — Latin for "being" or "essence," a key term in Böhme’s philosophy.</note>. It also shows how man should be ^d^ marked and sprinkled by that mark—namely, by the blood of the Lamb of God—and how God would give him the sweet substance of His sweet love for food. By this, the natural, foolish "fire-life" <note>In Böhme’s thought, the "fire-life" is the raw, wrathful nature of the soul before it is transformed by the light of God's love.</note> should be quickened again and attain a divine *substance* in its life’s essence, thereby being transmuted and changed back into the *angelic image*.

# Chapter 1. Showing how this Testament was in the Type.

...Fire of God's anger with the fire of love, and be offered to God. As this was then done in the humanity of Christ—when he sacrificed our humanity to the anger of God, yet introduced it with his *love* through death into *life*—just as a clear light springs up out of fire, or as a new life emerges from the dying of the fire, which consists in power and love.

<margin>Note.</margin>
11. But Moses *burned the heifer with fire—along with its hide, flesh, and dung—outside the camp*, and only sprinkled the blood of the heifer upon the horns of the altar and kindled the fat. This signifies that the gross, bestial body of our flesh, with its skin and bones, shall not come upon God's altar and inherit the Kingdom of God; instead, it shall be consumed with the essential fire of the earth, *outside the holy fire of God*. Just as Moses had to burn the heifer outside the camp <note>original: "host"—referring to the encampment of the Israelites</note>, so also must the gross, bestial man be burned up outside the City of God—namely, in its own principle, by that same natural fire, as we see happen before our eyes. But this earthly man's *blood*, in which the astral soul <note>the soul influenced by the stars or celestial bodies</note> lives, should be sprinkled upon the horns of the *altar*. This signifies the true man created in Adam out of the *limus* <note>the slime or clay of the earth</note> with the right *astrum* <note>celestial essence</note>, whose blood or power shall return at the *Last Day*. That same blood was in Christ's humanity, along with the inclusion of heavenly blood, sprinkled upon the horns of the altar during his suffering and death on the tree of the cross. This serves as a sign that *our blood*, in a truly human manner, has come upon God's altar through Christ, and that God has marked us in Christ upon the eternal *heavenly altar*.

12. But the fact that the rest of the blood had to be poured at the foot of the altar signifies that our human blood—in which our *outward* human life consists and which dies here—is poured out at the *foot* of the altar at death. That is, it is released into the [four] elements and reserved for the restoration of the first true man. The right life shall be kept at the foot of the altar—that is, in its own principle, as in the *Mysterio magno* <note>the Great Mystery</note> and the *Spiritu Mundi* <note>the Spirit of the World</note>—until God shall purge this altar of the four elements. Then He will bring forth again the same pure virtue and power of the blood, together with the elements, and bring them into the "temperature" <note>a state of perfect balance</note>; and so the human blood shall again return to the *soul*, according to the property of the spiritual world.

13. For this reason, Moses and Aaron had to pour out the heifer's blood at the foot of the altar as a symbolic figure. God was *not* concerned with the blood of beasts; rather, he established a symbol of man's restoration. He signified through it that we humans, according to the outward, gross, earthly man, were like such beasts, and that this gross, bestial property had swallowed up the true man within itself. Thus, he signifies how he would use his power to bring back and *newly* generate that same "inward devoured ground" <note>the original, pure spiritual essence of humanity that was lost or "swallowed" by the fall</note>. And as the power and virtue of our *mumia* <note>the vital essence or "balsam" of the body</note>—the oily property—shall be kindled again through the fire of God (just as Moses kindled the fat), so shall the power of the inward ground be kindled with the divine fire even *during this life*, and burn upon God's altar. This should be done in *us* through the *unction* <note>anointing</note> of the Spirit of God. Even as Moses kindled the fat, so should the Spirit of Christ kindle our inward ground, even in this lifetime. When this is done, the "heifer"—the bestial man—should be slain; that is, he should be daily *mortified* <note>put to death or disciplined</note>, and with his will and bestial desires be cast out from the camp of God. For he is but earth and a beast, *and not fit for the Kingdom of Heaven (John 6)*.

14. But the *ram* now signifies the true, anointed man in the humanity of Christ, as well as our own inward ground, which becomes living again through Christ's anointing in us. As God, through Aaron's sons (the *high priests*), would lay the hand of his anger upon it and skin it so that our human will might be slain, so shall the blood of this ram—the true humanity—be sprinkled everywhere upon the altar of God. <margin>Note.</margin>
15. *Note.* But the fact that the ram must be kindled with fire and offered to the Lord as a *sweet aroma to the Lord* contains a great *mystery* <note>original: "Mistery"</note>. The ram represents the true man created in *Adam*, which Christ—as the Word or the power of God—took upon himself from our human nature inherited from Adam <note>original: "Adamical Humanity"</note> in the body of *Mary*. The ram signifies that God, through Christ, would anoint our true *Adam-like* humanity with the holy anointing **oil** and bring it back to God again.

16. But because the human will had departed from God and entered into earthly, bestial lust, this ram (the humanity of Christ) had to be kindled with God's fire of anger. For the anger of God had become manifest in humanity. Therefore, God first anointed humanity with the *Spirit* of his love in Christ's humanity, and afterward offered this ram—the true human nature of Adam—to the fire of God. This was done so that, through the anointing of the oil of love, the fire of anger might be kindled; and through that oil of holy substance, the fire of anger would be transmuted and entirely transformed into a burning of love.

17. For our human soul had become a fire of anger—an *enmity* against God. Therefore, God reconciled it through the love of its substance; that is, God's anger within human life was reconciled. In the fire, God’s power "smelled" (or drew) human life back into the Eternal Word—back into God. God's fire of anger was the **mouth** which received human life again and swallowed up the human will, which had turned away from him.

18. When this great love surrendered itself into the human life of Christ, God's fire of anger—along with its devouring nature within the soul's fire—was turned into pure love, a total fire of love. Thus, **death** within the fire of God's anger (which held the soul captive by its influence, making the soul a darkness or a "dark fire") *was broken open* and turned back into the life of light.

19. This is what God represents through this sacrifice as a type <term>A "type" is a symbolic person, event, or object in the Old Testament that foreshadows something in the New Testament, usually Christ.</term> of Christ's coming. For *Moses* says, *'This was a sweet aroma to the Lord.'* Now, God does not favor the animal life, for that shall not inherit the kingdom of God. The work God performed through *Moses* was not actually about the ram or the heifer; rather, he was using them to represent humanity. God’s imagination focused on humanity through his spoken covenant of grace—that spoken Word of love which served as a goal or limit for man, continuing until *Mary*, when it manifested in human form. God’s imagination entered into this, and man’s imagination entered into the *type* (the sacrifice in the fire). Thus, the established covenant of grace, along with man’s imagination, entered the sacrifice of fire as a *symbol* <note>original: "Type"</note> of how Christ should reconcile God's anger within humanity.

20. In this way, the human will was ransomed in the fire as a symbolic representation of Christ. The established covenant of grace, along with human desire and prayer (which pressed into God through this sacrifice in the fire), entered the sacrificial fire together. This reconciled—meaning it destroyed—the earthly, bestial **nature** <note>original: "Property"</note> of the human will in the fire through love. Using the fire, God formed an image of a substance before him; in this fire-substance, God's own fire mirrored itself and reconciled the elemental fire within man. His eternal fire of love *favored* the human will through the established grace, using the **medium** of the fire; for *Moses* used holy fire to kindle the sacrifice.

This will not be based on personal conceit or opinion, but on the foundation of the *Scriptures* and true, certain knowledge through God’s grace.

For the anger-fire of God in the soul and flesh of man was imprinted together into the substantial Word—that is, into the Divine *Ens* <term>Ens</term> <note>Latin for "being" or "essence"; here referring to the spiritual substance of Christ.</note>. It made that essence living again—burning within itself through the *holy* fire—whereupon the Divine sacrifice in the fire was manifested in humanity.

He offered up to God the sweet humanity of the heavenly *Ens*, along with the Adamical <note>relating to Adam; the natural, fallen state of man.</note> humanity, into His anger-fire which burned in the Adamical humanity. Sin in the Adamical flesh was destroyed through the sweet heavenly flesh—that is, through the substantial Word of **LOVE**, through JESUS: God’s greatest *sweetness*.

He would bring the Adamical humanity through death (the anger of God) by enclosing the Adamical life within God’s love-fire, thereby breaking open the *prison* of death.

# Chap. 2. Showing how the Symbol has become Reality.

Testament—namely the Symbol—into the New, namely into his Flesh and Blood, which was the sacrifice of reconciliation for the sins of the world; and he gave them the <margin>b Or, Reconciliation.</margin> <sup>b</sup> atonement in his flesh to eat, and in his blood to drink.

7. For the reconciliation should no longer be performed in fire, where the Father’s anger burned away the vanity in man’s faith; but it should be done in the love-fire, in the flesh of Christ. This is no longer done with faith in the <note>original: "Type"; referring to a symbolic foreshadowing in the Old Testament</note> symbol, but in substance; no longer in power without substance, but with substantial Divine and human power, wherein the humanity of Christ himself should be the Passover Lamb: not Divinity without humanity, but Divinity and humanity together.

For every life desires an essence that matches its likeness; namely, every fire desires a fuel for its burning which is like that fire.

10. The foolish fire-life had become dark through the imprint of death, and therefore needed a light-essence from the Divine Light as a substance of light; like a holy anointing oil, wherein the dark, painful soul-fire changes itself into a desire for light and love. This was now conceived upon Christ’s *altar*—namely, out of Christ’s humanity—the substantial love, which is the substantial wisdom of God. That same fire in this substance was the *Name* and the power JESUS, namely God’s greatest *holiness*, which changes the soul’s fire into a light. Concerning this, Christ said, *He was the Light of the World* (John 8:12). For by his power, the soul has attained eyes of Divine light, so that it beholds God again.

11. And just as a person gives oil to an ordinary fire, out of which a light arises, so in a similar way we should understand the dark soul’s fire. It receives into itself Christ’s heavenly essence of Divine substantial love in this Testament, and rekindles the faded, even heavenly essence in Adam, and burns in its likeness. In this, the Kingdom of Heaven—namely, the *City of God*—is unlocked again, where the Divine Light shines once more in that same unlocked Paradisiacal Ground. This is the City of God in *Man*, where the Holy Spirit dwells; of which Christ says, *He that eats my flesh and drinks my blood, he continues in me, and I in him* (John 6:56).

12. In this unlocked Paradisiacal Ground, Christ—namely, the Divine love-essence—continues dwelling in the light. For the power in the light is the Divine essence, namely the supernatural heavenly flesh, a <term>Tincture</term> <note>In this context, a spiritual force or "inner quality" that transforms and purifies</note> of life. This <term>Tincture</term> permeates the soul and gives the heavenly fire-glance to the soul’s fire. But yet, so that a person may rightly understand it: the soul is the Father’s fire, which receives into itself (namely, into its fiery desire) the Son’s substantial love—meaning the holy love-fire, which has turned itself into the human <term>Tincture</term>, namely into flesh and blood. Understand this as the power of that same human life. Thus, the changing of the soul’s will is achieved.

13. Thus we see first this figure in *Moses’s* sacrifice of reconciliation: that the soul—namely, the faith’s desire of the soul—brought itself into the sacrifice as into a substance, and with the substance went into the fire, where the reconciliation through fire was...

## Of the Supper of the New Testament, etc. Chapter 2.

...made in the introduced Covenant of the Love-Fire, in the same manner and way that the substantial love of Christ would give itself up into the soul's fire (in which God’s anger burned) for food and reconciliation. Secondly, we see also through Moses not only how the soul is ransomed from sin through *fire* and, with the *love* in the Covenant, became fed with the holy fire of grace, but they also blessed the bread and meat through the reconciliation of the Grace-Covenant and ate them—namely, the holy bread and meat—as God also commanded them.

14. This signifies the oral eating and drinking of substantial grace, where not only the soul is fed, but—note—also the true Adamical man <term>Adamical man: the physical body and nature inherited from Adam</term> *who shall rise* from death again. For the earth was cursed because of man's sin, and man was forced by the curse of God’s anger to eat of the earthly fruit. But with this sacrifice and the blessing of the Covenant, God now establishes a *new blessing*, so that *Israel* ate of the blessed fruit again, where grace pressed through the curse once more, just as the sun presses and penetrates through water.

15. All of this was a *type* <term>type: a biblical person, event, or thing that foreshadows something in the future, particularly in the life of Christ</term> of the Testament of Christ, which would not only feed the soul with substantial fiery love, but—note—also the true Adamical *body*. When he ordained his New Testament under *bread* and *wine*, it [signified] how the inward grace of love would press through the outward man, just as the sun penetrates through water or as fire penetrates through iron.

16. And the oral eating and drinking of his New Testament is symbolized by the Paschal Lamb <term>Paschal Lamb: the Passover lamb whose blood saved the Israelites in Egypt</term> in the Old Testament. In that case, the Grace-Covenant of the divine blessing gave itself in a visible, elementary substance—that is, into a *medium* through which the human body received grace. It points toward the New Testament, where Christ (the substantial grace) would, with his love and the power of his flesh and blood (of both divine and human property), *give himself* into his fellow members, the Christians, through an elementary *medium* of blessed bread and wine for food and drink. Through this, the cursed body made from the *limus* <note>original: "limus," Latin for mud or slime; here referring to the dust of the earth from which Adam was created</note> of the earth (which has consumed the curse into itself) is blessed again.

17. We see this clearly in the Last Supper of Christ. With the institution of the New Testament, Christ did not intend to ordain any strange or new *thing*, but only to fulfill the Old Testament. With the substantial grace that had become MAN in his soul and flesh, he gave himself up into the Covenant of the Old Testament. He himself became the *fulfillment*—namely, the Paschal Lamb and the holy bread and meat—through which our true Adamical man is to be blessed. *For he first ate the Paschal Lamb with his disciples and incorporated himself with them in the Covenant of the Old Testament, and washed their feet for them. Afterward, he took the bread, gave thanks, broke it, and gave it to them, and said, "Take and eat; this is my body, which is given for you." In the same way, he also took the cup after the supper and gave thanks, gave it to them, and said, "Drink, all of you, from this; this is my blood of the New Testament, which is shed for many for the forgiveness of sins. I say to you, I will no longer drink of this fruit of the vine until the day that I drink it new with you in my Father’s kingdom."* ***Matthew 26; Mark 14; 1 Corinthians 11:23.***

18. This is now the true foundation and signifies: first, how the sweet grace of God’s Covenant has given itself up into our humanity; and, second, how that same Grace-Covenant (which in the Old Testament gave itself to *Israel* as a blessing under that same food through the sacrifices and Paschal Lamb) now gives itself to man under a *medium*—namely, under bread and wine—to be eaten and drunk with the assumed humanity of Christ. And, thirdly, it shows how he would not take away the first Covenant and begin some new thing, but how he himself would be that very Grace-Covenant. He now presents himself as a man and gives himself into man in a divine and human way, so that just as they had participated in him previously through his grace in the Covenant...

In the sacrifice, in a spiritual way in **power**, through a **medium**, so now they should participate in him also in a bodily and spiritual way, through the **medium** of bread and wine, and substantially participate in that same incorporated grace in the Covenant.

That the same new life, out of Christ's death and resurrection, might unlock even their life, which was shut up in death; therefore he gave this new unlocked human life of his assumed human life, with his flesh and blood, even under an **elementary medium** <note>original: "elementary medium" — a physical substance like bread or wine acting as a vehicle for spiritual grace</note>, so that faith might conceive it through a **medium**.

For as the participation of the Old Testament was done in a spiritual way, so now it should be both in a substantial and spiritual way alike. For the Deity has now presented the **Paschal Lamb** <note>The Passover lamb, symbolizing Christ's sacrifice</note> in the humanity of Christ; and God's imagination (which went formerly into the sacrifice) went now into the humanity of Christ; and the imagination of the humanity of Christ went with divine power into the **medium** of bread and wine, and through the same, in the participation thereof, **into the human life**.

## The Third Chapter.

->*How the Disciples of Christ have eaten and drunk Christ's Flesh and Blood; and how that is properly to be understood.*<-

<margin>1.</margin> Reason should here move from the "image-likeness" to that which is "un-imagelike" <note>Moving from the visible, physical symbol to the invisible, spiritual reality</note>, and forsake the **folly** for which men strive. For it was not an image-like participation, but is understood under an image-like one. Christ did not give his disciples his imaged, creaturely, outward, palpable, fleshy humanity—as if it were some piece of it. No, that is not consistent; for **he sat by them at the table**, and did not tear the imaged substance of his body. Instead, he gave them the spiritual humanity—namely, the power and virtue of his body and blood, his own **mumia** <note>original: "Mumia" — a term used in theosophy and alchemy to describe the essential spiritual life-force or "balsam" of a body</note>, in which the divine and human power is understood. This **mumia** is a true human substance of flesh and blood; it is a spiritual flesh, out of which the visible image grows, and is wholly **one** with the visible image.

2. See an analogy in the sun, which remains in its orb, but presses out with its luster, power, and whole substance—with all whatever it is in essence, power, and substance—forth out of itself into the **whole world**. It gives itself to every element, substance, and creature—to all herbs and trees, and also to every creaturely life—and works in all things whatever it will receive. And yet it does not tear itself apart when it goes forth from itself and gives itself to the other creatures; it continues always whole, and does not move away from its substance.

# How Christ's Disciples fed on his Flesh and Blood. Ch. 3.

<margin>3.</margin> In the same way, the *Supper* of Christ is to be understood; just as we see a similarity to it in the herbs and grass of the earth. These neither do, nor can do, anything without the power of the sun. The plant sets the "jaws" of its essence wide open toward the sun's power and virtue; that is, it hungers only after that. Into that hunger, the sun shines and *kindles the spirit*—namely, the brimstone <note>original: "Brimstone"; in alchemical terms, this refers to sulfur, representing the active, combustible principle of life.</note>, salt, and oil of the herb. As soon as this is done, and the sun's virtue finds or perceives itself within the brimstone, salt, and oil of the herb, it begins to work there. From this, the herb attains a perceptible warmth; it conceives and impresses the sun's virtue into itself, so that the sun's virtue and power become substantial within the herb. It grows with the herb and tinctures <note>permeates with a spiritual or essential quality</note> it, so that the herb becomes "sunny" or solar, and works toward bringing forth fruit.

4. In like manner, we are to understand Christ's testaments <note>The sacraments or the covenant established at the Last Supper.</note>. For he is the Sun of Life, and the *Light of the World* (John 8:12). According to his deity, he is the Eternal Speaking Word—that is, the power and virtue of the Godhead, the power of the Divine Light. According to his humanity, he is the formed, outspoken Word, which is entirely one with the Eternal Speaking Word. For he has *introverted* <note>turned inward</note> our received humanity with the Eternal Word; he has turned the outward inward (the substance of time) and turned the inward outward (the substance of eternity). Through our human substance, which he received from us, he has become "pressing forth" with the divine substance. Just as the *sun* presses forth from itself and gives of itself, so the divine substance gives itself forth through the human. *Note:* The divine substance brings the human forth with itself; for the divine desire goes forth toward the human essence, and the human essence goes in toward the divine, out-pressing delight or desire.

5. *Note:* But, because the divine power and virtue excel the human, the human is brought forth through the divine power. Thus, the human power and virtue give themselves, together with the divine, through the divine power. For the human power and virtue are a perception or "finding" of the divine, wherein the divine finds itself in something—namely, in the formed substance of the Word of Power. In this, the divine power loves itself as its own perceptible substance, just as the soul loves itself in its body.

6. *Note:* And thus God has poured his love through the human substance in the humanity of Christ, into the disciples of Christ. This happened in the same way and manner as the sun's power and virtue in the *Spirit of the World* <note>original: "Spiritu Mundi"; the vital spirit or life-force connecting the celestial and terrestrial realms.</note>. Just as the outflowing power and virtue of the stars mingle with the spiritual brimstone, salt, and oil in the higher elements—so that the sun captures their power and virtue in its glance and gives itself to them—and the power gives itself into the sun's power and virtue, and so they work together. By this, the "Light of Nature" is unlocked, and through such working, they give themselves into the earth, herbs, trees, and all creatures. Thus, in an herb or tree, such a virtue exists, from which the vegetation or budding forth of creatures arises. In such growth or life, a person must always understand two things: (1) an elementary, physical power and virtue; and then (2) a super-elementary, solar, and "starry" or astral power and virtue, where the solar and astral press forth with their strong power alongside the elementary.

7. *Note:* Now we see in herbs and all things that grow out of the earth that when they take hold of and "eat" this power and virtue of the sun and stars, they do not tear themselves apart or use a separate, physical mouth to do it. Rather, the essence of their desire (the natural brimstone, salt, and oil in the herb) is the "mouth" which takes hold of and eats the influence of the higher elements of the sun and stars. It is in this same manner that we should understand Christ's—

-># Ch. 3. How Christ’s Disciples fed on his Flesh and Blood.<-

7. The disciples and <insert>all other people</insert> have eaten and drunk Christ’s flesh and blood under the forms of bread and wine, as if through a *medium*, with the mouth of essential, longing faith; not with a limited human understanding, but with the desire of faith.

8. *Note:* Yet for a person to rightly understand this, they should know: (1) The outward mouth, with its physical grasp, takes in the outward material substance, bread and wine. The mortal, temporary substance of man—namely, the coarse flesh (which will not and cannot inherit the kingdom of heaven, John 6:63, 1 Cor. 15:50)—takes in and eats the bread and wine. For bread and wine are also earthly, temporary substances that go into the belly and out again, like all natural food (Matthew 15:17). 

And (2) the true, righteous man who was created in *Adam*—who, before the animal-like coarseness, was a true man and an image of the visible world according to his inward spiritual ground—this man eats Christ’s flesh. This flesh is just such a spiritual, substantial flesh, taken in with essential desire. *Note*: Understand this as the flesh he took upon himself in Mary—that is, our human nature—but not the outward foundation of the physical four elements, but rather the inward holy element: the ground from which the four elements proceed. Not fire, air, water, and earth, but the eternal pure element, which is a substance of Paradise hidden within the four elements—understand it as the substance of eternity, from which time has emerged into a visible substance. 

That same flesh acts as a spiritual <term>mumia</term><note>original: "mumia"; in the context of 17th-century mysticism and alchemy, this refers to the vital life-force or essential spiritual substance of a body, rather than a preserved corpse.</note> from which man, as a visible body, took his origin in the <term>*Verbo Fiat*</term><note>Latin: "The Word: Let it be done"; the creative command of God at the beginning of the world.</note>. This substance became blind to the kingdom of heaven in *Adam* when his desire entered the coarseness of the four elements. In Christ’s incarnation, this fleshly substance was filled with heavenly living substance and made alive again. *Note*: That is what the true Adam-like man eats, which remains hidden within the coarse shell of the four elements. In that substance, the true man eats Christ’s passion, suffering, and death—which, in Christ’s victory, has become eternal life. This life, risen from Christ's death, breaks our earthly evil will and has become a *death to our death*, which our outward nature mistakes for life.

<margin>Actively and effectively.</margin>
9. *Note: Note:* And here, Christ’s passion and death are put onto man in a way that is entirely essential and active. This death-bringing life of Christ swallows up our death, in which the body rests when it dies according to its material substance of the four elements, becoming dust and ashes. This same power and virtue of the true humanity remains in its source until the return of the physical substance.

10. But (2) the soul, which is a spiritual fire, eats the supernatural, substantial love of the name JESUS in its desire, as if with the mouth of true faith. This Name has become a substantial power and virtue—that is, the supernatural wisdom of God, in which the entire working Godhead is understood.

<margin>Or, Wisdom.</margin>

Just as light comes forth from fire, so wisdom—the property of divine power and of God—comes forth through the soul’s fire. Virtue goes forth, and in that outgoing power and virtue dwells the supernatural, non-material God in Trinity. 14. And when this holy ground of the soul and body was hidden, then the soul and body were in a dark <margin>valley</margin> dungeon, full of pain and torment. For God was hidden from it, and instantly the "principles," according to their properties, began to operate: 
(1) The **soul**, according to the anger-property of God the Father (which was hidden in the light shining within it); and 
(2) The outward body began to operate in the four elements—namely, in heat and cold, and in all other properties of the stars' power and virtue. Every awakened property impressed itself into a substance, which caused the body to become gross, hard, and beast-like, and the true image of God became a <term>wizard</term><note>original: "Wizard"; here meaning a grotesque, distorted, or unnatural creature</note> and a monster. (4) The **gross beast** of the coarse flesh, which is but a husk, receives only the outward husk of the sacrament—namely, the bread and wine. Under these, it receives the **judgment** of God, which breaks and kills the lust of this gross body. Therefore, **man should distinguish the body of the LORD and his blood from the animal man [who is] without faith, who receives only the judgment under the bread and wine; for as the mouth is, so also is the food in the mouth.**

But he said, *“My words are spirit and life.”* 
**Note:** This signifies that we should believe his words. He who understands and receives Christ's word into himself also understands the **Word** which has become flesh and blood. That Word has become a true human substance, and the "mouth of faith" receives it—namely, the true hunger or desire of the true humanity—in a spiritual way and manner. 
**Note:** Just as the Word of divine power has become man, so is it also received by faith, and it becomes **man in his members as well**.

17. That same spiritual, substantial Word takes on our humanity—meaning the spiritual humanity—and gives itself into it, and works and dwells within it...

# Ch. 3. How Christ’s Disciples fed on his Flesh and Blood.

17. Christ dwelled and worked substantially in a spiritual manner within the body he received from Mary. On the outside, men saw our flesh and blood—namely, the substance of the spiritual world—and yet within the visible was the invisible substance. Regarding this, he said in *John 3:13* that he had come from heaven with it.

<margin>* Senses.</margin>
18. In the same way, that invisible spiritual substance of Christ has united and turned itself inward into our humanity and into our faith’s desire. It happens in the same manner as a spark of fire falls into tinder and ignites it, consuming the substance of the tinder and making it entirely fire. So also the substantial power and efficacy of Christ consumes everything in his "tinder"—namely, in the human spiritual ground, the mind, thoughts, <margin>*</margin> and will. It consumes all evil influences in the thoughts and will, whether they came from the desires of the earthly flesh, from the Devil, or from the lusts of the world cast into it. That same spiritual fire consumes them all, for it takes hold of the life of man and rules it.

19. It is a light—namely, a spiritual oil—in the life of man, in which the true spiritual life (the natural <note>original: "foolish." Likely a transcription of "soul-ish," referring to the natural or psychic life as opposed to the spiritual life.</note> life) burns. *Without* this spiritual oil, there is no true light or life in man, but only an <term>Astral Light</term> <note>The "Astral Light" refers to the natural light of the stars and the physical world, which governs the biological and intellectual life but lacks divine illumination.</note>. Without it, the true soul stands in a dark dungeon in its essence and helps itself only with the astral light of the *sun*, which causes it to have vain earthly desires and lusts within it.

20. But that soul which attains this *holy* anointing oil of Christ within itself turns its longings and desires away from the *vanity of the world* and toward God’s word and power. It is like a new young child lying in the mother’s womb, allowing the mother to nourish it. Thus, it clings to Christ’s essence, substance, and power, and eats from the stock of the vine, Christ, just as the *branch eats from the stock of the vine (John 15).*

21. Reason should understand us correctly: it is not to be understood that Christ has turned himself into man with his gross, mortal flesh and blood. That physical flesh and blood is of no profit; it is only a receptacle or shell for the true spiritual man. Much less does the *Divine Substance* mingle itself with bread and wine. Therefore, when I look at the blessed bread and wine and receive it into my earthly, mortal mouth, I should not think that I grasp Christ’s flesh and blood with my *fleshly* mouth in the same way I grasp the bread and wine.

22. No, *that* cannot be. Bread and wine are only a *medium* or means for it, just as the earthly mouth is a medium or means for the spirit. The spiritual "mouth of faith" in man grasps Christ’s flesh and blood under the bread and wine, but it is not *inherent* in the bread and wine itself. For bread and wine do *not* change themselves into Christ’s flesh and blood; rather, they are an ordained *means* for it. This <term>medium</term> <note>A middle-ground or channel through which something acts.</note> belongs to the visible man, and through it, the invisible Christ gives himself into the invisible and spiritual man.

<margin>f By Bread.</margin>
23. In bread and wine, *two* properties are understood: (1) The gross, elementary, earthly substance that belongs to the mortal man; and (2) the power and virtue within it, where the <term>Tincture</term> <note>In Böhme’s terminology, the "Tincture" is the spiritual essence or "inner soul" of a substance that can transform or "tinge" other things with its quality.</note> of the bread and wine lies. This tincture is above the elementary substance, where the four elements lie in the <term>Temperature</term> <note>The "Temperature" refers to a state of perfect balance where no single element dominates, representing a heavenly or paradisical state.</note>, which is a heavenly, paradisical power and virtue. That same tincture of bread and wine is the *true medium* by which Christ, the human tincture, gives himself into the human life. For *man does not live by the four elements alone (Matthew 4:4).* The f <margin>*</margin> gross food <margin>f By Bread.</margin> which enters the mouth does not sustain life alone, but only the inward power and virtue—namely, the <term>Quintessence</term> <note>original: "fifth Essence." The purest or most concentrated essence of a substance.</note>, in which the tincture lies as a spiritual fire.

<margin>g Works,</margin>
<margin>h or effects.</margin>
24. Elementary food g <margin>g Works,</margin> <margin>h or effects.</margin> produces only mortal flesh and provides a source or h movement for the mortal life. But the spiritual man takes his nourishment from the tincture, for he himself is a tincture—namely, a spiritual fire. Therefore, Christ pours or overflows his heavenly flesh and blood—the holy anointing oil—into the life of...

### *How Christ's Disciples fed on his Flesh and Blood.* Chapter 3.

Man, through and with the nourishment of the true life, namely through the essence <note>original: "Tincture"; in this context, it refers to the essential spiritual quality or life-force within a substance.</note> of bread and wine: this is not to be understood as if the essence of bread and wine were able to grasp such a thing on its own, but it is only a facilitating medium <note>original: "permissive Medium"</note> for it. Just as the outward mouth of a person is only a medium through which the power and virtue of the nourishment's essence flows into the spiritual man. And because the highest essence—which is nearest to human life and sustains it most of all—lies in bread and wine, Christ has therefore ordained this Testament through them.

<margin>§ 1: 2</margin>
25. But (1) we should not be earthly-minded and suppose that after the bread and wine are blessed with the Words of Institution, Christ’s flesh and blood are inherent within the physical bread and wine, or that every wicked person may partake of it without the proper spiritual mouth. No; if that were so, then bread and wine could contain the Divine power and virtue within their own capacity, and Christ’s spiritual flesh and blood would have become bread and wine. It would no longer continue to be as Christ said: *My words are Spirit and Life* (John 6:63).

26. Man’s spiritual mouth takes Christ's words and life through faith; these words are a power of his flesh and blood, where the Divine Word *has become* a human substance. That same human and Divine substantial Word is given to man along with the essence of bread and wine, acting as a medium, so that there may be a visible sign of what is happening in the inner ground of the soul.

27. Note, note: (2) We should not depend on this means or medium alone, nor think that Christ’s flesh and blood are only participated in through the use of bread and wine—as common reason miserably errs today. No, that is not the case. Faith, when it hungers after God's love and grace, always eats and drinks of Christ’s flesh and blood, both through the medium of the blessed food and without it. Christ has not bound himself to bread and wine alone, but has bound himself to faith—promising that he will be in man and continue in him, and man shall continue in Christ. His powerful, living Word continues substantially in faith; the believer may always eat of this substance (as they always could), for it is the nourishment of faith, in which faith exists as a reality. Note: In such participation, faith itself becomes a substance—namely, a spiritual flesh and blood of Christ, in which the living God in Trinity dwells, works, and wills.

28. This substantial faith in man is Christ himself, who remains in man and is his life and light. *That is the temple of the Holy Spirit who dwells in us*; as Paul says: *Know you not that you are the temple of God, and that the Spirit of God dwells in you? Also, the temple of Christ is holy, which temple you are* (1 Corinthians 3:16-17). Also: *Shall we who belong to Christ still be sinners? Far from it; for then Christ would be a servant of sin in us* (Galatians 2:17). This same substantial faith is also the branch on the vine of Christ; its power and virtue penetrate through the whole person (just as the sun penetrates a plant) and kill the lusts and works of the flesh.

<margin>Note.</margin>
29. The mortal flesh is not the substantial faith; that flesh does not comprehend Christ’s flesh and blood, but endures it just as a rough stone endures the essence <note>original: "Tincture"</note> of gold. And as fine gold lies and grows within the rough stone, so also the love of Christ grows in the true life of man and penetrates through that life, as fire does through iron. This does not mean that such power originated in man’s life, as if he could receive the substance of God by his own power and virtue; no, it is given to him by grace, just as the sun gives itself to a plant by its own will. The plant cannot then say, "I am the sun," simply because the sun works within it. Likewise, man cannot say, "I am Christ," because Christ dwells and works in him as his expressed image. Rather, the creature is the passive vessel in which the Creator dwells and works.

<summary>This page explains that while bread and wine serve as a physical medium for the Eucharist, Christ's spiritual flesh and blood are received through faith rather than the elements themselves. It emphasizes that Christ dwells in the believer as a "substantial faith," transforming the individual into a temple of the Holy Spirit through grace.</summary>

30. We are members of Christ according to his humanity, and are therefore called Christians because Christ dwells and works in us; in that we are, in our life, his twigs and branches, in whom he brings forth fruit through his power and virtue <note>original: "virtue"; here meaning inherent power or efficacy</note>. Oh little children, it is a great mystery! Take note, take note: the *use* of this <term>Testament</term> <note>The "Testament" refers to the Sacrament of the Lord’s Supper or Holy Communion</note>, where we should partake of Christ's flesh and blood especially under the forms of bread and wine, is *therefore* ordained so that we should come together and eat of one bread, drink of one cup, and thereunder receive Christ. We do this so that we should *instruct* one another about what he has done for us, and declare his suffering, death, and bloodshed one *among* another, and *teach it to our children*. We should *bind* ourselves through this in love and exhort one another that we are members of one body in Christ—that in Christ, we are all but one.

31. Just as the one and only Christ gives himself into us *all in common*, to be our only life, and loves us all in his one and only humanity, and reaches out that same humanity with his great love and grace to us all in common under one bread and wine, and so binds himself to us in one single participation: thus *should we also, in such coming together and participation*, as members of one body, bind ourselves together in *true love* and faithfulness. We must seriously consider that in such participation, we are all but one in Christ; for we all partake of one and only Christ, and in that same one Christ we are one single body, which is Christ in his members. Oh little children, what a depth of mystery is this, if we would only rightly consider it! Satan, in the anger of God, has torn us apart and made us *at odds* so that we have *opposite* thoughts; but here Christ comes with his love and makes us all into one single man again within himself, which is himself in us. Thus, *all of us together* have become branches rooted in his tree, which he himself is; and *all live* from his power and substance, standing in one stock, which is himself.

32. Therefore, we should rightly consider this, and not draw near to this *communion* with unworthy hearts and mouths, supposing it is enough that we partake of bread and wine. No; it is a brotherly bond and covenant of membership. We bind ourselves through it to be one single man in Christ, and that same one man is every one of us in Christ. Therefore, our purpose in coming together should be that we, as members of one body, *will bind ourselves fast* with such participation, and forsake Satan with his contrary will, and *heartily love one another, as Christ has loved us and has given his life unto death for us*.

33. To this end is this testament of participation under bread and wine ordained: not to be understood as if it were a participation apart and separate, of which a Christian could not partake without the *use* of this ritual. For if we are in Christ, and he himself is in us and is our life and light, and we are thus rooted in him in <term>substantial faith</term> <note>faith that is not just a mental belief but possesses a real spiritual essence or "substance"</note>—the substance of which faith he himself is—why should that same desire for life not be able *always* to eat of it, if it only turns itself toward him? This ordinance is only a communal bond of love, so that we might instruct one another about what Christ has done for us until he shall *visibly* come to us again in his assumed <term>image-likeness</term> <note>Christ's recognizable human form or appearance</note> and, as our true high priest, be *ever with us and in us*.

# The Fourth Chapter.

## Regarding the Difference in such Participation: what the Wicked receive through this Testament, and how a Person should rightly prepare themselves for it, so they may be truly worthy.

1. As mentioned above, it does not depend on the imagination or the false idea that one only needs to physically approach this Communion. One should not think that because they have shared in the Bread and Wine with others, they have received the true Testament <note>original: "Testament"; here referring to the covenant promise and spiritual reality of the Lord's Supper</note> of Christ, through which sins are forgiven. No; *St. Paul says, He who does not distinguish the Body of the Lord from Bread and Wine receives it to his own judgment* (1 Corinthians 11:29). Bread and wine cannot grasp this Testament, much less can the unbelieving, who come to it only out of habit or because they wish to have the name of a Christian.

2. Likewise, it does *not* rest in the priest's power to bring the Body and Blood of Christ into the bread and wine through his blessing. Instead, it rests in the Divine Institution <note>original: "Institution"; the formal act of Christ establishing the sacrament</note>, which is *hidden* from the wicked mouth. It happens to such a person as it did to *Judas*, who, although he indeed ate and drank of the bread and wine at the Supper and was invited to the Testament, did *not* receive Christ's flesh and blood—namely, the Love of God. For *after the Supper, Satan entered into him* (John 13:27). This means that the power and virtue of the Testament touched him so that the "mouth" of his inward false faith was stirred and opened; but just as his faith's mouth was false, so was the Testament in his participation. As the Scripture says, *With the holy you are holy, and with the perverse you are perverse* (Psalm 18:26–27).

3. He received the Testament of Christ, but it was the *judgment* only. In the holy or the saints, this judgment kills the earthly will of the Serpent <note>The "Serpent" refers to the devil's influence or the "old" sinful nature within a person</note>. That is, when the soul is capable of receiving the holy power and virtue, so that it has a "mouth of faith" which receives the love in the Testament, then it also receives Christ's suffering, death, and resurrection in the same way. This kills sin in the soul and flesh. But the wicked mouth is not capable of receiving that love; therefore, it receives *only* Christ's suffering and death, and *not* his resurrection. With his false opinion, he applies his desire—the mouth of his false faith—to Christ's flesh and blood, and *kills Christ within himself* by this participation in his Testament. He is thereby guilty of the death of Christ; for with his false participation and false desire of faith, he touches the severe judgment of God found in Christ's agony, wounds, and death.

<margin>Or pierces.</margin>
<margin>Or against.</margin>
4. Therefore, because he is only capable of receiving judgment, the *judgment* of God—which killed Christ for the sake of our sins—is active within the soul and nature of the wicked person during this Testament. This judgment touches or stirs Christ's wounds and death in his Testament through this participation of a false nature. For the false "seed of the serpent" <note>The sinful nature or demonic influence</note> stings Christ in the heel <note>A reference to the prophecy in Genesis 3:15 regarding the conflict between the woman's seed and the serpent</note> with this touch. For Christ offers the soul his Testament and desires to slay the serpent; but while Satan holds the chief dominion in the soul, the soul will not receive it. Instead, through the soul’s essence, the person casts false, poisonous rays upon the wounds of Christ and desires to kill Christ.

5. Understand this: he desires to poison and *infect* that ground in man where Christ's blood and death, along with his resurrection, should be possessed. It stirs itself all the more in the false soul, just as it did in *Judas*. When he received this Testament, it was active in *Judas* and took over his life. Therefore, the Scripture says, *After the piece of bread <note>original: "Sop"; the morsel of bread dipped in the dish at the Last Supper</note>, Satan entered into him* (John 13:27). For his false heart had stirred the judgment...

Rather, they desire only to arise and live with their sins in Christ’s Spirit. They wish to rule in the resurrection of Christ with their earthly *Lucifer* <note>The spirit of pride and self-exaltation.</note>; therefore, they tread the death of Christ with the feet of their false desire and do the same thing the *Pharisees* did to Christ. Therefore, it would be better for such a person not to boast of being a Christian, and that they did not touch or meddle with Christ’s Testament.

## Of the Ground of Absolution. What the Forgiveness of Sins is.

<margin>d Or, Ignorance.</margin>
<margin>e Or, sharp.</margin>
8. THE false notion and gross misunderstanding when men *teach* that Christ’s Testaments destroy sin requires a more acute <note>original: "acute" meaning precise or sharp.</note> explanation, so that the wicked man may not hide himself under it, covering himself with Christ’s purple mantle and wearing it as a badge of falsehood. Christ’s blood-shedding—by which he destroyed God’s anger and turned that anger into love—*is what destroys sin*. In the person who worthily participates in Christ’s blood-shedding, sin is destroyed through Christ's victory and resurrection with his blood and love. He who comes to it with a penitent heart for his past sins, feeling anger toward them and having a strong purpose within himself to enter into them *no more*, lays hold of the testamentary grace through faith.

9. It is wrong for someone to defer their repentance until the participation in the Testament of Christ, thinking that the ritual itself will take away their sin. There is no forgiveness of sins, either by *Testament* or *Absolution* <note>The formal release from guilt or sin pronounced by a priest or through the sacrament.</note>, unless a person converts from sin and is *renewed* through earnest, sincere repentance and a turning toward the grace of God in faith on Christ in the Holy Ghost; so that he takes up *another* will and resolution to depart from falsehood and wickedness.

10. For the forgiveness of sins in Christ’s Testaments (and even *without* the use of them) is nothing else but this: when Christ arises from human death into human faith within the converting sinner, and a new obedient will arises out of his death and becomes a light in the person's life. So that the eternal night is turned into a clear day, then *sin is forgiven*. For if the eternal day of love dawns, then the night of the eternal darkness of God’s anger is turned into love, and there the *Wedding of the Lamb* <note>A biblical reference to the union of Christ and the soul (Revelation 19:7-9).</note> is rightly kept—and not with the unworthy heart, which, without repentance and the forsaking of—

## What Forgiveness of Sin is.
### Chap. 4.

its sins, *runs* to the Testament <note>original: "Testament"; likely referring to the Sacrament or the Lord's Supper</note>, and supposes that its sins are forgiven through the *laying on* of the priest's hand and participation in the Testaments.

**11.** The priest has no power to forgive sin; it does not reside in his own might and power. The power is in the ordinance <term>ordinance: a religious decree or ritual established by God</term> of Christ. Christ in man—and so far also as he is in the priest himself—*forgives* sin to the repenting conscience. The absolution <term>absolution: the formal release from guilt or sin</term> is only a *medium*, that is, an outward sign of forgiveness. It is meant so that we should receive one another in love and hearty forgiveness, binding and reconciling ourselves in the love of the bonds of Christ, in his *Bride* <note>The "Bride of Christ" is a traditional metaphor for the Church</note>, and in love receive one another into the *communion* of the body, **namely**, of the *Bride of Christ*.

<margin>The Church. Effectively.</margin>
**12.** The *minister* of Christ takes the faithful, penitent man, through an outward absolution in Christ's place, into the $^f$ *communion* or *congregation* of Christ. With his absolution, he is a *medium* or means of that which Christ himself, through his own absolution, $^g$ *effectively* performs in the inward soul. Thus, through such a *medium*, a person is outwardly confirmed. But if there is no faith and conversion there, but *only* a custom, then there is also no absolution. For the priest's absolution without Christ's co-working is powerless and dead; the power resides *not* simply in the outward ritual and in the priest, but in the communion of the saints in Christ—that is, in the Bride of Christ. This communion takes the repenting man into their fraternal membership; through the *faith* of what is to come, the Spirit of Christ in his members receives him.

**13.** A wicked priest, in whom the Spirit of Christ is not present, *cannot* absolve him nor receive him. Instead, the Office of Christ, through the word of his promise, receives him. A false priest is merely an outward, ineffective instrument in himself. He does no more in this act than a wicked priest does with *water baptism*, who only pours the water and speaks the words without any spiritual co-working. But the Spirit of the Office does not look upon the *unworthy minister* of the office, but upon those who come to the office with faith. He absolves the believer through his office and receives him with the Bride of Christ (in whom he works) into the church or *congregation*. This is not done by a wicked *Pharisee* <note>original: "Pharisee"; here used to mean a hypocritical or legalistic religious leader</note> who is himself incapable of the office and only sits there like an *idol* that people worship. Such a man is himself but a *devil* full of falsehood, attributing to himself that which he *does not have*.

<margin>* This refers to "Opus operatum" <note>Latin: "the work performed"; the theological idea that a religious rite is effective regardless of the priest's or recipient's spiritual state</note>, by which many deceive themselves.</margin>
**14.** There must be earnestness used when dealing with such an office of the power of God, or else Christ is merely mocked. Therefore, no one should *rely* upon the ritual and think that the ritual itself absolves him, or that he receives the Sacrament simply because of the ritual and Christ's institution. $^*$ If anyone wishes to receive Christ into himself as a guest, he must bring the "temple of Christ" (within which Christ absolves him) with him into the ritual. The absolution is only a receiving into the *communion* of the members of Christ. The priest receives him outwardly with the congregation, and Christ receives him in *faith* and binds himself effectively to him. This cannot be done without faith and an earnest turning toward God. And just as Christ works inwardly in him, so also the congregation or *church* (the Bride of Christ) works *as members* with him through their prayers, and they all are but one in Christ.

<margin>Note.</margin>
**15.** But it is a snare of the Devil when the wicked think: "I am a sinner indeed, but I will eventually go to the Office of Christ, to the communion of saints, and *I will be absolved and receive Christ's Sacrament* so that my sins may be forgiven." Then they intend to sin anew once their old sin is cleared away. *As it happens, many begin to hang their heads a little and put on a show of piety, but presently afterward they return to their old customs, to all abominations and blasphemy. These people crucify Christ again and* $^h$ *pierce him in his wounds.* It happens to such a person as it did with Judas, who, after he had eaten, Satan entered into him. It would be better if he stayed away from it altogether, as long as he is not in earnest, if he thinks he can remain a true Christian this way.

<header>Chapter 4. Of True Christianity.</header>

## On True Christianity: What a True Christian Is.

16. **CHRISTIANITY** is not merely a mental concept that a person needs only to acknowledge with the mouth and believe that Christ died for us and has satisfied [the debt] for sin. It is not enough that a person simply gives assent to the Gospel and considers the history of what Christ did to be true; nor is it enough for a person to merely go to His testament <note>original: "Testament," referring to the New Covenant or the scriptures</note> and there receive the grace He left behind, comforting himself with it and accounting it as merit and imputed grace <note>imputed grace: the theological concept that Christ's righteousness is credited to the believer</note>. It is not *enough* for a person to hear sermons preached, to be baptized into Christ, and to attend the [Lord's] Supper, simply to follow the custom. This by no means makes a person a Christian; it must be a matter of earnestness. No one is a Christian unless Christ *lives* and works in them, as Christ Himself says, *Without me you can do nothing (John 15:5).* Also, *He that does not gather with me, scatters (Matthew 12:30).*

<margin>i Glows <note>original: "gloweth"</note></margin>
<margin>Note</margin>
<margin>k Purest <note>original: "meetest"</note></margin>
17. A Christian must be one spirit in and with Christ, and must will and work in the power of Christ. It is a living, active, working grace within a Christian—a continually burning fire, a palpable power and virtue. Although it is often obscured by the desires of the flesh and the vanity of the world, it still <margin>i glows</margin> and burns in the heart like a fire; it reproves the flesh and the empty desire for untruth, rejects the false path, and does not desire it. That *same inward fire is the Spirit of Christ*, which without ceasing crushes the head of the serpent <note>A reference to Genesis 3:15, symbolizing the defeat of evil or temptation</note>—namely, the desires of the flesh. The flesh possesses the will of this world, but that same kindled foundation possesses *the will of God*. If anyone is a Christian, then he will hate and be angry at the will of the flesh; he will be an enemy to his own evil fleshly desires and constantly complain and consider himself *unworthy*. He will continually <margin>Note</margin> sink himself, with the inward will of his soul, into the <margin>k purest</margin> grace and into God's mercy. He will not say of himself, "*I am a true Christian*," but will continually press his desire into God's mercy and flee toward grace, so that he might become a true Christian. In all his conduct, he will always account himself *too unworthy* of such grace; and in continual, resigned humility, with weeping and prayer, he will only press into grace. His whole life will be a continual repentance, and he will evermore desire to take hold of grace, just as grace has taken hold of him.

<margin>l Strict <note>original: "severe"</note></margin>
18. A true Christian is *frightened by sin* when the desires of the flesh would perform it. Also, when he sees others commit sin, he *groans* within himself and wishes that such evil had not been done. It is an abomination in his eyes; he loves truth and righteousness and hates the false way. And although the earthly flesh often surprises him—falling into sudden, false desires without his will's intent, and many times bringing him to a fall (as happened with *David* and *Solomon* and many saints, and still happens today)—a man in whom the *Spirit of Christ* is does not remain in sin. Instead, the inward foundation—that is, the incorporated grace in the *Spirit of Christ*—comes quickly with God's <margin>l strict</margin> righteousness and enters into his conscience. This is just as the Prophet *Nathan* entered into *David's* conscience, touched it, and awakened the fire of anger <note>Referring to Nathan confronting David about his sins regarding Bathsheba and Uriah (2 Samuel 12)</note>. When *David* suddenly began to repent with great sorrow and acknowledge his sin, he entered into such earnest repentance that he would receive no comfort from all his friends. He would not allow his ears to be filled with comfort or the superficial "tickling" of grace until he felt the grace of the Lord in his conscience. No flattery could set his heart at peace until the Lord spoke to him with His grace *(2 Samuel 12:7).*

It emphasizes the necessity of continual repentance and the struggle between the Spirit of Christ and fleshly desires.</summary>
