19. Now we must consider this from the very beginning: first, from the divine will <note>original: "Lubet," a term Boehme uses for the initial inclination or "pleasure" of the divine spirit</note> of the Liberty; and second, from the desire toward nature, or the manifestation of the Abyss <note>the infinite, bottomless source of all things</note>.

20. First, in the salnitral flash, a sulfurous water is produced from the anguish through a painful transformation <note>original: "Mortification"</note>. This produces sulfur <note>original: "Brimstone"</note>, as we clearly see, and everything of that same kind and resemblance.

21. Second, a salt water is generated from the astringent, harsh, and attractive property that draws inward. Its substance <note>original: "Materia"</note> is salt. If it is compressed <note>original: "impressed"</note> again through fire or heat, it turns into salt. Everything sharp and attractive, whether in herbs or trees, proceeds from this. There is as much variety in sulfur and salt as there is variety of taste and fire found in all creatures, herbs, and trees. Everything that lives and grows contains sulfur and salt. The salt <margin>Body.</margin> property attracts and preserves the body, while the sulfur contains the oil or light in which the free divine will <note>original: "Lubet"</note> for manifestation exists, from which growth arises.

22. Third, through the salnitral flash, an earthy type of water is brought forth from the property of bitter, binding attraction in the first contraction <note>original: "Impression"</note> in the spirit. Its substance <note>original: "Materia"</note> is earth. This arises from the dark essentiality where darkness contracts itself in the first desire—where darkness itself begins, as mentioned before. Thus, out of its property during this contraction <note>original: "Impression"</note>, it produces a mist, smoky steam, or vapor, which the flash <note>original: "Flagrat"</note> in the Salniter seizes. Its essence is shocked or dies and falls downward; this is the matter <note>original: "Materia"</note> of the earth. However, the earth is not of only one kind; it contains everything that became physical <note>original: "corporeal"</note> in the flash. All these things spring forth through the "death" of the earth, according to how they were wrapped and driven together into a lump during the Creation, as we clearly see.

23. Furthermore, we must consider the highest secret <note>original: "Arcanum"</note>: the heavenly essentiality, and then the precious stones and metals, from which they all take their rise and origin. All things come from one Mother, which is the divine will <note>original: "Lubet"</note> and the desire of eternity for its own manifestation.

24. Now, regarding the incorruptible essence of physicality <note>original: "Corporality"</note>, it also arises in the first desire toward nature. Yet, it occurs in the contraction <note>original: "Impression"</note> of the free divine will <note>original: "Lubet"</note> and proceeds through all the forms into the highest sharpness, where it retires back into itself as a life out of the fire. The eternal fire is magical; it is a spirit and does not die. The Liberty is what ignites it, but the eternal nature is its sharpness. This same essence loses the property of wrath when it enters the light. In that fire, it is like a dying, yet there is no death, but rather an entrance into another source—moving out of a painful desire into a love-desire. It also yields spirit and essence from the fire-spirit, and the essence of gentleness <note>original: "Meekness"</note> from the light.

25. For that which dies to the Fire, or sinks through Death, is the divine Essence. This is also brought about through the <term>salnitral Flagrat</term> <note>original: "salnitral Flagrat"; Boehme uses this to describe a sudden, explosive flash of energy, like saltpeter igniting, representing a transformative moment in spiritual chemistry</note> of divine Joyfulness. In this state, the Property trembles in the joy of meekness and submerges itself through the "Death of the Fire"—which is called God’s Anger—and quenches it. Thus, God dwells in a gentle Light. The first Property used to ignite the Light is Fire and the Wrath of eternal Nature, and this ª makes the dark world.

26. The properties of the first Mother within the <term>Lubet</term> <note>original: "Lubet"; from the German "Lust," meaning a divine inclination, longing, or peaceful desire</note> and Desire also divide themselves into distinct parts during the joyful <term>salnitral Flagrat</term>, as can be seen in this outward world. This also produces Water, but of a very sovereign essence, resembling a spirit of pleasant, lovely desire. This is the Water of which Christ told us: *he would give us to drink, and whoever should drink the same, it should spring up in him to a fountain of eternal life.*

27. In this flash of disclosure, it also retains the fiery property which is called *Heaven*, in which the wonders of the divine kingdom of joy are known and manifest. In the watery property, it retains the pleasant Spring, or Paradise. From the fiery property, the eternal element arises; it is the real essence of the divine corporality, containing everything that can be known in God. This has been sufficiently explained in our other writings, such as *The Divine Revelation*, which treats of the *Divine Wisdom* and the *Divine eternal abyssal Birth*. Now we will turn to the essence of the outward world—namely, to the manifestation of the eternal in metals, herbs, and trees, as well as in humans and beasts.

<margin>ʳ Or Property.</margin>
28. We see that metals have a different kind of body than living creatures, and are different from the way earth and stones are. Now Reason asks: what is the origin of everything, seeing as in the beginning all things arose out of one Mother, and yet Eternity has no temporal beginning? Here we must again consider the Mother of the first <term>Pregnatrix</term> <note>original: "Pregnatrix"; the generative or birthing force of nature</note>, where and how one essence separates itself from another—specifically, how the beginning separates from the eternal, and Time from Eternity. They still exist within each other, but are severed into two "Principles": the Kingdom of God and the kingdom of this world. Yet all is God’s. But since Christ calls the Devil a *Prince of this world*, we are able to explain to what extent he is a prince. In truth, this world is not his own; he is the poorest creature in this world, and is not truly in this ʳ World at all. Now, therefore, look upon the first Ground—upon the Mother who has generated all creatures.

29. Regarding the earth, stones, and all metals: the earth’s property consists of a spiritual <term>Sulphur</term>, <term>Mercury</term>, and <term>Sal</term> <note>These are the "Tria Prima" of alchemy: Soul (Sulphur), Spirit (Mercury), and Body (Salt/Sal)</note>. Everything that has had a beginning has arisen in and out of her "Impression" <note>Boehme uses "Impression" to mean a contraction or hardening of spiritual forces into matter</note>. At its start, it came forth with the first form of the Mother—the astringent attraction—through the <term>Fiat</term> <note>The creative command, "Let there be"</note> into a created being. This provides a diversity of essence and spirit according to the original property of that separation.

30. First, the high spirits (which were created out of the free <term>Lubet</term> in the Desire, in the Fire’s property—that is, out of the Center of all essences) had within them the properties of both eternal worlds. But those who, after being made into creatures, remained with their desire in the property of the free divine longing and directed their will out of the Fire and into the Light, became Angels. The others, who directed their desire back into the Center (into the harsh and bitter properties), became Devils—outcasts from the free divine longing and the Light, as mentioned in other writings.

31. Therefore, the Devils possess neither the Kingdom of God nor the kingdom of this world. In the beginning of Creation, this world was created out of both inward properties (Light and Wrath); the Devil now has only the Wrathful part in his possession, and the other part profits him nothing. Thus he is in the world, and yet also not in the world.

...in the world, for he has but one part of it in his possession; from the other, he is cast out.

**32.** After the creation of the highest spirits, God created this visible world with the stars and elements as an external birth out of the Mother of All Essences <note>original: "Pregnatrix," a Latin term for a female generator or mother; here referring to the creative matrix of nature</note>. All of these proceeded out of the eternal beginning and took a temporal <note>i.e., time-bound or temporary</note> beginning. For here we must consider that the eternal Mother-generator moved herself and ignited her own form [or likeness], where the one then became physical within the other. Afterward, God created the Earth, which we are to consider in this way:

<margin>Or until.</margin>
**33.** The first desire toward Nature impresses itself and introduces itself through that impression into three forms: namely, into *Sulphur*, *Mercury*, and *Salt* <note>original: "Sal." In Böhme’s alchemy, these "Tria Prima" represent the soul/desire, the spirit/motion, and the body/matter</note>. In this impression, all things become rising and moving—which does not happen in the "still Nothing"—and so it forces itself into the highest anguish, even to the fiery-nitrous <note>original: "falnitral," referring to "salnitrum" or saltpeter, which Böhme associates with a sudden, explosive, or electrical spiritual flash</note> *explosion* <note>original: "Flagrat," a sudden flash or crack of transformation</note>, which is the origin of fire. Thus, the source-spring whirls within itself like the boiling of water upon a fire. For the harsh desire is attractive, and the fiery desire is repulsive <note>original: "expulsive"</note>; this is *Sulphur*. The tightening attraction is a wrathful sting [or prick], namely a grinding down <note>original: "Contrition"</note>. Yet it is held by the harshness so that it cannot move away; because of this, it is painful and causes pain, as if it were seething. Yet this is only spirit without physical essence, which occurs in *Mercury* and is *Mercury's* own form.

**34.** And there, the separation of two wills occurs. One remains and is the very essence of anxiety, since it originally arises from desire. The other, which arises out of the divine inclination <note>original: "Lubet," a term for the "delight" or longing of the divine will</note> of freedom, retires back into itself into that freedom. Yet there is no parting or dividing from one another; they go together throughout the ignition of the fire and the fiery-nitrous explosion. With the ignition of the fire, death is brought about within the wrath of the fire. There the source-spring dies—and yet there is no death, but a likeness of death. 

The real, eternal, and temporal death happens in this manner: where freedom catches itself within itself, the death or explosion falls down into that freedom as if powerless and freely resigns itself. Then the spirit (meaning the very sharp, fiery, anxious source-spring) becomes material and retains only a working of essence, like a powerless desire. In the ignition of the fire during the fiery-nitrous explosion, each property separates within itself, and the whole matter <note>original: "Materia"</note> is divided into particulars: namely, into metals, stones, and earth.

<margin>Or the highest or chiefest of the metals.</margin>
**35.** The most noble metal, Gold, arises from the freedom which is included throughout the explosion in the tightening impression. It is not free from the matter of the rest, for everything is wrapped up together. But because freedom—along with the property of *Sul* <note>Böhme’s term for the light-essence or "oil" within Sulphur</note> or light—is also contained within it, *Sul* pushes outward to manifest itself, as it is the property of freedom to do so. This is why metals grow, unlike the gross, hard stones, which are compressed too tightly in the impression of the wrathful essence and have too little *Sul* in them.

<margin>Body.</margin>
**36.** Concerning precious stones, with their radiant luster and great virtue <note>i.e., medicinal or spiritual power</note>, they have their origin in the flash of the fire where life and death separate. While one part descends because of the dark essence, the other ascends because of freedom; yet everything is brought into physical essence during the explosion. Thus, that same flash or glance also becomes material in the explosion. Therefore, they are hard and have a blinking glance like an eye. For this is also the origin of the eye or sight in the womb <margin>Body.</margin> when life ignites, all according to the laws of eternity.

<margin>Liquid.</margin>
**37.** Therefore, they possess such great power, efficacy, and virtue because they are so close to the Deity and carry the embodied names of divine power within them. Similarly, Gold is close to the divine essence, or heavenly body. If man could open [or disclose] the dead body and reduce it to a volatile <note>original: "flying"</note>, moving spirit—which can only be achieved through divine motion—then it would be seen what it truly could be. No mere reason believes or understands this without divine vision.

<summary>Böhme explains the alchemical and spiritual origins of matter, describing how the "Tria Prima" (Sulphur, Mercury, Salt) interact through a fiery "Flagrat" to create metals, stones, and the earth. He highlights Gold and precious stones as materials that retain a closer connection to divine light and freedom.</summary>

38. Further, we are also to consider the other metals and minerals, which in like manner take their origin; but in the salnitral flash <note>original: "salnitral Flagrat"; Böhme’s term for the explosive, creative spark of divine fire, analogous to the ignition of saltpeter</note> each property is separated. We see that the properties of the Fire and Light are different, and all come from the first impression <note>Böhme uses "impression" to describe the contraction or "pressing" of divine desire into material form</note>; where before the impression, the *Lubet* <term>Lubet</term> <note>original: *Lubet*; the divine will or "good pleasure" (from the Latin *libitum*)</note> and the desire of liberty stand mutually in each other, like a *Chaos*, a combination of great wonders. All colors, powers, and virtues are contained in this single *CHAOS*, or "Wonder-Eye." This *CHAOS* is God himself—the Being of all beings—who thus manifests himself in particular beings through the eyes of eternity. Each piece of matter <note>original: "Materia"</note> is an essence according to the spirit from which it was generated; and if it is ignited in the fire, it likewise yields such a light as the spirit that exists within the essence.

<margin>The Body <note>original: "y Corpus"</note></margin>
39. And thus we are also to consider the metals: whatever kind of spirit each of them has, it yields that specific shimmer and luster, and it also possesses such a body.

<margin>Boiling, growing, and increasing <note>original: "z Boyling, growing, and Waxing"</note></margin>
40. Just as the mind acts and moves the thoughts and senses from the highest to the lowest, and comprehends and commands by those thoughts, so the Eternal Mind has manifested itself from the highest majesty even to the lowest, most external thing—namely, to the greatest darkness. This world, with the sun, stars, and elements, and with every created being, is nothing else but a manifestation of the eternity of the Eternal Will and Mind. As it was in the beginning, so it still stands in its simmering and growth <note>original: "z Seething and Vegetation"</note>, and so it still moves forward toward Light and Darkness, toward Evil and Good. All things consist of these first three forms—namely, *Sulphur, Mercury*, and *Salt* <note>Böhme uses the Paracelsian "tria prima" (three primary principles) to describe the structural components of all matter</note>—as one degree in order after another. For the choirs of the spirits are arranged this way, as are the stars, trees, herbs, and all kinds of things that have been and are; so also are the inward heavenly choirs with their distinct divisions.

## The Fourth Chapter

### Of the Birth of the Stars and the Four Elements in the Metallic and Created Property

1. As mentioned before, all things proceed out of one only Mother, and separate themselves into two essences according to the Law of Eternity: into a mortal and an immortal, into life and death, and into spirit and body. The spirit is the life, and the body is the death—the house of the spirit. Just as the Holy Trinity exists in the "birth" <note>the process of divine self-unfolding</note>, so also is the external birth: there is likewise essence and spirit in Heaven. We see a representation of this in this outward world, where there are four elements, and yet there is but one single element, which separates itself into four properties: Fire, Air, Water, and Earth, as was mentioned above.

<margin>In this place <note>original: "a Loco"</note></margin>
<margin>Outgoing, Breathing <note>original: "b Outgoing, Breathing"</note></margin>
2. For we are to consider the creation of this world in this way: the whole essence of eternity moved itself in the place of this world, and the whole form was ignited and stirred in the desire for manifestation. There, the generation divided itself in the flash of the ignited fire into four parts: Fire, Water, and Earth, while the Air is its moving, outgoing spirit <note>original: "b egressive Spirit"</note>, just as is observed in *Sulphur*, which consists of these four things.

<summary>Böhme explains that all material substances, specifically metals and minerals, originate from a divine "Chaos" or "Wonder-Eye." He describes the cosmos as a manifestation of the Eternal Mind, structured by the three alchemical principles and the four elements.</summary>

# Signatura Rerum: Chapter 4

3. In the same way, the *Astrum* <note>original: "Astrum"; refers to the celestial or astral influence that shapes the physical world.</note> is generated from the first Mother [Nature]; and all things put together are only one Body. All things take their rise from the inward Spirit, just as a hand or foot grows out from the inward center and already has its shape in that center—that is, in the first operation—and so it only grows into a form that matches what the Spirit is.

<margin>Or in a seven-fold form.</margin>
4. The first Mother of all things—that is, the Lubet <note>original: "Lubet"; from the German *Lust*, referring to a divine longing or the "free will" of God before it hardens into a specific desire.</note> together with the Desire—introduces herself especially into seven forms, and yet remains steady in only three; however, she manifests herself in seven forms.

5. The first form is **astringent**, which is an austere attraction; this is the cause of coldness, salt, and all physical matter.

<margin>Or Sting. Stirring up, or Moving.</margin>
6. The second form is the **Compunction** <note>original: "Compunction"; here meaning a "sting" or "pricking" sensation that initiates movement.</note>—that is, the drawing or motion. This causes feeling, as well as pricking, aching, and torment; it is the affection of bitterness, enmity, and friendliness, as well as joy and sorrow.

7. The third form is the great **Anguish** within the "Impression" [the contraction of matter], which causes two wills: one toward the Fire (where the will of the free Lubet falls down into the wrath of the fire) and another that goes back into itself and creates a luster in the sharpness of the fire.

8. Now the fourth form is the **Fire** itself—that is, the first principle in Life, by which the dark and light worlds are separated. In this "Flagrat" <note>original: "Flagrat"; a sudden burst, flash, or explosion—the moment of transition or "shattering" in the spiritual process.</note> all material separations are carried out. Physicality and multiplication begin according to the property of the first Eternal Mind: according to its "essentiality" it creates a mortal *Ens* <note>original: "Ens"; a philosophical term for "being" or "essence."</note>, and according to the free Source it creates a living *Ens*.

9. The fifth form is the **second Desire**, which is created after the separation, according to two properties: one according to the Lubet of liberty out of the Light (which is the highest desire for Love), and the other according to the Fire’s Lubet (which leads its life of essence in the Love within the Light), from which joyfulness and every true life arises.

10. Love gives essence, for it is expressive and yielding—it gives of itself. For God gives himself to every essence, and the Fire is receptive; the Fire needs essence for its "wrathful hunger," otherwise it would extinguish. If that happened, the luster of the Light would go out and the desire of Love would cease, for the Fire makes the Light "desiring" (full of joyfulness). If the Fire dies, the Light grows dark and Love turns into anguish, as can be seen in the condition of devils.

11. The sixth form arises from the **turning wheel** before the Fire, where the multiplication of essence arises out of the property of *Mercurius* <note>original: "Mercurius"; refers to Mercury, symbolizing the principle of movement, communication, and chemical reaction in alchemy.</note> in the "salnitral Flagrat" [the explosive spark of nature]. With the igniting of the Fire, one form is introduced into another; and if the Love-Desire now penetrates all the forms, then all the forms grow very desirous of one another, for the dear, lovely child *Venus* <note>original: "Venus"; symbolizing the principle of love, harmony, and beauty.</note> is in them all.

12. Here begin taste, smell, hearing, seeing, feeling, and speaking; for the Light opens a different principle from a different source and fills everything. Here, life springs up in death—that is, Love in the midst of anger, and Light shining in the darkness. Here the Bridegroom [the Light] embraces his Bride [Nature], and God himself resists his own anger (the wrath of Nature). In this form, all speech, understanding, and the senses arise, along with the true, real life of all creatures; this is also true for the life in vegetables, such as trees and herbs, in each thing according to its own property.

13. The seventh form arises from all the others and is the **Body, dwelling-place, or food** of the others. It is created this way: when the other forms taste each other through their mutual penetration in the Love-Desire, an hunger or desire for Love (for the Light) is created in each form. Now, each hunger or desire reaches out for the thing it desires and eagerly attracts the property of that thing. Thus, out of two things, one essence is made—out of the hunger and that which the hunger desires. For this hunger does not exist in death; it no longer encloses itself in death unless the hunger or the imagination within the hunger becomes too great, and...

### Chap. 4.

If the Hunger <note>original: "the Hunger" — in Boehme’s thought, "hunger" refers to the driving desire or essential craving of a spirit to manifest or consume</note> cannot obtain that same thing, then it chokes. This happens many times when a child is choked or smothered in the mother's womb if this Form is ignited within another Form to eat of some external thing that the mother intensely longs for. If she cannot get it, the child also cannot get it; thus, it chokes in its hunger, or else a limb is spoiled from which that hunger arose.

<margin>The one is not the other.</margin>
14. The first Hunger in the Center before the fire is a spiritual hunger, which creates the dark world; and the hunger of the free <term>Lubet</term> <note>original: "Lubet" — from the German *Lust*, meaning a divine inclination, pleasure, or the "will" of the abyss to manifest</note> creates the light world. Both of these are only Spirit until they pass together through the ignition of the Fire, where they are then "mortified" <note>original: "mortified" — transformed or refined through a death-like process to the old form</note> to the Spirit and become a likeness of the first Spirit—namely, a manifestation of the incomprehensible Spirit, which is called God in both Love and Anger, in a two-fold source. Thus, each stands undivided in itself: God in Time, and Time in God. One is not the other, but they both come from one eternal origin. Thus, the temporal Spirit's hunger produces a temporal body, and the eternal Spirit's hunger provides an eternal body; both are mutually within each other, and yet they are distinct.

15. The seven Forms <note>original: "seven Forms" — the seven properties of nature that Boehme describes as the building blocks of reality</note> create a body for themselves according to their hunger and out of their own properties; therefore, everything that the Spirit possesses in all its properties lies within the body.

16. Furthermore, we should know that a separation was made in the creation of this world. This can be seen in the sun and stars, and likewise in all creatures, as well as in metals, stones, and earths; for this very thing is the manifestation of God.

17. We see seven planets in the firmament, and seven metals in the earth which are fixed, as well as seven planets which are fixed in their properties; the rest are minerals, and the same is true of the stars. And just as the planetary orb has its predominant stamp or influence, so is the birth of every thing.

<margin>Or out of.</margin>
18. As the Deity—namely, the divine Light—is the center of all life, so also in the manifestation of God—that is, in the physical figure—the Sun is the center of all life. In the highest life, the highest things took their beginning, and so they proceeded successively from one another down to the lowest. In every external thing there are two properties: one from Time, and the other from Eternity. The first property of Time is manifest; the other is hidden, yet it creates a likeness of itself within each thing.

19. Whatever has its beginning out of the <term>Lubet</term> of Liberty has its root in a heavenly property and its body in an earthly one; but the Eternal stands within Time and manifests itself through Time.

20. *Sulphur* <note>Boehme uses "Sulphur" and "Mercury" as alchemical principles representing qualities of the soul and nature, not just the chemical elements.</note> is, on one hand, internally heavenly, and as to the body, earthly; yet it produces a heavenly likeness out of itself according to the Eternal, which is fixed and steadfast. This can be seen in gold, and is much more to be understood in the human body, if it were not corrupted by the desire in *Mercury*; for the spiritual or heavenly man consists of *Sulphur*, and in *Mercury* is the corporeal—namely, the likeness of the divine Man. Likewise, the metallic property in *Sulphur* is the noblest, most excellent, and highest, for it is the highest spirit.

<margin>Boiling, or Decoction.</margin>
21. Understand it this way: in the heavenly being there is also a property of a seething <note>original: "Seething" — a process of boiling or refining, often called "decoction" in alchemy</note> when the Liberty is apprehended and ignited in the highest desire, where joyfulness arises. This is accomplished in the heavenly *Sulphur*, where it is made substantial in the heavenly *Mercury*—that is, in the eternal Word, which is a spiritual essence.

<margin>With.</margin>
22. But if that same spirituality longs to manifest itself in a likeness—both according to the property of the Spirit and the physical substance, and according to the Trinity of the Deity and the mortal and immortal essence—then that image is represented in the stars and elements. Finally, it is set forth in Man, who is a living image of the whole essence of both the divine and outward world. Also, the inward and outward worlds are represented by the metals in a mortal image, as a resemblance and likeness of the living heavenly substance.

**23.** The beginning is in *Sulphur*; for *Sul* is the inclination <note>original: "Lubet"—the divine will, desire, or longing for manifestation</note> of the Light, or the Liberty, which longs for manifestation, and it cannot otherwise be achieved except through Fire. In *Phur* arises the Desire—specifically, a harsh attraction which creates the dark, earthly property and the harshness of the Spirit, which is the fiery *essence*. In this harshness arises *Saturn*, which is the thing impressed; and *Mercury* is the desire of the hunger, and the one who rages, raves, and breaks; and *Mars* is the wrath in the hunger, a cause of anger. These three are the property of *Phur*—that is, the desire of the free inclination.

**24.** The property of the free inclination begets the *essence* in the three previously mentioned forms: *Saturn, Mercury*, and *Mars*. It gives itself into each property, and the property in the hunger of *Mercury* makes it a physical form. But if the free inclination also turns into a hunger in the harsh desiring, then it also makes three forms according to itself: *Jupiter*, who is the understanding of the inclination; *Venus*, which is the desire of the inclination; and *Luna*, which is the body of the inclination; and according to the property of the Light, it makes *Sol* <note>the Sun</note>. All of this is Spirit. But now, in every Spirit's hunger, there is also an *essence*, according to both the mortal and immortal *Ens* <note>being or substance</note>, a fixed and an unfixed; a figure according to the heavenly, and a figure according to the earthly being or property.

**25.** In the *Saturnine* property, the desire of the free inclination creates Lead (according to *Saturn's* own property), and Salt (according to the watery property in *Saturn*); and according to the mortal and earthly property in *Saturn*, it creates stones, earth, and everything else of that sort and appearance.

<margin>Or fashions.</margin>
**26.** But according to the Liberty—or according to the free desire's own property (in that it yields itself up to *Saturn*, that is, to the Desire)—it creates Gold in *Saturn*, according to the desire of the Light, where the Spirit and Body separate. The Spirit of its desire is *Sol*, and the body is Gold. Understand this: the golden body is in *Saturn* according to the property of the free desire, and not according to *Saturn's* own property. His own property in himself is lead, salt, and earth; but he keeps the golden child shut up in himself like a black raven—not in his gray form, but in a darkish cast. He is a great Lord, but his dominion, because of the golden child which he has in his bowels, does not stand in his own power. He is not the father of the child, but *Mercury* is the one who fashions <margin>*</margin> the child. However, *Saturn* puts his morning mantle <note>an outer covering or shell</note> upon it, so that he can have no joy with the golden child; he gives the fair child a body, for he is its *Fiat* <note>the creative command or "let it be"</note> or creator, and hides and covers it closely under his mantle. He cannot give it a body from his own property, for the golden body is the *essence* of the free desire in the highest degree of physical form within the fixed death—where yet there is no death, but an enclosing, and a representation in the likeness of the divine heavenly essentiality.

<margin>Or Faber <note>the Master-Craftsman</note>.</margin>
<margin>In a strange fire, and yet not strange; when the cloak is laid aside, it needs only its own fire.</margin>
<margin>Here must be its own fire only from within, and from without.</margin>
<margin>And it is the Tincture which colors the Body.</margin>
**27.** *Mercury* is the master-workman <margin>l</margin> of this child which *Saturn* hides. When he gets it into his hunger, he casts off his black cloak and rejoices in it; but he is too malignant in his fire-wrath <margin>m</margin>, he devours the child and turns it wholly to his own property. When he is most sharply hungry in the fire, then *Sol* must be given to him (she is his wife) so that his hunger may be appeased. Then, when he is satisfied, he labors in the matter of the child with his own hunger or fire <margin>n</margin>, and fills up his satisfied desire from *Sol's* property, which he had previously eaten. He nourishes the child until it takes upon itself all four elements with the constellation, and he grows exceedingly pregnant with the child. Then it is ready for a strange fire—and yet not strange, but an earnest fire—and then the Father gives it the soul, which is the fire-spirit. And its first Mother, whom *Mercury* consumed in his hunger and who was fixed and perfect, gives the soul's-spirit, which is the light-life. Then the death <margin>o</margin> arises, and the child is born and becomes afterwards its own, a child of the Liberty, and cares no more for its master-workman. It is better than its father, but not better than its mother in whose seed it lay before the father worked in it; it bruises the head of its father's fiery...

Essence, **namely** <note>original: "viz."</note> of the Serpent, and passes freely through Death in the Fire: Do you understand nothing here? Then you are not born to the highest knowledge of the alchemical <note>original: "spagirical"</note> science.

28. Further, we are to consider the degrees: what the liberty—**namely**, the eternal *longing* <note>original: "Lubet," a term Böhme uses to describe a divine inclination, pleasure, or pre-reflective will</note>—gives to the hunger of the other forms in *Sulphur*, within the property of the other planets. The form of the birth is like a turning wheel, which *Mercury* causes within the *Sulphur*.

<margin>Draws it to itself.</margin>
29. The birth of the highest degree turns round (**namely**, the Desire), for this world is round, and so also is the birth. When liberty has given its highest *longing* (as a golden hunger) to *Saturn*, and placed *Mercury* as the Master-Worker, then it betakes itself into itself—into its own desire, according to the property of meekness. For the first conception of the golden child is achieved according to the property of joyfulness; but out of goodness and meekness, it resigns itself to *Luna* <note>the Moon / Silver</note>. For it is a pleasant yielding <note>original: "Demission"</note> by reason of that meekness, which *Mercury* apprehends and works within as well. This body is Silver, and it comes from the first impression where the yellow and white separate in the fire—**namely**, the colors of the power <note>original: "Virtue"</note>. Then *Luna* arises out of the yellow and turns into white because of the divine meekness. Because its origin is from *Sol's* <note>the Sun's / Gold's</note> color, it has a perpetual hunger after *Sol*; it receives the Sun’s luster into itself, puts it on, and shines with it.

30. Now, as the superior is, so likewise is the inferior (namely, metals); therefore, Silver is the next degree to Gold. As Gold is generated, so also is Silver. *Venus* clothes it, which *Mercury* cannot endure since he is the Master-Worker, and he gives his garment also. But Silver has neither the property of *Venus* nor *Mercury*, for it retains the property of its mother—**namely**, the meekness in the liberty—and is hatched like Gold by reason of the Sun. The Moon has a heavenly property, but in reference to its own proper form from the property of desire, it is of a very earthly property; it is a cabinet and keeper of the earthly and heavenly essence. 

In the same way, the outward body of man before the Fall in *Adam* was comparable to Silver. But when he died to the *longing*, then only the earthly property lived in him. Therefore, he continually hungers after *Sol's* glance and glory; he would gladly take up his splendor again with *Luna* from the Sun, but he obtains only an earthly lunar luster, in which he acts and exercises pride. This remains so unless he is born again out of *Sol's* splendor—that is, out of God's power in the heavenly *Mercury* <note>the divine Word or creative spirit</note>. Thus, he becomes again the golden Silver-Child in divine essentiality, only covered and clothed during this lifetime with the earthly Moon—that is, with earthly flesh.

31. *Saturn* is also the house of Silver; he is likewise the cause of the first conception, but he turns his desire only upon the golden child and leaves Silver its garment. He takes it into his stony, earthly property and lets *Mercury* hatch it.

<margin>or Sphere.</margin>
32. The desire of the free *longing* is fixed and steadfast regarding the property of desire alone. This brings its will again from the body into the combat in the senses and creates *Jupiter*. *Jupiter* is on the orb <margin>or Sphere.</margin> upwards under *Saturn*, under the Saturnine wheel or power. Its metal is Tin, and it is the third degree; for the *longing* of liberty in the desire proceeds forth into the desire of the harshness <note>original: "Austereness"</note>, and so it gives itself into the *Fiat* <note>the divine command or "let it be"</note>.

33. We must understand it thus: the *longing* of liberty goes forth out of itself like a plant and creates one degree after another in order. However, *Mercury* creates the sphere, for he is the Master-Worker. Just as the eternal birth is within itself in the heavenly *Mercury*—**namely**, in the Eternal Word in the Father's generation—so likewise, with the motion of the Father, it came into a created being. It proceeds in its order, as can be seen in the wheel of the planets; for the order is placed exactly as man is in his own order.

# Signatura Rerum: Chapter 4

34. First, there is in him the true golden divine **Man**, who is the **Likeness** of **God**. Next, there is in him the man of heavenly substance, namely the inward holy **Body**, generated from the Fire and Light in the <term>Tincture</term> <note>In alchemy, the "tincture" is the spiritualizing principle or essence that can transform matter</note>, which is like pure silver, if it were not corrupted. Thirdly, there is in him the elemental man from the pure element resembling *Jupiter*. Fourthly, the <term>mercurial</term> <note>original: "mercurial"; referring to the qualities of the planet Mercury: fluidity, communication, and movement</note>, which is the growing or paradisiacal [Man]. Fifthly, the <term>martial</term> <note>original: "martial"; referring to the qualities of Mars: fire, energy, and sometimes wrath</note>, from the *Fire*, namely the foolish [Man], according to the Father's **Property**. Sixthly, the Venusian [Man], according to the outward Desire and the water's **Property**. Seventhly, the solar [Man], according to the Sun's property, namely according to the outward world, as a seer and knower of the wonders of God. And yet, he is but one single man, existing both in the inward and outward world. Likewise, this is the **Similitude** [or **Form**] of the seven metals: they have one property according to the inward world, and another visible and palpable property according to the outward world.

35. From *Jupiter*, the sphere rotates, and out of the separation, *Mercury* proceeds forth with a fragmented metal, according to his spirit's property. Externally, he is *Quicksilver*, and internally, he is a paradisiacal working. In his spiritual property, he is the distinguisher (or articulator) of words, voices, and speeches. It is written, *God has made all things by his Word*. The heavenly eternal *Mercury* is his Word, which the **Father** expresses in the kindling of his light; the "expressed" is his Wisdom. The Word is the worker, framer, and maker of the forms within the expressed Wisdom. Now, what the inward *Mercury* does internally in God's power, the outward *Mercury* also effects in the outward power of the created essence. He is God's instrument, with which He works externally toward both death and life; he builds up and breaks down each thing according to its own property.

<margin>Weakens or destroys.</margin>
36. According to *Saturn's* property, he builds; and according to his own property, he distinguishes and dissipates the hardness in *Saturn* (that which is enclosed) and opens it to **Life**. He opens the colors and creates forms and shapes. He carries within him both a heavenly and an earthly property. In the earthly, he carries out of the first desire toward Nature—namely, out of *Saturn* and *Mars*—the wrathfulness of the <term>Impression</term> <note>original: "Impression"; the process by which spiritual will solidifies into material form</note>. For Mars is his soul, in which *Mercury* lives; he gives him the fiery essence and stands under *Jupiter* in the upward order of the sphere. He carries the fire-spirit in <term>Sulphur</term> <note>In alchemy, "Sulphur" represents the combustible, active, and "soul" principle of a substance</note> into all planets, and forms and gives to each thing its source and true spirit of life.

37. *Mars*, in the first impression, is the great anguish, and he causes the Love-Will of the Liberty to separate from him. That which is separated is called God, and the anguish (or fire-source) is called God's Anger—the wrath of the Eternal Nature. Just as God's Love internally separates from God's Anger (that is, from the wrathful property of the Eternal Nature, like Heaven from Hell or God from the Devil), so too is this effect produced in the birth of the outward nature.

38. **Love** proceeds out of the Wrath and is an act of humility or submission. Likewise, it came into order during the Creation; therefore, *Venus* stands in the sphere on the line of *Mars* under the *Sun*, for such is the separation in Nature, and so one proceeds forth from another. Its metal is copper. The origin of copper is this: Love is a desire, and it desires only light and joy, for the matter <note>original: "materia"</note> is made out of the property of desire. But if the love-desire is to become corporeal in the impression, then it must resign itself to the wrathful <term>creative command</term> <note>original: "fiat"</note>—the desire of *Mars* in the fire, or in the fiery property—for the Saturnine property takes everything into its power and makes it corporeal.

39. Therefore, the metal of *Venus* is very closely related to gold because of her own property derived from the Liberty <note>The "Liberty" refers to the unmanifested, free divine state</note>, but *Mars* makes it too wrathful. Because it separates itself out of *Mars's* fire, it retains a great part of the property of *Mars* within it.

40. *Mars's* metal is iron, for he is the wrath in <term>Sulphur</term> in which the fire kindles and arises. His origin, along with the matter, is in the harshness of the desire. Copper...

### Chapter 4. The Signature of All Things.

[The spirit] separates itself in the generation out of *iron*, for it arises from the will of *Venus*, and they differ as body and soul. For *Mars* is the fire-soul of *Venus* and makes *Venus* corporeal; otherwise *Venus*, according to her own property, provides only water in the mortification <note>In alchemy, "mortification" refers to the process of breaking down a substance to its basic components.</note> in the salnitral flash <note>original: "salnitral Flagrat." This refers to a sudden, explosive ignition of spiritual energy, similar to the reaction of saltpeter (niter).</note>. For her fire is only a pleasant shining, a smile, or a love-fire, as she is alone and free of other mixtures. Therefore, she cannot produce any corporeal essence from her own power and ability that is hard and tough; she is only the mother to her child without a creaturely soul. <margin>Woman, Wife.</margin> *Mars* is her soul, and *Saturn* makes her body.

41. The spirit of *Sol* <note>The Sun, representing Gold.</note> may <term>tincture</term> <note>To "tincture" is to transform the inner nature of a substance, imbuing it with new qualities.</note> *Mars* and *Venus* and change them into the highest metallic perfection, namely into gold. This cannot be as easily achieved in silver, unless it is reduced into the <term>First Matter</term> <note>The original, undifferentiated substance from which all things are created.</note> where *Saturn*, *Mars*, and *Mercury* are together in the <term>Sulphur</term> <note>In Boehme's system, "Sulphur" represents the active, combustible principle of life and growth.</note>, and then it can be done. *Venus* receives its toughness from *Saturn* and its redness from *Mars* as the fire.

42. Now the desire of *Venus* is only eager and longing after *Sol*, as if after her first mother from whom she first sprang in her birth. For love comes forth originally from God, and it is the same in the external birth in this symbolic form. The desire of *Venus* goes into *Sol* (into the sun) and receives in its desire the property of the sun and shines from *Sol*. She has a very peculiar shining and luster above all the planets and stars, which she receives from her mother; and in her mother’s power consists her joy—namely, the pleasant, twinkling, smiling aspect she possesses. In her own property (as she is purely alone without the property of the other planets), she is a real daughter of the sun (understand this in the context of *Sulphur*, where all things are wrapped together). Therefore, she stands next under the sun as a child of the sun. This does not mean the sun generated that star, for she was created along with him; but in the *Sulphur* outside of the creation, merely in the process of generation, it is so, both in the heavenly and earthly being.

43. For God the Father generates *Love* through his heart; now the sun, by way of similarity, symbolizes his heart. It is a figure in the outward world according to the eternal heart of God, which gives strength and virtue to every life and essence.

44. And understand it correctly: all things proceed from the **Word** and Heart of God (which is the *Divine Sulphur*) in the birth of the Holy Trinity. They manifest themselves in and through the proceeded (or issued) essence, which is God’s Wisdom. They, in turn, eagerly force and press out of that issue, back toward his heart and power, and vehemently long after it—as Paul says, "all creatures groan and pant with us to be delivered from vanity" <note>A reference to Romans 8:22.</note>.

45. So also does the outward essence in the outward birth of metals, planets, stars, and creatures. Each thing longs after its center, namely after its first mother from whom it proceeded—which is the sun in *Sulphur*, for it is the tincture of all essences. Whatever the first desire (with the impression in *Saturn*) makes evil in the wrath of *Mars*, the sun turns back into good. Just as the divine Sun tinctures the anger or wrath of God, so that the wrathful property of God’s anger is changed into a joyfulness, so likewise the outward sun tinctures the outward *Sulphur* (specifically *Saturn* and *Mars*). This creates a pleasant temperature—a growth, springing, and blooming in all metals and creatures. Therefore, the sun is the center, which Reason <note>Boehme often uses "Reason" to refer to human logic that lacks spiritual insight.</note> will not believe; understand this as being in the planetary orb, and in all vegetables and animals.

He parallels this with the divine "Word" and Heart of God, suggesting that all creation longs to return to its source of Love.</summary>

# Chapter 5

## Concerning Sulphurous Death, and how the Dead Body is Revived and Restored to its Original Glory.

1. <image-desc>A large decorative woodcut initial 'A' featuring the letter within a square frame decorated with floral scrolls and alchemical symbols for Mercury, Sulphur, and Salt.</image-desc> All life and motion—along with understanding, reason, and the senses in both animals and plants—originate in *Sulphur*; that is, in nature’s desire and in the <term>Lubet’s</term> <note>original: "Lubet"; Boehme uses this term to describe a divine "delight," "longing," or "free will" that exists before the formal creation of nature.</note> desire for freedom.

2. Death and confinement arise from nature's desire, while openness and life arise from the desire for freedom. The desire for freedom "tinctures" <note>original: "tinctures"; in alchemy, to tincture is to infuse a substance with a new quality or spirit, transforming its essence.</note> the desire of dark nature, so that the <term>wrathful mother</term> <note>In Boehme’s philosophy, the "wrathful mother" refers to the harsh, contracting, and bitter forces of nature that exist without the softening light of God.</note> abandons her own rights and freely surrenders to the desire for freedom. Thus, life grows within death, for there is no life without light. However, if the light goes out within the essence of the *Sulphur*, it becomes an eternal death that no man can revive unless God moves Himself within the desire for delight in that same death. Death cannot receive life unless the primary desire—the free desire for delight—manifests itself within the desire for nature, where confinement and death are generated.

3. Therefore, when man died within the *Sulphur*, no one could have brought him back to life except for the free delight; that is, the desire for eternal life had to enter his <term>Phur</term> <note>original: "Phur"; Boehme breaks the word "Sulphur" into syllables, where "Phur" represents the energetic, fiery center or the "soul" of the substance.</note>—the birth-process of the nature of human property. It had to move the enclosed death—the center of nature—and give itself again into that center: into the soul-like property and the soul’s essentiality and physicality. And this is how it was accomplished.

4. We know that the true *Sulphur* is the source of all spirituality and physicality. Regarding its primary origin, where it is heavenly, it is the generation of the "Essence of all Essences." Everything that exists within eternity and time—everything it possesses or can achieve—lies within this birth. But regarding the kingdom of this world, it is earthly; it is a representation of the eternal. Within it, time and the created world exist, along with everything visible and invisible.

5. Now man—and indeed every form of life in the kingdom of this world—was created and generated from the outward *Sulphur*. Man was made from both the inward and outward *Sulphur*, while other creatures were made only from the outward. For man is an image and likeness of God, whereas other creatures are like a reflection, following the patterns in the internal generation of God’s wisdom—the expressed or procreated heavenly essence, according to both eternal principles.

<margin>Desire <note>original: "Lust," here meaning a deep-seated longing or will.</note></margin>
6. Man was created good and perfect from all three worlds as an image of the Deity in whom God dwelt. He was of the same essence as God relative to eternity and time in all three worlds. However, as a creature, he had a beginning and died through his own desire for delight regarding his heavenly and divine essence. The inward delight (<term>Lubet</term>) generated in the center—the fire where life stood in divine essence—is what ignited the essence of divine gentleness, which forms the joyful or angelic state. I say that this delight turned away from the inward desire for freedom and eternity and toward time—into the external birth and planetary properties. It departed from the pure divine element and into the four elements. Consequently, the inward divine essence, or inward physicality, no longer had a leader or life. This was death; for the soul’s fire, proceeding from the "Father’s property," turned away from the "Son’s property," <note>In Boehme's Trinitarian alchemy, the Father represents the raw power/fire of nature, and the Son represents the light/love that gives it life and form.</note> in which alone the divine life consists.

<summary>This page explains the alchemical and spiritual nature of Sulphur as the foundation of life, detailing how man’s fall resulted from a shift in desire from the eternal to the temporal. Boehme describes death as the loss of divine light within the "Sulphurous" essence and argues that only divine intervention in the "center of nature" can restore life.</summary>

<margin>* Or Immobility.</margin>
7. Thus the nature of the soul remained exposed, possessing only its will in the outward *Sulphur* <note>original: "Sulphur" — In Boehme’s alchemy, this represents the substance or "mother" of a thing's nature.</note>; its inward part disappeared and remained steadfast in eternal * immobility, as if in an eternal Nothing, where there was no longer any active influence or working power to accomplish anything.

8. Thus Man lived with his outward body purely and merely subject to Time; the precious gold of the heavenly substance, which permeated the outward body, had disappeared. Consequently, the outward body stood alone in the life of nature’s desire—that is, in the soul’s fiery nature. Understand this as the form and nature of *Mars* <note>Mars represents the fiery, forceful, or wrathful aspect of nature.</note>, which is the wrath of God—the wrath found in *Sulphur*—namely, the nature of God’s anger and the dark world. But seeing as the outward body was created out of Time, then Time—meaning the influence of the stars and the four elements—immediately gained dominion over him. The divine nature, which is the desire of the Deity (which once ruled and permeated Time, so that there was a holy life in the creature beyond Time), had vanished. Its own unique love in the divine desire was turned to water, and it became blind and dead to the will and desire of God; thus, the soul must now sustain itself with the light of the sun.

<margin>y Or he would die.</margin>
9. But since Time has a beginning and an end, and because the will and desire have surrendered themselves to this temporal leader, the dominion of Time destroys its own constructed spirit; thus, the body also dies and passes away. This is what God told *Adam: That he should not eat of the Tree, or Plant, of the Knowledge of Good and Evil, which contains both properties,* ^y lest he die. As it turned out, he died in the *Sulphur*—the *Sul* in the Kingdom of God—which is the <term>Lubet</term> <note>original: "Lubet" — A term used by Boehme to describe the divine longing, delight, or the "free will" of God.</note> of divine liberty, from which the light of God shines and in which the divine love (the love-fire) burns. This part disappeared and withdrew from him.

10. Now there was no remedy for him, unless God’s desire entered again into his dead *Sulphur*—that is, into his *Sul* which was dead—meaning into the dead or mortified essence, and enkindled it once more with the fire of love. This occurred in Christ. There, the heavenly body, in which God’s light shines, arose again. But for this to be achieved, the love-desire must again enter into the desire of the ignited anger and quench and overcome that anger with love. The divine water must enter again into the soul’s burning fire and quench the wrathful death in the astringent <term>Fiat</term> <note>original: "Fiat" — Latin for "let it be done," referring to God's creative command or the formative power in nature.</note>—the desire for nature—so that the love-desire, which longs for God, might be enkindled in the soul once more.

<margin>z Salvation.</margin>
<margin>a An upright, full, and unfeigned desire.</margin>
11. For man’s ^z happiness consists in this: that he has within him a ^a true desire for God. For out of that desire, love springs forth; that is, when the desire receives the gentleness of God into itself, the desire then plunges itself into that gentleness and becomes substantial. This is the heavenly or divine essence, or corporality; and within it, the soul’s spirit (which lay imprisoned in anger and death) rises again in the love of God. For love permeates the death and darkness so that it is once more capable of receiving the divine sunshine.

<margin>b Or therein.</margin>
<margin>c Leader or controller.</margin>
<margin>d In one or in unity.</margin>
12. And as this is done in man, it is likewise done in the transformation of metals: the *Sulphur* is locked up in *Saturn* <note>Saturn in alchemy represents lead, contraction, and the "death" or "prison" of the spirit of the metal.</note>—that is, in death—and yet there is no true death, but a vegetative life; and the outward *Mercury* is the life ^b of it. Now, if the metallic body is to reach the highest perfection, it must die to its external ^c ruler—the elements—and return to such a *Sulphur* as it was when it did not yet have the four elements upon it, but existed only in the single element ^d in unity.

13. But now, no one can restore it to such a body except the one who created it. He who gave it the four elements is the only one who can take them away; and he who first made it physical must bring it back to himself and transform it within himself into another body. This is the *Sulphur* which has *Mercurius* as its chief <term>Faber</term> <note>original: "Faber" — Latin for "craftsman" or "smith"; here, the creative force that works within the substance.</note> within itself. He must again take it out of dark *Saturn’s* bowels through the *Fiat* and introduce it into his own...

## Process

14. The body lies shut up in an undervalued form in *Saturn*—not entirely in *Saturn's* property, but in a dark color, marked by *Mercury* its father and *Sol* its mother, clothed in *Saturn*, and made manifest with the life of *Mars*. However, its mother is not outwardly visible or known on it, unless its <term>Faber</term> <note>original: "Faber"; Latin for "craftsman" or "maker." In this context, it refers to the internal creative force or "archeus" that shapes the substance.</note> becomes enraged by its own iniquity. This cannot happen unless an <term>Alienate</term> <note>A foreign or external substance added to the mixture.</note> is applied, by which its <term>Propriate</term> <note>Its own inherent nature or specific property.</note> is enraged. Then—if his anger is set into a fire or fury—he becomes extremely hungry and thirsty, yet can find no refreshment in himself. He then seizes upon the <term>Faber</term> who made him and fights against his creator, just as a wicked earthly man does against God, until he devours and consumes himself—much like a fiery, deadly poison consumes the body—unless you remedy, stop, and soothe its hunger. Yet there is no one who can still this horrible hunger but God Himself, who made him; and if He does not assist in due time, the hunger in that wrath consumes the body and casts it into eternal darkness.

<margin>' Or in divine love.</margin>
15. This hunger desires nothing but the mercy of God, so that it might be freed from the anguish of hell. But it cannot obtain this of itself, for it is shut up in the anger of God; and its dear mother, who nursed it in the beginning, is also shut up in death. But if God shows His grace and gives it His love again, then the anger is overwhelmed ' by the love; and this is a <term>Flagrat</term> <note>A "flash" or "burst" of light and joy; a key term in Boehme’s philosophy representing the moment of transformation or spiritual ignition.</note> of great joy. For it tastes the sweetness of its dear mother again, and then it knows full well that it has been vile and wicked; it repents of its iniquity and seeks to turn and mortify the old *Adam* <note>The "old Adam" refers to the sinful, fallen nature of humanity that must be overcome.</note> and cast it away.

<margin>g Or upon the love of God. h Depart.</margin>
16. So the artist immediately takes him away—along with the old *Adam*—from the strange anger and lays him in a soft bed, for the old *Adam* is sick and will die. Then his own <term>Faber</term> within the old *Adam* is g centered upon the love of God, which destroyed the anger; it will create a young child and rejoices in that child. The old *Adam* grows sick and weak, becoming completely dark and swarthy, and dies; and the four elements h depart from him with their colors. Thus the <term>Faber</term> even gives him leave to go, and continually labors on the new body which shall arise from death. No one sees his labor, for he works in the dark.

<margin>i Labour.</margin>
17. But the artist takes no concern for the i work, but gives the <term>Faber</term> his own food, until he sees a growing life appear in that dark death, with a new color emerging out of the blackness. Then, when the new man is ready, the artist comes and brings the soul, giving it to the <term>Faber</term>. At this, the <term>Faber</term> is startled that another life comes into him; he puts the soul into the new body, and it moves inwardly within the anger. Thus the new man arises from death in great power and glory; he bruises the head of the old serpent in the anger of God and passes through the anger, and the anger can do him no harm at all.

## The Sixth Chapter.

### *How Water and Oil are generated, the Difference between Water and Oil, and the Nature of Vegetable Life and Growth.*

1. <image-desc>Decorative initial capital letter 'A' inside an ornate square frame with floral and leaf motifs.</image-desc> All life, growth, and instigation <note>original: "instigation," meaning the inner driving force or impulse</note> consist of two things: namely, in the *Lubet* <note>original: "Lubet," from the Latin *libitum* or German *Lust*, meaning a free inclination, delightful longing, or pleasant will</note> and in the Desire. The Lubet is a free will, and is like a "nothing" in comparison to nature; but the Desire is like a hunger. In the Desire arises the moving spirit (the natural spirit), and in the Lubet arises the supernatural spirit—which nevertheless belongs to <margin>Of or belonging to Nature.</margin> nature, yet not from its own property, but from the property of the Desire.

2. The Desire is the instigation of the essence—a hunger—and the Lubet is that hunger’s <margin>Being, substance, or food.</margin> essence, which it takes into itself. For the Desire is only a hungry will, and it is the natural spirit in its various forms; but the Lubet comes from the Liberty <note>Boehme uses "Liberty" to describe the absolute freedom of the divine state before it manifests as nature</note>. God is without desire regarding His own essence, in as much as He is called God; for He needs nothing. All is His, and He Himself is all.

3. But He has a Lubet-will, and He Himself is the will to manifest Himself in the Lubet. Yet in the Lubet—which is free and without affection—no manifestation can be achieved, for it lacks desire. It is as if it were nothing in respect to nature, and yet it is everything. However, it is not everything according to the Desire (that is, according to nature), but according to the *satisfying* of nature. It is the fulfillment of the hungry Desire of nature; it freely and willingly gives itself into the hunger of nature. For it is a spirit without essence or desire, completely free as a "nothing"; but the Desire makes it essential <note>original: "essential," meaning the Desire gives the Lubet substance or materializes it</note> within itself. This happens according to two properties: one according to the eternal Liberty, which is free from the source <note>original: "Source" or *Qual*, meaning a state of tension or suffering</note>; and the other according to the Desire, which gives a vegetative life—that is, a growing or a bringing forth of itself.

4. The free essence exists and provides an oil, and the property of the Desire provides the life of that oil. The oil is a light, and the property of the Desire gives the essence to that light—the fiery property—so that the light shines, as can be seen in fire and light. The free Lubet remains a free will in itself, but it gives its meekness—a free resignation—into the Desire, so that it gains substance and luster. Its will is only good; it has no other desire than to be good, meek, and pleasant. No other possibility exists within it; for <margin>Understand the free will.</margin> it is like a "nothing" in which no disturbance or painful source can exist; it is meekness itself.

5. But since it cannot truly be "nothing" (because it is the cause and beginning of the Desire), it gives itself freely, just as sunshine freely gives itself to every object. The Desire conceives [or takes] this free Lubet—the luster or shining of the abyss of eternity—into itself, and turns it into essence according to its own property. Whatever property exists in the Desire, an equal amount of essence is created. We must consider that when the free Lubet gives itself into the hunger of the Desire, the Desire creates from the property of the Lubet a likeness of the Liberty. This likeness is as if it were nothing, yet it exists; this is Water and Oil.

6. Because the Desire (the hunger) is filled with the free Lubet, it also turns its own property into essence within the essence of the Liberty. Its essence is water, and the essence of the free Lubet is an oil. Thus, a two-fold property arises in a single spirit: a fiery property according to the property of the Desire, and a joyful or shining property according to the Liberty.

# Signatura Rerum: Chapter 6

<margin>Provides, produces, or makes.</margin>
7. The fiery nature gives of its essence—that is, in its "Water"—a sharpness from the harsh *Desire*, which is salt-like or a Salt. From the fiery anguish, it produces a Brimstone. From these, in the *Impression* <note>The "Impression" refers to the process by which spiritual forces contract or "press" themselves into physical matter.</note> and creation of the world, stones, earth, and metals were made. So also were the elements and stars, all according to the forms within the *Desire*. The oily property provides its gentleness—namely, a Love-Lubet <note>original: *Love-Lubet*; Jacob Böhme’s term for a divine, joyful inclination or delight</note>—in which the fiery nature is shaped by the *Desire* to create physical form. This oily property gives itself out in its gentleness and creates vegetable life—a springing and growing within the fiery Impression. In this process, the Fire must provide its essence and drive—namely, the vehement stinging <margin>Or raging sting.</margin> in the attraction of the Desire. This is the "Separator" within physical form: the distinguisher, the carver, and the cause of essence and variety.

8. Philosophers have called this form *Mercurius* <note>Mercury, considered in alchemy as the principle of volatility, motion, and life-force.</note>, from the anxious, driving sphere that is the cause of all life and motion, acting as a craftsman within the oily and watery properties.

9. Thus we must search and find out the great *Mystery*: how an Oil, Brimstone, and Salt exist in every thing and how they arise. For God has made all things out of Nothing, and that same "Nothing" is Himself—namely, a Love-Lubet dwelling in itself, in which there is no outside influence. However, this Love-Lubet would not be manifested if it remained as one in a stillness without essence. There would be no joy or movement in it, but only an eternal stillness.

<margin>Or when.</margin>
10. But since He introduces Himself into "Essence" through the Desire, His eternal stillness becomes an essence and a working power. This happens with two properties: first, in an Oil, in which the working power is a good spirit according to the nature of the Love-Lubet. This resists the wrath of the Desire found in the Brimstone, Salt, and poisonous *Mercury*. It appeases and heals Mercury's poisonous hunger with pleasant gentleness. Whatever *Mercury* destroys with the raging wheel <margin>Or furious wheel.</margin> of his own property, the delight of the Love-Oil heals again. Thus, there is Good and Evil in every life; and yet, there is no "Evil" in anything unless the Good—the Love-Oil—starves in its own delight. This happens when the hunger of the Desire contracts and hardens itself.

11. That is, if the Hunger-Spirit impresses itself too much into its own forms (longing for or imagining only itself) and hungers too eagerly for its own manifestation, it cannot receive the free Lubet <note>Free Lubet: The unconstrained divine joy or "Nothing" that exists before desire.</note> which would appease its hunger. Nature's property must be sincerely bent and inclined toward the property of the free Lubet—toward God’s Love-Essence—and direct its hunger wholly after Love. Then the hunger receives Love into itself and makes it substantial within itself. It is no longer a famished, dark hunger that rages and raves like a poisonous *Mercury*. Instead, the hunger becomes a Love-Desire, which is called "God’s Nature." The hungry, fiery [Desire] is called "God’s Anger." In outward nature it is called a Fire, but in the property of the inward world (where the Desire acts with the power of the free Lubet), this Desire is called the Divine Desire. In this, the fiery Love burns and joyfulness proceeds. The free Lubet gives itself into the harsh Desire specifically so that it may bring forth a fiery Love—a joyfulness—which could not exist in the still Lubet. For where there is stillness, there is no joy or motion.

12. Now the free Lubet—God's property—manifests itself through the fiery property. The fiery property then turns the essence of the free Lubet (the Oil that arises from the contraction of the Desire) into a Light or luster. The harsh Desire provides the anxious, darting flash—a sulfurous spirit—and the gentleness of the Oil gives its Love into it. This dispels the darkness that had been drawn in and manifests the eternal liberty—the "Nothing"—and this is now the act of Seeing.

13. For when the Fire-Splendor tastes the sweetness of the Light, the Fire’s Desire reaches after that gentleness. The gentleness of the free Lubet is like a "Nothing," completely incomprehensible. Now the hunger of the Desire grasps its own essence...

### Chap. 6. The Signature of all Things.

...and devours it, making it into nothing. This is the Darkness, which is the essence of Hunger; this fiery Hunger devours through the property of the Light, or the free **Lubet** <note>original: "free Lubet"; Boehme’s term for the divine "pleasure" or "longing"—a spontaneous, unconditioned will toward manifestation.</note>. As we see, as soon as the Light shines, it deprives the Darkness of its power. Therefore, God is a Lord over all beings, for he is the eternal Power and Light. We see a likeness of this in the Sun, which is the lord of the darkness and of all essences, ruling whatever grows, lives, and moves in this world.

14. Furthermore, we must consider the various **Salts**—how they arise in the Origin and separate into many properties. In the origin of the Impression—that is, in the **Verbum Fiat** <term>Verbum Fiat: Latin for "Let it be done," referring to the creative word of God in Genesis.</term>—a two-fold Salt arises. The first is spiritual and provides the sharpness in the essence of the free **Lubet**; it is a severing or a sharpness of powers. The other Salt is the sharpness of the **Impression** <note>In Boehme’s system, "Impression" refers to the process of spiritual forces contracting or solidifying into material form.</note>, according to the property of the harsh austerity, which is the anguish in the Impression; that is **Brimstone** <note>original: "Brimstone"; Sulfur.</note>, and its essential property is Water.

15. The Water is the inanimate, mortal property of the Salt. The sulfurous property, which comes from the anguish, is the property of the "living" Salt; for it contains the stimulus of motion—namely, the **Mercury**—within it, which forms the shape of Life. And yet the **Brimstone** is not the Salt itself, but it is the anguish within the Impression, which also becomes corporeal.

16. The Salt is the sharpness in **Brimstone** regarding its contraction. Salt causes the anguish to become corporeal; and so Salt dwells in the **Brimstone** and is the **Brimstone's** sharpness. It preserves the **Brimstone** in its corporeal essence, as well as the Spirit of the **Brimstone**, so that it does not fall to dust. The Salt imprints the powers of the anguish, and the imprinted life is the **Mercurial Life**. This is the life of the anguish—that is, of the **Brimstone**—and it separates the **Materia** <note>original: "Materia"; Matter or substance.</note> according to the forms of **Nature**. It also separates the matter of the free **Lubet** into two essences: first into a watery and oily essence, and then into a corporeal one.

17. The corporeal is two-fold, according to both the Darkness and the Light. According to the property of the harsh Desire, it creates a sandy or stony nature within the watery property, which is the origin of stones; understand this as coming out of the sulfurous property—that is, out of the **Brimstone’s** water.

<margin>According to, or after.</margin>
<margin>Or out of.</margin>
<margin>Inanimate or "Dumb."</margin>
18. The other property, regarding the mortification <note>In alchemy, "mortification" refers to the "death" or transformation of a substance into a new state.</note> in the **salnitral Flagrat** <term>salnitral flagrat: Boehme’s term for a sudden, explosive flash of natural force—like saltpeter—that marks the transition from dark "anguish" into light or life.</term>, is common running water. The other corporeal water is the metallic body from the free **Lubet’s** property in the imprinted form. From the watery property (where the **Brimstone** is in the water), it produces trees, herbs, and everything that grows in the earthly property—that is, in the mortified or dead substantiality, which nevertheless has a life without senses, namely, a **vegetative** life.

19. The oily property is also two-fold according to the Impression. One part strives back toward Liberty to be free from the wrath of the Impression; this is the good spirit, the Light in the Oil. The other part yields itself to the anguish of the **Brimstone** and remains in the corporality. It unites and applies itself to each thing according to that thing's Salt-property: in a fiery salt, it is fiery; in a bitter salt, it is bitter; in a contracting salt, it is contracting, and so on.

20. The first property, according to the Light, is sweet in all things. The other property of the Oil follows the form—that is, the taste of the thing—whether it be sweet, sour, contracting, sharp, bitter, or otherwise, as is found in herbs. In some, it is a bitter poison, while in others, it is a healing for that poison. But if the poisonous property is broken by **Mercury** in the **Oil of Gentleness**, then the love of the Light also inclines itself into the Oil; for the origin of both is from one Will, though it is altered in the Impression. This is like how the Devil, when he was an Angel, changed himself into a poisonous, devilish property, and how **Adam** changed from a heavenly to an earthly property.
