# Signatura Rerum: Chapter 6

21. Whatever grows, lives, and moves in this world consists of **Sulphur**, and **Mercury** is the life within that **Sulphur**. **Salt** is the physical existence produced by **Mercury’s** hunger, even though bodies take many forms. According to the specific property of the sulphur <note>original: brimstone</note> and salt, so too is the nature of the internal **Oil**, which arises throughout that power; for the **Oil** creates the potency <note>original: virtual influence</note> in every thing. Within the **Oil** of the physical impression—that is, the visible oil—exists another **Oil**: the spiritual one, which gives us Light. However, this spiritual oil belongs to a different principle; it accepts no other source into itself except the longing <note>original: lubet</note> of Love. It is divine essentiality. Therefore, God’s own essence is near to all things, but not essentially *within* all things. It exists in a different principle, yet it inclines itself toward all things. As long as a thing has any bit of the divine property within it, it receives virtue from that divine property, whether it is a vegetable or an animal. For there are herbs, trees, and creatures to be found in which something of the divine power is hidden. In magical healing, this power can be used to resist "false magic"—the corrupted, evil **Oil**—and change it back into a good **Oil**.

22. Every sharpness of taste is **Salt**, whatever it may be in this world, without exception. All smells proceed from **Sulphur** <note>original: brimstone</note>, and **Mercury** is the "distinguisher" in all motion or feeling, whether in smell, power, or taste. By "my **Mercury**," I mean the sphere where all essences are born, as mentioned before. I do not mean a dead, chemical mercury, but a living one—the strongest kind, according to the property of the "dry poison," etc.

<margin>If he can but obtain it.</margin>
23. Now, it is necessary for the artist and physician to understand these things; otherwise, he cannot cure any sickness or disease unless he hits upon the cure by sheer chance. He must know how the **Oil** in the body has been poisoned, what kind of "hunger" **Mercury** feels during the sickness, and what it hungers for. For if the physician can obtain the **Salt** that matches **Mercury's** hunger—the specific property it desires—along with the kind of **Oil** it craves, then the sickness is over very quickly. This is because he turns the **Oil** back toward the property of the Love of the Light, at which point life begins to shine brightly once more.

24. For every disease in the body is nothing other than a corruption or poisoning of the **Oil** from which the Life-Light burns or shines. When the Light of life shines or burns clearly in the **Oil**, it expels and drives away all poisonous influences and operations, just as the day expels the night.

<margin>Sting.</margin>
25. If the **Oil** from which life burns becomes infected or inflamed by a poisonous **Mercury** or **Salt**—whether from the influence of the stars <note>original: constellation</note> or from the salt in food (that is, from a contrary source)—a loathing <note>original: nauseous detestation</note> arises in the **Oil**. The **Oil** attempts to vomit this poison out, and **Mercury** assists in this. Then, **Mercury** anxiously troubles and exhausts itself within the sulphurous fire more and more, continually laboring to drive out the abomination. However, in this harsh effort, it only further inflames itself, kindling its own inward form. Consequently, the **Oil** grows darker and more poisonous, until at last it becomes entirely watery and earthy. Then the Light, and also the Fire, is extinguished. **Mercury**, along with the sulphurous spirit, departs from the body just as a candle is put out. Thus, **Mercury** passes out with the sulphurous spirit in the baneful steam <note>original: sting</note> of death, until it is also starved. For a time, it may sustain itself in the astral body <note>original: sidereal body</note> which passes along with it; but when **Mercury** has consumed and starved its property within the spirit of the great world, then the temporary life is wholly gone. As soon as the light of the vital **Oil** goes out, the elemental body falls into putrefaction—returning to the *Fiat* <note>The creative/destructive word of power</note> from which it first came to be. Then, time ends for that creature; this is death, dying, or departure. From that state, there is no deliverance or return unless the heavenly, divine **Mercury** moves within him once more. This cannot happen unless there was a good property of the **Oil** in him—one derived from the divine essentiality. The Light only rekindles itself in that specific property which is capable of receiving the divine essence.

<summary>Boehme explains the alchemical trinity of Sulphur, Mercury, and Salt as the foundation of life and health, defining disease as the poisoning of the "Oil" of life. He describes the process of death as the extinguishing of this internal Light and the departure of the spiritual essences from the physical body.</summary>

26. For the divine substance <note>original: "Essentiality"</note>, or this heavenly *Mercury*, transforms the lifeless oil once again into its own nature and becomes its life. The outward *Mercury*, which previously governed life, does not return; it served only for a time as a mirror of the Eternal. Instead, it is changed into another source; for once it is extinguished <note>original: "suffocated"</note>, it returns to the hidden realm <note>original: "the Mystery"</note> from which it first originated during the creation of the world, and the body also returns to that same hidden realm.

27. Thus it remains, waiting for another movement of the Deity—specifically, a "Separating," where the evil (which contained death) shall be separated from the good. Then the *Verbum Fiat* <note>Latin: "The Word: Let it be done," referring to the creative command of God</note> shall restore and bring forth everything that fell into death’s power.

<margin>Or taken from him.</margin>
28. The physician should know that the highest "Tincture" <note>a potent spiritual or medicinal essence</note> lies within the strongest *Mercury*, which is the most poisonous. However, it is not found in *Mercury's* own raw state, which must be broken or transformed. In its own natural state, even from its very center, it is a restless and poisonous life. But it contains another property within it: an oil derived from the Light, which gives it such strength and potency, acting as its food and preservation. If this oil can be separated from it, it becomes a transformative power capable of igniting all "obscured" lives—meaning all diseases and sicknesses. For within this oil lies the joyful life; it is a "hunger" after life, seeking to ignite what is weak and lift it up high.

<margin>Or Loathsomeness.</margin>
29. In a toad, viper, or adder, or similar poisonous beasts, worms, or insects, the highest Tincture is to be found, provided they are reduced to an oily substance and the "wrath" of *Mercury* is separated from them. For all life, both external and internal, consists of "poison" and light. We understand that the wrath and "anger-fire" of God is the actual cause of divine joyfulness; we should recognize the same principle in the external world. Any life that lacks this "poisonous" *Mercury* is dead <note>original: "mort"</note>, loathsome, and considered as nothing.

30. Now, *Mercury* is the igniter of the fire, and every moving life consists of fire. Even though some creatures live in the water, fire is still their life—specifically the "poison-gall" <note>the bitter, active principle in the body</note> where *Mercury* manages the life. But the water in the gall is a poison that hides an oil, and the life in *Mercury* burns and shines within that oil. Here is a comparison: if a creature possesses a strong, poisonous *Mercury* of a dry quality, that creature is strong, bold, courageous, and powerful because it also contains a clear oil. The fiery property of the *Mercury* consumes the watery parts; if its "fat" (oil) is ignited, it yields a clear light. This would be even more effective if the watery property were separated from the oily <note>original: "oleous"</note> part.

# The Seventh Chapter.

## *How Adam in Paradise, and how Lucifer was a fair Angel, and how they were corrupted and spoiled through Imagination and Pride.*

### *Process.*

1. WE will provide an opportunity for reflection to the earnest researcher and seeker. If he grasps our meaning, he shall indeed be able to find the noble Philosopher’s Stone—but only if he is chosen for it by God and if his own life aligns with the heavenly *Mercury*. Otherwise, we will remain a mystery to him. We will represent this to him through comparisons, in the most obvious and yet most mystical manner.

2. When Adam was created in Paradise, the heavenly *Mercury* guided him. His life burned in a pure oil; therefore his eyes and his understanding were heavenly.

Adam surpassed Nature, for his Light shone in the <term>Oil</term> <note>original: "Oyle"; in Böhme's alchemy, "Oil" represents the gentle, spiritual essence or fuel of the soul's light.</note> of the <term>divine Essentiality</term>; the external watery property was not manifest in his <term>Oil</term>. He was <term>*iliastrich*</term> <note>original: "iliastrich"; a term from Paracelsus meaning "angelic" or "pertaining to the celestial matter."</note>, that is, angelical, and became in the Fall <term>*cogastrish*</term> <note>original: "cogastrish"; a term from Paracelsus referring to the corrupted, mortal, or "earth-born" nature.</note>. This means the watery nature of the mortal property became manifest in his <term>Oil</term> and penetrated it, so that the <term>Mercury</term> <note>original: "Mercury"; the active, driving spirit or life-force within a being.</note> in him became an anxious poison, which before—in his <term>Oil</term>—was an exaltation of joyfulness.

3. For the salnitral <term>Flagrat</term> <note>original: "salnitral Flagrat"; a sudden, explosive flash of energy likened to the ignition of saltpeter.</note> in the contraction <note>original: "Impression"</note> of the coldness—namely, according to the <term>Saturnine Property</term> <note>The qualities associated with the planet Saturn: cold, dark, hard, and restrictive.</note>—was thereby elevated and gained dominion as a cold poison. This poison arises in the contraction of death, from which darkness was generated in the <term>Oil</term>, and *Adam* died to the divine Light. The Devil <sup>a</sup> persuaded him to do this <sup>b</sup> by the Serpent, that is, by the essence and property of the Serpent; for the Kingdom of Wrath, and also the outward kingdom, was manifest in the Serpent. It was more subtle than any beast of the field, and *Eve* desired this subtlety; for the Serpent persuaded her that her eyes should be opened, and she should be as God, knowing Good and Evil.

4. This was also the Will of the Devil: that he would know Evil. In the kindling of this knowledge in <term>Mercury</term>, he became corrupt and dark; for he entered with his imagination—according to his condition, knowledge, and desire—into the fiery <term>Byss</term> <note>original: "Byss"; from the Greek *abyssos*, referring here to the "groundless" or bottomless source of existence.</note>. And *Adam*, according to his knowledge and desire, went into the cold <term>Byss</term>, into the contraction, into the procreated watery property in the <term>Salniter</term>, where both kingdoms stand separated. He desired to prove and taste the watery <term>Mercury</term>, in which is the mortal poison; and *Lucifer* desired the fiery <term>Mercury</term>, which gives strength and might. From this his pride arose—namely, out of the fiery <term>Mercury</term>. But both—*Lucifer* and also *Adam*—lost the <term>Oil</term> of the meekness of the <term>divine Essentiality</term>.

5. Now we are to consider the Serpent, which deceived *Adam* with its craft; what it was, and what its subtlety was that *Adam* and *Eve* imagined; why they ate of the forbidden tree which was Evil and Good, and how they ate death by doing so; and what their salvation and restoration is, naturally and properly; what Evil and Good are, what the property of eternal life is, and then what the property of eternal death is; and finally, what the cure is by which the sickness introduced by *Adam*, and its death, may be healed and restored both to temporal and eternal life.

7. The Devil was a fair angel, the Serpent a subtle beast, and Man the likeness of the Deity. Now all three were <sup>d</sup> corrupted by imagination and pride, and received the curse of God for their false lust and cunning.

<margin>
e Or in.
f Or outwards.

8. Everything that is eternal proceeds originally from one Ground, such as angels and souls; but the Serpent is not out of the eternal Ground, but out of the Beginning <note>Referring to the beginning of time and the physical manifestation of the world.</note>, as we have previously explained. <sup>e</sup> With the kindling of the fire in the salnitral <term>Flagrat</term>, two kingdoms separate: namely, Eternity and Time. Eternity dwells in Time, yet only in itself; yet it is as near to Time as fire and light are to one another, which exist together and yet make two distinct kingdoms; or as darkness and light dwell in each other, and the one is not the other. We must consider the same regarding the initial poisonous <term>Mercury</term> in the Devil, in Man, and also in the Serpent: how an <term>Oil</term> corrupts, and yet the Essence or Being of God is not corrupted by this at all, but enters into itself—namely, into the "Nothing." The creaturely <term>Mercury</term>—which arises or is born with the beginning of the creature within the creature—goes <sup>f</sup> out of itself; that is, out of the eternal into Time, namely, into the "Beginning" of the creature. It desires its own self—the Beginning—and wants to be its own, or possess a selfish property. It forsakes the Eternity, in which it should be wholly contained and resigned with its desire, bringing its hunger into that Eternity; if it did so, its poison-source would not be manifest.

# Chap. 7. The Signature of all Things.

9. For whatever hungers for the eternal Nothing—that is, for the quiet, humble Freedom of God—is not visible to itself, but is visible in that still Freedom, which is God. For as the hunger is, so also is the essence within that hunger; every hunger or desire creates an essence for itself according to the nature of that hunger or desire.

10. In this way, the Devil creates darkness within himself; for he directed his desire into himself—into the core nature of desire—and abandoned Eternity (the "Nothing"), which is the <term>Lubet</term> <note>original: "Lubet of Love"; this refers to a divine inclination, longing, or peaceful pleasure</note> of Love. Thus, he ignited himself in his own poisonous *Mercury* <note>In Boehme’s thought, "Mercury" refers to the active, moving spirit or "life-force" within nature</note>—the forces that create life within him—and became an anxious source of fire in the darkness. He became like wood burned into a coal that only glows but has no true light, oil, or water remaining in it. That is what happened to him. Now, within his own nature—in the forms of his life—nothing grows but a stinging, envious quality, where one form hates and harms the others, even though they give birth to each other.

<margin>g Or set his desire upon the anger.</margin>
11. The Serpent was similar, though not because of its own ambitious pride. Rather, when God said, "Let all sorts of beasts come forth, each according to its kind," animals emerged from every quality of nature that was revealed during the Separation when God moved toward Creation. Because the Devil wanted to rule over God’s love and humility, he ^g directed his desire into the anger—into the harsh power where the "poison-life" begins. This was the <term>Fiat</term> <note>Latin: "let it be done"; the creative command of God</note> of the wrathful quality, and from this form came vipers, serpents, toads, and other venomous worms. It is not that the Devil created them—he cannot do that—but rather, as the desire existed in the impression of the <term>Fiat</term>, so the creature was formed in both evil and good.

<margin>h Original text: Into himself. i Out of itself.</margin>
12. For in the impression of the <term>Fiat</term>—in the origin of the outward *Mercury* (the life that is self-aware)—there occurred the Separation, where God and the World are distinguished: God ^h inwardly and the world ^i outwardly, like a reflection of the Abyss or a mirror of eternity. It was there that the inward wrath (the reason God is called an "angry, jealous God" and a "consuming fire") manifested itself externally in physical forms, as a likeness of the inner birth at the center. Just as the eternal <term>Lubet</term>, which is God himself, awakens the desire for eternal manifestation and gives itself into that desire, turning the wrath of desire into joy.

<margin>k Or wit, or subtlety. l Quickest or keenest.</margin>
13. This is also true of the Serpent’s ^k craft: the highest *Mercury* contains the sharpest proof of all things. The more poisonous a thing is, the more sharply it tests other things; for the ^l sharpest taste and smell exist within the great poison—that is, in a state of dying.

<margin>m Or begets itself. n Or form, or give substance to. o Affords, yields, or produces.</margin>
14. The eternal light is ^m generated out of the Father’s sharpness, so that it achieves its shine. It then flows with its own source through that sharpness—out of the source of anguish and back into freedom, into the "Nothing." There, because of the fire’s source and nature, the light also becomes a desire: the desire of divine love and joy. In this desire, *Mercurius* <note>The Eternal Word or divine understanding</note> is rightly understood and named. This outflow from the fire (referring to the eternal, magical, spiritual fire) is a procreation of the Word of power, colors, and virtue. This desire of the same *Mercury* (or Word) also ^n shapes that power into its own desire and makes it tangible. Then time is manifested with its <margin>Or works and effects.</margin> wonders in eternity.

24. In this manner also is the process of the wise men with the precious stone. There is no better way to understand this than to consider how the eternal Word—namely, the heavenly divine *Mercury* in divine power—became man and has slain death and the anger in man. That is, He changed the *Mercury* into divine joyfulness, whereby the human *Mercury* (which previously lay shut up in God’s anger, the source of death) now, with its newly kindled desire, which is called faith in the Holy Spirit, attracts divine essentiality—namely, Christ’s body—to itself. It sets itself in divine power and light above the anger of God and the poison of the serpent, and bruises the head of the anger—namely, the poison of death—with the life of divine joyfulness. That is, the anger was the master, but in the light, it became a servant, which must now be a cause of joyfulness, as is most plainly and clearly made known and shown to us in the life of *Mercury*.

### Signatura Rerum: Chapter 7

26. In the sweet Name, *Jesus Christ*, the entire process is contained—what the New Birth is, and how it moves out of death into life. This is very clearly understood in the "Language of Nature" <note>original: "Language of Nature"; the idea that the sounds and structures of words reveal the inner essence of the things they name</note>: For the name *Jesus* is the property of the free *Lubet* <note>original: "Lubet"; from the Latin *lubitus*, meaning a free desire, longing, or divine will</note> of eternity, which yields itself into the pregnant center—namely, into the Father’s property—and shapes itself in that center (in the Father's Fire) into a Word of eternal power.

27. Understand this: the Father—namely, the Father’s fiery forms—shapes this divine voice substantially within Himself in the desire of liberty. That is, the Father’s fiery property turns itself into a *Mercury* <note>In Böhme’s alchemy, "Mercury" represents the principle of motion, sound, and the life-force</note> of joyfulness within the divine essence of eternal love. For the Father’s property is the source of fire, and the Son’s property (the eternal *Lubet*) is the source of love. And yet, there would be no desire for love if the Father’s fire did not kindle it and make it move—that is, make it desirous; for from the fire arises the *desire*.

28. The Father of all essences generates this holy desire through His fire-source, which is now His heart of love; this gives the fire its shining luster and splendor. It is there that the "wrath" in the fire's property dies from eternity to eternity and is transformed into a love-desire.

<margin>A champion who breaks through irresistibly.</margin>
<margin>Or void of all source-properties.</margin>
29. Observe it this way: the property of the free *Lubet* is here called *Christ* within the property of the fire. In the Language of Nature, this signifies a potent champion who deprives "wrath" of its power; a shining of light in the darkness; a transmutation where the love-desire rules over the fire-desire (namely, over wrath), and light rules over darkness. Here, the "seed of the woman" (meaning the free *Lubet*, which contains no harsh source-property) bruises the head of the wrath of eternal nature—that is, of eternal desire. For the fire’s property is rightly called the "head," as it is the cause of eternal life; and the liberty (the free *Lubet*, or the "nothingness") is rightly called the "woman," for within that liberty, which is free of all agonizing sources, the birth of the Holy Trinity of the Deity consists.

<margin>Or becomes.</margin>
30. Now, the fire gives life, and the free *Lubet* provides the essence for that life. In this essence is the birth where the Father (the eternal ground) generates His essence—namely, His heart—out of the abyss within Himself into a *Byss* <note>original: "Byfs"; Böhme uses "Abyss" for the bottomless void and "Byss" or "Ground" for the established foundation of reality</note>. The Son is the Father’s *Byss*. Thus, the Father remains in Himself regarding His own property: the abyss of eternal nature. And the Son remains in the Father: the ground of the power and the kingdom of joy. You can see a resemblance of this in fire and light. In this way, the Son tinctures <note>original: "tinctures"; an alchemical term meaning to infuse, transform, or ennoble a substance</note> the Father with liberty (with the nothingness), and the Father tinctures the Son (the nothingness) so that there is an eternal life within it—no longer a "nothing," but a resonance or voice of the manifestation of eternity.

<margin>Body.</margin>
<margin>Or awakening, or stirring itself up.</margin>
<margin>Set or placed.</margin>
<margin>Or victoriously triumphed over.</margin>
31. Therefore, dear philosophers, observe the ground of how you should "tincture." Do not seek the Son to tincture with without the Father: they must be one body. The "Serpent-Bruiser" <note>Christ, as the one who defeats the serpent/evil</note> lies within it beforehand; for the seed of the woman did not bruise the serpent’s head without humanity, but within humanity. The source of the divine *Lubet* (meaning Love) manifested itself through a resurrection in the human essence. It became manifest in human life and tinctured the wrath of death with the blood of the divine tincture. There, the wrath of death was changed into a source of divine love and joyfulness. Thus, love bruised the head of anger and the oily poison in *Mercury*, deprived wrath of its dominion, and elevated that wrath into the highest joyfulness. In that moment, anger and astringent, cold death were made a public spectacle in a fiery love. Then it was said:
> *Death, where is your sting? Hell, where is your victory? God be thanked, who has given us victory.*

<margin>the blooming Spring of the paradisiacal New-Birth in Man.</margin>
32. Now it is necessary for the wise seeker to consider the entire process of the humanity of *Christ*, from his beginning in the womb of his mother *Mary* even to his Resurrection and Ascension. In this way, he may well find the Feast of *Pentecost* with the joyful Spirit, with which he may transform <note>original: "tincture"</note>, cure, and heal whatever is broken and destroyed. We declare this based on the foundation of Truth, as we have come to know it deeply; for the Rose shall blossom in the time of the Lily during the <margin>blooming Spring of the paradisiacal New-Birth in Man</margin> *May* when the winter is past—a source of blindness for the wicked, but light for those who can see.

33. May God be praised forever, who has granted us eyes to see through the poisonous heart of the *Basilisk* <note>a mythical serpent that could kill with a look; here representing the core of evil or the fallen state</note>, and to see the Day of Restoration of everything that *Adam* lost.

<margin>or pleasant Spring.</margin>
34. Now we will turn to the process of *Christ* and go with him out of eternity into time, and out of time into eternity, and bring the wonders of time back into eternity. We will openly present the Pearl for the honor of *Christ* and the scorn of the Devil; he who sleeps is blind, but he who wakes sees what the <margin>pleasant Spring</margin> *May* brings.

35. *Christ* said, *Seek, and you shall find; knock, and it shall be opened to you.* You know that *Christ* speaks in a parable concerning the wounded Samaritan <note>referring to the Parable of the Good Samaritan in Luke 10, here interpreted as an allegory for the fall and redemption of the human soul</note>, saying that he fell among murderers who beat him, wounded him, stripped off his clothes, and went away, leaving him half dead until the Samaritan came and took pity on him, dressed his wounds, poured oil into them, and brought him to the inn. This is a clear and living representation of the corruption of humanity in Paradise, and also of the corruption of the Earth under the curse of God when Paradise departed from it.

36. Now, do you wish to be a *Magus* <note>a practitioner of spiritual or natural "magic" or alchemy seeking the hidden secrets of God's creation</note>? Then you must become like the Samaritan; otherwise, you cannot heal the wounded and decayed. For the body which you must heal is half dead and severely wounded; its true garment has also been torn off, so that it is very hard for you to recognize the person you wish to heal unless you have the eyes and will of the Samaritan, and seek nothing else but to restore what the wounded person has lost.

37. Now consider! The Eternal Word manifested itself in *Adam* with divine, living essence—with the heavenly *Mercury*. But when the soul-fire in *Adam* was poisoned by the infection of the Devil, it corrupted the spirit of the will. Through the nature of the Serpent, it introduced earthly, deadly lust; consequently, the heavenly *Mercury* <note>in Boehme’s alchemy, Mercury represents the "vital spirit" or the power of movement and expression</note> of the heavenly essence withdrew. That is, the soul's will departed from it and focused its hunger on the earthly, mortal essence—specifically, the nature of the "cold *Mercury*" which created stones and earth. *Adam's* spirit wanted to test this [*Mercury*] and gain knowledge of both Evil and Good. Because of this, the *Mercury* of the four elements immediately pulled him into its poison and worked effectively within him, robbing him of his divine nature. It stung and wounded him with heat and cold, leaving him half dead and stripping him of his angelic clothing—the garment of the pure element where the heavenly source penetrates the four elements and infused <note>original: "tinctured"</note> them into *Adam's* body. At that time, he needed no other clothing, for heat and cold were essentially swallowed up within him; just as the day holds the night swallowed within itself—the night remains there, but it is not visible. This is what happened to Man when the nature and source of the Night seized him and began to dominate him; and the same happened to the Earth when God cursed it.

38. Now, do you wish to be a *Magus*? Then you must understand how to change the Night back into the Day; for the source of the Night (which is Darkness) is the painful source of Death, while the source of the Day (which is Light) is Life and the radiance within Life. *Christ* has reignited this radiance within humanity and brought Man back to life within himself. Now, if you wish to transform <note>original: "tincture"</note> things, you must change that which is shut up and closed in the death of the Night back into the Day. For the Day is the transformative power <note>original: "tincture"</note>, and yet Day and Night exist within each other as one essence.

<margin>or what shall I first do to effect it?</margin>
39. Now Reason says, "How may I begin <margin>or what shall I first do to effect it?</margin> to do it?" Look at the process of how God began with humanity when He intended to transform <note>original: "tincture"</note> it.

# Signatura Rerum: Chapter 7

40. Christ came into this world in the enclosed human form and brought the Tincture <note>original: "Tincture"—a spiritual essence or transmuting agent</note> of Life, namely the Deity, into the fortress of Death. He came into the world as a pilgrim in our poor form; he became ours so that he might transform us within himself. But what did he do? Did he live in joy? Did he behave and carry himself as a lord? No; he entered into death and died, and through us, he put away the source of the "Night" within himself. But how did he do it? He took the essence of our soul and body into the divine essence and quickened our essence with the divine, so that our essence entered again with its will and desire into the divine essence. Then the heavenly *Fiat* <note>Latin: "Let it be"—the creative command of God</note> was moved again in humanity, for humanity inclined itself again into the "Liberty," namely into the free *Lubet* <note>original: "Lubet"—the divine desire or inclination; the "good pleasure" of God</note> of the Deity.

41. This being done, the man Christ was tempted for forty days—as long as the first Adam was alone in Paradise and was tempted. Then outward earthly food was taken from him, and humanity had to eat of God’s essence through its desire. All the things the first Adam had become obsessed with <note>original: "amused himself in"—meaning to be distracted or to fix the mind upon earthly things</note>, and which he had imagined himself into and been captivated by—as if in the death of the "Night"—were presented to Christ. The Devil, being a prince of this world, now presented these to him in the property of death, just as he had presented them to Adam through the serpent, which Adam and his wife became obsessed with and entered into with their imagination.

42. Now behold! What did Christ do when he was to undergo the combat of this trial, when the human essence was to enter again with its desire into the Deity and eat of God’s bread (that is, of the divine essentiality)? He went to the Jordan River and was baptized by John. With what? With the water in the Jordan and with the water in the Word of Life, namely with divine essence, which had to transform our mortal essence in the outward humanity of Christ. From this, the divine hunger arose in the human essence, so that he desired to eat of God’s bread. Therefore, the Spirit of God took him and carried him into the wilderness, and there the Father’s property in "Wrath" opposed him through the "Prince in the Wrath." There, God’s bread was offered to him, as was the bread of God’s anger according to the desire of death. Now it was tested whether the soul, which was generated and created out of the Father’s property, would—after this transformation by baptism—enter again into the "Love-Desire," namely into the "Nothing" <note>In Böhme’s theology, the "Nothing" is the divine source or stillness beyond all created things</note> that exists outside of all sources.

<margin>*Work-master, or Faber.* <note>Latin: *Faber*—a craftsman or smith; here referring to the internal creative force</note></margin>
43. What is suggested here to the *Magus* <note>original: *Magus*—an alchemist or practitioner of spiritual magic</note>? A mystery is hinted to him: if he wishes to perform wonders like Christ and transform the corrupt body to a new birth, he must first be "baptized," and then he will gain a hunger for God's bread. This hunger contains the *Verbum Fiat* <note>Latin: "The Word: Let it be"</note>, namely the *Archeus* <note>original: *Archeus*—the vital, formative force within matter; the "inner master"</note> of the new generation, which is the *Mercury* <note>In alchemy, Mercury represents the spirit or life-force of a substance</note>. But I am not speaking here of a priest's baptism; the artist must understand it magically. God and man must first come together before you "baptize," just as it happened in Christ. The Deity first entered into humanity, but humanity could not immediately understand it until it was quickened through baptism, and the hunger—namely the dead *Mercury* in the human essence—was stirred up again in the heavenly part.

44. And here human "eating" began again; namely, the *Mercury* received divine property and will again. Then the inward *Mercury* (meaning man’s property) ate of the taste of the divine Word of God’s essence. The four elemental properties ate of the "Night's" property for so long that the human *Mercury* refined <note>original: "sublimed"</note> its life and changed the four elements into one. Then life transformed death, which was accomplished on the Cross. Then the four elements departed from him; that is, he died to "Time" (namely to the "Night," or the four elements) and arose in the pure element, living for eternity.

45. The *Magus* must also keep and observe this process in his alchemy. Do you ask how? I will not put the answer directly into your mouth because of the wicked, who are not worthy of it. Observe only the "baptism"—that you baptize the dead *Mercury*, which...

<margin>* Or whose Essence is in everything.</margin>
45. It lies in the heavenly *Essence* <note>original: Essentiality</note>, enclosed and shut up in powerlessness with its own baptism. [Note] what *Essence* it has in a thing; but you must have his divine water, and also the earthly. For the earthly *Mercury* <note>In alchemy, Mercury represents the principle of life, movement, and mediation between spirit and matter.</note> cannot otherwise receive the *Divine* [Being] unless the divine *Mercury* receives some of its power, at which point it stirs and hungers. Then the heavenly [*Mercury*] seeks, but still does not find divine *Essence* around it for food; therefore, it brings its will through the desire of death into itself—that is, into the *Verbum Fiat* <note>Latin: "The Word: Let it be done," referring to the creative power of God's word in Genesis.</note>, which has made and produced it—and sets its hunger upon that. At this, the divine *Essence* inclines itself toward it and will become joyfulness within it. Even then, the beginning of the new body arises out of the divine *Essence*, which the "Desire" nourishes and brings up. And when the new life is born—that is, the Day—then the four elements die. Then the new body is shut up in dark death, and on the third day it rises again from death; for the Night is swallowed up in the Grave, and the Morning rises.

46. If you understood this, then you would have the "Pearl" <note>A common metaphor in Böhme's work for divine wisdom or the "Philosopher's Stone."</note>. But my intent and purpose is otherwise; I will show you Christ along with this Pearl; therefore, no one shall find it except he who loves Christ.

<margin>† Or openly. Text: In the Air.</margin>
47. You ask, "Tell me about the Baptism?" and I have already told you. Every hunger is a *desire* for its own property. Now, if you give the property of death back to the hunger of death, then death increases; but if you give it heavenly property, then death does not receive it, for Hell is against Heaven. Therefore, you must give death and the anger of God to death, and in this anger give it heavenly *Essence*—that is, the Baptism—and so the Baptism will swallow up the death into itself. Then the anger dies in the death through the Baptism, but not immediately. You must first follow the "Process of Christ" and suffer the baptized one to preach—that is, to appear in his divine form and colors. He will be exceedingly persecuted and plagued, and given no rest; for in this way the true *Mercury* becomes working and active. And when he has shown all his wonders through the old *Adam*, then you must cast the old and new man into God’s great anger, and flay the old man, expose him to the air, and hang him † naked on the Cross, and again take him from there, and lay him into the putrefaction—that is, into the grave.

48. And then Christ will arise from death and appear; but only his own people know him. He walks about in heavenly form, and sometimes in his own [form which he had here on earth] until the Feast of Pentecost. For now, the highest perfection is tested in him: whether he will persist in the Angelic form and eat only of the divine *Essence*. And then comes the Holy Spirit and proceeds with his power out of the entire *Body* <note>original Latin: Corpus</note>—that is, out of the body and soul—which infuses <note>original: tinctures</note> the dead and broken *Being*. This could be seen on the Day of Pentecost, where Saint Peter "tinctured" <note>To "tincture" in an alchemical sense means to transform, heal, or infuse a substance with a new quality.</note> three thousand souls at once with his heavenly *Mercury* and delivered them out of death.

49. Dear Seekers, herein lies the Pearl. If you had the "Universal" <note>The "Universal Medicine" or "Universal Tincture," the ultimate goal of alchemy which can transform all things.</note>, then you could also transform souls as Saint Peter did; but your greedy death withholds you and shuts you up. For you seek only greed and temporal honor in the pleasures of the flesh, to reproduce yourselves in the properties of the Night. Therefore, the Pearl hides itself from you. Yet the Day shall again appear when the wrathful anger of God is fulfilled, satisfied, and appeased in the blood of the saints, and turned into a Life of Love; and that time is near.

Even as in Christ two kingdoms were manifest: one which worked according to God’s will and broke the outward world’s will of his parents (when Christ stayed behind contrary to his parents' will, at which they were troubled, though the divine will in Christ knew this well enough); and the other kingdom—namely, his parents' will—which "broke" the divine will in the sense that he went home with them and was obedient to them according to their will.

61. Also, let the *Magus* know that he does not need to try to implant the right will for perfection from the outside into his work; it is already in all things. He only needs to introduce a divine, desiring will (according to the thing's specific property) into the object he takes in hand. This intent wrestles with the divine will like *Jacob* and blesses the intent introduced to God’s will, so that the divine will yields itself freely into the "hunger" or inclines itself toward the desire. It makes the imperfect will (which earnestly presses into its compassion) perfect. Then it is rightly said: "You have wrestled with God and have overcome." Then your purpose obtains a transformed body, which is both heavenly and earthly.

Therefore, let him see to it that he does not allow too fierce a **Devil** to tempt the work, nor one too weak, lest *Mercury* become frivolous and desire to continue in his own poisonous, deadly property, devouring the baptism like a wolf so that the "old man" remains.

Then the artist has nothing left to do; the bride is in the bridegroom, and they are already † married. He only needs to get their bed ready; they will warm it well enough themselves. The bridegroom embraces the bride, and the bride the bridegroom; this is their food and pastime until they conceive a child.

Therefore, he must always be given his own earthly food—not into his "belly," but magically—so that he may satisfy only the hunger of his own will. His food is his "mother" who conceives him, as mentioned before.

68. In brief, the whole work that men speak of so much and so wonderfully consists of two things: a heavenly thing and an earthly thing. The heavenly must turn the earthly within it into a heavenly thing. Eternity must turn "Time" within it into eternity. The artist seeks Paradise; if he finds it, he has the great treasure upon the earth. But one dead man cannot raise another; the artist must be spiritually alive if he hopes to say to the mountain, "Arise, and cast yourself into the sea."

72. It seems strange to human reason that God followed such a process in the restoration of humanity through Christ—that he appeared in such a poor, despised form in human nature, and was reviled, mocked, scorned, scourged, crucified, and killed; and that he was buried and rose again from the grave, walking forty days upon the Earth before he entered his invisible kingdom. Reason is so blind that it understands nothing of the eternal birth; it knows nothing of Paradise, how *Adam* was in Paradise and how he fell, or what the curse of the Earth is. If reason understood this, the whole process would be obvious. As the eternal birth is in itself, so also is the process of restoration after the Fall; likewise, the process used by the wise men to create their Philosopher's Stone is exactly the same. There is not the slightest <note>original: "least Tittle"</note> difference between them, for all things originally arise out of the eternal birth, and all must be restored in one and the same manner.

73. Therefore, if the *Magus* <note>a spiritual seeker or master of divine secrets</note> wishes to seek and find Paradise within the curse of the Earth, he must first walk in the person of Christ. God must be manifest in him—specifically in his internal map <note>likely "internal man," the spiritual blueprint within</note>—so that he may have magical sight. He must treat his purpose as the world treated Christ, and then he may find Paradise, where there is no death.

74. But if he is not in this birth of restoration, and does not walk in the way Christ walked upon the Earth—if he does not step into the will and spirit of Christ—then let him give up and stop his seeking. He will find nothing but death and the curse of God. I tell him plainly and faithfully: the pearl <note>A reference to the "Pearl of Great Price," representing spiritual wisdom.</note> I write about is paradisiacal, and God does not cast it before swine, but gives it to his children for their play and delight.

75. And although much more could be mentioned here so that even reason might have its eyes opened, it is not to be done; for the wicked would only grow worse and more full of pride. Therefore, since the wicked person is not worthy of Paradise and cannot enter it, no heavenly jewel shall be given to him. For this reason, God hides it and allows the person to whom he reveals it to speak of it only "magically" <note>meaning through symbols, metaphors, or spiritual mysteries</note>. Therefore, no one attains it unless he himself is a *Magus* in Christ, and unless Paradise is manifest in his internal man; and then he may find it, if he is born to it and chosen by God.

# The Eighth Chapter.

## *Of the fiery sulfurous seething of the Earth, and how growth occurs in the Earth; also of the separation of the several kinds of creatures: An open gate for the wise seekers.*

1. Let the reader only consider what was previously written concerning the center of the generation of all essences, and then he may easily proceed here: All that is corporeal, whether it be spirit or body, consists in a sulfurous <term>sulphureous: relating to the sulfurous principle of alchemy, representing expansion and fire</term> property; the spirit in such a spiritual property, and the body, coming from the spirit, in such a corporeal property.

<margin>* Silent, senseless, mute.</margin>
2. For all things have arisen from the Eternal Spirit as a likeness of the Eternal. The invisible essence, which is God and eternity, has, through its own desire, introduced itself into a visible essence and manifested itself in time, so that He is as a life within time, and time is in Him as if it were \* dead. Just as a master who makes his work with an instrument, and the instrument is silent to the master—and yet it is the means of making, while the master only guides it—even so are all things confined within limit, measure, and weight according to the eternal generation; and they continue in their operation and generation according to the right and property of eternity.

<margin>y Governor.</margin>
<margin>z Reside.</margin>
<margin>a Body.</margin>

And He has appointed a type of its likeness, namely Reason, over this officer, which represents to the officer what he is to do and make; and this is the Understanding, namely God’s own dominion with which He rules the officer. Now the Understanding shows to the officer what the property of each thing is, and how the separation and degrees proceed from each other. For all things are <sup>z</sup> contained in the sulfurous body, and *Mercury* <note>In Böhme’s thought, Mercury represents the fluid, moving life-force</note> is *Sulphur's* life, and the Salt is the impression <note>The contractive force that gives solid form to things</note> that preserves the <sup>a</sup> body from falling to ashes, so that the spirit is known in a palpable essence.

4. The property of *Mercury* is in *Sulphur* like the boiling of water. *Sulphur* is the water in which *Mercury* seethes, and it continually produces two forms out of the water: namely, one oily <note>original: "oleous"</note> and living, from the freedom of the divine power's property; and one mortal, from the dissolution in the fire of the salnitral flash <note>original: "salnitral Flagrat"; a sudden, explosive burst of energy compared to the combustion of saltpeter</note>.

5. The oily property is in stones and metals, herbs, trees, beasts, and men; and the mortal property is in the earth, the water, the fire, and the air. Likewise, the oily property is in these four forms (namely in the earth, water, fire, and air) as a spirit or life, and these four properties are like a dead body in which the oil is a light or life. From this, the desire—namely growth—arises as a springing out of the dead property; this is the vegetative life, a springing, budding, and growing out of death.

6. But now the oily property could not be a life if it were not in the anguish of death. This anguish makes it sprout <note>original: "pullulate"</note> or move, because its will is to fly from and press out of the anguish, forcing itself eagerly forward, which is how growth arises. Thus, death must be a cause of life, so that life may be active; and therefore *Mercury* is the true moving life.

7. In the mortal property he is evil, and is called the life of death, of hell, and the anger of God; and in the oily property he is good, due to the efficacy of the gentleness and freedom of God. Each boils in its own property: the oily in joy and meekness, and the mortal in the anguish of darkness. Yet one is the cause of the other. The Light is the death and deadly destruction of the Darkness (that is, of the Anguish), for in the Light the Anguish has no strength. Instead, the Light changes it into the exultation of joy and the cause of joy; otherwise, there would be no joy. Meekness is like a stillness, but the source of anguish sublimes <note>original: "sublimes it" — in alchemy, to elevate or refine a substance into a higher state</note> it and turns it into a pleasant laughter. So also the Anguish (the Darkness) is the death and destruction of the oily property. For if it gains the upper hand in the oily property, it takes possession of the <margin>b Or Body.</margin> body <note>original: "Corpus"</note> and turns the oil into a poisonous source—a dark spirit or a body that is wholly earthly, as Adam was when he imagined <note>In Boehme's terminology, "imagination" refers to the creative or destructive power of the will's focus.</note> into evil.

<margin>c With, or in.</margin>
9. And yet we do not acknowledge that the oily property takes any poisonous source into itself. Instead, <term>Mercury</term> <note>original: "Mercury" — In Boehme's alchemy, Mercury represents the active, moving, and transformative life-force or "Fire-Life."</note> (the fire-life) insinuates itself into the anguish and poisons the essence of time, which the outward Mercury itself makes in its own desire. That is, he departs from the inward oily essence, and then the internal being remains immovable in itself. The essence and spirit of time separate from the essence and spirit of eternity, and yet there is no parting or dividing; both principles remain in one essence. Although there are two essences, one does not comprehend the other, just as eternity does not comprehend time. For this is also how Adam and Eve died: the soul's Mercury departed with its imagination from the essence of eternity into the essence of time (the source of anguish). Then the essence of eternity lost its leader, which Christ restored again <margin>c With, or in.</margin> by the divine Word, or Mercury. Thus, the essence of eternity, which in Adam was forsaken by the soul’s Mercury, obtained life again.

10. And thus we know that the essence of eternity lies hidden in the anxious Mercury as if in the fortress of death. Our writing and teaching are to show how a person may bring the poisonous Mercury with its desire so far as to enter again into the essence of eternity (the enclosed essence) and re-assume that eternity as a body. With that same <term>tincture</term> <note>Tincture: A spiritual or physical essence capable of transforming or "coloring" other substances.</note>, one may transform the essence of time and reconcile them into one. Then the whole body <note>original: "Corpus"</note> of the inward and outward world may be only one, so that there may be only one will in the spirit: a hunger for love. This hunger then makes for itself only one essence, and then every spirit eats of its own essence or body, so that afterwards no evil will can arise there anymore.

11. Thus we understand that joy and sorrow, love and enmity, originally arise through imagination and longing. For in the inclination (or earnest desire) towards God—which is free love—the kingdom of joy arises in the midst of the anguish of death. But if the desire departs out of free love into the anguish of death (the source of darkness), then the desire is filled with the source of death, and so Mercury works effectively in the source of death.

<margin>d Or if his poison-will be brought into the moving spirit of love.</margin>
<margin>e Gross stone.</margin>
12. Thus we declare with a true foundation <note>original: "Ground"</note> that there is nothing so bad that no good lies within it, though the badness is not capable of receiving the good. Also, the greatest pearl and jewel lie in the most poisonous Mercury. If his poisonous will may be <margin>d Or if his poison-will be brought into the moving spirit of love.</margin> introduced into that pearl, then he himself reveals it; for he changes himself. This is seen in the earth, where Mercury seeks its pearl and turns it in the <margin>e Gross stone.</margin> ore to gold and to other metals, according to the <term>sulfur</term> <note>Sulfur: In this context, the passive, combustible substance that works with Mercury.</note> present in each place.

<margin>f Wrestling.</margin>
13. For there is a continual <margin>f Wrestling.</margin> combat in the earth. Eternity travels with longing through time to be free from vanity, and in its longing, it gives itself to Mercury, as

He argues that even within the most "poisonous" elements of nature, a "pearl" of goodness remains hidden, which can be revealed through spiritual transformation.</summary>

## Signatura Rerum: Chapter 8

to its life and craftsman <note>original: "Faber" (Latin for craftsman or maker)</note>. When *Mercury* obtains it in his hunger, he becomes joyful and makes this free desire <note>original: "Lubet" (the divine longing or inclination)</note> physical within him. From this, gold and silver arise, along with other metals and beneficial herbs, all according to the powerful effectiveness of each location.
<margin>Or Boiling/Seething.</margin>
As the <margin>Boiling or seething</margin> occurs in each place, so the metal is formed, all according to the properties of the seven forms of nature. Whichever form is dominant in a location, a metal—as well as herbs and trees—grows according to that same property.

14. Here physicians must take note: they must learn to clearly identify which kind of property is strongest in each substance they use for healing. If they do not know this, they will often cause the death of their patients. They must also understand and know exactly the patient's property—specifically, which of the seven forms of nature represents the *Mercury* within the *Sulphur* <note>In Boehme's system, Mercury, Sulphur, and Salt (the Tria Prima) represent the spirit, soul, and body/materiality of all things.</note>, for that determines the kind of "Salt" the patient produces. Now, if the physician gives the patient an incompatible Salt, *Mercury* is only made more violently angry and poisonous. But if the <margin>The Mercury.</margin> *Mercury* obtains its own Salt according to its own property (for which it hungers), then it rejoices and readily leaves behind the source of poison in the fire of *Mars* <note>In this context, Mars represents the wrathful, fiery, and aggressive quality of nature.</note>. But the true physician has another <margin>Or such a physician has true skill to cure.</margin> method of healing: he first brings the *Mercury* he intends to use for the cure out of the "anguish of death" and into "the Liberty" <note>The "Liberty" refers to the divine, unconditioned state beyond the strife of material nature.</note>. He is truly able to cure, whereas the other way is dangerous and uncertain. If the other physician happens to cure, it is by chance and very inconsistent; he cannot cure any disease fundamentally because the outward *Mercury* is restricted. It can reach no further than the four elements and the mortal essence, and it can do nothing in the sidereal <note>pertaining to the stars or the astral/ethereal body</note> body. But if it is turned <margin>Or seizes upon.</margin> and introduced into "the Love"—as mentioned before—then it touches the very root and foundation, renewing it even to the level of Divine Power in the second principle <note>Boehme's "second principle" is the realm of light and divine love.</note>.

15. We have an excellent illustration of this in the way herbs bloom from the earth. Within the earth, *Mercury* is earthly and poisonous. But when the Sun tinctures <note>infuses or transforms with its quality</note> it, *Mercury* reaches for the Sun’s power and light. It brings this light into its hungry, fiery *Mars*-desire—into its "Salt" (its physical essence) and into "*Sulphur*" (its mother). It then wheels this power around within its essence as if it were boiling. Then the Liberty (the highest power) reaches after its own kind—the solar property—and seizes *Mercury* along with it.

16. Now, when *Mercury* tastes the heavenly being within itself, it becomes exceedingly desirous for the power of Love and draws that power into its own desire. At this point, *Mercury* transforms itself, its Salt, and its mother (*Sulphur*) into a pleasant source. If the Liberty is introduced into a living motion with *Mercury*, it becomes full of joy and springs up like light from fire, manifesting through the *Sulphur*-spirit in the Salt. This is how the root grows, and from this, the root acquires such a pleasant smell and taste. Originally, the sharpness of the Salt—formed by the first impression of *Saturn* <note>Saturn represents the contracting, hardening, and darkening principle in Boehme's thought.</note>—is the sharpness of death's anguish, but here it is transformed into a pleasant power. Indeed, all taste in herbs is derived from Salt.

<margin>Or by.</margin>
17. Understand us further <margin>Or by.</margin> regarding the root in the earth: when the inward power of the Liberty within *Mercury’s* property (which is now transformed) forces itself outward to manifest the Deity, the Sun’s power eagerly presses toward that divine power. It inclines itself with great desire toward the highest heavenly Tincture and draws it toward itself—namely, out of the earthly body and into a solar one. In this way, the Sun draws the power out of the root in the earth, and the joyful *Mercury* ascends along with it. *Mercury* continually draws the Sun’s power down from above and draws its mother, the *Sulphur*, up from beneath. Here, all seven forms of nature arise in a joyful contest, each striving to be uppermost. This is how taste is formed during the generation of nature: whichever form of nature becomes dominant determines the taste of the Salt in the *Sulphur*, and that determines what kind of herb grows from the earth. Although everything now springs from its own "mother" (its physical source), all things originally began this way and continue to do so, for such is the law of eternity.

### Chapter 8: The Signature of All Things

<margin>n. Shoot or twig.</margin>
18. Now we are to consider the stalk: when the herb or sprig emerges from the earth, it first comes up below with a white form, then further upward with a brownish color, and above with a green color. This is now its signature, showing what kind of form is internally in the essence, in the source. The white color of the branch <note>original: "n. Branch"</note> is from the liberty of the love-delight <term>original: "Love-Lubet"; a term used by Boehme to describe the joyful, free desire of divine love</term>, and the brown is the earthly property from Saturn's impression and from the wrath of Mars; and the green, which opens itself above, is Mercury's in the form of Jupiter and Venus.

<margin>o. Or in their wrestling combat.</margin>
19. For Jupiter is power, and Venus is love-desire, which hasten toward the Sun as toward their likeness; and the heaven, which is created out of the midst of the water, puts upon them its blue and green-colored garment according to the stars' might. For the spirit of the stars receives the new child also, gives him its spirit and body, and rejoices in it. Now the forms are in contest <note>original: "o. Contest"</note>, and Mercury is the craftsman <note>original: "Faber"</note> and separator; Saturn impresses, and Jupiter is the pleasant power in sulfur; Mars is the fire-source, namely, the might in sulfur; Venus is the water, namely, the sweet desire; Mercury is the life, Luna the body, and Sol the heart—the center toward which all forms tend and press.

20. Thus the outward Sun presses into the Sun in the herb, and the inward Sun presses into the outward, and there is a purely pleasing relish and delight of one essence in another. Saturn makes things sour, Jupiter creates a pleasant taste, Mars makes things bitter because of his anxious nature, Venus makes things sweet, Mercury distinguishes the taste, and Luna takes it into her sack <note>original: "Sack"</note> and hatches it; for she is of both an earthly and heavenly property, and she gives it the solvent <term>original: "Menstruum"; in alchemy, a solvent that dissolves solids and extracts their essence</term> in which the essence <term>original: "Tincture"; the spiritual or medicinal soul of a substance</term> lies.

<margin>*. Or growth.</margin>
21. Thus there is a stimulation in the taste; each form hastens to the sweet water and the Sun. Jupiter is pleasant and ascends aloft with the love-desire in the sweet source-water, in which Mars rages and thinks himself to be master of the house, seeing that he rules the fire-spirit in sulfur. At this Mercury is dismayed that Mars disquiets him so much, and Saturn makes the flash <term>original: "Flagrat"; a sudden, energetic burst or ignition in the process of manifestation</term> corporeal according to his austere impression. These are the knots upon the stalk; the flash is like saltpeter <note>original: "salnitral"</note>, according to the third form of nature in the first impression to the spirit-life—namely, in the anguish-form from which the sulfur takes its origin. In the flash, Mercury goes up in the saltpeter on the sides and takes Venus into it as well—that is, the love-desire—from which grow twigs and branches on the stalk, trunk, or body, whether they be herbs, trees, or shrubs; and each branch or sprig is then like the whole plant <note>original: "*. Plant"</note>.

<margin>p. Bag or sack.</margin>
<margin>q. Type or resemblance.</margin>
22. But the Sun gradually deprives Mars of his force, whereupon the saltpeter extinguishes and Mars loses his bitter property. Then Jupiter and Venus wholly yield themselves to the Sun in the Moon’s cabinet <note>original: "p. Cabinet"</note>, and the outward Sun takes full possession of the inward. Understand that the inward Sun is a sulfur in Mercury and is of the divine power's property, from the liberty of God, which imprints itself on all things and gives life and power to all things. Now when that is done—when Jupiter and Venus have given themselves to the power of the Sun—then Jupiter no longer forces upward, but Mars and Mercury do continually wind the stalk further up from the earth. Jupiter stays still above in the inward and outward Sun's power, and there is the pleasant conjunction with time and eternity; there, eternity beholds itself in an image <note>original: "q. Image"</note> in time.

23. And Paradise springs up or opens, for the sulfur and the salt in the sulfur are here transmuted into Paradise, and the paradisiacal joy puts itself forth in the smell and taste. This is now the head or bud of the blossoms where the seed <note>original: "Corn"</note> grows; the lovely smell is in one part paradisiacal (from the divine power, from the liberty) and on the other part earthly (according to the outward Sun and the outward world).

24. The heavenly property sets forth its signature with fair colors of the leaves on the blossoms, and the earthly represents its signature by the green leaves or sprigs.

regarding the Blossom; but seeing that this kingdom of the outward world is only temporary (in which the Curse exists), and *Adam* could not stand in Paradise, the paradisiacal property soon passes away with its signature. For God has cursed the earth, and therefore let no one think that the outward world is divine. It is only that the divine power penetrates and tinctures the outward being. For God said, *The Seed of the woman shall bruise the serpent’s head:* this is now accomplished after the Curse in all things which approach near to the Deity, wherein *Mercury* is a poison; there God bruises its head with the inward and outward Sun, and takes away the poisonous power in the Anger <note>In Boehme’s theology, "Anger" refers to the harsh, dark, or "wrathful" aspect of God's nature that must be transformed by Divine Love.</note>.

25. O that you would only learn to understand, dear sirs and brothers, what you are meant to cure with; not with the angry *Mercury*, which in many an herb is a source of evil poison, but with the inward *Mercury*. If you wish to be called doctors and masters, then you ought also to know how you may change the outward *Mercury* in the *Sulphur* into Love, so that he may be delivered from the source of anguish and brought into a state of joy—namely, that the earthly being be turned into a heavenly one, and death into life. This is your "doctor-ship" in its true meaning, and not by the authority <note>original: "Officer"</note> of reason alone.

26. God has placed Man above the "Officer" <note>Boehme uses "the Officer" to represent the mechanical laws of nature and human reason acting without spiritual insight.</note> and ordained him in his understanding to have his own dominion. He has the ability to change Nature and to turn evil into good, provided that he has first changed himself; otherwise, he cannot. So long as he is dead in his understanding, he is the servant and slave of the "Officer"; but when he is made alive in God, then the "Officer" is his servant.

27. You "haughty caps" <note>A reference to the academic or professional headwear of scholars and doctors whom Boehme often criticized for their intellectual pride.</note>, let it be told to you: pride, your own honor, and the earthly lusts of the flesh lie in your way, so that you are not masters of the mysteries but blind children. You will not lay your hands upon the coals <note>i.e., do the hard work of alchemical/spiritual labor</note>, but you take money from the poor and distressed. You give many a person that which it would have been far better if they had never bought, for which you must give a severe and strict account.

<margin>Virtue, or efficacy.</margin>
28. It is the same with the sulfurous "seething" <note>The alchemical process of "boiling" or maturing within the earth.</note> in the earth with the metals. The power is stronger in metals than in herbs; the tincture <term>Tincture: a spiritual or medicinal essence that can transform or "color" matter with its properties</term> is more heavenly than earthly. If the artist affords it his help, then it changes itself—namely, the earthly into a heavenly—which nevertheless happens in many places without the artist's ingenuity. As we see, *Mercury* in *Sulphur* captures the heavenly tincture in its boiling, whereby he changes his "made essence" (which he creates in the *Sulphur*) into gold and silver by the power and efficacy of the tincture. Understand this to be by that part of the heavenly property; for out of the earth, or out of the deadened property in the *Salniter* <note>Salniter: Saltpeter or nitrous earth, considered by alchemists to be a foundational salt containing a vital spirit.</note>, no gold can be made, for there is no stability <note>original: "fixedness"</note> within it.

29. Now we are to consider this process of the boiling in the *Sulphur* in the earth: Wherever the earth is in any place sulfurous in the *Saturnine* property <note>Saturnine: Related to the planet Saturn, representing coldness, contraction, and the metal lead.</note>, wherein the *Sun* bears chief rule, there is such a boiling. The outward *Sun* hungers after the inward Sun, which dwells in its own principle in the center of the *Sulphur*, and sets its desire upon time. For "time"—meaning the creaturely world—longs after eternity—namely, after the "liberty"—to be freed from vanity; as the Scripture says, *That all creatures do earnestly long with us to be freed from vanity.*

30. Even here, this *Liberty* gives itself into the solar property into time; and when *Mercury* tastes it, he becomes joyful and turns his wheel in joy. Then *Saturn* "impresses" <note>In Boehme’s system, "impression" is the act of hardening or giving form and physical weight to a spiritual essence.</note> the meekness; and *Mars*, who arises in the Mercurial wheel in that impression, gives the fire-soul to it, so that there is a driving forth and growth. For the *Liberty* puts itself forth in *Mercury's* property, and *Mercury* continually separates *Saturn* and *Mars* from it, for he desires a fair and pure child for his joy. He allows *Venus* to remain on the child, for she is akin to the child in property. Copper is nearest to gold by reason of the *materia* <note>Materia: the underlying matter or substance.</note>; it lacks only the *tincture*; *Mars* holds him too...

31. After *Venus*, *Mars* is akin to gold; for he has swallowed up *Venus* in his wrath and uses her for his body. Otherwise, in his own specific property, he has no physical essence, for he is only consuming wrath. He makes himself a body out of the water of *Venus*, which he devours, and *Saturn* makes it physical for him. Therefore, he defiles his iron with rust, and that is his property—namely, to be a devourer of his own body. But *Venus* is pleasant and causes growth within him; yet he devours again whatever the property of *Venus* creates in him. For *Venus* is the food of *Mars* within the Saturnine property. Therefore, the Artist must consider what lies within *Mars*. If he possesses only the solar tincture <note>original: "Solar Tincture"; the spiritual or medicinal essence associated with the Sun/Gold.</note>, he needs nothing else but to deprive *Mars* of his force, for *Mars* derives his toughness from *Venus*.

32. *Mars*, in his own specific property, is only brittle <note>original: "Spalt"; likely meaning prone to splitting or cracking.</note> and causes hardness, just as fire does. But *Saturn* is the "impressure" <note>The compressive force that gives solid form to matter.</note> of all things. *Venus* needs only the tincture, and then she is perfect. However, the Artist must rightly understand where the possibility lies—namely, in *Sulphur*, where *Saturn* holds the *Sulphur* in his belly. And where *Mercury* shows its color, <margin>* Or Mind.</margin> there he is in the will, but he cannot act, for *Saturn* holds him too imprisoned. But if the Artist lends a helping hand—advancing his wheel and giving him his mother’s food, which she has hidden in the center—then he grows strong, casts *Saturn* away, and reveals the Child. It is the same within the earth: where *Mercury* is alive <note>original: "quick"</note> in his mother (that is, in the *Sulphur*), if he is not held back so that he may reach *Venus* in his hunger for food, the Sun will soon shine forth, for she beams out through the meekness of *Venus*. He cooks <note>original: "dresses [or seeths]"</note> his food with his own fire and needs no Artist for that; the Artist must observe this well, for he has his own *Mars* within himself.

33. Now, just as this "boiling" <note>The natural alchemical process of maturation or digestion.</note> occurs within the earth, so it is also above the earth. When fruit grows out of the earth, it is at first sharp (astringent) and bitter, as well as sour and unpleasant, just as an apple on a tree is. For *Saturn* at first holds dominion—he contracts it—while *Mercury* forms it, and *Mars* gives the fire to *Mercury*, which *Saturn* receives into his cold property. *Venus* provides the sap, and *Luna* <note>The Moon.</note> takes everything into her body; for she is the Mother and receives the seed of all the planets into her *menstruum* <note>original: "Menstruum"; in alchemy, a solvent or the formative fluid of the womb.</note> and hatches it. *Jupiter* gives power to it, and *Sol* <note>The Sun.</note> is king within it, but at first *Sol* is weak because the *materia* <note>Matter.</note> is too earthly and cold. Now the whole essence in its "boiling" <margin>* Or Womb.</margin> lies in the body of *Sulphur*. And in the *Sulphur*, the "salnitral flagrat" <note>A term used by Boehme to describe a sudden, explosive ignition of spiritual force, similar to the reaction of saltpeter (niter).</note> creates a salt in the wheel of *Mars* according to each property. For the *Sulphur* turns into salt—that is, into taste—and in that same taste, there is an oil hidden in the center of the sulfurous property. This oil arises from the free "Love-Lubet" <note>original: "Love-Lubet"; a term for the divine desire or longing of the eternal will.</note> (that is, out of eternity) and manifests itself with an external essence in time, which is the manifestation of God.

34. Now, in this same oil is the hunger or love-desire for the essence of time—namely, for the manifestation of the Deity. This desire reaches out through the essence of time for its own property (the Sun), and the Sun’s property reaches for the oil in the center of the fruit and fervently longs for it. It gives itself freely into the fruit, sucks the virtue into itself, and releases it in joy into the harsh property of the fruit, softening and sweetening everything with the love it receives in the center from the "oil of liberty." Thus, a fruit that was at first sour and sharp becomes very pleasant and sweet so that a person may eat it. This is exactly how all fruits ripen.

35. Now, by the signature on the outside, you may see the inward form; for the forms within the salt (that is, in the power) show themselves externally.

36. There are commonly four colors: white, yellow, red, and green. According to which color the fruit (such as an apple) is most "signed" <note>Marked by a "signature" or outward sign of its inner nature.</note>, the taste in the salt corresponds. For example, white with a clear, thin skin slightly inclining toward dark yields sweetness, which belongs to the property of *Venus*. If the sweet taste is strong and powerful, then *Jupiter* is potent within it; but if it is weak and cloying <note>original: "fulsome"</note>, then the Moon is strong within it.

# Signatura Rerum: Chapter 8

But if it is hard and of a brownish color, then *Mars* is strong in it; but if the white color is of a grayish brown, then *Saturn* is strong in it. *Venus* <margin>Gives, or yields.</margin> makes a white color, *Mars* red and bitter in taste; *Mars* makes *Venus's* color light; *Mercury* gives a mixed color and opens the green in *Mars*; *Jupiter* inclines toward blue, *Saturn* toward black—almost gray. The *Sun* creates the yellow color and gives the proper sweetness in the salt, casting forth the pleasant smell which takes its rise from *Sulphur*. *Saturn* makes it astringent (sharp) and sour; and each property represents itself externally as it exists internally in its dominion, so also by the form <term>Signature</term> <note>original: "Signature" — the belief that the physical appearance of a plant or mineral indicates its medicinal use or spiritual essence.</note> of the leaf or branches.

37. Every root, as it is in the earth, may be known by its signature for what it is good or profitable; the earth itself has such a form, and it is discerned in the leaves and stalks which planet is lord over its properties—and even more so in the flower. For whatever the taste of the herb and root is, such a "hunger" is in it, and such a cure lies within it, for it possesses such a salt. The physician must know what kind of sickness has risen in the body, and in what salt the nausea <note>original: "Loathing" — here meaning a biological rejection or morbid aversion within the body's chemistry.</note> has risen in *Mercury*, so that he does not administer a further nausea <note>original: "Loathing [and Nausea]"</note> to his patient. For if he gives him the herb in whose property *Mercury* has previously received a nausea, then he administers poison to him; the poison in the nausea of the body then exceedingly inflames itself in *Mercury*, unless he burns that herb to ashes and gives it to him. Then the poison of the nausea loses its might, for these ashes are a death to the poison of the living *Mercury*.

38. We find this very effectively in magic; this also the physician must know: that all sicknesses arise from the nausea in the form of nature. When one form in the life is superior, if a contrary thing quite opposite to its property is introduced into it by force—whether from the stars, the elements, or the seven forms of life—then it deprives this superior (or chief) form, which is the leader and ruler of the life, of its strength and power in its salt. Then the *Mercury* of this superior form begins to work effectively—that is, to hunger and loathe. And if he does not obtain his own peculiar property (meaning the bodily form which is chief in the body among the seven properties or forms), then he ignites himself in his own poison-source according to his <margin>Or life's.</margin> vital property. He strives forcibly for so long that he becomes fiery, and then he awakens his own *Mars* and his own *Saturn*, which impress him and consume the flesh of the body in the poison-fire, wholly consuming the Oil of Light <note>The spiritual essence or vital fuel of the soul and body.</note>. At that point, the life’s light goes out, and it is past recovery.

39. But if the form of life <margin>Or whereby.</margin> in which *Mercury* is inflamed in <margin>Or Nausea.</margin> nausea, in anguish, and in the poison-source, can obtain that property for its hunger of which the spirit and body are chiefly composed, then he obtains his own natural food upon which he lives. He rejoices again and puts away the <margin>Or Loathing.</margin> nausea; then the nausea dissipates (or dissolves) and is spewed out. But the physician must take care whether or not that thing which he will administer to his patient is, in its property, also strong in the same essence from which the nausea has risen in the body.

40. For example: a jovial <note>A person dominated by the planetary properties of Jupiter (associated with joy, justice, and growth).</note> man receives a nausea (or loathing) from the lunar property. Now, if the physician knew that he had caught his nausea this way and prepared him a jovial cure according to the hunger of his own spirit or *Mercury*, this would be correct. But if the Moon’s property is strong in the salt which he would administer for the nausea, then he gives him further nausea. However, if the jovial cure is free from the Moon, then the jovial *Mercury* receives its own food with great desire and quits the nausea. And it is the same with diseases which arise in the <term>Salniter</term> <note>Boehme's term for the explosive, energetic spiritual essence in nature, similar to gunpowder or nitre, which acts as a catalyst for life and movement.</note>—namely, from fear or frightening. To that also belongs such a "flagrat" <note>A sudden flash, shock, or energetic burst.</note> as the first was, and then there is an immediate cure; or such an herb where the Salniter lies in the same property as it lies in that man.

41. I know, and it is shown to me, that the sophister <note>A deceptive or overly academic critic.</note> will cavil at me because I write that the divine power is in the fruit—that God’s power <margin>Unite, or give in.</margin> appropriates itself into the—
