## Chap. 8. The Signature of all Things.

41. The Generation of Nature: But hear, my dear friend, and gain insight. I ask you: How was Paradise in this world? Was it also revealed in Nature? Was it also in the fruit? Was it in the world, or outside the world? Did Paradise exist in God’s power or in the elements? Was the power of God revealed in the world or hidden? Or what is the curse of the earth, and the expulsion of *Adam* and *Eve* from Paradise? Then tell me: Does God not also dwell in time? Is not God all in all? It is written, *Am I not he who fills all things?* Also, *Yours is the kingdom, the power, and the glory, from eternity to eternity.*

42. Here, consider this yourself and do not judge me: I do not say that Nature is God, much less the fruit proceeding from the earth; but I say that God gives power to every life, whether it is good or bad, to each thing according to its desire, for he himself is All. And yet, he is not called God in relation to every being, but in relation to the Light with which he dwells in himself and shines with his power through all his beings. He gives his power to all his beings and works, and each thing receives his power according to its property; one takes darkness, the other light. Each hunger desires its own property, and the whole essence [or being] is all God’s, whether it is evil or good; for from him and through him are all things. Whatever is not of his love is of his anger. Paradise is still in the world, but man is not in it unless he is born again of God; then, as to that new regeneration, he is in it, and not with the *Adam* of the four elements. Oh, if only we would learn to know ourselves and understand it even through the created essence [or being].

43. Look! In *Saturn* <note>original: "Saturn"; in alchemy, Saturn represents lead or the base, unrefined state of matter</note> there lies gold shut up in a very disregarded and contemptible form and manner, which indeed resembles no metal; and though it is cast into the fire and melted, yet a man shall have nothing but a contemptible matter lacking any form of virtue <note>original: "virtue"; here meaning inherent power or excellence</note>, until the artist takes it in hand and uses the correct process upon it, and then it is revealed what was inside it.

<margin>Or so it is signed, or marked.</margin>
44. So likewise God dwells in all things, and the thing knows nothing of God; he likewise is not revealed to the thing, and yet it receives power from him. But it receives the power according to its own property from him, either from his love or from his wrath; and from whichever it receives, so it has its <gloss>signed</gloss> signature externally. The good is also in it, but as it were wholly shut up [or hidden] to the iniquity [or evil]. You have an example of this in bushes and other thorny and prickly briars, out of which a fair, well-smelling blossom grows regardless. There lie two properties within it, namely, a pleasant and an unpleasant one; whichever overcomes, that shapes [forms or marks] the fruit.

45. Thus it is also with man; he was created a beautiful blossom and fruit of Paradise, but the Devil raised up in him his thorny property by the serpent—meaning the center, the property of the wrathful nature, which in his paradisiacal source was not revealed in him. But when his hunger entered into the thorny, false property of the serpent, namely, into death, then the property of death and the false serpent within the Devil's desire forced its way into his hunger and filled soul and body. Thus, the hunger of the false serpent began to work effectively in him, and death awakened in him, and then Paradise hid itself in him. For Paradise withdrew into itself, and the poison of the serpent in death’s property also dwelt within itself; here now was the enmity. Then God said to him, *The seed of the woman shall bruise the serpent's head, and you shall sting the heel with death's poison.*

46. Understand that the paradisiacal image—which is shut up and captive in wrathful death, and in which the word of the Deity, namely the divine *Mercury* <note>original: "Mercury"; the quickening, transformative spirit or "life" of matter in alchemy</note> ruled and worked—disappeared. Just as the gold is disappeared in *Saturn*, so that nothing is seen but a contemptible matter, until the true artist sets upon it and again awakens the *Mercury* in the enclosed gold, and then the dead, enclosed body of the gold revives again in *Saturn*; for *Mercury* is its life, which must be introduced into it again, and then the dead...

# Signatura Rerum: Chapter 8

<margin>* Or puts itself forth, Text. Glances forth.</margin>
* The body of the Gold <note>original: "Gold ᵈ"</note> appears and overcomes the gross *Saturn* <note>In alchemy, Saturn represents lead, the heaviest and "lowest" of metals; spiritually, it represents the hardened, fallen state of man.</note>, wherein it lay shut up, and changes its mean, contemptible old body into a fair, glorious golden body.

47. Thus likewise it is with Man; he lies now shut up after his Fall in a gross, deformed, bestial dead image. He is not like an angel, much less like unto Paradise; he is as the gross ore in *Saturn*, wherein the gold is couched and shut up. His paradisical image is in him as if it were not, and it is also not manifest; the outward body is a stinking carcass while it yet lives in the poison. He is a bad, thorny bush, from which, notwithstanding, fair rosebuds may bloom forth and grow out of the thorns, and manifest what lies hidden and shut up in the wrathful, poisonous *Mercury* <note>In this context, Mercury refers to the active, driving spirit or "life-force" within a being, which can be either "wrathful" (corrupt) or "divine" (pure).</note>. This continues until the Artist who has made him takes him in hand and brings the living *Mercury* into his gold or paradisical image—which had disappeared and been shut up in death—so that the enclosed image, which was created out of the divine meekness and essential love, may again bud and spring forth in the divine *Mercury*, namely, in the Word of the Deity, which entered into the humanity that was shut up [and closed in death and the curse].

48. And then the divine *Mercury* changes the wrathful *Mercury* into its own nature, and Christ is born, who bruises the head of the serpent—namely, of the poison and death in the anger of God; understand this as the power of wrathful death. A new man arises in holiness and righteousness, who lives before God; [and his divine image] appears and puts forth its luster like the hidden gold out of the earthly property. Hereby it is clearly signaled to the Artist chosen of God how he shall seek: in no other way than how he has sought and found himself in the nature of the pure gold. The process is exactly the same, and not a whit otherwise; for Man and the Earth, with its secrets, lie shut up in the same curse and death, and both need one and the same restoration.

<margin>* Or Has the New-Birth in perfect Knowledge.</margin>
49. But we tell the seeker, and sincerely and faithfully warn him as he loves his temporal and eternal welfare, that he does not first set upon this way to try the earth and restore that which is shut up [in death], unless he himself be first born again through the divine *Mercury* out of the curse and death, and has the *full knowledge of the divine regeneration. Otherwise, all that he does is to no purpose; no learning [or studying] avails. For that which he seeks lies shut in the curse, in death, and in the anger of God. If he wishes to make it alive and bring it into its first life, then 그 life must first be manifest in him. Then he may say to the mountain, *Get thee hence, and be cast into the sea*; and to the fig tree, *No fruit grow on thee henceforth*; and it shall come to pass. For if the divine *Mercury* lives and is manifest in the spirit, then when the spirit of the soul’s will imagines into <note>meaning: directs its focused intent toward</note> anything, *Mercury* also goes along with it in the imagination and enkindles the *Mercury* held fast in death—namely, the similitude of God, or the manifestation with which the living God has made himself manifest.

50. I know and see that the mocker wearing the Devil’s mask <note>original: "Vizard"</note> will yet try to bring my writing into misapprehension, and make me seem more dark and doubtful because I write of the inward and outward *Mercury*. By the "inward," I understand the Word of God or the divine voice—the manifestation of the eternity of the Abyss. By the "outward" [*Mercury*], I understand the officer in Nature—the instrument which the inward, living, powerful Word or divine voice uses, and with which it ᶠ forms and works. Now the sophister will falsely interpret it and say that I mix them both together, making no difference, and ᵍ hold Nature to be God, as *Babel* <note>Boehme often uses "Babel" to refer to the confused and corrupted institutional religious authorities of his day.</note> has already done to me. But I bid him view my words well and learn to understand them right; for I speak sometimes from the heavenly *Mercury* and see that only, and then presently I name the instrument of the heavenly; therefore, let him pay attention to the sense. I write not as a heathen, but theosophically, from a higher ground than the outward ʰ *Faber* <note>term: Faber refers to the "smith" or "craftsman," the formative power in nature, often called the Archeus.</note> is, and then also from that same ground.

# The Ninth Chapter.

## *Of the Signature, showing how the internal signs the external.*

<margin>In, or with.</margin>
1. The entire outward visible world with all its being is a signature, or figure of the inward spiritual world. Whatever exists internally, and however it operates, it likewise has its character expressed externally. Just as the spirit of each creature sets forth and reveals the internal form of <gloss>in, or with</gloss> its birth through its body, so does the Eternal Being also.

<margin>Voice, or essence.</margin>
2. The Being of all beings is a wrestling power; for the Kingdom of God consists in power, as does the outward world. It stands especially in seven properties or forms, where each one causes and creates the next; none of them is the first or last, but they form an eternal bond. Therefore, God has appointed six days for man to work, and the seventh day is the perfection in which the six rest. It is the center toward which the desire of the six days tends. Therefore, God calls it the Sabbath or Day of Rest, for in it the six forms of the working power rest. It is the divine <gloss>voice, or</gloss> sound within the power, or the Kingdom of Joy, in which all the other forms are revealed. It is harmony—the formed world, or divine corporality—by which all things are generated and come forth to an <gloss>essence</gloss>.

<margin>In, or by.</margin>
3. This formed world has manifested itself through the motion of all forms <gloss>in, or by</gloss> this visible world, as a visible likeness, so that the spiritual being might be revealed in a corporeal, understandable essence. Just as the desire of the inward forms has made itself external, and the internal being resides within the external, the internal holds the external before it like a mirror <note>original: "Glass"</note> in which it beholds itself through the property of the generation of all forms; the external is its signature.

4. Thus, everything which is generated out of the internal has its signature. The superior form, which is primary in the spirit's operation within the power, most especially marks the body, and the other forms are attached to it. This can be seen in all living creatures: in the shape and form of the body, in behavior and deportment, and also in sound, voice, and speech. It is likewise seen in trees and herbs, in stones and metals. All according to how the wrestling occurs within the power of the spirit, so is the figure of the body represented, and so likewise is its will, as long as it so boils <note>referring to the active, energetic state of life</note> in the life-spirit.

<margin>Text: Wrestling power.</margin>
5. But if the Artist <note>meaning a spiritual seeker or alchemist</note> takes it in hand with the true *Mercury* <note>mercury: here used as a spiritual principle of transformation and expression</note>, then he may turn the weakest form so that it becomes the uppermost, and the strongest so it is the undermost. Then the spirit obtains another will, according to the most superior form; that which previously had to be a servant now becomes the lord and master among the seven forms. As Christ said to the sick, *“Arise, your faith has made you whole,”* and they arose. And thus it is here: each form hungers after the Center, and the Center is the voice of life—namely, the *Mercury*. This same is the *Faber* <note>Latin: craftsman or shaper</note> or former of the power. If this voice gives itself to the hunger of the lowliest form in the strong <gloss>wrestling power</gloss> combat, then it lifts up its property (meaning the property of that form), and thus its desire or faith has saved it; for in the desire, *Mercury* lifts up [or sublimes] itself; and thus it was for those Christ healed.

6. Sickness had taken possession of them, and the poison of death had gotten the upper hand in *Mercury*; but now the form of life in the Center set its hunger—as a famished and lowly property—after the liberty of being freed from the abomination. But seeing the *Mercury* was revived in Christ, the divine property, therefore the weak hunger

7. Thus, life prevails over death, and good over evil; conversely, evil can prevail over good, as happened with Lucifer and Adam, and still happens daily. In this way, everything is "signed" <note>Boehme uses "signed" to mean that every created thing bears an external mark or "signature" that reveals its inner spiritual essence.</note>; the form that is dominant determines the taste and the sound within *Mercury* <note>In alchemy, Mercury represents the principle of volatility, movement, and the "word" or sound of a substance.</note>, and it shapes the body according to its specific property. The other forms cling to it as co-helpers and also contribute their signature to it, though very weakly.

8. There are specifically seven forms in nature, both in the eternal and the external nature, for the external world proceeds from the eternal. The ancient philosophers gave names to the seven planets according to these seven forms of nature; however, they understood them to be something more than just the seven stars. They meant the sevenfold properties in the generation of all essences <note>original: "Essences" — the fundamental nature or "being" of a thing.</note>. There is nothing in the "Being of all Beings" that does not contain these seven properties; for they are the wheel of the center, the cause of *Sulphur* <note>In Boehme's alchemy, Sulphur represents the substance or "oil" that allows the fire of life to burn.</note>, in which *Mercury* causes the boiling in the source of anguish.

<margin>* Or Original.</margin>
9. These seven forms are as follows: the desire of the "impression" <note>The "impression" is the act of spiritual contraction or solidification.</note> is called *Saturn*, into which the "free lubet" <term>Lubet</term><note>A term used by Boehme for the divine "pleasure" or "inclination"—the spontaneous will of God that exists before any formal creation.</note> of eternity gives itself. Within this impression, it is called *Jupiter* because of its pleasant and praiseworthy virtue. The Saturnine power encloses and makes things hard, cold, and dark, and it produces the *Sulphur* (meaning the vital spirit—specifically the natural, moving vital spirit). The free "lubet" causes the impression to long to be freed from this dark, restrictive hardness; it is very rightly called *Jupiter*, being a desire of the * understanding, which opens the darkness and reveals a different will within it.

10. In these two properties, God’s kingdom is portrayed and exactly described—namely, the origin, and also the kingdom of God's anger, which is the dark abyss. This abyss is the cause of motion in *Saturn* (the impression). The impression, or *Saturn*, makes the "Nothing" (the free lubet) moveable and perceptible; it also creates opposition, for it causes the Nothing to become a tangible essence. *Jupiter* is the perceptible power proceeding from the free lubet toward manifestation—moving out of "Nothing" into "Something" within the impression of *Saturn*. These are two properties in the manifestation of God according to love and anger: a model of the eternal form. They are like a wrestling match—opposing desires acting against each other. One produces good, the other evil, and yet it is all good; it is only when we speak of the source of anguish and the source of joy that we must distinguish between them, so that the cause of each may be understood.

11. The third form is called *Mars*, which is the fiery property within the impression of *Saturn*. Here, the impression enters into great anguish—that is, into a great hunger. This is the source of pain and feeling, and also the cause of fire and consumption, as well as enmity and malice. However, in *Jupiter* (the free lubet or the "Nothing"), it causes the fiery desire for love; the "Liberty" (the Nothing) becomes desirous and enters into sensibility—that is, into the kingdom of joy. In the darkness, this property is a devil (God’s wrath), but in the light, it is an angel of joy. You must understand the property in this way: when this source became dark in Lucifer, he was called a devil, but while he was in the light, he was an angel. This is also how it should be understood in man.

12. The fourth property or form is called *Sol* (the Sun), which is the light of nature. It has its origin in "Liberty" (the Nothing), but without radiance. It enters with the "lubet" into the desire of the impression of *Saturn*, reaching the wrathful or fiery property of *Mars*. There, the free lubet—which has sharpened itself in the impression, in the property of *Mars*, in the consuming anguish, and in the hardness of *Saturn*—displays itself or powerfully breaks forth in *Jupiter* as a sharpness of the...

This gives understanding in *Saturn*, *Jupiter*, and *Mars*—namely, a spirit that knows what it is in its own properties. This spirit hinders or prevails against the wrath <note>In Boehme's system, "wrath" refers to the harsh, conflicting forces of nature before they are balanced by light.</note> and brings it out of the anguish, out of the property of *Mars* and into *Jupiter's*; that is, out of the anguish into a *love-desire*.

13. In these four forms the spirit’s birth consists—specifically, the true spirit in both the inward and outward being, the spirit of power in the essence. And the essence or corporality of this spirit is *Sulphur* <note>original: "Sulphur"; in Boehme’s alchemy, this represents the active, combustible principle of the soul and matter.</note>.

14. You rabbis and masters! If only you could understand how faithfully that which your predecessors intended and aimed at is given and revealed to you. You have been blind to this for a long time, the cause of which is your pride. This God, the highest understanding, sets this before you through humble and previously unlearned instruments <note>Boehme refers to himself here; he was a shoemaker with no formal academic education.</note> whom He Himself has grounded, if only you would finally see and escape the source of torment.

15. The fifth form is *Venus*, the beginning of all corporality—namely, of the Water. This arises in the desire of *Jupiter* and *Mars* (that is, in the *love-desire*), out of liberty and out of nature. It comes from the desire for "impression" <note>Referring to the contraction or densification of spiritual forces into physical matter.</note> in *Saturn* and *Mars*, in the great anguish, to be freed from that anguish. It carries two forms in its property’s desire: a fiery property from *Mars* and a watery property from *Jupiter*. Understand this as a heavenly and an earthly desire: the heavenly arises from the heavenly "impression" of the union (or the free outflow) of the Deity in nature for its own manifestation; the earthly arises from the impression of darkness in *Mars*, namely in the property of the wrathful fire. Therefore, the essence of this desire consists of two things: Water, from the origin of liberty, and *Sulphur*, from the origin of nature according to its impression.

16. The outward likeness of the heavenly being is Water and Oil. Understand that according to the Sun (*Sol*), it is Water; according to *Jupiter*, it is Oil; and according to the hard "impression" of *Saturn* following the heavenly being according to *Mars*, it is Copper. According to the Sun (*Sol*), it is Gold. According to the earthly "impression" and the property of darkness, it is grit, gravel, and sand in the *Sulphur*. According to the property of *Mars*, it is the cause of all stones; for all stones are *Sulphur* formed from the powerful dominance of *Saturn* and *Mars* in the property of *Venus*, according to the dark impression—meaning, the earthly part.

17. O, you dear wise men! If you only knew what lies in *Venus*, you would not adorn your roofs so sumptuously <note>Likely a critique of those who value the physical beauty of metals like copper without understanding their spiritual source.</note>. The ruler often loses his life for the sake of the servant, and he puts the master upon his roof; therefore, he is blind. His false *Venus-desire* causes this in him, leading him to form it in *Saturn* and *Mars* and bring it forth in the Sun (*Sol*). If he formed his *Venus-desire* in *Jupiter*, then he might rule over the fiery *Mars* which lies in *Venus* and has placed its coat upon *Venus* in *Sulphur*.

18. Thus *Mars* clothes all his servants who love him and *Saturn* with his garment, so that they only find the copper of *Venus* and not the gold within that copper. The spirit of the seeker enters into the Sun (*Sol*)—that is, into pride—and assumes he possesses *Venus*, but he actually has *Saturn*—that is, covetousness. If he went forth in the Water—that is, in the resigned humility of *Venus*—the <term>Stone of the Wise Men</term> <note>The Philosopher's Stone, the legendary alchemical substance capable of turning base metals into gold and achieving spiritual perfection.</note> would be revealed to him.

19. The sixth form is *Mercury*—that is, life and separation, or the form found in love and in anguish. In *Saturn* and *Mars*, on the one hand, he is earthly according to the hard "impression" where his motion and hunger are a pricking, adverse, and (according to the fire) a bitter pain and woe. And according to the Water in the earthly *Sulphur*—that is, in its <term>mortification</term> <note>In alchemy, the process of decay or "death" of a substance before it is reborn or purified.</note>—he is a source of poison.

# Signatura Rerum:
## Chapter 9.

20. And according to the other part—according to the Lubet <note>original: "Lubet"; from the German *Lust*, meaning a longing, divine desire, or the free will's inclination</note> of Liberty—he is the pleasant property of joy in *Jupiter* and *Venus*, as well as the property of springing and growing. According to the impression of the heavenly *Saturn*, and according to *Mars* in the desire for love, he is the sound in the spirit—understand this as the "distinguisher" of the sound, namely, of the tone. He is also the source of all pronunciations of speech and all various cries and notes; everything that sounds is distinguished by his power. *Venus* and *Saturn* carry his lute, he strikes upon *Venus* and *Saturn*, and *Mars* gives him the sound from the fire. Thus *Jupiter* rejoices in *Sol* <note>the Sun</note>.

<margin>† Or distinguishes the senses.</margin>
21. Here lies the pearl, dear brethren: *Mercury* creates the understanding in *Jupiter*, for he † separates the thoughts and makes them act and move. He takes the infinity of thoughts into his desire and makes them essential <note>real or substantial</note>. He does this in *Sulphur*, and his essence is the manifold power of smell and taste; *Saturn* adds his sharpness to it so that it becomes salt.

<margin>* Namely, the Mercury.</margin>
22. But I am referring here to the virtual <note>the essential power or "virtue" of</note> salt in the life of plants. *Saturn* creates the common salt in the water. * He is a heavenly and an earthly laborer, and he works in each form according to the property of that form; as it is written, *With the holy you are holy, and with the perverse you are perverse.* <note>Psalm 18:25–26</note> In the holy angels, the heavenly *Mercury* is holy and divine; in the devils, he is the poison and wrath of the Eternal Nature, according to the property of the dark impression. This continues through all things: as the property of each thing is, so is its *Mercury*, which is to say, its life. In the angels, he is the hymn of God's praise, and in the devils, he is the cursing and awakening of the opposing will of bitter, poisonous enmity.

<margin>* Namely, Mercury.</margin>
23. This is likewise to be understood in humans and all creatures—in everything that lives and moves. For the outward *Mercury* is the outward Word in the outward world. * He is the outward *Verbum* <note>Latin: Word</note>, and *Saturn* (with the "impression" or contraction) is his *Fiat* <note>Latin: "Let it be"; the creative command</note>, which makes his word physical. In the inward kingdom of divine power, he is the eternal Word of the Father, by which He has made all things in the outward principle <note>the physical realm</note>—understand, using the instrument of the outward *Mercury*.

24. The outward *Mercury* is the temporal word, the expressed word; the inward *Mercury* is the Eternal Word, the speaking word. The inward word dwells in the outward, and through the outward, it creates all outward things; and with the inward, it creates inward things. The inward *Mercury* is the life of the Deity and all divine creatures; the outward *Mercury* is the life of the outward world and all external physical forms in men, beasts, plants, and animals. It creates a specific principle, namely, a *likeness* of the divine world, and this is the *manifestation* of divine wisdom.

25. The seventh form is called *Luna* <note>the Moon</note>, the amassed essence. What *Mercury* has gathered together in *Sulphur* is a physical or substantial hunger of all forms. The property of all the six forms lies within it; it is like the physical body of all the rest. This property is like a "wife" to all the other forms; for the other forms all project their desire through *Sol* <note>the Sun</note> into *Luna*. In *Sol* they are spiritual, and in *Luna* they are physical. Therefore, the Moon takes the sunshine into itself and shines with the Sun's light. Whatever the Sun is and creates in the spirit-life within itself, *Luna* is and creates physically within itself.

<margin>* Thicken or curdle.</margin>
26. It is both heavenly and earthly, and it rules the vegetative <note>growing</note> life. It contains the *Menstruum* <note>original: "Menstruum"; here meaning a formative solvent or "matrix" of life</note>, namely the matrix of *Venus*. Everything that is physical * congeals in its property. *Saturn* is its *Fiat*, and *Mercury* is its husband who impregnates it. *Mars* is its "vegetable soul," and the Sun is the center of its hunger, yet not entirely within its property; for *Luna* only receives the white color from the Sun, not the yellow or the red (the majestic colors). Therefore, silver lies in the property of the Moon among metals, and gold in the property of *Sol*. But since *Sol* is a spirit without physical substance, *Saturn* holds the Sun’s physical essence within himself as a place to dwell; for he is the *Fiat* of the Sun. He keeps it shut up in his dark cabinet and only preserves and protects it; for it is not his own.

<summary>Böhme describes the planetary properties as spiritual forces, identifying Mercury as the "Word" or "Life" that manifests divine or dark qualities depending on the subject. He concludes by defining Luna as the physical container or "wife" that gives material form to the spiritual energies of the other six properties.</summary>

...essence, until the Sun sends him his craftsman <term>Faber</term> <note>original: "Faber," Latin for smith or craftsman</note> **Mercury**, to whom he gives it, and to no one else.

27. Observe this, you wise men! It is no fiction or fallacy; let the artist <note>The "artist" refers to the alchemist or spiritual practitioner.</note> but understand us correctly. He must bring the jewel shut up in **Saturn** into the mother of generation—namely, into **Sulphur**—and take the craftsman, and divide all forms, and separate the variety of hungers. This the craftsman himself does when the artist brings the work into the first mother, which is **Sulphur**. But he must first baptize the stubborn child with the philosophical baptism, lest he makes a bastard of **Sol** <note>Sol refers to gold or the sun-like spiritual principle.</note>; and then let him lead him into the desert, and try whether **Mercury** will eat manna in the desert after the baptism; or whether he will make bread of stones; or whether he will aspire upward as a haughty spirit and throw himself down from the temple; or whether he will worship **Saturn**, in whom the devil sits hidden. The artist must observe this: whether **Mercury**, the wicked and poisonous child, receives the baptism; and whether he can feed on God's bread or not.

28. If he now eats and stands firm through the temptation, then the angels will appear to him after forty days. Then let him go out of the desert and eat his own food; so the artist is ready and fit for his work. If not, then let him by all means leave it alone, and for now consider himself unworthy of it.

29. He must have an understanding of the generation of nature; otherwise, all his labor and pains are to no purpose—unless the grace of the Most High has bestowed upon him some particular gift <note>original: "Particular," referring to a specific alchemical secret or divine favor</note>, so that he is able to tincture <note>To "tincture" means to transform or imbue a substance with new properties.</note> **Venus** and **Mars**, which is the shortest and most ready way, if God shows him such an herb wherein the tincture lies.

30. The Lunar body of metals lies in the boiling <note>original: "seething"</note> of the earth, in **Sulphur** and **Mercury**, covered internally with the coat of **Venus** and clothed externally with the cloak of **Saturn**, as we see plainly. It is one degree more external than the Solar body. Next after **Luna**, **Jupiter’s** body is also one degree more external; but **Venus** is a cunning <note>original: "fly"</note> bird; she also has the inward Solar body. She takes the coat of **Mars** upon her and hides herself in **Saturn's** cabinet; but she is manifest and not hidden.

<margin>It gives a cursing or a blessing aspect.</margin>

31. Next to **Venus**, **Mars** is likewise one degree more external and nearer to earthliness. Next to **Mars**, **Mercury's** body is a representative particle <note>original: "particula"</note> of all the rest; on one hand, it is most close to the earthly physicality, and on the other hand, it is nearest to the heavenly. Next to **Mercury**, **Luna** is entirely earthly on the earthly part, and entirely heavenly on the heavenly part. It carries an earthly and heavenly face toward all things; to the evil it is evil, and to the good it is good. To a pleasant creature, it gives its best in the taste, and to a bad creature, it gives the curse of the corrupted earth.

32. Now in all this, just as the property of each thing is internally, so it has its signature externally, both in animals and vegetables. You shall see this in an herb, and likewise in trees, beasts, and in men also.

<margin>a stalk or blossom.</margin>
<margin>or of whitish buds in vegetables.</margin>

He soon awakens **Mars** with his hard impression; **Mars** makes his property bending and crooked, full of knots, and hinders the body from growing high, making it full of branches and rugged, as is seen in oak shrubs and similar trees.

<margin>In conjunction with Saturn.</margin>

It gives its sweetness into **Saturn's** impression, whereby **Saturn** becomes strong and lusty. If **Venus** is not hindered by **Mars**, it grows into a great, tall, slender tree, herb, beast, or man, or whatever it may be.

# The Signature of All Things: Chapter 9

[The] body is full of virtue <note>original: "Virtue," meaning inherent power or moral excellence</note> and power, and also has a pleasant taste. Its eyes are blue and somewhat whitish, with a gentle nature, yet very potent. If it happens that Mercury is positioned between Venus and Jupiter, with Mars at the bottom, then this quality in Saturn is elevated to the highest degree of power and virtue—manifesting in words, deeds, and great understanding.

36. If this quality is found in herbs, they are long with a middle-sized stalk and a very beautiful shape. They have fair blossoms of white or blue. However, if the Sun also casts its influence into the herb, its color will lean toward yellow because of the Sun’s presence. If Mars does not interfere, then the "Universal" <note>the *Universal Medicine* or the underlying divine force of nature</note> is sovereign in that thing, whether it be a person, another creature, or an herb of the earth. The *Magus* <note>a practitioner of spiritual or natural magic</note> should observe this well: it resists all malice, false influences, and assaults from spirits, provided the person themselves is not false or wicked and does not turn their desires toward the Devil, as Adam did—in whom the Universal was once completely whole.

37. With these herbs, a person may cure and heal without any "art" from a physician <note>meaning the herbs heal by their innate divine power rather than complex medical formulas</note>. However, they are rarely found; indeed, not one person among many sees them, for they are close to Paradise. The curse of God hides them from the eyesight of the wicked so they do not see them, even if the plants stand right before their eyes. Yet, during such planetary conjunctions, they are revealed and cannot be hidden. Therefore, a great secret lies within many an herb and beast, if the "Artist" <note>the alchemist or student of nature</note> knew it and had the true skill to use it; the whole *Magia* <note>Magic, specifically the understanding of nature’s hidden powers</note> lies therein. But I am commanded to remain silent because of the wicked, who are not worthy of this knowledge. They are justly afflicted with the same plagues they use to torment honest people, tumbling themselves in their own mire.

38. But if Mars in his own nature is next to Saturn, and Mercury casts an opposing influence, and the power of Venus is beneath Mars, with Jupiter beneath the influence of Venus, then everything arising from this alignment is corrupted and poisoned. This results in a poisonous herb, tree, beast, or whatever it may be. If this falls into a corrupt human nature, it becomes prone to evil. If the Moon then brings its powerful influence into the mix, then "false magic" is ready within the lunar *menstruum* <term>the vital fluid or medium of nature, here influenced by the Moon</term>, and witchcraft becomes manifest. I must also remain silent about this and will only show the "Signature" <note>the outward physical sign of an inward quality</note>.

39. In an herb, if the blossom is somewhat reddish and twisted or streaked—inclining toward white because of the red—then the power of Venus is present, providing resistance. But if it is only reddish with dark twists or streaks, and has a rough skin on the stalk, branch, and leaf, then the *Basilisk* <term>a mythical serpent whose breath and look were fatal; here used to describe a highly toxic or destructive quality</term> lodges there.

40. This is because Mars makes the plant rugged, and Mercury makes it poisonous (which creates the streaked color); Mars provides the red, and Saturn the dark, creating a pestilence within the lunar *menstruum*. But to the true Alchemist, this is an herb against the pestilence. If the Alchemist takes the poison from Mercury and gives it Venus and Jupiter for "food" <note>balancing the toxic elements with harmonious ones</note>, then Mars brings forth the vegetable soul in *Sol* <note>original: "Sol," the Sun, representing the perfected or divine state</note> and turns its wrathful fire into a "Love-Fire." This is what an Artist must know if he wishes to be called a Doctor.

41. This alignment likewise marks living creatures in both their voice and face. It gives a coarse, dull sound, though somewhat shrill because of Mars. Such a voice is soothing, flattering, and very false and lying. There are commonly red pimples or streaks in the eyes, or blinking, unsteady, rolling eyes. In herbs, this quality also produces a very loathsome taste. In human life—specifically in "Mercury" <note>the spirit or life-force</note>—if this quality is ingested, a stirring, boiling poison arises which darkens and obscures life.

42. The physician must be careful with herbs of this nature; they should not be taken into the body, for they are poisonous regardless of their name. Such a planetary conjunction often occurs, which can transform an herb that is usually good into one subject to Saturn and Mars. Likewise, it sometimes happens that an "evil" herb—due to a favorable conjunction at its beginning while it stands in the *menstruum*—may be freed from its malice. This change is always revealed by its Signature.

# Chap. 9. The Signature of all Things.

Therefore, the physician who understands the <term>Signature</term><note>The "Signature" refers to the outward appearance or qualities of a natural object that reveal its inner spiritual or medicinal nature.</note> may best gather the herbs himself.

43. But if **Mars** is positioned near **Saturn**, and **Mercury** is very weak, and **Jupiter** is also under the influence of **Mars** in its <term>property</term><note>original: "Property"; here meaning the essential nature or characteristic quality of the planet's influence.</note>, and **Venus** creates an opposite aspect or dissent through its desire, then it is good. This is because **Jupiter** and **Venus** change the wrath of **Mars** into joy. This produces hot, wholesome, and sovereign herbs which are to be used for all hot diseases and injuries. The herb is rough, and the leaves on the branches are somewhat prickly; likewise, the stalk is fine and thin, according to the nature of **Venus**. However, the virtue and power come from **Mars** and **Jupiter**, well-mixed and tempered. They commonly have brownish blossoms emerging in that property because **Mars** is strong there with his wrath; but seeing as his wrath is changed by **Jupiter** and **Venus** into a pleasant property, the wrath becomes a desire for joy.

<margin>The text says: That he stirs [it up].</margin>
44. The physician must not prescribe **Saturn** without **Mars** in "hot" diseases—meaning cold without heat—otherwise he ignites **Mars** in its wrath and stirs up **Mercury** in the hard "impression" <note>Boehme uses "impression" to describe the way spiritual forces solidify into physical matter.</note> of the property of death. **Mars** is necessary for the cure of every Mars-like sickness (which consists of heat and stinging pains). But let the physician know that he must first correct and qualify the **Mars** he intends to administer with **Jupiter** and **Venus**. In this way, the wrath of **Mars** may be changed into joy, and then it will also change the sickness in the body into joy. Cold is quite contrary to this.

45. If the physician administers **Saturn** alone and by itself to a "martial" <note>A disease caused by an excess of the Mars quality, typically characterized by fever or inflammation.</note> disease or injury, then **Mars** is overcome with death and falls with all his force and strength into the property of death. Since **Mars** is the "fire" in the body, the life-fire then becomes deadly in its elemental property, for it soon awakens **Mercury** in the property of cold. Yet, the physician must also take care that he does not administer raw, undigested, "hot" **Mars** in a hot disease, in which **Mercury** is wholly inflamed and burning; for this would ignite the fire even more vehemently in the body. He must first soften **Mars** and **Mercury** and put them into a state of joy; then it is right and good.

<margin>Sublime them.</margin>
46. The hotter an herb is, the better it is for this purpose—provided its wrathful fire is changed into love. Then it can also change the wrath in the body into joy, provided the disease is of a nature that can bear it. For a weak fire in the body—which is tired and languid because of the heat, and instead inclines toward cold (namely, the poison of **Mercury** where life is in danger)—requires a cure with a fine, subtle heat. In such a cure, **Venus** is strong, and **Mars** is very tender and mild because of the power of **Venus**. **Jupiter** need not be strong there, lest he make **Mars** and **Mercury** too strong, so that the weak life is overwhelmed and brought into the Mercurial poison before it can be quickened and refreshed.

47. An herb with this aforementioned property does not grow high and is somewhat rough to the touch. The rougher it is, the stronger **Mars** is within it. It is better to use such herbs outwardly for wounds and sores than to take them internally. The fine and subtle part of the herb is to be taken into the body and acts as an "expulsive" <note>A medicine that helps the body drive out morbid or poisonous matter.</note>. The more subtle it is, the closer it is to the life in the body, which the physician may clearly recognize by its "salt" <note>In alchemy, "Salt" represents the physical or solidified base of a substance.</note>. No rough, wild property should be taken into the body unless the body is inflamed with a sudden poison and the life is still fresh and strong; in that case, a powerful resistance must be used. Yet **Mercury** and **Mars** must not be administered in their wrath, but in their strongest power—**Mars** in the greatest heat, but transformed into joy first. Then he also changes **Mercury** to match himself. **Jupiter** is necessary for the <term>transmutation</term><note>The alchemical process of changing one substance or quality into another.</note> of wrathful **Mars**, but he must first be introduced into the property of **Sol** <note>The Sun, representing the highest spiritual light and balance.</note>, and then he is properly fit for it.

48. Every living creature is friendly and pleasant according to its kind in the previously mentioned property, if you deal with it in a friendly and gentle manner. But if it is dealt with roughly, then **Mercury** is stirred up in its poisonous property; for **Mars** soon boils up and rises into its bitter property, and then anger breaks out. For the ground of all malignity—

49. But if *Mercury* <note>In alchemy, Mercury represents the principle of fluidity, movement, and the "vital spirit."</note> is next to *Saturn* in its property, with the *Moon* following him, and *Venus* and *Jupiter* are beneath and also weak, then no matter where *Mars* stands, everything remains earthly. In a living creature, it produces a pleasant, courteous, and humble life, without deep reasoning <gloss>reach or capacity</gloss>. 51. There are three special salts <note>In the Paracelsian "Tria Prima," Salt represents the principle of materiality, stability, and the physical body.</note> which may be used to heal, belonging to the organic life <note>original: "vegetable life"</note>: namely, *Jupiter*, *Mars*, and *Mercury*. These constitute the working life, in which the Sun is the true Spirit that makes these salts operative.

Working, powerful, or effective.

52. The salt or power of *Jupiter* has a pleasant, good smell and taste, derived from the inward source <gloss>of the property</gloss> of the liberty of the divine essence, and from the external <gloss>principle or source</gloss> of the property of the Sun and *Venus*. However, it does not have sufficient power in nature on its own, for outward nature consists of fire and anguish—namely, in poison. *Jupiter’s* power is opposed to the fiery, poisonous life, which creates a balance <note>original: "temperature"</note> in the poisonous nature; it creates a desire for gentleness out of the enmity.

<margin>
The jovial virtue <note>The beneficial influence of the planet Jupiter.</note>.
</margin>

53. The salt of *Mars* is fiery, bitter, and harsh, and the Mercurial salt is anxious and raging, like a poison, inclined toward both heat and cold. This is because it is the life within sulfur and unites <gloss>or assimilates</gloss> itself according to the property of each thing. If it enters *Jupiter’s* salt, it causes joy and great power; but if it enters *Mars’s* salt, it causes bitter pangs, stabbing pains, aches, and woe. If it enters *Saturn’s* earthly salt, it causes swellings, anguish, and death, unless it is hindered by *Jupiter* and *Venus*. *Venus* and *Jupiter* are the opposites of *Mars* and *Mercury*, serving to temper them both. Without the power of *Mars* and *Mercury*, there would be no life in *Jupiter*, *Venus*, and the Sun <note>original: "Sol"</note>, but only a stillness. Therefore, the worst is as profitable as the best, and one is the cause of the other.

54. But the physician must take care and be mindful of what he undertakes, lest he inflame the Mercurial poison more and more in his patient, or introduce it into another hostile source. He truly ought to use the Martial and Mercurial salts for his cure, but he must first reconcile *Mars* and *Mercury* with *Venus* and *Jupiter*. In this way, both of these angry adversaries may submit their will to *Jupiter’s* will, so that *Jupiter*, *Mars*, and *Mercury* may all three obtain one shared will in their power. Then the cure is correct, and the Sun of life will again ignite itself in this union and agreement; it will also temper the sickness <note>original: "nauseate"</note> of the disease and the conflict within the salt of the disease, turning *Mercury’s* poison and the bitter fire of *Mars* into a pleasant *Jupiter*.

55. This is now to be understood only concerning the organic soul <note>original: "vegetable soul," the basic life force responsible for physical growth and health.</note>—that is, concerning the outward man who lives in the four elements—and concerning the properties of sense and feeling.

56. Reason likewise is to be cured by its likeness; for just as reason may be brought by words into a perceptible sickness and disease, so that reason may vex, fret, and tor—

ment itself and at last fall into a heavy, sorrowful sickness and death; so also it may be cured with the application of the same thing, [with its own likeness <note>original: "Affimilate"</note>].

57. For example: An honest man falls into great debts, care, trouble, and distress, which afflicts him almost to death; but if a good friend comes and pays his debt for him, then the cure is soon achieved with its likeness. It is exactly like this in all things: from whatever source the disease has risen, such a similar cure is required for the restoring of its health; and thus it is likewise in the mental soul.

58. The soul of the poor sinner is poisoned in the anger of God, and the *Mercury* <term>In Boehme's alchemical theology, Mercury represents the "spirit of motion" or the "working power" that drives life.</term> (understand the eternal *Mercury* in the eternal Nature) is inflamed in the soul's property in the fiery *Mars* of God's anger, which now burns in the eternal *Saturn*—that is, in the horrible impression of darkness—and feels the sting of the poisonous, angry *Mars*. His *Venus* <note>Venus represents the quality of love and fluidity.</note> is imprisoned in the house of misery, his water is dried up, his *Jupiter* <note>Jupiter represents understanding and wisdom.</note> of understanding is brought into the greatest folly, his Sun is quenched, and his Moon turned to dark night.

59. Now he cannot be cured and remedied any other way but with the likeness; he must again appease the mental *Mercury*. He must take *Venus*—meaning the Love of God—and introduce it into his poisonous *Mercury* and *Mars*, and tincture <term>A "tincture" is a spiritual or medicinal substance capable of transforming and refining the nature of a thing.</term> the *Mercury* in the soul again with Love; then his Sun will again shine in the soul, and his *Jupiter* will rejoice.

60. Now if you say that you cannot, and that you are too strongly captivated, I say also that I cannot; for it lies not in my willing, running, and toiling, but it lies in the compassion of God. For I cannot by my own strength and ability overcome the wrathful anger of God which is kindled in me. But seeing His dear Heart has freely given itself again out of love, and in love, into humanity—namely, into the poisonous kindled *Mercury* in the soul—and tinctured the soul (the poison-source of the Eternal Nature in the Eternal Father’s nature’s property); therefore I will cast my will into His tincture. I will go with my will out of the kindled poison-source, out of the evil *Mercury* in God's anger into His death, and with my corrupted will I will die with Him in His death and become a nothing in Him, and then He must be my life.

<insert>Hand-drawn bracket in the left margin with a pointer symbol indicating the following paragraph.</insert>
<margin>Or in.</margin>
61. For if my will is a nothing, then He is in me whatever He pleases, and then I know not myself any more, but only Him. And if He wills that I shall be something, then let Him effect it; but if He does not will it, then I am dead in Him, and He lives in me as He pleases. And so, if I am a nothing, then I am <gloss>at</gloss> the end in the essence out of which my father <gloss>Adam</gloss> was created; for out of nothing God has **created all things.** <note>The final phrase is underlined in ink.</note>

62. The "Nothing" is the highest good, for there is no *Turba* <term>The "Turba" refers to a state of disturbance, turmoil, or the "awakener" of divine wrath that breaks things apart.</term> within it, and so nothing can touch [or annoy] my soul; for I am a nothing to myself, but I am God’s, who knows what I am; I do not know it, nor should I know it.

63. And thus is the cure of my soul's sickness; he that will adventure it with me shall find by experience what God will make of him. For example: I write here, and yet I also do not do it; for I, as myself, know nothing, and have also not learned or studied it; so then I do not do it, but God does it in me as He pleases.

64. I am not known to myself, but I am known to Him as and how He pleases. Thus I live not to myself, but to Him; and thus we are in Christ only one, like a tree with many boughs and branches, and He begets and brings forth the fruit in every branch as He pleases. Thus I have brought His life into mine, so that I am atoned with Him in His love; for His will in Christ has entered into the humanity in me, and now my will in me enters into His humanity. And thus His living *Mercury*—that is, His Word, namely the speaking *Mercury*—tinctures my wrathful evil *Mercury* and transforms it into His own. And thus my *Mars* has become a love-fire of God, and His *Mercury* speaks through mine, as through His instrument, whatever He pleases; and thus my *Jupiter* lives in the Divine Joy,

# *The Signature of All Things:* Chapter 9.

...and I do not know it; the true Sun shines upon me, and I do not see it; for I do not live for myself, I do not see for myself, and I do not know for myself. I am a Thing, and I do not know what I am; for God knows what I am; and so now I tend and run to and fro as a Thing in which the Spirit drives [or actuates] me as he pleases; and thus I live according to my inward Will, which yet is not mine.

<margin>Or I am an enemy to.</margin>
65. Yet I find another life within me, which is what I am—not according to resignation [or self-denial], but according to the creature of this world, namely, according to the likeness <note>original: "Similitude"</note> of eternity. This life still exists in poison and strife, and shall yet be turned to Nothing, and then I will be completely perfect. Now, in this same life where I still find my self-centeredness <note>original: "Self-hood"</note>, there is sin and death, and these shall likewise be brought to nothing. In that life which God is within me, I <gloss>k</gloss> hate sin and death; but according to that life which is still in my self-centeredness, I hate the "Nothing"—that is, the Deity. Thus, one life fights against the other, and there is a continual contest within me. But seeing as Christ is born again in me and lives in my nothingness, Christ will—according to his promise made in Paradise—bruise the head of the serpent (meaning my self-centeredness) and mortify the evil man within me, so that he himself may truly live [in me].

66. But what shall Christ do with the evil man? Shall he cast him away? No. For he is in Heaven, and thereby accomplishes and effects his wonders in this world, which exists under the curse. Now each labors in its own [vineyard]; the outward man labors in the cursed world, which is both evil and good within the wonders of God—namely, in the mirror of glory which shall yet be revealed in him. The inward man is not its own, but is God's instrument, with whom God does whatever he pleases, until the outward man—with its wonders in the mirror—shall also be revealed in God. Then God is all in all, and he alone exists in his wisdom and deeds of wonder, and nothing else besides; this is the beginning and the end, eternity and time.

<margin>In, or by.</margin>
67. Now understand this correctly: for the outward man, there is a cure from the outward—namely, from the outward Will of God, who has made himself external <gloss>l</gloss> through this visible world. And for the inward man, there is a cure from the inward world, in which God is all in all; only one, not many—one in all, and all in one. But if the inward penetrates the outward and illuminates it with its sunshine, and the outward receives the sunshine of the inward, then it is tinctured <note>tinctured: imbued or permeated with a spiritual essence</note>, cured, and healed by the inward. The inward illuminates it just as the sun shines through water, or as fire makes iron glow brightly all the way through; here, no other cure is needed.

<margin>Or Water.</margin>
68. But since the Devil, in the wrath of eternal nature, opposes the soul as an enemy, and continually casts his poisonous imagination at the soul to tempt and test it—and since the anger or wrath of eternal nature is manifest in the outward man (which Adam awakened and stirred up)—this wrath is often stirred up by the Devil and his servants. It effectively works and burns in the outward body, and then the inward love-fire goes out in the outward man, just as a red-hot iron is quenched in <gloss>m</gloss> water. Yet this does not happen so quickly in the internal [man] as it does in the external, unless the outward man continues to lie in the mire of sin. So if the soul, which had given itself into the "Nothing"—namely, into liberty, into the life of God—enters again with its desire into the outward sinful man, then it loses the inward sun. For it goes out of the "Nothing" back into the "Something"—that is, into the source <note>original: "Source," often used by Boehme to mean a place of boiling, conflicting qualities or "sourness."</note>.

70. But now this herb <note>A metaphor for the divine love or the "Tincture" mentioned on the previous page.</note> is rarely to be found upon the earth; for men eat only of the forbidden tree. Therefore, the poison of the serpent springs up in them within the wrath of both eternal and external nature, so that they must also have an external cure for the serpent’s poison in the outward <term>Mercury</term> <note>In Böhme’s system, Mercury represents the "word" or the communicative, active force in nature, which can become poisonous when out of balance.</note>.

71. It is indeed possible for a person to live without sickness, but he must bring the divine <term>tincturation</term> <note>The process of spiritual infusion or "dyeing" the soul with God's grace.</note> from the inward man through to the outward man. This is very difficult to do in the world, for the outward man lives among the thorns of God’s wrath, which gall and sting him on every side and blow up the wrath of God so that it burns in the outward man. Then, the tincturation of God’s love may not remain there. It is indeed present, but not within the outward, ignited abominations; instead, it dwells within itself, just as the light dwells in the darkness, and the darkness does not comprehend it and knows nothing of it. But when the light is manifested in the darkness, then the night is changed into day.

72. It is the same for man; he is cured by the same light by which he lives. If he lives in the outward world, then the outward goodness and love—namely the outward <term>Jupiter</term> and <term>Venus</term> <note>Planetary archetypes representing benevolence (Jupiter) and love/beauty (Venus).</note> along with the Sun—must be his cure. Otherwise, he remains in the angry <term>Mars</term> <note>The archetype of fire, wrath, and conflict.</note> and in the poisonous Mercury, captivated by the earthly Moon and the "impression" <note>The restrictive, hardening force.</note> of <term>Saturn</term> <note>The archetype of cold, contraction, and melancholy.</note>—that is, in the earthly sulfur. This condition was made manifest and awakened in the outward man by Adam, and for this reason, the outward man must die, rot, and so enter again into the "Nothing"—that is, into the "End," or as I might better say, into the "Beginning" of creation, into the essence from which it departed with Adam.

***

## The Tenth Chapter:

### Of the Inward and Outward Cure of Man.

<margin>
<note>Ornamental woodcut initial 'L' containing the letters V, A, D, E, C, H, E, T and celestial symbols.</note>
</margin>

1. LET the lover of God understand us correctly; we do not rely on historical, heathenish conjecture, nor only upon the light of outward nature. Both "Suns" <note>The inner spiritual sun and the outer natural sun.</note> shine to us. Understand us correctly, and see how God cured man when the poison of the serpent and the Devil held him imprisoned in death, and how He still cures the poor soul held captive in God’s anger. The physician must follow the same process in curing the outward body.

2. The divine light and love were extinguished in Adam because his imagination focused on the serpent’s property—namely, on Evil and Good. Because of this, the poison of death began to work effectively in Mercury, the source of anger was inflamed in the eternal Mars, and the dark impression of eternal nature’s property took possession of him. His body became "earth" in that dark impression and in the poison of the ignited Mercury, and he was at enmity with God. He was utterly undone, and there was no remedy for him from any creature, neither in heaven nor in this world; wrathful death held him captive in both soul and body.

3. Now, what did God do to cure him and <term>tincture</term> <note>To spiritually transform or heal through a divine infusion.</note> him again? Did he take a foreign thing for this purpose? No, he took the "Likeness," and cured him with that which was cor-

# Signatura Rerum: Chapter 10.

...corrupted in him, namely with the divine <term>Mercury</term><note>original: "Mercury"; in Böhme’s system, Mercury represents the active, creative life-force and the "expressed word" of God.</note>, and with the divine <term>Venus</term><note>original: "Venus"; represents the quality of love and the "light-desire" within the soul.</note>, and with the divine <term>Jupiter</term><note>original: "Jupiter"; represents divine understanding, wisdom, and the "gentle" power of the mind.</note>. Understand this: in Man was the expressed Word, which I call the eternal Mercury in Man; for it is the true ruling, acting Life. It was inspired or "spoken into" Man’s Image (which God created out of His Essence into an image according to God) as into a creaturely Image. This was the Soul, possessing the properties of all three worlds: namely, the World of Light and Understanding, which is God; the Fire-World, which is the Eternal Nature of the Father of all beings; and the Light-Love-World, which is heavenly corporality—for in the Desire of Love is the Essence, namely, the Corporality.

4. The Desire of Love is Spirit, and is the Heart of God—the true divine Understanding. In the Love-Essence, Mercury is God’s Word; but in the fiery nature, he is the Wrath of God, the origin of all movement and enmity, as well as of strength and omnipotence. The fiery property makes the Light—that is, the Liberty—desirous, so that the "Nothing" becomes a Desire. This Desire is the Love of God, which <term>Adam</term><note>The biblical first man, used here to represent the archetypal fall of humanity into material desire.</note> extinguished in himself. For he focused his imagination upon Evil and Good, which is to say, upon Earthliness. This Earthliness emerged as a being out of both the Wrath and the Love-Being through God’s movement, so that the wonders of the "Abyss and Byss" <note>original: "Abyss and Byss"; the groundless "Unground" (Abyss) and the manifested foundation (Byss) of existence.</note> might be made manifest, and that Good and Evil might be known. But Adam, being the Image of God, should not have done this, for God had created him in His own image. He should have <term>tinctured</term><note>original: "tinctured"; an alchemical term meaning to infuse or transform the quality of one thing with another—here, balancing the harsh "Fire-World" with "Love."</note> the Fire-World and the outward world with the Word of Love, so that neither would be manifest in him—just as the Day keeps the Night swallowed up within itself.

5. But by false imagination, he awakened and manifested the dark and poisonous Mercurial Fire-World within himself. Consequently, his bodily essence of the "dark impression" has fallen toward the evil side in that poisonous Mercurial property, and the Soul has become manifest in the Eternal Nature of the Father’s Fire-property—that is, in the poisonous, hateful Mercury. Because of this, God calls himself an angry and jealous God, and a consuming fire.

<margin>⊕</margin>
6. Now, to help and restore this Image of God again, God must apply the correct cure, which is the same state Man was in during his innocence. But how did He effect it? Behold, O Man, behold and see! Open your understanding; you are being called.

<margin>⊕→</margin>
7. He introduced the holy Mercury into the Flame—that is, into the fiery Love with the desire for divine Essentiality (which desire creates divine corporality within itself). He brought this back into the expressed Word, namely, into the Mercurial Fire-Soul. (Understand: this occurred in the Soul’s essence within the womb of Mary.) Thus, He became that same Image of God again. He tinctured the Poison—namely, the Wrath of the Father of all essences—with the Love-Fire. He took only that same Mercury which He had breathed into Adam as an Image and formed into a creature. He took that same property, yet not in the Fire’s property, but in burning Love. With this Love, He reintroduced the light of the eternal Sun into the human property, so that He might tincture the wrath of the ignited Mercury in the human property and inflame it with Love. In this way, the human Jupiter—the divine Understanding—might again appear and be made manifest.

8. You Physicians: if you understand nothing here, then you are captivated by the poison of the Devil. Behold, I pray, the correct cure by which the ignited Mercury in Man’s life is to be remedied. It must be a Mercury again, but first ignited in Venus and Jupiter; it must have the property of the Sun, which it attains through Jupiter and Venus. Just as God deals with us poor Men, so must the outward, poisonous, sick Mercury be tinctured with such an external cure. It should not be treated with the dark impression of <term>Saturn</term><note>original: "Saturn"; in alchemy, Saturn represents coldness, contraction, lead, and melancholy.</note> or with Cold (unless it is first sweetly appeased and qualified with Jupiter and Venus, so that the Sun shines again in Saturn), but with meek Love. This is the correct <term>Physick</term><note>Medicine or the art of healing.</note>, by which Death is changed into Life. Yet, this is only a common manual cure, which the common people may learn.

He argues that Christ restored humanity by reintroducing divine love (the holy Mercury) into the human essence, providing a model for both spiritual and physical healing.</summary>

9. But it is necessary for the Doctor, if he wishes to be called a Doctor, to study the entire Process of how God has restored the *Universal* <term>Universal: The "Universal Medicine" or panacea, which in Boehme’s thought is both a physical alchemical goal and the spiritual restoration found in Christ.</term> in Man. This is fully clear and manifest in the Person of Christ, from his entrance into humanity even to his Ascension and the sending of the Holy Ghost.

10. Let him follow this entire Process, and then he may find the *Universal*, provided he is born again of God. But self-indulgence, worldly glory, greed, and pride lie in the way. Dear Doctors, I must tell you: the coals are too black, and you defile your white hands with them. True, unfeigned, self-denying humility before God and Man does not suit your taste; therefore you are blind. I do not tell you this of myself, but it is the Spirit of Wonders in its manifestation.

<margin>metaphorical</margin>
11. But we will give direction to the eager seeker who would gladly see, if he only knew the proper way to attain his goal. For the time is at hand when *Moses* is called from the sheep to be a shepherd of the Lord; this shall shortly be made manifest, despite all the raging and raving of the Devil. Let not dear and worthy Christendom think—even though it now seems as if she should go to rack and ruin—that she is utterly undone. No: The Spirit of the Lord of Hosts has, out of his love, planted a new *Branch* in human nature which shall root out the thorns of the Devil and make known his Child *Jesus* to all nations, tongues, and languages, and that in the morning of the eternal day.

<margin>(no nature) (dialectics)</margin>
12. Dear Brethren, behold, I pray, the right cure: What did God do with us when we lay sick in death? Did he completely cast away the created image—meaning the outward part, namely, the outward corrupt man—and make a wholly new man? No, He did not. For though he infused Divine properties into our humanity, he did not therefore cast away our humanity, but brought it into the Way or Process toward the New Birth.

<margin>a. Put its desire and imagination into the "Nothing" (the highest good or omnipotence) and eat of God's bread.</margin>
13. What did he do? He allowed the outward humanity—meaning the outward water, the "Essentiality of *Venus*" <term>Essentiality of Venus: In alchemical terms, the passive, receptive, and loving quality of nature that had become "shut up" or hardened by sin.</term> which was trapped in the wrath of death—to be baptized with the water of the Eternal Essence and with the Holy Ghost. This was done so that the fuel <note>original: "incentive", meaning the spark or material that feeds a fire</note> of the outward essentiality trapped in death might glow again, like a fire that falls into tinder. Afterward, he withdrew his outward food from the outward body and brought it into the desert and let it hunger. Then the spark ignited from the fire of God had to <gloss>a</gloss> focus its imagination <note>Boehme uses "imagination" to mean the creative power of the will and desire.</note> upon God and eat the Manna of divine essentiality for forty days. *Israel* was a type <term>type: A biblical person or event seen as a prophetic symbol or archetype of something to come later.</term> of this in the wilderness of *Sinai* with their Manna. The essential fire and hunger of eternity must overcome the essence of time; therefore it is called a "temptation of the Devil." For the Devil, as a prince in the wrath of God, tempted the outward humanity there and presented to it everything by which *Adam* fell and became disobedient to God.

14. There it was tested whether the Image of God would stand, seeing that internally there was God's love-fire and externally the baptism of the water of eternal life. Here the soul was tempted: would it be a king and occupy an angelic throne instead of the fallen angel? Would it possess the elected throne of God in the royal office from which Lucifer was taken and cast into darkness (meaning into the throne of poison and death)? But because he stood firm—in that the soul surrendered and submitted its will alone to God’s love-fire, desiring no earthly food nor the earthly kingdom of "good and evil" for outward dominion—the Process toward the *Universal* (the restoration of all that *Adam* had lost) continued to proceed: *He turned water into wine*.

15. You Physicians, observe this! It concerns you in your "process"; you must work in the same way. *He healed the sick*; so you must likewise make the form in your poisonous *Mercury* <term>Mercury: In alchemy, the principle of vitality, transformation, and volatility, which can be poisonous if not purified.</term> whole and sound by the power of the philosophical baptism. *He made the dead alive again, the dumb to speak, the deaf to hear, the blind to see, and cleansed...*

# Signatura Rerum: Chapter 10

...the lepers; all this must happen first, so that all the forms in *Mercury* may be pure, sound, and living. *Mercury* himself accomplishes this after the Baptism and Temptation, just as the living, speaking *Mercury* did this in the person of Christ. The Artist <note>In this context, the "Artist" is the alchemist or spiritual seeker performing the "work."</note> cannot do it; there must only be faith. For Christ also testifies that he could not perform many wonders at Capernaum, only healing a few diseased people, because the faith of those at Capernaum would not enter into the Divine *Mercury* of Christ.

16. So we see there that the person of Christ—that is, the creature—could not perform the wonders by his own power, but rather the *Mercury*—the living, speaking Word—within him. For the person cried and called out to God—that is, into the speaking Word—and placed his desire there. We see this at the *Mount of Olives* where he prayed until he sweat drops of blood, and with Lazarus, when he was about to raise him, saying:
> *Father, hear me; but I know that you always hear me; yet because of those who stand by, I say it, so that they may believe that you work through me.*

17. Thus, the Artist must not claim any credit for himself. The *Mercury* itself, after the philosophical baptism, performs these wonders before it manifests the *Universal*. For all the seven forms of nature must be crystallized and purified if the *Universal* is to be revealed. Each form undergoes a specific process when it is to be brought out of the property of wrath and entered into the pure and clear Life. It must transmute itself into the "crystalline sea" which stands before the throne of the Ancient One in the *Book of Revelation*, and change itself into Paradise. For the *Universal* is paradisiacal. Christ also came into our humanity for that reason: so that he might again open or make manifest the *Universal*—that is, Paradise—once more within humanity. The speaking Word in Christ performed wonders through all the seven properties or forms—through the expressed Word in his humanity—before the entire *Universal* was manifest in the body of his human nature and the body was glorified.

18. It is the same in the philosophical work: when the *Mercury* shut up in death receives the baptism of its refreshment in love, then all the seven forms manifest themselves in this property, just as happened in the process of Christ in his miracles; but as of yet, they are not perfect in the operation of their manifested properties.

<margin>Or other forms.</margin>
19. The Universal is not yet there until all seven surrender their will into one, forsake their property of wrath, and depart from it by their own will, taking into themselves the property of Love. They must take in the "Will of the Nothing" <note>Boehme's "Nothing" or *Ungrund* refers to the absolute, undifferentiated divine source before creation.</note>, so that their will becomes a "nothing." Then it can survive in the wrath of the fire, and there is no further *<term>Turba</term>* <note>original: Turba; the "disturber" or spirit of strife and destruction that arises when natural properties are out of balance.</note> within it. For as long as the desire for wrath is in a form, it is hostile and opposite to the second form and inflames the second form with its wrathful property. That is, it strikes the signature of the second form and awakens it in wrath, and then the voice or sound of the second enkindles the first form's property in *Mercury*. Thus, no form can reach any perfection that would allow it to enter into Love.

20. Therefore, the Artist can achieve nothing unless he provides a "food" to the forms which they all desire and love to eat, and in which there is no *<term>Turba</term>*. Now, the properties cannot eat because their mouths are frozen shut in the "impression" <note>In Boehme's system, the "impression" of Saturn refers to a state of cold, hard, spiritual contraction or spiritual death.</note> of *Saturn*. The Artist must first open their mouths and make them alive in their zeal, so that all the forms may be hungry. If there is Manna, they all eat of it together, and so the precious grain of mustard seed is sown.

21. Now when *Mercury* awakens from the death of the impression of *Saturn* and receives Manna into the mouth of its poisonous, deathly source, then arises the *Flagrat* <note>original: Flagrat; a flash, sudden ignition, or shining of spiritual joy.</note> of the Kingdom of Joy. For it is like a light which is kindled in the darkness, because Joy or Love springs up in the midst of anger. ### The Process in the Temptation.

22. *Jesus* was led by the Spirit into the wilderness, and the Devil came to him and tempted him. When the soul of Christ hungered, the Devil said to *Jesus*, "Open the center in the stones"—that is, the impressed *Mercury* <term>Mercury: in alchemical terms, the fluid, vital spirit or "worker" within matter</term>—"and make yourself bread; eat the substance of the soul’s property. What, will you eat of nothing, namely, of the speaking Word? Eat of the expressed Word <note>The "speaking Word" refers to the eternal divine essence, while the "expressed Word" refers to the physical, created world</note>, namely, of the property of good and evil, and then you are lord in both." This was also *Adam’s* bite <note>original: "Bit"; referring to Adam eating the forbidden fruit</note>, in which he ate death. Then Christ *Jesus* said: 
> *Man lives not by bread alone, but by every word which proceeds from the mouth of God.*

23. Take note! From where did the person of Christ get the will that he would not eat with the soul’s hunger the bread which could have been made of stones, which he could easily have done? Or how would it have been if the hunger of the human property, after the anointing <note>original: "Unction"</note> of baptism, had eaten the *Mercury* in the impression of death during the temptation? That is, if he had eaten of the *Sulphur* <term>Sulphur: the soul-fire or combustible essence that drives growth and desire</term> of the expressed Word, in which was the anger, and from which the love had fled, as it is in the earthly property?

24. Observe! The will and desire to eat of the speaking Word came into the soul’s property from the movement of the Deity. This happened when the Deity moved itself in the soul's essence—which was shut up in death in his mother *Mary's* essence or seed—and introduced the aspect of the eye of God in love into the dead soul’s essence. Having manifested love in death, then one divine property desired the other. The desire of the bodily hunger to eat of God’s bread or essence came from the baptism. When the water of the body—which was enclosed in death in the impression of the substance—tasted the water of eternal life in the Holy Spirit (namely, the Holy Spirit’s corporality or essentiality in the baptism), then the stimulus of divine hunger and the ardent desire for God’s essence arose in the flesh, like a divine hunger or a glimmering spark of divine property.

25. Now the man Christ must therefore be tempted in body and soul as to which he would eat. On one side, the expressed Word of love and anger was presented before his body and soul, in which the Devil would be lord and master and rule with all power. On the other side, the speaking Word in the love-property was presented to the soul and body.

26. Here now began the combat which *Adam* should have undergone in Paradise. On one side, God’s love-desire, which had manifested itself in the soul, eagerly reached for the soul and body’s property; it introduced its desire into the soul’s property so that the soul should eat of it and give the body manna <note>Divine food provided to the Israelites in the desert; here used as a metaphor for spiritual nourishment</note> from it. On the other side, the Devil, acting in God’s wrathful property, assaulted the soul’s property; he brought his imagination <note>In Boehme's philosophy, "imagination" is the creative or formative power of the will</note> into the property of the first principle, namely, into the center of the dark world, which is the soul’s fire-life.

27. Here was the contest over the image of God: whether it would live in God’s love or anger, in the fire or the light. For the property of the soul, regarding its fire-life, belonged to the Father according to the fire-world. Since the soul in *Adam* had extinguished the light-world, the light-world was again incorporated with the name *Jesus*, which occurred during the conception by *Mary*.
