O, you philosophers, take careful note of this: when this was done, Love transformed the fiery nature into its own Love-nature. Here, the Father gave the Fire-soul to the Son. Understand this as the fiery nature of the "expressed Mercury" <note>original: "expressed Mercury." In alchemy, Mercury represents the active life-force or "word" of a substance. Here, it refers to the human soul as a manifestation of God's power.</note> being given to the "speaking Mercury" <note>The divine Word or Christ.</note> in the Light. 30. At this point, God’s love gave eternal Love-life to corrupted humanity. Love gave itself entirely to the "Fire-Wrath" <note>Boehme's term for the harsh, consuming, and judgmental aspect of God's power that is felt as wrath by the fallen soul.</note> and transformed the wrath of the soul into a triumphant, joyful love. However, if the nature of the soul and body had obeyed the Devil within God’s wrath—and had made bread of the enclosed "Mercury" and eaten it—then the Will would have entered back into its own "self-hood" <note>The ego or independent will that seeks to exist apart from God's grace.</note> and could not have been transformed.

31. But because the Will entered into "resignation" <note>original: "Resignation" (German: *Gelassenheit*). This is a central concept for Boehme, meaning the total surrender of the self-will to God's will.</note>—into the speaking Word of God—and was willing to be and do whatever pleased God, the Will then left its self-hood. It passed through the wrathful death of God’s anger (the "expressed Word" which the Devil had poisoned with his imagination) and through the nature of the Wrath, and it blossomed anew with a new Love-desire in God. Here, the Will became Paradise: a divine love budding within death.

32. Now, because the Love-will was set in opposition to the poisonous "Mercury" of the soul’s nature in God's anger, the Devil came and said: "You are the King who has overcome; come and show yourself through your miracles and wonderful deeds." He brought him to the pinnacle of the Temple and said, *Fall down, so that men may see it; for it is written: He has given his angels charge over you, that they should carry you in their hands, lest you dash your foot against a stone.* Here, the Devil desperately wanted him to use the "Fire’s might" once more—the soul's self-hood in its own fiery nature—and to depart from resignation into an <insert>arrogation</insert> <note>Arrogating or claiming power for oneself without right.</note> of the self in its own Fire-will. This is exactly what the Devil had done, and also what *Adam* did when he turned his desire toward his own power in "evil and good" and wanted his eyes to be opened to both, as *Moses* writes concerning the Serpent's persuasion.

33. Here the fine, adorned Beast <note>The Serpent or the Devil.</note> came again and tempted the second *Adam* as well. God allowed this because the Devil claimed the "Fire’s Matrix" <note>The womb or fundamental source of fiery energy in the soul.</note> had pulled him, and he could not stand firm. This was now to be tested, for the Devil was an angel just like the human soul he had seduced. But the human nature in body and soul within the person of Christ had already cast itself into resignation, out of its self-hood and into God’s mercy. It stood still in that resignation—in the divine Will—and would not cast itself down or do anything except what God alone did through it. He said to the Devil: *It is written, You shall not tempt the Lord your God.* This is the same as saying: A creature of God should will and do nothing but what God wills and does through it. There must be no other God besides the Only One to rule and will; the creature must go and do as the Will-Spirit of God leads it. It must be God’s instrument, with which he works and does only what he pleases.

This, dear man, was the state of trial before the Tree of Temptation in Paradise. And here, that which the first *Adam* could not and would not do in divine obedience through resignation was fulfilled.

### Chapter 10

35. The Devil showed Christ’s human nature <note>original: "humanity"</note> all the riches of the world—everything that lives and moves in the expressed **Word** <note>The "expressed Word" refers to the physical universe created by God's speech</note> and all the power in outward nature, over which he calls himself a prince. However, he only possesses the part that exists in the wrath of death. He said to that human nature: *If you fall down and worship me, I will give you all this.*

36. He wanted humanity to abandon its state of resignation <note>original: "Resignation"; the spiritual act of yielding one's self-will to God</note> in favor of a desire for "propriety" <note>original: "Propriety"; here meaning selfish ownership or self-will</note>, and to desire to possess something of its own by claiming self-power in that cursed state of "Evil and Good." This would have been a delightful treat for the Devil; had it happened, he would have remained King, and his lies would have been the truth. This is also how Adam was corrupted: he entered into selfish "propriety," desiring worldly power and greed (which can be seen in the character of Cain). This greed is the heart of the poisonous <term>Mercury</term> <note>In Boehme's philosophy, "Mercury" is the principle of movement, desire, and life-force</note>—namely, its hungry desire, which creates its own essence according to the nature of its hunger. This essence is not Manna, but Earth. We can see this in the wild Earth—what it has become through the "enkindling" or movement of the Father in his fiery quality. In this inflammation (that is, in the poisonous wrath of the expressed Mercury), the Devil thought he would be a prince. He is indeed a prince in that same quality within the wicked, and also in the government of the world through wrath. But God holds him captive with the water and light of the "Third Principle" <note>The material world or nature</note>, so that he is not the prince of the entire dominion of the expressed Word, but merely the judge’s executioner. He must look for where the <term>Turba magna</term> <note>Latin: "Great Disturbance"; the awakening of divine wrath or destructive chaos</note> is ignited in wrath; he is busy only as far as that disturbance goes, and beyond that, his courage is cooled.

37. The Devil wanted to give Christ’s human nature this whole dominion to rule over, as a mighty God. Yet, the Devil himself only possesses it as part of the *Turba* in God’s wrath; he does not have full dominion over it. He wanted Christ to set his desire there and align his will with the Devil's. By doing so, the Devil would bring the creature's Mercury into a state of total power, making Christ a lord over both Good and Evil, having all things at his command to do with as he pleased—for this is exactly how Adam had been fooled.

38. Adam’s Mercury moved with desire into the "Impression" <note>The process of manifestation or becoming physical</note> from which cold and heat arise, and it focused its imagination there. Consequently, the qualities of cold and hot fire immediately began to boil within the Mercury of the human creature. Thus, outward heat and cold soon pierced into the ignited Mercury of the human nature, so that the body now suffers pain from heat and cold. Before this (when the human stood in the free will of God in a state of resignation), this quality was not manifest. In this way, Evil and Good began to rule and dominate in Adam.

<margin>Or Life’s</margin>
<margin>Or of.</margin>
39. For the center of wrath—the nature of the dark world—was made manifest in him as a poisonous, deathly quality. Even today, the Mercury in man is still poisonous and comes from a venomous source. While it is true that in the light of life it can be transformed into a "solar" quality <note>A state of light, clarity, or goodness</note>, the poison and quality of death still cling to it; it is the root of his light. We see this plainly: as soon as the instrument of his "martial" <note>Warlike or aggressive</note> fiery nature is even slightly struck or provoked, his evil, poisonous, fiery quality comes forward and shows itself. It inflames the body so much that it even trembles and shakes from the poison of wrath. It always wants to enter into the same ignited poison-source in the person who provoked it. It aligns its own malice with the malice of the one who started the conflict and struggles for its "rights" in that poisonous state. Then the body must use its strength as a servant to fulfill the will of that poison, arguing and fighting with its adversary, either beating them or being beaten. Whether it is by physical blows or by words, it all stems from this quality and the desire of this poisonous Mercury.

40. From this arises all war and contention: namely, from the dominion of God’s anger in the corrupt and ignited Mercury of the expressed Word, which plays out its delight and sport in the poisonous, wrathful nature of the dark world within man.

41. **Therefore the Warrior is a Servant of God’s Anger:** He is the **ax** with which the angry Husbandman cuts up the thorns and briars from his ground. He is the chief worker and achiever of God's wrathful anger. According to the **property of fire**, God’s anger wills it to be so, rather than his **love**. He who allows himself to be used for this purpose serves the **anger of God** according to the desire and property of the dark **fire-world**. Since the heavy fall of **Adam**, this has manifested itself in the human condition, turning man—the original angelic image—into a half-devilish mask <note>original: "vizard"</note> and likeness. In this condition and in the image of his own will, within the expressed, creaturely *mercury* <note>Böhme uses "mercury" to refer to the active, driving spirit or the "vital word" that gives life and movement to a being.</note> or vital word, man cannot inherit God’s kingdom. Instead, he must be born anew in his *mercury* and will, through and in Christ, within God’s love. This happens in the holy, speaking *mercury* and word of life, so that a new, obedient will—wholly surrendered <note>original: "resigned"</note> into God’s love—may come forth from his creaturely *mercury*. This new will neither desires nor does anything except what the will of the speaking divine *mercury* desires. In his own selfhood and selfish pride, his own will is as if dead, so that he may be the instrument of the Great God, through which God should act, work, and do however and whatever He pleases. Then God is all in all within him—his will and his deed—and he is a branch in the great tree which draws sap, power, and life from the **Tree of God**, growing and living in Him and bringing forth His fruit. Then the *mercury* of human life is a produced or expressed fruit that grows upon the Paradise-Tree of God. It gives forth its own note and sound, and strikes the **signature** in the speaking word of God—acting as God’s harp and lute to His praise. This is the purpose for which man was created, not that he should necessarily play upon the instrument of anger and death according to the Devil’s will.

<margin>* And all his legions of evil spirits.</margin>

42. **The Devil has made himself into such a lute player** who contrives and helps to perform and drive the music of wrath—that is, the music of darkness. He is the instrument and actor in the wrath of the eternal nature, which achieves its effects and goals with <sup>*</sup> him and in him as its instrument. The wicked man must do the same, as Saint **Paul** says: *The holy man is to God a sweet fragrance <note>original: "savour"</note> unto life, and the wicked a sweet fragrance unto death.* Everything that lives and moves must contribute <sup>y</sup> to the glory of God; one works in His love, the other in His anger. All things are generated and created in the infinite Being for the manifestation of the infinitely great God. From all the properties of evil and good, creatures were brought forth by the will of the speaking Word. The property of darkness and fire was in the "speaking" <note>the act of creation</note> just as much as the property of light; and therefore, there are both evil and good creatures.

43. **But the angels and men were spoken forth** <sup>z</sup> into the image of God’s love. They ought not to speak or incline their will toward the fire and the dark world, nor introduce their desire into it. They should not will to be their own masters at all, but should remain steadfast in surrender to the speaking will of God, as a form of that speaking will. They should have no inclination toward anything except the *Speaking* itself. In this role, they stand as an image or blueprint <note>original: "platform"</note> of the Expression—as a spoken word with which the speaking Word beholds itself in its own likeness. Through this, it manifests the eternal knowledge of the Eternal Mind, shapes the spirit’s will into a <sup>a</sup> form, and plays with it.

44. **As a painter <note>original: "limner"</note> who portrays his own image** and thereby sees what he is and what his form and features are; or as a musician composes a beautiful piece <note>original: "lesson"</note> or song and so plays and makes melody with his life and the will of his life—that is, with the sound of his own life’s *mercury* in the tune of the song, or upon some musical instrument as it suits his life’s *mercury*—with which his vital *mercury* rejoices and delights itself.

45. **In this same way, God created us** for his <sup>b</sup> consort of love, for his joy and glory, through which he exalts his speaking eternal word, or plays within that word with us as if we were his instrument.

46. Therefore, when this melodious instrument was broken in its sound by the wrathful power of His anger—that is, when man’s image chose to act in its own power, in both evil and good, in love and anger (namely, in its own self-will), and would not allow itself to be used for the purpose for which the *speaking Word* <note>original: "speaking Word"; the creative Logos or voice of God</note> had created it, and turned away from resignation <note>the mystical state of yielding one's will to God</note> into an arrogance of self, wanting to play however it pleased, now good, now bad—then this instrument was set against the love of God. In that love, no voice, breath, or smallest degree of anger is manifest, or can be, just as in the light of a fire, the pain of the fire is not manifest.

47. For the will of the human *Mercury* <note>in this context, "Mercury" refers to the active, vital spirit or principle of life in man</note> left the will of the divine *speaking Word* for its own self-will. Thus, it fell into the center of the mother <note>original: "Pregnatress"; the source or womb from which all essences arise</note> of all essences—that is, into *anguish, poison*, and *death*—where *God’s anger* (the *speaking in the wrath*) took *possession* of it.

> ->Oppressed in wrathful death and woeful scorn;<-

48. Thus, dear reader, it is clearly set before you why *Christ* was tempted: namely, to see whether the *soul* and the whole man (the *image* of the *speaking Word*) would now enter its original place again and be God’s melodious instrument in His love. This happened after God had reintroduced the spark of His love into the *human property* <note>the essential nature of humanity</note> and freely given Himself with that love back into it. The question was whether he would be a selfish seeker <note>original: "Arrogator"</note> in his own will, doing whatever his own "speaking" brought forth in the ignited *Mercury* of his life, or whether he would allow God’s will to strike the signature <note>the defining character or "tune"</note> upon his instrument, or the anger of God to strike it, as happened before [*namely, in the first Adam.*]

49. Here it was tested. Therefore the *Devil* (the *organist* <note>one who plays or directs the instrument of the soul</note> in God's anger) said to *Christ* that He should fall down and worship him, and then he would give Him all *dominion, power*, and *glory*. He claimed Christ should and could do whatever He pleased, living and delighting in His own self-will; He need only give the Devil His will, abandon *resignation*, and depart from God’s mercy and loving will. If this had happened, then the beautiful instrument would have been broken once again, and the human melody in God’s love and miraculous deeds would have ended. But *Christ* said, "*Get away from here, Satan! It is written: You shall worship the Lord your God, and serve Him only.*" Then the Devil left Him, and the angels came and served Him.

## The Magical Process.

50. In this (as has already been mentioned at length), the *Magus* <note>the spiritual seeker or practitioner of divine "magic"</note> must carefully consider his purpose and intent. He must not desire to possess the earthly kingdom with the greed of the Devil, nor should he "fly" [or cast himself down] from the temple, much less try to achieve his goals through the stones. He must remember that he is God’s minister and servant, not a selfish lord (who would only become a fool). If he wishes to help the poor captive—who is shut up in God’s anger and the bonds of darkness, swallowed by the curse of the earth—and deliver him from God’s anger, then he must think and carefully observe how God redeemed him through His entrance [*namely, into humanity*]. He must very exactly and intimately consider the temptation of Christ, rather than blindly groping after it with outward physical skill <note>original: "manual Art"</note>, thinking to himself, "I have a dead stone before [me]"—

52. For God did not take Man as he lay closed up in death and cast him into a furnace to be melted in wrath, as the false *Magus* <note>original: "Magus" — a practitioner of magic or alchemy; here, one who works without spiritual insight.</note> does. If you are a beast, then I do not give you my pearl; it belongs to God's children.

53. God must become man; man must become God. Heaven must become one thing with the earth, and the earth must be turned into heaven. Will you send one devil to another and expect to make an angel of him? In deed and in truth, I must laugh at such folly. The grain of wheat brings forth no fruit unless it falls into the earth; everything that will bring forth fruit must enter into the Mother from which it first came to be.

56. The Mother of all beings is *Sulphur* <term>Sulphur</term> <note>One of the three primary alchemical principles (Tria Prima); Boehme associates it with the "burning" or "lusting" quality of substance.</note>. *Mercury* is her life, *Mars* her sense, *Venus* her love, *Jupiter* her understanding, *Luna* her physical essence, and *Saturn* her husband. You must reconcile or lovingly betroth the man with the woman; for the man is angry, yet give him his dear spouse into his arms. But see that the spouse is a virgin, wholly chaste and pure; for *the Woman's Seed shall break the Serpent's head*—that is, the man's anger. The Virgin must be in real love, without any falsehood or unfaithfulness—a Virgin who never touched any man in anger according to his manhood. For the pure Deity espouses itself in clear love with humanity, even as *Mary* said, *"Be it unto me as you have spoken, for I am the Lord's handmaid."* And so the humanity assumed the Deity, and the Deity also assumed the humanity.

57. In the philosophical work, the chaste Virgin signifies the clear Deity. Humanity is *Mercury*, *Sulphur*, and *Salt*, both heavenly and earthly. The heavenly property has disappeared and is as nothing; the deadly property in the wrath is stirred up and lives for anger and in the properties of anger. Humanity—both in *Adam* and in *Christ*—was tempted. Do you ask with what? With the same opposite in the...

### Chapter 10: The Signature of All Things

Wrath, even with such a Devil as had all these properties in him, acting as a potent prince in all the properties of anger.

<margin>Or were.</margin>

58. The properties in *Sulphur* <note>original: "Sulphur"; in Böhme’s alchemy, Sulphur represents the substantial nature or the "womb" of existence from which life and desire arise.</note> were tempted with the likeness of the *Sulphur*; in the *Sulphur*, or from the *Sulphurous* property, the temptation did come and arise. Its forms are three-in-one in the Impression <note>original: "Impression"; the process of contraction or drawing inward, associated with the planet Saturn.</note>, which the philosophers call *Saturn*. The human spirit or will should open this in the property of *Venus* <note>Venus represents love, desire, and the light principle.</note> and therewith satisfy or feed its hunger—namely, the Fire. The other property was that he should live in his own awakened and opened *Venus* out of *Saturn*'s property, and aspire in self-will.

59. The third property was that he should introduce his will through the awakened love-desire back into the center—namely, into the *Sulphurous* Mother, which arises in the "Impression" within the anguish. And this he would not do, but the first *Adam* did it; and therefore God, when He would help him, tempted him in the *Sulphur* (the first mother of humanity) and suffered a wrathful devil, who was ignited in the *Sulphur*, to tempt him with his ignited malignity and malice in the *Sulphur*. Do you not understand this? What then shall I say more to you?

60. Sulphur is the womb into which we must enter if we would be born again. *Nicodemus* said well: *How can one being old enter into his mother's womb, and be born again?* But *Christ* said: *Except you be converted, and become as children, you cannot see the Kingdom of Heaven.* The self-will must enter again into the first mother which brought it forth—namely, into the *Sulphur*. By the "will," understand *Mercury* <note>Mercury represents the active spirit, the moving word, or the "worker" within the soul.</note>.

61. But now, who will persuade it to do so? For it has become a selfish thing, and must enter again into the mother and become nothing. This seemed a strange and wonderful thing to *Nicodemus*, but the Lord said to him: *The wind blows where it wishes, and you hear the sound thereof, but you know not from where it comes, or where it goes; even so is everyone that is born of God.* Behold, who persuaded the will of Christ in His humanity to enter again with the will into the Filiation <note>original: "Filiation"; the state of being a son, referring here to Christ’s divine sonship or adoption.</note>, as if into the mother's womb, and eat nothing for forty days? And He also desired to eat nothing, but remained in full, steadfast resignation in the Mother. Did not the Deity do it, which had entered into the humanity?

62. Thus likewise it goes in the philosophic work <note>The "philosophic work" refers to the Great Work of alchemy, which Böhme treats as a metaphor for spiritual transformation.</note>; therefore let the Artist <note>The "Artist" is the alchemist or spiritual practitioner.</note> observe well and rightly understand us: He must seek the evil, stubborn child (which has fled from the mother and entered into the center, desiring to be a selfish thing) in *Saturn*; for the wrath of God has shut him up with its "Impression" in the chamber of death.

63. Not that He has made him into *Saturn*, but He holds him shut up in the *Saturnine* death. The Artist must take that same child and bring him again into the mother's womb, and then send the angel with a message to *Mary*, and tell her: *She shall bring forth a son, whose name shall be called Jesus.* And if the mother shall yield her consent and receive the name *Jesus*, then the new humanity shall begin in the mother with the new child within the old apostate captive in the anger of God. The name *Jesus* will first give itself to the dead child which lay captive in *Saturn*, and eagerly draw the will of the evil, dead child to itself. This is the fair bride, who shows her crown of pearl to her apostate bridegroom; he need only receive her again, and she would give him her love. Now, if the apostate youth shut up in death does receive her again, then is the Artist well prepared and counted worthy by God to finish his purpose. Now the bride will love the bridegroom, and a virgin shall bring forth a son at which all the world will wonder; the virgin shall embrace the man, but he is a man and not a woman, and has the virgin's heart.

<margin>Royal Fort, dominant fortress.</margin>

64. Now he must be tempted, whether or not he will live in virgin-like chastity and in full resignation of his will to God; for he must be a valiant champion and destroy the devil's fortress of prey (which he has in his mother) in seven kingdoms; then...

# Signatura Rerum: Chapter 10

Let the Devil set his mother’s house on fire with his wrath and tempt him; he will now defend himself well enough with Christ against the Devil.

65. This being done, the young man <note>In Boehme's mysticism, the "young man" represents the soul or the regenerating alchemical substance.</note> with his virgin-like heart will wholly give himself up to the Mother. When the Tempter comes and assaults him, the Mother will wholly swallow him up into herself through the Devil’s wrath. He gives himself forth completely out of his own will into the Nothing <note>original: *das Nichts*, the divine void or the "Unground" from which all things originate</note>. Now, the Artist <term>the alchemist or spiritual seeker</term> thinks to himself, "I have lost everything," for he thinks that he has lost heaven, because he seeks "Nothing" and does not consider that a Virgin has now brought forth a child. But let him have patience; that which is impossible to the Artist is possible to Nature. After the night, it is day; when the Tempter has finished all his temptations, then comes the sign (or appearance) of the angels; then the Devil who has tempted him must depart.

<margin>Or kindred.</margin>
66. Let the Artist observe this well and send the Devil away. Let him allow the young man with his virgin-like heart to lie in his bed and eat his former food, for he has now become a physician to his sisters in his mother’s house. He will do great wonders in all the seven kingdoms of his mother (which are the seven forms of life <note>Boehme's "Seven Qualities" or "Source-Spirits" that govern all existence</note>) just as Christ has done.

<margin>Text: bodily.</margin>
<margin>By degrees.</margin>
67. In **Saturn**, he will raise the dead; understand that he will awaken the dead essence which held him captive in his former prison, for he shall change the earth into heaven. Just as the Virgin has raised up his will out of anger and into love, making him a worker of wonders, so must he also awaken—with his will, which is united to the Virgin’s heart—the form or "signature" in his mother’s womb. This is the womb from which she brought forth him and all her children. He must ignite it with the Virgin’s love and his own desire. This is effected and done in the *Sulphur* <note>The active, fiery principle in alchemy</note> of **Saturn** in the young man’s own personal property and in his mother. For before the espousing of the Virgin, the heavenly essence of the young man lies shut up in death. When God cursed the earth, then the heavenly, paradisaical body disappeared, and the "impression" of **Saturn** took possession of it until the restoration. At that time, God shall restore that which is hidden, so that Paradise springs forth afresh in the expressed Word <term>the manifest creation</term>, or so that the Artist opens the same in part by God’s permission.

<margin>Or Signatures.</margin>
68. In the second kingdom of the mother—namely, in **Luna** [the Moon]—he shall also do wonders; for Jesus fed five thousand people with five barley loaves. This is the work in the "essentiality" or corporality <term>the physical substance of the work</term>. *He turned water into wine.* These and similar miracles all belong to the Lunar property, where the champion with his Virgin opens Paradise and feeds the body where nothing else exists and where the outward **Mercury** has not labored or worked. Thus, the signatures in the Lunar property open themselves as if they are paradisaical; even then, the Artist thinks, "I am close to it," but he is still far from the end.

69. In the third kingdom of the mother—namely, in **Jupiter**—Christ made the babes and the ignorant (those of a very weak and average capacity) knowing and understanding. From poor fishermen, carpenters, and similar mechanics, he made Apostles and the most understanding men of all. Also, from poor, disrespected, and vilified people—such as women and simple folk—he made faithful, devout, dear, and godly children who understood the Universal <term>the Universal Medicine or the totality of Divine Wisdom</term> within themselves without any formal art.

<margin>Contemplates or beholds.</margin>
70. It goes the same way in the philosophic work: the essentiality which lies vanished in death—where the **Mercury** <note>The fluid, transformative principle</note> is entirely earthly, cold, and powerless—now arises in power as if the whole being and essence had become a new life. The Artist wonders at this and marvels at what it is or how it happens, and yet he also rejoices exceedingly that he sees the divine power spring forth before his eyes in a half-dead essence, even under the curse of God. He sees all four elements, each one apart, and sees how the wisdom of God represents itself therein as a harmony of joy. He sees all colors and the rainbow <note>The *Cauda Pavonis* or Peacock's Tail, a stage in alchemy where many colors appear</note> upon which Christ sits in judgment in the expressed **Mercury**.

The process involves awakening a "dead" earthly essence into a new, paradisaical life characterized by divine understanding and a harmony of colors.</summary>

# Chapter 10. The Signature of all Things.

71. The nature of this splendor arises out of the impression of *Saturn*; the benevolent *Jupiter* reveals himself to be seen in such a way as God will change the world and transform it again into Paradise. For this is the understanding found in the expressed Word, just as Christ made the foolish, unrefined, and ignorant people truly wise and knowledgeable in divine, real, and heavenly "jovial" understanding and knowledge. <note>original: "jovial" - here referring specifically to the planetary influence of Jupiter, associated in alchemy with wisdom, benevolence, and "Jove-like" joy.</note>

72. In the fourth kingdom of the Mother of all Beings—which is the *Mercurial* state in the <margin>orbit, rotation, or course</margin> wheel of the nature of life—Christ made *the deaf hear, the mute speak, and cleansed the lepers* from the poison of *Mercury*. All strokes, "the French Pox" <note>syphilis</note>, and poisonous sores arise from the Saturnine water in *Mercury*, which is called *Phlegm*. Christ healed all of these in the form or "Signature" of the young man and the virgin; for eternal virginity had wedded itself to the young man—namely, to humanity.

73. This also occurs in the alchemical <term>philosophic work</term>: the alchemist will see how the heaven separates itself from the earth, and how the heaven sinks back into the earth and changes the earth into a heavenly color. He will see how *Mercury* purifies the matter, how the purified colors appear in Antimony according to their nature, and how the miracle proceeds.

74. In the fifth kingdom of the Mother of all Beings, Christ expelled demons out of the possessed and healed the deaf in this form and property.

75. The alchemist will likewise see this in the alchemical work: how *Jupiter* within *Mercury* drives a black, flickering, fiery vapor out of the matter, which clings to it like soot. This is a "hunger" of the poison in *Mercury* and is very rightly compared to the Devil, for it shares his nature.

76. In the sixth kingdom of the Mother of all Beings—namely, in the wheel of life called *Venus*—Christ loved his brothers and sisters according to his humanity. He washed his disciples' feet and loved them even to the point of deepest <term>exinanition</term> <note>original: "exinanition" - the theological concept of Christ's voluntary "emptying" of his divine power to become human and suffer.</note>. He gave his life into the power of "Wrath" even unto death for them, and manifested himself among them as the Christ. When they perceived that the King had come to strip self-will of its might and dominion and destroy the Devil's kingdom, they cried out and said, *“We have no king but Caesar.”* They took him into their power in the dark of night, bound him, and brought him before their <margin>judgment seat</margin> council; they *mocked him, whipped him, beat him, stripped him of his clothes, and hung him on the cross*.

77. The alchemist will also see this very powerfully in the alchemical work. As soon as the dark fiery steam (the material Devil) leaves the matter, the Virgin *Venus* appears in her glorious and beautiful virginity. This signifies Christ's love, who humbled himself and manifested his love in our humanity. At that point, the alchemist thinks that he possesses the "philosophic child" and that he finally has the ultimate prize. But he "dances with the Jews" <note>An idiom for being prematurely confident or misled</note>, who thought when they had captured Christ, "Now we have him; we will keep him well enough." Thus the alchemist also thinks the work is finished and receives the "child." However, when he tests it, he finds he has *Venus* (a woman) and not the Virgin with the "Tincture" of the fire and light; he is <margin>deceived by the woman (or lets the woman deceive him)</margin> misled by the material appearance.

78. Now observe carefully: what do the properties of Saturn, Mars, and Mercury do when they see the Child—the Champion in royal color—and find that he does not exercise any external dominion or royalty with power and authority as they do, but will only rule with love within their poisonous, fiery power? They will not tolerate him.

79. For Saturn signifies worldly dominion, Mercury signifies spiritual dominion—namely, the <margin>priests who call themselves the ministers of Christ, but are not</margin> Pharisees—and Mars signifies the Devil. These three would not endure Christ among them, for he said that he was a King of Love and the Son of God, and that he had come to deliver his people from sin. Then the Devil thought, "Surely this does not suit me; you will lose your kingdom." And the worldly magistrates thought, "Is this a king and God's son? Then he will take away our power; we do not like this at all." And the rest are not...

The *Mercurial* priests thought, "This man is too lowly for us. We want a *Messiah* who might bring us worldly dominion and make us high and rich in the world, so that we alone may possess the world's honor. We will not receive him; he is too poor for us. We might lose the favor and respect of the worldly authorities <note>original: "Magistrate"</note> and be greatly harmed. We would rather stay in our power, respect, and authority, and abandon this beggarly King with his kingdom of love." In the same way, they are still of this mind today, and they treat the messengers he sends in the same manner.

80. It is the same in the philosophic work <note>The "philosophic work" refers to the alchemical process of transmutation, which Boehme uses as a metaphor for spiritual transformation</note>. When *Venus* <note>The principle of love and light</note> manifests herself with **love**—namely, in her own property within the three wrathful forms of *Saturn*, *Mars*, and *Mercury*—they cannot endure it. For it is completely against their harsh, dark, and fiery power, but especially against the poison of *Mercury*. They flash and strike with lightning against *Venus* and shoot their rays—the *Mercurial* poisonous rays—upon her, just as the Pharisees did to *Christ*. Meanwhile, *Jupiter* and *Luna* <note>The Moon</note> side with *Venus* and give her their power, for *Venus* stands here in the power of *Jupiter*. At this, the Pharisees laugh and think to themselves, "We are wise enough already; why do we need knowledge and understanding? We want power and honor." *Luna* represents the crowd of laypeople who stayed close to *Christ* while things were going well for him. So does *Luna* act toward *Venus* in her brilliance in the philosophic work, as long as *Saturn*, *Mercury*, and *Mars* do not interfere with or assault her. But when the power of wrath arrives, then *Luna* changes her will (that is, her color) and rises up, crying out with the rest, "Crucify him!" <note>original: *Crucifige*</note>. The artist will see this if he is chosen and deemed worthy by God for the work.

# The Eleventh Chapter.

### Concerning the process of *Christ* in his suffering, death, and resurrection:
### Concerning the wonder of the sixth kingdom in the mother of all beings:
### How "It is finished" <note>original: *Consummatum est*</note> was accomplished, and how it is symbolically fulfilled in the philosophic work.

<margin>*</margin>
1. **T**his must now be considered in this way: we should know that the essence of this world, together with man, consists of two properties: **fire** and **light**—that is, love and anger. Now, the fire is two-fold, and the light is also two-fold. There is a cold fire from the "impression" <note>Boehme’s term for the process where spiritual desire contracts and hardens into material density</note> and a hot fire from the power of *Mercury* in *sulphur*. Likewise, there is a cold **light** from the cold fire, and a warming light from the hot fire. The cold light is false, and the hot light is good. This is not because the cold light is false in its nature, but only in the impression within the cold *sulphur*. In the severity of the wrath, it turns into a false desire, namely a false love, which is contrary to meekness; for its desire is for *Saturn* and *Mars*.

2. It puts forth its sun—meaning its luster of life—in *Mars*. The warming light (which also receives its fiery severity in the impression in *sulphur* from *Mars*) brings its desire back into liberty, namely through dying in the fire, through <margin>It freely loses itself in the Nothing <note>In Boehme’s theology, "the Nothing" (*Ungrund*) is the absolute, undifferentiated source of all being from which everything emerges</note>.</margin> anguish. It wholly and freely gives itself up in the dying of the fire and abandons the property of wrath.

## Chap. 11.

3. And so it becomes a general joy, and not only its own, just like the sun that gives forth its shining luster universally. The sunshine itself is neither hot nor cold; only *Mercury* <note>In Boehme’s alchemy, Mercury represents the principle of life, movement, and the mediation between spirit and matter.</note> in the spirit of the "great world" <note>the macrocosm or universe</note> creates heat within the properties of *Mars* <note>associated with fire, anger, and force</note> and *Saturn* <note>associated with coldness, contraction, and melancholy</note>. For the sun kindles their desire, which makes them grow so very hungry, eager, desirous, and active that a fire is found within the light. This heat is not a property of the light itself, but of the "soul of the great world," which sharpens the pleasant light in its splendor until it is unbearable to the eye.

4. We must carefully consider and understand that if a different "fire-desire"—one unlike the outward life in *Mercury*—were to rule in the harsh wrath of outward nature, it would be an enemy to that harsh, cold, bitter, and fiery dominion and life. They would increase <note>original: "exalt [or exasperate]"</note> their wrath, eagerly desiring to be rid of it. This is exactly what happened when the divine "love-desire" manifested itself with great meekness to the false, cold, proud, and harsh fire-desire of the *Saturnalians*, *Martialists*, and especially the false *Mercurialists* <note>Boehme uses these terms to describe people dominated by the planetary qualities of Saturn (gloom/constriction), Mars (anger/conflict), and Mercury (fickle/poisonous movement).</note>. It was a great opposition and enmity to them that love should rule in the "death of poison" and dwell within it; they could not and would not endure this. For heaven had come into hell and would overcome hell with love and take away its power. This is seen in the person of *Christ*; he loved them, did them all kinds of good, and healed their diseases <note>original: "plagues [or diseases]"</note>. But because he did not arise from their wrathful power, and because he said he descended from above and was God’s Son, this was distasteful to the cold and hot power of "fire"—that he should rule over them with love.

<margin>¶ Manner, or humanity; condition</margin>
<margin>r Was born, or begotten.</margin>
5. The same thing happens in the "philosophic work" <note>The alchemical process of transmuting base matter into gold, which Boehme parallels with spiritual salvation.</note>. When the wrathful forms of earthliness—namely the outward *Saturn*, *Mars*, and *Mercury*—see the heavenly champion with the "Virgin’s property" <note>In Boehme's theology, the "Virgin" represents Divine Wisdom or the Sophia.</note> among them and perceive that he has a far different desire than they do, they become angry within themselves. For when the love-desire casts a glimpse on the *fire-shock* <note>original: "Fire-Flagrat" — a sudden, explosive burst or strike of fire or lightning.</note>, it awakens their own *fire-shock*, and then the wrath proceeds out of anxiety into love. From this arises a *death-shock* in the love; but since there can be no death within it, the love descends into the *fire-shock* and gives forth—or diffuses—itself into their desire, leaving its essence there. Thus, in their desire, they reach after its property in the *death-shock*. This is a *poison* to *death* and a *pestilence* to hell. In this ¶ property, death was deprived of its power in the hu- ¶ manity <note>referring to the human nature of Christ</note>. For when Christ shed his heavenly blood in the shock of death and left it there, the wrath of God was compelled to retain the heavenly *love-essence* within itself. At that very moment, the *fire-desire* in the ignited humanity was changed into a *love-desire*, and out of the *anguish* of death r proceeded a joy and strength of divine power.

6. I will now give the seeker <note>original: "Well-wisher"</note> a fundamental understanding of how it happened with *Christ*, and how, in the same way, it happens in his philosophic work; both follow exactly the same process. *Christ* overcame the wrath of death in the human property and changed the Father's anger into love within human nature. The philosopher <note>The alchemist.</note> likewise has the same goal: he wants to turn the wrathful earth into heaven and change the poisonous *Mercury* into love. Therefore, observe us correctly here; we will not write in parables, but as clearly as the *sunshine*.

7. God intended to change humanity back into the divine, heavenly property (after it had become earthly and had awakened the poisonous *Mercury* within the love-property, which then devoured that love and changed it into itself). He meant to make a heaven out of the human "earth," turning the four elements into only one in *one* desire, and changing God's wrath in human nature into love.

8. Now, His anger was a power of fire and wrath that was ignited in man; therefore, there had to be a true earnestness to withstand it and change it back into love. Love had to enter into the anger and completely surrender itself to the wrath. It would not have been enough for God to remain in heaven and only look

Just as fire is not made better by the light—it still holds its wrath within itself—but when a meek substance (such as water) enters the fire, then the fire goes out.

9. In the same way, heavenly divine substance <note>original: "essentiality"</note> (meaning heavenly water, which the spiritual power <note>original: "tincture"</note> of the fire and light changes into blood) must enter into the wrathful fire of God and become the fire's food. This was so that the fire of God might burn from a different substance; for water alone could not have done it. The fire does not burn in the water, but the meek, oily property of the fire and light in the substance of divine gentleness in the love-desire—that is what accomplished it.

<margin>] Last *</margin>
10. The human life-fire consists in the blood, and within it rules the wrath of God. Now another blood, which was born out of God’s love-substance, must enter into the angry human blood; they must both go together into the death of the wrath, and the wrath of God must be drowned in the divine blood. Therefore, the outward humanity in Christ had to die, so that it might no longer live in the property of wrath, but that the heavenly blood’s *Mercury*—that is, the speaking Word—might alone live in the outward humanity. It would rule solely in unique divine power in the outward and inward humanity, so that the self-will might cease in the humanity, and God's Spirit might be all in all, and the self-will only His instrument, through which He does whatever He pleases. I say, let the self-hood be solely God's instrument and be completely in resignation <note>original: "resignation" here refers to the mystical concept of *Gelassenheit*, or the total yielding of the individual will to God</note>. For God has not created man to be his own lord, but His servant; He will have angels under obedience, and not devils in their own fire-power.

11. Now, when His love would give itself into death and deprive death of its power, then the two worlds—namely, the Father's fire-world with the outward visible world, and also the divine love-world with the divine heavenly substance (that is, with heavenly flesh and blood, as well as with corrupted flesh and blood)—were formed into one person. God became man and made man into God. The seed of the woman (meaning the heavenly virginity which disappeared in *Adam*) and also the corrupted man's seed in the anger (meaning *Mary’s* seed) were formed into one person, which was Christ. The seed of the woman—meaning the virgin of God, or the heavenly substance—should bruise the head of the serpent (meaning the wrath of God in the corrupted man). The "head" is the power of God's anger. The divine man (meaning the divine property) should change the earthly into itself and turn the earth into heaven.

12. Now, when this person was born, heaven stood within the earth of man. Yet the incarnation alone could not have accomplished it; there had to be another serious trial. For as long as Christ walked on the earth, the humanity which came from *Mary’s* property was not almighty, but the humanity from God was omnipotent. They were set opposite each other in two principles, yet not shut away from one another; rather, both were manifest in each other—love against anger, and anger against love.

13. Here was the trial of the combat between the two, from which also proceeded the temptation of Christ. When the divine world overcame, then great wonders broke forth through the outward human world. But all this could not fully accomplish the work; there had to be an even greater earnestness. The human property—the expressed Word <note>the Word as manifested in creation</note>—was still stirring in the inflammable anger. The human *Sulphur* <note>In alchemical terms, "sulphur" represents the combustible substance or soul-fuel of a being</note> had to be changed into the heavenly part. Thereupon the human self—the expressed *Mercury* <note>In this context, the active, moving spirit or "speaking" force within the soul</note>—was terrified when, upon the Mount of Olives, the heavenly world in its love wrestled with the anger in the human world (that is, with the self-hood), so that the person of Christ sweated blood. Even there, one was dismayed by the other: the love was dismayed at the horrible death into which it must wholly yield and give itself with the divine substance to be swallowed up by the anger; and the anger was dismayed at its own death, in that it must lose its power within the love.

# Chapter 11. The Signature of all Things.

14. Hence, the entire person of *Christ* said, *"Father, if it be possible, let this cup pass from me; yet not as I will, but your will be done."* The *Love-World* in *Christ* said, "Can it not be otherwise than that I must drink down the cup of your anger? Then your will be done." And the *Anger* said, "If it be possible, let this cup of love pass from me, so that I may take revenge and rage in the wrath of man because of his disobedience." This is similar to when *God* said to *Moses* (who stood in the Spirit of *Christ* as a "type" or symbol of *Christ* before *God*), *"Let me alone so that I may devour this disobedient people."* <note>See Exodus 32:10. Boehme views Moses as a precursor to Christ’s role as a mediator between God’s wrath and humanity.</note> But the name *Jesus*—which had embodied itself in *Paradise* through the promise of the *Woman's Seed* <note>Genesis 3:15; the first prophecy of a savior.</note> in the goal of the human and divine *Covenant*—would not allow him. For the humility of the name *Jesus* has always interposed itself against the wrath of the Father—against his *fire-property*—so that his *fire* might not ignite the semi-poisonous *Mercury* in man. This happened except in rare cases when *Israel* walked entirely in wrath and disobedience, as can be seen in the stories of *Korah, Dathan, and Abiram*, and also *Elijah*. <note>Korah, Dathan, and Abiram were swallowed by the earth for rebelling against Moses (Numbers 16).</note>

15. <margin>* A</margin> So it was here on the *Mount of Olives*: the *Anger* wanted to live in the *fire's power* within *man*, and the name *Jesus* placed itself into that *Anger*. Here there was no other remedy except that the name *Jesus*, in divine *love* and heavenly *essentiality*, had to resign itself completely to be devoured by the *Anger*. The *Son* had to be, and was, obedient to the angry *Father*, even to the *Death of the Cross*, as the Scripture says.

16. The dear *Love-Humility* and *Meekness* allowed itself to be scorned, mocked, spit upon, and judged by the *Anger*; that is, the *Jews* had to execute the justice of *God*. Because sin was committed through *man's self-centered action*, then *death* and *sin* had to be wiped out through *man's self-centered action*. <note>Boehme argues that since humans chose their own will over God's, the restoration required a human will (Christ's) to freely surrender back to God.</note> *Adam* had introduced his will into the poison of the outward *Mercury*; <note>In alchemy, Mercury represents the vital, moving, and often volatile spirit of a substance.</note> therefore *Christ* (the *Love*) had to freely give up his will into that same poisonous *Mercury*. *Adam* ate from the evil *tree*; *Christ* had to eat of *God's anger*. As it happened inwardly in the *spirit*, it also happened outwardly in the *flesh*—and so it also occurs in the alchemical work <note>original: "philosophic Work"; the process of creating the Philosopher's Stone.</note>.

17. *Mercury* in the alchemical work represents the *Pharisees*; <note>Mercury acts as the "accuser" or the volatile element that reacts against the pure substance.</note> he will not endure the *Love-Child*. When he sees it, he causes it trembling and anguish. *Venus* <note>In this context, Venus represents the "Love-Child" or the soft, receptive, and pure quality of the metal/soul.</note> also stands dismayed at the poison of the angry *Mercury*. They react to one another as if sweat were dropping from them, as the *Artist* <note>The alchemist.</note> shall observe.

18. *Mars* says, "I am the lord of *fire* in the *body*; *Saturn* is my strength, and *Mercury* is my life. I will have none of this *Love*; I will devour it in my *wrath*." This represents the *Devil* in the *Anger of God*. Seeing that he cannot do it, he raises up *Saturn* (meaning the *Impression*, <note>Boehme uses "Impression" to describe Saturn's contractive, hardening force that gives physical form.</note> which signifies the worldly *government* or *magistracy*) and reaches out with it toward *Venus*. Yet he cannot pull her into himself, for she is a deadly poison to him. *Mercury* can endure this even less, for *Love* took away his *dominion*—just as the *High Priests* thought that *Christ* would take away their *government* because he said he was *God's Son*.

19. Thus, *Mercury* is irritated by the *child Venus*, because *Venus* has fully revealed herself and freely given herself up. They may now do what they please; she will even go into the *dragon's mouth* if he only opens his jaws. *Mars* (within *Mercury*) does not understand this; instead, they take the beautiful child and shoot their venomous *darts* against it. They bind it with *Saturn's power* in their wicked *bonds*, and the *Artist* will see how they surround the *color of Venus*.

20. *Mars* first brings the work to *Mercury* (since he is the *life*), just as Christ was brought before the *High Priest*, who must examine and test the beautiful child. But he hates it; he cannot reach into the *heart* to find its *love-will*. He only judges it externally because it does not share his *property*. Even though it appears in the same form as *Mercury* himself, it possesses a different *power, virtue, and will*.

21. But because there is another *Mercury* that lives in its *love* within the *child Venus*, he cannot kill it. Instead, he brings it to *Saturn*, just as the *Jews* brought *Christ* from

<margin>• In the heat of his trial.</margin>
<note>In this chapter, Jacob Boehme uses the biblical story of Christ’s Passion as an allegory for the "Great Work" of alchemy—the purification of base matter into gold, or the transformation of the soul.</note> Caiaphas brings the Child to Pilate, who represents Saturn. Saturn takes the Child, but because he is a lord of the "impression"—that is, of darkness—he does not care at all for the Child's inner nature, but only for dominion. He seizes the Child with his dark influence and strips it of its beautiful Venus garment <note>original: "Venus Garment." In Boehme's system, Venus represents the principle of love and beauty.</note>. When Luna <note>the Moon</note>, with the white splendor of the Sun, sees this, she hides herself—just as Christ’s disciples fled. Even the enraged, common multitude, who boasted that they would stand by him during the cross and persecution, fly away when the earnestness begins. For Luna is inconstant; she does not hold the Sun's heart within the flame of love. Then Saturn, with his sharp and "thorny" influence, places Sulphur upon the Child—the mother of all beings—along with a purple-colored robe of her own nature, which contains and hides the wrath of Mars.

22. When Mars (representing the Devil’s crew) and Mercury (representing the pride of life) see that Venus wears her royal garment—understand this as the purple robe of Saturn and Mercury mixed with the Sun's color and fiery Mars, and decorated with Mercury's sulfur-color in a bright blaze—the artist <note>The "Artist" is the alchemist performing the work.</note> must observe the material <note>original: "Materia"</note> closely. He will then clearly see the color of the Venus-like property, as has been described.

23. When Mars, Mercury, and Luna also see this, they cry out *crucifige* <note>original: Latin for "crucify him"</note>, "Away with him! He is a false king in our clothes; he is a man like us and wants to be God." That is, they cast their poisonous desire through the purple garment onto the Child. Thus, the artist will see the Child appear in its own form, as if covered in streaks from the poisonous rays of Mercury and Mars, which they project through Saturn’s influence—just as Pilate whipped Jesus. The artist will see the prickly crown of thorns standing very sharp, pressing into the nature of the Child. He will also see that Venus does not move herself at all, but stands still and allows herself to be treated this way.

24. Furthermore, we are to understand that Adam had taken on a cold, false love. With this, he presented himself before God as if he possessed his own power and will, and as if he were God’s child, though he was merely mocking God. This is how the desire for love appears when it is trapped in the state of death.

25. Thus must the "Second Adam," Christ, take all of this upon himself. He must enter into the same shame and scorn, be clothed in a purple garment like a king of this world, and be mocked. Adam had put on the "purple garment" of the outer world’s self-power, reflecting his own ego; here, it was exposed before the anger of God. The white garment that Herod put on Christ to mock him represents a cold, false love—a cloak of dishonesty. In this cloak, humans boast as if they were angels, putting on Christ’s purple mantle and white robe, covering themselves with his pure, snow-white garment (his suffering and death), while still harboring the "Man of Falsehood"—that is, a false love—underneath a veil.

26. Christ had to embody this figure, and it was represented on his body; for he was to overcome and kill the Man of Falsehood residing in human nature. Thus, the situation was fully presented before God. Christ had to be called and reviled as if he were the same as Adam; the innocent one took the blame upon himself.

27. This is also how it goes in the alchemical work <note>original: "philosophic Work"</note>, when the curse of God’s anger in the earth is to be changed into love. Since Mercury sets the "Child of Love" before Saturn, and Saturn cannot and may not test it, Saturn puts the purple-colored garment with stripes onto it and sends it before the Sun’s <note>original: "Sol's"</note> splendor, which glimmers in Mars. The Sun then applies its white color (the "Lunar" property), the purple disappears, and the Child stands in a simple, lunar-white color—appearing very humble and without luster. The Sun would like to see this Child display its golden color, for it senses a "solar" virtue <note>original: "solar Virtue" or divine power</note> in the Child, and therefore it gives...

## Chapter XI.

...it the white color from the property of the eternal liberty. The Child should only give the power of the fire’s center to it—namely, the divine might. Then it would be like the Sun, and would be a lord over the *Sulphur* of *Mars* and *Mercury*. However, it would only be a lord over the essence of the outward world, a governor in the "Wrath," just as *Sol* <note>original: "Sol"; the Sun, representing gold in alchemy and the divine light in theology.</note> is.

28. But *Christ* said to *Pilate*, "*My Kingdom is not of this world*," and he would not answer *Herod* anything when he put this white clothing on him, nor when he wore the purple robe. For both the purple robe and the white clothing were false; they were put upon him to disgrace and mock him because *Adam* had put them on and proudly paraded <note>original: "pranked up"</note> in them with falsehood. *Christ* would perform no miracle <note>original: "Sign"</note> in those robes before *Herod*, though Herod desired it. Through this, the shame of Man—who was an image of God and yet had made himself a false king—was represented before God’s face. This is like how a poor sinner confesses and displays his abominations before God when he commits to abstinence and repentance.

29. Thus, *Christ* represented the abominations <gloss>or sins</gloss> of Man to his Father in this false garment. He stood before Him as a disgrace <note>original: "Ignominy"</note> and confessed the sins of Man to his Father in the place of all men. When his Father beheld him through His perception <note>original: "Imagination"</note> in this garment, He would have none of this robe. Therefore, *Pilate* had to pull it off him again and set him before the *Jews* in his own form. But they cry, "*Away, away with him, he must be put to death*." For his Father willed it so: that he should give himself up to death in His Wrath and drown that same wrath.

<margin>Hold [the text].</margin>
30. And *Pilate* condemned him to death, for he would not acknowledge him as a King. It happens the same way in the philosophic work <note>This refers to the "Great Work" of alchemy: the process of purifying matter into the Philosopher's Stone.</note>. *Saturn* will not receive the Child, for it is not of his property; *Mars* and *Mercury* likewise will not have it in their property. But what do they do? The Child is among them, and they would gladly be rid of it, but they cannot. They grow angry and enraged, like the *Jews* against *Jesus*. They take the Child into their arms—namely, into their false, poisonous, angry desire—and seek to murder it. They completely sting and pierce through the *materia* <note>Matter or substance.</note> of the Child with their sharp, fiery, and poisonous rays, which act as three sharp nails.

31. One of these nails is *Saturn*—the impression of the dark world, representing the Wrath of the dark world. The second is *Mars*, which signifies the Devil—the Serpent’s property in the anger of God. The third is *Mercury*, which signifies the false life—namely, how the wrath of God is ignited in the "expressed Word" <note>In Boehme's thought, the "expressed Word" is the created world and human nature as a manifestation of God's voice.</note> within human nature.

32. These three nails pierce through the property of the Child. Thus *Venus*—the essence of Love—wholly yields itself to the three murderers. It completely gives up its jovial <note>original: "jovial"; here referring to the property of the planet Jupiter, associated with joy and expansion.</note> life as if it died. The *mercurial* life of human nature (meaning the Child’s power) also falls to the three murderers in its "mother’s house"—that is, in the physical essence where the young man received his Virgin <note>In Boehme’s mystical theology, the "Virgin" represents Divine Wisdom (Sophia), which joins with the human soul (the young man).</note> and where God became Man.

33. Now, when the heavenly body and the earthly body both yield to these three murderers, the image of *John* and *Mary* appears by the Cross as a symbol <note>original: "Type"</note>. For the young man’s life, and also the Virgin’s life within the young man, has freely surrendered and given itself forth. Now the two properties—the divine and the human—divide themselves into the form of each power. An artist <note>The "Artist" refers to the alchemist or the spiritual seeker who understands these transformations.</note> may see this if he has the eyes and understanding for it.

34. And here, when *Saturn* with his dark sharpness, *Mars* with his wrath, and *Mercury* with his poisonous life powerfully enter the property of *Venus*, then the Wrath forces itself into the Love, and the Love into the Wrath. They become essentially mixed, as if one is absorbing the other. Here, wrathful Death is terrified at Love, so that in the act of "dying," it falls into a faint <gloss>or a swoon</gloss>, for it loses the power of its wrath. Meanwhile, Love exists even within the source of Wrath and Death...

# Signature of All Things: Chapter 11

The <term>Flagrat</term> <note>original: "Flagrat"; Boehme uses this to mean a sudden, explosive flash or stroke of spiritual fire</note> becomes powerless [as if in a swoon] and gives itself forth entirely into the stroke of death. Even then, the heavenly essence—that is, the heavenly blood—flows from it into the property of the third <term>principle</term> <note>original: "Principle"; here referring to the physical or natural world</note>, which is the "young man." Here the Virgin gives her pearl to the young man as his own property, and God and man become one.

35. For the Virgin’s blood, coming out of the divine essentiality, now drowns the young man’s blood (his self-centered nature) with its love-essence. The "three murderers" <note>Boehme’s term for the first three harsh properties of nature that "kill" the spiritual life</note> surrender their life in the blood of the Virgin. Then the red glow from the fire and the white glow from the life of the champion arise together: life arises from the wrath, and meekness arises from the love. Both the life of anger and the life of love ascend together as one single life, for in death they become one. Death dies away in love and becomes, within that love, the life of the divine kingdom of joy. This is not a total extinction, but a free surrendering of its power, might, and will—a transformation. The Virgin’s blood changes the human blood, which was dead toward God, into a heavenly blood. The selfish life of the young man dies, and the life of the Deity remains fixed and steadfast, for it stands by its own nature in the *Nothing* <note>The "Nothing" or "Unground" is Boehme's term for the absolute, undifferentiated source of God</note>.

36. And here, dear seeker, when you see the crimson-colored blood of the young man arise out of death joined with the Virgin’s white blood, then know that you possess the <term>Arcanum</term> <note>original: "Arcanum"; a secret or great mystery of nature and spirit</note> of the whole world. You have a treasure in this valley of misery that surpasses the value of gold. Take it and value it as more excellent and sovereign than anything else that shall arise from death. If you are born of God, then you will understand what I mean.

37. For this is the *type* <note>a symbolic pattern or foreshadowing</note> of Christ, showing how Christ has drowned sin and the ignited anger of God within the human nature. It is not merely a symbolic offering, for if it were, Moses would have accomplished it. It is not just a verbal forgiveness, as <note>original: "Babel"; Boehme's term for the confused and divided institutional churches</note> Babel teaches. No. The human will must enter with all its powers into this death, into this blood—that is, into the highest <term>Tincture</term> <note>original: "Tincture"; in alchemy and Boehme's thought, a spiritual force that transforms and perfects matter</note>.

38. The purple robe that Christ wore could not do it, and the white, hypocritical coat of the Pharisaic priests could not effect it either. No flattery or demure hypocrisy is of any use here. No comforting words, soothing talk, or giving God "good words" are effective here. The crafty, malignant man must be put to death in Christ’s blood; he must be drowned in the Virgin’s blood.
> *The seed of the woman must bruise the head of the serpent;*
The will must entirely disclaim and depart from its selfish property. It must become like an ignorant child and enter wholly into God’s mercy, into the virgin-like blood of Christ, so that sin and the poisoned <term>Mercury</term> <note>the restless, driving force of the soul</note> may be drowned in its <term>Mars</term> <note>the fiery, angry property of the soul</note>, so that the "white lion" may arise. For the lion which now appears in white and crimson-red is the *Mercury of Life*—the expressed Word, the soul—which before was a wrathful devil in its self-centeredness, ruling and dominating in the anger of God through the three forms of the poison-source: <term>Saturn</term>, <term>Mars</term>, and <term>Mercury</term>. Now it is the white, scarlet-colored lion from the house of David and Israel, fulfilled in the covenant of promise.

39. **Note well.** But so that we may satisfy the seeker, we will further show the whole foundation, even to the resurrection of Christ: When the Jews had hung Jesus upon the cross, and he had shed his human and heavenly divine blood, and drowned the <term>Turba</term> <note>original: "Turba"; the spirit of confusion or the "disturber" that brings judgment and destruction</note> in the human blood, then Jesus said:
> *Father forgive them, for they know not what they do.*

40. When Jesus had broken the power of death in humanity and removed the "Self," he did not then completely discard the human nature in which death and the anger of God resided. Instead, he then truly assumed it for the first time. Understand this: he even then truly took the outward kingdom into the inward kingdom. For the outward kingdom was born as a wonder out of the eternal wisdom in the speaking Word, and spoken forth into a form as a manifestation of the Deity in love and anger, in good and evil. So it was that Jesus would...

## Chap. 11.
## The Signature of all Things.

...not that the outward form <note>original: "Type"</note> of the wonders in the likeness of God should perish [or quite vanish]; but the wrath which had overpowered the love in man should be forgiven—that is, it should be given into the *Nothingness*, namely into the freedom <note>original: "Liberty"; Boehme refers to the *Ungrund*, the divine nothingness before manifestation</note>, so that it might not be manifest in its own self-centered nature <note>original: "Self-Property"</note>. It must be a servant, and only a cause of the fiery love and divine joyfulness. Nothing should perish [or be lost] in man, for God had created him in His image.

<margin>Are drowned.</margin>
41. Thus, let the philosopher observe that when the three murderers—namely, *Saturn*, *Mars*, and *Mercury* <note>In Boehme's alchemy, these represent the restrictive, aggressive, and volatile qualities of nature</note>—sink into the crimson-colored blood of the Lion, they do not perish; but they are pardoned. That is, their wrath is changed into a love-desire, *namely* out of *Venus* into *Sol* <note>original: Sol (the Sun, representing gold or divine light)</note>; for when the fiery desire enters into the watery desire, then a shining—that is, a glorious splendor—arises from and in the fire; for *Venus* <note>representing love and the water element</note> is white, and the fire-desire is red.

42. Now it is changed into one color, which is yellow—that is, white and red both in one color—which is the majestic luster. For when *Mercury* is changed into the power of joy, then the multiplication <note>an alchemical term for the increase of the power of the philosopher's stone</note> arises. He changes his mother, in whom he lay shut up in death, into *Sol*; he makes the earthly heavenly in one quality <note>original: "Property"</note>, as the Virgin was. For here the Virgin loses her name, for she has given her love and pearl to the champion, who is now called the white lion—as the Scripture speaks of the Lion of the house of *Israel* and *David*, who should demolish the Devil's kingdom and destroy hell, which is to say, break the anger of God and change it into love.

43. This champion or lion is neither man nor woman, but he is both. The tincture <note>original: "Tincture"; the spiritual essence that transforms matter</note> of the fire and light must come into one, *namely* of the essence which is *Venus*, and of the spirit which is *Mars* in *Mercury*. The Father's love and anger must become one thing, and then this one thing is called the Kingdom of Joy. So long as it is separated, there is in the thing only anguish and torment and mere desire; but when it burns in one will, it is a joyful proceeding forth from itself. And this outgoing property is called the Holy Ghost, *namely* the life of the Deity.

44. Therefore know that the blood of the Virgin and the young man must both be shed together so that the fire-lion might die. This was manifest in the human quality, so that the love of the Virgin might change his wrath in her dear love-blood into her own quality, and obtain the soul from the young man. For in *Adam* the Virgin <note>Boehme's concept of the "Sophia" or heavenly wisdom that Adam lost</note> disappeared, for the soul departed from its love-will and out of its surrender <note>original: "Resignation"; the German *Gelassenheit*</note> into its own will, and became disobedient to God.

45. Here the Virgin again takes the soul into herself and gives it her crown of pearl, as to a noble champion, and calls him by his own name: the white lion or champion. O you children of men, observe it, I beseech you! Open the gates of the world in your heart; open them wide so that the King of Glory may come in—even the great champion in battle, who has deprived death of its might, destroyed the hell in God's anger, and made paradise out of the world.

46. O you wise seekers, how the Lord opens his windows! Why do you sleep in the desire for much increase [in your greed], which is multiplied in the wrath? Only enter into divine surrender <note>original: "Resignation"</note>; you may partake of that which the powers of heaven are able to afford. If you only forsake your selfishness, then the earth shall become heaven to you, says the Spirit of Wonders; but you shall not obtain it in your wicked ways and covetous doings.

47. [The thief on the left hand was] not capable of his bloodshed; and the other at the right hand, who was converted from his sins to Jesus, said, *Lord, remember me when you come into your kingdom*; to whom Jesus answered, *Truly, today you shall be with me in Paradise.*

48. Thus we are to rightly consider that when the wrath of God is drowned in the blood of Christ, so that it changes its power into love, it is only then that Paradise is open again. For when Jesus had infused <note>original: "tinctured"</note> the human blood (which was corrupted in sin) with the Virgin’s blood <note>In Boehme’s theology, the "Virgin" often refers to the Divine Sophia or the pure, eternal spirit of wisdom, rather than just the earthly Mary.</note> in love, then the Virgin received the manhood—namely, the self-hood—into her Virgin's love. This was Paradise: a habitation of God with and in man, where God dwells in humanity and is all-in-all within it.

49. This also occurs in the "philosophic work" <note>Boehme uses "philosophic work" to refer to both alchemical transmutation and the spiritual transformation of the soul.</note>: when *Mars* and *Mercury* die according to the property of the dark impression of *Saturn*, then *Venus* takes them into her love-blood. *Venus* gives her love into the poisonous fire-desire: she gives herself wholly into the fire of MARS in MERCURY and yields herself fully to be their own. But seeing as *Mars* and *Mercury* become powerless (in terms of their fire and poison) within that love, the love and anger then change themselves into one essence and one desire. Here, when the fire—that is, the fire-desire—gives its desire over to love, then love says: *Today you shall be with me out of your fire-anguish in Paradise*—namely, in joy. That is, you shall be changed in me. And here *Venus* gains the soul in the philosophic work, so that *Mars* and *Mercury* become her soul, and the strife ceases; for the enmity is appeased and quelled. Thus the "Child" <note>The alchemical "Child" or "Lapis" represents the perfected result of the process.</note> subsists immovably in the fire without any change; for *Mars* does not annoy it at all, and likewise *Mercury* and *Saturn* do not hurt it, for they are in the "Child" at the end of nature, where there is no more *Turba* <term>The spirit of turmoil, destruction, or divine wrath that breaks things apart.</term>.

50. *Mercury* is pure in *Saturn*; he has no more poison with which to create soil <note>original: "soil [or rust]"—referring to the oxidation or corruption of metals.</note> in the water—namely, in the salt of *Saturn*. Let both the philosopher and the theologian observe this: that in Paradise there is a perfect life without any shadow of change, and also without any false or evil desire. It is a continual day, where the paradisical man is as clear as transparent glass, in whom the divine Sun shines through and through, like gold that is thoroughly bright and pure, without any spot or foulness.

51. *And when Jesus knew that all was finished, he sees his mother and John his disciple standing by under the cross, and says to his mother: "Woman, behold, this is your son!" And to the disciple: "Behold your mother!" And immediately the disciple took her into his own home.*

52. This is an excellent type <term>A symbolic representation or prophetic model.</term> of how Christ has forsaken this world—namely, the human self-hood—and has gone again to the Father. He saw his mother according to this world and his disciple (who was his uncle according to the outward humanity from his mother's side), yet said to his mother: *Woman, behold, there is your son.* He meant: "I am no longer your son according to my outward humanity; it is changed into God’s Son and is no longer of the world, but lives to God. But since you are to remain yet in the world, take John—who is not yet changed—to be your guardian; and you, John, take her as your mother." And he immediately took her to himself.

53. This is the type of the Christian Church upon Earth. For we, the poor children of Eve, are not immediately changed in our outward form; we must also pass into death and decay <note>original: "putrify"</note> so that the wrath in the flesh may also rot and decay, and the spirit might rest in the death of Christ until the general resurrection and transformation <note>original: "transmutation"</note> of the outward man. At that time, the "earth" of man shall be transformed into heaven, and the mirror <note>original: "Mirror [or Type]"</note> of wonders shall appear within it.

54. Thus he commanded his disciple to take care of his mother. His mother is the Christian Church upon Earth, in which the children of God are born according to the spirit. The disciple should take care for, guide, and lead them until the full number of humanity has been gathered out of the flesh. Then the spiritual body shall arise and shall be tested in Christ’s death, in his entrance into the anger, where he—

## Chap. 11.
