55. But in this lifetime, though the spirit be <margin>x. Changed</margin> changed in the divine power, and the spirit be baptized with the Virgin’s baptism and puts on the image of Christ internally—namely, *Venus's* body <note>original: "Venus's Body in the Love"; in Boehme’s system, Venus represents the planetary property of meekness and divine love</note> in the love—yet *Adam* <note>the fallen, mortal nature of humanity</note> is not capable of it until he also enters into the transmutation of Christ, which comes to pass in death [or in the dying to this mortal life].

<margin>y. Taken, or received.</margin>
56. But in the meanwhile, *John*, as the teacher of Christ in Christ's stead, must provide for the outward mother according to the outward man, and feed and teach the lambs of Christ with Christ's spirit. And it exactly shows us how the outward man is not God's mother; for Christ separates himself from his outward mother and gives her to *John*. He has put on the eternal mother—namely, the Father of the eternal birth—and therefore they do very ill who honor and worship the outward mother of Christ as "God’s Mother."

57. The whole of true Christendom is Christ's mother, which bears Christ within her. And *John*—that is, the servants of Christ—are her nurses, who take care of the mother of Christ as *John* did. He immediately received the mother of Christ and provided for her as her son, and not as her lord; for Christ said to him, *Behold, she is your mother*. So should all the disciples and teachers of Christ do: take care of poor Christendom as sons, with great humility toward the mother, providing for and cherishing her with diligence and caution. They should serve her with all discreet modesty, courtesy, and humility, feeding and comforting her with the spirit of Christ—not as the priests in *Babel* <note>the "City of Confusion"; Boehme uses this to describe the corrupt, divided institutional churches of his day</note> do, who ride over her as wealthy, rich, domineering masters. They wish to be lords over the mother and only seek honors and to fatten their bellies in pleasure, living in strife and contention. These, by whatever name or title they hold, are not *Johannites* <note>those who follow the humble, loving example of the apostle John</note>, but are the poisonous *Mercurial Pharisees* <note>leaders characterized by intellectual cleverness and volatility ("mercurial") rather than spiritual peace</note> in whom there is nothing but mere anguish, vexation, pain, and torment, where one property continually torments, envies, and hates the other, and considers it false. And yet they all come from only one root and have only one will, except that one color does not shine quite like the other.

58. For *Saturn* is not as *Jupiter*; *Jupiter* is not as *Mars*; *Mars* (the fire-spirit) is not as the light of the Sun; and the Sun is not as *Venus* with her meek water-source; and *Venus* is not as *Mercury* with his sound, for she is meek and still, while *Mercury* sounds and sets up his note. And *Mercury* also is not as *Luna* <note>the Moon</note>, which as a simple body gives a physical form to all the rest for their manifestation. One is far different from another and does not have the same property or will; and yet they are in the center of the essence—namely, in *Luna* and *Saturn*, in the property of the soul and body—all of them one and the same lump. Thus the partial, sectarian "Mercurialites" and *Baal's* servants are divided in these properties; they are the *Pharisees* who judge and condemn Jesus in his members.

<margin>z. In war for their proud, unrighteous mammon, and in bitter strife about their outward worship of Christ.</margin>
59. They wrangle and contend only about the church, and yet none will take care of the poor, forsaken mother of Christ. They are mad in their martial and <margin>z.</margin> mercurial contest and are not *Johannites*. They do not enter into the sheepfold through the door of Christ in Christ's spirit; they are wolves, lions, and bears—yes, foxes and fearful hares who fly from and forsake the mother. Their rise and origin is out of *Babel*, where they continually contend, wrangle, grin, and bite one another over the "letter" <note>the literal text of scripture, used as a weapon rather than understood spiritually</note>. Every one wants to be lord and master over the letter, transposing and placing it as he pleases, only for the honor, applause, and pleasure of this world. They do not consider that the mother is a widow, and that Christ has left and ordained them to be such caretakers for her as *John* was.

# Signatura Rerum: Chapter 11

...shelter themselves where they please and regard these evil beasts no longer. Instead, follow *John*, the disciple of Christ, who teaches love and humility.

61. O you dear and worthy Mother, are you not the only one? Why do you allow the "lions" to rend and tear you into pieces? Christ is your husband; all these others are strangers and hired servants, unless they walk in your filial love and humble themselves toward the Mother, providing for her as ministers. Otherwise, they are all wolves, bears, and tearing lions. Even if there were many thousands of them, not one is any better than another unless he comes forth in the spirit of *John* and takes care of Christ’s Mother, providing for her with earnestness in *Christ's* Spirit. If he does not have this Spirit, he is not called by *Christ* to be a guardian or curate <note>A "curate" here refers to a spiritual caretaker or priest.</note> for the Mother. Rather, he is a "Mercurialite" <note>original: "Mercurialite"; in Boehme's terminology, this refers to someone driven by a restless, worldly, or legalistic spirit rather than divine peace.</note>, a Pharisee, such as *Christ* called the "seed of serpents" and "generation of vipers," who crucify Jesus in his members.

<margin>Altogether.</margin>
62. And thus the philosopher must consider and well observe *Christ's* Mother, whom he recommended to *John’s* care. He must likewise act like a *John* and know that his business concerns the Mother, and that his work in this world is not entirely heavenly. He will not manifest Paradise so clearly that God will appear and be manifest face-to-face in his work. No, he remains in the "Mother" (nature), yet he obtains the Universal <note>The "Universal" refers to the Alchemical Tincture or the "Philosopher's Stone," a substance believed to heal all things and perfect nature.</note> within the Mother. For the Mother of *Christ* obtained it also, as it was said to her: *You are blessed among all women.*

63. Similarly, the philosopher reaches for the blessing in this valley of misery, so that he is able to bless his corrupt body—that is, "tincture" <note>To "tincture" in alchemy is to infuse a substance with a spiritual or medicinal power to transform and heal it.</note> it and free it from sickness, even to the limit of the highest constellation according to *Saturn* <note>Saturn often symbolizes the limits of time, contraction, and the physical decay of the body.</note>. Therefore, let him beware of covetousness, for by greed he introduces the *Turba* <note>original: "Turba"; the spirit of destruction, wrath, or chaotic "uproar" within nature.</note>.

64. By the example of *John* and the Mother of Christ, he is to know that the Kingdom of God and the kingdom of this world are two separate things in his work. God's Kingdom lies shut up within the Mother (that is, within his work), which he must take care of. He must be a minister to it and not a "Lord" of the Mother, but an alms-giver and not a gatherer of treasure and wealth—not a covetous muck-worm <note>A "muck-worm" is a derogatory term for a person obsessed with amassing worldly wealth.</note>. Furthermore, no one shall attain to this or understand our meaning if they will not be a guardian of the Mother. <margin>Understanding of folly.</margin> The Most High has placed a barrier before the foolish understanding so that it remains blind until it is weary with seeking; I speak from the foundation of truth.

65. And when Jesus had commended his Mother to *John*, he again turned his desire into the "Mother" of the human property <note>In this context, "human property" refers to the essential nature or characteristics of humanity.</note> and said, *I thirst.* He thirsted after the members of human nature and desired the salvation of mankind—that is, the health of his members (meaning his children, who should be reborn in him). And the Jews gave his humanity gall and vinegar to drink; and when he tasted it, he would not drink it.

66. Here again is the outward type, showing what was happening inwardly: The Name *Jesus* (the Love of God which had entered into humanity and espoused itself to it) thirsted in a love-desire for the corrupt humanity. It longed to taste the pure water of humanity within itself. However, the wrathful anger of God, which was ignited in the human property, offered itself along with the human property to satisfy that thirst of love. When the Love-Desire tasted of it, it would not drink it. Instead, it sank down into it, wholly resigned or freely yielded up. It united and essentially inclined itself into the anger of God as a full and perfect obedience, being fully and freely given over as a personal sacrifice into it.

67. This was the *Flagrat* <note>original: "Flagrat"; Boehme uses this term to describe a sudden, transformative spiritual flash, crack, or shock wave that occurs when two opposing principles (like love and wrath) meet.</note> of the wrath when Love entered into it. Because of this, the earth trembled and the rocks split apart, for death was terrified by the Life. Here, the property of the awakened wrath separated itself into the Center—that is, into the first principle, the "Fire-Root." And now, from that Center, there proceeded a hunger for the New Birth in the human property.

## Chap. II. *The Signature of all Things.*

...towards Death was made into a hunger for Life; for Love infused the Anger, so that the Fire-desire toward the dark impression became a desire for Life.

68. Understand it correctly here: God the Father, who gave his dear Heart into humanity to help mankind, did now thirst after humanity—namely, after his Heart or Word of Power. And the Deity in humanity—namely, the Heart of the Father—thirsted after the Father; and the Love, or the essence of the Light, thirsted after the fire’s essence. For the soul’s essence in Adam <note>The first human, representing all of humanity's original state</note> had departed out of the Love-Essentiality (in which Paradise consisted) into selfishness, and had become disobedient to God. Thereupon, the essence, life, and being of the Light and Love died in its growth—that is, it withered as to its vegetative life <note>original: "vegetative Life"; refers to the natural, flourishing growth of the spirit</note>, or its heavenly growth, blooming, and the perception of the paradisiacal source; instead, it awoke and arose to the earthly world.

69. Here the Father brought the soul, which had entered into his wrath and had manifested itself in his anger, back into Love—namely, into the disappeared paradisiacal image. And here the dark world was terrified in <term>Death's Flagrat</term> <note>original: "Death’s Flagrat"; in Boehme’s philosophy, a "flagrat" is a sudden, explosive flash or crack—like lightning—that marks a transformation or a discharge of spiritual energy</note> at the Fire-Flagrat, which arose in Love within Death as a joyful flash. This joy-flash entered into the dead bodies of those in Israel who had hope (who hoped for the Messiah) like a sound of the power of God, and awakened them from death.

70. This flash tore in two the <term>Veil in the Temple</term> <note>A reference to the curtain in the Jerusalem Temple that separated the "Holy of Holies" from man; its tearing symbolized direct access to God</note>—namely, the **Veil of Moses**, which hung before the clear face of God so that man could not see God. Therefore, man previously had to serve him with offerings and symbolic types of this final discovery, in which God manifested himself again in humanity. This flash broke the symbolic "type" found in the offerings and sacrifices, revealed the clear face of God, and united human time with eternity.

71. Everything that the Jews did outwardly to Christ was a symbolic "type" of the inward reality—namely, how things went between God and humanity, or between eternity and time. The Jews gave Jesus gall and vinegar in his thirst; both of these properties are a **Mercury** in the **Sulphur** of **Saturn**—that is, in the "impression" <note>original: "impreſſion"; refers to the spiritual state of contraction, hardening, or ego-centeredness</note>. This is the very image and full resemblance of the soul’s property as it is in itself alone, void of the other properties of Love.

72. God gave this property of the soul back into his Love—bringing Death into Life. He brought the disappeared Love-essence (which the Word of God had taken to itself in the essence and seed of Mary and quickened to life) into the property of Anger, into the soul’s essence—namely, into the center of the fire and the dark world. Whereupon, the soul-like fire and dark world became an exceedingly triumphant, joyful, paradisiacal life. And here the Champion <note>Refers to Christ as the victor over death</note> rebuked Death and Hell—namely, the dark world in the soul—and said: *Death! Where is your sting now in man? Hell! Where is now your victory in the wrath of the poison-source in the expressed Word or Mercury? All is now dead. O Death, I am a death to you; Hell, I am a conqueror to you! You must serve me for the kingdom of joy; you shall be my servant and minister to the kingdom of joy; you shall kindle the flames of Love with your wrath, and be a cause of the spring in Paradise.*

73. Thus we give the <term>Philosopher</term> <note>original: "Philoſopher"; here meaning an alchemist or a seeker of the hidden truths of nature</note> to understand our meaning and the deep ground of Nature. He desires to seek and open the disappeared essence of the Earth, which lies shut up in death—namely, in the curse of God. The **Veil of Moses** hangs also before him, and a very sincere earnestness is required to tear the veil in two so that he may be able to see the face of Nature; otherwise, he is not fit for it.

74. And as it went in the humanity of Christ, between God’s Love and Anger, where both were transformed into one, so it is likewise in the "Work of Nature." The poisonous **Mercury** in the **Sulphur** of **Mars** and **Saturn** <note>Alchemical symbols representing active, forceful energy (Mars) and cold, restrictive, or leaden energy (Saturn)</note> gives its <term>Lunar Menstruum</term> <note>original: "Lunar Menſtruum"; an alchemical term for a dissolving solvent or the receptive, feminine principle of the moon</note>—namely, the greatest poison of the dark source—into the property of **Venus**, when **Venus** thirsts after the fire of...

74. Love then causes <term>Mercury</term> <note>original: "Mercury"; in Böhme’s alchemy, this represents the active, communicative, or "word" principle.</note> to give its poison into the thirst of <term>Venus</term> <note>original: "Venus"; representing the passive, desiring, and loving quality.</note>, and Venus's thirst gives itself wholly to the poison as if it died. It completely yields up its desiring life, whereupon a great darkness arises in the <term>philosophic work</term> <note>The alchemical process of spiritual and material transformation.</note>. For the <term>materia</term> <note>original: "Materia"; the substance or matter being transformed.</note> becomes as black as a raven because Venus has resigned its life, from which the <term>splendor</term> <note>original: "Glance [or Splendor]"; the radiant light of the spirit.</note> arises. This was seen in the case of Christ, when the sun lost its light and there was a great darkness contrary to the common course of nature.

75. For when the inward Sun gave itself up to the Anger—namely, into the darkness of God—then the outward sun, which receives its power and luster from the inward as a <term>mirror</term> <note>original: "Glass"</note> or resemblance of the inward, could not shine. This is because its root, from which it shines, had entered into the darkness in the place of this world, intending to turn the darkness in the curse of God into light; namely, it would make the place of this world into Paradise again.

<margin>c Or Number three.</margin>
76. Thus likewise, the sun of the outward world (which is a figure of the inward, all-essential Sun) had to stand still with its splendor in the darkness from the sixth hour until the ninth. This is the very time of Adam's sleep, when he entered with desire into the center of eternal nature—namely, into the birth where love and anger separate into two centers. He wanted to test the cold and hot fire, which took hold of him and worked powerfully within him. Here there are three hours according to the <term>Ternary</term> <note>original: "Ternary"; referring to the Trinity or the number three.</note>, and in the grave three days according to time—namely, according to his humanity.

<margin>d Mirror, Resemblance.</margin>
77. When Adam was in the image of God, and was neither man nor woman but both, he stood forty days in Paradise without wavering. When he fell, he remained in that state until the third day—namely, forty hours in sleep—until God made or built the woman out of him. Thus, Israel had to be tempted forty days on Mount Sinai to see whether they would live in obedience to God amidst wonders and mighty acts. When that could not be, God gave them the Law of his covenant as a mirror of what was promised in the covenant. Therefore, the temptation of the body was upon them for forty years, so that the body had to eat <term>manna</term> <note>The miraculous food provided by God to the Israelites in the desert.</note> to test whether man could be cured. And when the body (or outward person) could not stand, then Joshua brought them through the water with the covenant of the <term>type</term> <note>original: "Type"; a person or event in the Old Testament seen as a symbolic precursor to Christ.</note>. There, Israel had to serve with sacrifices in the covenant as a symbol of the final accomplishment until the time of restoration arrived. Then the valiant champion <note>Referring to Christ.</note> stood in battle for forty days in the wilderness during his temptation, and endured the first trial of Adam in Paradise. The three hours of darkness on the cross are the three hours of Christ's temptation when the Devil tempted him. Again, the forty hours of Christ in the grave correspond to the forty days of Adam in Paradise, the forty days of Moses upon the Mount, the forty years in the wilderness, and the forty days after the Resurrection before the Ascension—they are all one and the same. Now, when the champion had endured Adam's trial, the soul was tempted for forty days in its human property to see whether it would eat of God’s Word and live in full, resigned obedience to the will of God, being a true image, likeness, and similitude of the Divine power in the unsearchable eternity, according to the Trinity of the Deity.

78. In the same way, the philosopher should observe that the essence of time also exists in such a property. For man was created out of the essence of time into an image—as an extract of all essences, a complete image and likeness according to both time and eternity—ruling and existing in time and in eternity as an instrument of the great, infinite God, with whom (by and with His Spirit) He would make and do whatever He pleased.

79. Now man is the instrument of God, by whom He manifests His hidden nature both in man's own human property—namely, in the essence and image of God—and

...then also through Man, acting as the instrument within the Mother of all Beings, as in the grand Mystery—that is, in the Soul of the great World.

<margin>d Things to be joined together.</margin>
80. Humanity has power, to the extent that a person acts as an instrument of God in divine obedience and is guided and led by His Spirit, to bring the Earth—which currently exists under God’s curse—into His blessing. Through this power, one can turn the anguish of death into the highest triumphant joy within the outward, generative Mother <note>The "pregnant Mother" refers to the *Materia Prima* or the physical world in its creative, unfolding state.</note>. However, the person does not do this alone; rather, their will labors alongside their understanding to join together the compressed elements <note>original: *Compacta*</note> that belong together, such as life and death, which stand opposite to one another. These the person must join and bring into unity by the same skill <note>original: "Art," likely referring to the alchemical or spiritual process</note> through which time and eternity are united in the Man Christ, and through him, united in all those who submit their will to it.

<margin>e With.</margin>
81. In his work, the person will see everything that God did for humanity when He brought it back into the Universal realm—that is, into Paradise. He will see how Wrath devours and swallows the fair *Venus* <note>In Böhme’s system, Venus represents the quality of love, sweetness, and desire.</note> into its sharp, thorny essence, and how *Venus* fully yields herself up. He will see how the Wrath also dies away within *Venus* and becomes as dark and black as a coal; for death and life lie together in death—that is, in obedience to God. They both remain still before Him and allow the Spirit of God to make of them and with them whatever He pleases. He introduces them again into the eternal will of God for which He first created them. Thus, the essence stands again in the beginning, in the order God created. It must only remain in its "impression," in the "Word of Making" <note>original: *Verbum Fiat*, Latin for "Let it be done," the creative word of God</note>, until the day of God’s separation, when God will change time back into eternity.

82. And when Jesus had drunk the cup and tasted the vinegar mixed with gall in his outward humanity, and felt the wrathful anger of God inwardly in the property of Love—that is, in the Virgin <note>Böhme often uses "the Virgin" or "Sophia" to represent Divine Wisdom or the pure, heavenly humanity.</note>—then the whole man Christ said, *“My God, my God, why have you forsaken me?”* For God’s speaking Word stood still for a moment in the human property, and the new-born spiritual substance <note>original: "Essentiality"</note> which had died in Adam and was brought back to life in Christ, cried out with him, *“My God, my God, why have you forsaken me?”* For the anger of God had entered into the image of the divine substance through the soul’s property and had devoured the image of God.

<margin>f The Sun.</margin>
83. At this moment, the image within the creaturely soul cried out, *“My God, my God, why have you forsaken me?”* For the human image which disappeared in Adam, and was revived again in Christ’s incarnation, was meant to bruise the head of God’s anger in the fiery soul and change its fiery power into the Sun <note>original: *Sol*, representing the divine light or gold in alchemical symbolism</note>. Here, the speaking Word of God forsook it, and it fell into the soul's wrath where it felt God's anger; for the speaking Word brought it through that anger into death, and out of death again into the solar life—meaning into the eternal Sun.

84. Just as a candle dies in the fire, and out of that death the light and power proceed—namely, the great painless life—so out of Christ’s dying and death, the eternal divine Sun should and must arise in the human property. But the selfishness of the human property—that is, the soul’s own self-will to live in its own fiery power—must die here and be drowned in the image of Love. The image of Love must also resign and give itself up to the wrath of death, so that everything might fall down into death and arise in God’s will and mercy through death, in the paradisical source of Resignation <note>original: "Resignation," translating Böhme's concept of *Gelassenheit*, or yielding the self-will to God</note>, so that God’s Spirit might be all in all. Hell’s eye must see through the Love, just as light shines out of fire, and fire from darkness, and darkness takes its origin from the eternal desire.

<margin>g Or wild.</margin>
85. And as Adam changed the likeness of God into the form of dark death, so God changed that likeness again through His fiery wrath out of death and into the light. He drew the likeness forth again out of death, just as a blossom grows from the harsh earth.

86. Thus it goes likewise in the philosophic work <note>The "philosophic work" refers to the Great Work of alchemy, which Böhme treats as a physical manifestation of spiritual truths</note>; *Venus* <note>In Böhme’s system, Venus represents the power of love and the light of the second property of nature</note> is forsaken when she receives the three wrathful properties into herself in wrath. Their wrath—that is, death—devours her life, whereupon she loses her color; yet she becomes a death to the three forms in the wrath, for she drowns death with love. Thus life is made a death to death—that is, *to the wrath*—and now they both lie in the will of the Eternal Nature,
<margin>Goes out.</margin>
namely, in the *Verbum Fiat* <note>Latin: "The Word made" or "Let it be done," referring to God's creative command</note>, which <gloss>he</gloss> proceeds with them in the divine way, in the same manner as it proceeded forth into essence in the beginning of the creation. For in the beginning, Paradise—the Universal—was manifest, and love shone through death or anger. It must be so again: *Venus* must become the eye or sight within the wrath, and then out of *Saturn, Mars*, and *Mercury* there will be a *Jupiter*. *Mars* becomes the Sun, and *Saturn* the Moon; thus *Mars* shines with the Sun out of *Saturn* in *Luna* <note>Latin: the Moon</note> from *Venus*'s eye, and all seven <note>The seven properties of nature or planetary spirits</note> are only one. Thus the strife has an end, and all is accomplished until the resurrection of the body.

87. And when Jesus had drunk the cup and said, *My God, why hast thou forsaken me?* then he said, *All is finished*—meaning the work of man's redemption—and he said further, *Father, into thy hands I commit my spirit*, and bowed his head and gave up his spirit. Here the whole life of Christ resigned itself into the Father's desire, namely, into the will of the Eternal Nature. He fully gave the will of his self-hood—his creaturely <note>the will belonging to a created being rather than the Creator</note> will—back into the center, into the first Mother from which the soul-like creature was produced; that is, into the grand mystery of eternity. The self-will must again enter into nature's end, so that selfishness may wholly die, so that God's eternal will and spirit may be and do all in all within humanity, and so that the creature might afterwards be only his instrument, wherein he might do and work according to his good pleasure. And thus God the Father has, in Christ's death and entrance into our humanity, again received our self-hood into his will. To make this possible, he first tinctured <note>permeated or transformed with a spiritual essence</note> humanity with the deity, so that humanity might be a pleasant, sweet savor and offering to him in his power, for before this, death lay before it.

88. Here love destroyed death and opened the firm seal, so that the will might again enter into that which it was before it became a creature. We all must follow him upon the path which he has opened for us; no one can see God unless God first becomes man in him, which is brought to pass in the desire of faith. Even then, the corrupt will (which is caught in the death and anger of God, and which flourishes in earthly essence and brings forth fruit unto death) must be wholly mortified and fall into free resignation, into the will and mercy of God. Then one's own will is with and in Christ at nature's end in the grand mystery of God—that is, in God's hands. God's hands are the eternal desire, or the eternal will, which is unchangeable. Thus
<margin>fick <note>likely "fixed" or "finally"</note></margin>
the creaturely self-will dies; it enters wholly into the *Nothing* <note>The "Nothing" or Unground: Böhme's term for the absolute, undifferentiated source of God's being</note>, so that it might no longer live to itself, but to God.

89. It happens this way also in the philosophic work: when the artist <note>The alchemist or seeker</note> has first seen great wonders which the creaturely and natural will has wrought in the power of *Venus*, to the point that he supposes he is close to the goal, even then nature first dies in his work and becomes a dark night to him. The property and power of all the

All freely yield themselves over as one dead essence, and there is no longer any effective working within it; all is divided in the crown into the thousandth number, and then it is again in the mystery at nature's end, just as it was before it came into creaturely being. Understand this: the essential desire—namely, the expressed *Mercury* <note>The "expressed word" or the manifest power of movement and communication</note>—must again come to the end of its selfishness and resign itself into the speaking Word.

# The Twelfth Chapter.

## Of the seventh form in the Kingdom of the Mother; how the seventh kingdom, namely, the Kingdom of the Sun, is again opened and made alive; set forth in parable, or by way of similitude of Christ's Resurrection.

<margin>Soulish Deity;</margin>
<margin>towards light</margin>
1. <image-desc>A decorative woodcut drop cap for the letter 'W'. It contains a heraldic shield with a heart and the initials 'W' and 'M', supported by cherubs or angelic figures amidst scrolling foliage.</image-desc> **WE** are not to think that when Christ died the natural death in the human property, that he died as to his created soul, much less as to the Deity; also he did not disappear or die in the heavenly essence and being <note>original: "Essentiality"</note> in the heavenly tincture <note>In alchemy and Böhme's theology, a "tincture" is a spiritualizing essence that transforms whatever it touches</note>. This cannot be; only the will and rule of the self, namely, of the outward world, which ruled in man toward his own will and the own powers of the selfish creature (wherein man was disobedient to God)—he gave that wholly into the Father's hands, namely, into the end of nature, into the Father's great mystery <note>original: "Mysterium Magnum," the source of all things</note>. This was not so that it should be dead, but so that God's Spirit might alone be the life of it, so that the divine rule might be in Christ's person, and so that the Eternal Father might rule and reign with his eternal Spirit in his image. Therefore, God has determined to hold the last judgment through this Jesus.

2. Now, the creature of Christ does not act alone, but God acts in his image through the creature in the rule of his eternal Spirit of all the three principles <note>Böhme’s "three principles" refer to the dark world of fire/will, the light world of love/spirit, and the outer material world</note>, which is the life and rule of every being, in each thing according to its property.

3. And understand us correctly: when Christ died on the cross, the name *Jesus* did not also die; it was the name that destroyed death and permeated <note>original: "tinctured"</note> the expressed word—namely, the form of the Deity (or the formed word), which is the soul—with love. No, it cannot be that eternity dies; only the spoken word dies, which stands again in the desire of the speaking, namely, in the *Fiat* <note>Latin: "Let it be," the creative command</note>, which changes itself in its own speaking, namely, in its self-desire, and brings its own sound into another form and source than the speaking word had spoken it, and set it forth with the *Verbum Fiat* <note>Latin: "The Word: Let it be"</note> into a form, signature, and will. This is as Lucifer with his royal throne and *Adam* also did, when they both departed out of resignation <note>Surrender of the self-will to God</note> into self-hood; the instrument wanted to be the master.

<margin>man standing before God to <unclear>return</unclear> <unclear>soul</unclear></margin>
4. The outward, working, sensitive life, wherein the anger of God was set on fire, did wholly die away. It was not that it should become *nothing*, but it fell into the *Nothing*, namely, into God's will, into God's working and feeling, quite apart from the will of the outward world (which is both evil and good). It fell so that it might no longer live to the world—that is, to the *Astrum* <note>The stars or celestial influences</note> in the boiling <note>original: "Walm"</note> or seething power of the four elements—but the life of the outward world died to the Eternal Father's nature in the boiling of the pure divine element.

5. Thus the true human life fell immediately again into that place from where *Adam* had brought it, namely, into Paradise; because of this, Christ said to the thief, *Today you shall be with me in Paradise*. It fell into *Adam's* death, by which he died to Paradise, and—

# *The Signature of All Things:* Chapter 12

...sprang up in *Adam’s* death as a new creature out of the old, just as a branch springs from a grain of corn. And this it did from the might and power of the speaking Word <note>original: "speaking Word"; the creative Logos or divine command of God</note>, which by grace had entered with living substance into the vanished heavenly substance of man. It had freely given itself into the center of the soul-like nature, and also into the wrath of the anger and death in the flesh, and changed the anger into love, and infused the corrupt blood in the anger with that love.

6. The divine tincture <note>original: "tincture"; an alchemical term for a spiritual essence that transforms and purifies whatever it touches</note> infused the human; the divine Sun entered into the human; the divine Sun entered into *Adam’s* night—namely, into *Adam’s* sleep. God’s Sun, with the name *Jesus*, entered with *Adam’s* soul and humanity in *Christ’s* person into death; understand this as entering into *Adam’s* sleep.

7. When *Christ* died, then *Adam* also died to his self-hood <note>original: "Self-hood"; the state of being centered on one’s own ego rather than on God</note> in *Christ’s* death. The name *Jesus* was in *Christ* the "Serpent-Destroyer" in *Adam’s* humanity. *Christ* entered into the image of the first *Adam*, so that the first *Adam* in the humanity of *Christ* became that same *Christ* and Serpent-Destroyer—not indeed in the same individual person, but in the same properties of soul and body.

8. The first *Adam* fell into sleep—namely, into the impotence of the divine world—and died in the death of death. The second *Adam* entered into the death of death and took the death of death captive in himself—that is, in the humanity of *Adam*. He was a death to death itself and brought forth life out of death into eternal liberty. He arose in divine omnipotence in the essence of the first *Adam*. God’s Spirit in the speaking eternal Word brought *Adam* out of death in *Christ’s* humanity. *Adam* arose in *Christ’s* humanity, and all the children of *Adam* who are partakers of *Christ’s* kingdom arise in *Christ*; all rise in *Christ’s* flesh and blood, soul and spirit, but every one in the specific body which he had here, which was mortified in *Christ’s* death.

9. Every person is a particular twig, but there is only one tree, which is *Christ* in *Adam* and *Adam* in *Christ*; only one, not two. There is only one *Christ* in all *Christians*, so that I may say: *If I am dead in Christ to the world, I am that same Christ—that is, a branch on the same tree.*

10. But seeing that I, in the outward man, still live in my self-hood, I must also die with the outward man in *Christ’s* death, and arise and live in him. Now, therefore, I live with the will of faith in the mind in *Christ*, and I am a Christian in the will of the mind in the desire of faith. I receive *Christ* with his humanity into my will and cast my will into his death; and thus my inward man is also dead in *Christ’s* death and lives no longer to self-hood, but I am resigned <note>original: "resigned"; having practiced 'Gelassenheit' or the yielding of the self-will to God</note> in him and lie buried in his death. But seeing he has risen in God’s will, I also live in his resurrection in him. However, my earthliness in its selfish property lives to the earthly world until it also dies completely to self-hood and enters into resignation and decay <note>original: "Putrefaction"; an alchemical term for the decomposition of the old state necessary for new growth</note>. Then *Christ* will awaken it through my inward man, which now lives in him.

11. Just as he has risen from the dead, even so shall I, who shall die to earthliness in him—namely, in my first father *Adam*, in the name *Jesus* as a Christian in *Christ*. My twig, which withered in sin on the tree, shall obtain strength and sap in the name *Jesus* unto life. I shall and must spring forth afresh with my humanity in him as in my stem, who has become a heart and power in my father *Adam*, and I shall bring forth fruit to the praise of God.

12. The spirit of my will, which is now in *Christ’s* humanity and lives in *Christ’s* spirit, shall, by *Christ’s* power, give sap to the dry tree. Thus it shall rise again at the last day at the sound of the trumpet of the divine breath in *Christ’s* voice—which is also my voice in his breath—and spring afresh in the tree *Christ*, namely, in Paradise. Paradise shall be in me; everything that God has and is shall appear in me as a form and image of the divine world’s being. All colors, powers, and virtues of his eternal wisdom shall be manifest in me and on me, as his likeness. I shall be the mani-

...manifestation of the spiritual divine world, and an instrument of God’s Spirit, in which he makes melody with himself. With this voice—which I myself am, as if with his signature—I shall be his instrument and the organ of his expressed Word and voice. And not only I, but all my fellow members in the glorious, tuned instrument of God: we are all strings in his joyful concert; the Spirit from his mouth strikes the tune and note on our strings.

13. And therefore God became man, so that he might again repair his glorious instrument which he had made for his praise—which had perished in relation to him and would not sound according to the desire of his joy and love—and introduce the true sound of love back into the strings. He has introduced the voice which sounds in his presence back into us—namely, into his instrument. He has become what I am and has made me what he is, so that I may say that in my resignation <note>original: "Resignation"; in Boehme's theology, this refers to *Gelassenheit*, a state of total yielding or surrender of the self-will to God</note> in him, I am his trumpet and the sound of his instrument and divine ᵃ breath <note>original: "Voice"</note>, at which I now rejoice in all my fellow strings and voices. Together with me, these are tuned and set as an eternal work for the praise, tune, and glory of God.

14. Thus, my fellow voices in the praise of God, know now that I have found my string played upon in the Spirit according to your note, and so I sing to you: whatever Jesus has done through the Christ—namely, through his and my humanity—he still does today in me and in all my fellow members. He died to my selfhood <note>original: "Self-hood"; the ego or the self-centered nature that acts apart from God</note> in his death, and I also die to my selfhood in his death. He is given up to his resignation in God his Father, and God his Father has raised him up with the Spirit of his mouth in him and set him forth as the royal image according to the Holy Trinity, through whom and with whom God will judge all things in this world.

15. Thus God has also awakened my spirit and soul in him through his Spirit in the great name Jesus in Christ, so that in my resignation in him I do not need to die, for he died in me and for me. His death, because he is risen from death, has become my eternal life, so that now I live in his death as one dying; and yet there is no longer any death in him. Instead, I die to myself and sin in him, seeing that my desire and will press forth from my selfhood into it, so that I die daily to myself until I finally reach the limit of my selfhood. When my selfhood—with its earthly will and desire—wholly dies to its selfishness, then my selfhood, and everything in me which seeks and loves itself, shall fall into the death of Christ—namely, into the first Mother from whom God created me—and my selfhood shall become a nothing. Even then, my selfhood lies in Christ’s death in resignation as an instrument of God, who will then make it his instrument as he pleases.

16. But seeing now that my soul and spirit live in his resurrection, and his voice [breath or spirit] is in me according to my resignation in him, as St. Paul says:
> *Our conversation <note>original: "Conversation"; here meaning citizenship, conduct, or way of life (Philippians 3:20)</note> is in heaven, from where we wait for the Savior Jesus Christ;*
therefore also his voice—which is in me because I no longer live for my selfhood, but he alone [is and lives in me]—shall raise up my dead body, which I resign to him, and bring it into his first image, for which he created it.

17. Thus I now live in God, and my selfhood does not know it, for it does not live in God but in itself (God is indeed in it, but it does not grasp him) and it hides the pearl which I am in Christ. It is not I, but he in his humanity in my creature <note>original: "Creature"; here referring to the created human being or physical vessel</note> in himself. And so I speak and write of the Great Mystery of all beings—not because I have understood it in my selfhood, but because he strikes my signature in my desire, which presses into him as he pleases.

18. I am known to myself, but not in my selfhood; rather, I am known in his mirror which he has graciously put into me to allure my selfhood to him—namely, into resignation. And so likewise, dear brothers, it shall again be represented to you out of his glass ᵃ, <gloss>mirror</gloss> which he has set forth through my capacity in him as his instrument.

<meta>This page continues the discussion of the alchemical and spiritual transformation of matter and the soul, focusing on the transition from a state of "self-hood" and wrath to a state of divine resignation and perfection.</meta>

19. This is also how it happens in the alchemical <note>original: "philosophic"</note> work; *Sulphur, Mercury,* and *Salt* <note>The three primary principles of Paracelsian alchemy</note> have entered into their "self-hood" <note>an egoic, self-centered state of being</note> through the curse of God—that is, into a state of self-working and self-living. Everything now works within the curse and anger of God according to the properties of the first principle <note>the dark, fiery foundation of nature</note>. If God had not placed the Sun within it as a "nature-god" of the outward visible world to provide a tincture <note>an essence or spiritual quality</note> for every living thing—even everything that grows and moves—all things would exist in the impression of dark death, namely, in the abyss of hell.

20. Now, if anything is to be freed from this self-hood—from this wrathful death—and be brought back into the "Universal" (the state of highest perfection), then it must die completely to its self-hood. It must enter into the stillness, which is the death of "resignation" <note>original: *Gelassenheit*, a total surrender of the self-will</note> at the end of nature. *Mars* <note>representing the fire and wrathful energy</note> must completely lose the power of its fire and wrath, and *Mercury* must also lose its poisonous life. *Saturn* <note>representing contraction and leaden darkness</note> must become a death to itself, to such an extent that the artist sees nothing but a great darkness. Even then, the light appears in that resignation; for St. John says, *The light shines in the darkness, and the darkness does not comprehend it.* That is, in its self-hood—in its own will and working—the darkness cannot grasp the light; but in the state of resignation, the "Nothing" (which is the liberty of God) shines within it.

21. For the "Nothing" manifests itself through its "lubet" <note>original: *lubet*, meaning a divine inclination, delight, or longing</note> out of that liberty within the darkness of death. The Nothing will not and cannot remain a "nothing," yet it can only manifest itself according to the property of that free delight. This delight is now fixed and steadfast, existing within the Nothing, for there is no *turba* <note>original: *turba*, meaning a source of disturbance, turmoil, or chaotic interference</note> there. The self-will and its hunger are dead and absorbed into the Nothing, and the delight of eternal liberty is now its life. Since the highest Being has moved itself once and entered into a visible, comprehensible essence, it once again shapes <note>original: "figures"</note> that same essence. Once the essence departs from its self-hood and enters into the Nothing, it returns to the kind of being it was before the beginning of the world. But because the *Verbum Fiat* <note>Latin: "The Word, Let it be done"—the creative power of God's word</note> still stands to this day creating physical matter, it again creates a fixed, perfect essence. This is exactly what is achieved in the alchemical work, where a new life arises out of death—just as God raises us up in Himself through Christ, if we die to our self-hood and wholly resign ourselves to Him.

22. Thus, when the expressed *Mercury* within the *Sulphur* of *Saturn* surrenders its self-hood into *Venus* <note>representing love and harmony</note>, then the *Verbum Fiat* changes it again into an essence according to the delight of divine liberty. The "death" arises in a new body out of the darkness of death, appearing in a beautiful white color, yet as a hidden luster where the color is not yet fully and distinctly known. This continues until it dissolves itself and the *materia* <note>matter</note> becomes "desiring" <note>longing for union</note>. Then the Sun arises in the center, and *Saturn* appears in the properties of *Jupiter* and *Venus* in all the seven forms (that is, in the *Verbum Fiat*) as a new creation. The desire of all seven forms tends toward the luster of *Sol* <note>the Sun</note>—namely, toward the white and red colors derived from fire and light, which is the majestic <note>original: "majestical"</note> color, luster, or glory.

<margin>a Or conversed.</margin>
23. After his resurrection, CHRIST <gloss>a</gloss> walked <note>original: "conversed"</note> for forty days in the mystery of all three principles at once, in the same state as the first Adam after his creation but before his sleep and before Eve was formed. He appeared to his disciples in the property he had received from the outward world, eating with them and showing them his assumed humanity, proving that he had in no way completely cast it off.

<margin>o Or was.</margin>
24. In the same way, let the artist understand that in the alchemical work, the primary matter does not completely pass away or vanish. Instead, it enters into the "death" of its wrathful life-property and dies to the curse of God, only to rise again in its former being, which it <gloss>o</gloss> possessed <note>original: "had"</note> before the curse of God. Only the curse is destroyed within it, and the original life rises up again. Therefore, it is "fixed" <note>stable or permanent</note> and survives the fire, for it is dead to the dominion of the four elements and lives in the "fifth essence" <note>the quintessence or pure spiritual substance</note>. It is not that it possesses that same life as before, but it stands still within it; yet the Spirit of the newborn essence...

25. And just as Christ tinctured <note>original: "tinctured"; here meaning to infuse, dye, or spiritually transform</note> our corrupt humanity—in which *Mercury* was turned to poison—with the heavenly blood of the eternal divine purity and essence, whereby the human self-centeredness died in the poison and the surrendered life arose again; so too the poisonous *Mercurial*, *Martial*, and *Saturnine* <note>These refer to the "harsh" planetary properties: volatility (Mercury), aggression (Mars), and contraction or melancholy (Saturn).</note> will and desire die in the blood of *Venus* <note>Venus represents the property of love and sweetness in Böhme’s system.</note> during the alchemical work. Then the "white lion" appears upon his "crimson-colored beast"; right there lies the cure for sickness and the "death of death."

28. The body is dissolved in the blood of love, passing through death from an earthly property into a heavenly one. The tincture gives itself into the new body; and afterwards, when the body rises in the splendor of *Sol* <note>Sol: The Sun, representing gold or spiritual perfection.</note>, it also forsakes its own will. It resigns itself wholly into the body’s essence and becomes its beauty, splendor, and color, which the artist can never separate. For they are joined together in the "fifth essence" <note>original: "fifth essence" or quintessence; the purest form of a substance.</note>—namely, in the mystery of the *Verbum Fiat* <note>Latin: "The Word, 'Let it be done'"; the creative power of God.</note>—and belong to God’s motion on the final Day of Separation. In this present time, it serves as His own manifestation for His honor and wonderful deeds; but after this time, it belongs to the crystalline world in the "glassy sea" before the "Ancient of Days" in the *Apocalypse* <note>A reference to the Book of Revelation.</note>.

# A Brief Summary of the Alchemical Work.

29. Our meaning might seem very difficult to the reader because we go so far afield and show Christ all along within it. Let no one wonder at this; we do not seek gold or any temporary goods by this, nor do we wish to drive people into vain curiosities. We speak only with the "children" whom God has chosen for this; for the time has come when that which was lost shall be found again—yes, not only the "Universal" <note>The Universal Medicine or Philosopher's Stone.</note> for the body of this world, but also for the soul.

30. The process is very short in both cases and consists of only one property, which is this: The Tree (meaning Life) is divided into seven forms <note>The "Seven Properties of Nature" in Böhme’s cosmology.</note>. Now, the curse of God has entered into these seven forms so that they are in strife and enmity; one form annoys the other, and they can never agree unless all seven enter into death and die to their "self-will." Now, this cannot happen unless a "Death" comes into them which breaks all their individual wills and acts as a death to them—just as the Deity in Christ was a death to the human self-centeredness and to the seven forms in the human life. It is the same here: the human will was changed in Christ into the eternal Sun—namely, into resignation to God. So must all the forms in the alchemical work be changed into one, namely into *Sol*. Seven must become one, and yet remain as seven, but with one desire, where each form desires the other in love; then there is no more strife or contest.

<margin>¶ It makes itself, or it has its own Maker within itself.</margin>
31. Therefore, let the artist only consider how he may "give death to death" with the pure life, and how he may awaken the dead and vanished life which is heavenly and lies hidden and captivated under the curse, so that it may again receive the "fire-soul." If he can only bring it that far, it will work by itself.

<summary>Böhme explains the alchemical "Great Work" as a mirror of Christ’s transformation of humanity, where the seven warring properties of nature must die to their self-will to be unified in love and spiritual splendor. He emphasizes that this process applies both to the purification of matter and the salvation of the soul.</summary>

# Signatura Rerum: Chapter 12
<note>original: "Signatura Rerum"; Latin for "The Signature of All Things."</note>

32. When the Virgin <note>Boehme uses "the Virgin" to represent divine wisdom or the pure, heavenly counterpart of the soul.</note> again receives her bridegroom, who has been faithless, then he is prepared and fitted for the work; otherwise, he is not fit in any way, and everything he attempts is in vain and to no purpose. There is no possibility for the heavenly image—made in God's likeness—to be helped and restored after the Fire-Soul <note>The "Fire-Soul" refers to the human soul in its raw, energetic, and often wrathful state, separated from God’s light.</note> had entered into its own selfhood. This restoration can only happen if the Spirit of God introduces itself into the disappeared image (that is, into the heavenly essence) and gives itself, along with the awakened image, into the soul's fire (the wrath of death). In this way, it becomes a "death to death"—that is, a death to the wrathful anger of God—so that the wrath might be drowned in the love and the blood of the heavenly essence. Although there could be no actual parting or dying of the soul, there was a "dying" of the wrath, so that the anger was changed into joy and love.

33. Thus, the Artist's <note>original: "Artist"; here referring to the alchemist or spiritual practitioner.</note> work is exactly the same throughout: for man was created out of all beings, out of the Heaven and Earth. But when he became wholly earthly and the curse seized him, that curse also fell upon the earthly being from which man was made. Thus, Heaven was shut away from man, and Heaven was also shut up within the Earth—hidden in metals, trees, and herbs, and in the food of man, and everything that belonged to his ornament and delight.

<margin>¶ From.</margin>
<margin>† Or, as dead.</margin>
34. The soul of the Earth (the property ¶ of the fire of the first principle) has entered into its own selfhood, which is God's anger. Now, Heaven is hidden within it. Therefore, the Artist in his work must reduce the soul (which is under the curse) and Heaven back into one. He must introduce the soul back into Heaven, or else there is no possibility of success. Now, he cannot bring the soul in its iniquity into Heaven, for it will not go; therefore, he must bring Heaven into the soul. He must wholly give Heaven over to the soul, so that the soul must eat of Heaven whether she wants to or not. Heaven must be like † death in the soul, so that the soul cannot get rid of it, no matter how angry she is or how vehemently she rages against it. This continues until she is overcome in her wrath and enters with her desire into Heaven (the disappeared essence) and seeks to "murder" it, just as the Jews did to Christ. And if she enters the heavenly essence in this way, then the image of the heavenly essence falls into the jaws of the murderer.

<margin>• Or, Leave.</margin>
35. Thus, when the heavenly essence gives its desire to the murderer, the murderer is startled by the precious love-life and rises up in the Flagrat <note>original: "Flagrat"; a term Boehme uses for a sudden, intense spiritual flash or turning point of transformation.</note> within the heavenly essence. In this way, the disappeared essence receives the fire-flash into itself again and unites itself completely with the fire-life. Thus, the fire must burn in love and meekness and • forego its "right" in the center, just as light shines forth from a fire. In this way, and no other, the heavenly essence obtains its life. Just as fire thoroughly heats an iron until the iron appears to be fire itself—and indeed it is, though the iron still retains its own substance—so the disappeared essence (Heaven) becomes manifest in the poisonous, mercurial, and martial fire-soul. It turns seven conflicting wills into only one; the seven remain, but the enmity between them ceases.

<margin>† Contrariety.</margin>
36. This is a "Universal" <note>original: "Universal"; in alchemy, a medicine or substance that can cure all diseases and transform all things.</note>, which also changes the † enmity or malignancy of all diseases in the human body into one will (into unity). The result is that the raging and raving—the seven forms of life <note>Boehme’s "seven forms" are the foundational qualities of all existence, which cause conflict when out of balance.</note> in their enmity—become unanimous. Then the hunger of the disease ceases. The process for reaching this Universal is the same as what has already been mentioned. It is not my intention to provide a clearer declaration of it here; it is clear enough already. He who does not seek to become a new man born in God through this work, and does not apply himself diligently to that goal, should not meddle with my writings.

37. I have not written anything for such a seeker. Furthermore, he will not be able to fundamentally understand our meaning, no matter how much he struggles with it, unless he enters into "Resignation in Christ." <note>original: "Resignation"; the spiritual act of surrendering one's self-will to God's will.</note> Only there can he apprehend the spirit of the Universal; otherwise, all effort is to no purpose. We faithfully warn the curious critic not to...

# The Thirteenth Chapter.

<margin>Contrary Will, conflict.</margin>
### Of the *Enmity* <note>original: "Enmity"; refers here to the state of conflict or opposition between the spiritual and physical realms</note> of the *Spirit* and of the *Body*, and of their *CURE* and *REMEDY*.

<margin>Or, signs and marks itself in the Body.</margin>
1. **E**very thing is in itself a senseless and, as it were, a dead thing or being; it is only a manifestation of the spirit which is in the body. The spirit imprints itself <margin>marks itself</margin> upon the body; whatever the spirit is in itself in an imperceptible operation, the body is the same in its perceptible and visible working. There is one form of the seven forms of nature that is superior and chief; the others cling to it and also give their signs, according to how strong each of them is in its essence. As the forms stand in their order in each thing, so they sign the body of every thing and creature in its kind. This is the manifestation of the Divine Wisdom in the expressed Word <note>The "expressed Word" refers to the physical creation as the spoken result of God's creative thought</note> of love and anger.

<margin>Or understood, or conceived.</margin>
2. There is nothing that does not have its soul within it according to its property, and the soul is a kernel for another body. Whatever lives and grows has its seed within it. God has included all things in His Word and spoken them forth into a form. As the will had conceived <margin>conceived</margin> itself in the desire, the expressed Word is a blueprint <note>original: "platform"</note> of the speaking Word, and it contains the power of speaking within it once more. This same speaking is a seed for another image according to the first; for both work together—namely, the speaking [Word] and the spoken [Word].

<margin>Colours of Distinction. Element.</margin>
3. The speaking works in itself (that is, in eternity) and the spoken also works in itself (that is, in time). The speaking is the master, and the spoken is the instrument. The speaking creates the nature of eternity, and the spoken creates the nature of time. Each creates within its scope two properties, namely Light and Darkness, in which the Element of all beings consists. In the expressed Word, this element operates as four elements, but in the speaking Word there is only one. The Element in itself is neither hot nor cold, nor dry nor moist; but it is a *Lubet* <note>original: "Lubet"; from the Latin *libitum*, meaning a "pleasure" or "delightful longing"—a desiring will</note>, a desiring will, in which the Divine Wisdom creates different and various colors <margin>colors of distinction</margin> according to the property of the desire, in which <margin>element</margin> there is neither number nor end. But in the four elements there is number and end; for when they were expressed (in that they have become self-sufficient), they took a beginning and formed themselves into a model or blueprint of time, which runs like clockwork <note>original: "Watch-work"</note>; it forms, frames, and destroys.

4. This clockwork consists of seven forms or properties (as mentioned before) which create within themselves a threefold spirit: namely, a vegetative, sensitive, and rational spirit. The vegetative spirit consists in the four elements; the sensitive spirit in the seven forms of nature; and the reasoning power in the constellation <note>referring to the astrological influences of the stars</note>. However, true understanding proceeds only from God, for it rises out of the eternal nature. All life whatsoever, which has its limit in the expressed Word, consists of *Sal*, *Sulphur*, and *Mercury* <note>The "Tria Prima": salt (stability/body), sulfur (combustibility/soul), and mercury (fluidity/spirit)</note>; for in these consist the seven properties of every life in this world, as well as the spirit of vegetation, sensation, and reason.

<summary>This chapter explores the relationship between the spiritual and physical realms, explaining how the eternal "speaking Word" manifests as the temporal "spoken Word" (the physical world), which operates like a mechanical clockwork governed by seven natural forms and the alchemical principles of Salt, Sulfur, and Mercury.</summary>

5. **Sulphur** is the mother of all spirituality and physicality; **Mercury** governs the dominion within it; and **Salt** is the house where it lives, which Mercury itself creates within the Sulphur. Reason arises in the "Oil of the Sulphur," into which the constellation <note>original: "constellation"; here referring to the collective influence of the stars or spiritual forces</note> pours its desire—that is, the essence of its nature—from which the senses and thoughts immediately arise. However, true understanding proceeds from the "Oil of the Element"—namely, in the free delight <note>original: "lubet"; a term for divine longing or will</note> within the "speaking Mercury" <note>the active, creative Word</note>.

6. Since it is very necessary for us poor children of Eve to know the source of the disease and conflict in our lives—and what it is within us that makes us our own enemies, vexing, perplexing, and plaguing us—it is even more necessary to know the cure. Through this cure, we may heal ourselves in our own being and bring ourselves into the boundary of rest <margin>Into the desired end or perfection of rest.</margin>.

7. We will describe and explain this for anyone who has a mind to pursue it and truly test it. We will set forth how good and evil originally arise and how they develop, giving the searching mind the opportunity to seek further. We will show how the will toward good and evil arises, and how evil is the death of good, just as good is the death of evil.

8. When we consider what the **mercurial** life <note>the active, spirited life force</note> is, we find that it consists of **Sulphur**. For Sulphur is a dry hunger for matter which creates a harsh impression <note>original: "impression"; here, a contraction or drawing-in of force</note>. In this harsh impression, it contains fire, but also the "oil" from which the life-flame burns. Now, this compression creates coldness, and its "compunction" <note>original: "compunction"; a stinging or pricking movement</note> or attraction creates heat, <margin>And so it is.</margin> thus there is both a cold fire and a hot fire in one thing. The cold creates hardness and darkness within itself, and the heat creates light within itself. Yet there could be no light if the oil in the Sulphur did not "die" in hot anguish, just as a candle dies in the fire to produce light!

9. Now, there is a two-fold "dying" in Sulphur, from which a two-fold life is generated. First, the compression or desire draws in, contracts, encloses, and makes things hard, cold, and thick. This hardness—the enclosed state—causes a kind of death in the thing enclosed. Yet in that spirit, there is no total death, but rather a stinging, raging, and anxious "cold fire-life" that is generated by the compression and is the life of the darkness.

10. Second, within that same anguish in the harsh desire, the hot fire is generated. This fire consumes the substance which the coldness (the compression of the desire toward nature) creates. Thus, a conflict remains in the fire between the cold and the heat. The cold wants its life according to its own nature, and in its struggle for life, it ignites the heat in its compression. Immediately, the heat strips the cold of its power and consumes the cold substance. Then the fire-spirit itself cannot survive, for unless it has substance to burn, it goes out. Therefore, it must continually and without pause "die" within itself in the fiery, anxious desire. As long as it has the cold substance to live upon, its life arises; yet it is nothing but a constant dying and consuming, and its devouring creates the greatest hunger for substance. This same hunger passes out of the dying fire through the act of devouring and dwells in "the Nothing." Yet it cannot truly be nothing; therefore, it draws the fire back into itself, for its own desire is directed toward its mother <note>the original source or Sulphur</note>. But since it has already "died" to the fire-source, it cannot die any more in the fire of heat or cold. Instead, it continually proceeds out of the fire, and the fire continually draws it back in, and so it becomes the life of the fire. This is the air, which within the fire is rightly called "wind" because of its strength and force; but in that which has proceeded outward <margin>In the outward principle, in the expressed, formed Word.</margin>, it is properly called "air" because of its life of gentleness.

11. And in the "dying" of the fire, we should understand the Oil, from which the fire receives its shining light, in which the true life is understood. For that which proceeds out of the fire-death, desiring to be delivered and freed from the fire-source,

...that is a desire for meekness, and takes its origin in the first will toward nature, in which the eternal Nothing brings itself with its *lubet* <note>original: "Lubet," a term used by Boehme to describe the divine longing, delight, or imagination that precedes creation.</note> into a desire.

12. This *lubet* brings itself forth through the cold and hot death (through both types of dying) back into the Liberty, namely, into the *NOTHING*; and so it is manifested in the harsh contraction <note>original: "austere Impression."</note> through the fire, and brought into a principle, and yet it is not part of either the fire or the cold, but that is how it manifests.

13. But since the eternal *lubet* for nature introduces itself into a desire along with nature, this desire cannot die in either the cold or the heat. This is because it takes its origin in neither the heat nor the cold, but in the *Nothing*; and so, after it proceeds from the dying in the fire, it is desiring again—namely, of its own quality—and it contracts itself, for it has taken that contraction from the fire.

14. Now it can conceive of nothing in its contraction but an *essence* <note>original: "Essence," here meaning a spiritual substance or fundamental being.</note> according to its desire, which is now water; understand that according to the quality of the dark contraction it is water, and according to the fire it is oil; and that which is completely enclosed in hardness within the cold contraction—as a conception according to the quality of wrath—is earth.

15. Thus the wrathful, fiery desire continually draws this same air, water, and oil into itself and consumes it; so the fire-wrath is changed into a shining light within the air, oil, and water. For the Nothing desires nothing else but power and radiance, and so it makes itself manifest and brings itself into *essence*. And the spirit which proceeds forth out of the fire burning in the oil (that is, in the light from the fire and light) gives reason and understanding; for it originally took its rise in the Nothing and was the desire for nature. It has brought itself through all the properties of nature—through heat and cold, through the dying in the fire, and through the light—and dwells again in the Nothing.

16. It is a tester and knower of all properties, for it is generated through all and has proceeded from all. It is like a *NOTHING*, and yet possesses all things. It passes through heat and cold, yet neither of them can seize it; just as we see that the life of a creature dwells in heat and cold, and yet the true life is neither hot nor cold.

17. Now, therefore, understand us correctly: this birth in eternity is spiritual, but in time it is material. I cannot say of God that he is darkness and fire, much less air, water, or earth; but in his eternal desire, he has so formed himself within time—in the place of this world—into such a substance. He formed this in the speaking *MERCURY* <note>In alchemy, Mercury represents the fluid, transformative, and communicative principle of nature.</note> according to the properties of the will, and brought it with the expressed Word into such a formation according to the properties of desire in eternal nature, namely, in the *Verbum Fiat* <note>Latin: "The Word made manifest" or "Let the Word be done."</note>.

18. Now the expressed Word (the property of eternal nature) is understood as *Sulphur* <note>In this context, Sulphur represents the soul or the inward fire that fuels growth and existence.</note>, for within it is the seven-fold wheel of birth. In the spirit (in the first conception of nature), this is a constellation, and it divides itself out of that constellation in its own unique birth into seven properties, and out of those seven properties into four elements.

19. This constellation is a chaos where all things lie hidden. It is the first body, but a spiritual one; and the seven-fold wheel is the first unfolding [or working forth] of the chaos and makes the second body, namely, the reason. The second manifests the first and is also a spiritual body; the third body is elementary, a container <note>original: "Cabinet."</note> for both of the first two, and is a visible, tangible body.

20. Since the first body (the chaos or first constellation) is spiritual, it is the Word expressed out of the eternal conception. This same Word has its own "speaking" within itself, which is the mercurial wheel within the *Sulphur* with its seven forms, which in turn speaks forth the four elements from itself.

<margin>• Constellation.</margin>
21. Thus, one proceeds from the other. The first, before the Chaos, is the **Delight <note>original: "Lubet," from the German 'Lust' or 'Liebe,' referring to God's longing, inclination, or divine "good pleasure."</note> of Eternity** in the Abyss <note>The 'Abyss' or 'Unground' refers to the infinite void or the nothingness out of which God manifests.</note>, which takes within itself a Will for its own manifestation; this is entirely God. The Will conceives within itself a Desire in the Delight; this is the Chaos, or the first *Star <note>original: "Astrum," a term used by Boehme and Paracelsus to describe a spiritual governing principle or essence.</note>*, in which the Eternal Nature exists. With the Desire for Nature, it introduces itself into seven Forms (as mentioned before) and so reveals the Chaos—that is, the eternal, hidden Wisdom of God. With the Desire in the Mercurial Wheel <note>The "Mercurial Wheel" represents the dynamic, driving motion of life and the spirit's activity.</note>, the Element is formed, being a spiritual Body of the Mercurial Life.

22. Now all this is twofold: the Desire creates Darkness within itself through its Impression <note>The 'Impression' is the inward contraction or "drawing in" of spiritual force.</note>, where the strong power of the Igniting of Nature exists, and it is painful. The free Delight, following the Desire, creates Light and pleasing motion within itself through the Igniting of the Desire. The Light is the power and luster, and the Element is its body or essence—though as yet it is only spiritual. Thus, the Fire-Desire is a joyfulness within the free Delight, but in the Darkness, it is an aching, painful source.

<margin>† Sphere.</margin>
23. Man was created in the Image of God out of this entire essence. Understand us correctly: after and during his creation, he stood within the dominion of the Element. The *Mercurial Wheel* in *Sulphur* <note>In Boehme’s alchemical philosophy, "Sulphur" represents the soul's fire or the essential substance of life.</note> stood in the Light and in the free Delight of Eternity; but he wandered further with his desire into the four elements <note>The physical elements of the material world: Earth, Air, Fire, and Water.</note>—namely, into the center of Darkness, from which *Heat and Cold* arise.

24. In the beginning, his desire was directed [inclined] toward the Liberty of God—that is, into the Element, where he was resigned <note>Resignation (German: *Gelassenheit*) is Boehme’s term for the total surrender of the self to God's will.</note> in God. Then God’s Love-Will ruled him with the property of the free Delight. However, he departed from the free Delight of God and from that state of resignation into a "Self-will," which he forged in the Center of Nature. From this, pain and torture arise—namely *Heat and Cold*—as well as astringency, sour bitterness, and all the properties of the dark Impression.

<margin>‡ Or then.</margin>
25. It was then that he fell into eternal Death—that is, into the dying source where the *Mercurial Life* in the *Sulphur* rules in poison. In this state, one form in the *Mercurial Sphere* envies, hates, annoys, and destroys the other; there is nothing but anguish, aching, torment, and enmity. The free Delight was quenched in him—the delight in which the holy Element (the divine Body) consists—and in that same pure Element, the four elements of the outward source arose. There, the Image of God was cursed, which simply means that God’s Love-Will (which ruled in the Image of his Likeness) withdrew from Man. Thus, Man fell under the dominion of Nature. Since the four elements have a temporal beginning and end, and must eventually return to that end, the human body—which has now become entirely earthly in the four elements—must also fall back into the four elements and be destroyed by them. Therefore, we must now consider his cure and restoration: how he may be delivered from Death once more and be reintroduced with his body into the pure Element, and with his spirit into the dominion of God’s Will.

26. Now, there is no other remedy but this: the spirit—which arises in the Chaos and was breathed by God’s Will-Spirit into the created image—must again depart from its "Self-hood" <note>original: "Self-hood," referring to the ego or the individual will that has separated itself from the divine source.</note> (that is, out of its natural will) and resign itself fully and freely to the first Will that formed it into an image in the beginning. He must die completely to his self-hood within the death of the dark Impression (insofar as he lives there according to his own will in the self-desire of the outward life of the four elements). He must cast himself with total resignation into God's Will—that is, into God's mercy—so that he no longer lives and wills for himself, but for God (the first Will of God which created him in His image, whereby God manifested Himself). In this way, he returns with the first *Star* <note>original: "Astrum"</note>—that is, with the Chaos of the soul—into the same understanding in which God created him in His image.

29. Now we are to consider how the poor soul, held captive in God’s anger and lacking heavenly food, lives in mere anguish, distress, and restless pain. By the influence of the pure element, if the "Universal" <note>The underlying divine harmony or medicine.</note> resists this poison, then the body may stand in quiet rest; yet this lasts no longer than the inward spirit penetrates and **tinctures** the outward [body]. There is no perfection in the four elements until the body is changed back into the pure element; therefore, it must enter again into that source from which the four elements arise.

30. Now, in this time of the four elements, there is mere pain and <sup>k</sup> vexation. The soul distracts itself with the outward ***Astrum***, which forces its way into the soul and gives rise to false imaginations; meanwhile, the body stirs up the poisonous **mercurial wheel**, from which sickness and pains happen to it. Therefore, the soul must be cured with inward perfection—namely, by the **speaking Word** wherein it stands in God’s hand, which alone is able to **tincture** the soul and bring it into rest. The outward body must be **tinctured** and healed with the **expressed *Mercury***; <note>The "expressed Mercury" refers to the manifested or physical applications of the life-force used in healing.</note> and if the outward ***Mercury*** also exists under the "curse" as a "poison-wheel," then he must be **tinctured** with his own light in his "mother" within the body [or womb] of ***Sulphur***. ***Mercury’s*** own will and hunger must be broken, so that the envious, odious hunger may become a desire for love.

Indeed, nothing can resist it but its own mother who brings it forth, in whose womb it is held. Just as nothing can resist cold except heat, and yet heat is the "son" of cold; so also the poisonous ***Mercury*** must be resisted with its own child, which it generates out of itself from heat and cold within its mother’s womb.

All corruptions in the body proceed from the cold; if the sulfur <note>original: "brimstone"</note> is too vehemently ignited by the heat, then the right and nature of the cold dies and enters into sorrow.
