<summary>Boehme describes the spiritual struggle between the "resigned Will," which surrenders to God, and "Self-hood," the egoistic earthly nature that seeks worldly glory. He argues that true spiritual understanding comes not from intellectual study, but from becoming a passive instrument for God's voice.</summary>

<meta>This page continues Chapter 15 of Jacob Boehme's "The Signature of all Things," focusing on the distinction between the internal "speaking Word" of God and the external "expressed Word" or literalism of religious scholars.</meta>

# Chap. 15. The Signature of all Things.

...expressed Word, how it exists in its Ground; for it is only born into the Form from the outside, and not in the Power of the universal Pregnatress <note>original: "universal Pregnatress"; Boehme refers here to the divine generative power of nature or spirit that brings all things forth.</note>, whose Ground has neither beginning, limit, nor end.

22. Now, whoever is born from within out of the speaking Voice of God in God’s Will-Spirit moves freely everywhere in the Byss <note>original: "Byss"; from the Greek *byssos* (bottom), used here to mean the manifest foundation or ground of being.</note> and Abyss <note>original: "Abyss"; the bottomless, unmanifested void from which all things originate.</note> and is bound to no specific form. For he does not walk in Self-hood <note>original: "Self-hood"; the ego-driven nature that seeks its own will instead of God's.</note>, but the Eternal Will guides him as its instrument, according to God's pleasure. But he who is born only in the Letter <note>i.e., literal scripture without spiritual insight</note> is born in the Form of the expressed Word and continues in Self-hood; he is a self-willed voice, for he seeks what pleases himself and argues about the Form, while abandoning the Spirit which created that Form.

23. Such a person is a "Doctor Babel" <note>Boehme's term for theologians and scholars who argue over the literal text of scripture without spiritual understanding, evoking the confusion of the Tower of Babel.</note>; he contends, wrangles, and rages about the Form of the Word. He continually introduces his own self-willed spirit and understanding into the Form and cries out, "Here is the Church of Christ!" Yet it is only a self-willed voice, understanding nothing of the Spirit of the Form (which is incomprehensible), and he strikes upon his prepared instrument without limit or measure as he pleases. For conjecture, opinion, or one's own self-willed imagination which arises in the expressed voice [or literal outward Word] is not God’s Word. Instead, that which arises in God’s Spirit—in the wholly resigned Will <note>original: "resigned Will"; a translation of the German *Gelassenheit*, referring to a soul that has surrendered its own desires to God.</note> in Divine Power in the eternal speaking Word—takes its origin from God’s Voice and shapes the heart into a Divine Desire, by which the soul’s will is drawn into God.

<margin>That Christ died and suffered for us, etc.</margin>
24. He is a shepherd and teacher of Christ who enters through the Door of Christ—that is, who speaks and teaches by Christ’s Spirit. Without this, there is only the Form: the history of what once happened, which a man thinks he only needs to accept and comfort himself with. But this person's will remains outside; he wants to be a child of an assumed grace without wholly dying to his Self-hood within that Grace and becoming a child of Grace in the resigned will.

25. All teaching concerning Christ’s Satisfaction <note>original: "Satisfaction"; the theological doctrine that Christ's suffering paid the debt for human sin.</note> and comforting oneself with Christ’s suffering is external and not in the "speaking voice" of God (the Door of Christ), unless it also teaches the true Ground: how a person must wholly die to Self-hood in that Death and surrender themselves in the resigned will entirely to the obedience of God, as a new child with a new will.

26. No amount of flattery or self-comforting is of any use unless one dies to the false will and desire in Christ’s death, and arises in the wholly resigned will in Christ’s resurrection within him. One must continually mortify the earthly Self-hood and quench the evil which the earthly will introduces into the imagination, like an evil fire that constantly wants to burn.

27. Placing the suffering of Christ in the foreground for comfort is not true faith; no, that is only external. True faith is a converted will that enters into sorrow for its earthly wickedness and wants nothing more to do with it. Yet, finding itself held back by earthly lusts, it departs with a sincere converted will out of this abomination and false desire into God’s mercy. It casts itself with great, earnest desire into Christ’s obedience, suffering, and death. In this converted will, it wholly dies to earthly lust in Christ’s death—refusing to leave that death—and continually cries, "*Abba* <note>Aramaic for "Father," used in the New Testament to express an intimate relationship with God.</note>, loving Father! Accept your dear Son’s obedience for me; let me live only in his death and in his obedience to you. Let me die in him, so that I may be nothing in myself, but live and exist in his will, in his humanity within you. Receive me entirely in his resurrection, and not in my own unworthiness; let me be dead in him and give me his life, so that I may be your obedient son in him. Let his suffering and death be mine, so that I may stand before you in the same Christ who has stripped death of its power—as a branch or twig of his life."

<summary>Boehme distinguishes between a literal, academic understanding of religion ("Doctor Babel") and a true internal transformation. He argues that mere intellectual belief in Christ's atonement is insufficient without a total "resignation" of the self-willed ego and a spiritual rebirth into Christ's life.</summary>

<meta>This page continues the discussion from Chapter 15 of *Signatura Rerum*, where Jacob Boehme explores the internal process of spiritual transformation and the nature of true faith versus mere outward religious form.</meta>

28. This, and no other way, is the true Christian faith; it is not only a comforting thought, but an unceasing desire. This desire obtains the suffering of Christ. This desire would continually and gladly be obedient, if it only knew how it should behave before him; it continually falls down before him and immerses itself in the deepest humility. It suffers and does all things readily, only so that it might receive grace. It is willing to take the cross of Christ upon itself and disregards all the contempt of the world toward its <term>Self-hood</term> <note>original: "Self-hood"; Boehme's term for the egocentric, fallen nature that seeks its own will over God's.</note>, but continually presses forward into Christ’s desire for love. This desire grows only out of Christ’s death and out of his resurrection in God; it brings forth fruit in patience which is hidden in God, of which the earthly man knows nothing, for he only finds himself in his own self-centeredness.

29. A true Christian is a continual warrior and walks entirely within the will and desire of Christ’s person, just as Christ walked up and down upon the Earth. When Christ was on the Earth, he desired to overcome death and bring human self-centeredness into true <term>resignation</term> <note>original: "Gelassenheit"; the spiritual act of surrendering one's own will to the divine will.</note> and divine obedience. A true Christian desires to do this likewise; he desires continually to die to the wickedness of death and wrath, to give himself up to obedience, and to arise and live in Christ’s obedience in God.

30. Therefore, dear brothers, be careful not to put on Christ’s purple mantle without a surrendered <note>original: "resigned"</note> will. The poor sinner who lacks sorrow for his sins and a conversion of his will only takes that mantle in mockery of Christ. Stay away from that doctrine which teaches of self-sufficient abilities and of justification through works.

<margin>* Or the desire of works.</margin>
31. A true Christian is himself the great and earnest work, which continually desires to work in God’s will. He struggles against the selfish lusts of the ego and wills continually to do so, yet is many times hindered by his own self-centered nature. He breaks his "self" like a vessel in which he lies captive, and buds forth continually in God’s willing spirit with his desire surrendered to God (just as a beautiful blossom springs out of the earth) and works in and with God, whatever pleases God.

<margin>* To bear or carry.</margin>
32. Therefore, let true Christendom know and deeply take to heart what is now told and spoken to her: namely, that she must depart from the false assumption or opinion of finding comfort without a conversion of the will. That is only an outward, expressed form of being "born again." A Christian must be one spirit with Christ and have Christ’s will and life within him. The outward form does not renew him; neither comforting oneself nor speaking good words helps or avails at all. Rather, it is the mortifying <note>original: "mortifying"; the practice of "killing off" or subduing sinful desires.</note> of the evil, inbred will which is God’s child and is born out of Christ’s death; no other will attains Christ’s inheritance. Having great knowledge does not do it either; the herdsman in the field is as near to it as the scholar <note>original: "Doctor"; referring to a Doctor of Divinity or a highly learned person.</note>. No wit or subtle art in debating about the way of God helps or avails anything; it is only a hindrance and an obstacle. 

The true will enters into the love of God and his children; it seeks no outward form but falls down before its Creator and desires the death of its false self-centeredness. It seeks to perform works of love toward all people. It will not flourish in the world’s praise, but in its God; its whole life is pure repentance and a continual sorrow for the evil that clings to it. It seeks no glory or applause to show itself off but lives in humility. It always acknowledges itself as unworthy and simple; its true Christianity is always hidden within its own self. Such a person says, "In my own self, I am an unprofitable servant and have not yet even begun to practice repentance rightly." He is always at the beginning of working toward repentance and would always gladly reach the gates of sweet grace. He labors for that purpose as a woman in labor <note>original: "travel"; an archaic term for the labor of childbirth.</note> struggles to give birth, and he does not know how it fares with him. The Lord hides his face from him so that his internal work toward God may be great. He sows in anguish and tears and does not know his own fruit, for it is hidden in God. Just as a weary traveler goes a long way, aiming for his desired journey’s end, so he runs after the far-off mark of his rest and does not find it—unless his "Pearl" <note>The "Pearl of Great Price," a common mystical metaphor for the discovery of the divine Spark or Christ within the soul.</note> appears to him in its beauty and embraces him in its love. If it departs from his self-hood again, then fighting and sorrowing arise once more.

<summary>Boehme defines true Christianity not as intellectual belief or outward ritual, but as an internal struggle to surrender the ego (Self-hood) and align one's will with Christ. He emphasizes that this "New Birth" requires constant repentance, humility, and a sincere desire for God rather than academic knowledge or "works."</summary>

...with continual desire; and one day calls another, the day the night, and the night the morning; and yet there is no place of rest in the earthly selfishness <note>original: "Self-hood"</note>, but only in the fair solar luster of his precious pearl. When the Sun arises to him in the darkness, then the night departs, and all sorrow and anguish fly away.

33. Therefore, dear brothers, learn to take heed and beware of contention, where men argue about the literal form <note>meaning: the outward words or rituals of religion</note>. A true Christian has nothing to contend for, for he dies to the desires of his own reason; he desires only the knowledge of God in His love and grace. He lets go of everything that contends and strives about outward forms, for Christ’s Spirit must create the form within himself; the outward form is only a guide. God must become man, or else man does not become God <note>This refers to the doctrine of "theosis" or divinization, where the believer is transformed by divine grace</note>.

34. Therefore a Christian is the most simple (or plainest) person upon the earth; as *Isaiah* says, *Who is so simple as my servant?* All heathens <note>original: "Heathens"; here meaning those who do not know God</note> desire selfishness, and tear and devour one another for authority and honors. But a true Christian desires to die to those things; he seeks not his own, but Christ’s honor. Everything that contends for selfishness—namely <note>original: "viz."</note>, for the selfish honor and pleasure of this life—is heathenish, and far worse than heathenish; yes, it is like the Devil, who departed from God into selfishness. Let such a person cover themselves with Christ’s mantle as much as they want, yet the man of false selfishness is lodged under it. If he will be a Christian, then he must completely die to selfishness, so that it only hangs upon him from the outside like a garment of this world, in which he is a stranger and a pilgrim. He must always consider and think that he is but a servant in his high office, and serves God there as a servant, and is not his own lord and master.

35. Everything that lords itself over others without God’s call and appointment comes from the Devil, and serves the Devil in his own power and form. Defend and flatter yourself as much as you want, it does not matter before God; your own heart accuses you that you are a false branch. Your nobility and high status do not help you at all in the sight of God if you do not act according to God’s order. Your office is not yours, but God’s; if you walk falsely in it, then your own judgment is upon you and condemns you to death. You are a servant; and though you are a king, yet you serve, and must enter into the New Birth <note>original: "New Birth"; the spiritual rebirth described in the Gospel of John</note> along with the poorest, or else you shall not see God.

36. All selfishly assumed (or arrogated) laws and authority, by which the poor are troubled and oppressed, come from selfishness, whose origin is in the "expressed form" <note>Boehme's term for the outward, material manifestation of the divine Word</note>, which has introduced itself into a state of self-interest and removed itself entirely from God. Whatever does not serve in a servant’s office before God is entirely false, whether it be high or low, learned or unlearned. We are altogether servants of the great God; nothing brings itself into a state of selfishness unless it be born in God’s anger through the "impression of nature" <note>The process by which spiritual reality hardens into material or selfish existence</note>. And though a Christian possesses property <note>original: "Own-hood"</note> which is not false, he is still only a servant within it—namely, a distributor for his Master, a steward and overseer of his Master’s work. He deals for his Master there, and not for his own selfishness only. Everything he plots and devises to bring into his own selfishness, he brings into the anxious cabinet of covetousness, envy, and the selfish pleasure of the flesh—that is, into a vessel that is separated from God, into the "impression of nature." He steals from his Lord and Master who has set him up as a steward; he is a sacrilegious person, no matter how he excuses himself or what he pretends.
<margin>A thief <note>original: "Pilferer"</note> from God and His substance.</margin>

37. A true Christian acknowledges himself as a servant of God, to whom it is given as a responsibility to deal rightly with God’s works. He is not his own, for he is also not at home in this earthly work of this tabernacle <note>A biblical metaphor for the human body or temporary earthly life</note>. Let him seek, search, plant and build, traffic and trade; and whatever else he does, he must always know that he does...

<summary>Boehme argues that true Christianity requires the complete abandonment of selfishness and worldly ambition in favor of humble stewardship. He warns that those in power are merely servants of God and that any authority used for self-interest rather than divine service is a form of spiritual theft.</summary>
<keywords>Christian humility, stewardship, selfishness, Self-hood, spiritual rebirth, social justice, divine order, Jacob Boehme</keywords>

# Signatura Rerum : Chap. 15.

37. ...it to God, and shall give an account for it. He must realize that he is a stranger and a servant in this work, and that he serves his Master. He must not look at all upon the way of his ancestors who walked in the pleasures of the earthly life. Whoever does so is far from the Kingdom of God and cannot, with any conscience or foundation, call himself (or think himself to be) a Christian. For such a person stands only in the form of Christianity and not in the Spirit of Christ; the form shall be destroyed and cease with time, but the Spirit remains steadfast forever.

38. A true Christian is a Christian in the Spirit, and is in continual practice to bring forth the Spirit’s own form—not only with the sound and show of words, but in the power of the work, as a visible, tangible form. This is not about thinking, conjecturing, or speaking good words out of the self-centered selfhood <note>original: "self-ful Self-hood"</note> while still remaining in that selfhood. Instead, it is a dying to the ego and a growing forth in the will of God through the "love-selfhood" as a servant of God in God’s deeds of wonder. It is a helping to play His instrument in God’s will, being a true-sounding string in God’s harmonious concert. It is a continuous making of the Word in God’s voice—namely, in the *Verbum Fiat* <note>Latin: "The Word: Let it be done," referring to God's creative command</note>—which makes and works in and with God what God makes, forms, and works, as an instrument of God.

<margin>Being spit out.</margin>
39. Therefore, O you dear Christendom <note>The collective body of Christians or the Christian world</note>, behold yourself! See whether you work in the active Word of God in His will, or whether you stand only in the outward form of Christianity and work for your own self-interest in falsehood. You will find how you have become an abomination before the Most High. Your being cast out <note>original: "casting forth," likely referencing the "spewing out" of the lukewarm church in Revelation 3:16</note> by the Most High from this form (which you, in your self-interest, have introduced into His manifested form) shall soon follow. This is because you cover yourself with the true form while being a false child within it. Therefore you are sought out and found with a false veil [or covering] in your own form.

40. And as you have brought yourself into a false, self-centered form under the guise of the true form, so you shall also destroy yourself. The heavens, which you have served in obedience for a long time, will help in this, and there is no stopping it. Your work is found to be in the <term>Turba</term>, which shall fully satisfy and gorge itself in destroying, just as you have built yourself up in your unfaithful falsehood under the name of the true form. You have acted the hypocrite before God with the show and ostentation of holiness, while only serving the earthly man. But the servant of the Lord shall be sought and found; the Lord feeds His lambs in His own form and brings them into His pasture. All the haughty and wealthy of the world shall find by experience what judgment the Lord will bring upon the face of all the earth, and all wicked hope shall be destroyed; for the day of the harvest draws near:

> *A terror from the Lord shakes the earth, and His voice sounds in all the ends of the earth; and the star of His wonders arises. No one can hinder it, for it has been decided in the counsel of the watchmen in the gates of the deep.*

<margin>The Lubet or longing desire.</margin>
41. Therefore, let everyone seek and find himself, for the time of visitation <note>A time of divine inspection or judgment</note> is at hand, so that he may be found in God's love. For the <term>Turba</term> has found all false lust within itself, and the Most High Worker of all essences manifests the <term>Turba</term>. Then all false lust or imagination becomes manifest, and each thing enters into its eternal keeper; for all things are generated out of imagination <note>In Boehme's philosophy, "imagination" is the formative power of the will that gives shape to reality</note>. So also shall each thing receive its own quality in the imagination, and every imagination reaps its own work which it has performed. For all things have appeared to this end: that eternity might be made manifest in time. With deeds of wonder, eternity brought itself into the form of time, and with deeds of wonder, it carries itself forth again out of time into its first place.

<margin>This is always the end.</margin>
42. All things enter again into that from which they proceeded; but they keep their own form and model, as they have introduced themselves into the manifested Word. Every thing shall also be received by its own likeness, and the end is always present; and as all things...

He emphasizes that all things originate from "imagination" (willful formation) and will eventually return to their eternal source, reaping what they have sown.</summary>

...generate themselves in the expressed Word, so also they are signed in their inward *form*, which also signs the outward.

43. The *self-centered <note>original: self-ful</note> will* makes a *form* according to its innate *nature*; but a *form* is made in the *surrendered <note>original: resigned</note> will* according to the *platform* or *model* of *eternity*, as it was known in the *mirror* <note>original: Glass</note> of *God's eternal wisdom* before the *times* of this *world*. So the *eternal will* shapes and forms it into a *model* of its *likeness* for the *honor* and wonderful *acts* of *God*; for whatever goes on in its *self-hood*, that thing forms itself; but what resigns itself freely is formed by the *free will*. Now, no *self-centered form* with its own *self-will* can inherit the only *eternal being*; for where there are two *wills* in one, there is *hostility* <note>original: enmity</note>.

44. Seeing then that *God* is the only one *God*, then all that would live in him must be like his *will* and *word*. As a *concert* of *music* must be tuned into one *harmony*, though there are many *strings* and manifold *voices* and *sounds* within it, so must the true human *harmony* be tuned with all *voices* into a *melody of love*. That *will-spirit* which is not tuned to the only *concert* in the *divine voice* is cast out of this *tune* and brought into its own *self-centered tune*, namely <note>original: viz.</note> into its true *fellow-voices* of its own *likeness*; for every *likeness* shall receive its own.

45. If anyone here has been an evil *spirit*, then he shall be introduced into the *root* of his *likeness*; for every *hunger* receives its like into itself. Now the whole *manifestation* of *eternity* within this *time* is nothing else but a *hunger* and *generation*; as the *hunger* is, so also is the *essence* of its *satisfaction* <note>original: satiating</note>. For with the *hunger* the *creature* had its *beginning*, and with the *hunger* it enters into its eternal *[being].*

46. In the *hunger*, the *spirit* with the *body* is generated, and in that same *hunger* it goes into its eternal *being*—unless it breaks its first *hunger* and brings itself into another by *mortification* <note>original: the spiritual practice of "killing" the selfish ego or desires</note>. Otherwise, all is at its *end* as soon as it is born; but *death* is the only *means* by which the *spirit* may enter into another *source* and *form*. If it dies to its *self-hood* and breaks its *will* in *death*, then a new *twig* springs forth out of it—not according to the first *will*, but according to the *eternal will*. For if a *thing* enters into its *nothingness*, then it falls back to the *creator*, who makes that *thing* as it was known in the *eternal will* before it was created as a *creature*. There it is in the right *aim* or *limit* of *eternity* and has no <term>*turba*</term> <note>original: Turba; Boehme’s term for the "disturber," the destructive or chaotic element in nature that arises when things fall out of divine order</note>, for it is in *nature's end*.

47. Whatever runs on in *nature* torments itself, but that which attains *nature's end* is at *rest* without any painful *source* <note>original: Source; here implies the boiling, active quality of the lower nature</note>, and yet it works, but only in one *desire*. All that creates *anguish* and *strife* in *nature* creates pure *joy* in *God*. For the whole *host* of *heaven* is set and tuned into one *harmony*; each *angelic kingdom* is like a unique *instrument*, but all are mutually composed together into one *music*—namely, into the only *love-voice* of *God*. Every *string* of this *melody* exalts and rejoices the other; and it is only a pure, ravishingly lovely, and delightful *hearing*, *tasting*, *feeling*, *smelling*, and *seeing*. Whatever *God* is in himself, the *creature* is also in its *desire* in him: a *God-angel* and a *god-man*, *God all in all*, and without him, nothing else. As it was before the *times* of this *world* in his *eternal harmony [or voice]*, so also it continues in the creaturely *voice* in him throughout his *eternity*; and this is the *beginning* and the *end* of all *things*.

# The Sixteenth Chapter.

### *Concerning the Eternal Signature and Heavenly Joy; why all Things were brought into Evil and Good.*

1. **T**HE creation of the entire universe is nothing else but a manifestation of the all-essential, unsearchable God. Everything that He is in His eternal, beginningless generation and sovereignty is also present in creation—though not in His full omnipotence and power. Rather, creation is like an apple growing upon a tree: the apple is not the tree itself, but it grows from the power of the tree. In this same way, all things have sprung forth out of the divine desire and were created into an essence <note>original: "Essence," referring here to a physical or spiritual substance</note>, whereas in the beginning, no such substance was present, but only the same mystery of the eternal generation, in which there has always been an eternal perfection.

2. For God did not bring forth creation so that He might become perfect through it, but for His own manifestation—that is <note>original: "viz." (videlicet), meaning namely</note>, for great joy and glory. This is not to say that this joy first began with creation; no, for it existed from eternity in the Great Mystery <note>Boehme uses "Great Mystery" (Mysterium Magnum) to describe the source of all manifestation—the "chaos" or womb from which all things flow</note>, yet only as a spiritual melody and play <note>original: "Sport"</note> within itself.

3. Creation is that same play expressed outside of Himself; it is a platform or instrument of the Eternal Spirit, with which He makes music. It is like a great harmony of many different instruments which are all tuned into one symphony. For the Eternal Word—or Divine Sound or Voice, which is a Spirit—has introduced itself through the generation of the Great Mystery into various forms, namely into an "expressed" word or sound. And just as the joyful melody exists within the Spirit of the eternal generation, so too does the instrument—the expressed form—exist within itself. The living Eternal Voice guides this instrument and plays it with His own Eternal Will-Spirit, so that it sounds and makes music. Just as an organ of many different sounds or notes is moved by a single breath of air—so that each note, and indeed every pipe, has its own unique tune, and yet there is only one kind of air in all those notes, sounding in each note or pipe according to how the instrument is built.

4. Thus, in eternity there is only one Spirit in the entire work of the divine manifestation. He is the Manifestor in both the "expressed" voice <note>the created world</note> and the "speaking" voice of God <note>the divine source</note>. This Spirit is the life of the Great Mystery and of all that is generated from it; He is the Manifestor of all the works of God.

5. All the angelic kingdoms are like a completed work—a manifestation of the eternal sound of the Voice of God. They are specific details <note>original: "Particularity"</note> arising out of the Great Mystery, and yet they are all one within the divine, eternal, speaking Word or Voice of God. Only one Spirit rules them. Each angelic prince is a specific quality <note>original: "Property"</note> originating from the Voice of God and bears the great name of God. We see a symbol <note>original: "Type and Figure"</note> of this in the stars of the sky, and in the kingdoms and governments on Earth among all generations, where every lord bears his high title, respective name, and office. The stars in the sky work the same way: they are all one single dominion of power, where the great stars bear the name and the office of the forms in the mystery of the "seven properties" <note>the seven qualities of nature in Boehme's system</note>, and the others follow them as specific divisions or "houses," where every one is a unique harmony or operation, like a kingdom. Yet all of them proceed in one harmony, like a clockwork mechanism which is entirely self-contained, where all the pieces work together as one. Even so, the great fixed stars keep their unique qualities in their actual functioning—especially the seven planets, according to...

<summary>Boehme explains that creation is a physical manifestation of God's eternal nature, comparing it to a musical instrument or a clockwork mechanism played by the Divine Spirit for the purpose of joy and self-expression.</summary>

# Chapter 16

The seven properties of nature, as a secondary womb <note>original: "under Pregnatress"</note> of the eternal mystery, **or** as an instrument of the spirit out of the eternal mystery.

6. This birth of the *Astrum* <note>the astral or stellar spirit</note> begets joy and sorrow in the four elements—namely, in its body or essence—and all is very good in itself. Only the alteration of the creature proceeds from the desirous imagination <note>original: "lustful Imagination"</note>, by which the creature elevates the wrath of the fire in the properties and brings them forth out of the balance <note>original: "Likeness"</note> of their harmony <note>original: "Accord"</note>. Nothing is evil that remains in the equal harmony; for that which the worst causes and makes by coming out of the harmony, the best also makes within that same balance. That which causes sorrow there, also causes joy in that state of balance. Therefore, no creature can blame its Creator as if he made it evil; all was very exceedingly good. But with its own elevation and departure out of that balance, it becomes evil and brings itself out of the form [or property] of love and joy into a painful, tormenting form and property.

7. King *Lucifer* stood in the beginning of his creation in the highest joy, but he departed from that balance and put himself out of the harmony [or heavenly concert] into the cold, dark, fiery generation <note>the process of coming into being</note>, from which the hot, fiery generation arises. He forsook his order and went out of the harmony in which God created him. He wished to be lord over all, and so he entered into the domination of the austere fire; he is now an instrument in the power of that austere fire, upon which the all-essential Spirit <note>the Spirit that is the essence of all things</note> strikes and sounds. But it sounds only according to the property of the wrathful fire: just as the harmony (namely, the form of life) is in each thing, so also is the sound or tone of the eternal voice within it. In the holy, it is holy; in the perverse, it is perverse. All things must praise the Creator of all beings; the devils praise him in the power of wrath, and the angels and men praise him in the power of love.

<margin>Blue pencil bracket</margin>
8. The Being of all beings is but one single Being, but in its manifestation <note>original: "Generation"</note> it separates itself into two principles—namely, into light and darkness, into joy and sorrow, into evil and good, into love and anger, into fire and light—and out of these two eternal beginnings [or principles] into the third beginning, namely, into the creation, for its own love-play and melody, according to the property of both eternal desires.

9. Thus each thing goes into its harmony and is guided [or driven] by only one Spirit, which is in each thing according to the property of that thing. This is the clockwork <note>original: "Clock [or Watch-Work]"</note> of the great mystery of eternity in each principle according to the property of that principle, and then according to the innate form of the composed instrument of those same creatures, even in all these beginnings [or principles].

10. Death is the boundary-mark <note>original: "Bound-Mark"</note> of everything that is temporal, by which evil may be destroyed. But that which arises out of the eternal beginnings, and in its harmony and life-form enters into another figure, departs from God's harmony and out of the true order in which God created it. It is cast out of that harmony into its own likeness, as a dissonant, discording melody or sound in the great, excellent, well-tuned harmony; for it is an opposite, contrary thing and carries another tone, sound, and will, and so it is introduced into its likeness. Therefore, Hell is given to the Devil for his house and habitation because he introduced his life-form into the anger of God and into the fiery wrath of eternal nature. Now he is the instrument in the eternal fire of God, and the spirit of anger strikes his instrument; yet it must still stand to the honor and wonder of God, serving as the activity <note>original: "Sport and Play"</note> within the desire and property of wrathful anger.

11. The anger and wrath of God are now his joy—not as if he feared, sorrowed, or lived in weakness <note>original: "Impotency"</note>; no, but in great strength and fiery power, as a potent king and lord, yet only in the same property of which he himself is: namely, in the first principle in the dark world.

12. We should also know the same concerning the angelic world—namely, the second principle—where God's light and glorious beauty shine in every being [or thing], and the divine voice or sound rises up in all creatures in great joy, where the Spirit pro- <meta>Text ends mid-word; likely "proceeds."</meta>

# Signatura Rerum; Chapter 16

[...pro-]ceeding from the Divine Voice creates a joyfulness and a constant, continual desire for love in those creatures and in all divine, angelic beings. Just as there is a source of anguish and trembling in the painful fire, so in the same way there is a trembling joyfulness in the light and "love-fire"—namely, a great elevation of the Voice of God. This creates a great manifestation of divine joyfulness in the angels and in similar creatures, such as the souls of men.

13. The Voice [or Breath] of God continually and eternally brings forth its joy through the creature, as if through an instrument; the creature is the manifestation of the Voice of God. What God is in the eternal generation of his Eternal Word—out of the great mystery of the Father's property <note>The "Father's property" refers to the foundational, paternal aspect of the Trinity from which all things originate.</note>—that is what the creature is in his image: a joyful harmony through which the Eternal Spirit plays or makes music.

14. All properties of the great eternal mystery of the pregnancy <note>original: "pregnatness"; meaning the state of being full of potential or ready to bring forth life.</note> of all beings are manifest in the holy angelic and human creatures. We should not think that these creatures only stand still, rejoice at the glory of God, and wonder in joy. No, it is as the Eternal Spirit of God works from eternity to eternity in the great mystery of the divine generation and continually manifests the infinite and numberless wisdom of God. Just as the Earth always brings forth beautiful blossoms, herbs, and trees, as well as metals and all kinds of beings—producing them sometimes more powerfully and beautifully than at other times, and as one arises in essence while another falls away—there is an incessant, lasting enjoyment and labor.

15. Likewise, the eternal generation of the Holy Mystery exists in great power and reproduction [or *paradisiacal budding forth* <note>original: "pullulation"</note>], where one divine fruit of the great desire for love stands with another in the divine essence. It is all like a continual "love-combat" or a delight of wrestling; a blooming of beautiful colors and a pleasant, ravishing smell of the <term>Divine Mercury</term>, according to the properties of the divine nature, and a continual good taste of love from the divine desire.

16. Everything in this world is an earthly symbol and resemblance of what exists in the Divine Kingdom in great perfection within the spiritual essence. It is not only spirit, as a will or thought, but essence—corporeal <note>In Boehme's thought, "corporeal" refers to a spiritual body or substance rather than dense, physical matter.</note> essence, sap, and power—though it is incomprehensible to the outward world. For this visible world was generated and created out of that same spiritual essence in which the <term>Pure Element</term> exists. It was also created out of the dark essence in the mystery of the Wrath (which is the origin of the eternal manifest essence from which all properties arise) as a "spoken-out" breath from the Being of all beings. It was not made *of* the eternal essence itself, but out of the breathing-forth or expression of that eternal essence; out of love and anger, out of evil and good, as a distinct generation of a specific <term>Principle</term> held in the hand of the Eternal Spirit.

17. Therefore, everything in this world is a symbol and figure of the angelic world. This does not mean that the evil—which is manifest alongside the good in this world—is also manifest in Heaven. No, they are separated into two "principles." In Heaven, everything is good that would be evil in Hell. Whatever is anguish and torment in Hell is good and a joy in Heaven; for there, everything exists in the source of light, while in Hell, everything exists in the wrath of the dark source.

18. Hell, namely the dark world, also has its generation of fruits; and there is an essence and governing power in them just as in Heaven, but in the manner of the wrathful property. The fiery property makes everything evil in the darkness, while in the light it makes all things good. In summary, all is entirely one in both eternal worlds, but light and darkness separate them so that they stand in eternal opposition to one another. This is so that it may be known what is evil or good, joy or sorrow, love or anger. There is only a distinction between the love-desire of the light and the anger-desire of the darkness.

19. In the origin of the eternal nature, in the Father's property in the great mystery...

<meta>This page continues the discussion of the "Great Mystery" (Mysterium Magnum) from page 134, specifically how the unity of the divine source splits into the dualities of light/dark and love/anger.</meta>

# Chap. 16. The Signature of all Things.

19. [Mys]tery of all beings, it is completely one: for the same single fire is even in the angelic world, but in another state <note>original: "Source" - here meaning a state of being or fountain-spring</note>, namely, a love-fire. This same fire is a poison and a fire of anger to the devils and to hell; for the love-fire is a death, a suppression <note>original: "mortification"</note>, and an enemy to the anger-fire. It deprives the wrath of its power, and the wrath does not want this, nor can it be otherwise; for if there were no wrath, there would be no fire, and also no light. If the eternal wrath did not exist, the eternal joy also would not exist; in the light, the wrath is changed into joy. The essential nature of the wrathful fire is suppressed <note>original: "mortified"</note> regarding the darkness within the wrathful fire, and out of that same dying, the light and love-fire arise—just as the light burns forth from a candle, and yet in the candle, the fire and light are but one thing.

20. Thus also the Great Mystery <note>original: "Great Mystery," referring to the *Mysterium Magnum*, the hidden source of all existence</note> of all beings is, in eternity, within itself only one thing; but in its unfolding and manifestation, it proceeds from eternity to eternity into two essential natures, namely, into evil and good. What is evil to one thing is good to another. Hell is evil to the angels, for they were not created for it; but it is good to the hellish creatures. So also Heaven is evil to the hellish creatures, for it is their poison and death, an eternal dying and an eternal captivity.

21. Therefore, there is an eternal enmity, and God is only called "God" according to the light of His love. He is indeed everything Himself, but according to the darkness He says, *I am an angry, jealous God, and a consuming fire.*

22. Every creature must remain in the place where it was conceived <note>original: "apprehended"</note> in its creation and formed into an image, and not depart from that same harmony; otherwise, it becomes an enemy of the "Being of all beings."

23. And thus Hell is even an enemy of the Devil, for he is an alien guest <note>original: "strange guest"</note> within it—namely, a traitorous <note>original: "perjured"</note> fiend cast out of Heaven. He wants to be lord in that for which he was not created; the whole creation accuses him of being a false, traitorous, apostate spirit who has departed from his proper order. Yes, even the nature within the wrath is his enemy, though he is of the same character; yet he is a stranger and wants to be lord, even though he has lost his kingdom and is only an inmate in the wrath of God. He who was too rich has now become too poor; he had everything when he stood in humility, and now he has nothing and is, moreover, imprisoned in the abyss. This is his shame: that he is a king and yet has foolishly thrown away his kingdom through pride. The royal creature remains, but the dominion is taken away; from a king, he has become an executioner. Whatever God’s anger seizes, there he is a judge—namely, an officer of God’s anger—yet he must do whatever his Lord and Master wills.

<margin>* Balanced <note>original: "Counter-poised"</note></margin>
24. Human reason most ignorantly opposes this, saying, *"God is all-powerful and all-knowing; He has made it. He has done with His work as He pleased; who will argue with the Most High?"* Yes, dear Reason, now you think you have it right; but first learn the A-B-C's in the Great Mystery. Everything that has arisen out of the eternal will—namely, out of the Great Eternal Mystery of all beings (as angels and the souls of men are)—stands in equal balance <note>original: "equal weight"</note> between evil and good in free will, just as God Himself does. Whichever desire works most powerfully and predominantly in the creature, and completely overtops the other, determines the character of that creature. As a candle puts forth a fire from itself, and out of the fire comes the wind, which the fire draws back into itself and yet gives forth again; and when this spirit has gone forth from the fire and light, then it is free from the fire and light; whatever character it receives again, it becomes that. The first mystery in which the creature consists is the all-essential mystery, and the other in the outgoing spirit is its own property and a self-determined will. Does not every angel have its own peculiar spirit, which is generated out of its own mystery, which has its origin in eternity? Why would this spirit choose to be a tempter of God and test the mystery, which immediately imprisons it in wrath, as happened to Lucifer? It has the attraction toward God's wrath and God's love within it; why does not the spirit (which is generated...

He argues that creatures like angels and humans possess free will to choose between these two balanced forces, using the fall of Lucifer as a warning of what happens when a spirit departs from its created harmony.</summary>

25. You say it cannot; *it is not so: Every spirit stands in the place where it was created in equal weight and has its free will. It is a spirit with the all-essential Eternal Spirit and may take to itself a <term>Lubet</term> <note>original: "Lubet"; a technical term for Böhme meaning a "longing," "delight," or "imagination" that moves the will.</note> in the all-essential Eternal Spirit as it wills, either in God’s love or anger; into whichever it introduces its longing imagination, it receives the essence and property of that thing in the great mystery of all beings.

26. In God, the birth is manifest in love and anger; why not also in the creature which is created out of God’s essence and will, out of His voice and breath into an image? Whatever property <gloss>[or Note]</gloss> of the voice the creature awakens in itself, the same sounds within and rules the creature. God’s will toward the creature was only one—namely, a general manifestation of the Spirit—as each <gloss>[creature]</gloss> was grasped in the property of the Eternal Mystery. Yet, Lucifer was grasped in the good angelic property, which plainly testifies that he was an angel in Heaven; but his own embodied will-spirit forced itself into the wrathful mother to awaken that same wrath within itself, and thereby to be a lord over every created being. Now the will-spirit is free; it is the eternal original; let it do what it will.

27. Therefore we are to know this, and it is not any other way, that the will-spirit—which takes its origin out of love and anger, out of both eternal principles—has given itself into the wrath. By this, the wrath has powerfully gained the upper hand and dominion, putting itself out of the equal harmony and into a dissonance or discord, and so it must be driven into its likeness. This is his fall, and so it is also the fall of all evil men.

28. Now human reason alleges the Scripture where it is written: *Many are called, but few are chosen;* also, *I have loved Jacob and hated Esau;* also, *Has not a potter power to make of one lump* <gloss>[of earth]</gloss> *whatever he pleases?* I say the same also: *That many are called, but few are chosen;* for they will not come. They give their free will into God’s anger, where they are seized, and so are chosen to be children of wrath; whereas they were all called in *Adam* into Paradise, and in Christ into the regeneration. But they would not; the free will would not. It exalted itself into the wrath of God which seized it, and so they were not chosen children; for God’s love chooses only its likeness, and so likewise God’s anger. Yet the gate of regeneration stands open to the wicked whom the anger of God has seized. Man has death in him, by which he may die to the evil; but the devil does not, for he was created to the highest perfection.

<margin>† Or: Die.</margin>
29. Thus it is also with *Jacob* and *Esau:* In *Jacob,* the line of Christ gained the upper hand in the wrestling wheel <note>original: "wrestling wheel"; the "Wheel of Nature," Böhme's term for the dynamic, spiraling forces of creation and spiritual conflict.</note>; and in *Esau,* the fall of *Adam.* Now Christ was therefore promised into humanity so that He might heal the fall of *Adam* and redeem *Esau* (who was captivated in the wrath) from that wrath. *Jacob* represents Christ, and *Esau* represents *Adam.* Now Christ is to redeem *Adam* from death and wrath, in which he was captivated. But did *Esau* † die in sin? That I do not know; the Scripture also does not declare it. The blessing belonged to *Esau*—that is, to *Adam*—but he fooled it away in the Fall, and so the blessing fell upon *Jacob*—that is, upon Christ—who should bless *Adam* and *Esau,* so that the kingdom and blessing might be given by free grace again to *Adam* and *Esau.* Though he was seized in the curse, yet the door of grace stood open in *Jacob,* that is, in Christ. Therefore *Jacob* said afterward—that is, Christ, when He had entered into *Adam’s* soul and flesh—*Come unto me all you that are weary and heavy laden with your sins, and I will refresh you.* Also: *I am come to call the sinner to repentance;* not *Jacob,* who needs it not, but *Esau,* who needs it. And when he <gloss>(namely Esau)</gloss> has come, then says Christ, *There is more joy in heaven for him than for ninety-nine righteous ones who need no repentance;* <gloss>[namely, for one Esau that repents,]</gloss> there is more joy than for—

30. But who are the righteous, since we have all become sinners in *Adam*? Answer: They are those whom the line of *Christ* in humanity seizes at life’s beginning [or at the first point of the opening of life within them]. It is not that they cannot fall like *Adam*, but that they are held in *Christ’s* will-spirit in the wrestling wheel <note>original: "wrestling Wheel." In Boehme’s cosmology, this refers to the dynamic, conflicting forces of nature (the seven properties) before they find harmony in the light.</note>, where love and anger are balanced, and they are chosen for life. This happened to *Jacob*, and also to *Isaac* and *Abel*. But this line should be the preacher and teacher to *Cain*, *Ishmael*, and *Esau*, urging them toward repentance and to turn away from anger. And this line gave itself into the anger that was ignited in *Adam*, *Cain*, and *Ishmael*, and destroyed the Devil’s sting with love, so that *Cain*, *Ishmael*, and *Esau* had an open gate to grace. If they would only turn and "die" in *Jacob*—that is, if they would enter into *Christ’s* death and die to sin in *Abel*, *Isaac*, *Jacob*, and *Christ*—then they would be received into the election of grace.

31. *Jacob* took *Esau’s* place in the blessing. Why did that happen? In *Jacob* was the promised seed of *Abraham* and *Adam*; from this line, the blessing should come upon the sinful *Adam* and *Esau*. *Jacob* had to be filled with God’s blessing so that he might bless the firstborn of the angry *Adam* and *Esau*. For the blessing—which is *Christ*—must be born in our flesh and soul so that the "seed of the woman" might bruise the head of the serpent <note>A reference to Genesis 3:15, traditionally interpreted as the first prophecy of Christ's victory over evil.</note>.

<margin>Or, Birthright.</margin>
32. The anger must be drowned and appeased in humanity. A mere ritual offering did not do it; it required this surrender into the wrath so that love might drown the wrath. *Jacob* in *Christ* must drown *Esau* in the power of love in his blood, so that *Esau* might also become a *Jacob* in *Christ*. But *Esau* was not willing to receive his brother *Jacob* and fought over the birthright; that is, *Adam* in his sin will not and cannot receive [or accept] *Christ*; he must die to the sinful flesh and will.

33. Therefore *Esau* has always fought against *Jacob*, for *Jacob* was meant to drown him in *Christ’s* blood. The evil *Adam* in *Esau* did not want this; he wanted to live in his "self-hood" <note>Boehme uses "self-hood" to describe the ego or the self-centered will that is separated from God.</note>. Therefore, he struggled with the earthly *Adam* against *Jacob*. But when *Jacob* met him with his gifts—that is, when *Christ* came with his free gift of love into humanity—then *Esau* fell upon his brother *Jacob’s* neck and wept. For when *Christ* entered into humanity, *Adam* wept in *Esau* and repented of his sins and his evil intent to kill *Jacob*. When God’s love in humanity entered into God’s anger, the "angry Father" <note>Boehme refers to the "First Principle" of God—the dark, consuming fire of justice—as the "angry Father" when it is not balanced by the "Second Principle" of Light/Love.</note> lamented our sins and misery. *Jacob*, through his humility, drew mournful tears out of his brother *Esau*. That is, the love in humanity brought forth great compassion out of and through the angry Father, so that the angry Father—in the midst of his ignited wrath in humanity—set open a gate of mercy for *Adam* and all his children. For his love broke the anger by placing itself into death, creating an open gate to grace for poor sinners even in the midst of death.

34. Now the poor sinner, whom anger has chosen for the condemnation of eternal death, is commanded to enter into this same death and die to sin in *Christ’s* death. Then *Christ* drowns that sin in his blood and chooses the person again to be God’s child.

35. Here is the calling: *Christ* calls us into his death, into his dying. The sinner does not want this. Now there is a struggle within the sinner between the "seed of the woman" and the "seed of the serpent." Whichever one overcomes is the one that conceives the "child" <note>The birth of the new spiritual self.</note>. Now the free will may reach toward whichever it pleases; both gates stand open to him. Many who...

Those who are in Christ's lineage are also brought through imagination and lust into wickedness, just as *Adam* was. They are indeed called, but they do not persevere in the election <note>original: "Election"; here referring to the "Election of Grace" or God’s choice of the saved</note>, for the election is set upon those who depart from sin. He is elected who dies to sin in Christ's death and rises in Christ's resurrection—who receives God in Christ, not only with the mouth, but in divine desire within the will and the new birth, as a new fiery generation. Knowledge does not grasp it; only the earnest desire and the breaking of the sinful will can grasp it.

36. Thus, there is no sufficient ground for the "Election of Grace" as human reason presents it. *Adam* is chosen in Christ; but if many a twig withers on the tree, it is not the tree's fault. The tree does not withdraw its sap from any twig; rather, the twig spends itself too eagerly with its own desire. It runs on in "self-will"—that is, it is consumed by the inflammation of the sun and the fire <note>In Böhme’s cosmology, the "fire" represents the harsh, consuming quality of God’s nature without the light of love</note> before it can draw sap again from its mother and refresh itself.

37. Thus also, man perishes among evil company in wicked, vain ways. God offers him His grace so that he should repent, but evil company and the Devil lead him in wicked ways until he is held too fast in "the Anger" <note>The "Anger" refers to the "dark world" or the wrathful side of the divine nature</note>; and then it goes very hardly for him. He indeed was called, but he is evil. God chooses only "children." Since he is evil, the choice passes over him; but if he reforms and amends his life, the eternal election receives him once again.

<margin>The original text says, "comforted us."</margin>
38. Thus the Scripture says, *Many are called;* but when the choice through Christ's suffering and death comes upon them, they are not capable of receiving it because of the self-centered, evil will they had previously embraced. And so they are not the elected, but evil children. Here it is then rightly said, *We have piped to you, but you have not danced; we have mourned to you, and you have not lamented to us.* <note>Matthew 11:17</note> *O Jerusalem, how often would I have gathered your children together, as a hen gathers her chickens under her wings, and you would not!* <note>Matthew 23:37</note> It is not said, "you *could* not," but "you *would* not." And while they remain in the wickedness of sin, they also *cannot* come. *God will not cast his pearl before swine; but to the children who draw near to Him, He gives the pearl and His bread.*

39. Therefore, whoever blames God despises His mercy, which He has introduced into humanity, and brings judgment headlong upon their own body and soul.

40. Thus I have truly warned the reader and set before his eyes what the Lord of all beings has given me. He may behold himself in this mirror <note>original: "Looking Glass"</note> both within and without, and find what and who he is. Every reader shall find profit in this, whether he is good or evil. It is a very clear gate to the mystery of all beings. No one shall grasp it with superficial explanations <note>original: "Glosses"</note> or their own cleverness <term>Self-Wit</term>; but it may well embrace the sincere seeker and create much profit and joy for him. It may even be helpful to him in all natural things, provided he applies himself correctly and seeks it in the fear of God—seeing as this is now a time of seeking. For a Lily <note>In Böhme’s writing, the "blossoming Lily" symbolizes a future age of spiritual enlightenment and the restoration of purity</note> blossoms upon the mountains and valleys in all the ends of the earth: he that seeks finds. *Amen.*

->HALLELUJAH.<-

# POSTSCRIPT
## BY THE
### TRANSLATOR.

The preceding book is a brief signature—or a description of the character—of natural and divine knowledge. However, it will seem strange and foolish to the proud, self-conceited pretenders of wisdom—those "wiselings" of pedantic reason who will carp and cavil at anything that does not dance to their tune or agree with their own private notions. But their criticisms are not to be valued; their mock productions of science, based only on literal learning, are to be pitied, being merely the shadows chased by their own distracted imaginations. Such as these, being held captive in the mystery of *Babel* <note>Babel: A reference to the biblical Tower of Babel, symbolizing human confusion, pride, and the divided state of languages and religions.</note>, wonder only after their beast *Mammon* <note>Mammon: Wealth or material profit, personified as a false god.</note>, upon which they ride in pride. They scorn anything that does not please and flatter them in their admired works of greedy wickedness, which they gild over with a veneer of holiness. But the Babylonian structure of their *Turba Magna* performances <note>original: "Turba-Magna"; Latin for "Great Turmoil," a term used by Boehme to describe the chaotic state of human systems and the coming judgment.</note> will fall when it has reached the highest limit of its fate, and no human wit shall be able to prop it up. In the meantime, the *Antichrist* in *Babel* will rage and tyrannize, executing the sentence of wrath—his own dismal doom—upon himself.

But, not to wander too far from the intent of this postscript with a large digression, its principal design is to explain some words which are used in this translation, such as:

->FLAGRAT, LUBET, SOURCE, SUDE.<-

### FLAGRAT.

The word in the German is *Schrack* <note>original: "Schrack"; modern German "Schreck," meaning a sudden fright, shock, or flash.</note>, which properly signifies a fright, sudden astonishment, or dismay. In other books, it is translated as "terror" or "crack," but I have used the word *Flagrat*, from the Latin word *Flagro* <note>original: "Flagro"; to burn, blaze, or glow.</note>. By this, I do not mean only a burning, but even the powerful opening of life or death at the enkindling of the fire in nature. For this fire is the dividing boundary in which the life of both "principles" <note>principles: In Boehme's philosophy, the different realms of existence, such as light/love and darkness/wrath.</note> is opened and separated: the life of the first is the dying death in the darkness, and the life of the second is the living life in the light. 

You may perceive a resemblance of this *Flagrat* in thunder and lightning, as well as in gunpowder and similar things. Take, for instance, various sulfurous, <term>salnitral</term> minerals <note>original: "salnitral"; relating to saltpeter (potassium nitrate), which was considered a volatile, "fiery" substance in early chemistry.</note> exactly mixed. Right now, their powers are, so to speak, contracted or shut up in a harsh, dark desire or state of "death." But touch them correctly with the true fire, and you will see how they will soon open, disclose, and flash forth. They will even display and stream themselves forth into diverse properties, colors, and virtues. It is essentially the bursting forth of the ardent desire in nature. It is, as I may term it, the magical fire-breath, by which the powers of either light or darkness are startled into being. In short, it is the pregnant echo of the sound of eternity everywhere speaking, working, and opening itself in love or anger—in each thing according to its own will and desire. In some, it is the horrible *Flagrat* leading to death; in others, it is the pleasant, triumphant *Flagrat* leading to life.

### LUBET.

The word in the <note>The translator says "Dutch," but Jacob Boehme wrote in German; at the time, "Dutch" often referred generally to Germanic languages (Deutsch).</note> is *Lust*, which signifies a longing desire or a will toward a thing; it also means a delight or contented joy, and sometimes imagination. But because our English word "lust" is commonly used in the worst sense (a longing after evil and vanity), and...

<page-num>140</page-num>
<header>The Signature of All Things: Chapter 16.</header>

Since the word "lust" would not properly agree with or fully express the German word *Lust* <note>In Boehme’s German, *Lust* refers to a holy longing or a neutral "desire" rather than specifically carnal lust.</note> in all places, I have generally translated it as *Lubet*, from the Latin word *Lubitum* <note>original: *Lubitum*, meaning "pleasure" or "will"</note>, which refers to the Divine *Beneplacitum* <note>original: *Beneplacitum*, meaning "good pleasure"</note>. By this, we understand the origin of a desire in the "Eternal Nothing" or "pregnant magic"—God’s free delight in the desire to manifest nature and all creatures. Without this, everything would have remained an eternal stillness within the Nothingness. This *Lubet* in man is the driving will toward good or evil, light or darkness, love or anger.

### S O U R C E <note>original: *Quelle*, meaning a spring, fountain, or the origin of a quality.</note>

By this word, the author means the first original qualities or properties of both inward principles <note>The "principles" are Boehme’s cosmic forces: the dark world, the light world, and the visible world.</note> as they break forth in the "sude" <note>seething/boiling</note> of the fire during the "flagrat" <note>original: *flagrat*, meaning a sudden flash or spiritual ignition</note> of love or anger within nature or a creature. 

In the darkness, the "love-essence" <note>original: *Love-Ens*</note> or paradisiacal light is trapped within death, creating a harsh, dark source of pain, horror, torment, or unrest. Thus, it is the fundamental property of the warring elements and stars under God's curse. Conversely, in the light, the life of love breaks forth and swallows up this wrathful source of darkness and death, turning it into joy or a divine source. Therefore, by "source," we understand the original quality, property, or characteristic of evil, darkness, anger, sorrow, cursing, damnation, death, and hell—or the exact opposites of these in their divine source or essential working property, occurring in both time and eternity.

### S U D E

The word *Sude* is German and signifies a boiling or seething. It represents the stirring of the seven properties in nature, arising from the assimilation or essential shared influence of the outward and inward *Sol* <note>the Sun</note> in *Sulphur* <note>In alchemy, Sulfur represents the active, combustible principle of the soul or nature.</note>. From this process, the blooming growth of the Earth proceeds; the generation of metals and minerals also originates here.

These are some uncommon words used in translating this book into English. Words are *Vehicula Rerum* <note>original: "vehicles of things"</note>; they are formed to express actual things, not just empty sounds or mere air. He who truly understands the foundation of the *Cabala* <note>Kabbalah, the Jewish mystical tradition</note> and *Magia* <note>Divine Magic</note>, and knows how the "Language of Nature" speaks in every tongue, might be well-equipped to translate this author. However, the literal text of his writings—no matter how exactly translated—will not grant understanding of them. That understanding comes only through the spirit of regeneration in Christ, in whom the fullness of the Deity dwells in bodily form.

**Note:** There is **ONE CHARACTER** by which God has marked both Himself and all creatures, showing that His presence is in all things. Yet, each creature has its own unique mark, shape, and figure so that it may appear as a unique wonder of either the heavenly or the earthly mystery. This is the <image-desc>A cross potent symbol (a cross with crossbars at the ends of the four arms)</image-desc> in the sphere and "mercurial wheel" <note>The cycle of transformation and movement in nature.</note> of nature. This mark extends through all three principles, and in the third principle, it reaches through all the kingdoms of minerals, vegetables, and animals, throughout heaven and earth. The wonderful depth of this mystery is revealed in this book to those who seek the divine mysteries.

# Great Philosophical Work

->Three joined in one, a complete and admirable work—<-

# PREFACE.

## TO THE

# READER.

<margin>decorative woodcut initial J</margin>
**Jakob Böhme** <note>original: "Jacob Behmen"</note> writes here concerning the highest point of controversy, which is **Predestination** <term>the doctrine that God has ordained all that will happen, especially regarding the salvation of some souls and not others</term>. This subject has not been satisfactorily resolved by any writer since it first arose. Every different party argues for and against <note>original: "pro and con"</note> it, still relying on the biblical texts brought to support their own side. 

However, despite all the disputes that have been held between them, those texts and that great mystery remain unresolved. The principal cause of this may be the apparent contradictions <note>original: "seeming Opposition"</note> in the texts they cite. One party assumes that the verses on their side should dominate the meaning of those used by the opposing party, whereas all these texts must be acknowledged as entirely true. Truth in any opinion cannot contradict the Scriptures, even if the parties are unable to reconcile the meanings of those texts or their own opinions. Because they cannot see how both sides might be true, they continue to remain at a wide distance from one another in their feelings and attitudes.

<margin>
a See his Preface, verse 92.
b See the book, Chapter 13, verse 68 to the end.
</margin>
But this author does not engage in dispute at all. He only desires to discuss and offer his own understanding and basis for interpreting the texts on both sides. He answers the objections raised by human logic and demonstrates his knowledge for the <sup>a</sup> joining, uniting, and reconciling of all parties in <sup>b</sup> **love**, despite their differing and varied understandings.

He has done this here and there in **all** his writings, which explain the basis for understanding all mysteries, both natural and divine. He began in his *Aurora* <note>Böhme’s first book, *Aurora: The Root of the Day-Star* (1612).</note>, at the end of which he promised: "If God would permit me to live a while, I would sufficiently declare and explain Saint Paul's teaching on election and predestination." But he was prevented from writing further, as the book was taken from him immediately <note>original: "presently"</note> after he wrote those words. Thus, that book never had anything more added to it, but remained unfinished. This was in the year 1612.

But in the year 1619, he addressed the deficiency of that work in *The Three Principles* and in *The Threefold Life of Man*.

In the year 1620, he proceeded further in *Forty Questions Concerning the Soul* and in the treatise *The Incarnation of Jesus Christ*.

In the year 1621, having been challenged during a conference with some friends by Balthasar Tilken <note>A contemporary critic of Böhme who accused him of heresy.</note> regarding **Election** <term>the theological concept of God's choosing of individuals for a specific purpose or for salvation</term> and some other matters in his writings, he wrote an *Apology*...

Some of the learned also are very unwilling to take so much pains as to read and consider anything that is offered to their view; though some sincere lovers of good literature have by reading this author found that which is *more excellent*, than what they and others had spent their time in for a long time together; because these account themselves filled so full with their present wisdom and knowledge, that they have no room to desire any other, especially that which cannot be attained without casting away the high esteem of what they have laid up as a *treasure* to themselves already; and so every little difficulty of uncouth <note>original: "uncouth" — here meaning strange, unfamiliar, or unusual in style.</note> words or phrases, and expressions which they cannot presently see to fit and square with their former building, makes them unwilling to be troubled about that which they think themselves to have more and *better* knowledge of already. teaching. If the writings of the holy prophets and apostles are examined, it will appear that there is not the smallest thing done in this world that does not, by way of similarity <note>original: "Similitude"</note>, signify and teach us something about the most transcendent and richest mysteries of eternity. All visions, which were the clearest revelations, were represented by something or other—in part or in whole—*like* that which is in this outward world. However, the thing representing it is but a *shadow* compared to the inward *substance* it resembles. For example, Christ and faith are a *substance*, while a rock is but a *shadow*. The Holy Spirit, the Word, God, and the Divine Nature are *much more* truly a substance, while the things in this world that resemble them are barely even an exact shadow of them.

So also the Sun of Righteousness, the City of God, the trees in the Paradise of God, the fallow ground of our hearts, the grain of mustard seed which the Kingdom of Heaven *is represented by and likened to*, a steward, a husbandman, a door, a vine, a sheepfold, a candle set upon a table or put under a bushel, a boiling <note>original: "seething"</note> pot with the scum rising up, a rose, a lily, briars, thistles and thorns, the seven stars, the dragon, the woman, the candlesticks, the temple, the moon, rivers, fountains, fire, brimstone, and so on—every one of these denotes to us some mystery or other in the spiritual world, as will in due time be revealed. We could know nothing of these mysteries except by way of similarity, for it is the Spirit alone that teaches the mystery by and through them. We cannot understand the demonstration of things we have *never seen* except through similarity to those things the physical man has seen or conceived. Our minds *are opened* just as the understanding of a child *is in learning*. We must be like children regarding all our great knowledge, or else we cannot be taught any *new* thing that is beyond our former reach, understanding, and capacity. But when the similarity is declared and weighed, the knowledge of the thing itself will be easier, and then the demonstration of it may be briefly and exactly made by those who are *teachers in Christ’s school to students practiced to some degree in such spiritual matters*. Otherwise, that question of our Savior may well be asked of them: *If you do not believe when I tell you earthly things, how shall you believe if I tell you heavenly matters?*

This serves as a just defense <note>original: "Plea"</note> for this author’s teaching the mysteries of divinity through examples and similarities to natural, earthly things. In these, he lays out his basis for interpreting the Holy Scriptures, by which men test the deepest questions and controversies in religion, so that the apparent differences within them may be cleared up and resolved—that all may understand them rightly, including Christians, Jews, and Heathens <note>meaning: non-Christians or Gentiles</note>, and so prize them as they ought. In his own preface, he states to this effect: the assumption that God is *only* far off in a heaven above and beyond the stars and firmament *exclusively*, and not in everything and everywhere present as he is in himself—*substantially* and totally, with all that is in *essence* in the unity of the Deity and the trinity of manifestation in his whole kingdom, power, and glory (though not discernible or perceptible to the creature, except by his Word revealing himself in and to the creature according to its kind)—is the only reason why men cannot satisfy themselves regarding that great secret <note>original: "*Arcanum*"</note> of predestination and other high and necessary mysteries mentioned in the Old and New Testaments.

The *Heathens* would value the Scripture if it were only suggested to them that they might consider it—that what is mentioned and contained within it, and of which it is chiefly appointed to testify, *is the same as that which is in their very hearts*. They would rejoice to hear the living demonstration and effects of that God and his graces, which lie like a deep fountain and hidden spring in their own souls. Then they would soon taste the *eternal Gospel* of the love of God poured out in their hearts upon reading the Holy Scriptures, if they were shown how everything lies within their own hearts and souls.

The *Jews* also cannot be fully persuaded that Jesus Christ, whose name is *Immanuel* <note>meaning "God with us"</note>, is and was the true *Messiah*, because they cannot perceive the truth except by understanding *how*...

# PREFACE to the READER

The promised Seed <note>original: "Seed"; a theological term referring to Christ or the divine spark within humanity</note> was placed by God into—or rather, raised up or caused to sprout forth within—the souls of Adam and Eve after they ate the forbidden fruit. In this way, salvation was continually taking effect for all people who became the offspring of that Seed by forsaking their sins and being obedient to that Seed of God. This is the Word of Life, the Word of Promise, which is the Word of *Grace*, the Word of God, the commandment, his testimonies, his ways, statutes, precepts, and judgments, which are so strongly emphasized in the books of *Moses* and in the *Psalms* of *David*. 

All of this is *Christ* within them. In relation to this Seed in the line of the Covenant, according to his manifestation in the flesh, *Christ Jesus* (their *Messiah* and our *Savior*) came and took on our nature, being born of *Mary*. He finished our redemption in a *human soul*—a soul just like all of ours—and therefore he condescends so low as to call us his brothers, even though the fullness of the Godhead lived bodily within him. Thus he worked and perfected our salvation, so that everyone who was born again and grew up in him—that is, in his grace and covenant within their souls—should be partakers of the *Divine Nature*. In this way, he might rule in them to subdue the "seed of the serpent" (the lusts of the flesh) in *anyone*, whoever they may be. This is that *Light* that enlightens every person—even *every* heathen, Jew, and Christian—at the moment the soul takes *life* in the womb, thus *entering* into the physical substance of the elementary body of *this world*.

The Word of the Lord does not contradict itself, neither in its operation in the *works* of the outward world, nor in the inward teachings of the Holy Spirit in the soul, nor in the written Word of the Holy Scriptures. The Scriptures were written as holy men spoke as they were moved by the Holy Spirit, which neither teaches, *nor can* teach, anything other than what the Holy Word speaks, from which the Spirit proceeds. Therefore, the *Essential* Word must be considered in every respect before men are able to fundamentally decide a deep controversy, question, or doubt in any matter. 

We see that God’s ordinance in the outward world, which we call *Providence*, appoints the profession and condition of life every person shall have in nature. Because of this, *Caiaphas* was High Priest that year in which Christ was crucified, even though he was inwardly a *conspirator* against Christ; likewise, *Judas* was appointed to be one of the Apostles, even though inwardly he was a *devil*. Similarly, *King Saul* was among the prophets, and there are many *false apostles* gone out into the world, and many *false Christs*. But the true ones are what they are in spirit and truth in the inward, hidden man of the heart. 

Therefore, everyone should labor to be—in spirit, mind, soul, and affection—that which is right in the sight of God according to his *Word and ordinance* within their honest outward calling or office, whether low or high. One should not, under the pretense of an outward calling, think he is righteous without the Spirit; nor should he despise or conspire against those who *are* righteous in Spirit, even if they have no outward calling at all. For most of the eminent prophets, as well as the apostles, disciples, evangelists, elders, bishops, overseers, pastors, doctors, or teachers, were not called from the "schools of the prophets," nor from among the learned or noble—though some of them were. These were called by God just as *Moses*, *Aaron*, *David*, *Peter*, *Paul*, *Timothy*, *Barnabas*, and others were. So too were the greatest part of those called who were the first writers of the books of the Old and New Testament.

But the Seed continued under the evil life and *conduct* <note>original: "conversation"; meaning behavior or lifestyle</note> of the old world before the Flood, even though they had the preaching of *Adam* himself, and *Abel*, *Seth*, *Enoch*, *Noah*, and others. After the Deluge they were *more* depraved, even though they were under the preaching of *Noah*, *Shem*, *Eber*, and others until *Abraham*, to whom God sealed his Covenant of Promise with circumcision, for a stronger...
