Teaching directed to the outward nature of man <note>original: "outward Man"</note> was observed by Isaac, Jacob, and his sons, the twelve patriarchs, until Moses, who was raised up by God. Moses received a further, clear external teaching through the institution of the Passover as another seal of the Covenant. He also gave the Law of the Ten Commandments, which the "outward man" had so darkened within the human heart that very few people still understood it. Furthermore, Moses provided the law of sacrifices and other ceremonies, along with the **Judicial Law** <note>The civil and legal codes governing the nation of Israel.</note> for the government of God's own people.

This dispensation remained all along among a wicked and stubborn <note>original: "stiff-necked"</note> generation in the world, even under the evangelical <note>Gospel-like</note> teachings of the Prophets, until Christ himself. During His outward teaching while He was on earth, men were so very wicked that—according to His own parable—when the Lord sent His Son to the vine-dressers <note>Referencing the Parable of the Wicked Tenants in the Gospels.</note> thinking they would have respected him, they said, "This is the heir; let us kill him, and the inheritance shall be ours." And so they **killed him** and cast him out of the vineyard. 

At this time, as it was necessary to help the outward man so that the inward Word might grow within him, a **greater teaching** was provided than in the time of Moses or Solomon. This was done through the ministry of John the Baptist and by Christ's own most significant institutions and instructions while He was incarnate. Yet the Apostles could not comprehend or remember what He told them, nor could they bear what He would have taught them before His death, until the **Comforter**, the Holy Spirit, was sent after His ascension and glorification to bring to their remembrance whatever He had told them. 

Then, this great manifestation of the **Power of God** sprang up and spread so effectively that many were converted by it who had not been won over by the former teaching. It even reached Saul, who was also called Paul, and who was made an apostle of the highest mysteries to the Gentiles. This knowledge was brought to him by the Holy Spirit, having **never heard** it directly from Christ as the other Apostles had; and through his preaching, the Gentiles became Christians. 

But in the age that followed, the wickedness of nominal Christians <note>Christians in name only.</note> was like that of the Jews before them. This caused the Ark of the Testimony, the Book of the Law, their Temple, City, and Country, and **every excellent thing** they possessed to be taken away or destroyed. Similarly, these Christians caused the powerful effects of the Holy Spirit to be **withdrawn** after the death of those first preachers and faithful brethren. Eventually, a thick darkness spread over all nations, and there were only some of the holy men's writings left, contained in the Old and New Testaments. These were eventually brought to light and compiled into a **Book**. 

The understanding of these texts was limited in the following ages, except among those who suffered martyrdom and declared the power of the Word through mighty wonders. Eventually, **much teaching** began to spring up successively; yet the Holy Scriptures were not so closely examined nor so publicly shared until the time of **Luther**. He was motivated and assisted by a small book called *Theologia Germanica* (*The German Theology*) and the sermons of **Tauler** <note>Johannes Tauler (c. 1300–1361), a prominent German mystic whose work influenced the Reformation.</note>, both of which are most excellent in nature and were compiled during the obscure times before him.

Then Calvin arose, followed by many others afterward, who studied the literal text <note>original: "the Letter"</note> of the Scripture even more closely. Through this, a variety of **questions** were raised in divinity, though they have not been fully decided or resolved to the satisfaction of the differing parties by the efforts of all who have labored in **scholastic learning** <note>Academic or formal theological study.</note> to this very day. This has caused some to believe that the time had not yet come for the clear discovery of such things. 

But this **point of predestination** <note>The doctrine that God has ordained all that will happen, especially regarding the salvation of souls.</note> is considered the most hidden from human knowledge for the most part. However, there are those who, to the great comfort of their souls, have had most mysteries clarified for them by this author—including predestination, in this treatise of his. This raises a hope in them that the time is not far off when all the mysteries of God shall be revealed, and the manner in which this will be achieved will be perceived **in its season**. Furthermore, they have found that it is true of this book—<margin>Eph. 13.58. <note>This citation is likely a printer's error or refers to a specific external index, as Ephesians has only 6 chapters.</note></margin>—that **the more men read it, the better they will like it**; and by following the advice given within, they will find the **key** that unlocks all mysteries.

<summary>This preface outlines the history of divine revelation from the Patriarchs to the Reformation, arguing that spiritual understanding declined into "darkness" until being revived by the recovered scriptures and the mystical insights of authors like the one presented here.</summary>

# PREFACE to the READER.
5

If the inner Word is primarily considered in the reading and searching of the Scriptures, it will make them clearer and more delightful to the enjoyment <note>original: "Relish"</note> of our souls—provided there is any sense or feeling of God’s presence in our hearts. As in this following instance, <margin>Hebrews 1:1.</margin> where we may observe that formerly God spoke by the same inner Word at various times and in diverse ways to the fathers through the prophets, such as in dreams, visions, and voices. But in these last days (this was spoken in the time immediately after Christ lived on the earth), he has spoken to us by his Son. This is not to be understood only as he was in the flesh, but by his Spirit, through which the divine revelations of the mysteries of the New Testament are shown to be in a much more precious way than those of the Old. The <margin>1 Peter 1:17, 18, 19.</margin> Apostle Peter, who heard a voice from heaven out of the excellent glory of Christ on the Mount, says: *We have also a more sure word of prophecy.* The prophets had voices and things manifested to them in several other ways by the Word of prophecy. Some of the other apostles also heard this voice on the Mount; but he says, *“We,”*—which may mean himself, the other apostles, and the faithful—have also (just as the prophets had), besides the voices from angels or God himself externally, a more sure word of prophecy. *What is more sure than the implanted <note>original: "ingrafted"</note> Word, which is able to save our souls?* This is <margin>Romans 10:8.</margin> Christ in us, the Word of Faith by which we are saved. This, the Apostle Paul says, <margin>1 Peter 1:25.</margin> we teach; and the Apostle Peter calls it *“The Word of the Lord which endures forever.”* He says it is the *“Word of the Gospel which the apostles preach,”* which must certainly be the inner Word of prophecy. For it is the Eternal Word, by which all who have ever prophesied have been enabled and instructed, and no other; and since it is within the soul itself, it is certain they possessed it, and in that way, it was even more sure to them. And the faithful to whom the Apostle Peter wrote had it manifested, giving light to them in their souls; otherwise, if it had been related to them only outwardly without inner light, they could not have paid attention to it, in the judgment of the Holy Spirit in the Apostle. As he said to them: *“You do well to pay attention to it, as to a light shining in a dark place.”* This is the same light that shone in the darkness, and the darkness did not understand <note>original: "comprehended"</note> it—namely, in their dark souls—until the day dawned and the morning star <note>original: "Day-Star"</note> arose in their hearts. Since this light enlightens everyone coming into the world, being the most sure word of prophecy to and in us all, we should be obedient to it, so that after the morning star, the Sun <note>original: "Son," referencing Malachi 4:2</note> of Righteousness may arise in our hearts with healing, eternal life, and salvation in his wings.

For though the light is in all our darkest hearts and souls and shines there, yet if we do not pay attention to it, we cannot understand the light—or rather, we shall not be understood by it. Nor will the day dawn, neither shall we have any "morning" in us, <margin>Isaiah 8:20.</margin> as the Hebrew text in Isaiah expresses it. Then we cannot speak according to that Word which is the Law and Testimony—not that which is written with ink or on tables of stone, which do not endure forever, but the substance of it in the fleshy tables of our hearts. This was written by the finger of God when he created the soul at the very beginning <margin>1 Peter 1:25.</margin> of life in the womb. It is that which endures forever, as is suggested in the Psalms <margin>Psalm 93:5.</margin> in this manner: *“The testimonies of the Lord are very sure”*; <margin>Psalm 119:152.</margin> *“He has established them forever”*; <margin>Psalm 119:111.</margin> *“David took them as an inheritance forever”*; <margin>Psalm 119:160.</margin> *“Every one of the Lord’s righteous judgments endures forever.”*

He who attends to this innate Word of Life will soon have a clearer understanding of the Scriptures. Not only that, but he will at length attain what those who spoke and wrote them knew themselves. As the time of the world proceeds further toward its end, that shall be understood regarding the Eternal Word which neither the angels, nor prophets, nor apostles knew—who saw what the angels desired to look into but were not able. For the Word of God is the maximum that can ever possibly be known at all; by this, the holy men had their knowledge, having it manifested to them in their hearts; and their knowledge has been expressed by their words to them from the beginning of the world.

<header>PREFACE to the READER.</header>

...and will be so until the end of time. Some of them wrote these things in books that have been preserved for us, so that we might read those writings of men filled with the Holy Spirit. This Spirit proceeded from the Father and the Son through them—namely <note>original: "viz."</note>, Christ, whose name is called *the Word of God*. 

The words of those men may be called the words of God, and their minds—so instructed by divine wisdom and understanding—may be called the mind of God, or His thoughts, sense, and meaning. This is because these thoughts are not their own; rather, God Himself—His will, mind, word, and spirit, His light, wisdom, and understanding—is manifested in theirs. This is true for all people who speak or write of such things with a true and real knowledge of them. These truths will be manifested in everyone who is obedient and willing to be taught and enlightened by them toward a holy life; for God is the same yesterday, today, and forever in the souls of everyone, and He reveals His secrets to His holy people.

These things, and much more, are accurately revealed in this treatise and the author’s other works, for the purpose of clarifying the issue of predestination <note>original: "the Point of Predeſtination"; the theological doctrine that God has ordained all that will happen, especially regarding the salvation of some and not others</note>.

When I ponder this in my mind, I cannot help but value even more and love most highly the divine writings of the Holy Bible. I rejoice that God has bestowed such a great gift and endowment upon the blessed, childlike *Jacob Behmen* <note>Jacob Boehme (1575–1624) was a German Christian mystic whose writings were highly influential in the 17th century despite their complexity</note>, *so that he might, through his writings, lead us in such a simple way to understand the Scriptures of the holy prophets and apostles—which he has done in a fundamental and most convincing manner.*

### THE
## AUTHOR’S
# P R E F A C E.

<image-desc>A decorative square woodcut initial block containing a floriated letter W.</image-desc>

W *HEN* **Reason** *hears anything said concerning* **God** *suggesting what He is according to His* **Being**, **Essence**, **Substance**, *and* **Will**, *it imagines within itself that* **God** *is some strange thing far away, dwelling outside and beyond the* **place** <note>original: "Place"; here referring to the physical dimension or locality</note> *of this* **world**, *high above the* **stars**, *and that He governs the* **place** *of this* **world** *only by His* **Spirit** *with* **omnipotent power**.*

2. *But it supposes that His* **Majesty** *in the* **Trinity**—*in which* **God** *is especially revealed—dwells in* **Heaven**, *outside and beyond the* **place** *of this* **world**.*

3. *Because of this,* **Reason** *falls into a human* <note>original: "creaturely"; meaning an opinion limited by the perspective of a created being</note> **opinion**, *as if* **God** *were a foreign being. It imagines that before the* **time** *of the* **creation** *of* **living beings** *and of this* **world**, *He held a* **consultation** *within Himself in His* **Trinity**, *using His* **Wisdom** *to plan what He would make and what* **purpose** <note>original: "End"</note> *everything should serve. It assumes He framed a predestined* **purpose** *within Himself, deciding what He would ordain everything to be.*

4. *This is where the controversial* **opinion** *comes from regarding* **God’s determination** *concerning* **humankind**. *It suggests that* **God**, *in His* **purpose** *or* **predestination**, *chose one* **group** <note>original: "Part"</note> *of* **people** *for* **Heaven** *to live in His holy* **dwelling**, *while He appointed the other* **group** *to eternal* **damnation**, *in whom He will demonstrate His* **wrath**. *Conversely, it suggests that in the others—the chosen and elect—He will demonstrate His* **grace**.*

5. *And so it is thought that He has made a* **separation** *through* **predestination** *so that He might show His* **power** *in both* **love** *and* **anger**. *Therefore, it is believed that everything must, by* **necessity**, *be exactly as it is.*

6. *It is conceived that the* **group** *ordained to* **wrath** *is so rejected* <note>original: "reprobated"</note> *and hardened by* **God’s purpose** *and* **predestination** *that no* **possibility** *remains for them to attain the* **salvation** *of* **God**. *On the contrary, for the others, there is no* **possibility** *of* **damnation**.*

7. *Although* **Holy Scripture** *uses almost these exact* **words**—*which human* **reason** *accepts without truly understanding what* **God** *is—* **Scripture** *also says much more to the contrary. It states that* **God** *does not desire* **evil**, *nor has He purposefully, by way of* **predestination**, *created anything that is evil.*

8. We will offer a way to unite and reconcile both of these contradictory views, showing how each is to be understood in its own **foundation** <note>original: "Ground"; a central term in the author's philosophy referring to the underlying reality or origin of a thing</note>, to Christian and impartial readers who seek and love the truth. I say, we will give them a short explanation to consider and present our gift or talents—as they have been understood and grasped through the grace of the highest Good—for them to examine with a good intention.

9. By this, I do not mean to argue against or despise anyone for their personal opinion. Instead, I aim for a Christian and brotherly joining and uniting of the gifts that have been bestowed upon any of us by **divine grace**.

10. The branches and twigs of a tree do not appear identical in form, yet they all grow from the same trunk. One part provides and shares its essence <note>original: "Entity"</note> and strength <note>original: "Virtue"</note> with the others; all of them flourish and rejoice, blossoming and bearing fruit from a single source, without any resentment or dislike—

# The Way from Darkness to True Illumination.

The Soul, being heavy and sad, began to consider where it might find a suitable place to perform true repentance—somewhere it might be free from business, cares, and the hindrances of the world. It also searched for the means by which it might gain God's favor. Eventually, it decided to retreat to a private, solitary place and give up all worldly employment and temporal things. It hoped that by being bountiful and compassionate toward the poor, it would obtain God’s mercy.

In this way, the Soul devised all kinds of methods to find rest and regain the love, favor, and grace of God. But nothing worked. Its worldly business still followed it in the desires <note>original: "lusts"</note> of the flesh, and it was now trapped in the devil’s net just as much as before and could not find rest. Although for a short while it was somewhat cheered by earthly things, it quickly became as sad and heavy again as it had been before.

The truth was that the Soul felt the awakened wrath of God within itself, but it did not know how that had happened or what was wrong with it. Many times, great trouble and terror fell upon it, which made it comfortless, sick, and faint with sheer fear. The first "bruising" <note>original: "bruising"; likely referring to the crushing of the ego or the initial painful conviction of sin</note> it felt from the ray or influence of the movement of grace worked mightily upon it. 

And yet, it did not know that Christ was present within that wrath and severe justice of God. It did not realize that Christ was there, struggling against Satan—that spirit of error which had become part of the Soul and Body. Nor did the Soul understand that the hunger and desire to turn and repent came from Christ himself, by which it was being drawn in this manner. It did not know what hindered it from reaching a state of divine feeling. It did not realize that it had become a "monster" and bore the "image of the serpent" <note>In the mystical theology of the 17th century, the "image of the serpent" refers to the corrupted human nature resulting from the Fall.</note> in which the devil had such power and access. This influence had confounded all its good desires, thoughts, and motions, and led them away from God and goodness. Concerning this, Christ himself said: *The devil snatches the word out of their hearts, lest they should believe and be saved.*

->*An enlightened and regenerate Soul met the distressed Soul.*<-

By the providence of God, an enlightened and reborn <note>original: "regenerate"</note> soul met this poor, afflicted, and distressed soul and said:

"What is wrong with you, distressed soul, that you are so restless and troubled?"

->*The distressed Soul answered,*<-

"The Creator has hidden his face from me, so that I cannot reach his rest. Therefore, I am troubled and do not know what I should do to regain his loving-kindness. Great cliffs and rocks lie in my way to his grace, so that I cannot come to him. Even though I sigh and long for him ever so much, I am held back, so that I cannot share in his power, virtue <note>original: "virtue"; here meaning inherent spiritual power or efficacy</note>, and strength."

->*The enlightened Soul said,*<-

"You carry the monstrous shape of the devil and are clothed in it. Because that shape is the devil's own property or principle, he has access to you and the power to enter you. By this, he keeps your 'Will' from penetrating into God. If your Will could penetrate into God, it would be anointed with the highest power and strength of God through the resurrection of our Lord Jesus Christ. 

That anointing <note>original: "unction"</note> would break the monster you carry into pieces, and your original image of Paradise would be revived in your 'Centre' <note>original: "Centre"; the mystical core of a person's being where the divine spark resides</note>. This would destroy the devil's power within you, and you would become an angel again. Because the devil envies you this happiness, he holds you captive to his desire in the cravings of the flesh. If you are not delivered from this, you will be separated from God and can never enter our society."

<summary>A distressed soul struggles to find peace through outward works and solitude, only to be told by an enlightened soul that its inner "monstrous" nature and corrupted will are what truly block its connection to God.</summary>
<keywords>repentance, spiritual struggle, Jacob Boehme, the Serpent, the Will, divine illumination, grace, regeneration, inner monster</keywords>

# ON ELECTION.

## Chapter 1.

### Concerning the single Will of God, and the introduction of His revealed Essence into Manifestation; and what the One Only God is.

<margin>a That is, in such a way that the outward person, composed of the four elements, could hear Him.</margin>
<margin>b Exodus 20:2, 3.</margin>
1. <image-desc>Ornate woodcut initial letter G, surrounded by stylized floral and leaf patterns.</image-desc> God says through Moses, in a manifest, revealed, and open voice to the people of Israel (among whom He introduced Himself from His hidden secrecy in such a voice—a manifest sound after a formed, creaturely <term>creaturely: relating to or characteristic of a created being, as opposed to the Creator</term> manner—and caused them to hear so that the creature might understand Him), saying: ᵇ *I the Lord your God am but one only God; you shall honor no other gods besides me.*

<margin>c Deuteronomy 4:24.</margin>
<margin>d Deuteronomy 4:31.</margin>
2. Also Moses says, ᶜ *The Lord our God is a jealous and angry God, and a consuming fire*; and in another ᵈ place, *God is a merciful God*. Also, His Spirit is a *flame of love*.

3. These seem to be contradictory, in that He calls Himself an angry God and a consuming fire, and then also a *flame of love*, which can be nothing but good; otherwise He would not be God—that is, the only Good.

4. For we cannot say of God that He is this or that evil or good thing which has distinction within itself; for He is Himself beyond nature and creature, and without creaturely passions <note>original: "creaturely Affections"</note>.

5. He has no inclination toward anything, for there is nothing before Him to which He should incline, neither any evil nor good.

6. He is Himself the Abyss <note>original: "Abyss", referring here to the "Unground" or the bottomless void that exists before any created thing</note>, without any will at all. In respect to nature and the creature, He is as an eternal Nothing. There is no passion or pain in Him, nor anything that can either move toward Him or turn away from Him.

7. He is the one only Being, Essence, or Substance; there is nothing either before Him or after Him, out of which or within which He could form or grasp a will for Himself.

8. He also has nothing that can create Him or give to Him. He is the *Nothing and the All*, and is one single Will in which the world and the whole creation lie.

<margin>*</margin>
9. In *Him*, everything is equally eternal, without beginning, and equal in weight, measure, and limit. He is neither light nor darkness, neither love nor anger, but is the eternal ONE. Therefore Moses says: *The Lord is one only God*.

10. This unsearchable, inconceivable Will without nature—which is only one, having nothing before it or after it, which in itself is but one, which is as nothing and yet all things—this is, and is called, the one only God, who conceives and finds Himself in Himself, and generates God from God.

<summary>This chapter introduces God as a singular, unified Will that exists beyond nature and creaturely traits, explaining how He reveals Himself to humanity despite being an eternal "Abyss" or "Nothing." It addresses the apparent contradiction between God's identity as a "consuming fire" and a "flame of love."</summary>

### What the One Only God is. Chapter 1.

11. Thus the *first* and only Will without beginning, which is neither evil nor good, generates within *itself* the only eternal Good as a comprehensible will. This is the **SON** of the *abyssal* <term>abyssal: relating to the "Abyss," the infinite and bottomless void before creation</term> bottomless Will, and yet is equally eternal within that unbeginning *will*.

12. And that *second* Will is the first Will’s eternal perception and discovery, in which the "Nothing" finds itself to be "Something" within itself.

13. And the unsearchable—that is, the bottomless Will—goes forth through its eternal discovered or conceived will, and brings itself into an eternal *visibility* of itself.

14. Thus, the *bottomless* Will is called the Eternal **FATHER**.

<margin>But <unclear>may</unclear></margin>
15. And the *conceived* Will of the Abyss is called his generated, begotten, or innate **SON**; for it is the **ENS** <term>Ens: a Latin term for "being" or "essence"</term> or Being of the Abyss, in which the Abyss conceives of itself as having a ground or foundation.

16. And the *going forth* (exit) of the bottomless Will, through the conceived *Ens* or Being or Son, is called **SPIRIT**; for it drives the conceived *Ens* or Being forth from itself, into the movement or *life* of the Will, as a life of the Father and the Son.

17. And that which has gone forth is the *Longing* or *Delight*—that is, what is found by the Eternal Nothing—in which the Father, Son, and Holy Spirit (the Deity) find and behold themselves. This is called God’s *Wisdom* or Visibility.

18. This threefold Being, Essence, or Substance in its birth—in its visibility of itself within Wisdom—has *always* been from eternity, and possesses no other ground or place within itself except *only itself*.

19. It is one single life and one single Will, without *desire*, and is neither thick nor thin, neither high nor deep. It is neither space, time, nor place; it does not possess thickness or thinness, height or depth, space or time, but is through all and in all, and yet is to all things like an *incomprehensible* Nothing.

20. Just as the *influence* of the *sun* works in the whole world, in all things and through all things, and yet those things cannot take anything away from the sun but must be its *patient* <note>original: "Patient"; here meaning a recipient that is acted upon by an outside force</note> and operate with the virtue and power of the sun; in such a manner is God to be considered as he is, *without* nature and creaturely form in himself, in a self-contained *Chaos* <term>Chaos: in this context, an undifferentiated, infinite state of potential before form or nature</term> without ground, time, or place.

21. In this state, the Eternal Nothing comprehends itself in an *Eye*, or eternal seeing, for its own self-visibility, perceptibility, and capacity to be found.

22. Therefore, man *cannot* say that God has two wills, one for evil and the other for good.

23. For in the "creatureless" Deity <note>the Divine state before any created beings existed</note>, without nature, there is no more than *one* single Will, which is also called the *one and only God*.

24. He also wills nothing in himself except to find and understand himself, and to go out from himself, and so, with that going forth, *introduce* himself into visibility.

25. In this, men may understand the Trinity of the Deity together with the mirror <note>original: "Glass"</note> of his wisdom, acting as the *eye* of his vision or intuition.

26. In that one single wisdom, all powers and virtues, colors, wonders, and beings are understood in equal weight and measure, without specific properties, as *one* single *ground* of the Being of all beings.

27. It is a delight or longing found in himself toward *Something*: a delight or longing for the manifestation, revelation, or discovery of properties.

28. This delight, longing, or wisdom within itself, in the first ground, is still wholly *without* properties. For if there were properties, then there would also have to be something else that causes those distinguishing properties.

29. But now there is *no cause* for the production of the divine delight, longing, or wisdom, except barely and only the one single Will—that is, the one only God—who introduces himself into a *Trinity*, which is to say, into a comprehensibility of himself.

### Chap. 1.

30. This state of being contained is the *Centre*; namely, the *Eternal* contained ONE, and it is called the Heart or Seat of the Eternal Will of God. Within this, the Abyss <note>original: "Abyss"; here referring to the infinite, bottomless void of God's existence before he reveals himself</note> takes hold of itself in a "Ground" <note>original: "Ground" (German: *Grund*); a foundation or basis for existence</note>, which is the sole and only Place and Seat of God.

31. And yet, there is no possibility of division, separability, or distinction within it. It is also totally unmeasurable, without any form or likeness, for there is nothing before it that can be compared to it.
<gloss>as in paragraph 7</gloss>

32. This Heart or Centre of the Abyss is the Eternal *Mind*, namely of the Will. Yet it has nothing before it that it can desire, except for the one single Will that contains itself within this Centre. The first Will toward the Centre also has nothing that it can desire, except for this one single Place or Seat where it can find itself.

33. Thus, the first Will is the Father of its Heart—the place where it finds itself—and it is the *Possessor* of that which is found: namely, of its inborn or only-begotten Will, or Son.

34. The bottomless, unfathomable Will, which is the Father and Beginning of all beings, generates within itself a Place of containment; or, as we might say, it *possesses* the Place. This Place is the Ground and Beginning of every being, and it *holds* the unfathomable Will in return, which is the Father of the Beginning, so that it may have a Ground.

35. Thus the Father and his Son—namely, the Place of *Self-hood*—are one single God, having one single Will.

36. This one single Will in the contained Place of the Ground or Foundation goes forth out of itself, out of that containment; in this *Exit*, it is called a Spirit.

<margin>* Produces or brings about.</margin>
37. And the one single Will of the Abyss divides itself—along with the first eternal, unbeginning containment—into a threefold *Operation*, and yet it remains only *one Will*. Namely: the *first Will*, which is called Father, * produces or generates within itself the Son, namely the Place or Seat of the Deity.

38. And the Place or Seat of the Deity, which is the Father’s Son, operates within itself, in its own perceptibility, the powers and virtues of Wisdom; all of these powers arise in the Son.

<margin>*</margin>
39. And yet, here all powers are but one single Power, and that is the perceptible, discoverable *Deity* in itself, in its own Will and Being, without any separability or distinction.

40. These discovered, generated, or produced powers—acting as the *Centre* of the Beginning of all beings—are breathed forth by the first Will (called Father). He breathes them out of the one single Power, which is his Seat or Son, into the perceptibility of himself. This happens in the same way that sunbeams shed themselves forth out of the *magical fire* <note>original: "magick Fire"; Boehme uses 'magic' to describe the supernatural power of manifestation and the divine spark</note> of the sun, manifesting the power, virtue, or influence of the sun.

<margin>f Or stirring.</margin>
41. And so that *Exit* is a *Beam* of the power of God, acting as a moving Life of the Deity. In this, the unfathomable Will has brought itself into a Ground or Foundation, as into a power of <gloss>stirring or</gloss> willing; and that Will breathes forth the power, out from the power itself.

42. And this *Exit* is called the Spirit of God, which makes the third Operation or *Effect*: namely, the Life or stirring within the Power.

43. The fourth Operation is now performed in the out-breathed powers, namely in the Divine Visibility or *Wisdom*. Here, the Spirit of God (which rises out of the powers along with the out-breathed powers as one single Power) plays with itself.

<margin>*</margin>
44. Here, the Spirit introduces itself into *Formations* within the Divine Delight and Longing. It is as if it would introduce an <gloss>as a first image</gloss> *Image* of this generation of the Trinity into a distinct Will and Life of its own, as a modeling of the one single Trinity.

45. And that imprinted Image is the *Delight* or Longing of the Divine Visibility. Yet, one must not understand this as a physical, creature-like image that could be limited or outlined. Rather, it is the Divine *Imagination*, namely the first Ground or Foundation of the *Magia* <note>original: "Magia"; the divine, creative power that brings spiritual ideas into being</note>, from which the *Creation* has taken its beginning and origin.

It explains how God moves from a bottomless void into a contained "Ground" of existence, eventually leading to the Divine Imagination or "Magia" that precedes the physical creation.</summary>

61. For the first *Will*, which is called *Father*, loves its Son—namely, the "Heart" of its own manifestation—because the Son is the Father’s *Perceptibility* <note>The quality of being able to be perceived or known.</note> and Power.

64. Yet one must not imagine any division or separation here; for all the senses exist in *perfect balance* within the one and only Deity. The Holy Spirit is therefore called *Holy* and the "Flame of Love" because he is the power proceeding from the Father and the Son—namely, the moving *Life* within the first will of the Father and the second will of the Son in his power. He is the *Framer*, worker, and driver of the longing that has gone out from the Father and the Son—namely, within the *Wisdom*.

66. Therefore, dear brothers—you poor people confused by *Babel* <note>original: "Babel"; Böhme uses this to refer to the "City of Confusion," or the divided and institutionalized churches of his day.</note>, which has seduced you through Satan’s envy—take note of this: when people tell you about three persons of the Deity and the Divine Will, know that the Lord our God is one only God, *who neither wills, nor can will, any evil*.

67. For if he willed some evil and also willed some good within himself, there would be a *tear* and division in him, and there would have to be something else that caused this conflict.

68. But since there was nothing before God, there is nothing that can move him toward anything. If anything *could* move him, then that thing would be prior to and greater than himself; God would be at odds and divided within himself; and that thing would also have to be subject to change from a *beginning*, since it moved itself.

69. But we tell you, in accordance with the Word of the Only ONE, that the being, essence, or substance of God—insofar as he is called God—is understood to be *without* ground, place, or time. He dwells within himself and is not to be thought of as residing in any specific, distinct location with a separate dwelling.

70. If you want to know where God dwells, remove the concepts of Nature and created things, and then God is *All*. Take away the spoken, formed Word, and then you will see the eternal *Speaking Word* which the Father speaks through the Son, and you will see the hidden *Wisdom* of God.

71. But you will say: "I cannot remove Nature and created things from my mind; for if I did, I would be nothing. Therefore, I must represent the Deity through an image or resemblance, because I see both evil and good within myself, and the same is true for all created things."

## The Second Chapter.

### Of the Origin of *God’s Eternal Speaking Word*: And of the *Revelation* or *Manifestation* of the *Divine Power*; that is, of *Nature* and *Property*.

1. <image-desc>A decorative woodcut initial letter "C" contained within an ornate square border featuring stylized floral and vine motifs.</image-desc> **H**uman reason <note>original: "creaturely reason"</note> exists within the *formed, contained, expressed,* or *out-spoken Word*. Therefore, reason is a substance shaped by mental images. It always thinks that God is also an image or a shaped substance with some form or another, capable of being provoked and entering into properties of evil or good—much like how reason itself has imagined regarding this high *article* of the Divine Will.

2. First, reason supposes that God has, from eternity, framed within Himself a *predestined* and *predetermined* purpose and *election*, decreeing what He would do with His creation.

3. Second, it assumes that He has entered into a *decisive resolution* so that He might manifest His love and mercy to His chosen and elect.

4. Third, it believes that His wrath must be a *cause* so that His mercy and compassion might be made known. Fundamentally, this view suggests that God's wrath must manifest and reveal His majesty, just as fire reveals light.

5. However, human reason has no correct understanding of the will of God, nor of the *distinct divisions* <note>original: "divided distinction"</note> of the Word and of the creature.

<margin>*</margin> 6. For if God had ever held a *consultation* within Himself to manifest or reveal Himself in this way, then: 1. His manifestation would not have existed from eternity without a mind, intention, or place.

7. And 2. That council would have had to have a beginning.

35. And then it is rightly said here: *The Word* (namely, the eternal formed Word) was IN the beginning WITH God. For here two "beings" are to be understood: the **unformed** power (which is "IN") and the **formed** power (which is { **WITH** **BEY** } <note>WITH is English; BEY (bei) is German, implying a presence alongside or near.</note>), for the latter has entered into something involving movement.

36. The "IN" is still and *quiet*, and the { **WITH** **BEY** } is *compacted*; out of this compaction and active principle arise Nature, the Creature, and every existing being.

37. And here we should open the eyes of our understanding wide, so that we may know how to **distinguish** God and Nature; we should not merely say, "God wills it" or "God creates it."

38. It is not enough for men to play games with the Holy Spirit and **consider him a devil**, as enslaved reason does when it says, *God wills evil.*

39. For every willing of evil is a devil—namely, a **falsely formed** will for the sake of the self, a rift or splinter broken off from the entire Being, and a **delusion**.

40. Therefore, I deeply urge the reader to grasp our meaning and to avoid the delusion of making conclusions and determinations without the true inward ground or foundation. We will set down the true ground for him here.

41. Understand this: The powers used for the production of the Word are God, and the <term>active principle</term> <note>original: "Science"</note> or root—namely, the magnetic attraction—is the **beginning of Nature**.

42. Now, the powers cannot be revealed without this **desire for attraction**. God’s majesty in the working power of joy and glory would not be *revealed* without that attraction of desire; and there would be no light in the divine power if the desire did not attract and *overshadow* itself.

43. In this, the basis of darkness is understood, which then introduces itself to the kindling of fire. According to this, God calls himself an angry God and a consuming fire, in which there is great **divisibility**, as well as death and dying; furthermore, the gross, visible, creaturely life exists and is understood here.

44. You have an **analogy** <note>original: "Similitude"</note> of this in a *burning candle*; where the fire attracts the candle into itself and consumes it, where the being or substance dies. That is, in dying, the darkness transforms itself in the fire into a spirit and into another quality or source, which is to be understood as the *Light*.

45. Regarding this, people cannot understand that there is any true, tangible life in the candle. Out of which painful, tangible life, the Nothingness—namely the One—becomes *shining* and shines far and wide.

46. This is also how we are to conceive of God: that he has therefore introduced his Will into a <term>Science</term> <note>here meaning a focused point of knowledge or contraction</note> or root of nature so that his power in light and majesty may be manifested, and so that there might be a kingdom of *joy*.

47. For if no nature arose in the Eternal *One*, then *all* would be still and quiet.

48. But nature introduces itself into pain, perceptibility, and a power of being discovered, so that the eternal *stillness* might be movable and so that the powers of the **Word** might be apparent.

49. Not that the Eternal becomes painful—no more than the light becomes painful from the fire—but rather that the fiery property in the painfulness might *move* the still longing or delight.

<margin>
Operation or effect <note>original: *Wirkung*</note>.
Or self.
</margin>
50. Nature is the *instrument* of the still eternity, with which it forms, makes, and distinguishes, and therein compacts itself into a kingdom of joy.

51. For the Eternal Will reveals its **Word** by and through nature.

52. The **Word** takes *nature* to itself in the <term>Science</term> or root.

53. Yet the Eternal O N E, namely God J E H O V A H, takes *no nature* to himself, but dwells through and through nature, as the sun dwells in the elements, or as the nothingness dwells in the light of the fire; for the flash of the fire makes the nothingness *shining*.

54. And yet people must not say it is *merely nothing*, for the nothingness is God and all things. We only speak this way so that it might be possible to give the reader our *sense* and understanding.

55. Nature in its origin with its <term>Science</term> or root—namely in the attracting *desire*—is understood to be as follows. I will set before you an analogy in fire and light, through which the reader, by the *assistance* of divine power, may enter into the true sense and understanding.

56. Look upon a lit candle, and you see an analogy of both the *divine* and the *natural* being, essence, or substance.

<margin>In balance <note>original Latin: *Equilibrio*</note>.</margin>
57. In the candle, all things lie among one another in one substance, in *equal *weight*, without distinction: namely the fat or tallow; also the fire, the light, the air, the water, and even the earth; also the sulfur, the mercury, the salt, and the oil, out of which the fire, the light, the air, and the water exist. <note>Boehme uses these alchemical terms to describe the fundamental building blocks of all reality.</note>

58. While a person can observe *no distinction* in the candle—no way to say "this is fire," "this is light," "this is air," or "this is earthy"—and one sees *no cause* for sulfur, salt, or oil; one may say there is salt or tallow, and it is very *true*.

<margin>In balance <note>original Latin: *In equilibrio*</note>.</margin>
59. Yet all those properties lie within it, but in no *known* distinction; for they all stand in *equal *weight* in the <term>Temperature</term> <note>a state of perfect balance where no single quality dominates</note>.

60. In like manner, we are also to conceive of the Eternal O N E; namely of the hidden, unrevealed God, without or beyond the eternal <term>Science</term> or root—that is, without the powerful revelation or manifestation of *his Word*.

61. All powers and properties lie in the unbeginning God J E H O V A H, in the <term>Temperature</term>.

62. But, as the Eternal Will (which is the Father of every being and the origin of all things) compacts itself in Wisdom into a *Mind* for its own seat and power, and breathes forth that <term>introcompaction</term> <note>the act of folding or concentrating inward</note>; so its own Will compacts itself in the out-breathing of *its power* in the <term>Temperature</term>, in the going forth of itself into a <term>Science</term>.

<summary>Jacob Boehme uses the analogy of a burning candle to explain how the "nothingness" of God manifests as light through the "painful" friction of nature. He describes God as a state of perfect balance (Temperature) that reveals its Word and power by moving from stillness into the active qualities of nature.</summary>

63. And in this *knowledge* <note>original: "Science"; here meaning the root-seed of consciousness or potential.</note> or root, or indrawing *desire*—as one might, in a way, offer it to the understanding—eternal nature begins, and in nature, *substance* begins.

68. As is also to be seen in metals, earths, stones, plants, trees, and elements; everything has its beginning and origin from here.

69. And in nature, one thing is always set opposite to another, the one being an enemy to the other.

<margin><image-desc>A circular symbol with a cross or X inside, likely the alchemical symbol for the Earth or a marker for a specific point in the text.</image-desc></margin>
70. Yet not for the *purpose* <note>original: "End"</note> of being at enmity with one another, but so that in the *strife*, one should stir up the other and manifest it; that the *Mysterium Magnum* should enter into distinction and be an exulting and joyfulness in the eternal **One**.

71. It is so that the *nothing* might have *something* to work in, and to sport or act its part with—namely, the *Spirit of God*. Through the wisdom of eternity, the Spirit has introduced itself into such a *Mysterium Magnum* for its own visibility.

72. This *mystery* it has also introduced into a beginning for creation and for time, and condensed <note>original: "compacted"</note> it into a substance and the movement of the four elements, making the invisible spiritual world visible in and with time.

73. And we show you the true image of this in and by the *world*, namely in and by the sun, stars, and elements; and also of the mystery from which the four elements exist.

<margin>Abyss of the earth</margin>
74. We see that the *sun* gives light in the deep abyss of the world, and its beams kindle the *Ens* <note>Latin: "being" or "essence."</note> or being of the *earth*, out of which all things spring.

75. Also we understand that it kindles the *Ens* in the *Mysterium Magnum*, namely in the *Spiritu Mundi* <note>Latin: "Spirit of the World."</note>; that is, in *sulphur, mercury*, and *salt* <note>original: "Sulphur, Mercurius, and Sal"—the "Tria Prima" of alchemy representing the soul, spirit, and body/matter of all things.</note>, wherein the magic fire is opened, out of which the air, the water, and the earthiness take their origin.

76. That is, the one only element in the *Mysterium Magnum* of the outward world afterwards divides or distinguishes itself into four elements. These indeed existed before in the mystery, but they stood in the *knowledge* <note>original: "science"</note> or root in the magnetic impression, hidden within one another in the great mystery, and lying in only one essence or substance.

77. Now, just as the power <note>original: "virtue"</note> and beams of the sun unlock the *mystery* of the outward world so that creatures and plants proceed from it, so also on the contrary, the *mystery* of the outward world is the cause for the sun's beams to unlock and kindle themselves within it.

78. If the great mystery in *sulphur, mercury*, and *salt* did not lie in a spiritual manner and property in the *Spiritu Mundi*—namely, in the knowledge or root of the property of the stars, which is a *quintessence* <note>The pure, essential core of a substance; the "fifth element" beyond the standard four.</note> above or beyond the four elements—then the sun's beams could not be manifested.

<header>Chapter 2. *The Eternal Speaking Word in itself.*</header>

79. But the Sun is nobler and exists a degree deeper in Nature than the *Mystery* <note>original: *Mysterium*; the hidden inner core of reality</note> of the outward world—that is, the *Spirit of the World* <note>original: *Spiritus Mundi*</note> found in Sulphur, Mercury, and Salt, and in the *quintessence* <note>original: *quinta Essentia*; the purest essence</note> of the stars. Because of this, the Sun presses into the outward *Mystery* and kindles it, as well as itself, so that its beams become fiery; otherwise, they would not be fiery.

<margin>reciprocal connection?</margin>
80. Just as the Sun eagerly directs its desire into the active principle <note>original: *Science* or Root; the fundamental creative drive</note> of the *Great Mystery* <note>original: *Mysterium Magnum*</note>—meaning into the three primary elements of Sulphur, Mercury, and Salt—to kindle and manifest itself in them, so too does that active principle bring its desire out from the quintessence of the stars through those same three elements toward the Sun. It seeks the Sun as if it were the God of its nature, for the Sun is the "soul" of the *Great Mystery* in the outward elementary world, serving as a likeness of the inward, hidden God.

81. We also see how greedy and hungry the stars are for the power and virtue (or influence) of the Sun. They direct their active principle and desire in a magnetic way into the *Spirit of the World* and into the three primary elements, drawing the Sun’s power and influence into themselves.

82. On the other hand, the Sun also presses powerfully into the stars to receive their active principle or root, which is why they receive their shining from the Sun's power, virtue, or influence.

83. They, in turn, inject their kindled power like a fruit into the four elements. In this way, they influence one another; one is continually the manifestation, power, and life of the other, just as one can also be the destruction and corruption of the other.

84. To prevent any one property from rising above all others, the Most High has spoken or expressed them in *equilibrium* <note>original: *Equilibrio*</note>, balance, or harmony, according to His own Being. He spoke them out of His Eternal speaking Word and out of the eternal Great Mystery (which is entirely spiritual) into a state of "Time." He placed the Eternal into Time within a "Figure" or form, in which every created life exists and exercises its authority.

<margin><insert>Internal</insert></margin>
85. However, the angels and eternal spirits are exceptions, as is the true inner soul of humanity. These have their origin in the eternal, unbeginning active principle, root, or nature, as will be discussed later.

86. Now, understand this comparison in this way: God is the Eternal Sun, the only Eternal Good. But without the Eternal active principle or root—which is Eternal Nature—God would not be manifested with His solar power (His *Majesty*) without that eternal *spiritual nature*.

87. For without Nature, there would be nothing in which God could manifest His power, for He is the *beginning* of Nature.

88. Yet, He does not move Himself out of the Eternal ONE into an eternal beginning of Nature because He wishes to be something evil; rather, He does so so that His power might manifest as Majesty—that is, through *distinction* <note>the ability to tell one thing from another</note> and perceptibility.

89. He does this so that there might be motion, a "sport" and a scene, as if on a theater, in which the powers might play or act their parts together. In this way, they manifest, find, and perceive themselves in their interplay of love and *struggle*. From this, the great immeasurable Love-Fire becomes active within the bond and the birth of the Holy Trinity.

<margin>*</margin>
90. We present a further comparison of this through fire and light. Fire, in its painfulness, represents *Nature* in its active principle or root; Light represents the *Divine* Love-Fire.

<margin>* Giving.</margin>
91. For the Light is also fire, but it is a <gloss>yielding fire</gloss>, because it gives itself into all things. In its giving, there is life and being—namely, "Air" and a "spiritual Water." The Love-Fire of the Light brings its life into this oily Water, for that Water is the food of the Light.

<margin>Nature or Condition.</margin>
92. For otherwise, if the *Light* were shut in, and the spiritual *Water* could not separate itself from the fiery Quality—and so resolve, dissolve, or mix itself within the Nothing (that is, with the *Abyss* <note>original: "Abyss," here meaning the "unground" or the infinite void before creation</note>)—then the Light would go out.

93. But because it resolves, dissolves, or mixes itself with the Abyss (where the Eternal *Byss* <term>Byss: the ground or foundation, as opposed to the abyss/unground</term> or Foundation lies)—that is, with the <term>Temperature</term> <note>original: "Temperature," meaning the state of perfect balance where all spiritual powers are in harmony</note> where all the powers exist as One—the Light-Fire (or Love-Fire) draws that spiritual *Water* back to itself as food. Through this process of dissolving and mixing, the water becomes an "Oil" or <term>Tincture</term> <note>original: "Tincture," the essential spiritual essence or "color" of a substance that gives it life and power</note>; specifically, it becomes the power and virtue of the Fire and the brilliance of the Light.

<margin>*John 7:38*</margin>
94. And here lies the greatest <term>Arcanum</term> <note>original: "Arcanum," a deep, hidden secret</note>, or secret mystery of spiritual nourishment. Dear children, if you understood this, you would have the foundation of all hidden mysteries regarding the Being of all Beings. It was concerning this that Christ said:
> *He would give us the Water of Eternal Life, which would flow in us as a wellspring of Eternal Life.*
This is not the outward water generated from the physical light-fire, but the inward water generated from the *divine* Light-Fire, of which physical water is merely a type, image, or shadow.

95. Understand this comparison in this way: The Eternal and only Good—the Word of the holy "Mental Tongue" which the Most Holy JEHOVAH speaks out of the balance of his own Being, into the <term>Science</term> <note>original: "Science," here meaning the root-source or the "seeing" within the will</note> or Root of Nature—He speaks it for this reason only: to create a root of distinction or opposition. This is done so that his holy power and virtue might be distinct and enter into the brilliance of His Majesty; for it must be manifested through the fiery nature.

<margin><image-desc>A hand-drawn symbol resembling a sun or a star with eight rays.</image-desc></margin>
96. The Eternal *Will*, which is called "Father," brings its "Heart" or *Son* (which is its power) through the Fire into a great triumph of the Kingdom of Joy.

<margin><image-desc>A hand-drawn blue square bracket pointing toward paragraph 97.</image-desc></margin>
97. In the Fire is *Death*. That is, the Eternal Nothing "dies" in the Fire, and out of that dying comes the Holy Life. This is *not* a literal death, but it describes how the Life of Love exists through the intensity of the process. The "Nothing" thus takes an Eternal Life into itself so that it becomes tangible, yet it goes out from the Fire again as a "Nothing" <note>Meaning it remains spiritual and free from the limitations of matter</note>.

98. Just as we see that light shines from fire and yet is like "nothing" tangible, it is actually a lovely, giving, generous, and active power.

99. Understand it this way: in the separation or distinction of the "Science" (the root-source) where Fire and Light divide themselves, you should understand "Fire" to be the *Eternal Nature*. This is why God says He is an angry, jealous, or zealous God, and a consuming fire.

100. This fire is *not* called the Holy God, but rather his Zeal or Jealousy. It is a consuming power that acts upon whatever the desire—in its separation from the root—comprehends or conceives within itself. This happens when a distinct part of the root elevates itself into a "Self-Will" to go beyond the divine balance (<term>Temperature</term>), breaking itself off from the *total Will* and entering into <term>Phantasy</term> <note>original: "Phantasy," here meaning a state of illusion or a self-created reality apart from God</note>.

101. This is what Lord Lucifer and the soul of *Adam* did, and it is still done today in the human "Science" or root of the soul. From this is generated a "Thistle-Child"—a wicked and false nature of a *devilish* kind. The Spirit of God knows this well, and Christ said of such people:
<margin>*John 10:26*</margin>
> *They were not his sheep.*

<margin>*John 1:13*</margin>

104. Just as we understand two *beings* in the kindling of a fire—one in the fire and the other in the light, as two principles—we are to understand the same concerning God.

105. He is called God *only* according to the Light; that is, in the Powers of the Light, wherein the Knowledge <note>original: "Science"; in this context, it refers to an active root of consciousness or the "sensing" of the will</note> or Root is also manifested in endless variety or divisibility. However, all of this exists in the Love-Fire, where all properties of the powers surrender their will into the *One only*; that is, into the Divine Harmony <note>original: "Temperature"; the perfect balance of spiritual forces</note>. In this state, only one Spirit and Will rules in all properties, and the properties all surrender themselves into a great *Love* in and toward one another. Here, one property desires to taste and relish the other in great fiery Love, and all is but one entire lovely Power, flowing into one another; yet they manifest themselves through the diversity or separability of the Knowledge or Root and manifold powers, colors, and virtues, for the *manifestation* of the infinite Divine Wisdom.

106. We have an example of this in the sprouting Earth, in the herbs and plants, where fair, lovely fruits grow out of the Knowledge or Root of the Harmony—out of the *good part*.

107. *And on the contrary*, out of the knowledge of the fiery nature, with the impression of the *Curse* of the Earth (since the *Lord has cursed it because of the Fall of Man* and the Devil, and reserved it to be purged at his judgment), purely evil, stinging, and thorny fruits grow.

108. Yet these still have some good in them regarding their origin, where the Harmony still lies within the pure essence <note>original: "Quintessence"</note>, and at the end it shall be separated.

109. In this place, we must correctly understand that in the Divine Power—so far as it is called "God"—that is, in the Word of the *Divine Property*, there can be no will to evil, nor is there any experimental knowledge of evil within it.

110. But the knowledge of Good and Evil is found only where the unsearchable, bottomless <note>original: "abyssal"</note> Will separates itself into the fiery Knowledge or Root, in which the natural and created foundation lies.

111. For out of the divine Love-Knowledge or Root, no creature can be generated *by itself* and alone; it must have within it the fiery Triangle of the fiery Knowledge or Root, according to its suffering <note>original: "painfulness"</note>—that is, *its own self-will.*

112. This goes forth into a specific form out of the Harmony of the unsearchable, bottomless Will as an *expressed* or *spoken-out* Knowledge or Root—that is, a beam or ray from the whole, entire Will where the Word of Power separates itself into *Fire*, and *out of the Fire* back into *Light.*

113. Here the Angels and the souls of men *exist*; namely, out of the fiery knowledge of the beginning of Eternal Nature. There, that beam of the fiery knowledge shall again unite itself into the Light’s Harmony—that is, into the entire Total. Then it eats of the holy essence <note>original: "Tincture"</note> of the fire and of the light, out of the spiritual water, by which the fire becomes a kingdom of *Joy.*

<margin>soul mystic tempering</margin>
114. For the Spirit’s Water is a daily mortifying <note>the spiritual subduing of the lower nature</note> of the fiery knowledge, by which the fiery knowledge, through the Love-Fire, becomes a Harmony. Then there is also only one Will within it: to love everything that stands in this Root.

115. This is to be understood concerning the Angels of God, as well as the blessed souls, who all have their origin out of the *Knowledge or Root of the Fire.*

<margin>p Or Root of the Senses or Thoughts; see the *Key* <note>original: "Clavis"</note>, Verse 214.</margin>
116. In this Knowledge p the Light of God shines, so that they have a continual hunger after Divine Power and Love. They bring *Holy Love* into the fire as food, by which the fiery triangle is changed into pure holiness and love in great joy.

<margin>q See the word "Knowledge" <note>original: "Science"</note> in the *Key*, verses 210, 219.</margin>
117. For nothing exists or lasts eternally unless it has its origin out of the Eternal, beginningless Will—out of the fiery q Knowledge of the Word of God, as shall be mentioned hereafter.

3. This "conceiving" or "comprehending" is the act of *creating*. The "Science" or "Root"—which is the "Desire"—is the *beginning* that moves out of the balanced state <note>original: Temperature</note> toward distinction, variety, or divisibility.

5. The Science or Root is eternally in the Word, for it arises in the Will. While in the Word, it is God; but in the "partition" or distribution—that is, in the comprehension—it is the *beginning of Nature*.

### On introducing the Science into Nature.

The "shriek" or "crack" of this kindling is called *Salnitri* <note>original: *Salnitri*; a term for the explosive, creative catalyst in nature, often associated with spiritual saltpeter</note> in Nature. It is the root of all the "salts" (powers) and represents the divisibility of Nature, where divine knowledge <note>original: "Science"; here meaning the conscious power or "Scientia" of the spirit</note> divides itself into infinity. Yet, it remains constant within that "crack" of division or distinction in the substance.

40. In the kindling of the Fire—understood as the inward, magical Fire—the Spirit of God begins to move, just as air rises out of fire. For there, the <gloss>spiritual</gloss> "One Element" exists, which in the external world has unfolded itself into the *four elements* (earth, air, fire, and water). This is how it should be understood.

<margin>q Glimpse, or lightning, or sparkling, or twinkling.</margin>
41. In the <gloss>q</gloss> glimpse or sparkling of the Fire and Light, there is a *distinction* or separation. The Spirit—that is, the fiery knowledge or root of all powers—divides itself upward. It goes forth from the fiery "crack" as a new life; and yet, it is not truly a "new" life, but has simply taken on the form of Nature.

42. The *Ens* <term>essence or being</term> of Love remains in the middle, standing as the center of the Spirit. It yields a spiritual oil in which the Light lives, for it is the essence of fiery Love.

<margin>s Or waterish.</margin>

44. O you beloved wise men, if you only knew this, it would be well for you.

45. This same *dew* is true, modest humility, which is suddenly transformed by the Tincture and drawn back again by the Light; for it is the *Soul* of the Light according to Love.

46. And the Fire is the *husband* or man—namely, the Father's property—which is the Fire-Soul.

<margin>t Matthew 13:46.</margin>

## Chapter 3. *On introducing the Science <note>In this context, "Science" (from the Latin *scientia*) refers to a spiritual knowledge, a root-potential, or the divine "know-how" embedded in creation.</note> into Nature.*

67. For it is the eternal, continuous, and perpetual *manifestation* of the **Triune Deity**, in which all the properties of holy wisdom interact and mix in a perceptible way. This happens as a savor, a taste, and a unifying life of the "love-fire," where each property works within the others.

<margin>The 5th Form</margin>
68. It is called the power of the glory of God, which has poured itself out into the whole creation and all created things. It lies hidden in the center of *every* thing, according to that thing's specific nature, acting as a *tincture* <note>original: "Tincture"; in Böhme’s thought, this is a spiritual essence or transformative power that gives life and color to matter.</note> in the living or animate body.

69. From this "science" all things grow, blossom, flourish, and yield fruit. This power lies within the *quintessence* <note>original: "Quinta Essentia"; the fifth element, or the purest spiritual essence underlying the four physical elements.</note> and is a cure for sickness. If the four elements could be brought into a "temperature" <note>original: "Temperature"; a state of perfect balance or harmony where no single element dominates the others.</note>, then the glorious pearl <note>A metaphor for the divine spark or the Christ-spirit within nature.</note> would be revealed in its full operation.

<margin>Physicians.</margin>
70. However, the curse of God's anger holds this power captive within itself because of humanity's unworthiness—a fact well known to *physicians*. This power also exists outside of the four elements and is manifested in the "fire" through the "light" of love-desire.

<margin>The 6th Form: Jupiter, the Source of Life.</margin>
71. The sixth form in this "science" is the *speaking* within the divine power—that is, the Divine Mouth, the sound or voice of power. Here, the Holy Spirit, held in the embrace of love, goes forth clearly from the power that has been formed or conceived.

72. We can understand this by looking at the image of God in humanity, specifically in our *speech* and *discourse*. Similarly, there is a perceptible, active "speaking" within the divine power in its state of balance.

73. This active "speaking" is correctly understood through the *five senses* as a spiritual seeing, hearing, smelling, tasting, and feeling, where the manifestation of these powers works one within another.

74. This operation of the Spirit speaks itself forth in a clear, distinct sound. This is understood in humans, but it is also found in the "out-spoken Word" within all creatures—both those that are animate and those that are inanimate, like plants.

75. Through this, we understand how the spiritual world—the "spiritual sound"—has given itself into the creation. This is where the *sound* of every being or substance comes from. In the physical world <note>original: "Materiality"</note>, this is called a "mercurial power" arising out of a fiery "hardness." Other powers cooperate with this to create a noise, a tune, or a song, as we see in living creatures. Even in inanimate things, there is a noise or tune; for example, in a viol, lute, or other *musical instrument*, all harmony and melody lie together in a single work or instrument, waiting for the human understanding to bring it forth.

76. Furthermore, in this sixth form or disposition, we can perceive the true *understanding* of the five senses. When the Spirit has brought itself forth out of these properties, it returns to a state of balance and contains all properties within itself.

77. Just as the body is a physical power, the spirit is a volatile power—that is, it is sensitive and *thoughtful*. Within this spirit, the *mind* is found, and from the mind, the senses and thoughts arise.

78. These senses and thoughts arise from a multitude of infinite properties, born out of the "crack" or "shriek" <note>original: "Crack or Shriek, or Terror"; Böhme uses this to describe the sudden flash of differentiation or the "shock" of the fire-spirit transitioning into light.</note> of the fire. Therefore, they contain both centers within them: God's love and God's anger.

<margin>How did Christ's temptation affect his own nature?</margin>
79. As long as these thoughts remain in "temperature" (balance), they are *right*. But as soon as they leave that balance and try to prove themselves—seeking to find themselves only in specific properties and to know themselves in isolation—then the "Lie" is born. This is because they then speak from a "self-will," regarding other properties as false and despising them. In this way, they quickly fall into "self-longing" or *lust*. This is how we should understand the heavy fall of *Adam* and of *Lucifer*.

80. *Adam* was originally placed in a state of balance regarding these properties. However, his "science" (his internal root-potential) moved into *divisibility* and distinction, leading to false or evil desire and lust through the infection and persuasion of the *Devil*.

# The Fourth Chapter.
## Concerning the Origin of Creation.

1. <image-desc>Decorative woodcut initial 'C' containing floral patterns and scrolls.</image-desc> COURTEOUS Reader, I assume you are a human being and not an irrational beast. Do not let the vain babbling and long, frivolous speeches of the *sophisters* <note>original: "Sophisters"; academic or religious scholars whom the author views as deceptive or overly focused on logic rather than spiritual truth.</note> seduce you with their foolish <note>original: "calvish"; literally calf-like, meaning stupid.</note> understanding. They do not know what they are babbling about; they do nothing but dispute and wrangle, and they do not understand the very things they shout against, having no foundation in the true sense and meaning.

2. Neither be offended by this *pen*, or the *hand that holds the pen*. The Most High has *fashioned it and made it so*, and breathed His breath into it, which allows us to know, see, and understand *this very well*. We do not know this from the opinions or ideas of others, nor by some astrological influence or suggestion, as we are sometimes accused.

3. <margin>In the Paradisaical Substantiality.</margin> A gate is opened to us in the Holy *Ternary* <note>original: "Ternario Sancto"; referring to the Holy Trinity or the divine triad of power, heart, and spirit.</note> to see and to know what the LORD wishes to be known in man at this time.

4. God manifests himself so that conflict may end, and so that men might *no longer argue about God*.

5. This should be no wonder to us; rather, we ourselves should be that "wonder" which He has brought forth in the fullness of His time. We would realize this if we only knew what we truly are, and if we moved away from conflict into the harmony of the one Will and loved one another.

6. The entire creation—including both eternal and temporal creatures and substances—exists within the Word of Divine Powers.

7. Eternal things arise from the active principle of the *speaking*—that is, from the one Will of the Abyss <note>original: "Abyss"; the "Ungrund" or the bottomless, incomprehensible source of all existence in Böhme's theology.</note>, which introduces itself into individual existence through the Word and the active drive of the Will.

**10.** Three principles generate themselves within the "substance of substances" <note>the underlying essence of all things</note>, where one is the cause of the other. In this, one must also understand a *threefold life*—that is, a threefold, distinct *divine revelation* or manifestation.

He commanded every creature to come forth, each according to its own property.*

27. But we must understand that in the *Verbum Fiat* (the "Word of Command"), the *Mysterium Magnum* is condensed or conceived into a *substance*. It moves from an inward spiritual substance into a tangible one; and within that tangibility lies the "science" or the root of life.

37. This happens in the same way that the inward magical Sun of the *Light* of God ignites inward Nature, which is where paradisaical growth and blossoming reside.

38. Understand this as occurring within the "temperature" <note>original: "Temperature"; here meaning a perfect balance or harmonious mixture of elements</note> of the single Element that is hidden from earthly things. But we will now show the reader, in a summary way, what the "Being of all Beings" truly is.

# Chapter 4: Of the Origin of the Creation.

## Reason's Objection.

85. But now *Reason* says: it was *God's will* that his *wisdom* might be distinguished from *folly*, so that it might be understood what *wisdom* is and what *folly* is. Otherwise, people would not know what wisdom is or what folly is. *Therefore, God allowed him to fall and hardened his heart so that he was forced to do it; otherwise, it would not have happened.* This is as far as *Reason* can reach, and no further.

## Answer.

86. When the *Abyss* with the *self-will* was introduced into a fiery *division* and *distinction*, then the <term>science</term><note>original: "Science" — In this context, the term refers to an innate "spark" or the capacity for knowledge and creative will, rather than modern empirical science.</note> in the *fire* was *free* within that *distinction* or *division*. Thus, every *science* divided itself during that *distribution* into its own *will*. The *multitude* of *wills* were all placed in a state of <term>temperature</term><note>original: "Temperature" — A state of perfect harmony or balance where all opposing qualities (like heat and cold) are unified and at peace.</note> and had the three hierarchies depending on them.

87. In that state, every *heavenly host*, through the *comprehension* of the *creature* in the first three principles, could introduce itself into a *hierarchy* however it chose. The truth of this appears as follows:

88. The *devils* were originally *angels* and stood in a state of *balance* within their *free will*. They could turn or incline themselves toward whatever they desired, and they would be confirmed or established in that choice.

## Objection.

89. You might say, "No! God could do with them *whatever he wanted*!" Yet you must understand this correctly.

## Answer.

90. The *science* or *root* is God's eternal, *unsearchable will* itself, which has introduced itself into *nature* and *creature*.

91. Only in the *science* of the *creature* did the *will* exist to introduce itself into <term>phantasy</term><note>original: "Phantasy" — Here meaning a distorted, self-centered realm of imagination or a false reality created when the soul turns away from God.</note>—namely, into the *center* of the *fire-life*. Following this was the *separation* and *confirmation*, as well as the casting out from the *balance* into *torment*, into which the *science* had converted itself by its own *free will*.

92. This *hierarchy* (the *phantasy*) assumed *that will* and confirmed it within *itself*. Thus, an *angel* became a *devil*—namely, a *prince* in the *wrath of God*—and in that state, he is "good" in his own eyes.

<margin>]</margin>
93. For, as the *anger* of God is, such is also its innate *throne-prince*. He is and remains eternally a *prince* with his *legions*, but within the *kingdom* of *phantasy*. Just as the *kingdom* of *that power* is within itself, so also is its innate *prince*.

<margin>Or killing.</margin>
94. The *source* or *torment* of the wrathful *kingdom* is the *mother* of his *falsehood*—namely, *his god*. He must now do what his *god wills*. Thus, he is an *enemy* to the *good*, for *love* is his *poison* and *death*.

<margin>Or quality.</margin>
95. Even if he sat within the *holy power* of the *light*, he would attract nothing <margin>Or quality.</margin> to himself but the *source* or *torment* <margin>Or killing.</margin> of *poison*. For that would be *his life* and *nature*. It is as if a *man* were to put a *toad* into a *box of sugar*; it would draw only poison out of it and would poison the sugar.

<summary>This page argues that evil arose not because God forced it, but because angels used their free will to move from a state of balance into a self-centered "phantasy." Once established in this wrathful state, the devil's nature is so corrupted that he perceives good as poison.</summary>
<keywords>Jacob Boehme, free will, origin of evil, fallen angels, Phantasy, Science, Temperature, divine wrath, Lucifer</keywords>
