<header>Of the Origin of the Creation. Chapter 4.</header>

## Objection.

96. But Reason says: if *God had infused His Love into him* again, he would have been an Angel again; therefore, it depends on God’s *predestined purpose*.

## Answer.

97. Listen, Reason: look at a *thistle* or *nettle*. The sun shines on it all day, and its power and virtue penetrate it, willingly giving its beams of love into the plant's *venomous, stinging essence* <note>original: "Ens," a philosophical term for the core being or essence of a thing</note>.

<margin>This is an upside-down world</margin>

98. The *thistle* also delights itself in the *essence* of the sun; but because of it, it only grows to be a more prickly thistle; it becomes even more *stubborn*.

99. This is also how we should understand the Devil: even if God had infused His love into him, the *root* <note>original: "Science," here meaning the active, knowing root of a being's will</note> or source of that unsearchable will had already transformed itself into the nature of a thistle. That is, the Eternal Will, which has no foundation or location, is a will unto itself that cannot be broken or *resisted*.

100. And yet we must *not* think that the "Will of the Abyss" <note>the Abyss, or "Ungrund," is Böhme's term for the absolute, groundless nothingness from which God and all existence emerge</note> caused this; for that Will is neither evil nor good, but is simply a Will—a *root* of consciousness without understanding or inclination toward anything specific.

101. For it is only one thing, and is neither desire nor longing, but is a movement or *willing*. It is like how the physical world in the *Spirit of the World* <note>original: "Spiritu Mundi"</note> has a certain drive or volatility, or like how the air has a fluidity; it is neither evil nor good.

102. We must understand that the "three first" <note>the first three properties of eternal nature in Böhme's system: contraction, friction, and fire</note>, along with their sensory foundation, pressed into that will and took possession of it. Although they arise out of that same *will*, they treat it as their own property.

103. In the same way, we should understand the root—that is, the single Eternal Willing from the Abyss—which arises out of the Eternal One and has surrendered itself into the "creature of fantasy" <note>here, "fantasy" refers to the illusory, self-centered, or prideful state of being</note>, namely into the wrath of Eternal Nature, leading to *evil*.

104. That Will *is not* the cause of the "fantasy." Rather, the cause of the Fall is the "three first" properties in which the creature exists—that is, the Nature within the Eternal Bond, from which understanding and "fantasy" arise.

105. For the Abyssal Will is not the creature itself; it has no image or representation. It is only in Eternal Nature that images or representations arise, as well as the creaturely will toward specific things and toward multiplicity.

106. The Abyssal Will belongs to God, for it exists in that Oneness.

107. And yet it is not God Himself. For "God" is only understood when the Will of the Abyss centers itself within the Trinity during the process of *generation* <note>original: "Geniture," the eternal birth of God</note> and expresses itself through the *longing of Divine Wisdom*.

108. The foundation of Nature has also been generated from eternity out of that Will in which the Deity expresses itself as the Trinity.

109. For in this, there is no predetermined plan, but rather a *birth*: the "eternal birth" is the predestined purpose—namely, that God will generate God and manifest Him through Nature.

110. Now Nature shuts itself up in its own *willing*—that is, into a painful, hostile life. And that same hostile life is the cause of the Fall.

111. For that life surrendered itself to the *fantasy* of Nature, or the play of generation; it made itself the promoter or lord of that fantastical nature. In turn, the "fantasy" took that life into itself and gave itself up completely to it.

<margin>* Or "into"</margin>

112. And now the *fantasy* and the life have become one thing. This thing contains the Will of the Abyss—the Divine consciousness <note>original: "Science"</note>—through which God generates Himself within God.

<summary>Böhme argues that the Devil's fall was not caused by a lack of God's love, but by the creature's own internal nature turning God's light into "prickly" wrath, much like a thistle uses sunlight to grow its thorns. He distinguishes between the neutral "Abyssal Will" and the "fantasy" of self-centered nature that causes spiritual separation.</summary>

<keywords>Jacob Böhme, Abyss, Ungrund, Phantasy, Free Will, Divine Love, Predestination, The Fall, Eternal Nature, Trinity, Spiritu Mundi</keywords>

<page-num>183</page-num>
## Chapter 4. Of the Origin of Creation.

113. But in this included <term>Science</term><note>original: "Science"; here referring to a divine, foundational knowledge or the "root" of all possibilities and existence.</note>, God does not generate *himself*; indeed, he generates himself *within it*, but he is not manifested in the Science or Root so far as it contains and takes hold of Nature.

114. God is immovable and does not act within it. He does not generate a Father, Son, Holy Spirit, and Wisdom there; instead, he generates a <term>Phantasy</term><note>original: "Phantasy"; in this context, it refers to an illusory or distorted image that lacks the substance of divine reality.</note> according to the property of the dark world.

115. God is indeed a God within it, but only dwelling in himself—not in the creature, but in the <term>Abyss</term><note>original: "Abyss"; the infinite, bottomless depth or the "Unground" out of which all things emerge.</note> beyond all movement, and without the willing or the living of the creature.

116. Now, if the creature does anything, God does not do it within the will of the Abyss (which is also in the creature); rather, the living and willing of the creature's own life does it. This is how we are to understand and know the nature of the Devil.

117. He <note>original: "It repents him"; meaning the Devil regrets.</note> regrets that he has become a devil, seeing that he was once an angel.

118. Now, he does not regret this in the *will of his life* as a creature, but according to the will of the Abyss, where God is so near to him.

119. There, he is ashamed before God’s *holiness* that he was once such a holy angel and is now a devil.

120. For the <term>Science</term> of the Abyss is ashamed that such an image is manifested and stands within it, so that the Abyss itself appears outwardly as a Phantasy.

121. But that will cannot break or *destroy* the Phantasy, for they are one and the same thing. Also, there is no source of pain or torment within it, nor any *perception* or feeling of the Phantasy; it is simply a Science or Root in which the Phantasy images or forms itself.

122. And now that Phantasy receives nothing into itself except a *similitude*, or something like itself; and that likeness is the power of its life.

123. If anything else entered into it, then the Phantasy would have to cease and vanish. Then, that from which it is generated—namely, Nature—would also vanish with it. And if Nature ceased and vanished away, then the *Word* of the Divine Power would not be speaking or manifest, and *God* would remain *hidden*.

124. Thus, understand that all of this is inevitable—both that which is *evil* and that which is *good*. For in God all is good, but in the creature, there is distinction or difference.

125. The life of the eternal creature was *wholly free* in its beginning, for it was manifested in the <term>Temperature</term><note>original: "Temperature"; a state of perfect balance or harmony among the various qualities of existence.</note>.

126. That is, the angels were created in Heaven out of the quality and property of that nature.

127. The *Dark World* and the Kingdom of Phantasy were both present there, but they were not manifested in Heaven.

128. But the *Free Will* in the fallen angels made it manifest in themselves; for the will inclined itself toward the Phantasy, took hold of it, and gave itself up to it in its life.

129. Now, that Dark Kingdom, the Phantasy, and the creaturely nature of the fallen angels have, at that instant, become *one thing*—one will and one substance.

130. But because that <term>apostate will</term><note>The rebellious or fallen will of the angels who turned away from God.</note> wanted to dwell and govern not only in the Phantasy, but also in the Holy Power in which it stood at the beginning, the Holy Power—namely, the Science or Root in the Light of God—*pushed that will out from itself* and hid itself from it.

131. That is, the <term>Inward Heaven</term><note>The internal, spiritual state of divine presence and light.</note> shut it out, so that it no longer sees *God*. This is the same as saying it died to the Kingdom of *Heaven*, or the Kingdom of the Good Will.

132. And yet, it is still in God, just as the *night is in the day*. Night is not manifested in the day or the sunshine, and yet it is still there.

<margin>John 1:5</margin>
133. But it dwells only in itself, as it is said in John: *The light shined in the darkness, and the darkness did not comprehend it.* <note>original: "comprehended it not."</note>

<summary>This page explains the metaphysical origin of evil and the fall of angels, arguing that while God is present in all things as an "Abyss," the creature's own free will creates the distinction between good and evil. It describes how the fallen angels' will became one with a distorted "Phantasy," leading to their exclusion from the "Inward Heaven" while still existing within the totality of God's presence.</summary>
<keywords>Free Will, Fall of Angels, Science, Phantasy, Abyss, Temperature, Inward Heaven, Darkness and Light, Jacob Böhme, Divine Manifestation</keywords>

# A brief clearing of some Questions. Chapter 12.

24. But the separability, or distinction, in the fiery science <term>original: "fiery Science"; a term in Boehme's mystical philosophy referring to the soul's origin within the "fire" of God's nature</term> continues as long as souls are being born.

25. There is no certain decree <note>original: "Ordination"</note> from eternity upon any particular soul which is yet to be born; there is only a common, *universal* foresight of grace. The decree begins at the same time as the person's life <note>original: "the Time of the Tree"</note>.

26. This foresight exists even in the *seed* before it becomes a living creature, and then God knows what the foundation of that soul will be.

27. But the judgment belongs to the *harvest* time, just as Christ speaks in all his parables or metaphors.

### Of *Lydia, the Seller of Purple.*

<margin>* Acts 16:14.</margin>
28. It is written of her: *The Holy Spirit, or the Lord, opened her heart, so that she believed in the name of JESUS.*

29. It was with Lydia as it is with all strangers and foreigners who do not know the name of Jesus, and yet live according to their inner spirit <note>original: "inward Ground"</note> without any preconceived mental images <note>original: "imaginary Conception"</note>. These people *desire* to know the one and only God and to surrender themselves to him. They are taken hold of by the incorporated grace of the inspoken Word <term>the "inspoken Word" refers to the divine breath or power placed within human nature at creation</term>; even without the knowledge of human reason, they are chosen and born as children of grace. This is how we should understand the case of *Lydia*.

30. In the beginning, she might have taken Paul for an unfamiliar teacher. But when she heard him preach the law of righteousness—and that the law of sin, which held humanity captive, was fulfilled by such grace—then her inner spirit, in its hunger for justification, was stirred by the incorporated grace. Christ became living in her, so that she received and recognized Christ’s voice in the words of Paul. What Christ taught within her was effective because Christ had become audible in her soul.

31. But it was not so with the other pagan people, for they remained only in their own mental images and imagination. Their hearts were not inclined to know the one and only God, for they had their pagan idols whom they served; they only wanted to hear some *new thing from Paul*.

32. Nevertheless, the Word entered their ears and pressed into those who had a good foundation. These people were converted later when they heard more preaching about Christ; just as in that same place, *many thousands were eventually converted* as the Word took hold of them more and more.

33. Likewise, many of those who heard *Peter* on the *Day of Pentecost* were converted later, even though they *scorned him on that very day.*

<margin>* John 19:34.</margin>
34. But when the Word echoed more and more within them, the hour of their inward hearing arrived. This was the case with *Longinus* <note>the traditional name of the Roman soldier who pierced Jesus' side</note>, who *pierced Christ in the side. The hour of his conversion came when he heard many people say Christ was the Son of God; he eventually became a martyr for Christ's sake, as historical accounts mention.

35. We should not say here that *Lydia*, above all others, was ordained from eternity for this—that she *alone* should hear or listen to Paul. Rather, at this time she was in a state of divine preparation and truly wanted to understand the truth about God. Her heart panted for it, and therefore God opened her heart.

<margin>* Acts 17:11.</margin>
36. Others were not prepared at *that specific time*. But when the Holy Spirit began to knock at their hearts, it first took hold in their ears until they opened to him. Then they thought and reflected upon it, and searched the Scriptures to see whether what Paul said was true—as is mentioned concerning the *Ephesians* <note>The author likely means the Bereans, as referenced in the margin for Acts 17:11</note>.

37. When they heard the Word more and more, the hungry doors of their hearts were opened wide, providing a place for Christ to dwell with his Word.

<summary>This page argues against individual predestination from eternity, suggesting instead that God's grace is universal and that conversion occurs when a person is spiritually prepared. Using the examples of Lydia and Longinus, the author explains that the "inner ground" of a seeker allows the "inspoken Word" of God to take root and bring about faith.</summary>

# Chap. 12. A brief clearing of some Questions.

<margin>* Matthew 27:54. † Virtuous or honest.</margin>
38. As it has gone also with all the <term>Heathen</term> <note>original: "Heathen"; referring here to non-Christians or pagans of the ancient world.</note>, and also with the *Jews*, who first mocked Christ when he hung upon the Cross; but when they saw what was done then, *they were struck in their hearts and converted, and said, "In truth, this man was a* † *virtuous man, and the Son of God."*

39. This happened to those *Jews* whose <term>inward Ground</term> <note>Böhme uses "Ground" (German: *Grund*) to refer to the deepest, most essential foundation of the soul or being.</note> stood open at this time, to whom God opened the embodied *Grace* in the *Spirit* of Christ.

40. As one often finds in histories, many people in their contrived pagan <term>imaginations</term> <note>original: "imagibility"; the capacity for mental imagery or the state of being shaped by worldly thoughts.</note> have for a long time mocked Christ; and yet in the end, when they have entered into the sincere depths of themselves and have clearly perceived what kind of "fables" (as they call them) have been told concerning Christ, they have converted.

41. For as soon as the heart stops its imagining and sinks deeply into its own inner foundation, then the voice of Christ in the *Word* enters in and knocks at the essence of the soul.

42. The imagination, or the impression of earthly matter, *prevents* the heart from standing still before God and entering into its inward depth where *God* teaches and listens.

43. For God himself is present in all places, through and through all things; as it is written, *Do I not fill all things?* Why then should the soul <term>immerse</term> <note>original: "demerse"</note> itself into anything else to hear God than into its own <term>Abyss</term>? <note>original: "Abyss"; Böhme uses this to describe the infinite, bottomless depth of the divine presence within the soul.</note> There God is, and dwells from eternity to eternity; he only needs to be manifested within the creature.

44. Moreover, he stands in the Spirit of Christ in that same inward depth and knocks at the door of the soul: Now, if the soul only turns toward him, then Christ himself opens the door of grace to it and draws near, and shares a meal with it, and the soul with him (*Revelation* 3).

->Also, Matthew 13<-

45. b "To you it is given to understand the Kingdom of God, but to others it is given in parables or analogies, *so that they hear and do not understand*." Also, c "He explained the parables or analogies to the disciples, and not to others."

46. Here now, human reason lies so dead that it sees nothing without the Divine Light, and it assumes that Christ would not *grant* it to others because they were not worthy of it. Although the people flocked after him and with an eager longing heard him teach, this matter has a different "A, B, C"—a different fundamental logic and meaning.

<margin>d John 14:16, 17, 26.</margin>

48. The voice of the Father in Christ, within God's <term>Righteousness</term> <note>original: "Righteousness"; here implying God's strict justice or holiness.</note>, was not meant to enter into the hearts and ears of the simple common people, except for those through whom the Father wished to work wonders or *miracles*.

49. But this voice was meant to enter into them which the Holy Spirit brought with it out of Christ's suffering, death, and resurrection—namely, the voice of the open door of grace.

50. For before Christ's suffering, the voice of the Holy Spirit in Christ was still within God's *justice* in the Law; but through Christ's death, the Law of the justice of God was *fulfilled*.

51. Therefore, the Holy Spirit afterwards went out through that fulfillment—through Christ's wounds, blood, and death—into the *greatest* compassion and mercy in the Spirit of Christ; *this is what poor sinners should hear, those who seek after him with sincere desire.*

### A brief clearing of some Questions. Chap. 12.

52. But to the disciples was given the Father's voice in God's righteousness, so that they should hear it from Christ; for they were to first begin with that same fiery righteousness in which the Father's omnipotence stood—namely, the soul's ground. <note>original: "soulsh Ground"; the fundamental spiritual essence of a person.</note>

53. Afterwards, on the Day of Pentecost, the Holy Spirit was given to them out of the grace-love from Christ's fulfillment of righteousness, entering into the fiery righteousness of the Father in the Law.

<margin>Acts 2:13.</margin>
54. And when that was done, <gloss>e</gloss> then the tongues in them—namely, the Father's righteousness—were divided; and the Spirit of Christ went forth through the division of God's righteousness with the flame of love.

55. And that was done for them so that they might be grounded in grace within the Spirit, according to the spirit of both the Law and the Gospel; for they were to perform wonders or miracles.

56. For the power of wonders or miracles comes from the Father's omnipotence and property, and not through the property of love and humility. This love must now suffer and surrender itself to God's Law and righteousness in His anger, fulfilling that anger with love and suffering, and thus being transformed into the love of compassion and mercy.

57. As we see clearly in Christ's person: when he wanted to perform miracles, he first prayed to his Father in the fiery omnipotence of righteousness.

58. But when the Father's righteousness was fulfilled by his love and humility in his blood of the love-tincture <note>original: "Love-Tincture"; in this context, a spiritual essence or "medicine" that transforms the soul from a state of anger to a state of love</note> of the name JESUS, then the Father's righteousness in His anger was subjected to the love of Christ.

59. And out of that subjection, *others* besides the disciples would hear the Holy Spirit speak after Christ's ascension into heaven and would understand Christ's parables or allegories; and so it happened that they later understood all the parables well.

<margin>Luke 24:13.</margin>
60. For the Spirit of Christ, through his fulfillment and resurrection, opened their understanding—as happened with <gloss>f</gloss> the two disciples on the way to Emmaus. A great company of people also heard the Spirit of Christ speak through the mouths of the apostles after his resurrection, sent by the true Sender out of Christ's sufferings and death; they understood the parables without needing the explanation of obscure words.

<margin>Matthew 13:34.</margin>
61. Therefore, before his suffering, when he lived and walked upon Earth, <gloss>g</gloss> Christ taught only in parables or allegories, so that they would not grasp the Spirit of Christ except through the righteousness of the Father.

<margin>Acts 2.</margin>
62. For that was not the true foundation <note>original: "Ground"</note> which he intended to bestow upon them out of his grace; rather, that foundation was what happened <gloss>h</gloss> on the Day of Pentecost, proceeding from his merit, when he overthrew sin and sealed it up within God’s righteousness.

<margin>John 17:12; 18:9.</margin>
63. They were not *all* meant to travel around performing wonders and miracles like the disciples, who were ordained or appointed for it from the Father's righteousness. Concerning them, Christ said: <gloss>i</gloss> *Father, I have lost none of those whom you have given me out of your righteousness, except for the lost child of perdition* <note>original: "Perdition"; eternal ruin or damnation, referring to Judas Iscariot</note>, who was already lost so that the Scripture might be fulfilled.

64. By this, Christ means all those whom his Father had given him for his order, ordinance, and for the *offices* of his invited kingdom.

64. But others are born through the spirit of humility out of Christ's love, through the process or way of Christ's suffering and death. They follow him in his path and process under the banner of his cross in patience, surrendering themselves out of God's righteousness and offering themselves in humility to the *Spirit* of Christ. Because of this, the *Jews* and *heathens* began murdering them.

...Christians, which at present has ceased for a long time, since men insist on setting the Spirit of Christ within themselves upon soft cushions, and placing it in fat bellies, in might, authority, pomp, state, and glory.

<margin>l Christ in the Christians.</margin>
67. ^l Who has appeared and been manifested for this reason only: that he would suffer and fulfill God's anger within his righteousness, by giving himself up to his sufferings.

68. ^m Therefore, look at yourself, you so-called "Christendom," and consider whether your righteousness currently stands in the patience of Christ's sufferings. Foreign languages are supposed to make you an Apostle; striving, raging, fierce wrath, and contention make up your "apostolic" heart—under which nothing remains but your own honor, full of the desires and thirsting of the *black devil*.

72. You wicked, evil one! Behold, a messenger comes out of God's righteousness who will require an account of your Christian name—one that hangs *over you* with *fire and sword* to overthrow you in your falsehood, perjury, treachery, and unfaithfulness, and to manifest his true children of obedience in his love. You will shortly find this by experience; we speak as we must. AMEN.

### Objection.

<margin>o Luke 23:34.</margin>
73. The words of Christ are also raised as an objection, where he says, ^o *Father, forgive them, for they know not what they do.*

### Answer.

74. As mentioned above: the <term>mysteries</term><note>The hidden spiritual truths of the faith.</note> of the kingdom of Christ, and of the true <term>justification</term><note>The process by which a sinner is declared righteous before God.</note> of poor sinners in God's sight, were not manifested to the *Jews* before the justification in the blood of Christ was accomplished.

75. Therefore, those whom the Father had chosen as *instruments* for the process, way, and course of Christ were not meant to know beforehand what they were doing.

76. But after they had done it, God opened their *understanding* for their conversion. Therefore, Christ prayed to the righteousness of his Father (which would have devoured these murderous and bloody judges in its anger) that God's righteousness would forgive them through Christ's blood.

77. No one knew the Savior of the world correctly—no, not even the *Apostles themselves*—until the manifestation or revelation following his death.

78. And people should not say that God specifically hardened these men *for this purpose* so that they were unable to know Christ.

79. No: almost no one knew him rightly, nor what his <term>office</term><note>His specific divine role or duty as Savior.</note> was, until after he fulfilled that for which he had come.

80. Those men who sentenced and put Christ to death were serving in the <term>office of the Law</term><note>The legal and religious authority of the Old Covenant.</note> of God's righteousness. The *Law*—that is, God's righteousness—put Christ to death.

81. But *they supposed they were doing God a service in this* and were zealous in the Law of God's righteousness; they were also chosen to be instruments of that Law to fulfill it in Christ—acting, that is, as officers of the Law.

<summary>The author critiques superficial Christianity as being motivated by pride and power rather than Christ's suffering, and explains that those who executed Christ acted as blind instruments of God's Law to fulfill divine justice.</summary>

# A brief clearing of some Questions. Chapter 12.

<margin>* Later called Paul.
* Acts 22:3.</margin>
82. Just as *Saul* was, *so it was with others:* *he was zealous for the Law of God's Righteousness with true divine zeal, as the Law required, until the fulfillment of the Law took hold of him in the very heat of his purpose.* This showed him that this zeal for the Law was fulfilled with blood. From then on, he must no longer be zealous for the Law of the Father's Righteousness in the Fire <note>In Boehme's theology, the "Fire" often represents the Father's strict justice and the Old Testament Law</note>, but in the Law of *fulfillment in the love of* Christ.

83. For those who crucified Christ are not the greatest sinners; they had to do it *according to the official duty they held under the Law.*

84. Instead, the greatest sinners are those who, after the fulfillment of the Law, *despise and scorn* Christ, *put him to death in his members* <note>original: "Members"; referring to his followers or the Church as the "Body of Christ"</note>, *and lie dead in sins.* This is especially true after the grace of the Law's fulfillment was proclaimed to them through the power of the Spirit with wonders and miracles. Those who stop their ears and blaspheme it are blaspheming the Holy Spirit in the merits of Christ—in his glorious revelation and *the freely presented grace that was proclaimed to them.*

<margin>* Luke 23:34.</margin>
85. Therefore, we should look at the Scripture correctly and not speak of a particular, individual hardening of hearts; for Christ said, *“they know not what they do.”* No one knew who Christ was until his death, and then they knew him.

86. But based on Christ's words, it follows that some might say, *"I do this, and I do that, but I do not know what I do; God has so hardened me that I must do it. I must also steal, lie, extort, be greedy, and be angry to promote my own pride and status."* *Let such a person consider well what he is—whether he is not a child of the* Devil, *who has hardened him with such schemes and imaginations.*

87. If God had hardened him so that he was forced to do it, then the Law of God's Righteousness would be far from him, as would the teaching of the Gospel. For in that case, he would only be doing *what he should and must do, and inevitably could do nothing else.*

88. All of this runs counter and is contrary to the Law of the Father's Righteousness and is against the Law of the Son in the Gospel. No one can show how such a person can excuse himself with any plea when God's Truth casts him as a liar into Hell. *He is a child of the caught Anger of God* <note>original: "caught Anger"; meaning the person is ensnared or captured by divine wrath due to their nature</note>—*namely, born of the Father of Lies, as* Christ *says of* Satan.

### Further Objections of Reason.

<margin>* Luke 22:32.</margin>
89. ***CHRIST*** *prayed for* Peter *that his faith should not fail or cease; why did he not pray for others also, so that their faith would not fail? Therefore, there must be a predestined purpose,* says Reason.

### Answer.

90. As was mentioned above, Peter *and the other Apostles received the foundation of faith from* Christ's *voice* before the fulfillment of the Law; their faith still rested in the Law of the Father, *namely, in the Spirit of God's Righteousness.*

<margin>* John 14:16.</margin>
91. Therefore, Christ said to them *that he would send them another Comforter, namely the Spirit of Truth. This Spirit would receive faith from* Christ's *fulfillment and death, and from his resurrection and restoration. This same Spirit would remain with them, lead them into all truth, and receive what is Christ's to declare it within them.*

92. The first faith was given to them by the Father when he gave them to Christ to be his disciples; *within that faith still lay the Righteousness of God in the Anger.*

<margin>* Right, Dominion, Government, Might, and Authority.</margin>
93. *This faith* Satan *desired to sift and press through, to test whether it was the force that would take away his* <gloss>right, dominion, government, might, and authority</gloss> *over man and destroy Hell. Such faith, rooted in God's anger, could not yet withstand the true test of trial in the fire.*

## Chap. 12.

### A brief clearing of some Questions.

94. Therefore the Name **JESUS** prayed for them, so that this foundation—in which it would later perform **wonders** or **miracles** through the faith of love and *humility*—should not cease within them. Otherwise, those wonders and miracles would not have followed or been so powerful <note>original: "fiery"</note> over life and death—namely, over God’s justice <note>original: "Righteousness"</note>, which the love in the blood of Christ overcame.

95. But to *others* this faith was not yet given; for they were not yet Apostles, but had to wait for the promise, when the faith of grace was given to them.

96. And because of that faith of grace, Christ also prays for them, just as he did for *Peter*, so that their faith should not fail or cease. As it is written, *he sits at the right hand of God, making intercession for us*; and he prays to the justice of God without ceasing, with *ineffable sighs for us within ourselves*.

97. If we would only learn to see and understand the Scriptures and move away from useless babbling toward the foundation of the truth,

98. Then *no one* would say that Christ does not pray for all people as he prayed for *Peter*—that his faith might not fail or cease. For he, namely Christ, is the actual praying—the prayer itself within us.

99. Why then do we play games with such objections? We have cleared them at the request of friends and intend it faithfully.

100. When Christ said, *Father forgive them, they know not what they do*, he then prayed for all who *did not yet know him* and yet would learn to know him.

### Objection.

101. But it is objected that he allowed *Judas* to fall into despair.

### Answer.

<margin>* Psalm 41:9.</margin>
102. Consider what the Scripture says of *Judas*. Christ said, *I have lost none of them that you have given me, except for the lost child of destruction <note>original: "Perdition"</note>; so that the Scripture might be fulfilled which says, He that eats my bread, tramples me with his feet.*

103. Do you not see that Christ calls him the lost child of destruction? He was clearly a *thistle* <note>In the author's symbolic language, a "thistle" represents a person rooted in God's wrath or "anger" rather than His love.</note> before, which the anger of God’s justice had generated within itself as its own life.

104. Therefore, this *Judas* had to be called an apostle as a *symbol* <note>original: "Figure"</note> and as a betrayer of Christ, to signify what kind of people would be among Christ's teachers in the future. Namely, they would feed upon the bread and cup of Christ under a pretense of great holiness, yet would only betray and help to sentence Christ to death in his members <note>referring to the "Body of Christ," meaning his true followers and the church</note>.

105. For a long time, ministers of the *antichristian* churches in various sects have done so, and they do so to this day: they betray, defame, slander, and brand true Christians, and *help* to crucify and put Christ to death.

106. Therefore Christ said that the Scripture must be fulfilled in this way, which suggests concerning Christ that he would *continually* be so betrayed and put to death in his members; thus God’s justice might also be continually fulfilled *in Christ's members until the end of the world*.

107. Therefore these *Judases*, or brothers of *Judas*, must be instruments of God’s justice in his anger, and they must be numbered and counted among the apostles so that *men believe* them to be apostles.

108. They must have an apostolic calling from *men* and sit in Christ’s place and eat the bread of Christ, so that Christ—in his path <note>original: "Process"</note> and way of life within his members—should always be betrayed. This path and way of Christ will not cease until he comes again to bring home his bride <note>The Church</note>.

# A brief clarification of some Questions. Chapter 12.

<margin><sup>y</sup> 2 Cor. 2:15, 16.</margin>
109. For these "brothers" of Judas also serve God in His stern, severe righteousness, so that His righteousness may continually be fulfilled in the blood of Christ within His members. As it is written: *For the wicked are a sweet aroma of death to God, just as the holy are an aroma of life.*

<margin><sup>z</sup> Original text reads: "in."</margin>
110. Since God is both an angry and a loving God, the symbolic figure and Christ’s office must always stand near each other. One drives the other forward, and they are revealed through one another, to the praise of God’s glory at the day of His appearance.

111. But no one can truly claim that God, out of a specific will or predestined purpose, hardened Judas so that he was unable to convert.

112. No; rather, God’s righteousness acting through His anger had taken hold of him. it formed him into a thistle <note>original: "Thistle"; a metaphor for a prickly, spiritually unproductive person, often used by Böhme to describe those born into a state of "wrath."</note> even before he was an apostle—in his very seed, before his soul was even formed. This resulted from inherited, innate sin, which God punishes to the third and fourth generation.

113. Therefore, God’s righteousness uses Judas as a symbol, showing how a person is gripped by God’s justice leading to the damnation of death.

114. And just as this righteousness was meant to reveal Christ’s death—showing that He died to sin for the sake of the people to satisfy that righteousness—

115. —so God's anger places its own symbol in Judas alongside Christ’s work. This was done so people would know it was God’s will to overcome His anger in humanity. Yet, the anger's own will within God’s righteousness remains in itself as a *center* <note>original: "Center"; in Böhme’s philosophy, a "center" is a foundational point of manifestation or a core state of being.</note> for the manifestation of God, as previously explained regarding the *center*.

116. But if someone asks, "How can a child in the mother’s womb help the fact that it is a 'thistle'?"

117. The answer is that the fault lies in the *root* from which the thistle grows. As Christ says, *A corrupt tree cannot bring forth good fruit.*

118. God’s anger also takes on a created form; but this does not come from God’s predestined purpose. Instead, it comes from the wrath of Eternal Nature itself. This nature is not God but wrath—the cause of the fire from which light is revealed. If you cannot see this, may God help or advise you.

119. But if someone says that Judas was sorry for his misdeed and fault—

<margin>Note.</margin>
120. That is very true: the *Devil himself* is also sorry that he cannot be both a good angel and a *devil* at the same time. Because that is impossible, he despairs of God’s grace, and that despair is his eternal hell.

121. Similarly, Judas was sorry that he was cast out from God’s grace, but *he did not actually desire the grace itself*. The source of the desire for grace was not in him; he was not born out of faith—that is, out of the promised seed.

122. Although he came from the same nature where faith exists, and even had the indwelling Word in the depths <term>Abyss: the "Unground" or "Abyss" of the soul, referring to its deepest, most foundational essence.</term> of his soul, his soul clearly had the character or disposition of darkness. In the presence of grace, that darkness was dead and incapable of receiving life.

<margin><sup>a</sup> Matt. 26:26, 27, 28.</margin>
123. For even if a thistle is planted in honey, only a large, robust thistle will grow from it. Grace does not belong to such things. For Christ said to his disciples, <sup>a</sup> *Take and drink; this is my blood, which is shed for you and for many.*

124. The "tincture" <term>Tincture: a spiritual or medicinal essence that transforms or "colors" the soul.</term> was in the blood. The sun does not give its holy essence to the thistle, because the thistle has a nature that is hostile to that essence. The sun does provide the thistle with its being <term>Ens: being, essence, or the fundamental internal substance of a thing.</term> and substance, but the thistle is *not capable of receiving the jewel* <note>original: "Jewel"; here meaning the spiritual treasure of grace or the divine light.</note>. It only takes from the sun whatever serves its own nature. It should be understood the same way here.

<margin><sup>b</sup> 1 Cor. 11:29.</margin>
125. St. Paul says, <sup>b</sup> *Because they do not discern the Lord’s body, the wicked receive it to their own judgment,* just as the thistle receives the sun.

Böhme emphasizes that God's anger and love work in tandem to manifest His glory.</summary>

### Objection.

<margin>John 9:2–3.</margin>
126. Also, based on human reason, a further objection is raised concerning the blind man, specifically when the Disciples asked Christ, <gloss>Who sinned, this man or his parents?</gloss> <note>original: "Who hath sinned, this Man, or his Parents?"</note> To whom Christ gave this answer: *Neither his parents nor this man sinned; but it was so that the works of God might be manifested.*

### Answer.

<margin>Dominion, Government, Working, and Effects.</margin>
127. God has enclosed the <gloss>kingdom of this world</gloss> <note>original: "Kingdom of this World"</note> within time, number, or limits, and measure and weight. God’s works exist in a moving, active pattern; when that pattern is to be revealed and explained, then it exists within that through which it will be shown.
128. When Christ was to be *manifested* in this faithful man who was born blind—before Christ’s suffering and his fulfillment of the Law of Nature—the Law, viewed through the Eye of Nature, must *first* kill him <note>meaning to deprive him of natural sight</note> so that Christ may open the Eye of Faith for him. This Eye of Faith would afterwards also open the Eye of Nature through *Grace*. It was a *symbol* <note>original: "Figure"</note> showing how we, in *Adam*, were blind toward God, and how we, in Christ, should receive our sight again.
129. For the blindness of this man did *not* come from a special, particular, inherited, or innate sin, for he was a *Seed of Faith* <term>The innate spiritual potential for faith within an individual.</term>; in whom Christ was stirring as he took on humanity, and in whom the man also believed in him. But this inward seeing of faith through Christ was *not yet* sufficient; he first had to receive sight through a human voice.
<margin>Or Christ,</margin>
130. For when <gloss>JESUS</gloss> became man, then the human nature was brought into God's vision. But the Law of God still held this vision *captive* in the poor sinner, until our eyes saw the fulfillment of the Law through his death.
131. Therefore, because this man—possessing the Seed of Faith while in his mother's womb—was to receive sight through Christ’s entrance into and manifestation in *humanity*, Nature killed his sight. This was because he must not see through the light of nature using faith, for the righteousness of God within the Law of Nature was not yet satisfied or fulfilled.
132. *Therefore*, this man had to be born blind so that the divine eye in faith might give him sight through the "speaking-in" <term>The divine act of speaking the Word into the soul (German: *Einsprechen*).</term> of the holy name JESUS, so that the holiness of God might be manifested.
133. And people must not say that this man was born blind through a special, peculiar, or predestined purpose. Rather, he was one who sprang from the root of the Seed of Faith; it was this faith that the name JESUS (which is God’s light in love) was meant to bring into sight.
134. He was a part of the <gloss>clockwork</gloss> <note>original: "Clock-work or Motion-work"; a metaphor for the complex, mechanical-like orchestration of divine providence.</note> of *Christ*, having been given by God the Father to Christ for the journey and path he was to walk. Similarly, the Pharisees were part of the clockwork of the Law of God’s *Righteousness*, and they also played their part in the trial of Christ.

### Objection.

<margin>Matthew 24.</margin>
135. Also, that saying in Matthew 24:24 is brought up by human reason, by which you might try to maintain that God wills for man to be deceived, seduced, and damned. There, Christ says: <gloss>False Christs and false prophets shall arise; so that in their errors, if it were possible, the very elect might be deceived.</gloss>

## *Answer.*

136. This text says they shall arise, but it does not say that they are *sent* from God, much less *out of* Christ, to whom all power and authority was given in heaven and upon earth.

137. Therefore, these false prophets would arise out of the predestined purpose of *God’s anger*—specifically, out of the zeal for righteousness—and sift the hearts of those "verbal" Christians who call themselves Christians in name only.

138. Through this embittered spirit of God’s anger resulting from the process of Christ, these people would be sifted so that they would *believe lying spirits*. This happens because they call themselves Christians, yet Christ is *not* in them; instead, they are children of the anger <note>likely a reference to being "children of wrath" as described in Ephesians 2:3</note>.

139. Therefore, they would represent their image of abominations, false expositions, and schemes, so that the children of the *false name* of Christ—covered with the purple mantle of Christ <note>an allusion to the robe placed on Jesus during his passion, often used by this author to symbolize worldly power or mock piety</note>—might depend on and cling to them. This separates the true Christians from them, so that it might be known who truly belongs to Christ.

140. And so Christ might also be manifested through the *false prophets* of the "process of Christ" <note>original: "Process of Christ"; likely referring to the ongoing spiritual reenactment of Christ's suffering and crucifixion within the world</note> through their acts of betraying, killing, and causing him to suffer. In this way, Christ is continually put to death by the Pharisees and heathens for the sake of their false worship.

141. For God’s righteousness requires the Church of Christ to be established in blood, and it always provides a cause for this through false prophets and *false Christians*.

142. These false prophets, together with the heathens (namely, the tyrants), unceasingly put Christ to death within his members <note>referring to individual believers as part of the "Body of Christ"</note> and offer them up as a sacrifice to the righteousness of God. Through this, God’s *anger* is "killed" <note>meaning satisfied or neutralized</note> within the *true Christians*.

143. If people today want to *know* who those false prophets are, let them look at those who have scraped together *opinions* based solely on the *letter* <note>the literal text of scripture without spiritual insight</note>. They have compiled and published elegant and refined <term>postils</term> <note>original: "Postils"; books of sermons or commentaries on the Gospels and Epistles</note>—expositions full of scandalous libels and personal fancies, clever interpretations, and quibbles about God’s *anger*. Through these, one sect attacks another in the face and eyes and denounces them as *false*.

144. And yet those very accusers live in the same manner as those they criticize. They write only for their own honor, so that they might appear to be *highly* learned men whom the whole world should admire and view as representing Christ. However, they are merely titular, verbal, and *lip-Christians* <note>Christians in speech only</note> who lack grace.

145. Furthermore, they live entirely apart from the way and process of Christ, indulging in vain, fleshly lusts. Every day they devise more and more new orders, ceremonies, and *ways* of worship to create a glittering outward show. Consequently, people revere and honor them even more and endow them with riches to satisfy the appetite of their *Belly-God, <term>Mauzim</term>* <note>original: "Mauzim"; a reference to the "god of fortresses" in Daniel 11:38, used here to represent a god of worldly power and physical gluttony</note>.

146. These men do *not have Christ’s Spirit* in them, nor are they the apostles of Christ. Instead, every one of them is merely a *false prophet* who interprets the scriptures based on the *letter* alone, without spiritual knowledge or experience.

147. For they neither know nor *believe* what they say. They are the devouring wolves of whom Christ says that they do not have the knowledge of Christ *within them*, and yet they still *prophesy*.

148. But concerning those who are in Christ, he says that it is not *possible* for them to be deceived. These are the ones in whom *Christ has become man* <note>referring to the internal spiritual rebirth of Christ within the believer</note>. In their inward core, they exist in Christ, in heaven, and in God, and they hear Christ speaking within them. They listen only to God’s Word and not to the false prophets.

<margin>e Schaar.</margin>
149. If people today were to eject and cast out these false prophets from the various sects, then the <gloss>e</gloss> *apostolic* hierarchy <note>The marginal note "Schaar" is a German word for "host" or "multitude," suggesting the author is referring to the vast numbers of religious officials</note>—those who call themselves apostles—would soon become very small.

<sig>Pp 2</sig>

150. Therefore, people should not say at all that God permits false prophets to come *because* he will *not* offer salvation to those who might otherwise attain it. Human reason is mistaken in thinking that God has ordained one group for salvation and another for damnation, or that God wills it to be so and therefore <gloss>h</gloss> *sends them strong and powerful delusions, or errors, so that they might fall and he might show his anger upon them.*

151. Dear brothers and sisters who are overwhelmed with such notions <note>original: "conceits"</note>, we advise you not to learn such fictions. First, be fundamentally assured by Christ’s Spirit *within* you; otherwise, you will be seized by God’s righteousness along with the number of the false prophets.

<margin>i John 10:9.</margin>
152. If you do not have the door of Christ *open* in your soul so that you may <gloss>i</gloss> go in and out in the Spirit of Christ and find true, certain, and assured pasture for the sheep—so that you may feed them with Christ’s nourishment—then leave it alone.

<margin>k Victory based on human reason will not be enough.</margin>
153. Your *university* arts and sciences of the schools—where you strike, defeat, and flay one another with words of human reason, and afterward write and teach such <gloss>k</gloss> victories of reason as the *truth* of Christ—will not help you in the sight of God.

<margin>l John 10:8.</margin>
154. For Christ calls <gloss>l</gloss> *these people thieves and murderers who*—without his Spirit and the knowledge of him—creep and climb in through another door; namely, through the logical deductions of reason without the knowledge and will of Christ.

<margin>m Note: 1 Kings chapter 22.</margin>
155. If you are not armed with Christ’s Spirit, then do not enter into battle against such a potent and mighty enemy as the Devil. You shall not prevail against God’s righteousness in his anger using your logical conclusions without the blood of Christ within you. <gloss>m</gloss> Instead, you shall be imprisoned by God’s stern, severe righteousness within your own conclusions, and be chosen as false prophets in the anger of God.

<margin>n Within the created world.</margin>
156. For no one is a prophet unless he is generated within the great "clockwork" <note>The author uses the metaphor of a clockwork to describe the complex, mechanical, and predestined timing of God's plan for creation.</note> of the divine ordinance, in the <gloss>n</gloss> outspoken or *expressed* Word, at the specific point in time <note>original: "Limit"</note> ordained by God’s righteousness, where the *Holy Spirit* speaks through that moment in the divine order.

<margin>o Ephesians 1:4; 1 Peter 1:20.</margin>
157. He must be a *point of transition* <note>original: "Limit"</note> *in the clockwork of the Great Mystery* <note>original: "Mysterio magno"</note>, through whom the Spirit of God points to another period of manifestation. Such were the prophets of old, and such are they today who stand at the transition point of the great clockwork, in the foresight of grace in Christ Jesus, in which <gloss>o</gloss> *God has foreseen—that is, seen—us in Christ Jesus before the foundation of the world.*

158. He must stand in God’s righteousness with his prophetic spirit, and even at the transition point where God has viewed the name of his *love* within that righteousness. This is so he may be generated out of the ground of the law—from the righteousness of God’s predestined, purposed grace—so that he may teach the law (God’s righteousness) and also the Gospel (God’s love and the fulfilling of the law).

159. Such a person is a true prophet and *no other*, for he is a transition point <note>original: "Limit or Period"</note> of a kingdom or government within the *Great Mystery* <note>original: "Mysterio magno"</note>. It is by and from this mystery that the order and course of earthly kingdoms and governments have arisen; he is the voice of that kingdom.

160. But since he must teach how God’s righteousness in his anger is to be overcome <note>original: "killed"</note> by grace, and that grace must first completely surrender itself to that anger to be struck down by righteousness, he is also offered as a sacrifice in the process of Christ. He is subjected to that same righteousness of God by the false prophets and Pharisees.

161. For it must be that his specific time <note>original: "Limit or Number"</note> in the blood of Christ may be brought entirely through the anger, and that the boundary of righteousness within grace may be established. Therefore, <gloss>p</gloss> the prophets of Christ must be martyrs.

# A brief clearing of some Questions. Chap. 12.

<margin>Those who are like this will understand this author and praise God for his revelation. <note>original: Manifestation</note></margin>
162. **q** Mark this well, all of you who wish to teach and *suppose* you are called to it; look well to the calling *within* you, whether you are also called by God in Christ—whether Christ has called you with his voice within you.

163. If not, then you are nothing other than *false prophets* who run without being sent and do not enter into the sheepfold through the door of Christ.

164. Though you steer your course by a *human call*, which has value before men, and God is pleased to *permit* what men do when it is done in his order or according to his ordinance, you must still surrender yourselves from man's call *into* God's call. Consider also how you will be capable of the *divine* calling within your human calling.

165. Where that is not done, and you insist only upon your *human* calling in your own self-will, then you sit upon the stool or chair of pestilence and are Pharisees and *false prophets*.

166. And even if there were many hundreds of thousands of you, the *office* itself does not make you prophets and shepherds of Christ unless you enter through Christ’s living door.

<margin>Note.</margin>
167. Although it is plain that the Pharisees will *not like* <note>original: relish</note> this, the time has come, and the limit is at hand when it shall be revealed. Therefore, no human subtlety or craftiness will be of any use anymore. Woe to those people who *despise* this; they will be devoured in God’s righteousness, zeal, and jealousy.

### Objection.

<margin>r Jonah 1.</margin>
168. Furthermore, Reason also brings up the case of the prophet *Jonah* as a demonstration or proof that God *compels* and constrains men toward both evil and good—namely, toward his predestined purpose—just as **r** *he compelled Jonah to go to Nineveh*.

### Answer.

169. Listen, Reason, and do not be mistaken; God’s Spirit does not allow itself to be judged by *reason*. *Jonah* was born a prophet within the bounds of the Covenant and served as a *symbol* <note>original: Figure</note> <margin>s Jonah 1:17.</margin> of Christ, signifying how Christ would be cast into the anger of God, **s** *into the jaws* <margin>t Jonah 1:15.</margin> *of the great whale* of divine righteousness to fulfill it, and how he would go **t** *into the sea of death*.

170. And just as the anger of God, which he overcame in that same whale of death, <margin>u Jonah 2:10.</margin> allowed him to go forth from it unhurt and alive, so did *Jonah* when he was **u** *cast out of the whale’s belly*.

171. He was a symbol of Christ, born or generated from the boundaries of the great <term>clockwork</term> <note>original: "Clock-work"; likely referring to the mechanical or systematic unfolding of the universe</note>, <term>from the great mystery</term> <note>original Latin: "ex Mysterio magno"</note>, out of both the predestined purposes of God—namely, out of his grace and out of his righteousness. He was presented as a symbol for a theatrical scene of the Spirit of God, in which the Spirit saw and pointed toward Christ through this figure.

<margin>x Jonah 1:3.</margin>
172. This signifies how the humanity of Christ—that is, our human nature which he took on—would **x** *be afraid or astonished at Nineveh*, meaning the danger to his life.

173. Just as when the time came for Christ to enter into "Nineveh"—that is, into <margin>y Matthew 26:39.</margin> God’s anger—he said, **y** "*Father, if it be possible, let this cup pass from me.*" He also frequently hid himself from the Pharisees (the Ninevites of his time), just as *Jonah* hid from the Ninevites.

174. This symbol also signifies that when we poor *Jonahs* <note>original: "Jonabes", a plural form of Jonah</note> ought to warn people of God's punishment and judgments and *risk* our lives among them for the sake of the truth, we instead seek excuses. We give ourselves up to the sea of the world, seeking easy and pleasurable days, fleeing from God's command and remaining silent for fear of the *Ninevites*. Then the whale of God's anger comes and swallows the prophets.

<summary>The author distinguishes between a purely human appointment to the ministry and a true divine calling, warning that those without the latter are false prophets. The story of Jonah is reinterpreted as a symbolic prefiguration of Christ's sacrifice and a warning against avoiding spiritual duty for the sake of worldly comfort.</summary>
<keywords>divine calling, false prophets, Pharisees, Jonah, Nineveh, Christology, predestination, spiritual symbolism, spiritual cowardice</keywords>

--- Page 482 ---
<meta>This page continues the discussion on the biblical figure of Jonah as a symbol of Christ and begins a summary conclusion regarding the nature of predestination and God's grace.</meta>

<page-num>293</page-num>
<header>Chap. 13. A Close to all these Questions.</header>

175. But the fact that *Jonah* was driven out from there with *Power* signifies that the predestined purpose of God the Father in Christ should and must stand. Even though *Adam* departed from obedience to God into <term>Imagibility</term> <note>original: "Imagibility"; the state of being caught up in worldly images, mental fantasies, or sensory desires rather than divine reality</note>—the imaginations or desires of this world, by which humanity was given up to the great whale of **Death**—yet God's predestined purpose shall stand, and *Adam* shall arise in Christ out of the belly of Death.

176. Dear brethren, *this* is the symbolic figure of *Jonah*, and *not* your "predestined purpose" or a compulsion toward evil and good; it is the figure of Christ.

177. Abandon such conclusions, and do not blaspheme the Holy Spirit in his wonders within the figure of Christ by teaching perverse opinions and interpretations. Otherwise, through your own conclusions, you shall be cast into the sea of God's anger. We must and will warn you in love, in a brotherly manner.

---

# The Thirteenth Chapter.

## A summary Close to all these Questions.

### Objection.

<margin>1.</margin>
<margin>* John 17:6.</margin>
<image-desc>Decorative woodcut initial letter R, ornate with floral scrollwork and enclosed in a square frame bordered by stars.</image-desc>
**R**EASON lastly brings in the speech of Christ, where he says: *Father, I have revealed or manifested your Name to the men whom you have given me out of the world.*

2. By this, they try to prove that Christ reveals or manifests his Name to *no one* unless the Father gives them to him beforehand out of his predestined purpose—*whether they will or not*.

### Answer.

<margin>* <term>Science</term>, Root, or Ground.</margin> <note>original: "Science"; here used in the archaic sense of an internal knowledge or the fundamental essence/root of the soul's will</note>
3. Oh, you most miserably blind Reason! Why are you so blind? Do you not know what the "Father's giving" is? It is the **center of the soul**—namely, the Father's will in the <term>science</term> of eternal righteousness.

4. Within that state, the <term>science</term> is weighted or swayed either by the desire for abominations or by the divine love of grace. The speaking Word in God's righteousness gives itself into that state, whether it be into the root of a thistle or into the root of the **seed of faith**.

5. To the root in the seed of **faith**, Christ becomes manifest; for it is Christ's own root, out of which a Christian is generated in Christ.

6. To these Christian men, Christ has continually manifested himself from the beginning of the world and given them the Name of God; for he *himself* is the **Name of God**.

7. This text is not to be understood as if God had made a conclusion or determination before the beginning of the world, setting that determination in a fixed course, ordinance, or compulsory destiny regarding how many *and whom* he would bestow himself upon. Captivated Reason understands it this way—as if people cannot fail or avoid it, or go one step outside of it.

8. No, no: The tree of Christ is immeasurable; God's grace, and also his righteousness in the fire, are both immeasurable.

<sig>4</sig>

<summary>The author argues that Jonah's story symbolizes humanity's resurrection through Christ rather than a fixed destiny of individual salvation or damnation. He critiques the idea of "compulsory destiny," suggesting instead that Christ manifests to anyone whose internal "root" or will is directed toward faith.</summary>
<keywords>Jonah, Adam, Christ, predestination, free will, Imagibility, Seed of Faith, Name of God, divine grace, eternal righteousness</keywords>

--- Page 483 ---
<meta>This page concludes the author's exploration of divine love, anger, and the nature of the soul's conversion, continuing the themes of spiritual "science" (inner consciousness) and the "Abyss" from previous chapters.</meta>

# A Conclusion to all these Questions. Chapter 13.

9. For had God set a limit or boundary on *Love* and *Anger*, then they would have been measurable and would have had a *Beginning*; and then people would also think they must have an *End*.

10. No, no: The Tree of Knowledge of Good and Evil stands in the *Eternal Foundation* <note>original: "Ground"</note>, where there is no time nor limit.

11. God’s grace in Christ is immeasurable and exists from eternity.

12. And so it is also with the Kingdom of Nature in the *Great Mystery* <note>original: "Mysterio magno"</note>—the vast hidden source from which the fiery consciousness <note>original: "Science," meaning the active root of will or knowledge</note> has revealed itself out of the will of the *Abyss* <note>original: "Abyss," referring to the bottomless void or the ungrounded source of all being</note>.

13. And just as Christ has revealed God’s name to humanity—specifically to the root of the seed of *faith*—from the *beginning* of the world, so He continues to do until the end of it.

<margin>b Matt. 24:27.</margin>
14. For ^b *He also said this to His disciples when they asked Him about the end of the world; He answered: "For as the lightning comes from the east and flashes to the west, so will be the coming of the Son of Man."*

<margin>c John 8:12.</margin>
15. And as the sun gives itself to everything all day long, shining upon and penetrating into every thing—whether it be evil or good—so also does the Divine Sun, Christ, who is ^c *the true light of the world.*

16. Christ does not withdraw His light of grace from anyone; He calls them all and cries out with His voice within them, with no one excepted.

<margin>d John 8:47.</margin>
17. But ^d *not everyone hears or sees Him, because they are not of God.*

18. The consciousness <note>original: "Science"</note> of the bottomless will of the Father has, in the foolish creature, entered into strange mental images or *dispositions* <note>original: "Imagibility," the capacity to form internal images or desires</note>, becoming like the "thistle of the serpent" <note>representing a prickly, sinful nature</note>. This nature neither sees nor hears; for God’s righteousness speaks within it, saying, *“Do what is right, or I will destroy you; this is sin, and that is sin; do not do it, or else you will be cast out from God.”*

19. When the soul hears this warning within itself, the Devil arrives with his "serpentine image" or *disposition*. He says to the inner consciousness, *“Stay a while longer in the flesh—indulge in this or that desire,”* such as greed, pride, envy, anger, lust, pleasure, luxury, drunkenness, or mockery. He tells the soul, *“There is still plenty of time for you to repent at the end of your life.”*

20. "First of all, gather great *wealth* <note>original: "Treasure"</note> so that you no longer need anything from the world. Then you can begin an honest, virtuous, and good life. You can *live independently* without being mocked by the world, needing nothing it possesses."

21. In this way, one day and year after another are *postponed* until the very hour of death. Then, the person expects to be a child of grace and to be saved, blessed, and happy, even though they have remained stuck in the nature of the "Serpent" for their *entire* life.

22. At that point, the priest arrives with the "Body of God" <note>the Eucharist or Host</note> in his hand, intending to bring about the "Angelical New Birth." However, many a priest *does not possess this birth himself*; he is a stranger to that spiritual reality, or merely a guest in that place.

23. These people, while they remain stuck in the nature of the "Serpent," are *not* given to Christ, but belong instead to the Anger of God.

24. God’s Anger will not release them unless the consciousness of the soul converts and turns itself toward the grace that resides within it.

25. And if that is done, then *that* is the act of being "given" to Christ.

26. For the *Divine Sun* immediately shines into the consciousness that has become still, and sets it ablaze.

27. And this "kindling" is the *Name of God* which Christ gives to the soul. From this, the soul begins to form or create itself anew, to act and grow in Christ, and to work through *repentance* toward forgiveness—that is, when it begins to stop imagining or planning falsehood and wickedness.

<summary>This page argues that God's grace and the "Divine Sun" of Christ are eternally available to all, but the soul is often distracted by worldly desires and the "serpent's" influence, delaying repentance until death. True salvation occurs when the soul's inner consciousness turns away from sinful imagery and is "kindled" by the light of Christ.</summary>
<keywords>Jacob Böhme, Grace, Repentance, The Serpent, Divine Sun, Mysterio Magno, Science (Consciousness), Abyss, Salvation, Ethics</keywords>

<meta>This page continues the concluding thoughts of Chapter 13 from Jacob Boehme's work, focusing on the internal nature of repentance and the presence of Christ within the soul as the only true source of forgiveness.</meta>

## Chap. 13.
# A Conclusion to all these Questions.

28. For people say, *“Never to do or commit evil is the best and greatest repentance.”* This occurs when the ground <note>The "ground" refers to the deepest, most fundamental level of the soul.</note> of the soul begins to be still and quiet from the imagining, framing, or picturing of *evil*, and enters into its *Abyss* <note>original: "Abyss," referring here to the divine nothingness or the infinite foundation of God where the soul finds rest.</note>.

29. The soul has the power and strength to do this *unless* it is a mere thistle <note>Meaning a soul that has become entirely prickly, stubborn, and unproductive of good.</note>; and then it runs on, works, and grows until the *end* of its *time*.

30. Yet there is *outwardly* no sentence of judgment upon it, but only its own judgment *within it*, all the while it is in this life, until the *time* of the *harvest* <note>The "harvest" refers to the end of life or the final judgment.</note>.

31. But it is *hard* for the soul if the inward and outward ground of the outward constellation or configuration of the stars <note>Boehme often refers to "constellations" to describe the astrological and natural influences that shape a person's temperament and worldly inclinations.</note> be *evil* or *false*. Such people commonly continue that way until the end.

32. Then comes only *Judas's* repentance <note>A reference to the despairing, too-late regret of Judas Iscariot.</note>; and then the tickling and comforting with the sufferings of Christ avails little, when there is no *Ens* <note>original: "Ens," a philosophical term meaning the essential being, substance, or "seed" of something.</note> of faith left.

33. The *pomp* of the glorious funeral and burial of the *dead beast* <note>Referring to the physical body of a person who lived without spiritual life.</note> is only the scorn of the devil, with which he mocks it.

34. For imputed grace <note>Grace that is "credited" to someone from the outside without changing their inner nature.</note> from the outside avails nothing—the idea that we should be absolved and pronounced free just by speaking outward words of grace, as a lord or prince freely grants a murderer his life out of grace.

35. No, no; the imputed grace of Christ must be *manifested in us* in the inward ground of the soul, and be our *life*.

36. People should *not* defer repentance until the end; for an old tree takes root very poorly.

37. If *Christ is not* in the soul, there is no grace nor forgiveness of sins in it then.

38. For Christ himself is the forgiveness of sins; he, with his *blood*, transforms the introduced abominations of God's anger in the soul and changes them into the *Divine Fire*.

<margin>e Mark 2:5. f Or paralysis.</margin>
39. As he said <gloss>e</gloss> before the *Pharisees* to the man sick with the <gloss>f</gloss> palsy <note>original: "Palsy," an archaic term for paralysis or tremors.</note>, *"Your sins are forgiven you."* That was done when the man laid hold of the voice of Christ *in his soul*; then the *living Word* in him forgave him his sins.

40. That is, *it* overcame the sins and crushed or trod upon the head of the *will* of the serpent's introduced abominations <note>An allusion to Genesis 3:15, where the seed of the woman bruises the serpent's head.</note> with the fire of love.

41. Therefore, now no one can forgive sins but *Christ in man*. Where *Christ in man* lives, *there is absolution* <note>The formal release from guilt or sin.</note>.

<margin>g John 20:22, 23.</margin>
42. For when Christ says, <gloss>g</gloss> *"Receive the Holy Spirit; whose sins you remit or release, to them they are released; and whose sins you retain or reserve, to them they are reserved,"* this concerns the *true Apostles* and their right followers or successors who have received the Holy Spirit out of Christ, who themselves are, and *live in Christ*, and have Christ's voice in them.

43. These have the might and *power* to speak into the hungry soul the *living Word* of Christ that dwells in them; and no one else has that power.

44. Let them make whatever high pretense and show they want, and be called whatever they want, yet they must be the very *Apostles* of Christ if they wish to administer and manage his office; otherwise, they are but *Pharisees* and wolves.

45. Also, the *soul* must open its mouth to the inward speaking <note>original: "inspeaking," the internal communication of God's Word to the spirit.</note>, otherwise the Word does not enter into it.

<margin>h Matthew 5:6.</margin>
46. Indeed, it did not enter into everyone when Christ *himself* preached and taught, but only into the hungry and thirsty souls, concerning whom Christ says, <gloss>h</gloss> *"Blessed are they that hunger and thirst after righteousness, for they shall be satisfied"*—understand this as being filled with the fullness of his Word.

47. For the forgiveness of sins lies not in *man*, but in the power of Christ's Word, which dwells in man.

<image-desc>A small decorative flourish or manicule in ink at the bottom right corner of the page, following the final paragraph.</image-desc>

<summary>Boehme concludes that true repentance is an internal transformation where the soul finds rest in God's "Abyss." He argues that forgiveness is not an external legal decree but the living presence of Christ within the soul, which overcomes sin through love.</summary>
<keywords>Jacob Boehme, repentance, Abyss, Ens, Christ in man, absolution, Holy Spirit, imputed grace, spiritual transformation, Pharisees</keywords>
