<page-num>296</page-num>
<header>A brief clearing of some Questions. Chapter 13.</header>

**48. A human's speaking does not forgive sins; rather, it is God speaking through a human's words.**

**49. However, this does not enter into a false or wicked heart <note>original: "Thistle"</note>, but into the soul, where the seed of faith lies within the sound of spiritual movement. This happens when the soul stops imagining or creating the desires of the "Serpent" <note>original: "Serpent's Desire," referring to the ego or worldly temptation</note>.**

**50. Therefore, do not rely on humans; they cannot forgive your sins or grant you grace unless you hunger and thirst for righteousness yourself.**

**51. To put off repentance until the end of life is like the repentance of Judas <note>meaning a despairing or late regret that lacks true spiritual transformation</note>; no comfort is effective unless you are regenerated or born again.**

->Thus,<-

**52. Dear brothers, I have wanted to answer the previously mentioned points raised in objections from their foundation. My firm meaning and sense is that the texts of Scripture are entirely true; however, human reason <note>original: "Self-Reason," or intellect independent of divine guidance</note> errs and cannot understand them without Christ.**

<margin>i Romans 8:15</margin>
**53. The Apostle says:** i *We have not received a servile, slavish spirit that should make us fear again, but a child-like spirit which cries out "Abba, Dear Father."*

<margin>* Romans 8:2</margin>
**54. It is not the mind or perception of the world or the flesh that we have received through promised grace, but the child-like mind of Christ,** \* *who has made us free from the law of sin.*

<margin>l Romans 15:5; m Philippians 2:5</margin>
**55.** l *So everyone should have the same mind as Jesus Christ, the only man truly in grace, as the Apostle says; and* m *whoever does not have Christ's mind or perception does not understand the things of the Spirit. To such a person, spiritual things are foolishness, and they cannot grasp them.*

<margin>Note to readers of these writings.</margin>
**56. In this very direct explanation, we might seem silent or confusing to many, and even a "stumbling block" to those who claim we use strange, crude, and unusual language in our foundational teachings. Yet we declare with truth before God that we share these things only as they are given to us through the mind and perception of Christ.**

<margin>Note to those who despise mysteries.</margin>
**57. Those who belong to Christ will understand this well. As for others—the mockers and "wise-acres" <note>original: "Wiselings," those who think themselves wise through human intellect alone</note> who take human reason as their master—we have not written for them.**

**58. But we advise our dear brothers in Christ to read this treatise through with patience; for its name is: *The longer it is read, the better it is liked; the more it is sought, the more is found.***

**59. Since Christ himself has told us to seek, knock, and pray, and has promised that we shall receive and find, we should not: 1. Be willing to remain stagnant in sin; 2. Wait for the grace of God to fall upon us and force us to change; or 3. Think that God's Spirit will turn an evil thing into a good thing without transformation.**

**60. But for the poor sinner who has not yet become completely hardened like a thorn-bush <note>original: "Thistle"</note>, God often comes upon them in their sin and draws them away from it.**

<margin>n Luke 12:10</margin>
**61. If the sinner yields and allows himself to be drawn, then it is well. But if he refuses entirely, returning to the way of the "Serpent" and crucifying Christ anew,** n *such a person blasphemes the Holy Spirit. Concerning this, the Scripture says there is no eternal forgiveness.*

**62. No one—not even the most wicked person—should dare to say that they are never, not even in their thoughts, drawn toward God.**

**63. Christ appears to all people: to some in his revealed name <note>the specific name of Jesus</note>, and to others simply as the name of the one and only God.**

**64. He draws everyone to himself. This drawing is indicated by the knowledge written in their hearts—the inner sense that there is a God whom they ought to honor. If they do not do so, they will be judged.**

<margin>o Romans 1:18; p Romans 1:25</margin>
**65. How much more serious is it for us, then? We call ourselves Christians and have the true knowledge, yet we** o *withhold the truth* p *and turn it into lies for the sake of a manufactured opinion—one we have imagined, declared to the world, and used to make ourselves famous.*

<summary>The author explains that true repentance and the forgiveness of sins come from a spiritual transformation and the "mind of Christ" rather than human reason or the words of men alone. He emphasizes that God draws all people toward Himself through an inner conscience, and warns against those who prioritize their own intellectual opinions over spiritual truth.</summary>
<keywords>repentance, seed of faith, mind of Christ, self-reason, Holy Spirit, universal drawing, judgment, hypocrisy</keywords>

--- Page 486 ---
<meta>Boehme continues his discussion on the nature of spiritual unity and the dangers of intellectual pride, concluding this chapter with a call for brotherly love and a warning against sectarian conflict.</meta>

<page-num>297</page-num>
<header>Chap. 12. A brief clearing of some Questions.</header>

## A brief clearing of some Questions.

66. And though we are afterwards brought to the Light, yet we ascribe the honor to *ourselves* more than to God; we try to hide, cover, *obscure*, and defile the Light with strange explanations, so that human inventions and fictions might *sit in Christ’s place* like an idol.

67. This often happens, and *Babel* <note>original: "Babel"; referring to the biblical Tower of Babel, symbolizing religious confusion and sectarian discord</note> is built *entirely* upon it, so that many will not allow their own declared opinions to be questioned, but instead twist all of Scripture <note>original: "withdraw the whole Scripture by the Hair"; a metaphor for forcing a text to fit one's own agenda</note> to make their views stand.

68. Dear sirs and brothers, let us give the honor to Christ and be kind to one another in a friendly manner. Let us meet and present one another with modest, gentle, and meek instructions: let each person present their gifts with a brotherly mind and good will, and lay *them* before one another.

69. For there are many sorts of knowledge and interpretations; if they now proceed from *Christ’s* own sense and mind, then they all stand upon one and the same ground and foundation.

70. We should not persecute one another because our different gifts are *unlike*; but we should rather rejoice in love with one another, because God’s wisdom is so *inexhaustible* that it can never be drained dry.

71. And think upon the future, how well it will be with us when all this different knowledge will be manifested from one and in one soul, so that we shall *all* acknowledge God’s gifts and have our joy in one another, and everyone will rejoice in the gifts of another.

72. Like the fair, beautiful, and pleasant flowers in their different colors and virtues that rejoice near one another upon the Earth in one and the same Mother; so also is our *resurrection* and coming again.

<margin>Colossians 2:3.</margin>
73. Why then should we dispute, contend, and wrangle here about the knowledge of these gifts? ¶ *In Christ lie all the treasures of wisdom*.

74. If we have *that*, we have everything; but if we lose *that*, we lose all, including ourselves.

<margin>
Ephesians 6:24.
John 14:13.
</margin>
75. The only true ground of our religion is *that we love Christ within us*; and also *love one another, just as Christ has loved us, so that he has given up his life to death for us*.

<margin>
John 15:12, 17.
Ephesians 5:2.
</margin>
76. This love will not be manifested in us unless Christ becomes Man and is born and manifested within us; he *then* gives us his love, so that we love one another in him, just as he loves us.

<margin>Galatians 2:20.</margin>
77. For he continually gives his flesh and blood to our souls to be eaten and drunk by them; and that soul which does not eat and drink of it has no divine life in it.

78. Therefore I advise the loving reader that if anything in this treatise seems to be of too *difficult or intense a meaning*, he should give God the honor, pray, and read it rightly.

79. In *Man* lies *everything* that the sun shines upon or heaven contains, as well as hell and all the deeps; he is an inexhaustible fountain that cannot be drained dry.

80. In a little while, he may very well and thoroughly grasp and comprehend this deep foundational truth which God has given to us—*that is*, to an *ordinary* man <note>original: "simple man"; meaning a person without formal theological training or of humble status</note>.

81. Only we would have him warned against despising and mocking, as he loves his own soul and eternity; for in doing so, he will not touch us, but rather the wrath of God within himself.

82. But as for me, who have worked on this as an *instrument*, he may well touch and hurt me; for regardless of his actions, I am in the bonds of *Christ*.

83. But I would have him lovingly encouraged to behave as a brother in *Christ*; and if he can provide any clearer explanation of it through his own divine gifts:

84. If I am able to see it, I will rejoice in his gifts and thank the Most High, who gives us so richly all sorts and manners of gifts among one another. *Amen*.

Dated the 8th of February, 1623.

2. The Scripture calls him the ª *Image of God*, the ᵇ *Temple of the Holy Spirit*, who dwells in him, and a *Member of Christ*, and offers the *Flesh* and *Blood of Christ* to him to be his <note>original: "Meat and Drink"</note> food and drink.
He should therefore well consider with himself, whether he is indeed possessed of as great a measure of *grace* as is implied in these names, and if he is really worthy of the *high title* of a *Christian*. He should examine his whole life—what he has done, and how he has spent his past time. He should see whether he finds himself to be in Christ, or moved by a *godly will* and *holy desires*. He should ask to what he is *chiefly* inclined; whether he feels at any time in himself a *will* or *desire* heartily *panting* after God, and longing to be saved by him.

3. Now, if on this examination he finds in himself a *will*, though it be ever so *weak* and *deeply hidden*, which would gladly turn to the *grace of God* if it could, let him know that this will is the <term>ingrafted, incorporated, and in-spoken Word</term> of God. This was "in-spoken" into our first father *Adam* in Paradise after sin was committed; and God the Father, **JEHOVAH**, draws him toward Christ by it.

4. For in *self* <note>In the author's theology, "Self" refers to the ego or the fallen nature apart from God.</note> we have no will at all toward obedience. Instead, *that drawing of the Father*—namely, the ingrafted, incorporated, in-spoken Word of grace—draws everyone, even the most ungodly, provided he is not altogether a <term>Thistle</term> and will only stand still from his evil-working for a moment.

<margin>
ᵉ Psalm 95:7.
Hebrews 3:7.
</margin>
5. So no man has cause to doubt the grace of God if at any time he finds in himself a *desire* or *inclination* to *turn*. Only let him not delay his *turning* for one moment, but set about it instantly, remembering what is written: ᵉ *Today when you hear the voice of the Lord, do not harden your ears and hearts.*

6. For that *desire* or *inclination* to *turn* even once is the *voice of God* in man. The **Devil** smothers and suppresses this through the representations or *images* <note>original: "Images"; likely referring to worldly distractions or mental idols.</note> which he brings into the mind. By these, turning is delayed and put off from one day to another, and from one year to another, until at length the soul becomes a mere *thistle* <note>A soul so hardened and prickly that it cannot receive the seed of grace.</note> and can no longer reach grace.

7. But let him who finds a *desire to turn <note>original: "turn"; meaning to repent or undergo a spiritual conversion</note>, deliberate well with himself, and then resolve to examine his whole course of life, and compare it with the rule of the Ten Commandments and the love required by the Gospel, which commands him to love his neighbor as himself.* ... Let him consider that he is a child of *Grace only* so far as he is in that *spirit of Christian love;* and then see how widely he has departed from it in his *daily thoughts and inclinations.* That drawing of the *Father* <note>original: "drawing of the Father"; the internal divine influence that attracts a soul toward God</note> will bring him to a sight of the *pure and lovely righteousness of God* on the one hand, and will reveal to him on the other the *images or properties* <note>original: "properties"; here meaning the inherent qualities or character traits of the soul</note> that are naturally imprinted in his own heart, which he has all his *life loved instead of God, and still accounts his best treasure.*

8. These *properties* he shall find to be: 1. *Pride*, in seeking and loving *himself*, and desiring also to be *honored* by all others; a *property* inclining him to seek *power and dominion* in his *pride*, and to have the *preeminence*. 2. The *property of a swine, covetousness*, which *would have everything for itself alone*; even if it had the *whole world and heaven* too, it would still want to have *dominion in hell* as well. It desires more than this temporal life needs and has no *faith* toward God at all, but is a defiled *swine* that would gladly *swallow everything into its own belly.* 3. The *property of envy, stinging the hearts of others, envying and grudging* that anyone should have more temporal *goods or honor* than *itself* has. 4. The *property of anger*, which, when *envy* (like a poisonous *sting*) irritates and inflames it, will upon every small, frivolous occasion *storm, fight, wrangle, rage*, and seek to vent itself in *revenge*. Also, there will be found, descended from these, a great multitude and variety of *earthly beasts* living in him, which he loves and *fosters*; for he loves everything that is in the *world*, has set it in the place of *Christ*, and worships it more *heartily and truly than he worships God.*

9. Let him only observe the *words* of his mouth, and he will soon find how he *slanders and speaks evil of others secretly, and represents them in the worst light to their friends and acquaintances.* Let him only observe his *thoughts*, and he will perceive how, without any just ground or cause, he inwardly rejoices at his neighbor’s *misfortune*, and even *wishes it upon them*; all of which are the very *claws and talons of the Devil, and the image of the Serpent, which every natural man carries about him.*

10. Then let him compare this *hellish state of his heart and life with the Word in the Law and in the Gospel, and he shall find that he is more a beast and a devil than a man.* He shall clearly perceive how these innate evil *properties* rooted in his soul keep him back and lead him astray from the *Kingdom of God*; so that many times when he would gladly repent and turn to God, he is held back by these *cloven paws* of the Devil, who persuades the poor soul that this *infernal monster* which it has become may justly pass for a *good and holy creature.* And thus blindly going on day after day in his evil nature and lusts, the wretched sinner sticks fast in the *anger of God*, and at length, when the *grace and drawing of the Father ceases, falls into the abyss or bottomless pit.*

## The Key to Divine Mysteries.

12. ...abominable **Beasts** <note>original: "minable Beasts"; the "a-" likely appeared at the end of the previous page</note> which live in him, let him think no otherwise of himself than that he is that filthy **Keeper of Swine** <note>A reference to the Parable of the Prodigal Son (Luke 15)</note> who has spent the entire **Portion of Goods** which his **Father** bestowed upon him as his **Birthright** upon those **Swine**, the **evil Beasts in himself**. Thus he now stands in the presence of God as a miserable, naked, lost, and ragged **swineherd** who has spent and cast away his paternal **inheritance** in **prostitution** <note>original: "Whoredom"; here meaning spiritual infidelity or the pursuit of worldly lusts</note> with these beastly **images**, and has no more **right** to the **grace** of God; neither is he in the least measure worthy of it, much less to be called a Christian or the child of God. He must also **despair** of all the good **works** that he ever did, for they proceeded only from a hypocritical, false, or merely **external holiness**, for which the man who is inwardly a devil would gladly be considered an angel; whereas *without faith it is impossible to please God*, as the **Scripture** says.

13. Yet let him not **despair** of **divine grace**, but of **himself** only and of his **own abilities**. Let him, with his whole **strength** and with all his **powers**, bow himself down in his soul in the presence of God. And though his own heart be utterly against it and say to him, "*Do it not, wait a while, it will not be convenient today*," or if it says, "*Your sins are too great, it cannot be that you should attain the grace of God*"—so that he falls into such **anguish** that he cannot pray nor receive any comfort or **strength** in his heart, but feels as if his soul were quite blind and dead to God—yet he must remain resolute. He must consider that the **promise** of God is a **certain, infallible truth**. With a submissive heart, he must sigh for divine mercy and, in his great **unworthiness**, wholly resign himself to it.

14. And though he indeed considers himself quite **unworthy**, as being a **stranger** and an **alien** to whom the **inheritance** of Christ no longer belongs—having forfeited and lost his **right** to it—yet he should steadfastly **rest** upon Christ’s word, knowing it to be certainly true: namely, *that he came to seek and save that which was lost*. That is to say, he came for the **poor sinner** who is **blind, dead, and lost to God**. He must firmly imprint **this promise** within himself and take up a strong **purpose** and **resolution** that he will not turn away from the promised **grace** of God in Christ, even if body and soul should **perish**, and even if he should get no **comfort** in his heart all the days of his life, nor the least **assurance** of the **remission of his sins**. He must consider and know that the **promises of God** are more **sure and firm than any comfort** whatsoever.

15. Also, let him purpose to himself and bind his **will** most firmly in this resolution: that he will never again enter into his former beastly **images** and **vices**. Indeed, even if all the **swine** and **evil beasts** in him should mourn to the death the **loss** of their **food** and **pastime**, and even if he himself should be considered a **fool** in the eyes of the **world** for doing so, he must still be faithful to his resolution of clinging to the promised **grace of God**. If he must become a **child of death**, he should desire to be so in the **death of Christ**, to die and live to him as Christ pleases. Let him act and execute this **purpose** by continually praying and sighing to God, committing all his endeavors, undertakings, and labors unto him, and ceasing from the **imagination** or inclination toward **pride, covetousness, and envy**. Let him but deliver up these three **beasts**, and the rest will soon become weak, faint, and ready to die. For Christ will soon take **form** in the words of **his promise**, which that man imprints in himself and wraps himself in, and so come to **life** and begin to work in him; whereby his prayers will become powerful, and he will be more and more **strengthened** and confirmed in the **Spirit of Grace**.

16. And as the **seed** in the mother's **womb** undergoes the risks of nature and many outward accidents while growing to be a **child** before it gets **life**, so it is here. The more resolutely—and through the more **opposition**—a man goes forth from **himself** and out of these **images**, the more speedily and thoroughly he enters into God, until at length Christ comes to be **living in the incorporated grace**. This is effected in and through the great **earnestness** of the **purpose** and **struggle**. Upon this there presently follows the **betrothing** or **espousal** with **Virgin Sophia** <note>In the mystical theology of Jacob Boehme, "Virgin Sophia" represents Divine Wisdom and the pure, heavenly humanity that the soul must be reunited with</note>, namely, the precious humanity of Christ, wherein the two **lovers**,

# The Key to Divine Mysteries.

<margin>• Luke 15:7–10.</margin>
...the soul and the *humanity* of *Christ* receive and embrace one another with *joy*, and together with the most inward *desire*, penetrate into the sweet *love* of *God*. And immediately the *Marriage* of the *Lamb* is solemnized, where *Virgin Sophia*—that is, the precious *humanity* of *Christ*—is vitally united to the *soul*. <note>In the theology of Jacob Boehme, "Virgin Sophia" represents Divine Wisdom and the pure, spiritual humanity that a believer recovers through union with Christ.</note> Now, what is done at *that marriage*, and with what *joy* it is celebrated, *Christ* himself indicates by saying, *There is greater joy in heaven (which is within humanity) and among the angels in the presence of God for one sinner who repents than for ninety-nine just persons who need no repentance.*

17. But we have neither *pen* that can write nor *words* that can express how exceedingly sweet the *grace* of *God* in the *humanity* of *Christ* is, and what they enjoy who come worthily to the *Marriage* of the *Lamb*. We ourselves have indeed found it by *experience* in this our *way* and *course*, and therefore know for certain that we have a sure *foundation* from which we write. We would, from the *bottom* of our *heart*, most willingly share the same with our *brothers and sisters* in the *love* of *Christ*. If they would believe and follow our faithful, child-like *counsel*, they would also find by *experience* within themselves the source from which this *simple hand* <note>original: "simple Hand"; a humble self-reference by the author, likely Jacob Boehme.</note> knows and understands these great *mysteries*.

<margin>• The following book, called *The Way to Christ*.</margin>
18. But having previously written a lengthy *treatise* specifically concerning *repentance* and *regeneration*, we refrain from writing more in this short *guide* and refer the *reader* to *that treatise*. We also refer the reader to the great *work* on *Genesis* called the *Mysterium Magnum*, <note>original: *Mysterium Magnum*; Latin for "The Great Mystery," Boehme's extensive and influential commentary on the Book of Genesis.</note> in which he may find the *basis* of whatever he will or can ask, laid down sufficiently. And we encourage him, in true *Christian love*, to follow us in our *process* and *way*, and then he shall attain the *Divine Vision* within himself and hear what the *Lord*, through *Christ*, speaks in *him*. With this, we commend him to the *love* of *Christ*.

->Dated the 9th of February, 1623.<-

### TO THE
# R E A D E R .

*DEAR Reader, if you will use this book correctly <note>original: "aright"</note> and are truly sincere <note>original: "in good Earnest"</note>, you will certainly find the benefit of it. But I want you to be warned: if you are not sincere, do not meddle with the precious <note>original: "dear"</note> names of God. It is through these names that the Most High Holiness is invoked, moved, and powerfully desired; do not use them lightly, lest they ignite <note>original: "kindle"</note> the anger of God in your soul. Such people will discover what kind of words are within it and from where they originate <note>original: "whence they are born"</note>. I hereby commend you to the eternal goodness and mercy of God.*

<meta>This page begins a treatise on the nature of repentance, focusing on the psychological and spiritual preparation required for a person to turn back toward God.</meta>

### OF
# TRUE REPENTANCE.

---

->*How a person must stir themselves up in mind and will; and what their consideration and earnest purpose must be, when they perform powerful and effectual repentance: And with what mind they must appear before God, when they would ask for, so as to obtain, the remission of sins.*<-

1. When a person enters into *repentance*, and turns to God with their prayers, they should—before they begin to pray—seriously consider the state of their own *soul*. They should see how it is completely and utterly turned away from God, having become faithless to *Him*, and is only focused on this temporal, frail, and earthly *life*. It bears no sincere love toward God or its neighbor, but instead entirely desires and walks contrary to the *commandments* of God, seeking only *itself* in the temporary and passing *desires of the flesh* <note>original: "Lusts of the Flesh"</note>.

2. Next, they should consider that all of this is an utter *hostility* <note>original: "Enmity"</note> against God, which *Satan* has raised and worked within them through his *deception* of our *first parents*; for the sake of this abomination, we must suffer death and undergo *corruption* within our bodies.

3. They should consider the three horrible *chains* with which our *souls* are fast bound during the time of this earthly *life*.
— The *first* is the severe *anger* of God, the *abyss* and *dark world*, which is the *center, root, or constituent principle* of the soul’s life.
— The *second* is the *desire of the devil* against the soul, by which he continually sifts <note>original: "fifteth"; a reference to Luke 22:31, where Satan desires to "sift" the disciples like wheat</note> and tempts it, striving without ceasing to throw it from the *truth* of God into his own evil *nature* and *element*—namely, into *pride, greed <note>original: "Covetousness"</note>, envy, and anger*. With his *desire*, he blows up and kindles those evil *properties* in the soul, causing its *will* to turn away from God and enter into *self*.
— The *third* and most harmful *chain* of all, with which the poor soul is tied, is the *corrupt* and altogether vain, earthly, and mortal *flesh and blood*, full of evil *desires* and *inclinations*.

Here, the person must consider that they lie as a close *prisoner*, soul and body, in the *mire* of sins, in the *anger* of God, and in the *jaws* of hell. They must see that the *anger of God* burns in their *soul* and body, and that they are that very loathsome *keeper of swine* <note>a reference to the Parable of the Prodigal Son in Luke 15</note> who has spent and consumed his father’s *inheritance*—namely, the precious *love* and *mercy of God*—with the "fatted swine" of the *devil* in earthly pleasures. They have not kept the dear *covenant* and *atonement* of the innocent *death and passion* <note>the suffering of Christ</note> of *Jesus Christ*, which *covenant* God, out of *pure grace*, has given to or placed into our *humanity*, reconciling us in *Him*. They must also consider that they have totally forgotten the *covenant* of holy *baptism*, in which they promised to be faithful and true to their *Saviour*, and have so completely defiled and clouded their *righteousness* with *sin* (which *righteousness* God had freely bestowed upon them in *Christ*), that they now stand before the *face* of God like a dirty, ragged, and patched *keeper of swine* who has defiled the beautiful *garment* of *Christ’s* innocence...

**4.** He should earnestly consider that *wrathful Death* awaits him every *hour* and *moment*. He will regret that he did not take care during that *short time* to secure for himself a *share in the communion of the saints*, so that he could have enjoyed with them *Eternal Light* and *Divine Glory*.

**6.** He must consider that the ungodly man loses his noble *Image*. God created him in and for *His own Image*—as a representative of the Creator—but he gains instead a *deformed* or *monstrous shape*, like a *hellish worm* or *ugly beast*. In this state, he is an *enemy to God, Heaven*, and all *holy angels and men*. His *communion* is, and will be forever, with the *devils* and *hellish worms* in horrible *darkness*.

They may never see the *Land of the Saints* for all eternity, nor get any *ease* or *refreshment*, as appears by the *example of Dives* the rich man. <note>original: "Dives" is the Latin word for "rich man," referring to the parable of the Rich Man and Lazarus in Luke 16:19–31.</note>

God created him out of his *goodness* for man's own eternal *bliss and glory*, so that he might dwell with the *holy angels and children of God* in great *happiness, power, and glory*. He was meant for the *Eternal Light* and the praiseworthy and melodious *harmony* of the *angelic and divine Kingdom of Joy*. There he should rejoice continually with the *children of God* without any *fear* of an *end*. In that place, no *evil thoughts* could touch him, nor any *care*, *trouble*, *heat*, or *cold*. No *night* is known there; there is no *day* or limited *time* anymore, but an *everlasting blessedness* wherein *soul* and *body* tremble for *joy*.

He must consider that he so willfully loses all this *eternal glory and happiness* for the *sake* of such a *short and poor time*. Even in this *state of vanity and corruption*, the evil *life* of the voluptuous *flesh* is full of *misery, fear*, and utter *vexation*. In this life, it goes the same for the *wicked* as for the *righteous*: as the one must die, so must the other. The only difference is that the *death of the saints* is an *entrance* into *Eternal Rest*, while the *death of the wicked* is an *introduction into Eternal Anguish*.

It goes with the *rich* and *mighty* just as it does with the *poor* and the *beggar*. In the deep consideration of these weighty truths, a person shall come to *feel* in his *heart* and *mind*—especially if he at the same time visualizes and sets before his eyes *his own end* <note>original: "his own end"; meaning the moment of his death and subsequent judgment</note>—a hearty *sighing* and longing after the mercy of God. He will begin to bewail the sins he has committed and be sorry he has spent his days so ill, failing to observe or consider that he stands in this world as in a *field*, growing to be a *fruit* either in the *love* or in the *anger* of God. He will then first begin to find in himself that he has not yet labored at all in the *vineyard* of Christ, but that he is a *dry, fruitless* branch of the *vine*. And thus in many a person whom the *Spirit* of Christ touches in such a consideration, there arises abundant sorrow, *grief of heart*, and inward lamentation over the days of his wickedness which he has spent in vanity, without any work in the *vineyard* of Christ.

Such a man, whom the *Spirit* of Christ thus brings into *sorrow* and *repentance* so that his heart is opened both to know and bewail his sins, is very easily helped. He needs only to draw to himself the *promise* of Christ, namely: *That God does not will the death of a sinner, but rather wishes them all to come to him, and he will refresh them*; and, *that there is great joy in heaven for one sinner who repents*. Let such a person but lay hold on the *words* of Christ and wrap himself up in Christ's *meritorious passion and death* <note>original: "meritorious Passion and Death"; referring to the theological belief that Christ's suffering and death earned the merit necessary for human salvation</note>.

But I will now speak to those who feel indeed in themselves a *desire* to repent, and yet cannot come to *acknowledge* and *bewail* their committed sins. The *flesh* says continually to the soul, "*Stay a while, it is well enough; or there is time enough tomorrow*"; and when *tomorrow* has come, then the *flesh* says again, "*Tomorrow*." The soul, meanwhile, sighing and fainting, conceives neither any true *sorrow* for the sins it has committed, nor any *comfort*. To such a person, I say, I will write a *process* or *way* which I myself have gone, so that he may know what he must do and how it went with me, if perhaps he is inclined to enter into and pursue the same; then he will come to understand what he shall find written here afterwards.

## A Process of Repentance; or Way to Conversion.

When any man finds in himself—by the former or any other considerations pressed home upon his mind and conscience—a *hunger* or *desire* to repent, and yet feels no true *sorrow* in himself for the *sins* which he has committed, but only a *hunger* or *desire* for such *sorrow*; so that the poor captive soul continually *sighs, fears*, and must acknowledge itself guilty of sins before the *judgment* of God—such a person, I say, can take no better course than this: namely, to wrap up his *senses, mind*, and *reason* together and make for himself instantly, as soon as he perceives in himself the *desire* to repent, a mighty, strong *purpose* and *resolution*. He must resolve that he will that *very hour*, nay, *that minute*, immediately enter into repentance and go forth from his wicked way, and not at all regard the power and respect of the world. 

Indeed, if it should be required, he would forsake and devalue all things for the sake of true *repentance*, and never depart from that *resolution* again, even if he should be made the *fool* and *scorn* of all the world for it. But with the full intent and strength of his mind, he will go forth from the beauty and pleasure of the world, and patiently enter into the *passion* and *death* of Christ in and under the *cross*, and set all his *hope* and *confidence* upon the life to come. Even *now*, in righteousness and truth, he will enter into the *vineyard* of Christ and do the will of God. In the *spirit* and *will* of Christ, he will begin and finish all...

He must firmly visualize, and wholly wrap up his soul in this persuasion: that in this purpose he *shall obtain the love of God in Christ Jesus*. He must believe that God will give to him, according to his faithful promise, that noble pledge, the *Holy Ghost*, as an *earnest* <term>earnest: a down payment or deposit given as a guarantee of a future total payment</term>; that, in the humanity of Christ, as to the *heavenly substance*, he shall be born again within himself; and that the Spirit of Christ will renew his mind with his love and power, and strengthen his weak faith. Also, he must believe that in his *divine hunger* he *shall receive the flesh and blood of Christ for food and drink* in the desire of his soul—which hungers and thirsts after it *as its proper nourishment*—and with the *thirst* of the soul, drink the *water of eternal life out of the sweet fountain of Jesus Christ*, just as Christ’s most true and steadfast promise declares.

He must also wholly and firmly visualize and set before himself the great *love* of God: that *God does not desire the death of a sinner, but rather that he repent and believe*; that Christ calls poor sinners very kindly and graciously to himself and will *refresh* them; that *God has sent his Son into the world to seek and save that which is lost*, namely, the poor repentant and returning sinner; and that for the poor sinner’s sake *he has given his life unto death* and died for him in our human nature which he took upon himself.

Furthermore, he must firmly persuade himself that God in Christ Jesus will much more readily hear him and receive him into grace than he can even approach; and that God, in the love of Christ and in the most dear and precious name JESUS, *cannot desire any evil*. There is no *angry* countenance at all in *this name*; rather, it is the *highest and deepest love and faithfulness, the greatest sweetness of the Deity* within the great name JEHOVAH, which he has manifested in our humanity—corrupted as it is and perished in regards to the *heavenly part* which disappeared in Paradise through sin. He was, therefore, moved in his *heart* to flow into us with his *sweet love*, so that the *anger* of his Father, which was kindled in us, might be quenched and turned into *love* by it. All of this was done for the poor sinner’s sake, so that he might obtain an open gate of grace again.

In this consideration, he must firmly visualize that at this very hour and instant he stands before the face of the *holy Trinity*, and that God is really present within and without him, as the Holy Scripture witnesses, saying, *“Do I not fill all things?”* And in another place, *“The word is near you, in your mouth and in your heart.”*—Also, *“We will come to you and make our home with you.”* And, *“Behold, I am with you always, even to the end of the world.”* And again, *“The kingdom of God is within you.”*

Thus, he must firmly know and believe that, in his *inner being*, he stands truly before the face of Jesus Christ—even before the *holy Deity*—on whom his soul has turned its back. He must resolve that he will this very hour turn the *eyes* and *desire* of his soul toward God again and, like the poor, lost, and returning son <note>This refers to the Parable of the Prodigal Son in Luke 15.</note>, come to the Father. ## A Short Form of Confession Before the Face of God.

->*Everyone, as their case and necessity requires, may organize and expand*<-
->*this confession as the Holy Spirit shall teach them. I will only set*<-
->*down a brief guide.*<-

O you great, unsearchable God, Lord of all things; you, who in Christ Jesus—out of great *love* toward us—has manifested yourself with your *holy substance* <term>Substance: In this context, the divine essence or spiritual reality that makes up God's nature.</term> in our humanity: I, a poor, unworthy, sinful wretch, come before your presence, which you have manifested in the *humanity* of *Jesus Christ*. Though I am not worthy to lift up my eyes to you, I acknowledge and confess before you that I am guilty of unfaithfulness and of breaking away from your great *love* and *grace*, which you have freely bestowed upon us. 

I have left the *covenant* <term>Covenant: A formal, sacred agreement or promise between God and his people.</term>, which out of mere grace you made with me in *baptism*, in which you received me as a child and heir of eternal life. Instead, I have turned my *desire* toward the vanity of this world, defiling my soul with it and making it altogether bestial and earthly. Consequently, my soul does not even know itself because of the mire of *sin*; it considers itself a stranger before your face, unworthy to even desire your grace. I lie in the guilt and filth of sin and the vanity of my corrupt flesh, up to the very lips of my soul, and have only a *small spark* of the *living breath* left in me which still desires your grace. I am dead in sin and corruption, so that in this woeful condition, I dare not lift up my eyes to you.

O God in Christ Jesus, you who became man for the sake of poor sinners to help them: to you I complain. To you I still have a spark of refuge in my soul. I have not respected the *purchased inheritance* which you bought for us poor men by your bitter *death*, but have instead made myself a partaker of the heritage of vanity. I am caught in the *anger* of my Father and the curse of the earth; I am ensnared in sin and half-dead to your kingdom. I lie in weakness regarding your strength, and a *wrathful death* waits for me. 

The *Devil* has poisoned me so that I do not know my Savior. I have become a *wild branch* on your tree and have consumed my *inheritance* (which is in you) with the *Devil’s swine* <note>original: "Devil's Swine"; a reference to the Parable of the Prodigal Son in Luke 15, where the son reaches his lowest point feeding pigs before returning to his father.</note>. What shall I say before you, I who am not worthy of your grace? I lie in the *sleep of death* which has captured me, and I am fast bound with *three strong chains* <note>In the author's theology, these often represent the three "principles" or bonds of the fallen human condition: the wrath of God, the desire of the flesh, and the illusions of the world.</note>. 

O you *Breaker-through-Death* <note>original: "Breaker-through-Death"; a poetic title for Jesus Christ, celebrating his victory over the grave and his ability to liberate souls from spiritual death.</note>, assist me, I beseech you! I cannot do it; I am able to do nothing! I am dead in myself and have no strength before you; neither do I dare, out of great shame, lift up my eyes to you. For I am the defiled *keeper of swine* and have spent my *inheritance* with the false, adulterous *whore* of vanity in the lusts of the flesh. I have sought *myself* in my own lust, and not *you*. Now, in myself, I have become a fool. I am naked and *bare*; my *shame* stands before my eyes, and I cannot hide it. Your judgment waits for me. 

What shall I say before you, who are the judge of all the world? I have nothing to bring before you. Here I stand naked and *bare* in your presence, falling down before your face and bewailing my misery. I fly to your great mercy, though I am not worthy of it. Receive me into your *death*, and let me die from my death into *yours*. Cast me down, I pray you, to the ground in my innate *self*, and kill this *self* of mine through your *death*, so that I may live no more to *myself*—seeing as I, in *myself*, work nothing but *sin*. Therefore, I pray you, cast this wicked beast to the ground—this beast which is full of false deceit and *self-desire*—and deliver this poor soul of mine from its heavy bonds.

# Of True Repentance.

> I wait for your promise, which you have made, saying, *“As I live, I do not desire the death of a sinner, but rather that he should turn and live.”* <note>original: “As I live, I will not the Death of a Sinner, but that he ſhall turn and live.” A reference to Ezekiel 33:11.</note> I sink myself down into the *death* of my *Redeemer Jesus Christ*, and wait for you, whose Word is Truth and Life. *Amen.*

In this, or a similar manner, everyone may confess their sins as they find them when examining their conscience—specifically, what sins they have brought upon their soul. Yet, if their intent is truly earnest, using a set form of prayer is unnecessary. The *Spirit of God*, which at that moment is present in the *will of the mind*, will itself create the prayer for them within their *inner being*. For it is the Spirit of God that works repentance in a truly earnest desire and intercedes for the soul before God through the death of Christ.

But I will not hide from you, beloved reader with a *Christian intent*, how things usually go for those who have such a firm purpose and resolution. To be sure, it happens differently for one person than for another, depending on whether their purpose is more or less earnest and strong. For the Spirit of God is not restricted but uses various ways or processes according to what he knows is best for each individual. Yet, just as a soldier who has been in many battles can explain how to fight and instruct another who might find themselves in a similar situation, so can I share this experience.

Now, when such a heart—with strong resolution and purpose—comes before God and enters into repentance, it happens to that heart as it did to the *Canaanite woman* <note>In Matthew 15:21-28, Jesus initially appears to ignore the Canaanite woman’s plea for help to test the strength of her faith.</note>; that is, it seems as if God will not hear. *The heart remains without comfort; its sins, follies, and neglects also present themselves before it, making it feel unworthy of any comfort. The mind is, as it were, speechless; the soul groans in the depths; the heart receives nothing, nor can it even pour out its confession before God; it feels as if the heart and soul were completely shut up.* The soul desperately wants to go toward God, but the flesh keeps it captive. The Devil also shuts it up tightly, presenting the path of vanity to it once more, tickling it with the desires of the flesh, and saying inwardly, *“Wait a while; do this or that first; get enough money or goods beforehand so that you don’t need the world’s help, and afterward enter into repentance and a holy life; it will be time enough then.”*

O, how many hundreds perish in such a beginning if they turn back again to vanity! They become like young grafts <note>term: “grafts” refers to young shoots or branches joined to a tree; here, a metaphor for a new convert’s spiritual life.</note> broken off by the wind or withered by the heat!

Beloved soul, take note: if you wish to be a champion in your Savior Christ against death and hell, and want your young graft to grow and become a tree in the kingdom of Christ, you must press on and stand firm in your first earnest purpose. It is worth as much as your eternal inheritance—and your body and soul too—whether you become an angel in God or a devil in hell. If you want to be crowned, you must fight; you must overcome in Christ and not yield to the Devil. *Your purpose must stand firm; you must not prefer worldly honor and goods over it.* When the spirit of the flesh says, *“Wait a while, it isn’t convenient yet,”* then the soul must say, *“Now is the time for me to go back again to my native country <note>That is, the spiritual Paradise or state of grace.</note>, from which my father Adam brought me. No creature shall hold me back. Even if my earthly body should decay and perish because of it, I will now enter—with my will and whole desire—into the rose-garden of my Redeemer Jesus Christ. I will enter into him through his suffering and death, and in the death of Christ, I will subdue you, you earthly body! For you have swallowed up my pearl <note>A reference to the “Pearl of Great Price” (Matthew 13:45–46), representing the divine light or the purity of the soul.</note> which God gave to my father Adam in Paradise. I will break the will of your lustful pleasures <note>original: “Voluptuouſneſs”</note>, which live in vanity, and bind you like a mad dog with the chain of my earnest purpose. And even if you should become a fool in the eyes of all people because of this, you must and shall obey the firm resolve of my soul. Nothing shall loosen you from this chain except physical death. May God and his strength help me in this.”*

->I<-

<header>Of True Repentance.</header>

# *A short instruction on how the poor soul must return to God and fight for the noble crown; what kind of weapons it must use if it will go to war against God's anger, against the Devil, the world, and sin, against flesh and blood, against the influence of the stars and elements, and all its other enemies.*

BELOVED soul, *earnestness* is required to do this, and not just a mere recital of words! No, an earnest and resolved *will* must drive this work; otherwise, nothing will be achieved. For if the soul wishes to obtain the *victorious crown* <note>original: "triumphal Garland"</note> of Christ from the noble *Sophia* <term>the personification of Divine Wisdom in mystical theology</term>, or *Divine Wisdom*, it must woo her with a great desire of *love*. It must entreat her in her most *holy name* and come before her with the deepest humility—not like a *lustful bull* or a *wanton Venus* <note>original: "wanton Venus"; a reference to seeking spiritual gifts for selfish or carnal pleasure</note>. For as long as anyone is in such a state, they must not seek these things, for they shall not obtain them. Even if something were obtained by those in such an impure state, it would be no more than a *glimpse* of the *true glory*. 

But a *chaste* and *modest mind* may prevail so far as to have the soul—in its noble image, which died in *Adam*—quickened in the *heavenly corporality* <note>the spiritual substance or "body" of the soul</note> within its *inward ground*, and have the precious *crown* set upon it. Yet if this should happen, the crown is taken off the soul again and laid aside, just as a *crown* is usually stored after a king has been crowned with it. So it also happens with the *heavenly crown* or *gift*. It is taken from the soul again because the soul is still surrounded by the *house of sin* <note>the fallen physical body or the corruptible nature</note>; this is done so that if the soul should unhappily fall again, its *crown* would not be defiled. This is spoken plainly enough for the "children" who know and have tried these things; none of the wicked are worthy to know more about them.

## *The Process, or Way.*

A person must bring a *serious mind* to this work. He must come before God with *sincere earnestness, deep humility, and hearty sorrow for his sins, and with a deliberate and firm resolution not to enter the old, broad way of vanity anymore.* And even if the whole world should account him a fool, and he should lose both honor and goods—and even his temporal life as well—for the sake of his *new choice*, he must resolve firmly to abide by it.

If he is ever to obtain the *love* and *marriage* of the noble *Sophia*, he must make such a *vow* in his *purpose* and *mind*. For *Christ himself says, "He who does not forsake wife and children, brothers and sisters, money and goods, and all that he has—and even his earthly life also—to follow me, is not worthy of me."* Here, Christ refers to the *mind* of the soul. If there were anything that would keep the *mind* back from Him, no matter how fair and glorious a pretense or appearance it has in this world, the *mind* must not regard it at all. Instead, the soul must rather part with it than with the *love of the noble virgin Sophia, in the bud and blossom of Christ, in his tender humanity within us as the heavenly corporality.* For this is the *Flower of Sharon and the Rose of the Valley of Jericho* <note>biblical metaphors for beauty and divine favor from the Song of Solomon and Ecclesiasticus</note> in which *Solomon* delighted and called his dear *love*, his chaste *virgin* whom he loved. Indeed, all other saints before and after him did the same; whoever obtained her called her his *pearl*.

As for the manner in which to pray for it, you may see by the short directions following. The work itself must be committed to the *Holy Spirit* <note>original: "Holy Ghost"</note>; He forms and frames the prayer for the soul in every heart where He is sought.

## The P R A Y E R.

I, a poor unworthy creature, come before you, O *great and holy God*, and lift up my eyes to you. Though I am not worthy, yet your great mercy and your faithful promise in your Word have *now* encouraged me to lift the eyes of my soul’s *desire* up to you. For my soul has *now* taken hold of the Word of your promise and received it into itself, and with it, comes to you. And though it is but an *estranged child* <note>original: "strange Child"; meaning a child who has become alienated or like a stranger through disobedience</note> which was disobedient to you, yet *now* it desires to be obedient. It does *now* enfold itself with its desire into that *Word* which became *man*, which became *flesh and blood*, and has broken the power of sin and death in my humanity. This Word has changed the *wrath* of God into *love* within the soul, has deprived *death* of his power, and *hell* of its victory over soul and body; it has opened a gate for my soul to the bright face of your strength and power. 

O *great and most holy God*, I have brought the *hunger and desire* of my soul into this *most holy Word*, and now I come before you. In my hunger I call to you, *you living fountain*, through your *Word* which became *flesh and blood*. Your *Word* having been made the life in our flesh, I receive it firmly into the *desire* of my soul as my own life. I pierce into you with the *desire* of my soul through the *Word* in the flesh of *Christ*; through his holy conception in the *Virgin Mary*, his incarnation, his holy birth, his baptism in the *Jordan*, and his temptation in the wilderness, where he overcame the kingdom of the Devil and this world in his *humanity*. 

I come through all the miracles which he did on earth; through his reproach and disgrace, his innocent *death* and *passion* <term>The "passion" refers to the period of intense spiritual and physical suffering of Jesus leading up to and including the crucifixion.</term>, and the shedding of his blood, wherein God’s anger in soul and flesh was drowned. I come through his rest in the tomb, when he awakened our father *Adam* out of his sleep—he who had fallen into a dead sleep regarding the Kingdom of Heaven. I come through his love, which pierced through the *wrath* and destroyed *hell* in the soul; through his resurrection from the dead, his ascension, the sending of the *Holy Spirit* into our soul and spirit, and through all his promises. One of those promises is *that you, O God the Father, will give the Holy Spirit to those who ask for it, in the name and through the Word which became man.*

O you life of my flesh and of my soul in Christ my brother, I beseech you in the *hunger* of my soul. I entreat you with all my *powers*, though they are weak, to give me what you have promised me and freely bestow upon me in my Savior *Jesus Christ*: his *flesh for food* and his *blood for drink* to refresh my poor hungry soul. May it be made alive and strengthened in the *Word* which became man, so that it may long and hunger after you rightly.

O you deepest love in the most sweet name JESUS, give yourself into the desire of my soul. For this reason you have moved yourself and, according to your great sweetness, manifested yourself in human nature and called us to you—*us who hunger and thirst after you*—and have promised *that you will refresh us*. I now open the lips of my soul to you, O you sweet Truth; and though I am not worthy to desire it of your holiness, yet I come to you through your bitter *passion* and *death*. You have sprinkled my uncleanness with your *blood*, sanctified me in your *humanity*, and made an open gate for me through your *death* to your sweet love in your *blood*. Through your five holy wounds, from which you shed your *blood*, I bring the desire of my soul into your love.

O Jesus Christ, you Son of God and man, I pray you receive into yourself your purchased inheritance, which your Father has given you. I cry within me, that I may enter through your holy blood and *death* into you. Open yourself in me, that the spirit of my soul may reach you and receive you into it. Lay hold on my thirst in me with your

> Thirst; bring your thirst for us humans, which you had upon the cross, into my thirst, and give me your *blood* to drink in my thirst. Let that death within me which holds me captive be drowned in the *blood* of your love. Let my extinguished or suppressed image—which disappeared in my father *Adam* through sin as it relates to the kingdom of heaven—be made alive through your powerful *blood*. Let my soul be clothed with it again, as with the new body which dwells in heaven. In this image, your holy power and the *Word* that became man dwell; this is the *temple of the Holy Spirit*, who dwells in us according to your promise, saying, *“We will come to you, and make our home with you.”*
> 
> O you great love of Jesus Christ, I can do no more than sink my *desire* into you. Your *Word* which became man is truth; since you have invited me to come, now I come. Let it be to me according to your word and will. *Amen.*

## A Warning to the Reader.

BELOVED reader, out of love for you, I will not hide from you what has been earnestly revealed to me. If you still love the *vanity* of the *flesh* and do not have an earnest purpose on the way toward the *new birth* or *regeneration* <note>original: "Regeneration," meaning the process of being spiritually reborn.</note>—intending to become a *new man*—then leave the prayers written above unspoken. Otherwise, they will turn into a *judgment* of God within you. You must not take the holy names in vain; you are faithfully warned. They belong to the *thirsty* soul. But if your soul is in earnest, it shall find through experience what kind of words they are.

## *Instructions on how the soul must meet its Beloved, when she knocks in its center, or inner chamber.*

BELOVED soul, if you will be earnest without ceasing, you shall certainly obtain the favor of a kiss from the noble *Sophia* <note>original: *Sophia*, a Greek term for "Wisdom," personified here as a divine feminine guide for the soul.</note> (*or divine wisdom*) in the holy name JESUS. For she stands forever before the door of the soul, knocking and warning the sinner of his wicked way. Now, if he once desires her love, she is ready for him and kisses him with the beams of her sweet love, from which the heart receives joy. But she does not immediately lie down in the *marriage-bed* with the soul; that is, she does not immediately awaken the *extinguished* heavenly *image* within herself, which disappeared in *Adam* in *Paradise*. No, there might be danger to man in that; for if *Adam* and *Lucifer* fell even though it was manifested within them, the same might easily happen to man, who is still so strongly enslaved by vanity.

The bond of your promise must be firm and steadfast. Before she will crown you, you must be tempted and tried. She withdraws the beams of her love from you again to see whether you will prove faithful; she also lets you stand at a distance, as it were, and does not answer you with even one look of her love. For before she will crown you, you must be judged, so that you may taste the bitter dregs of the potion you have filled for yourself through your abominations. You must first come before the gates of *hell* and there demonstrate your victory for her in her love, using the strength with which she supported you against the devil’s malignant influence.

Christ was tempted in the wilderness; and if you wish to "put on" <note>To "put on Christ" refers to the Pauline concept in Galatians 3:27 of being clothed in Christ's nature.</note> him, you must go *through* his entire process or journey, from his incarnation to his ascension. And although you are neither able nor required to do exactly what he has done, you must still enter completely into his *process* and there die continually to the corruption of the soul. For the *Virgin Sophia* does not betroth herself to the soul except in this state, which springs up in the soul through the *death* of Christ, like a new plant growing in heaven.

# Of True Repentance.

The earthly body cannot understand her during its lifetime, for it must first die to the vanity of corruption. However, the *heavenly image* that was lost in *Adam*—specifically the true *Seed of the Woman* in which God became man and brought his living seed, the *heavenly substance*—is capable of receiving the Pearl, just as it happened in *Mary* at the *fulfillment* <note>original: "End or Fulfilling"</note> of the Covenant.

Therefore, be careful what you do: when you have made your promise, keep it; and then she [the Virgin Sophia] will *crown* you more readily than you wish to be crowned. But when the Tempter comes to you with the pleasures, beauty, and glory of the world, you must be sure that your mind rejects them and says, "*I must be a servant and not a master in Christ's vineyard; I am only God's steward over everything I possess, and I must use it as his Word teaches me; my heart must dwell with the simple and lowly in the dust and always be humble.*" Whatever your state or condition, *humility* must be at the forefront, or else you will not win the noble *Virgin* <note>The "Virgin" refers to "Sophia" or Divine Wisdom, a central figure in Boehme's mysticism representing the feminine aspect of God's glory.</note> in *marriage*. The *free will* of your soul must face the struggle like a champion; for if the *Devil* cannot defeat the soul with vanity, nor trap it with that bait, he then attacks with the soul's *unworthiness* and its *list of sins*. There you must fight hard, and the *merits of Christ* must be placed at the front, or else the creature cannot prevail against the Devil. In this conflict, it goes so terribly for many a poor sinner that human *reason* thinks him to be mentally disturbed <note>original: "distracted"</note> or possessed by an *evil spirit*. The Devil defends himself so horribly in some—especially if he has held a great *stronghold* <note>original: "Fort of Prey"</note> in them—that he must be stoutly attacked before he will depart and leave his castle. In this kind of combat, *Heaven* and *Hell* are fighting against each other.

Now, if the soul remains constant and gains the *victory* over the Devil in *all* his assaults—valuing the love of the noble *Sophia* more than all worldly things—then the *precious wreath* <note>original: "Garland"</note> will be placed upon it as a sign or banner of *victory*.

Here the *Virgin* (who reveals herself in the dear name of JESUS CHRIST, the *Treader upon the Serpent* <note>A reference to the prophecy in Genesis 3:15 that the seed of the woman would crush the serpent's head.</note> and *God's Anointed*) comes to the soul. She kisses it with her sweetest love in its innermost *essence* and impresses her love into its *desire* as a token of victory. And here *Adam’s heavenly part* rises again from *death* in Christ. I cannot write of this, for no pen in this world can express it: it is the *Wedding of the Lamb*, where the noble pearl is sown with great triumph, though in the *beginning it is as small as a grain of mustard seed*, as Christ says.

Now, when the *wedding* is over, the soul must take care that this *Pearl-Tree* (or *Tree of Faith*) sprouts and grows, as it promised the *Virgin*. For the Devil will immediately come with his furious storm: ungodly people who will mock, despise, and denounce this path as *madness*. Then a person must enter into the *experience* <note>original: "Process"</note> of Christ, carrying his *cross*. Here it will be shown in deed and in truth what sort of *Christian* he is. For he must allow himself to be labeled a *fool* and a godless *wretch*; indeed, even his closest friends, who once supported or flattered him in his worldly desires, will now be his *enemies* and hate him, even though they do not know why. Thus it is that Christ completely hides his *bride* under the *cross*, so that she may not be known in this world. The Devil also strives to keep these children hidden from the *world*, lest perhaps many such *branches* should grow in that garden which he believes belongs to him.

I have written this for the information of the Christian-minded reader, so that he may know what to do if the same should happen to him.

## A very earnest Prayer in Temptation,

### Against God’s *Anger* in the *Conscience*; and also against *Flesh* and *Blood*, when the Temptation comes to the *Soul*, and wrestles with it.

> Most deep Love of God in Christ Jesus, do not leave me in this distress. I confess I am guilty of the sins which now rise up in my *mind* and *conscience*; and if you forsake me, I must perish. But have you not promised me in your Word, saying, *If a mother could forget her child, which can hardly be, yet you will not forget me?* You have set me as a *sign* in your hands, which were pierced through with sharp nails, and in your open side from which *blood* and *water* gushed out. Poor wretch that I am! I am caught in your *anger*, and can in *my own* ability do nothing before you; I sink myself down into your *wounds* and *death*.
>

I have no refuge in anything, but only in your *holy wounds* and *death!* Into you I sink down in the *anguish* of my conscience; do with me what you will. In you I will now live or die, as it pleases you; let me but die and perish in your *death*; only bury me into your *death*, so that the *anguish* of Hell may not touch me. How can I excuse myself before you, who knows my *heart* and *inner thoughts* <note>original: "reins," historically viewed as the seat of emotions and secret thoughts</note>, and sets my sins before my eyes? You have freely given me *his anguish*, and drowned your *wrath* in *him:* and though I have not accepted it, but have departed from him and become faithless, yet you have given me this precious pledge in my *flesh* and *blood*. Drive him out of me, so that he may not overcome me; for no one living can stand in your sight, if you withdraw your *hand* from him.
>

O mortify the desire of my vanity in flesh and blood, which the Devil has now kindled by his false desire, by *hellish anguish* and desperation. O quench it with your *water of eternal life*, and bring my *anguish* forth through your *death*; I wholly sink myself down into you; and though soul and body should this hour faint and perish in your wrath, yet I will not let you go. Though my heart says utterly, *No, no*, yet the desire of my soul

## Instruction Regarding Temptation.

BELOVED reader, this is no *jesting matter*; he who considers it so has not tried it, nor has he yet passed the *judgment*; but his *conscience* is still *asleep*. Even if it should be delayed until his final days—which is very dangerous—he must still pass through this *judgment*, or *fiery trial*. Happy is he who passes through it in the *time* of his *youth*, before the devil builds his *fort of prey* too strong; he may afterwards prove a *laborer* in the *heavenly vineyard* and sow his seed in the *garden of Christ*, where he shall reap the *fruit* in due time. 

This *judgment* continues for a long time for many a poor soul—even several years—if he does not earnestly and early put on the *armor of Christ*, but waits until the *judgment of tribulation* first drives him to repentance. But to him who comes of his own accord, out of his own earnest *purpose*, and endeavors to depart from his evil ways, the temptation or trial will not be so *hard*, nor will it continue *so long*. Yet he must stand out valiantly until victory is won over the devil; for he shall be *mightily assisted*, and all shall end for the *best* for him. So, afterwards, when the day *breaks* in his soul, he turns it to the great praise and glory of God, seeing that his grand enemy and persecutor was overcome in the conflict.

>
> O my noble *Vine*, I beseech you give *sap* to me, your *branch*; so that I may *bud* and *grow* in your strength and sap, in your *essence*; create in me true strength by your strength.
>
> O *sweet Love*, are you not my light? Enlighten my poor soul in its confined prison of flesh and blood. Bring it into the right way. Destroy the will of the devil, and bring my body through the whole course of this world, through the chamber of death, into your death and rest; so that at the last day it may arise in you from your death, and live in you forever. O teach me what I must do in you: I beseech you, be my *willing*, *knowing*, and *doing*; and let me go nowhere without you. I surrender myself wholly to you. *Amen.*

->*For obtaining the divine working, protection, and government; showing also how the mind should work with and in God, in Christ the Tree of Life.*<-

> O you living Fountain, in you I lift up the desire of my soul, and cry with my desire to enter through the *life* of my Savior Jesus Christ into you.
>
> O you *life* and *power* of God, awaken yourself in the *hunger* of my soul with your *desire of love*, through the *thirst* which Jesus Christ had upon the cross for us, and carry my weak *strength* through by your mighty hand in *your Spirit*; be the *working* and *will* in me with your own strength. Blossom in the strength of Jesus Christ in me, so that I may bring forth praise to you, the true *fruit* of your kingdom. O let my heart and desire never depart from you more.
>
> But I swim in vanity in this valley of misery <note>a traditional reference to the earthly world as a place of sorrow and trial</note>, in this outward earthly flesh and blood; and my soul and *noble image* <note>the divine likeness or "Imago Dei" within the human soul</note>, which is according to your similitude, is surrounded with enemies on every side: with the desire of the devil against me, with the desire of vanity in *flesh* and *blood*; and also with all the opposition of wicked *people* who do not know your name. I beseech you, let his angels that minister to him attend upon my soul and the souls of my loved ones, and encamp themselves about us, and defend us from the fiery arrows of the desire of that wicked one, which he shoots into us daily by the curse of the *anger*—

Build up the holy city *Zion* in me, in which we all live together as children of Christ in one city—which is Christ in us. I plunge myself wholly into you; do with me what you please. *Amen*.

# Of True Repentance.

Briars tear me on every side, and I am afflicted and despised by my enemies. They scorn my soul and revile it as an evildoer who has broken faith with them; they deride my walk toward you and consider it foolish. They think I am *senseless* because I walk in this *straight and thorny path* and do not go along with them in their *hypocritical broad way*.

O Lord JESUS CHRIST, I fly to you under the cross. O dear Immanuel, receive me and carry me into *yourself* through the path of your pilgrimage in which you walked in this *world*—namely, through your *incarnation, poverty, reproach, and scorn*; also through your *anguish, passion, and death*. Make me conformed to your *example*. Send your good angel along with me to show me the way through the horrible, thorny wilderness of this *world*. Assist me in my *misery*; comfort me with that *comfort* with which the angel comforted you in the *garden* when you prayed to your Father and sweat great *drops of blood*. Support me in my *anguish and persecution* under the *reproach* of the devils and all wicked men who do not know you and refuse to walk in your paths. O great *love of God*, they do not know your *way* and do this in *blindness* through the *deceit of the devil*. Have pity on them and bring them out of their *darkness* into your *light*, so that they may learn to *know themselves* and see how they lie captive in the *filth and mire* of the devil, in a *dark dungeon* fast bound with *three chains* <note>original: "three chains" likely refers to the spiritual bonds of sin, death, and the devil often cited in mystical literature</note>. O great God, have mercy upon *Adam* and his children; redeem them in Christ, the new *Adam*.

I fly to you, O *Christ*, God and man, in this pilgrimage and journey which I must take through this *dark valley*, despised and troubled on all sides and considered an ungodly, wicked man. O Lord, it is your *judgment* upon me, so that my *sins and inbred corruption* <note>original: "inbred corruption" refers to the theological concept of original sin or the inherent fallen nature of humanity</note> may be judged in this earthly pilgrimage before you. Let me, as a *curse*, be made an *open spectacle* on which your *anger* may satisfy itself, thereby taking the eternal *reproach* away from me. It is the *token* of your *love* by which you bring me into the *reproach, anguish, suffering, and death* of my Savior *Jesus Christ*, so that I may die to *vanity* and spring up in his *spirit* with a *new life* through his *reproach, ignominy, and death*.

I beseech you, O *Christ*, you *patient Lamb of God*, grant me *patience* in this my *way of the cross* through all your *anguish and reproach*, your *death and passion*, and your *scorn and contempt* upon the *cross* where you were *despised in my place*. Bring me, as a *patient lamb*, to you and into your *victory*. Let me live with you and in you; and please convert my persecutors who (unknown to themselves) sacrifice my *vanity and inbred sins* before your *anger* by their reproaching. They do not know what they do; they think they do me harm, but they do me good! They do that for me which I should do myself before you; for I should daily lay open and acknowledge my *shame and vileness* before you, and thereby sink myself down into the *death* of your beloved Son so that my *shame* might die in his *death*. But because I am too negligent, weary, faint, and feeble, you use these enemies of mine in your *anger* to open and reveal my *vileness* before you, which your *wrath* takes hold of and sinks down into the *death* of my Savior.

O merciful God, my vain *flesh* cannot understand how well you intend toward me when you allow my enemies to take my *vileness* from me and sacrifice it before you. My *earthly mind* supposes that you afflict me for my *sins*, and I am extremely troubled by it; but your *spirit* in my inward *new man* <note>original: "new man" is a biblical term (Ephesians 4:24) for the regenerated spiritual nature of a person</note> tells me that it is out of your *love* toward me and that you intend good for me by it. When you allow my enemies to persecute me, it is best for me that they perform the work in my place and unfold my sins before you in your *anger*, so that it may swallow up the *guilt* of them. Thus, they may not follow me into my *native country* <note>original: "native country" refers to the soul's heavenly home or spiritual origin</note>; for my enemies are still strong and mighty in your *anger*, and therefore can do it better than I, who am already feeble and fainting in the *will of vanity*. This you know full well, O righteous God.

I beseech you therefore, O righteous God, since you use them as *friends* to me, to do such a good service for me—even though my earthly *reason* does not know it—that you would also make *them* understand and follow my course, and send *them* such friends in turn. But first, bring them to the *Light*, that they may *know* you and give you thanks.

O merciful God in Christ Jesus, I beseech you out of your deep *love* toward us poor men, which you have manifested in me in the *hidden man*, call us all in you, to you. O stir yourself in us yet once again in this last trouble; since your *anger* is kindled in us, may you resist it, lest it swallow us up entirely, both *soul* and *body*.

O you dawning of the *day-spring* <note>original: "day-spring"; a biblical reference to the sunrise or the advent of Christ (Luke 1:78)</note> of God, break forth to the *full*! Are you not already risen? Manifest your *holy city Zion*, your *holy Jerusalem*, in us.

O great God! I see you in the depth of your *power* and *strength*. Awaken me wholly in you, that I may be quickened <note>original: "quickened"; meaning to be made alive or revitalized</note> in you. Break off the *tree* of your *anger* in us, and let your *love* spring forth and bud in us.

O Lord, I lie down in your sight, and beseech you not to rebuke us in your *anger*. Are we not your *possession* which you have purchased? Forgive all of our *sins*, and deliver us from the evil of your wrath and from the malice and envy of the Devil; and bring us under your cross in patience into *Paradise* again. *Amen.*

*Here follows a prayer or dialogue between the poor soul and the noble Virgin Sophia in the inner ground of man. This is a conversation between the Spirit of Christ in the "New Birth"—arising from his humanity within us—and the soul. It shows how great a joy there is in the heaven of the newly regenerate man, and how lovingly and graciously the noble Sophia presents herself to her bridegroom, the soul, when it enters into repentance, and how the soul behaves toward her when she appears to it.*

## The Gates of the Paradisiacal Garden of Roses.

->*This is understood by none but the children of Christ, who have known it by experience.*<-

**W**hen Christ the cornerstone stirs himself in the extinguished image of man during his sincere conversion and repentance, then Virgin *Sophia* <note>In Boehme's mystical theology, Sophia represents Divine Wisdom, often personified as a feminine spiritual guide or the "mirror" of God</note> appears. She appears in the stirring of the Spirit of Christ within that extinguished image, wearing her virgin's attire before the soul. At this, the soul is so amazed and astonished by its own *uncleanness* that all its sins immediately awaken within it, and it trembles before her. For then judgment passes upon the *sins* of the soul, so that it even shrinks back in its unworthiness, being *ashamed* in the presence of its fair love. It enters into itself, feeling and acknowledging itself utterly unworthy to receive such a *jewel*. This is understood by those who are of *our tribe* <note>Meaning those who share this specific mystical spiritual experience</note> and have tasted of this heavenly *gift*, and by no one else. But the noble Sophia draws near in the *essence* of the soul and kisses it in a friendly manner, and *tinctures* <note>original: "tinctureth"; an alchemical term meaning to infuse, transform, or dye with a new quality</note> its dark *fire* with her *rays* of *love*, and shines through it with her bright and powerful *influence*. Penetrated with the strong sense and feeling of this, the soul leaps in its body for great joy; in the strength of this virgin *love*, it exults and praises the great God for his blessed gift of *grace*.

I will set down here a short description of what it is like when the *bride* thus embraces the *bridegroom*, for the consideration of the reader who perhaps has not yet been in this *wedding-chamber*. It may be that he will be desirous to follow us and to enter into the *inner choir*, where the soul joins hands and dances with *Sophia*, or *Divine Wisdom*.

# I.

->*When that which is mentioned above comes to pass, the soul rejoices in its body and says:*<-

> Praise, thanksgiving, strength, honor, and glory be to you, O great God, in your *power* and *sweetness*, because you have redeemed me from the <term>anguish</term> of the <term>fiery driver</term> <note>original: "fiery Driver"; in this mystical context, the "driver" is the harsh, restless, and tormenting force of the ego or the devil</note>. Lead me in the right way. I give myself up to your *love*. I am dark before you; please *enlighten* me. O noble *Love*, give me your <term>sweet pearl</term> <note>original: "sweet Pearl"; a metaphor for the divine spark or the "Pearl of Great Price" mentioned in the Gospels</note>; put it, I pray, into me.

My bones rejoice in your *strength*, and my heart delights in your *love*. Thanks be to you forever, because you have delivered me out of *Hell* and turned *death* into *life in me*. O *sweet Love!* Let me not depart from you again. Grant me your <term>garland of pearl</term> <note>original: "Garland of Pearl"; a symbol of the soul’s restoration and spiritual victory</note> and stay within me.
