## II.

### The Soul says again to its noble Sophia, its Love, who is born again in it,

O my noble Pearl <note>In Böhme’s theology, the "Pearl" represents the divine spark or the kingdom of heaven within the soul.</note>, and opened Flame of *Light* in my anxious fiery *Life*, how you change me into your *Joy*! O beautiful *Love*, I have broken my *Faith* with you in my Father *Adam*, and with my fiery *Strength* have turned myself to the *Pleasure* and *Vanity* of the outward *World*. I have fallen in *Love* with a *Stranger* <note>original: "Stranger"; referring to the worldly or material nature that distracts from the divine.</note>, and would have been forced to walk in the Valley of *Darkness* in this strange *Love*, if you had not come into the House of my *Misery*, in your great Faithfulness, by your piercing through and destroying God’s *Anger*, *Hell*, and dark *Death*, and restored your Meekness and Love to my fiery *Life*.

O sweet *Love*! you have brought the *Water* of eternal *Life* out of the Fountain of God, with you into me, and refreshed me in my great *Thirst*. I behold in you the Mercy of God, which was hidden from me before by the strange *Love*. In you I can rejoice; you change my *Anguish* of *Fire* into great *Joy* in me. O lovely *Love*, give me your Pearl, so that I may continue in this *Joy* forever.

---

### Upon this the noble Sophia answers the Soul again, and says,

MY dear *Love* and faithful *Treasure*, you highly rejoice me in your Beginning. I have indeed broken into you through the deep *Gates* of God, through God’s *Anger*, through *Hell* and *Death*, into the House of your *Misery*, and have graciously bestowed my Love upon you, and delivered you from the Chains and Bonds with which you were fast bound. I have kept my Faith with you, though you have not kept yours with me; but you desire now an exceedingly great Thing of me, which I cannot willingly trust in your Hands. You would have my Pearl as your own property. Remember, I pray, O my beloved *Bridegroom*, that you did carelessly lose it before in *Adam*; and you yourself still stand in great Danger, and walk in two dangerous Kingdoms; for in your original Fire you walk in that Country where God calls himself a *strong jealous God*, and a *consuming Fire*. The other Kingdom which you walk in is the outward *World*, where you dwell in the vain corrupt *Flesh* and Blood, and where the Pleasures of the World and the Assaults of the Devil beset you every Hour. You might perhaps in your great Joy bring *Earthliness* again into my *Beauty*, and thereby darken my *Pearl*; or you might possibly grow proud, as *Lucifer* did, when he had the *Pearl* in his Possession, and so turn yourself away from the *Harmony* of God, as he did, and then I must be deprived of my *Love* forever afterward.

No. I will keep my *Pearl* in myself, and dwell in the Heaven in you, in your extinguished—but now in me revived—*Humanity*; and reserve my *Pearl* for *Paradise*, until you put away this *Earthliness* from you, and then I will give it to you to possess. But I will readily present to you my pleasant Countenance, and the sweet *Rays* of the *Pearl*, during the *Time* of this *Earthly Life*. I will dwell with the *Pearl* itself in the inner Choir <note>The "inner choir" refers to the deepest, most spiritual part of the human soul where the divine resides.</note>, and

# Of True Repentance

...be your faithful, loving Bride. I cannot marry myself to your *earthly flesh*, for I am a *heavenly Queen*, and my *Kingdom* is *not of this world*. Yet I will not throw your outward life away, but will refresh it often with my *rays of love*; for your external human nature shall return again <note>This refers to the Christian belief in the resurrection of the body.</note>. But I cannot admit the *beast of vanity* <note>original: "Beast of Vanity"; referring to the corrupted, ego-driven nature of man after the Fall.</note> into my embraces, nor did God create it in *Adam* with the purpose of having it so coarse and earthly. But in *Adam*, your desire—through the power of its strong lust—formed this beastly coarseness from and with all the *essences* <term>The fundamental spiritual qualities or substances of a being.</term> of the awakened vanity of earthly property, where heat and cold, pain and *enmity*, division and corruption exist.

Now, my dear love and bridegroom, simply surrender yourself to my *will*; I will not forsake you in the dangers of this earthly life. Though the *wrath* of God should pass over you, so that you grow frightened and disheartened, or think that I have deserted you, I will still be with you and preserve you; for you yourself do not know what your *office* <note>original: "Office"; here meaning one's divine duty, role, or purpose in life.</note> is. During this lifetime, you must work and bear *fruit*. You are the *root* of this *Pearl-Tree* <note>A mystical image representing the growth of Christ or Divine Wisdom within the soul.</note>; *branches* must be produced out of you, all of which must be brought forth in *anguish*. But I come forth together with your *branches* in their sap, and produce *fruit* upon your *boughs*, though you do not know it; for the *Most High* has ordered it so, that I should *dwell* with and in you.

Envelop yourself, therefore, in *patience*, and beware of the *pleasures* of the flesh. Break its *will* and *desire*; bridle it like an unruly *horse*; and then I will often visit you in the *fiery essence* <note>original: "fiery Essence"; in the theology of Jacob Böhme, this refers to the soul's energetic, longing nature which must be tempered by light.</note>, and give you my *kiss of love*. I will bring a *garland* for you out of *Paradise* as a token of my affection and put it upon you, and you shall rejoice in it. But I do not give you my *pearl* as a permanent possession during this lifetime. You must continue in *resignation* <term>original: "Resignation" (German: Gelassenheit); a state of total surrender and openness to God's will.</term>, and listen to what the Lord plays on His instrument in the *harmony* within you. Moreover, you must give *sound* and *substance* to your tune, out of my *strength* and *virtue*, for you are now a messenger of *His* Word and must set forth His *praise* and *glory*. For this reason, I have entered into a *new* covenant with you and placed my triumphal garland upon you, which I won in the *battle* against the Devil and Death. But the *crown of pearl* with which I crowned you, I have laid aside for you. You must wear *that* no more until you have become *pure* in my sight.

# III.
## The Soul says further to the noble *Sophia*,

O you beautiful and sweet companion, what shall I say before you? Let me be wholly committed to you, for I cannot preserve myself. If you will not give me your pearl, I submit to your *will*; but give me your *rays of love*, and carry me safely through my pilgrimage. Awaken and bring forth whatever you will in me; from now on, I will be your own. I will or desire nothing for myself, but only what you yourself *will* through me. I had foolishly wasted your sweet *love* and broken my *faith* with you, by which I had fallen into the *wrath of God*. But seeing that out of *love* you came to me into the *anguish of hell* and have delivered me from *torment* and received me again as your *partner*, I will now break my *will* for the sake of your *love*. I will be obedient to you and wait for your *love*. I am satisfied now, knowing that you are with me in all my troubles and will not *forsake* me.

O gracious *love*, I turn my fiery countenance toward you. O beautiful *crown*, take me quickly into you and bring me out of this restlessness: I will be yours forever and never depart from you again.

<summary>Sophia (Divine Wisdom) explains to the Soul that it must remain in a state of patient resignation and earthly labor before it can fully possess the heavenly pearl. The Soul responds with a total surrender of its will, committing to follow Sophia through the trials of earthly life.</summary>

## *The noble Sophia <note>original: "Sophia," representing Divine Wisdom, often personified as the spiritual bride of the soul in mystical Christian traditions.</note> answers the Soul very comfortably, and says,*

My noble Bridegroom, be of good comfort. I have betrothed you to me in my highest Love, and bound myself to you in my faithfulness. *I will be with you and in you always to the end of the world.* I will come to you and make my *abode* with you, in your *inner chamber*. You shall *drink* of my *fountain*; for now I am yours, and you are mine; the *enemy* <note>Referring to the devil or the forces of spiritual darkness.</note> shall not separate us. *Work in your fiery property <note>In the theology of Jacob Böhme, the "fiery property" refers to the soul's essential drive or vital energy.</note>, and I will put my rays of love into your working.* And so we will plant and cultivate <note>original: "manure," which in the 17th century meant to till or work the land by hand.</note> the vineyard of Jesus Christ. Provide the *essence* <note>original: "Essence," meaning the fundamental spiritual substance.</note> of fire, and I will provide the *essence* of light, and the *increase*. Be the *fire*, and I will be the *water*, and thus we will perform in *this world* that for which God has appointed us, and serve him in *his temple*, which we *ourselves are*. Amen.

## To the READER.

BELOVED Reader, do not consider this an *uncertain fiction*; it is the *true ground, sum, and substance* of all the *Holy Scriptures*. For the *Book of the Life of Jesus Christ* is plainly set forth here, as the *author* certainly knows; it being the way that he himself has gone. He gives you the *best jewel* that he has. God grant his *blessing* with it. A heavy sentence and judgment are pronounced against the *mocker* of this. Be therefore warned, so that you may *avoid the danger and obtain the benefit.*

## A MORNING PRAYER,

### *Commending ourselves to God when we rise, before we suffer any other thing to enter into us.*

> BLESS me, O God—the Father, Son, and Holy Spirit—you who are the only true God. I thank you through Jesus Christ our Lord and Savior, for your preservation of me, and for all other benefits. I now commend myself—both soul and body, and all that you have set me to do in my *employment* or *calling*—into your protection. Be the beginning of my *conceptions* <note>original: "Conceptions," meaning the very first thoughts or ideas.</note>, my *undertakings*, and all my *doings*. Work in me so that I may begin all things to the glory of your name, and accomplish them in your love for the good and service of my neighbor. Send your holy angel to go with me, to turn the temptations of the devil and corrupt nature away from me. Preserve me from the malice of evil men, make all my enemies reconciled to me, and bring my mind into your vineyard, so that I may labor in my office and employment, and behave as your obedient servant. Bless me, and all that I am to go about and do this day, with the blessing of your love and mercy. Continue your grace and love in Jesus Christ upon me, and give me a mind cheerfully to follow your guidance <note>original: "Leadings."</note> and execute your appointment. Let your *Holy Spirit* guide me in my beginning and my progress, on to my last end, and be the *willing, working, and accomplishing* of everything in me. Amen.

# TRUE RESIGNATION.

## The First Chapter.

1. <image-desc>Decorative drop cap 'W' set within a square frame featuring an intricate repeating floral or star-like pattern.</image-desc> We have a clear example in *Lucifer*, and also in *Adam* the first man, of what the *self* <note>original: "Self"; here referring to the egoistic will that acts independently of God.</note> does when it acquires the *light of nature* as its own and is allowed to walk with its own *understanding* in its own *dominion*. We see this also in men learned in the *arts* and *sciences*: when they take the *light* of this outward *world* or *nature* into the *possession* of their *reason*, nothing comes of it but *pride in themselves*. And yet, the whole *world* so passionately desires and seeks after this *light* as the *best treasure*. Indeed, it is the *best treasure* this *world* affords, if it is used correctly.

2. But while the *self*—namely, *reason*—is captivated and bound fast in a narrow and strong *prison* (that is to say, in the *anger of God* and in *earthliness*), it is very dangerous for a person to make use of the *light of knowledge in the self*, as if it were their own *possession*.

3. For the *wrath* of both eternal and temporary *nature* will soon take pleasure in it. Then the *self* and a person’s own *reason* will rise up in *pride* and depart from true, resigned *humility* toward God. They will no longer eat of the *fruit of paradise*, but of the *property of the self*—that is, of that *dominion* of life where *good* and *evil* are mixed, just as *Lucifer* and *Adam* did. Both of them, driven by the *desire of the self*, returned to the *origin* from which all *creatures* were brought forth, and back into the [limited] *condition of creatures*. *Lucifer* entered the *center* and *wrathful nature*, into the *matrix* <note>original: "Matrix"; the creative womb or generative source of all things.</note> or *womb* which brings forth *fire*; and *Adam* entered the earthly *nature*, into the *matrix* of the outward *world*—namely, into the *lust* for *good* and *evil*.

4. This happened to them both because they had the *light of understanding* shining within the *self*, through which they could behold *themselves*. Because of this, the *spirit of the self* entered into the *imagination* (specifically, into a *desire* to control the *center*), so that they might exalt themselves in *might*, *power*, and *knowledge*. When *Lucifer* searched for the *mother of fire* <note>In the author's mystical cosmology, the "Mother of Fire" is the raw, foundational energy of existence which becomes a hellish wrath when separated from God's light.</note> in his *center* and thought to reign with it over the *love of God* and all the *angels*; and when *Adam* also desired to experience in his own *essence* <note>original: "Essence"; the fundamental being or substance of a thing.</note> the *mother* or *root* from which *evil* and *good* spring, and intentionally focused his *desire* there to become *knowing* and full of *understanding*: both *Lucifer* and *Adam* were captured by their evil or false *desire in the mother*. They broke away from *resignation* <note>original: "Resignation"; the spiritual practice of surrendering one's personal will to the divine will.</note> which proceeds from God, and so were caught by the *spirit of the will*—by the *desire in the mother*. This *desire* immediately gained *dominion in nature*. Thus, *Lucifer* became stuck fast in the wrathful *source of fire*, and that *fire* became manifest in the *spirit* of his *will*. Through this, the *creature* (Lucifer), in his *desire*, became an *enemy* to the *love* and *meekness* of God.

5. *Adam*, in the same way, was immediately caught by the *earthly mother*, which is both *evil* and *good*, created out of the *love* and *anger* of God, and compacted into one sub- <note>The text ends mid-word; likely "substance."</note>

<summary>This page introduces the concept of spiritual resignation by contrasting it with the "self-will" of Lucifer and Adam, who fell by seeking knowledge and power for themselves rather than remaining humble before God. The author warns that human reason and the "light of nature" can lead to pride and spiritual imprisonment if not properly surrendered to the Divine.</summary>

...substance. Because of this, the earthly *nature* <term>original: "Property"</term> immediately gained the *dominion* over *Adam*. Consequently, *heat* and *cold*, *envy* and *anger*, and all *malice* and *opposition* to God became evident and ruled over him.

6. But if they had not turned the *light* of *knowledge* toward the *self*, then the *mirror* <term>original: "Glass"</term> of the *knowledge* of the *core* <term>original: "Center"</term> and the *origin* of the *creature*—that is, the *power* which it had within *itself*—would not have been revealed. It was from this focus on the self that *imagination* and *lust* arose.

7. We often see today how this same *error* endangers the *enlightened children of God*. When the *sun* of God's holy *presence shines* upon them, their *life* enters a state of *triumph*. *Reason* then looks at itself in that light as if in a *mirror*, and the *will* proceeds into the *self*, conducting its own search. It tries to discover what the *core* is from which the *light shines*, and by its own *motion* and *strength*, it tries to force its way into it. From this arise abominable *pride* and *self-love*. The creature's own *reason*—which is merely a *mirror* or *glass* reflecting *eternal wisdom*—imagines it is greater than it actually is. Then, whatever it does, it thinks God's *will* is doing it through them, and the person believes he is a *prophet*. In reality, he is moved only by *himself* and follows his own *desire*. In this state, the *core of nature* <note>In this context, the "core of nature" refers to the raw, unrefined spiritual forces within a human being.</note> immediately rises up and enters into that *false desire* of the *self* against God; thus the *will* falls into *self-conceit* and *arrogance* <term>original: "Exaltation"</term>.

8. Then the subtle Devil creeps into the *creature* and sifts through the *core* of *nature*, bringing evil or false *desires* into it. A man then becomes, as it were, intoxicated with *self*, yet still persuades himself that he is driven by God. By these means, the *good beginning*—where the *divine light shone* in *nature*—is spoiled, and the *light* of God departs from him.

9. Yet the outward *light* of external *nature* still remains shining in the *creature*; for the *self* throws itself into that light and assumes it is the *primary light* of God; but it is not so. Into this *self-exaltation*, within the *light* of his outward *reason*, the Devil returns (though he was forced to leave during the *first light*, which was *divine*). He returns with a *seven-fold desire*, of which *Christ* spoke, saying: 

> *When the unclean spirit departs out of a man, he wanders through dry places seeking rest, and finds none; and then he takes to himself seven spirits worse than himself, and returns to his first house; and finding it swept and garnished, he dwells therein, and so it is worse with that man than it was before.* <note>A modernization of Matthew 12:43-45.</note>

10. This *house*, which is thus swept and decorated <term>original: "garnished"</term>, is the *light of reason* within the *self*. For if a man directs his *desire* and *will* toward God, refrains from this wicked *life*, and heartily desires the *love of God*, then that *love* will reveal itself to him with a most friendly and cheerful *countenance*. By this, the *outward light* is also kindled. For where the *light of God* is lit, all will be *light*; the Devil cannot stay there but must depart. He then searches through the *mother* of the *origin of life* (the *core*), but it has become a *dry, feeble place*. For the *anger of God* (the *core of nature*) is, in its own *nature*, altogether feeble, *barren*, and dry, and cannot gain *dominion* in its own wrathful *principle*. *Satan* searches through these *places* to find an *open gate* to enter with his *desire*, so that he might sift the *soul* and cause it to exalt itself.

11. And now, if the *spirit* of the *will* of the *creature* throws itself—along with the *light* of *reason*—into the *core* (the *self*) and enters into *self-exaltation*, then it departs again from the *light* of God. Immediately, the Devil finds an *open gate* to enter and a *decorated house* to live in—namely, the *light of reason*. Then he takes for himself the *seven forms* of the *properties of life* within the *self*—those *flatterers* who have turned away from God toward the *self*. He enters there and places his *desire* into the *lust* of the *self* and into evil *imaginations*. In these, the *spirit* of the *will* views itself through the *forms* of the *properties of life* in the outward *light*. Then the man sinks into himself as if he were drunk, and the *stars* lay hold on him and bring their strong *influ-*

[influ]ences into him (into outward *reason*), so that he might seek the **wonders of God there**, so that they may manifest themselves within it. *For all creatures groan and long after God.* And although the stars cannot grasp the *Spirit of God*, yet they would rather have a *house of light* in which they may rejoice than a *house shut up* where they can have no rest.

12. Thus, such a man goes on as if he were drunk in the *light of outward reason* (which is called the *stars*), and grasps great and wonderful things, and has a continual guide within them. And then the devil immediately watches to see if any gate stands open for him, through which he may kindle the *center of life*, so that the *spirit of the will* may mount upward in pride, *self-conceit*, or *covetousness*. From these, *self-arrogance* arises—the *will of reason* desiring to be honored—for he <note>original: "it"; referring to the spirit of the will or the man</note> supposes he has attained the sum of all happiness once he has gained the *light of reason* and can judge the *house of hidden mysteries* that is shut up, which nevertheless God can easily unlock. The deluded man then supposes that he has reached the mark and that honor is due to him because he has gained the *understanding of reason*. He never considers that the devil makes himself merry with his desire in his *seven forms of life of the center of nature* <note>A reference to Boehme's complex mystical system of the "Seven Properties" or forms of nature</note>, nor what abominable error he establishes.

13. From this *understanding of reason*, false *Babel* <note>Babel refers to the biblical tower representing human confusion and prideful religious systems</note> is brought forth in the *Christian Church on Earth*, where men rule and teach by the conclusions of reason. They have set the child—who is drunk in its own pride and *self-desire*—as a beautiful *virgin upon the throne*.

14. But the devil has entered into its *seven forms of life of the center*—that is, into its own *self-conceited reason*—and continually brings his *desire* into this adorned *virgin*, which the *stars* <note>In Boehme’s cosmology, "the stars" often refer to the astral or natural influences on the human mind</note> receive. He is her beast on which she *rides*, well-decorated with her own powers of life, as may be seen in the *Book of Revelation*. Thus, this child of *self* has taken into its possession the outward appearance of *divine holiness* (namely, the *light of reason*) and supposes itself to be the fair child in the house, even though the devil has his lodging within it all the while.

15. And so it is with all those who have been once enlightened by God and afterwards go forth again from *true resignation* <term>the state of yielding one’s will to God</term> and wean themselves from the pure *milk of their mother* (namely, *true humility*).

## The Second Chapter.

1. <image-desc>Decorative initial letter 'H' set within an ornate square frame featuring scrolling floral patterns and vine-like details.</image-desc> **HERE** *reason* will object and say: *Is it not right for a man to attain the light of God, and also the light of outward nature and reason, so that he may be able to order his life wisely, as the Scripture directs?*

2. **Yes, it is very right**; nothing can be more profitable to a man, nor is he capable of anything better; indeed, it is a *treasure above all earthly treasures* for a man to have the **light of God and of time**, for it is the *eye of time and of eternity*.

3. But notice how you ought to use it: when the *light of God* first manifests itself in the soul, it shines forth like light from a *candle* and immediately kindles the *outward light of reason*. Yet it does not yield itself entirely to *reason* so as to be under the dominion of the *outward man*. No, the *outward man* sees himself in this

through-shining *Lustre* <note>original: "Lustre"; meaning brilliance or radiant light</note>, as he does his *Likeness* in a *Looking-Glass*, whereby he immediately learns to know himself, which is good and profitable for him.

4. Now when he does so, *Reason*, which is the <term>creaturely Self</term> <note>The "creaturely self" refers to the ego or the part of a person that identifies only as a created being, separate from God.</note>, cannot do better than to behold itself in the *Self* of the *Creature*, and not enter with the *Will* of the *Desire* into the *Centre* while seeking itself. If it does, it breaks itself off from the *Substance* of God (which rises together with the *Light* of God, of which the *Soul* ought to eat and refresh itself), and instead eats of the outward *Substance* and *Light*, and thereby draws the *Venom* <note>original: "Venom"; here referring to spiritual poison or the corrupting influence of the worldly self</note> into itself again.

5. The *Will* of the *Creature* ought to sink wholly into itself with all its *Reason* and *Desire*, accounting itself an unworthy child that is not at all worthy of this so high a *Grace*. Nor should it claim any *Knowledge* or *Understanding* for itself, or *Desire* of God to have any *Understanding* in its creaturely *Self*; but sincerely and simply sink down into the *Grace* and *Love* of God in *Christ Jesus*. It should desire to be, as it were, dead to itself and its own *Reason* within the *Divine Life*, and wholly resign itself to the *Spirit* of God in *Love*, so that he may do how and what he will with it, as with his own *Instrument*.

6. Its own *Reason* ought not enter into any speculation regarding divine matters or the *Ground* <note>original: "Ground"; meaning the foundation or underlying essence</note> of *human matters*; nor should it will or desire any *Thing* but the *Grace* of God in *Christ*. And just as a *Child* continually longs for the *Breasts* of the *Mother*, so must its *Hunger* be continually entering into the *Love* of God, and not allow itself to be broken off from that *Hunger* by any *Means*. When the outward *Reason* triumphs in the *Light*, saying, "*I have the true Child*" <note>Meaning, when the intellect pridefully believes it has attained spiritual maturity or "captured" the divine.</note>, then the *Will* of the *Desire* must bow itself down to the *Earth*, and bring itself into the deepest *Humility* and most simple *Ignorance*, and say, "*You are foolish, and have nothing but the Grace of God.*" You must wrap yourself up in that *Belief* with great *Humility*, and become nothing at all in yourself, and neither know nor love yourself. All that you have, or is in you, must esteem itself as nothing but a mere *Instrument* of *God*; and you must bring your *Desire* only into *God’s Mercy*, and go forth from all your own knowing and willing; and esteem it as nothing at all, nor ever entertain any *Will* to enter into it again.

7. As soon as this is done, the natural *Will* becomes weak and faint, and then the *Devil* is not able to <term>sift</term> <note>original: "sift"; a biblical reference (Luke 22:31) meaning to test, harass, or shake one's faith.</note> it anymore with his evil *Desire*, for the *Places* of his *Rest* become very *powerless, barren, and dry*. Then the *Holy Spirit* proceeding from *God* takes possession of the <term>Forms of Life</term> <note>In Boehme’s mystical philosophy, the "Forms of Life" are the fundamental spiritual qualities or energies that constitute an individual's existence.</note>, and makes his *Dominion* prevail. He kindles the *Forms of Life* with his *Flames of Love*, and then the high *Knowledge* of the *Centre* of all *Things* arises, according to the inward and outward *Constellation* or *Complexion* <note>original: "Complexion"; meaning the physical and spiritual temperament of the person.</note> of the *Creature*, in a very subtle drying *Fire*, attended with great *Delight*. Thereupon the humbled *Soul* presently desires to sink down into that *Light*, and esteems itself to be nothing, and quite unworthy of it.

8. And thus its own *Desire* pierces into that *nothing*—namely, into that in which God creates—and does what God wills there. The *Spirit of God* springs forth through the *Desire* of the *resigned Humility*, and so the *human Self* immediately follows the *Spirit of God* in *Trembling* and humble *Joy*; and thus it may behold what is in *Time* and *Eternity*, for *All* is present before it.

9. When the *Spirit of God* rises up as a *Fire* and *Flame* of *Love*, then the *Spirit* of the *Soul* descends, and says, "*Lord, Glory be to your Name, not to me; you are able to take to yourself Virtue, Power, Strength, Wisdom, and Knowledge; do as you will, I can do nothing, I know nothing; I will go nowhere but where you lead me as your Instrument; do in me and with me what you will.*"

10. In such an humble and total *Resignation*, the *Spark* of *Divine Power* falls into the *Centre* of the *Forms of Life*, like a *Spark* into *Tinder*, and kindles it—namely, the *Fire* of the *Soul*, which *Adam* caused to be a dark *Coal* in himself, so that it merely glimmers. And when the *Light* of *Divine Power* has kindled itself within it, the *Creature* must go on as

It becomes an instrument of God's Spirit and speaks what the Spirit of God dictates to it; then it is no longer in its own possession but is the instrument of God.

11. But the *will of the soul* must, without ceasing, in this *fiery-driving* <note>original: "fiery-driving"; a term describing the intense, active energy or impulse of the soul’s inner life</note>, sink into nothing—that is, into the *deepest humility in the sight of God*. For as soon as the *will of the soul* engages in its *own speculation or searching* even in the slightest measure, *Lucifer* seizes it in the center of the *forms of life* and sifts it, so that it enters into *Self* <note>original: "Self"; referring to self-centeredness or the ego-driven nature</note>. It must, therefore, remain close to *resigned humility*, as a well stays close to its *spring*, and it must suck and drink from God's fountain and not depart from the ways of God at all.

12. For as soon as the soul feeds on *Self* and on the *light of outward reason*, it follows its own opinion. Then its actions, which it presents as *divine*, come only from the *outward constellation* or the *influence of the stars* <note>original: "outward Constellation"; the idea that human thoughts are being governed by worldly or astrological influences rather than God</note>, which immediately takes hold of the soul and makes it dry. Then the soul wanders into errors until it yields itself up again in resignation. Acknowledging itself anew as a *defiled child*, it resists reason and so regains the love of God. This is harder to do in that case than it was at first; for the Devil now brings in strong doubts and will not easily abandon his *fort of prey*.

13. This may be seen clearly in the saints of God from the beginning of the world. For many who have been moved by the Spirit of God have still often departed from resignation into *Self*—namely, into their own reason and will. In this state, Satan has cast them into sins and into the anger of God, as is shown by *David* and *Solomon*, and also by the patriarchs, prophets, and apostles, who often committed great errors when they departed from resignation into *Self*—that is, *into their own reason and lusts* <term>lusts: here meaning strong worldly desires or selfish cravings</term>.

14. Therefore, it is necessary for the children of God to know how to behave when they wish to learn the way of God. They must subdue and cast away their very thoughts. They should desire nothing and have no will to learn anything unless they find themselves to be in *true resignation*, so that God’s Spirit leads, teaches, and guides the human spirit. The human will, which is attached to itself, must be wholly broken off from its own desires and resigned to God.

15. All speculation into the wonders of God is very dangerous, for the spirit of the will may soon be captivated by it—unless the spirit of the will follows after the Spirit of God. Then it has the power, within *resigned humility*, to behold the wonders of God.

16. I do not say that a person should research and learn nothing in the *natural arts and sciences*. No; such knowledge is useful. But a person must not begin with their own reason alone. One ought not only to govern one’s life by the *light of outward reason*—which is good in itself—but should sink with that light into the *deepest humility* before God. One must set the Spirit and Will of God foremost in all searching, so that the *light of reason* may see and know things through the *light of God*. And though *reason* may be very wise in its own sphere and help a person gain much knowledge, it must not claim such wisdom and knowledge for itself as if they were its own possession. Instead, it must give the glory to God, to whom alone all wisdom and knowledge belong.

17. For the more deeply *reason* sinks itself down into simple humility in the sight of God, and the more unworthy it accounts itself in His sight, the more truly it dies to *self-desire*. Then, the more thoroughly the *Spirit of God* penetrates it and brings it into the highest knowledge, so that at length it may come to behold the great mysteries and wonders of God. For the *Spirit of God* works only in resigned humility—in that which neither seeks nor desires itself. The *Spirit of God* takes hold of whatever desires to be simple and lowly before Him and brings it into His wonders. He takes pleasure only in those who fear and bow themselves before Him.

18. For God has not created us for ourselves alone, but to be instruments of His *wonders*, through which He desires to manifest His wonders. The resigned will trusts—

God, and expects all good from him alone; but Self-Will rules itself, for it is broken off from God. All that Self-Will does is sin, and against God; for it has left that order in which he created it and entered into disobedience, desiring to be its own lord and master.

19. When a person's own will dies to itself, then it is free from sin, for it desires nothing but what God desires for his creature. It desires only to do that for which God has created it, and that which God will do through it. And although the person is and must be the one acting, yet they are but the instrument of the action, by which God does what he wills.

20. For this is true faith in a person: namely, to die to oneself—that is, to one’s own desire. In all their undertakings and designs, they must bring their desire into the will of God, claiming the credit for doing nothing themselves. Instead, they should esteem themselves in all their doings to be but a servant or minister of God, and think that all they do and undertake is for God. For in such a disposition, the Spirit of God leads them into true uprightness and faithfulness towards their neighbor. For such a person thinks to themselves, *I do my work not for myself, but for God, who has called and appointed me to do it; I am but a servant in his vineyard.* They listen continually for the voice of their Master, who commands them from within what they shall do. The Lord speaks in them and bids them do what he would have done by them.

21. But the "Self" does what outward reason—influenced by the stars <note>original: "Stars"; Boehme refers to the astrological or cosmic influences that govern the physical mind and natural world.</note>—commands, and the devil flies into that reason with his own desire. *Whatever the "Self" does is without the will of God, and is done altogether in the fantasy <note>original: "Phantasy"; here meaning a deceptive mental construction or an imagination disconnected from divine truth.</note>, so that the anger of God may play its part through it.*

22. *No work done without the will of God can reach the kingdom of God;* it is all but an unprofitable imagery, or a work created by the self, within this great agitation of mankind. For nothing is pleasing to God except what he himself does through the human will, acting as his instrument. For there is only one God in the Essence of all Essences <note>original: "Essence of all Essences"; the ultimate divine reality from which all things originate.</note>, and all that works with him in that Essence is one spirit with him; but that which works in itself, in its own will, is in itself only, and not in his dominion. It is indeed under that universal dominion of Nature, by which God holds every life (both evil and good) subject to him, but it is not under that special divine government within himself, which includes only the good. *Nothing is divine which does not walk and work in the will of God.*

23. Christ says, *Every plant which my heavenly Father has not planted shall be rooted out and burned in the fire.* <note>Reference to Matthew 15:13.</note> All the works of man, which he has performed without the will of God, shall be burnt up in the final fire and given over to the wrath of God—namely, to the pit of darkness to satisfy itself. For Christ says, *He that is not with me is against me; and he that does not gather with me, scatters.* <note>Reference to Matthew 12:30.</note> Whoever works and does not do it in a <term>resigned will</term> with confidence in God, only causes desolation and scattering; it is not acceptable to God. For nothing is pleasing to him but that which he wills with his Spirit and does through his own instrument.

24. Therefore, whatever is done by the conclusions of the human "Self" in matters of religion is a mere fiction. It is <note>original: "Babel"; a reference to the Tower of Babel, symbolizing human confusion and prideful religious systems built on human reason rather than divine revelation.</note>, and only a work of the stars and of the outward world, not acknowledged by God to be his work. It is only the play of the <term>wrestling wheel of nature</term>, wherein good and evil struggle with one another; what one builds, the other destroys. And this is the great misery of the vain turmoils of men, the outcome of which must be left to the judgment of God.

25. Whoever, therefore, stirs or labors much in such turmoils, works only for the judgment of God; for not one bit of it is perfect and permanent. It must all be separated in the <term>putrefaction</term>. For that which is wrought in the anger of God will be received by that anger, and kept in the mystery of its desire until the day of God's judgment, when evil and good shall be severed.

## The Third Chapter.

<image-desc>Ornate woodcut initial 'W' with floral and vine patterns.</image-desc>

1. Whoever, therefore, intends to do any good and perfect work, in which he hopes to rejoice eternally, let him depart from *himself*—that is, <note>original: "viz."</note> from his own desire—and enter into resignation <note>original: "Resignation"; in the author's mystical context, this refers to 'Gelassenheit' or the total yielding of the self-will to God's will</note>, into the will of God, and work with God. And then, even though the earthly desire of *self* in flesh and blood clings to him, if the will of the soul does not receive that desire into itself, *self* cannot perform any work. For the resigned will continually destroys the substance of *self* again, so that the anger of God cannot reach it. And if it should happen to reach it sometimes, as may be the case, the resigned will prevails with its superior power. Then, it bears the form of a victorious work among the wonders and may inherit *filiation* <term>filiation: the state of being a child of God; sonship</term> or childship. Therefore, it is not good to speak or do anything when reason is inflamed in and by the desire of *self*. Because that desire springs from and works within the anger of God, through which a person would suffer loss. For his work is brought into that anger and kept there until the great day of *God's* judgment.

2. Every evil or false desire, by which a man devises how to craftily gather much worldly gain for himself from his neighbor to his neighbor’s harm, is taken into the anger of God and belongs to the judgment. There, *all things shall be made manifest*, and every power and essence, every cause and effect, both in good and evil, shall be presented to everyone in the mystery of the *Revelation*.

3. *All evil works, done on purpose, belong to the judgment of God.* But he who turns away from that will escapes their power, and those works of his belong to the fire. *All things shall and must be made manifest in the end.* For this reason, God brought his working power into essence <term>essence: the underlying substance or reality of a thing</term> or substance, so that his love and anger might be made manifest and become a representation of his deeds of wonder, for his glory.

4. And every creature ought to know that it should continue in the condition in which it was created; otherwise, it runs in opposition and enmity to the will of God and brings itself into pain. For every intelligent creature that has lost its place or state in which God first created it is in disorder and misery until it recovers it. A creature that is created out of darkness has no pain in the darkness, just as a venomous serpent has no pain from its venom. The venom is its life; but if it should lose its venom and have some good thing brought into it instead, and have that manifest in its essence, that would be pain and death to it. Thus, good is torment to a being whose nature is evil, and evil is likewise pain and death to the good.

5. Man was created from, for, and in *Paradise*; from, for, and in the love of God. But if he brings himself into anger, which is like a poisonous pain and death, then that opposite paradisical life of *love* is a pain and torment to him.

6. If the devil had been created out of the wrathful matrix <term>matrix: the source or environment in which something originates or develops</term>, for and in hell, and had not possessed the divine *ens* <note>original: "Ens"; a Latin term for 'being' or 'essence'</note> or essence, he could have no pain in hell. But because he was created for and in heaven, and yet stirred up the source or property of darkness within...

...himself, and thereby brought himself totally into darkness; therefore, the Light is now a pain to him. That is, it causes an everlasting despair of God’s grace and a continual enmity toward God, because God cannot endure him within Himself but has cast him out. Therefore, the Devil is angry and wrathful against *his own Mother* <note>original: "his own Mother" — referring to the "Eternal Nature" or the foundational matrix from which all spirits are born</note>, from whose essence and substance he has his origin—namely, the *Eternal Nature*, which keeps him prisoner in his own place as a revolter or fallen spirit, and sports within him with its property of anger. And since he would not perform his part in promoting the divine joy for which he was created, he must now do the contrary and be an enemy to all goodness. For *all things are of God and in Him: darkness and light, love and anger, fire and light*; but He calls Himself "God" only regarding the light of His love.

7. There is an eternal opposition <note>original: "Contrariety"</note> between darkness and light; neither of them comprehends the other, and neither of them is the other. Yet there is only one essence, being, or substance in which they both subsist. But there is a difference in quality and will; yet the essence or substance is not divided—rather, a "Principle" <note>Boehme uses "Principle" to describe a distinct realm of existence or state of being, such as the world of light versus the world of darkness</note> makes the division. So the one is a *nothing* in the other, and yet it is there, but not manifest in the property of that thing in which it exists.

8. For the Devil remained in his own dominion or principality—not indeed in that where God created him, but in the aching, painful birth of eternity, in the center of nature and the property of wrath, in the property which begets darkness, anguish, and pain. Indeed, he is a prince in the space of this world, but in the "first principle," in the kingdom of darkness, in the pit or abyss.

9. Not in the kingdom of the sun, stars, and elements; he is no lord or prince there, but in the wrathful part—namely, in the root of evil in every thing. And yet, he does not have the power to do whatever he pleases with that.

10. For there is some good in every thing, which holds the evil captive and shut up within it. But he can walk and rule only in the evil part or property when it stirs up an evil desire in itself and brings its desire into wickedness. Inanimate creatures cannot do this; but man can do it through the inanimate creature if he brings the center of his will, with its desire, out of the eternal center into it. This is the basis of enchantment and false magic. The will of the Devil can also enter into that evil where man brings the desire of his soul, which is also born out of the Eternal Nature.

11. For the origin of the soul and of angels from the Eternal Nature is the same. But the Devil has no further power over time, or the temporary condition of this world, than in the great *Turba*, or *Turba magna* <note>Latin: "Great Disturbance" – in Boehme's philosophy, this refers to the "curse" or the destructive element within nature that leads to chaos and death</note>, the curse. Wherever that kindles itself in eternal and temporal wrath, there he is busy—as in wars, fighting, and strife, as well as in great storms without rain. In fire, he proceeds as far as the *Turba* (mischief or hurt) goes in great showers or tempests of thunder, lightning, and hail; but he cannot direct them, for he is not lord or master in them, but a servant only.

12. Thus the creature stirs up, through its desire, good and evil, life and death. The human or angelic desire stands in the center of the eternal nature which is without beginning; and whatever it kindles itself in—whether in good or evil—it accomplishes its work in that.

13. Now God created everything for and in the place where it should be: the angels for and in Heaven, and man for and in Paradise. If, therefore, the desire of the creature goes forth from its own "mother," then it enters into the contrary will and into enmity; it is tormented with the opposition there, and so a false will arises within a good one. Then the good will enters into its "nothing" again—namely, into the end of nature and the creature—and so leaves the creature in its own evil or wickedness, as appears by *Lucifer* and also by *Adam*. ### Chap. 3. Of True Resignation.

With *Adam*, and of mere mercy entered into humanity or human nature again, there could be no good will in man.

14. Therefore, all speculation and inquiry about God's will is a vain thing unless the mind is converted. For when the mind stands held captive in the self-desire of the earthly life, it cannot comprehend what the will of God is; it runs only within the "self," moving from one way into another, and yet finds no rest; for self-desire always brings disquiet. But when it sinks itself wholly into the mercy of God—desiring to die to itself and to have God's will for a guide to the understanding, so that it acknowledges and esteems itself as nothing and wills nothing but what God wills—then it shall both know and do the will of God. And if the desire of anger in the earthly flesh should go along with or join the Devil’s imagination and assault the will of the soul, yet the resigned desire cries to God and says, *Abba, loving Father, deliver me from evil*. And then, though the earthly will should grow too strong in the wrath of God through the infection of the Devil, the desire of anger would work only in or upon itself. This is according to what St. Paul says: *Now if I sin, I do it not, but sin that dwells in my flesh*; also, *Now I serve the law of God in my mind, but in my flesh the law of sin*. Paul does not mean that the will of the mind or soul should consent to the will of the flesh; rather, sin is so strong in the flesh—namely, the awakened anger of God in "self"—that the mind is often brought into lust as if by force, through the evil incitements of the wicked or by beholding worldly pomp and glory. In these cases, it absolutely bears down the resigned will and rules by force.

15. Now when sin is performed in the flesh, then wrath indulges itself <note>original: "sporteth itself"</note> with it and catches at the resigned will. Then the resigned will cries to God for deliverance from the evil and prays that God would remove the guilt away from it and bring sin into the center—namely, into death—so that it might die.

16. And St. Paul says further, *Now there is no condemnation to those that are in Christ Jesus, who are called according to the purpose of God*. That is, those who are called again in that same purpose of God in which he first called man, to stand once more in that purpose of God wherein he originally created man to be his image and likeness.

17. So long as man's own will stands in "self," it is not in the purpose and calling of God. It is not "called," for it has gone out from its original right place. But when the mind turns itself back again into the calling—namely, into resignation <note>The act of surrendering one's own will to God</note>—then the will is in the calling of God. That is, it is in the place for which and in which God created it, and then it has power to become the child of God again, as it is written: *He has given us power to become the children of God*.

18. The power which he has given us is his purpose, for which and in which he created man in his image. God has brought this back into human nature and has given power to that power to break the head of sin in the flesh—namely, the will and desire of the serpent. That is, the resigned will in Christ treads upon the head of the desire of the sinful will of the serpent <note>A reference to the biblical promise in Genesis 3:15</note> and kills again the sins which were committed. This power that is given becomes a death to death and the power of life to life.

19. Therefore no one can make any excuse, as if they could not choose <note>original: "will"</note>. Indeed, while someone sticks fast in themselves, in their own desire, and serves only the law of sin in the flesh, they cannot. For they are kept back as a servant of sin. But when they turn the center of their mind away and direct it into the will and obedience of God, then they can.

<margin>Note: The following point about the mind’s origin in eternity is vital.</margin>
20. Now the center of the mind has come out of eternity, out of God's omnipotence; it can bring itself into whatever it wills and wherever it wills. *For that which is out of the eternal has no law.* But the will has a law to obey God and is born out of the mind; it must not tear itself away from that out of which God created it.

21. Now God created the will of the mind for and in Paradise, to be a companion with him in the kingdom of divine joy. It ought not to have removed itself from there; but since it has removed itself, God has brought his will back into the human flesh. In his newly restored will, he has given us the power to bring our own wills into it, to kindle a new light there, and so become his children once again.

22. God hardens no one; rather, a person's own will, which persists in the carnal life of sin, hardens their own heart. The self-centered will brings the vanity of this world into the mind, which is consequently shut up and remains in that state.

23. God—insofar as he is called God and is God—cannot will any evil; for there is only one single will in God, and that is eternal love. It is a desire for that which is like himself: namely power, beauty, and virtue.

24. God desires nothing except what is like his own desire; his desire receives nothing except what it already is.

25. God receives no sinner into his power and virtue unless the sinner leaves their sins and enters into God with their desire. And then, *he will not cast out those who come to him in this way.* He has given the will an open gate in Christ, saying, *“Come to me, all you who are heavily burdened with sins, and I will refresh you; take my yoke upon you”*—that is, the cross of the hostility in the flesh <note>original: "Enmity in the Flesh," referring to the struggle between one's spiritual desires and physical impulses.</note>. This was the yoke of Christ, which he had to bear for the sins of all people. The resigned <note>term: "resigned" (original: resigned) here means a will that has surrendered itself entirely to God's purpose.</note> will must also take this cross or yoke upon itself in the evil, earthly, sinful flesh, and follow Christ in patience and the hope of deliverance. It must also continually "break the head of the serpent" <note>This is a biblical reference to Genesis 3:15, meaning to defeat the power of the devil or sin.</note> in and through Christ’s will and spirit. It must kill and destroy the earthly will through God's righteous anger, not letting it rest on a "soft bed" when sin is committed by thinking one will repent at some other time.

26. No, the earthly will grows strong, fat, and unruly upon this "soft bed" of procrastination. As soon as the light of God shines in you and reveals your sin to you, the will of your soul must sink itself down into the suffering and death of Christ and wrap itself up closely within it. It must take the passion of Christ as its own possession; it must become a master over the death of sin through the death of Christ, killing and destroying sin by that same death.

27. The sinful will must die, no matter how unwilling it may be. Therefore, be at odds with the pleasure-seeking earthly flesh; do not give it what it wants. Let it fast and suffer hunger until its cravings cease. Treat the will of the flesh as your enemy and do not do what the carnal desire wants; in doing so, you shall bring death upon the *death-filled nature* in the flesh.

28. Do not worry about the scorn of the world, considering that the world only scorns your enemy—the carnal self—which has become a fool to the world. Indeed, you should account that self as your own fool, which Adam caused you to possess and made to be your false heir. *Cast out the son of the bondwoman from the house—that strange child which God did not intend to be in the house of life in Adam at the beginning; for the son of the bondwoman must not inherit with the son of the free woman.* <note>original: "Bond-Woman" and "Free-Woman." This is an allegory from Galatians 4, where the "son of the bondwoman" (Ishmael) represents the natural, carnal man, and the "son of the free woman" (Isaac) represents the spiritual man born of God’s promise.</note>

29. The earthly will *is merely the son of the bondwoman.* The four elements <note>The classic elements: earth, air, fire, and water, believed to compose the physical body.</note> should have been man’s servants, but Adam brought them into "sonship"—adopting them into his very being. Therefore God said to Abraham, when he had opened the covenant of the promise in him: *“Cast out the son of the bondwoman, for he shall not inherit with the son of the free.”* This *son of the free* is Christ, whom God in his grace has brought back into the flesh for us—namely, a new or renewed mind. In this mind, the eternal will of the soul may draw and drink the *water of life* of which Christ speaks, saying, *“Whoever drinks of the water that I will give him, it shall spring up in him and be a fountain of eternal life.”* This fountain is the renovation of the mind or the will of the soul.

<summary>This page argues that humans must surrender their "earthly will" and carnal desires to align with God's "eternal love." Using the biblical allegory of Hagar and Sarah, it explains that the physical, sinful nature (the son of the bondwoman) must be cast out so the spiritual nature (the son of the free woman, or Christ) can inherit eternal life.</summary>

->Of True Resignation.<-

## Chap. 3.

30. Therefore I say that all fictions and devices used to reach God—whatever name they may be given—which men invent as ways to God, are nothing but lost labor and empty efforts without a new mind. There is no other way to God but a new mind, which turns away from wickedness and enters into repentance for the sins it has committed. This mind moves away from its iniquity and desires it no more; instead, it wraps its will up in the death of Christ. With all earnestness, it dies to the sin of the soul through the death of Christ, so that it no longer wills to sin.

31. And even though all the devils should press hard upon it and enter the fleshly mind with their desires, the will of the soul must stand still and hide itself in the death of Christ, willing and desiring nothing but the mercy of God.

32. No hypocritical flattery or outward comforting of ourselves is of any use. This happens when men try to cover the sin and iniquity of the flesh with the "satisfaction" <note>original: "satisfaction of Christ"; the theological concept that Christ's death paid the debt for human sin.</note> of Christ while remaining in their "Self" <note>In Böhme’s writing, "Self" refers to the ego or the fallen, unregenerate nature that acts independently of God.</note> still. Christ says, *Unless you turn and become as little children, you shall not see the kingdom of God.* The mind must become entirely new, like a child that knows nothing of sin. Christ also says, *You must be born again, or else you shall not see the kingdom of God.* A completely new will must arise in the death of Christ. It must be brought forth out of Christ’s incarnation (his entering into humanity) and rise in Christ’s resurrection.

33. Now, before this can be done, the will of the soul must die in the death of Christ. For through *Adam*, the soul received the *son of the bond-woman* <note>original: "Son of the Bond-Woman"; a biblical reference to Ishmael (Galatians 4), symbolizing the natural, earthly, and enslaved state of humanity before spiritual rebirth.</note>—namely, sin—into itself. The will must cast this out. The poor, captive soul must earnestly wrap itself in the death of Christ with all the power it has, so that the *son of the bond-woman*—the sin within it—may die in Christ's death.

34. In truth, sin must die in the will of the soul, or else there can be no vision of God. For the earthly will, existing in sin and a wrathful nature, shall not see God. It is the regenerated nature only that is capable of divine vision or enjoyment. The soul must put on the spirit and flesh of Christ; it cannot inherit the kingdom of God in this "earthly tabernacle" <note>A biblical metaphor for the physical body.</note>. For the kingdom of sin clings to the body outwardly; it must decay in the earth and rise again in new power.

35. Hypocrisy, flattery, and merely verbal forgiveness achieve nothing. We must be children, not by "outward imputation" <note>original: "outward Imputation"; the legalistic idea that God simply "counts" a person as righteous without changing their inner nature.</note>, but by being born of God from within, in the *new man* who is resigned in and to God.

36. All such flattering of ourselves—saying, "*Christ has paid the ransom and made satisfaction for sin, and he died for our sins*"—is a false and empty comfort if we do not also die to sin in him, put on his merit through new obedience, and live within it.

37. He who is a bitter enemy and hater of sin can and may comfort himself with the sufferings of Christ. He who does not willingly see, hear, or taste sin, but is at enmity with it and would always willingly do what is good and right if he only knew what he ought to do—such a person has indeed put on the spirit and will of Christ and is his true disciple.

38. But the outward flattery of being considered a child of God by imputation or external application is false and vain. Work done in or by the outward flesh alone does not make one a child of God; rather, the working of Christ in the spirit makes, and indeed is, the child of God. This inward working is so powerful that it shines forth as a new light in the outward life, proving itself to be the child of God through its external conduct and actions.

39. For if the eye of the soul is light, then the whole body is light in all its members. Now, if anyone boasts that he is a child of God and yet allows his body to burn in sin, he is no true child, nor is he capable of the inheritance. Instead, he lies bound by the chains of the devil in gross darkness. And if he does not find in himself an earnest and sincere desire to do well in love, then his claim to be a child of God is but an...

<summary>Böhme argues that salvation requires an internal transformation and the actual death of the sinful will, rather than a mere intellectual or "imputed" belief in Christ's atonement. He emphasizes that true faith must be visible through a person's conduct and a genuine hatred of sin.</summary>

### Of True Resignation. Chap. 3.

...invention of reason proceeding from **Self**. He cannot see God unless he be born anew, and show forth by his power and life that he is His true child. For there is no fire that does not have light in it; and if the divine fire is in the mind, it will shine forth, and the mind will do that which God wants to be done.

40. But perhaps you will say, *“I truly have a will to do so; I would willingly do it, but I am so hindered that I cannot.”*

41. No, you wretched man! God draws you to be His child, but you will not; the comfort <note>original: "soft Cushion"</note> of evil is dearer to you than to be so readily given up. You prefer the joy of wickedness to the joy of God. You are still wholly swallowed up in **Self** and live according to the law of sin, and that hinders you. You are unwilling to die to the pleasures of the flesh, and therefore you are not in **filiation** <term>filiation: the state of being a child of God; sonship</term>. God draws you to it, but you yourself are unwilling.

42. Oh, how fine a thing **Adam** would think it if he might be taken into heaven with this will of the pleasure-seeking flesh still about him, and have the "child of wickedness"—which is full of deceit—seated upon the throne of God! **Lucifer** also would have gladly had it so, but he was spewed out.

43. It is a troublesome thing to mortify <note>original: "mortify," meaning to put to death or subdue through discipline</note> the evil will; no one is willing to do it. We would all gladly be the children of God if we could be so while wearing this rough garment of fallen nature. But that cannot be. This world passes away, and the outward life must die; what good can "adoption" do me if it is only in the mortal body of flesh and blood?

44. If we would inherit **filiation**, we must also put on the **new man** who can inherit it, being like the Deity. God will have no sinners in heaven, but only those who are born anew and become children, and so have "put on" heaven.

45. Therefore, it is not as easy a matter to become a child of God as people imagine. Indeed, it is not a troublesome thing to one who has achieved **filiation**, whose light shines; for it is a joy to such a person. But to turn the mind and destroy **Self**, a strong and continued earnestness is required, and such a stout and steady purpose that even if the body and soul should be torn apart by it, the will would persevere constantly and not enter into **Self** again.

46. A man must wrestle until the dark center that is shut up tight breaks open, and the spark lying hidden within kindles. From there the noble **Lily-branch** <note>a recurring symbol in Boehme's work representing the growth of the reborn soul</note> sprouts, as from the **divine grain of mustard seed**, as Christ says. A man must pray earnestly, with great humility, and for a while become a "fool" in his own reason, seeing himself as void of understanding, until Christ is formed in this new incarnation.

47. And then, when Christ is born, **Herod** is ready to kill the child—which he seeks to do outwardly through persecutions and inwardly through temptations—to test whether this **Lily-branch** will be strong enough to destroy the kingdom of the Devil, which is manifested in the flesh.

48. Then this "Destroyer of the Serpent" is brought into the wilderness, after he is baptized with the Holy Spirit, and is tempted and tried to see whether or not he will continue in resignation to the will of God. In this temptation he must stand so fast that, if necessary, he would leave all earthly things and even his outward life to be a child of God.

<note>The following paragraph is numbered 48 in the original text, repeating the previous number.</note>

48. No temporary honor must be preferred before **filiation**. Instead, he must with his will leave and forsake it all, not accounting it his own, but esteeming himself only as a servant in it who is to obey his Master. He must leave all worldly property <note>original: "Propriety"</note>. We do not mean that he may not have or possess anything; but his heart must forsake it, and not bring his will into it, nor count it his own. For if he sets his heart upon it, he has no power to use it to serve those who are in need.

50. **Self** is merely a slave to its temporary possessions, but **Resignation** rules over all that it has. **Self** must do what the Devil wants it to do in fleshly pleasure and pride of...

# Chapter 3: Of True Resignation

Life; but *Resignation* tramples it all under the feet of the mind. *Self* despises that which is *lowly* and *simple*; but *Resignation* sits down with the lowly in the dust. It says, *"I will be simple in myself, and understand nothing, lest my understanding should exalt itself and sin. I will lie down in the courts of my God at his feet, that I may serve my Lord in whatever he commands me. I will know nothing of my own accord, so that the will and power of my Lord may lead and guide me, and that I may only do what God does through me, and wants done by me. I will rest in myself until the Lord awakens me with his Spirit; and if he will not, then I will look up to him in silence, and wait for his commands."*

51. Beloved Brethren: People at this time boast much of faith; but where is it to be found? Modern faith is nothing more than a historical record <note>original: "the History"; Boehme distinguishes between "historical faith"—an intellectual belief in the facts of the Bible—and a living, transformative faith</note>. Where is that child of God who believes that Jesus is born? If that child were in existence, and did believe that Jesus is born, he would also draw near to the sweet child Jesus, and receive him and nurse him.

52. Alas! The faith of this day is merely historical—a simple agreement with the facts that Jesus Christ lived and died; that the *Jews* killed him; that he left this world, and is not a king on Earth in a physical sense. People believe they may do as they please, and do not need to die to sin and their evil lusts. All this the wicked child *Self* rejoices in, so that it may fatten the Devil by living in luxury.

53. This shows plainly that true faith was never weaker since Christ's time than it is now. Even so, the world cries aloud and says, *"We have the true faith,"* and they argue about the "Child" with a bitterness that has never been worse since humanity was on Earth.

54. If you are truly *Zion* <note>Zion: here representing the true, spiritual church or the soul in a state of grace</note>, and have found that newborn child who was lost and is found again, then let it be seen in power and virtue <note>original: "Virtue"; here meaning spiritual efficacy or moral power</note>. Let us all openly see the sweet child Jesus brought forth by you, and see that you are his nurse. If not, then the children in Christ will say that you have found nothing but the child's cradle—that is, the historical account.

55. Where do you keep the sweet child Jesus, you who are so puffed up with the history and with your false and outward faith? Oh, how the child Jesus will visit you one day in the Father's essence—the essence of anger—in your own *Turba* <term>Turba: a term used by Jacob Boehme to describe a state of spiritual "turmoil" or "disturbance," specifically the awakening of divine wrath within a soul that has rejected God's love</term> which you have fattened! He calls you now in love, but you will not hear, for your ears are stopped with greed and sensual pleasure. Therefore, the sound of the trumpet shall one day alarm you with the harsh thunderclap of your *Turba*, and rouse you up, if perhaps you will then seek and find the sweet child Jesus.

56. Beloved brethren, this is a time of seeking—of seeking and of finding. It is a time of great earnestness; whoever it touches, it touches deeply. He who watches shall hear and see it; but he who sleeps in sin, and says in the self-satisfied days of his gluttony, *"All is peace and quiet, we hear no sound from the Lord,"* shall be blind. But the voice of the Lord has sounded to all the ends of the earth, and a smoke rises, and in the midst of the smoke there is a great brightness and splendor. *Hallelujah. Amen.*

### THE
# AUTHOR'S PREFACE
### TO THE
# READER

*Although I have in my other writings set down a clear description of regeneration <term>regeneration: the spiritual "New Birth" or the process of being spiritually reborn</term>, or the New Birth, from its very foundation; yet because not everyone possesses those books, nor does everyone have the capacity to understand them, I have therefore—as a service to the simple children of Christ—set down here a short summary concerning the New Birth.*

*But if anyone desires to search the deep foundation from which everything flows, and has the gift to understand it, let them read:*

I. *The Three Principles of the Divine Essence.*

II. *The Threefold Life of Man.*

III. *The Forty Questions of the Original Essence, Substance, Nature, and Property of the Soul.*

IV. *The Incarnation and Birth of Jesus Christ the Son of God; also of his suffering, death, and resurrection.*

V. *The Six Points treating of the Three Worlds—how they exist within one another as one, and yet create three principles (namely, three births or centers).*

VI. *The Mysterium Magnum <note>original: Mysterium Magnum; "The Great Mystery"</note>, which is an interpretation of the book of Genesis.*

*In these works, the reader shall find everything they could ask, reaching as deep as the mind of man is able to reach. I have written this for the true Israelites <note>Israelites: used here figuratively to mean the spiritually faithful or the "chosen" seekers of truth</note>—that is, for the hungry and thirsty hearts that long for the fountain of Christ, who are my fellow members in the Spirit of Christ. But I have not written this for the Ishmaelites <note>Ishmaelites: a biblical reference used here to describe mockers or those who reject the spiritual inheritance</note> and mockers; for they have a "book" within themselves with which they vex, persecute, and suppress the children of Christ who live "under the cross" <note>under the cross: a theological phrase referring to believers who undergo suffering or persecution for their faith</note>. And yet, though it is unwillingly and unknowingly to themselves, they must be servants to such children of Christ.*

# OF
# REGENERATION.

---

## The First Chapter.
### *Showing how Man should consider himself.*

1. **C**hrist said, "Unless you turn and become like children, you shall not see the Kingdom of God." Again, he said to Nicodemus, "Unless a man is born again, of water and of the Spirit, he cannot enter into the Kingdom of God; for that which is born of the flesh is flesh, and that which is born of the Spirit is spirit."

2. Also, the Scripture positively declares that the fleshly, natural man <note>original: "fleshly natural Man"; refers to the unregenerate person driven by physical instincts rather than spiritual awareness.</note> does not receive the things of the Spirit of God, for they are foolishness to him; neither can he know or understand them.

3. Now, since we all have flesh and blood and are mortal—as we know by experience—and yet the Scripture says that *we are the temples of the Holy Spirit, who dwells in us,* and that *the Kingdom of God is within us,* and that *Christ must be formed in us*; also, that *He will give us his flesh for food, and his blood for drink:* And that, *whoever shall not eat of the flesh of the Son of Man, and drink his blood, has no life in him.* Therefore, we should seriously consider what kind of person within us is capable of being like the Deity in this way.

4. For it cannot be said of the mortal flesh—which turns to earth again, lives in the vanity of this world, and continually lusts against God—that it is the temple of the Holy Spirit. Much less can it be said that the <term>New Birth</term> <note>original: "New-Birth"; the spiritual transformation or regeneration of the soul.</note> happens in this earthly flesh, which dies and decays, and is a constant house of sin.

5. Yet, since it remains certain that a true Christian is born of Christ, and that the New Birth is the temple of the Holy Spirit which dwells in us, and that only the "New Man" who is born of Christ partakes of the flesh and blood of Christ; it appears that being a Christian is not such an easy matter.

6. And Christianity does not consist in the mere knowing of the history, and applying that knowledge to ourselves, saying that *Christ died for us, and has destroyed death and turned it into life in us, and that he has paid the ransom for us, so that we need do nothing but comfort ourselves with that, and steadfastly believe that it is so.* <note>The author is arguing against "historical faith"—a belief that relies only on acknowledging facts without experiencing an internal change.</note>

7. For we find within ourselves that sin is living, lusting, strong, and powerfully working in the flesh. Therefore, there must be something else—which does not cooperate with sin in the flesh, nor desire it—that constitutes the New Birth in Christ.

8. For St. Paul says, *There is no condemnation to those who are in Christ Jesus.* And further, *Should we who are Christians still be sinners? God forbid, since we are dead to sin in Christ.*

<summary>The author introduces the concept of spiritual regeneration, arguing that true Christianity requires a literal "New Birth" of the spirit rather than a mere intellectual belief or "historical" faith. He distinguishes between the mortal, sinful flesh and the spiritual "New Man" who serves as the temple of the Holy Spirit.</summary>
<keywords>Regeneration, New Birth, Holy Spirit, Flesh vs Spirit, Nicodemus, St. Paul, Historical Faith, Indwelling of Christ</keywords>
