## *Of Regeneration.* Chapter 1.

9. Besides, the <term>Man of Sin</term><note>original: "Man of Sin"; a biblical reference to the embodiment of lawlessness, used here to represent unregenerate human nature.</note> cannot be the Temple of the Holy Spirit; and yet *there is no man who does not sin, for God has shut up all under sin.* As the Scripture says, *No one living is righteous in Your sight, if You <term>impute</term><note>original: "imputest"; to attribute or credit a quality (like sin or righteousness) to someone.</note> his sins to him. The righteous man falls seven times a day;* and yet it cannot mean that the righteous part falls and sins, but rather his mortal and sinful nature. For the righteousness of a Christian in Christ cannot sin.

10. Moreover, *St. Paul* says, *Our <term>citizenship</term><note>original: "Conversation"; in the 17th century, this word referred to one's conduct, way of life, or citizenship.</note> is in heaven, from where we await our Savior Jesus Christ.* Now, if our citizenship is in heaven, then heaven must be in us; Christ dwells in heaven; and so if we are His temple, that heavenly temple must be in us.

11. But despite all this, since sin tempts us from within (by which the Devil has access to us), hell must also be in us too. For the Devil dwells in hell; wherever he is, he is in hell and cannot come out of it. Indeed, when he possesses a man, he dwells in hell—namely, in the anger of God within that man.

12. Therefore we ought to consider well what man is, and how he is a man. Then we shall find that a true Christian is not a mere <note>original: "historical *new Man*"; someone who has only an intellectual or "historical" knowledge of Christ without undergoing a spiritual transformation.</note> **historical new man**, as if it were enough for us to outwardly confess Christ and believe that He is the Son of God and has paid the ransom for us. For righteousness is worth nothing if it is only <term>imputed</term><note>To be "imputed" means to be legally credited with righteousness from the outside.</note> from the outside—that is, by only believing that it is so credited. Rather, it is an inherent righteousness born within us, by which we become the children of God, that matters.

13. And just as the earthly flesh must die, so also the life and will must die to sin and become like a child that knows nothing, but longs only for the mother who gave birth to it. In the same way, the will of a Christian must enter again into its mother—namely, into the Spirit of Christ—and become a child in its own will and power, having its will and desire inclined and directed only toward its mother. And a new will and obedience in righteousness, which wills sin no more, must rise from death out of the Spirit of Christ within him.

14. For that will is not born anew which still desires and admits vanity into itself; and yet there remains a will which longs for vanity and sins, even in the **new-born** or **regenerated man**. Therefore the image or nature of man should be well understood, and how the **New Birth** comes to pass. For it is not created in the mortal flesh, and yet it is created truly and really in us—in flesh and blood, in water and spirit, as the Scripture says.

15. We should therefore rightly understand what kind of man it is in us who is the member of Christ and the temple of God who dwells in heaven. And then also what kind of man it is that the Devil rules and drives; for he cannot meddle with the temple of Christ, nor does he care much for the mortal flesh. And yet there are not *three* separate men inside one another, for they all make up but *one* man.

16. Now if we want to understand this rightly, we must consider time and eternity, and how they are within one another; also light and darkness, good and evil; but especially the origin of man.

->*This may be understood in this way.*<-

17. THE outward world with the stars and four elements, in which man and all creatures live, neither is, nor is called, God. Indeed, God dwells in it, but the substance of the outward world does not contain Him.

18. We see also that the light shines in darkness, and the darkness does not understand the light, and yet they both dwell in one another. The four elements are also an example of this, which in their origin are but *one* element, which is neither hot nor...

He distinguishes between the "historical" Christian and the truly "born again" Christian who possesses inherent righteousness through the Spirit of Christ.</summary>

# Of Regeneration.
## Chap. I.

[Neither] cold, nor dry, nor moist; and yet by its stirring, it separates itself into Four Properties: fire, air, water, and earth.

19. Who would believe that fire produces or generates water? Or that the origin of fire could be found in water, if we did not see it with our own eyes in storms of thunder, lightning, and rain? We also find that in living creatures, the essential fire of the body lives in the blood; the blood is the mother of the fire, and the fire is the father of the blood.

20. Just as God dwells in the world and fills all things, yet possesses <note>In this context, "possesses" means to be limited by or to take ownership of in a way that changes the original nature.</note> nothing; and just as fire dwells in water yet does not possess it; and as light dwells in darkness yet does not possess the darkness; as day is in the night and night is in the day, time in eternity and eternity in time; so is man created according to his outward humanity. He is time and exists *within* time, and time is the outward world, which is also the outward man.

21. The inward man is eternity—the spiritual time and world. This also consists of light and darkness: the love of God acting as the eternal light, and the anger of God acting as the eternal darkness. Whichever of these is manifest within him, his spirit dwells in that, whether it be darkness or light.

22. For light and darkness are both *within* him, but each of them dwells in itself, and neither of them possesses the other. However, if one enters into the other and tries to possess it, then the other loses its right and power.

23. The *passive* element loses its power; for if the light is made manifest in the darkness, then the darkness loses its "darkness" and is not known or perceived. Conversely, if darkness arises in the light and gains the upper hand, then the light and its power are extinguished. This is also to be observed in man.

24. The eternal darkness of the soul is hell—a painful source of anguish called the "Anger of God." But the eternal light in the soul is the Kingdom of Heaven, where the fiery anguish of darkness is transformed into joy.

25. The same nature of anguish that causes sadness in the darkness becomes a cause of outward, stirring joy in the light. For the source or origin in the light and the source in the darkness are but one eternal source and one nature. Yet, the light and darkness have a massive difference in their source: one dwells in the other and gives birth to the other, and yet is not the other. The fire is painful and consuming, but the light is yielding, friendly, powerful, and delightful—a sweet and lovely joy.

26. This may also be found in man; he exists and lives in *three worlds*. The first is the *eternal dark world*, the center of the eternal nature, which produces or generates the fire—the source or property of anguish.

27. The second is the *eternal light world*, which gives birth to eternal joy. This is the divine habitation where the Spirit of God dwells, and where the Spirit of Christ receives the human substance and subdues the darkness, so that it must become a cause of joy in the Spirit of Christ in the light.

28. The third is the *outward visible world* made of the four elements and the visible stars. Indeed, every element has its own particular constellation <note>In Boehme's thought, a "constellation" refers to an internal arrangement of spiritual forces or influences.</note> within itself, from which desire and properties arise, much like a mind.

29. Thus, you may understand that the fire in the light is a fire of love—a desire for meekness and delight. But the fire in the darkness is a fire of anguish; it is painful, tedious, hostile <note>original: "inimicitious"</note>, and full of conflict <note>original: "Contrariety"</note> in its essence. The fire of the light has a good flavor or taste, but the taste in the essence of darkness is unpleasant, loathsome, and wearying. For all the forms or properties in the eternal nature are in great anguish until they reach the state of fire.

->## The Second Chapter.<-
->### *How Man is Created.*<-

30. **H**ere we are to consider the creation of man. *Moses says, "God created man in his image; in the image of God he created him."* <note>Genesis 1:27</note> This we understand to be from both the eternal and the temporal birth; out of the inward and spiritual world, which He breathed into him, into the created image; and then out of the substance of the inward spiritual world, which is holy.

31. For just as there is a nature and substance in the outward world, so also in the inward spiritual world there is a nature and substance which is spiritual. From this, the outward world is breathed forth and produced out of light and darkness, and created to have a beginning and a time.

32. And out of the substance of the inward and outward world, man was created; out of, and in the likeness of, the birth of all substances. The body is a <term>Limbus</term> <note>original: "an Extract or a Kind of Seed, which containeth all that which the Thing from whence it is taken hath." In alchemical terms, the *Limbus* is the primordial matter or "dust" from which all things are formed.</note> of the earth, and also a <term>Limbus</term> of the heavenly substance; for the earth is breathed forth, spoken out, or created out of the dark and light world. In the word <term>Fiat</term> <note>Latin: "let it be done." The creative command of God.</note>—namely, in the eternal desire—man was taken out of the earth and so created as an image out of time and eternity.

33. This image was in the inward and spiritual element from which the four elements <note>The classic elements: Earth, Air, Fire, and Water.</note> proceed and are produced. In that one element was Paradise; for the properties of nature from the <term>fire-dark-and-light-world</term> <note>This refers to the author's complex view of reality, where God's nature consists of a "Dark World" (wrath/fire) and a "Light World" (love/light) existing in harmony.</note> were all in harmony and agreement in number, weight, and measure. One of them was not manifested more prominently than another; therefore, there was no frailty within it. For no one property was predominant over another, nor was there any strife or conflict among the powers and properties.

34. Into this created image, God breathed the spirit and breath of understanding out of the <term>three worlds</term> <note>The three realms of existence: the Dark World (divine wrath), the Light World (divine love), and the Outward World (the physical universe).</note> as one single soul. In its original principle or essence, this soul consists of the inward dark <term>fire-world</term> of the eternal spiritual nature, according to which God calls himself <term>a strong, jealous God and a consuming fire.</term> <note>Deuteronomy 4:24</note>

35. And this is now the eternal, created soul: a magical breath of fire. In this fire lies the origin of life, derived from the great power of separation. God’s anger, or the eternal darkness, exists in this property insofar as fire exists without giving light.

36. The second property of the breath of God is the spirit of the source of light, proceeding from the great fiery desire of love and from great meekness. According to this, God calls himself <term>a loving, merciful God</term>; in this consists the true spirit of understanding and of life in power.

37. For as light shines from power, and as the power of understanding is perceived in the light, so the breath of the light was joined to the breath of the fire of God and breathed into the image of man.

38. The third property of the breath of God was the outward air with its <term>Astrum</term> <note>Latin for "star" or "constellation." In this context, it refers to the celestial and astrological influences that govern the physical body.</note>, in which the life and configuration of the outward substance and body consisted. This He breathed into his nostrils; and as time and eternity are joined together, and as time is produced out of eternity, so the inward breath of God was joined to the outward.

It describes the human soul and body as a "Limbus" or extract of both eternal and temporal substances, originally created in perfect harmony.</summary>

## Chap. 2. Of Regeneration.

39. This threefold soul was breathed into man at once, and each substance of the body received the spirit according to its specific property. The outward flesh received the outward air and its astral influences <note>original: "Constellations"</note> to sustain a rational and vegetative life, intended to manifest the wonders of God. Meanwhile, the light-body (the heavenly substance) received the breath of the light of the great divine powers and virtues; this breath is called the Holy Ghost.

40. In this way, the light pierced through the darkness—specifically through the dark breath of fire, the breath of the outward air, and its astral influence <term>astrum</term>—and so stripped all those properties of their independent power. Consequently, neither the anguish of the "fire-breath" within the soul's inner nature, nor heat, nor cold, nor any other property of the outward stars could be felt or manifested.

41. The properties of all three worlds within the soul and body were in perfect agreement, balance <note>original: "Temperature"</note>, and weight. That which was inward and holy ruled through and over the outward—that is, over the external parts of life, the stars, and the four elements. This original and universal power of the inward over the outward is what constituted the Holy Paradise.

42. Thus, man existed both in Heaven and in the outward world simultaneously, and he was lord over all the creatures of this world. Nothing could destroy him.

43. The Earth was also in this state until the curse of God broke forth. The holy property of the spiritual world grew up through the Earth and produced holy, paradisiacal fruits, which man could then eat in a magical, paradisiacal manner.

44. At that time, he had no need for teeth or internal organs in his body. Just as light swallows up darkness, and as fire devours water yet is never filled by it, man possessed a similar "center" for a mouth to eat with, according to the laws of eternity.

45. He was also able to generate others like himself out of his own being without any dividing or opening of his body and spirit. This was done in the same way that God generated the outward world: God did not divide Himself, but through His desire—specifically in the Word *Fiat* <note>Latin: "let it be done"—God's creative command</note>—He manifested Himself and shaped that desire into a form according to the eternal spiritual birth. In this respect, man was created as an image and likeness of God, belonging to both time and eternity, yet intended for an immortal life free from enmity or conflict.

46. However, the Devil—having once been a prince and high-ranking celestial leader <note>original: "Hierarch"</note> in the realm of this world—was cast out for his pride into the dark, anguishing, painful, and hostile source of the wrath of God. He envied man for the glory of being created in and for the spiritual world—the very place he himself once possessed. Therefore, the Devil directed his imagination and desire into the image of man, making man's own desire so full of "lusting" that the dark world and the outward world rose up within him. Man then departed from the equal agreement and balance in which he had stood, allowing one property to dominate the others.

47. Then, each of these properties became manifest on its own, and each lusted after what was like itself. That which came from the birth of the dark world, and that which came from the birth of the light world, each wanted to eat of the *Limbus* <note>The "Limbus" refers to the essential spiritual or material "soil" or "extraction" of the earth</note> of the Earth according to its own hunger. Thus, both Good and Evil became manifest in Adam.

48. When the hunger of these properties turned toward the Earth (from which the properties of the body were originally drawn), the *Fiat* pulled a "branch" or growth out of the Earth that these properties could eat in their newly awakened vanity; for this was now possible.

49. For the spirit of the strong and great magical power of time and eternity was in Adam, the same power from which the Earth and its properties were first breathed out. And so the *Fiat*—the strong desire of eternal nature—attracted the essence of the Earth. And

# Of Regeneration. Chap. 2.

Thus God let the *Tree of Knowledge of Good and Evil* grow for *Adam*, according to his awakened properties; for the great power of the soul and of the body caused it.

50. And then man had to be tested, whether he would stand and remain in his own powers before the tempter, the Devil, and before the wrath of the Eternal Nature; and whether the soul would continue in the perfect balance of the properties in true yielding <note>original: "resignation"; here meaning a state of humble submission to God's will</note> under God's Spirit, as an instrument of God's harmony—a tuned instrument of divine joyfulness for the Spirit of God to play upon. This was tested by that tree, and this severe commandment was added: *Thou shalt not eat thereof, for on that day that thou eatest thereof, thou shalt surely die.*

51. But since it was known to God that man would not stand, and that he had already imagined and lusted after *Good* and *Evil*, God said, *It is not good for man to be alone; we will make him a helper fit for him.*

52. For God saw that *Adam* could not then generate magically, having entered with his *lust* into *vanity* <note>original: "vanity"; the author uses this to describe the fleeting, empty, and corruptible nature of the material world</note>. Now therefore *Moses* says, *God caused a deep sleep to fall upon him, and he slept;* that is, seeing man would not continue in the obedience of the divine harmony in his properties, submitting himself to stand still as an instrument of the Spirit of God; therefore God allowed him to fall from the divine harmony into a harmony of his own—namely, into the awakened properties of evil and good. The spirit of his soul entered into these.

53. And there in this sleep he died to the angelical world and fell under the power of the outward *fiat* <note>original: "fiat"; the creative command or "word" of God that shaped the physical world</note>, and thus bade farewell to the *Eternal Image*, which was of God's begetting. Here his angelical form and power fell into a swoon and lay on the ground.

54. And then by the *fiat*, God made the woman out of him, out of the *matrix of Venus* <note>original: "Matrix of Venus"; a mystical term for the feminine, receptive, and generative principle of love and desire</note>—namely, out of that property wherein *Adam* had the *begettress* within himself. And so out of one body he made two, and divided the properties of the *tinctures* <note>original: "tinctures"; spiritual qualities or essences that define the nature of a thing</note>—namely, the watery and fiery constellations in the element; yet not wholly in substance but in the spirit—namely, the properties of the watery and fiery soul.

55. And yet it is still but one thing, only the property of the *tincture* was divided; the desire of *self-love* was taken out of *Adam* and formed into a woman according to his likeness. And from this it follows that man now so eagerly desires the *matrix* of the woman, and the woman desires the *limbus* <note>original: "limbus"; the essential masculine seed or spiritual matter</note> of the man—namely, the *fire-element*, the origin of the true soul, by which is meant the tincture of fire. For these two were one in *Adam*, and in that unity consisted the *magical begetting*.

56. And as soon as *Eve* was made out of *Adam* in his sleep, both *Adam* and *Eve* were at that instant set and established in the outward natural life, having the members given them for propagation after the manner of the brute animals, and also the fleshly carcass into which they might put their gross earthliness and live like beasts.

57. Of which the poor soul that is captivated in *vanity* is at this day ashamed, and sorry that its body has acquired such a bestial, monstrous shape. Nothing can be clearer than this. For it is because mankind are ashamed of their members and nakedness that they borrow their clothing from the earthly creatures. For they would have no need of this had they not lost the angelical form and assumed that of a beast.

58. This borrowed clothing, together with the awakened earthliness and subjection to the powers of heat and cold, is a plain and full proof to man that he is not truly at home in this world. For all earthly appetites, cares, and fears, together with this false clothing, must perish and be severed from the soul again.

59. Now when *Adam* awoke from sleep, he beheld his wife and knew that she came out of him; for he had not yet eaten of *vanity* with his outward mouth, but only with the *imagination, desire, and lust*.

# Chap. 2. Of Regeneration.

60. It was the first *desire* of *Eve* to eat from the *Tree of Vanity* <note>original: "Tree of Vanity"; here, vanity refers to the empty, transitory, and illusory nature of the material world</note>, of *evil* and *good*. The *Devil*, in the form of a *serpent*, persuaded her by saying *that her eyes should be opened and she should be like God himself*. This was both a *lie* and a *truth*.

61. But he did not tell her that she would lose the *Divine Light* and *power* by doing so. He only said *her eyes should be opened so that she might taste, prove, and know evil and good, just as he had done*. Neither did he tell her that *heat* and *cold* would awaken within her, or that the properties of the physical *constellations* <term>the astrological and physical influences of the stars and planets</term> would have great *power* over her *flesh* and her *mind*.

62. His only *aim* was for the *angelical image*—namely, the *substance* that came from the inward *spiritual world*—to disappear within them. If that happened, they would be forced to live in *subjection* to gross *earthliness* and the *constellations*; he knew well enough that when the outward *world* perished, their *souls* would remain with him in *darkness*. He saw that the *body* must die, which he understood from what *God* had hinted, and so he expected to remain Lord for all eternity over this *world* in the false *shape* he had taken. For this reason, he seduced *man*.

63. For when *Adam* and *Eve* ate the fruit of *evil* and *good* into their *bodies*, the *imagination* of the *body* accepted the *vanity* within the fruit. Then *vanity* awoke in their *flesh*, and the dark *world* gained the upper hand and dominion over their earthly *vanity*. Because of this, the beautiful *image* of *heaven*, which proceeded from the *heavenly divine world*, instantly disappeared.

64. At this moment, *Adam* and *Eve* died to the *Kingdom of Heaven* and woke up to the outward *world*. The beautiful *soul*, as it once stood in the *love of God*, vanished in terms of its holy *power*, *virtue*, and *property*. In its place, a wrathful *anger*—namely, the dark *fire world*—awoke within it. Thus the *soul* became, in its inward *nature*, half *devil*, and in its relationship to the outward *world*, a *beast*.

65. Here are the *bounds* of *death* and the *gates* of *hell*. It is for this *cause* that *God* became *man*: so that he might destroy *death*, defeat the *devil’s purpose*, and change *hell* back into great *love*.

66. Let this be told to you, you *children of men*; it is told to you with the *sound* of a *trumpet* so that you might instantly turn away from this abominable *vanity*, for its *fire* is burning.

# The Third Chapter.

## Of the Lamentable Fall of Man, and of the Means of His Deliverance.

<image-desc>Decorative woodcut initial letter 'N' for paragraph 67, featuring an ornate square border with floral vine patterns and a small stylized face or mask at the bottom center of the frame.</image-desc>

67. **N**ow, when *Adam* and *Eve* fell into this vanity <note>original: "Vanity"; here meaning the empty, illusory state of material existence separated from God</note>, the wrath of nature awoke in every property <note>Böhme uses "property" to describe the fundamental forces or qualities of existence</note>. Through this impressed desire, the vanity of the earthliness and the wrath of God were drawn into the self.

68. Then the flesh became coarse and rough, like the flesh of a beast, and the soul was captured in that same essence. The soul saw that its body had become a beast and had gained animal organs for reproduction <note>original: "Beſtial Members for Multiplication"</note>, as well as a filthy carcass into which the desire would stuff the loathsomeness of which it was ashamed in the presence of God. Therefore, *Adam* and *Eve* hid themselves under the trees of the Garden of *Eden*; heat and cold also seized them.

69. At this point, the "heaven" within man trembled with horror—just as the earth quaked in wrath when God's anger was destroyed on the cross by his sweet love. In that later moment, the anger trembled before the sweet love of God.

70. For the sake of this vanity which was awakened in man, God cursed the earth, so that the holy element <note>a spiritual, pure substance in Böhme's cosmology that underlies the material world</note> should no longer spring or shine forth through the outward fruit, nor bring forth paradisiacal fruit. For there was then no creature that could have enjoyed it, nor was the earthly man worthy of it anymore.

71. God would not cast precious pearls before beasts. An ungodly man in his body is nothing but a coarse, animal creature; and although he is of a noble essence, he is wholly poisoned and loathsome in the sight of God.

72. Now when God saw that his fair image was spoiled, he revealed himself to the fallen *Adam* and *Eve* and had pity on them. He promised himself to them as an everlasting possession. He promised that, through his great love in the humanity he would receive, he would destroy the power of the serpentine property <note>the egoistic, fallen nature associated with the serpent in Eden</note>—namely, the vanity awakened in them by the wrath of God. This was the *breaking of the head of the serpent* which he would perform; that is, he would destroy dark death and subdue anger with his great love.

73. He placed this covenant of his future incarnation into the light of life. The Jewish sacrifices pointed toward this covenant as a mark or *limit* <note>original: "Limit"; a specific theological term in Böhme's work referring to a destined point in time or a boundary where the divine meets the human</note>, to which God had committed himself with his love. For the faith of the *Jews* entered into those sacrifices and offerings, and God’s "imagination" <note>God's creative intent or spiritual focus</note> entered into the covenant.

74. The offering was a symbol <note>original: "Figure"</note> of the restoration of that which *Adam* had lost. Thus, God expiated his anger in the human property through the offering within the "limit" of the covenant.

75. In this covenant, the most holy, sweet name JESUS—proceeding out of the holy name and great power of JEHOVAH—had incorporated itself. He did this so that he might again move and reveal himself in the substance of the heavenly world which had disappeared in *Adam*, and kindle the holy, divine life within it once more.

76. This mark or "limit" of the covenant was passed down from *Adam* and his children, from person to person, and went through from one to all—just as sin and the awakened vanity also went through from one to all.

77. In the end, this promise of the covenant stood in the root of *David* in the Virgin *Mary*, who was, in the inward kingdom of the hidden humanity (namely,

...of the spiritual essence <note>original: "Essentiality"</note> that disappeared regarding the Kingdom of God. She was the Daughter of God’s Covenant, but in her outward nature—according to her natural humanity—she was conceived by her true biological father, **Joachim**, and her true mother, **Anna**, out of the essences and substance of their souls and bodies, like all other children of **Adam**; she was a true daughter of **Eve**.

78. In this **Mary**, from the Virgin (namely, the **Wisdom of God**) <note>In Boehme’s theology, the "Wisdom of God" or Sophia is a divine mirror or feminine principle distinct from the earthly Mary.</note> within the promised limit of the Covenant—of which all the prophets have prophesied—the eternal Speaking Word, which created all things, did in the fullness of time move itself in the Name **JESUS**. According to its highest and deepest love and humility, it brought back living, divine, and heavenly substance <note>original: "Substantiality"</note> into the heavenly part of humanity that had disappeared in **Adam** (the part from which he died in Paradise). This was brought into the seed of **Mary**, into the spiritual quality <term>original: "Tincture"; an alchemical term used here to mean a transforming spiritual essence or "color" that changes the nature of a thing.</term> of love—into that property in which **Adam** should have reproduced himself in a magical and heavenly manner—into the true Seed of the Woman, of heavenly substance, which disappeared in Paradise.

79. And when the Divine Light in the heavenly essence was extinguished, the Word of God (the Divine Power of the Understanding) brought in heavenly and living substance, awakened the disappeared substance in the seed of **Mary**, and brought it to life.

80. And so now God’s substance, in which He dwells and works, and the disappeared substance of man, have become one Person; for the Holy Divine substance did anoint the disappeared part; therefore that Person is called **CHRISTUS**, the **Anointed** of God.

81. And this is the "dry rod of **Aaron**" that blossomed and bore almonds <note>A reference to Numbers 17:8, used here as a symbol of life miraculously springing from death.</note>, and the true High Priest; and it is that humanity of which Christ spoke when He said that *He had come from Heaven, and was in Heaven; and that no man could ascend into Heaven but the Son of Man who has come from Heaven, and is in Heaven.*

82. Now when he says, *He has come from Heaven*, it refers to the heavenly substance, the heavenly body; for the power and virtue of God do not need to "come" anywhere, because God is everywhere, immeasurable and undivided. But *substance* requires coming; the power or virtue needs to move itself and manifest itself in substance.

83. And that substance entered into the human substance and received it—not only that part of heavenly substance which disappeared in **Adam**, but the whole human essence in soul and flesh, according to all the "three worlds" <note>Boehme’s "Three Worlds" are the Dark World (fire/wrath), the Light World (divine majesty), and the Outward World (the visible universe).</note>.

84. But He did not receive or take upon Himself the awakened or imprinted "vanity" <note>meaning: futility, corruption, or the emptiness of sin</note> which the Devil brought into the flesh through his imagination, by which the flesh committed sin. However, He did take upon Himself the "awakened forms of life," as they had strayed from their original balance <note>original: "equal agreement"</note>, each of them following its own selfish desire.

85. For therein lay our weakness and the death which He was to drown with His heavenly, holy blood. In this, He took upon Himself all our sins and weaknesses, as well as Death and Hell in the **Wrath of God**, and destroyed their power within human properties.

86. The **Wrath of God** was the "Hell" into which the Spirit of Christ went when He shed that heavenly blood into our outward human blood, and transformed <term>original: "tinctured"</term> it with love. By doing so, He changed that Hell of the human property into Heaven and restored the human properties into their original balance and heavenly harmony.

<summary>This page explains the mystical process of the Incarnation, describing how Christ (the Speaking Word) merged divine substance with human substance through Mary to restore the spiritual life lost by Adam. It emphasizes that Christ took on human suffering and "wrath" to transform them into divine harmony through the power of love.</summary>

# The Fourth Chapter.

## *How we are born anew; and how we may fall into God's anger again.*

87. <margin>1 John 3.
2 Cor. 6.
1 Pet. 1.</margin> **NOW** here we may rightly understand what our *new birth* or *regeneration* is; and how we may become and continue to be the temple of God, even though in this lifetime, according to our outward humanity, we are sinful, mortal men.

88. Christ, in his human essence, has broken open the gates of our inward heavenly humanity, which was shut up in Adam. Because of this, nothing is now lacking except for the soul to draw its will out of the vanity <note>original: "vanity" refers to the emptiness and fleeting nature of the fallen world</note> of the corrupted flesh and bring it into this open gate through the Spirit of Christ.

89. Great and sincere earnestness is required here. It is not only a matter of learning and knowing, but a real hunger and thirst after the Spirit of Christ. For simply knowing is not *faith*. Faith is a hunger and thirst after that which I lack, so that I draw it into myself, lay hold of it with desire and imagination, and make it my own. This is the truth and essence of a *Christian's faith*.

90. The will must depart from the vanity of the flesh and willingly surrender itself to the suffering and death of Christ. It must accept all the mockery of vanity which ridicules it because it leaves the "house" in which it was born and no longer cares for worldly emptiness, but merely desires the love of God in Christ Jesus.

91. In such hunger and desire, the will receives and imprints into itself the Spirit of Christ with his heavenly corporality <term>Corporality: the spiritual "body" or substantial form of Christ that exists beyond the physical world</term>. That is, in its great hunger and desire, the soul takes hold of and draws the body of Christ—namely, the heavenly substantiality—into its own "disappeared" image <note>original: "disappeared image" refers to the divine likeness lost by Adam, which remains dormant or hidden within the soul until regeneration</note>, within which the Word of the power of God is at work.

92. The hunger of the soul brings its desire entirely through the bruised nature of its humanity in that heavenly part which was lost in Adam. The sweet fire of love in the death of Christ broke through this nature when the death of that heavenly humanity was destroyed.

93. And so, through this desire, the soul’s hunger receives into its "disappeared" corporality the holy, heavenly substance—namely, Christ's heavenly body. This body fills the Father everywhere and is near to and within all things. Through this, the lost heavenly body rises in the power of God, in the sweet name of JESUS.

94. This raised heavenly spiritual body is a member of Christ and the temple of the Holy Spirit—a true home for the Holy Trinity, according to Christ's promise: *We will come to you, and make our home in you.* <note>John 14:23</note>

95. The essence of that life eats the flesh of Christ and drinks his blood. For the Spirit of Christ—the Word—which made itself visible through Christ's humanity within our own lost humanity, swallows its holy substance into its own fiery essence; for every spirit eats from its own body.

96. Now, if the soul eats of this sweet, holy, and heavenly food, it ignites itself with the great love found in the name and power of JESUS. Then its fire of anguish <note>Böhme's term for the restless, searching state of the soul before it finds peace in God</note> becomes a great triumph of joy and glory, and the true Sun rises within it, by which it is born into a new will.

<summary>This chapter explains that regeneration is a literal spiritual transformation where the soul "eats" of Christ's heavenly substance to restore the divine image lost by Adam. True faith is described not as intellectual knowledge, but as a practical hunger that draws the Spirit of Christ into the soul.</summary>
<keywords>Regeneration, New Birth, Faith, Christ's Body, Soul's Hunger, Adam, Holy Trinity, Spiritual Body, Jacob Böhme</keywords>

# Chap. 4. Of Regeneration.

97. And here the *Wedding of the Lamb* <note>original: "Wedding of the Lamb" — a biblical metaphor for the mystical union between Christ and the soul (Revelation 19:7-9).</note> takes place. We heartily wish that those who are Christians in name and word only might once find this through their own experience, and so pass from mere history into the true substance.

98. But the soul does not obtain this "Pearl" of Divine Wisdom and Virtue as its own property during this lifetime, because it still has the outward, bestial <note>original: "Beſtial" — referring to the animalistic or purely biological/instinctive nature of human life.</note> flesh sticking to its outward person.

99. The power of this Pearl of Divine Wisdom betrothes itself in this *Wedding of the Lamb* and sinks down into the heavenly image—namely, into the substance of the "heavenly man," who is the temple of Christ. It does not sink into the "fire-breath" <note>In Boehme’s theology, the "fire-breath" represents the soul’s primary, energetic, and potentially harsh nature, which must be tempered by light.</note> of the soul, which is still—during this whole lifetime—fastened to the outward kingdom and the bond of vanity by the breath of the air, and is in great danger.

100. It does indeed often dart its beams of love into the soul, by which the soul receives light. However, the Spirit of Christ does not yield itself up to the "fire-breath" during this lifetime, but only to the "breath of light" which was extinguished in *Adam*. The temple of Christ exists within that light, for that is the true and holy *Heaven*.

101. Understand correctly now what the *New-Birth* or *Regeneration* is and how it happens, as follows: the outward, earthly man is not born anew during this lifetime. This means neither the outward flesh nor the outward part of the soul is reborn. They both continue in the vanity of their wills that awoke in *Adam*. They love their "mother" in whose body they live—namely, the dominion of this outward world—and in that world, the birth of sin is clearly present.

102. The outward man, in both soul and flesh (meaning the outward part of the soul), has no divine will. Neither does he understand anything of God, as the Scripture says: *The natural man does not perceive the things of the Spirit of God, etc.* <note>1 Corinthians 2:14.</note>

103. But the "fire-breath" of the inward world, if it is once enlightened, understands it. It has a great longing, sighing, hunger, and thirst after the sweet fountain of Christ. It refreshes itself by hungering and desiring (which is true faith) for the sweet fountain of Christ from his new body—from the "heavenly substantiality"—like a hungry branch on the vine of Christ.

104. The reason why the fiery soul cannot attain perfection during this lifetime is because it is bound fast by the outward bond of vanity. Through this bond, the Devil continually casts his poisonous rays of influence upon it, testing it so that it often bites at his bait and poisons itself. From this, misery and anguish arise, so that the noble *Sophia* <note>original: "Sophia" — Greek for "Wisdom," personified here as a divine feminine principle or the "Bride of Christ."</note> hides herself in the fountain of Christ, in the heavenly humanity; for she cannot draw near to vanity.

105. For she knew how it went with her in *Adam* when she lost her Pearl. This Pearl is now freely bestowed again upon the inward humanity by grace; therefore she is called *Sophia*, namely, *The Bride of Christ*. See *The Three Principles*, Chapter 16, from verse 47 to verse 51.

106. Here she faithfully calls to her bridegroom, the fiery soul, and exhorts him to repentance—to unburden himself or to go forth from the abomination of vanity.

107. And now war assaults the whole man. The outward, fleshly man fights against the inward, spiritual man, and the spiritual against the fleshly. Thus, man is in continual warfare and strife, full of trouble, misery, anguish, and care.

108. The inward Spirit says to the fiery soul:
> *O my soul! O my love! Turn, I beseech you, and go forth from vanity, or else you will lose my love and the noble Pearl.*

109. Then the outward reason—namely, the bestial soul—says:
> *You are foolish; do you want to be a laughingstock and the scorn of the world? You need the outward world to maintain this life. Beauty, power, and glory are your proper happiness; only in these can you rejoice and take delight. Why would you cast yourself into anguish, misery, and reproach? Take your pleasure, which will do both your flesh and your mind good.*

<sig>* H 2</sig>

<summary>This page describes the mystical process of regeneration as an internal conflict between the "fire-breath" of the soul, tied to worldly vanity, and the "Sophia" or Divine Wisdom that seeks to unite with the spirit. It emphasizes that while the inward man can be enlightened, the physical and "bestial" parts of human nature remain subject to the world and the Devil's temptations during this life.</summary>

110. With such filth the true man is often defiled; that is, the outward man defiles himself like a sow in the mire <note>original: "as a Sow in the Mire," a common biblical metaphor for returning to sin (2 Peter 2:22)</note>, and obscures his noble pearl <note>The "pearl" refers to the "Pearl of Great Price" (Matthew 13:45-46), symbolizing the inner divine spark or the purity of the soul</note>. For the more vain the outward man becomes, the darker the inward man becomes, until at length it disappears altogether.

111. And then the beautiful paradisical tree is gone, and it will be very hard to recover it again. For when the outward light—namely, the outward soul—is once enlightened, so that the outward light of reason is kindled by the inward light, then the outward soul commonly tends to turn hypocrite and considers itself divine, even though the pearl be gone. This lamentable error clings fast to many a man.

112. And thus it happens that the "tree of pearl" in the garden of Christ is often spoiled. Concerning this, the Scripture makes a stern conclusion <note>original: "hard Knot or Concluſion"</note>: *namely, that those who have once tasted the sweetness of the world to come, and fall away from it again, shall hardly see the kingdom of God.* <note>A reference to the warning in Hebrews 6:4-6</note>

113. And though it cannot be denied that the gates of grace still stand open, yet the false and dazzling light of the soul's outward reason so deceives and hinders such men that they suppose they possess the pearl while they still live for the vanity of this world and "dance to the devil’s pipe" <note>original: "dance with the Devil after his Pipe," meaning to be led into sin by the devil's temptations</note>.

# The Fifth Chapter.

## How a person may call themselves a Christian, and how not.

114. <image-desc>Decorative woodcut initial letter 'H' featuring floral patterns and stars within a square border.</image-desc>ERE, therefore, a Christian should consider why he calls himself a Christian and examine truly whether he be one or not. For surely, my learning to know and confess that I am a sinner, and that Christ has destroyed my sins on the cross and shed his blood for me, does not make me a Christian.

115. The inheritance belongs only to the children. A maidservant in a house knows well enough what the mistress wants done, yet that does not make her the heiress of her mistress’s goods. Even the devils know that there is a God, yet that does not change them back into angels. But if the maidservant in the house is married to the son of her mistress, then she may come to inherit her mistress’s goods. And so it is to be understood also in the matter of being a Christian.

116. The "children of the history" <note>original: "Children of the Hiſtory," referring to those who have a mere intellectual or historical knowledge of the Bible without spiritual transformation</note> are not the heirs of Christ’s goods; rather, the legitimate children, regenerated by the Spirit of Christ, are the only true heirs. For God said to Abraham, *Cast out the son of the bondwoman; he shall not inherit with the son of the free woman.* <note>Genesis 21:10; Galatians 4:30</note> For he was a scorner, and only a "historical" son of the faith and spirit of Abraham; and as long as he continued as such, he was not a true inheritor of Abraham’s faith, and therefore God commanded that he should be cast out from inheriting his goods.

117. This was a type <note><term>Type</term>: A biblical person, event, or thing that is believed to foreshadow something in the future, particularly in the New Testament</note> of the future of Christendom. For the promise of Christendom was made to Abraham; therefore, the type was also set forth by two brothers, Isaac and Ishmael, foreshadowing the different states and manners of Christendom—showing how two sorts of people would be in it: namely, true Christians and "lip-Christians" <note>original: "Lip-Chriſtians," those who are Christian in name or speech only, but not in heart or deed</note>. These latter, under the title or outward profession of Christianity, would be but

Mockers, as *Ishmael* was, and *Esau*, who also was a type of the outward *Adam*, just as *Jacob* was a type of *Christ* and his true *Christendom*. <note>In this context, Ishmael and Esau represent the "old self" or the carnal nature, while Jacob and Christ represent the spiritual "new self."</note>

118. Thus, everyone who calls himself a Christian must cast out the son of the *bondwoman* <note>original: "Bond-Woman"; a reference to Hagar in Galatians 4, representing the legalistic or earthly nature</note>—that is, the earthly will. He must constantly kill and destroy it, rather than letting it settle into his inheritance.

119. Neither give the "pearl" <note>A common term in this period for the spark of divine grace or the soul's inner light</note> to the bestial man for him to please and amuse himself with in the outward light and the lusts of the flesh. Instead, we must follow our father *Abraham* and bring the "son of the right will" to Mount *Moriah*, being ready in obedience to God to offer it up. We must always be dying to sin in our will through the death of Christ, giving no place to the "beast of vanity" in the kingdom of Christ, nor letting it become wanton, proud, greedy, envious, or malicious. For all these are the properties of *Ishmael*, the son of the *bondwoman*, whom *Adam* fathered in his vanity upon that wanton whore, the false *bondwoman*, through the devil’s imagination out of the earthly property in flesh and blood.

120. This mocker and <term>titular Christian</term> <note>A Christian in name only, without actual faith or transformation</note> is the son of the false *bondwoman* and must be cast out; for he shall not possess the inheritance of Christ in the kingdom of God. He is not fit; he is only *Babel*, a confusion of the one true language into many. He is merely a talker and a wrangler about the inheritance, thinking to claim it for himself through arguing and debate, or through the hypocrisy of his lips and a pretense of holiness. In his heart, however, he is no better than a bloodthirsty murderer of his brother *Abel*, who is the rightful heir.

121. Therefore, we say what we know: that he who calls himself a true Christian must examine himself. He must find what kind of qualities drive and rule him—whether the Spirit of Christ moves him toward truth, righteousness, and the love of his neighbor, so that he would willingly do what is right if he only knew how.

122. Now, if he finds that he has a real hunger for such virtue, then he may rightly believe that he is being "drawn" <note>referring to the theological concept of "divine drawing," where God pulls the soul toward salvation</note>. He must then begin to practice accordingly, and not be satisfied with merely having the "will" without the "doing." The Father’s drawing of a person to Christ exists in the will, but the true life consists in the doing; for the right spirit does what is right.

123. But if there is a will to do good, yet the doing does not follow, then the "true man" is still imprisoned by vain lusts which suppress his actions. Therefore, such a person is only a hypocrite and an *Ishmaelite*; he says one thing and does another. He proves by his own life that his mouth is a liar, for he himself does not do what he teaches, and consequently, he only serves his bestial nature in vanity.

124. For there are those who say, *"I have the will and would gladly do good, but the earthly flesh I carry holds me back so that I cannot. Yet I shall be saved by grace through the merits of Christ. I comfort myself with his merit and sufferings; he will receive me by pure grace, without any merits of my own, and forgive my sins."* I say that such a person is like someone who knows which food is healthy but refuses to eat it, eating poison instead, which will certainly lead to sickness and death.

125. For what good does it do the soul to know the way to God if it will not walk in it, but continues on a contrary path? What good will it do the soul to comfort itself with the <term>filiation</term> <note>The state of being a child/son of God</note> of Christ, and with his passion and death—flattering itself with the hope of inheriting the estate—if it will not enter into the "filial birth" <note>The process of being spiritually "born again" as a child of God</note>? One must be a true child, born out of the Spirit of Christ, out of his suffering, death, and resurrection. Surely, tickling and flattering oneself with Christ's merits without this true, inner "childship" is a falsehood and a lie, regardless of who teaches it.

126. This comfort belongs only to the penitent sinner who struggles against sin and the anger of God. When temptations come and the devil assaults such a poor...

He uses the allegory of Ishmael and Isaac to distinguish between those who merely talk about faith and those who truly live it.</summary>

<page-num>62</page-num>
<header>Of Regeneration. Chap. 6.</header>

...repentant soul, then it must wholly wrap itself up in the merits and death of Christ as its sole armor of defense.

127. Christ alone indeed has earned <note>original: "merited"</note> redemption for us; but not in such a way that, for the sake of his own merit, he will freely grant us the status of children through an outward adoption only, receiving us as children when we are not. No, he himself is the merit; he is the open gate that leads to death <note>Boehme refers here to the death of the "old self" or the ego.</note>; and through that gate we must enter. He receives no "beast" into his merit, but only those who turn and become like children. Those children who come to him in this way are his reward, which he has earned.

128. For he said this:
> *Father, the men were yours, and you have given them to me [as my reward], and I will give them eternal life.*

But the *life* of *Christ* will be given to no one unless they come to him in his *spirit*, into his *humanity*, *sufferings*, and *merit*, and are therein born as true *children of the merit*.

129. We must be born of his *merit* and "put on" the merit of Christ in his *passion* and *death*. This is not done outwardly with verbal *flattery* <note>original: "flattery" refers here to superficial or insincere profession of faith</note> only, or by merely comforting ourselves with it while we remain *aliens* and strange *children*—possessing a foreign *essence* or *nature*. No; a foreign *nature* does not inherit the status of a *child*, but the innate *nature* inherits it.

130. This innate *nature* <note>original: "Essence"</note> is not of this *world* but in *heaven*, of which *St. Paul* speaks, saying:
> *Our citizenship <note>original: "Conversation"</note> is in heaven.*

The nature of a child of God walks in *heaven*, and *heaven* is within *man*.

131. But if *heaven* within a *man* is not open, and the *man* stands outside of *heaven* flattering himself, saying, "*I am still outside, but Christ will take me in through his grace; is his merit not mine?*" such a person exists in *vanity* and *sin* with the outward *man*, and with the *soul* in *hell*—namely, in the *anger of God*.

132. Therefore, learn to understand rightly what *Christ* has taught us and done for us. He is our *heaven*; he must take *form* in us, or else we shall not be in *heaven*. Thus, the *soul’s* inward *man*, together with the holy *body* of *Christ*—that is, in the *new birth*—is in *heaven*, and the outward mortal *man* is in the *world*. Of this, *Christ* spoke, saying:
> *My sheep are in my hand, and no one shall pluck them away; the Father who gave them to me is greater than all.*

## The Sixth Chapter.

### *Of the right and of the wrong way of going to church, receiving the sacraments, and absolution.*

133. <image-desc>A decorative woodcut drop cap for the letter B, featuring ornate foliage and patterns.</image-desc> **B**ELOVED brothers, we will teach you faithfully—not with flattering *lips* to please the *Antichrist* <note>Boehme often used "Antichrist" to refer to institutional religious structures that he felt lacked true spiritual life.</note>, but from our *pearl* <note>The "pearl" is a frequent metaphor in Boehme's work for the inner spark of divine wisdom or the presence of Christ in the soul.</note>, the *virtue*, *power*, and *spirit* of *Christ* in us. We speak from a *Christian nature* and *knowledge*; not from the *husk* and *history* <note>That is, not from mere outward tradition or historical facts alone.</note>, but from a newborn *spirit*, from *Christ's knowledge*, like a *branch* growing on the *vine of Christ*; according to the *measure* of that *knowledge* which is opened in us by the *will* and *counsel of God*.

134. *People* tie us in these *days* to the *history* and to material *churches* of *stone*. These *churches* are indeed good in their *kind*, if *people* did also bring the *temple* of...

<meta>This page continues the discussion on the nature of regeneration, focusing on why outward religious rituals like the sacraments and absolution do not benefit a person who has not undergone internal spiritual transformation.</meta>

## Chapter 6: On Regeneration

Christ into them. They teach, moreover, that their absolution <note>original: Absolution; the formal release from guilt or sin pronounced by a priest</note> is a forgiving of sins, and that the Supper of the Lord takes away sin; also, that the Spirit of God comes into men through their ministry. All of this has a proper meaning if it were rightly understood, and if men did not cling merely to the husk <note>original: Husk; the outer shell or superficial form of a thing, as opposed to its inner essence</note>.

135. Many a man goes to church for twenty or thirty years, hears sermons, receives the sacraments, and hears absolution declared, and yet at the last he is as much a beast of the devil and vanity as he was at the first. A beast goes into the church and to the Supper <note>original: the Supper; the Lord’s Supper or Holy Communion</note>, and a beast comes out from there again.

136. How will he eat if he has no mouth? Can any man eat that food which is so locked away that he cannot reach it? How will he drink if he cannot get to any water? Or how will he hear if he has no hearing?

137. What good purpose does it serve for me to go to physical churches of stone and there fill my ears with empty breath? Or to go to the Supper and feed nothing but the earthly mouth, which is mortal and corruptible? Can I not feed and satisfy that with a piece of bread at home? What good does it do the soul, which is an immortal life, to have the bestial man <note>original: Beastial Man; the unregenerate human nature that is driven by animal instincts rather than the Spirit</note> observe the form and worship the shell of Christ's institution, if it cannot obtain the kernel within it? For *St. Paul says of the Supper, "You receive it to condemnation, because you do not discern the Lord’s body."*

138. The covenant stands firm and is activated through the use of the institution. Christ offers his Spirit to us in his word (namely, in his preached word), his body and blood in the sacrament, and his absolution in a brotherly reconciliation with one another.

139. But what good does it do a beast to stand and listen if he has no hearing to receive the inward living Word, nor any ground in which to plant the Word so that it may bring forth fruit? Of such people Christ says, *The devil plucks the Word out of their hearts, lest they should believe and be saved.* But how can he do so? Because the Word finds no place in the hearing mind to take root.

140. And so it is with absolution also: What benefit is it to me for someone to say, *“I pronounce or declare to you the forgiveness of your sins,”* when my soul is entirely shut up in sin? Whoever says this to a sinner who is so closed off is in error; and he who receives it without the voice of God within himself confirming the same is deceiving himself. None can forgive sins but God alone.

141. The preacher does not have the forgiveness of sins in his own power; rather, it is the Spirit of Christ in the voice of the priest that has the power, provided the priest himself is a Christian.

142. What good did it do those who heard Christ himself teaching on Earth, when he said, *“Come to me, all you who are weary and burdened <note>original: heavy laden</note>, and I will give you rest”*? What good did this blessed promise do for those who heard it if they did not labor or were not burdened? What became of the refreshment or rest then? Since they had dead ears and heard only the outward Christ, and not the Word of Divine Power, they certainly were not refreshed. The bestial man receives exactly that much benefit from his absolution and sacraments.

143. The covenant is open in the sacraments; the covenant is also activated in the office or ministry of teaching. The soul receives it, but only according to the property <note>original: Property; a term in Jacob Boehme’s mysticism referring to the essential quality, nature, or spiritual state of a person</note> of the soul’s “mouth.”

144. That is, the outward beast receives bread and wine, which he might just as well have at home. And the fiery soul receives the testament according to its property—namely, in the anger of God, it receives the substance of the eternal world, but according to the *property of the dark world*. Therefore, it receives it, as the Scripture says, *to its own judgment or condemnation*. For as the mouth is, so is the food which is taken in by the mouth. And in this same manner, the wicked shall behold Christ at

<summary>This page argues that external religious acts like attending church, receiving communion, or hearing absolution are useless unless the participant has the internal spiritual capacity ("mouth of the soul") to receive them. The author emphasizes that true spiritual nourishment and forgiveness come from God's Spirit within, not from the mere physical performance of rituals.</summary>

<meta>This page continues Chapter 6, "Of Regeneration," discussing the difference between the spiritual experience of the "Saints" and the "Wicked" regarding the Sacraments, preaching, and the nature of the true Church.</meta>

## Of Regeneration. Chap. 6.

145. At the last Judgment, the wicked will see God as a severe judge; but the Saints shall behold him as a loving Immanuel <note>original: Immanuel; a Hebrew name meaning "God with us."</note>.

146. God’s anger stands open in his Testaments toward the wicked; but toward the Saints, his heavenly loving-kindness and the power of Christ in the holy name JESUS stand open. What good, then, does the "holy thing" do for the wicked, who cannot enjoy it? Or, what is there that can take away a person's sins when their sin is only stirred up and made obvious by it?

147. The Sacraments do not take away sin, nor are sins forgiven simply through them. Instead, it works like this: when *Christ* arises, then the *Adam* <note>original: Adam; referring to the fallen, sinful nature of humanity</note> dies in the essence of the *Serpent*. Just as when the *sun* rises, the *night* is swallowed up by the *day* and is no more, that is exactly how sins are forgiven.

148. The Spirit of Christ eats of his holy substance; the inward man is the receiver of this holy substance. He receives what the Spirit of Christ brings into him—namely, the temple of God, Christ’s flesh and blood. But what does this concern a "beast" <note>referring to a person living only by worldly or animal instincts</note>? Or what does it concern the devils, or the soul that remains in the anger of God? These eat of the "heavenly body" that exists in the heaven where they dwell, which is the abyss, or bottomless pit.

149. This is also how it works in the office or ministry of preaching: the ungodly man hears what the outward soul of the outward world preaches, and that is what he receives—the mere history. If there is "straw" or "stubble" <note>metaphors for worthless or superficial ideas</note> in what is taught, he sucks the vanity out of it. Indeed, if the preaching is mere slander, railing, and uncharitable abuse—as is sometimes the case—then his soul sucks the venomous poison and the murdering cruelty of the devil from it. He tickles himself with this and is pleased with learning how to judge and condemn others.

150. Thus, if the preacher is one who is *dead* and *has no true life in him*, but sows only venom and reproach proceeding out of his own evil affections, then it is the devil who teaches and the devil who hears. Such teaching is received into a wicked heart and brings forth wicked fruits; by these means, the world has become a mere den of murdering devils. So, if you look among the herd of such teachers and hearers, there is little to be found but reviling, slandering, and reproaching, together with contention about words and wrangling about the husk <note>original: "the husk"; the external, superficial parts of religion rather than the spiritual core</note>.

151. But the Holy Spirit teaches through the holy teacher, and the Spirit of Christ hears through the soul, which is the divine house of the divine sound or voice in the holy hearer.

152. The holy man has his church within himself, where he hears and teaches. But *Babel* <note>original: Babel; used here to represent the "city of confusion" or the false, worldly church</note> has a "heap of stones" <note>referring to a physical church building</note> into which she goes with her seeming holiness and real hypocrisy. There she loves to be seen in fine clothes and makes a very devout and godly show; the church of stone is her god, in which she puts her confidence.

153. But the holy man has his church about him everywhere, even within himself; for he always stands and walks, sits and lies down in his church. He lives in the true Christian church—indeed, in the temple of Christ. The Holy Spirit preaches to him out of every creature. Whatever he looks upon, he sees a preacher of God within it.

154. Here the scoffer will say that I despise the "church of stone" where the congregation meets, but I say that I do not. I am only exposing the hypocritical "Whore of Babylon," who commits adultery with the church of stone and calls herself a Christian, but is indeed a prostitute.

155. A true Christian brings his holy church with him into the congregation. For the heart is the true church, where a person must practice the service of God. If I should go a thousand times to church and to the Sacrament every week, and hear absolution <note>the formal forgiveness of sins</note> declared to me every day, yet did not have *Christ in me*, it would all be false—an unprofitable fiction and a "graven image" in *Babel*, and no real forgiving of sins.

<summary>This page argues that true religious experience and the forgiveness of sins happen internally through the "Spirit of Christ" rather than through external rituals or buildings. It distinguishes between the "holy man," who finds God in his own heart and nature, and the hypocrite in "Babel," who relies on outward displays and physical churches.</summary>
<keywords>regeneration, sacraments, true church, Babel, inner man, hypocrisy, preaching, forgiveness of sins, Jakob Böhme, spiritualism</keywords>

<meta>This page continues the discussion of regeneration and the internal spiritual life versus outward religious formality, likely from a collection of Jakob Böhme’s works.</meta>

155. A holy man does holy works from the holy strength of his mind. The work itself is not the atonement or reconciliation <note>original: "Atonement or Reconciliation"; the author emphasizes that works are a result of faith, not the cause of salvation</note>, but it is the building which the true Spirit builds in his very substance; it is his habitation. However, fiction and fancy are the habitation of the false Christian, into which his soul enters with hypocrisy <note>original: "Dissimulation"</note>. Outward hearing reaches only the outward man and works only on the outside; but inward hearing goes into the inner being and works within.

156. Pretend, roar, cry, sing, preach, and teach as much as you want; yet if your inward teacher and hearer are not open, all is nothing but a *Babel* <note>original: "Babel"; a reference to the Tower of Babel, signifying spiritual confusion and the divided, worldly church</note>, a fiction, and a graven image. By these, the spirit of the outward world models and creates for itself a false image in the likeness of the inward truth. It makes a holy show of this, as if it were performing some divine or holy service to God; whereas many times in such worship, the devil works powerfully in the imagination and greatly tickles the heart with those things in which the flesh delights. Indeed, this often happens to the children of God in their outward nature if they do not take great care, so busily does the devil beset and test <note>original: "sift"</note> them.

# The Seventh Chapter.

## Of useless opinions and conflict over the literal text.

158. <image-desc>An ornate woodcut initial letter 'A' featuring floral motifs and small figures.</image-desc> A true Christian, who is born anew of the Spirit of Christ, lives in the simplicity of Christ and has no strife or contention with anyone about religion. He has enough strife within himself against his own <term>bestial</term> <note>original: "Bestial"; referring to the animalistic or lower carnal nature of man</note> evil flesh and blood. He constantly considers himself a great sinner and is afraid of God; but the love of Christ gradually pierces through and drives out that fear, just as the day swallows up the night.

159. But the sins of the unrepentant <note>original: "impenitent"</note> man rest in the sleep of death, bud forth in the pit, and produce their fruit in hell.

160. The "Christendom" that exists in *Babel* <note>referring to fragmented, institutional religion focused on external rules</note> argues about the way men ought to serve and glorify God, as well as how they are to know him and what his <term>essence</term> <note>fundamental nature</note> and will are. They preach dogmatically that whoever does not agree with them in every detail of knowledge and opinion is no Christian, but a heretic.

161. Now I would gladly see how all their sects can be brought to agree in the one thing that might be called a true Christian church, when all of them mock one another—every party reviling the rest and proclaiming them to be false.

162. But a Christian belongs to no sect. He can live in the midst of sects and attend their services without being attached or bound to any of them. He has only one source of knowledge, and that is *Christ in him*. He seeks only one way, which is the desire to always do and teach what is right; and he places all his knowledge and will into the life of Christ.

163. He sighs and wishes continually that the will of God might be done in him, and that his kingdom might be manifested in him. He daily and hourly kills sin in the flesh; for the *Seed of the Woman* <note>A biblical reference to Genesis 3:15, interpreted here as the Christ-nature within the believer</note>—that is, the *inward man in Christ*—continually crushes the *head of the serpent*, which is the power of the devil found in vanity.

<summary>This page contrasts the "Babel" of outward, sectarian religious conflict with the internal, peaceful life of a true Christian. It emphasizes that true faith is found in the "inward man" rather than in external ceremonies or dogmatic disputes.</summary>
<keywords>Regeneration, Babel, sectarianism, inward man, Christ in him, spiritual warfare, Seed of the Woman, Jakob Böhme</keywords>

<page-num>66</page-num>

# Of Regeneration. Chapter 7.

**164.** His **faith** is a **desire** for **God** and **goodness**, which he wraps up in a certain **hope**, trusting in the **words** of the **promise**, and he lives and dies within that hope; though as for the true **man** <note>The "true man" refers to the inner, spiritual self that Boehme believes is immortal and born of God.</note>, he never dies.

**165.** For **Christ** says, *Whoever believes in me shall never die, but has passed through from death to life; and rivers of living water shall flow from him*, namely, good **doctrine** and **works**.

**166.** Therefore I say, that whatever fights and argues over the **letter** <term>the literal or outward text of scripture as opposed to its spiritual meaning</term> is entirely **Babel** <note>original: "Babel"; Jacob Boehme uses this term to describe the "City of Confusion," representing institutional churches that prioritize human logic, dogma, and conflict over spiritual experience.</note>. The **letters** of the **Word** all come from and stand in one **root**, which is the **Spirit of God**; just as various **flowers** all stand in the **earth** and grow alongside one another. They do not fight with each other over their **difference** in **color**, **scent**, or **taste**, but they allow the **earth**, the **sun**, the **rain**, the **wind**, the **heat**, and the **cold** to do with them as they please; and yet every one of them grows in its own unique **essence** and **property**.

**167.** It is exactly the same with the **children of God**; they have various **gifts** and **degrees** of **knowledge**, yet all come from one **Spirit**. They all rejoice at the great **wonders** of **God** and give **thanks** to the **Most High** for his **wisdom**. Why then should they argue about him *in whom they live and exist, and of whose substance they themselves are made?*

**168.** It is the greatest **folly** within **Babel** for **people** to fight about **religion**, as the **devil** has caused the **world** to do. They argue fiercely over **opinions** of their own making—that is, over the **letter**—when the **Kingdom of God** does not consist of any **opinion**, but of **power** and **love**.

**169.** As **Christ** said to his **disciples**, and left with them at the end, saying: *Love one another, as I have loved you; for by this men shall know that you are my disciples.* If **men** would seek after **love** and **righteousness** as fervently as they seek after **opinions**, there would be no **strife** on **earth**, and we would be like **children** of one **father**, needing no **law** or **ordinance**.

**170.** For **God** is not served by any **law**, but only by **obedience**. **Laws** are for the **wicked**, who will not embrace **love** and **righteousness**; they are, and must be, compelled and forced by **laws**.

**171.** We all have only one single **order**, **law**, or **ordinance**, which is to stand still before the **Lord** of all **beings**, to surrender our **wills** to him, and to allow his **Spirit** to play whatever **music** he wishes. In this way, we give back to him as his own **fruit** that which he works and reveals within us.

**172.** Now, if we did not argue about our different **fruits**, **gifts**, **kinds**, and **degrees** of **knowledge**, but instead recognized them in one another like **children** of the **Spirit of God**, what could condemn us? For the **Kingdom of God** consists not in our **knowing** and **supposing**, but in **power**.

**173.** If we did not know half as much, and were more like **children**, and had only a **brotherly mind** and **goodwill** toward one another, living like **children** of one **mother** and as **branches** of one **tree**, drawing our **sap** from a single **root**, we would be far holier than we are.

**174.** **Knowledge** serves only this purpose: to know that we have lost the **divine power** in **Adam** <note>referring to the biblical Fall of Man, where humanity lost its original spiritual connection to God</note> and have now become inclined toward **sin**; to know that we have **evil properties** in us and that doing **evil** does not please **God**; so that through our **knowledge** we may learn to do right. Now, if we have the **power of God** in us and desire with all our **hearts** to act and live rightly, then our **knowledge** is merely our **delight** or a **matter** of **pleasure** in which we rejoice.

**175.** For true **knowledge** is the **revelation** of the **Spirit of God** through **eternal wisdom**. He knows what he wills in his **children**; he shows his **wisdom** and **wonders** through his **children**, just as the **earth** puts forth its various **flowers**.

176. Now if we live with one another like humble children in the Spirit of Christ, each one rejoicing in the gifts and knowledge of the other, who would judge or condemn us? Who judges or condemns the birds in the woods that praise the Lord of all beings with various voices, each one in its own essence <note>original: "essence"; here meaning their unique nature or inherent being</note>? Does the Spirit of God reprove them for not bringing their voices into a single harmony? Does not the melody of them all proceed from His power, and do they not play before Him?

177. Those people, therefore, who fight and argue about the knowledge and will of God, and despise one another on 그 account, are more foolish than the birds in the woods and the wild beasts that have no true understanding. They are more useless in the sight of the holy God than the flowers of the field, which stand still in quiet submission to the Spirit of God and allow Him to manifest divine wisdom and power through them. Yes, such people are worse than thistles and thorns that grow among beautiful flowers; for those at least stand still and are quiet, whereas those arguers are like ravenous beasts and birds of prey, which frighten the other birds from singing and praising God.

178. In short, they are the offspring, branches, or sprouts of the Devil in the anger of God, who, nonetheless, must be made to serve the Lord through their very tormenting. For by their plaguing and persecuting, they squeeze the sap through the essence <note>original: "essence"; the inner spiritual substance or life-force</note> of the children of God, so that they move and stir themselves in the Spirit of God with prayer and continual fighting. In this exercise of their powers, the Spirit of God moves within them.

179. For by this the desire is activated, and so the children of God grow green, flourish, and bring forth fruit; for the children of God are revealed in tribulation <term>tribulation</term> <note>original: "tribulation"; a state of great trouble, suffering, or distress</note>, as the Scripture says, *When you discipline them, they cry fervently to you.*

---

### The Eighth Chapter

->*In which the Christian religion consists; and how people should serve God and their brothers.*<-

180. <insert>A</insert>ll Christian religion consists entirely in this: to learn to *know ourselves*—where we have come from and what we are; how we have gone out from unity into dissension, wickedness, and unrighteousness; how we have awakened and stirred up these evils within us; and how we may be delivered from them again and recover our original blessedness.

181. First, how we were in unity when we were the children of God in *Adam* before he fell. Secondly, how we are now in dissension and disunity, in conflict and opposition. Thirdly, where we go when we pass out of this corruptible condition—where the immortal part goes, and where the mortal part goes.

182. And lastly, how we come out of disunity and vanity and enter again into that one tree—Christ within us—from which we all grew in *Adam*. In these four points, all the necessary knowledge of a Christian consists.

183. So we do not need to fight about anything; we have no cause for contention with each other. Let everyone only practice learning how he may enter again into the love of God and his brother.
