# Of Regeneration. Chapter 8.

184. The Testaments <note>original: "Testaments"; refers to the covenants or formal agreements between God and humanity</note> of Christ are nothing else but a loving bond or brotherly covenant, with which God in Christ binds himself to us, and us to him. All teaching, willing, living, and doing must imply, aim at, and refer to that. All teaching and doing otherwise, whatever it may be, is Babel <note>original: "Babel"; a reference to the Tower of Babel, symbolizing spiritual confusion and the "noise" of conflicting human opinions</note> and a fiction; it is a mere graven image of pride in useless judgments, a disturbing of the world, and a hypocrisy of the devil, with which he blinds simplicity <note>original: "Simplicity"; referring here to simple-hearted or innocent believers</note>.

185. Every preacher lacking the Spirit of God, who without divine knowledge sets himself up as a teacher of divine things, pretending to serve God thereby, is false. He only serves his belly—his idol—and his own proud, insolent mind, desiring to be honored on that account and esteemed holy, or a theologian in *holy orders* <term>the formal status of an ordained minister or member of the clergy</term>. He holds an office to which he is set apart and chosen by human beings, who only flatter him and have ordained him for the sake of favor.

186. Christ said, *Whoever does not enter by the door—that is, through his Spirit—into the sheepfold, but climbs up some other way, the same is a thief and a murderer, and the sheep do not follow him, for they do not know his voice.*

187. He does not have the voice of the Spirit of God, but only the voice of his own skill and learning; the man teaches, and not the Spirit of God. But Christ says, *Every plant which my heavenly Father has not planted shall be uprooted.*

188. How then will he who is ungodly plant heavenly plants, when he has no seed alive in its power within himself? Christ says expressly, *The sheep do not hear his voice; they do not follow him.*

189. The written Word is only an instrument by which the Spirit leads us to itself within us. That Word which will teach must be living within the literal word. The Spirit of God must be in the literal sound, or else no one is a teacher of God, but a mere teacher of the letter—one who knows the history, but not the Spirit of God in Christ.

190. Everything with which people intend to serve God must be done in faith—namely, in the Spirit. It is the Spirit that makes the work perfect and acceptable in the sight of God. All that a person undertakes and does in faith, they do in the Spirit of God; this Spirit of God cooperates in the work, and then it is acceptable to God. For God has done it himself, and his power and virtue <note>original: "virtue"; here meaning divine essence or power</note> are in it: it is holy.

191. But whatever is done in *self* <note>original: "Self"; refers to the ego or human nature acting independently of God's grace</note>, without faith, is but a figure and a shell, or the husk of a true Christian work.

192. If you serve your brother, but do it only in hypocrisy and give to him unwillingly, then you do not serve God. For your faith does not proceed from love, nor does it enter into hope through your gift. Indeed, you serve your brother, and he for his part thanks God and blesses you, but you do not bless him. For you give him your gift with a grudging spirit, which does not enter into the Spirit of God or into the hope of faith; therefore, your gift is only half-given, and you have only half your reward for it.

193. The same is true of receiving a gift. If anyone gives in faith and in divine hope, he blesses his gift by his faith. But whoever receives it unthankfully and grumbles in his spirit, he curses it in the use or enjoyment of it. Thus it is that everyone shall have his own; *Whatever he sows, that shall he also reap.*

194. So it is also in the office of teaching; *Whatever a man sows, that also he reaps.* For if any man sows good seed from the Spirit of Christ, it takes root in the good heart and brings forth good fruit; but in the wicked, who are not capable of receiving the good seed, the anger of God is stirred.

195. If anyone sows contentions, reproaches, and misinterpretations, all ungodly people receive that into them; it takes root in them as well and brings forth fruit accordingly. So they learn by this to despise, revile, slander, and misrepresent one another.

<summary>This page argues that true Christian ministry and service must proceed from the Spirit of God rather than human learning or selfish motives. It emphasizes that actions performed without faith or love are spiritually empty, and that both teachers and recipients "reap what they sow" in their spiritual lives.</summary>

### Chap. 8. Of Regeneration.

From this root, the great "Babel" <note>original: Babel; referring to the biblical Tower of Babel, symbolizing a state of confusion, pride, and division within the church</note> has sprung and grown. Within it, people argue out of mere pride and conflict over historical details and the justification of a poor sinner in the sight of God. By doing this, they cause simple people to stumble and speak profanely, to the point that one brother reviles and curses another. They excommunicate one another or condemn each other to the devil, all for the sake of literal interpretations and historical accounts.

196. Such mockers and abusers do not fear God; instead, they build a great monument of dissension. Since corrupt desires still reside in the earthly flesh of all people, these leaders awaken abominable thoughts even in God’s simple children. They cause both God's people and the "children of iniquity" <note>original: Children of Iniquity; those who live in sin or lawlessness</note> to blaspheme. In this way, they become the master-builders of the world’s great Babel. They are as useful to the Church as a "fifth wheel on a wagon"—and worse, they are actually erecting a building that is hellish in nature.

197. Therefore, it is absolutely necessary for the children of God to pray earnestly so they may learn to recognize this false building. they must withdraw their minds from it and refuse to help build it up or persecute their fellow children of God. By participating in such things, they hold themselves back from the Heavenly Kingdom and turn away from the right path.

198. This is according to the saying of Christ to the Pharisees: "Woe to you, Pharisees! For you travel across sea and land to make a single convert <term>original: Proselyte; a person who has converted from one opinion or religion to another</term>, and when he is converted, you make him twice as much a child of hell as yourselves." This is unfortunately very true of the modern factions and sects led by those who preach and shout for conflict.

199. Therefore, based on the gifts revealed to me by God, I desire to faithfully warn all God's children who wish to be true members of Christ: depart from such abominable arguments and "bloody firebrands" <note>original: bloody Firebrands; people who passionately incite conflict, anger, or violence</note>. Leave all strife with your brothers and sisters behind, and strive only for love and righteousness toward all people.

200. For a person who is like a good tree must produce good fruit. Sometimes he must allow "swine" to devour his fruit, yet he must remain a good tree regardless. He must always be willing to work with God and not allow any evil to overcome him. Then he stands and grows in God's field, producing fruit to be placed on God's table, which he shall enjoy forever. Amen. Let everything that has breath praise the name of the Lord. Hallelujah.

<summary>The author warns against the "Babel" of religious sectarianism and literalist arguments, urging believers to abandon prideful strife in favor of love and spiritual growth. He emphasizes that true children of God produce good fruit regardless of the hostility they face from "firebrands" and divisive teachers.</summary>

# THE FOURTH BOOK.

->A<-

# DIALOGUE

->BETWEEN<-

## A SCHOLAR AND HIS MASTER,

->CONCERNING<-

# THE SUPERSENSUAL LIFE. <note>original: "Supersensual Life" refers to a state of existence beyond the reach of the physical senses.</note>

->SHOWING<-

How the soul may attain to *divine hearing* and *vision*, and what its *childship* <note>original: "childship"; the spiritual state of being a child of God.</note> in the *natural* and *supernatural life* is; and how it passes out of *nature* into *God*, and out of *God* into *nature* and *self* again; also what its *salvation* and *perdition* <note>original: "perdition"; eternal ruin or damnation.</note> are.

<summary>This title page introduces a mystical dialogue exploring the soul's transition between the natural world and the divine, supersensual realm. It outlines themes of spiritual hearing, vision, and the state of the soul in relation to God and self.</summary>
<keywords>Jacob Boehme, mysticism, supersensual life, divine vision, childship, salvation, nature, soul</keywords>

## I.

### 1 Corinthians 2:7, 8, 9, 10, 11, 12, 13, 14, 15.

*We speak the hidden, mystical wisdom of God, which God ordained before the world for our glory—which none of the rulers <note>original: "Princes"</note> of this world knew. For had they known it, they would not have crucified the Lord of glory. But, as it is written: "Eye has not seen, nor ear heard, nor has it entered into the heart of man to imagine the things which God has prepared for those who love him."*

*But God has revealed them to us by his Spirit; for the Spirit searches all things—yes, the deep things of God. For what man knows the things of a man, except the spirit of the man which is in him? Even so, no one knows the things of God except the Spirit of God. Now we have received, not the spirit of the world, but the Spirit which is from God, so that we might know the things that are freely given to us by God.*

*We also speak of these things, not in the words which human wisdom teaches, but which the Holy Spirit teaches, comparing spiritual things with spiritual. But the natural man <note>original: "natural man"; referring to a person relying solely on human reason and instincts without divine inspiration</note> does not receive the things of the Spirit of God, for they are foolishness to him; neither can he know them, because they are spiritually discerned. But he who is spiritual judges <note>original: "judgeth, or discerneth"</note> all things.*

<summary>This page presents a modernized excerpt from 1 Corinthians 2, emphasizing that divine wisdom is a hidden mystery revealed only through the Holy Spirit rather than human intellect.</summary>

### OF
# THE SUPERSENSUAL LIFE,
### OR,
## THE LIFE WHICH IS ABOVE SENSE.
#### IN
### A DIALOGUE between a Scholar or *Disciple* and his *Master*.

---

->*Disciple. Master.*<-

<margin>Decorative initial T</margin>
THE *Disciple* said to his *Master*: Sir, how may I come to the *supersensual life* <term>supersensual life: a spiritual state that exists beyond the reach of the five physical senses</term>, so that I may see God and hear God speak?

The *Master* answered and said: Son, when you can throw yourself into THAT where no created thing dwells—even if only for a moment—then you will hear what God speaks.

->*Disciple.*<-
Is that place where no created thing dwells near at hand, or is it far away?

->*Master.*<-
It is *within you*. And if you can, my son, cease for a while from all your own thinking and willing, then you shall hear the unspeakable words of God.

->*Disciple.*<-
How can I hear Him speak when I am standing still from thinking and willing?

->*Master.*<-
When you stand still from the thinking of self and the willing of self; when both your intellect and will are quiet and passive to the impressions of the eternal Word and Spirit; and when your soul is raised up above that which is temporal <term>temporal: relating to time; worldly or fleeting things</term>—the outward senses and the imagination being locked away by holy abstraction <term>holy abstraction: a state of meditative withdrawal from the physical world</term>—then the eternal hearing, seeing, and speaking will be revealed in you. In this way, God hears and sees through you, as you are now the instrument of *His Spirit*. Thus God speaks in you and whispers to your spirit, and your spirit hears His voice.

<summary>This page introduces a dialogue on reaching a "supersensual" or mystical state of being. The Master explains that to hear God, one must temporarily silence the self, the will, and the physical senses to become an instrument for the Divine Spirit.</summary>
<keywords>Jacob Boehme, mysticism, supersensual life, meditation, divine voice, self-will, spirituality, 17th-century theology</keywords>

*You are blessed, therefore, if you can stand still from self-thinking and self-willing, and can stop the wheel of your imagination and senses; because by doing this, you may eventually arrive to see the great salvation of God, being made capable of all manner of divine sensations and heavenly communications. Since it is nothing indeed but your own hearing and willing that hinder you, so that you do not see and hear God.*

<gloss>1 2 0 4</gloss>
->Disciple.<-

But by what means shall I hear and see God, since he is *above nature and creation <note>original: "Creature," meaning anything created by God rather than the Creator himself.</note>?*

<gloss>4 0 8</gloss>
->Master.<-

Son, when you are *quiet and silent*, then you are as God was before nature and creation; you are that which God then was; you are that from which he made your nature and created form. Then you hear and see even with that through which God himself saw and heard in you, before ever your own willing or your own seeing began.

->Disciple.<-

What now hinders or keeps me back, so that I cannot come to *that* state through which God is to be seen and heard?

->Master.<-

Truly, nothing but your own willing, hearing, and seeing keeps you back from it, and hinders you from coming to this *Supersensual State* <note>The "Supersensual State" refers to a level of existence beyond the reach of the physical senses.</note>. It is because you strive so much against *that* source from which you yourself are descended and derived. In doing so, you break yourself off by your own willing from God’s willing, and by your own seeing from God’s seeing. 

Inasmuch as in your own seeing, you see only by your own will; and with your own understanding, you understand only in accordance with this will of yours, as it stands divided from the divine will. Furthermore, this willing of yours stops your hearing and makes you deaf toward God through your own thinking upon *earthly things* <note>original: "terrestrial Things"</note> and your attention to what is outside of you. In this way, it brings you into a foundation where you are caught and held captive in *nature*. Having brought you here, it overshadows you with that which you *desire*; it binds you with your own chains and keeps you in your own dark prison which you make for yourself. Thus, you cannot leave that place or come to that state which is supernatural and supersensual.

->Disciple.<-

Since I am *in nature*, and thus bound by my own chains and by my own *natural will*, please be so kind, sir, as to tell me how I may come *through nature* into the supersensual and supernatural foundation, without destroying nature?

->Master.<-

Three things are required for this. The *first* is: you must surrender <note>original: "resign up"</note> your will to God and sink yourself down to the dust in his mercy. The *second* is: you must hate your *own* selfish will and stop doing that which your own will drives you to do. The *third* is: you must bow your soul under the Cross, heartily submitting yourself to it, so that you may be able to endure the temptations of nature and creation. If you do this, know that God will speak into you and will bring your surrendered <note>original: "resigned"</note> will into himself, into the supernatural foundation. And then you shall hear, my son, what the Lord *speaks in you*.

<summary>The Master explains that a believer can only experience God by silencing their own selfish will and sensory distractions to reach a "supersensual" state. He outlines a three-step process of spiritual resignation, self-denial, and submission to the Cross to achieve this divine connection.</summary>

# Of the Supersensual Life.

->Disciple.<-

This is a hard saying, Master; for I must forsake the world, and my life too, if I should do this.

->Master.<-

Do not be discouraged by this. If you forsake the world, then you enter into that from which the world was made; and if you lose your life, then your life is in that for whose sake you forsake it. Your life is in God, from where it came into the body; and as you find your own power becoming faint, weak, and dying, the power of God will then work in you and through you.

->Disciple.<-

Nevertheless, since God has created man in and for the natural life—to rule over all creatures on earth and to be a lord over all things in this world—it does not seem at all unreasonable that man should therefore possess this world and the things in it for his *own*.

->Master.<-

If you rule over all creatures only *outwardly*, there cannot be much value in that. But if you have a mind to possess all things, and to be a true lord indeed over all things in this world, there is a completely different method you must take.

->Disciple.<-

Please, how is that? And what method must I take to arrive at this sovereignty?

->Master.<-

You must learn to distinguish well between the *Thing itself* and that which is only an *image* of it; between that sovereignty which is *substantial* (and in the inward ground or nature) and that which is imaginary (and in an *outward* form or appearance); between that which is properly *angelic* and that which is no more than *bestial* <note>original: "bestial", meaning animal-like or driven by base instincts</note>. 

If you rule over the creatures externally only, and not from the *right internal ground* of your renewed nature, then your will and ruling is truly in a *bestial way*. Yours is, at best, only a sort of imaginary and temporary government, being void of that which is substantial and permanent—the very thing you were made to desire and pursue. Thus, by your outward lording it over the creatures, it is very easy for you to lose the substance and the reality, while you have nothing remaining but the image or shadow only of your first and original lordship. 

You are capable of being invested with this lordship again if you are wise and take your authority from the Supreme Lord in the right course and manner. However, by willing and ruling in this *bestial manner*, you also bring your desire into a *bestial essence*. By this means, you become infected and captivated within it, and you acquire a bestial nature and condition of life. 

But if you put off the bestial and *wild* <note>original: "ferine"</note> nature, and if you have left the *imaginary* life and quit its low, image-based condition, then you have entered into the *state beyond images* <note>original: "super-imaginariness"</note> and into the *intellectual life* <note>In this context, "intellectual" refers to the life of the spirit or pure mind, rather than just academic study</note>. This is a state of living *above* images, figures, and shadows. And so you rule over all creatures, being reunited with your Origin in that very ground or source from which they were and are created. Henceforth, nothing on earth *can hurt you*. For you are like all things, and nothing is *unlike* you.

<summary>The Master explains that true power over creation comes not from outward ownership, but from forsaking the "bestial" self to find life in God. By moving beyond the world of temporary images into a spiritual, "supersensual" state, man regains his original sovereignty over all things.</summary>
<keywords>sovereignty, internal ground, bestial nature, intellectual life, Jakob Böhme, spiritual transformation, mastery over nature</keywords>

## Of the Supersensual Life:

->*Disciple.*<-

O loving Master, please teach me how I may take the shortest path to become like *all things*.

->*Master.*<-

With all my heart. Only think on the words of our Lord Jesus Christ, when he said, *“Unless you are converted and become as little children, you shall not enter into the Kingdom of Heaven”* <note>Matthew 18:3</note>. There is no shorter way than this; nor can a better way be found. Truly, *Jesus says to you*: unless you turn and become as a child, depending upon him for *all things*, you shall not see the Kingdom of God. Do this, and nothing shall hurt you; for you shall be at friendship with all things that exist, as you depend on the Author and Fountain of them, and become like him through such dependence and the union of your will with his will. 

But take note of what I have further to say, and do not be startled by it, even though it may seem hard for you to understand at first. If you want to be like *all things*, you must forsake *all things*. You must turn your desire away from them all and not long for or hanker after any of them. You must not stretch out your will to possess something as your own, or for yourself, no matter what that *something* might be. For as soon as you take *something* into your *desire* and receive it into yourself as your own property <note>original: "propiety," referring to the state of self-centered ownership or "self-hood"</note>, then this very *something* (whatever its nature may be) becomes the *same* as yourself. It works with you in your will, and you are then bound to protect it and take care of it, just as you would your *own being*. 

But if you receive no *thing* into your *desire*, then you are free from *all things* and rule over all things at once, like a prince of God. For you have received nothing as your own, and you are nothing to all things, and all things are as nothing to you. You are like a child who does not understand what a *thing* is; and even if you do understand it, you understand it without becoming entangled with it and without it noticeably affecting or touching your perception. This is the manner in which God rules and sees all things: he comprehends all, and yet nothing comprehends him.

->*Disciple.*<-

Ah! How shall I arrive at this heavenly understanding—at this sight of *all things* in God? How do I reach this pure and naked knowledge which is separated from the senses, this light above nature and creation, and this participation in the Divine Wisdom which oversees all things and governs through all intellectual beings? For, alas, I am *touched* every moment by the things that are around me, and *overshadowed* by the clouds and vapors <note>original: "fumes"</note> which rise up out of the earth. I desire, therefore, to be taught, if possible, how I may attain such a state and condition where no creature may be able to touch me to hurt me; and how my mind, being purged from sensory objects <note>original: "sensible objects"</note> and things, may be prepared for the entrance and dwelling of the Divine Wisdom within me?

->*Master.*<-

You desire that I would teach you how you are to attain it; and I will direct you to our Master, from whom I have learned it, so that you may learn it yourself from him, who alone teaches the heart. Listen to him. Would you arrive at this; would you remain untouched by *sensory things* <term>sensibles: things perceived by the physical senses rather than the spirit</term>; would you behold light in the very light of God and see all things by it? Then consider the words of Christ, who is that *Light* and who is the *Truth*. O consider now his words, who said, *“Without me you can do nothing”* <note>original text cites John xix. 5, but the verse is John 15:5</note>. Do not delay in applying yourself to him, who is the *strength* of your salvation and the *power* of your life, and *with whom* you can do all things through the faith which he works in you. But unless you wholly give yourself up to the—

<header>Of the Supersensual Life.</header>

# Of the Supersensual Life.

...[the] Life of our Lord Jesus Christ, and resign your Will wholly to him, and desire nothing and will nothing without him, you shall never come to such a Rest as no Creature <note>original: "Creature"; in this context, Jakob Böhme refers to any created thing or worldly distraction that is not God.</note> can disturb. Think what you please, and be ever so much delighted in the activity of your own reason, you shall find that in your own power, and without such a total surrender to God and to the life of God, you can never arrive at such a rest as this, or the true quiet of the soul, where no creature can molest you, or even touch you. 

When you have, by Grace, attained to this, then with your body you are in the world, as in the properties of outward nature; and with your reason, you are under the Cross of our Lord Jesus Christ; but with your will, you walk in Heaven and are at the End from which all creatures proceeded, and to which they return again. And then you can, in this END—which is the same as the BEGINNING—behold all things outwardly with reason and inwardly with the mind; and so may you rule in all things and over all things with Christ, to whom all power is given both in Heaven and on Earth.

->*Disciple.*<-

O Master, the creatures which live in me hold me back, so that I cannot wholly yield and give myself up as I willingly would. What am I to do in this case?

->*Master.*<-

Do not let this trouble you. Does your will go forth from the creatures? Then the creatures are forsaken in you. They are in the world; and your body, which is in the world, is with the creatures. But spiritually you walk with God and converse in Heaven; being in your mind redeemed from Earth and separated from creatures to live the life of God. 

And if your will thus leaves the creatures and goes forth from them—even as the spirit goes forth from the body at death—then the creatures are dead in the will and live only in the body in the world. Since if your will does not bring itself into them, they cannot bring themselves into it, nor can they by any means touch the soul. And hence St. Paul says, 
> *Our conversation <note>original: "Conversation"; in the 17th century, this meant one's "citizenship" or "conduct/way of life."</note> is in Heaven*; 

and also, 
> *You are the temple of God, and the Spirit of God dwells in you.* 

So then true Christians are the very temples of the Holy Spirit, who dwells in them; that is, the Holy Spirit dwells in the will, and the creature dwells in the body.

->*Disciple.*<-

If the Holy Spirit now dwells in the will of the mind, how ought I to keep myself so that he does not depart from me again?

->*Master.*<-

Mark, my son, the words of our Lord Jesus Christ: 
> *If you abide in my words, then my words abide in you.* 

If you abide with your will in the words of Christ, then his word and Spirit abide in you, and all shall be done for you that you can ask of him. But if your will goes into the creature, then you have broken yourself off from him. Then you can only keep yourself by abiding continually in the most resigned humility and by entering into a constant course of penitence, wherein you will always be grieved at your own creaturely nature, and that creatures still live in you—that is, in your bodily appetite. If you do this, you stand in a daily dying from the creatures and in a daily ascending into Heaven in your will; which will is also the will of your Heavenly Father.

<summary>This page describes the mystical "Supersensual Life," where the believer's will is detached from worldly "creatures" to find rest in God, even while the physical body remains in the world. The Master instructs the Disciple on maintaining this state through humility, penitence, and abiding in the words of Christ.</summary>
